The wise priests praise with hymns of praise the goddess Uṣas, who has a shining chariot, is of great form, is worshipped through the sacrifice, has a golden-coloured form, shines dispersing the darkness, has the nature of a deity and goes before the sun.
The wise priests celebrate with hymns the divine, bright-charioted, expanded Dawn ; worshipped with holy worship, purple-tinted, radiant, leading on the sun.

दर्शता (*darśatā*): this lovely Uṣas, बोधयंती (*bodhayaṃtī*), awakening: whom? The person who is asleep, this is the meaning. Making the paths सुगान् (*sugān*), easy to travel, she goes अग्रे (*agre*), before the sun. What is this Uṣas like? बृहद्रथा (*bṛhadrathā*), having a large chariot; बृहती (*bṛhatī*), great; विश्वमिन्वा (*viśvaminvā*), pervading the whole world. Such a Uṣas bestows light, brilliance, at the beginning of the days.
- दर्शता (*darśatā*)—she who has an attractive form
- बृहद्रथा (*bṛhadrathā*)—she who has a chariot of huge form
- बृहती (*bṛhatī*)—she who is of great form
- अग्रे (*agre*)—in the first parts (in the morning)

Uṣas, who has an attractive form, goes awakening the people and making, in front of the sun, paths easy to travel. Uṣas, who has a chariot of huge form, is of great form and pervades the world, spreads brilliance in the first parts of the days (in the morning).
The lovely dawn, arousing man, goes before (the sun) preparing practicable paths, riding in a spacious chariot; vast, expanding everywhere, she diffuses light at the commencement of the days.

This Uṣas, harnessing to the chariot the oxen of ruddy colour, अस्रेधंती (*asredhaṃtī*), unwithering, or unwasting. What does she do? रयिं (*rayiṃ*), wealth, अप्रायु (*aprāyu*), that which does not go away, unshaken, she makes. Doing what? रदंती (*radaṃtī*), making the paths shine; for what purpose? सुविताय (*suvitāya*), for good going. देवी (*devī*), shining; पुरुष्टुता (*puruṣṭutā*), praised by many; विश्ववारा (*viśvavārā*), to be chosen by all, she shines forth; she makes light.
- पुरुष्टुता (*puruṣṭutā*)—she who is praised by many
- विश्ववारा (*viśvavārā*)—she who is cherished by all, Uṣas
- सुविताय (*suvitāya*)—so as to be fit for excellent travel

Uṣas, harnessing golden-coloured oxen to her chariot, without weariness, makes wealth firm. Uṣas, who is shining, praised by many and cherished by all, shines, making the paths shine so as to be fit for the excellent travel of the sun.
Harnessing the purple oxen to her car, unwearied she renders riches perpetual: a goddess, praised of many, and cherished by all, she shines, manifesting the paths that lead to good.

This Uṣas becomes व्येनी (*vyenī*), especially white. द्विबर्हा (*dvibarhā*): of the two, the first and the middle, Uṣas being परिवृढोषाः (*parivṛḍhoṣāḥ*), ⟨NOTE:109⟩ afterwards, तनूमाविष्कृण्णाना (*tanūmāviṣkṛṇṇānā*), making her own body manifest. Where? पुरस्तात् (*purastāt*), in the eastern quarter. Moreover, she follows well the path of ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*), of the sun. Moreover, प्रजानतीव (*prajānatīva*), as if knowing, making the world aware; the word इव (*iva*) is in the sense of "now". न दिशो मिनाति (*na diśo mināti*): she does not injure the quarters; on the contrary she illumines the quarters. Or else, as if knowing clearly what is to be followed, she follows the path of ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*).
notes: ಅಶ್ವಮ printed; Aśvins?

en: - द्विबर्हाः (*dvibarhāḥ*)—although she has traversed the two places, earth and atmosphere
- व्येनी भवति (*vyenī bhavati*)—she is of a very bright colour
- साधु (*sādhu*)—the excellent path on which she has to travel
- न मिनाति (*na mināti*)—she does not injure

Although Uṣas has traversed the two places, earth and atmosphere, she is of a very bright colour, making her form manifest only in the eastern direction. As if she knew well the excellent path on which she has to travel, she goes following the path of the sun. She does not injure any quarter.

Lucidly white is she, occupying the two (regions, the upper and middle firmament), and manifesting her person from the east: she traverses the path of the sun as if knowing (his course), and harms not the quarters of the horizon.

This Uṣas, like a woman pure white in colour, spotless and well adorned, making known her limbs, and like one who has bathed and rises up from the bath, has risen for our sight, that is, before us, so that all may see her; she rises in the eastern quarter. What does she do? Driving away the hateful darknesses, Uṣas, the daughter of heaven, comes with radiance, that is, with brilliance.
- शुभ्रा न (*śubhrā na*)—like a woman adorned with bright garments and ornaments
- स्नाती (*snātī*)—like a woman who has gone down to bathe
- ऊर्ध्वेव (*ūrdhveva*)—appearing as if rising up from the water, swaying modestly
- अप बाधमाना (*apa bādhamānā*)—afflicting and driving them far away

This goddess Uṣas, like a woman adorned with bright garments and ornaments, showing her limbs, and like a woman who has gone down to bathe and rises up from the water swaying modestly, appearing, has risen and stands for our sight. Uṣas, the daughter of the atmosphere, afflicting the hateful dense darknesses and driving them far away, comes with her own brilliance.

Exhibiting her person like a well-attired female, she stands before our eyes, (gracefully) inclining like (a woman who has been). bathing : dispersing the hostile glooms, Ushas, the daughter of heaven, comes with radiance.

This Uṣas, facing the west, the daughter of heaven, sends forth her form towards all beings, like an auspicious woman, one of fair dress; she sends it out. Further, to the giver of oblations, the sacrificer, she bestows desirable riches; ever young, that is, ever in youth, or else mingling with all things everywhere, she again now makes light as before.
- दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—to the sacrificer who gives oblations
notes: reference missing in the print after ರಲ್ಲಿಯೂ: "in ... also"

en: Uṣas, the daughter of the atmosphere, facing the west, provides form to all beings like an auspicious woman. Providing the much desired riches to the sacrificer who gives oblations, the ever young Upasu again produces brilliance as before.

Ushas, the daughter of heaven, tending to the west puts forth her beauty like a (well-dressed) woman, bestowing precious treasures upon the offerer of adoration : she ever youthful, brings back the light as (she has done) of old.

The wise priests and sacrificers apply their own minds to all the rites, that is, they make a resolve for the favour of Savitṛ. Also they apply their actions, that is, they engage in them. By whose leave? By the leave of the wise, great, learned or praiseworthy Savitṛ. The Śruti says that Savitṛ is the lord of impulses ⟨NOTE:118⟩. He alone, the Savitṛ, ordains the proper acts of the seven Hotṛs. He is वयुनाविद् (*vayunāvid*): वयुन (*vayuna*) is a name for knowledge; he who knows the knowledge concerning each performance alone ordains and fixes each separately. Further, the praise of that divine Savitṛ is great, very abundant; the meaning is that it is within the range of praise.
notes: ಆಶ್ವಲಾಯನಶೌತಸೂಕ್ತದ and ಸೂಕ್ತದಿಂದ printed (sūkta) where sūtra is expected

en: - बृहतः (*bṛhataḥ*)—of the one of great form
- वयुनावित् (*vayunāvit*)—Savitṛ, who knows the form of each rite
- वि दधे (*vi dadhe*)—makes them perform individually

The wise priests and sacrificers apply their minds to the rites themselves. And they apply their rites to Savitṛ, who is wise, of great form and learned. Savitṛ, who knows the form of each rite, alone makes the seven Hotṛs perform their acts individually. The praise of the divine Savitṛ is full of greatness.

The wise apply their minds: they perform sacred rites for the propitiation of the intelligent, great, adorable Savitri : he alone, knowing their functions, directs the priests: verily, great is the praise of the divine Savitri.

विप्राः मनः युंजते । मेधाविनः ऋत्विग्यजमानाः स्वीयं मनः सर्वेषु कर्मसु योजयंति । सवित्रमनुग्रहाय संकल्पं कुर्वंतीत्यर्थः । (*viprāḥ manaḥ yuṃjate | medhāvinaḥ ṛtvigyajamānāḥ svīyaṃ manaḥ sarveṣu karmasu yojayaṃti | savitramanugrahāya saṃkalpaṃ kurvaṃtītyarthaḥ |*). "The wise" means the intelligent priests and the sacrificer: they join their minds in all the rites connected with the sacrifice. That is, they perform all the activities with a willing mind, so that the god Savitṛ may be pleased; this is the meaning.

विप्रस्य बृहतः विपश्चितः—मेधाविनः महतः स्तुत्यस्य ज्ञानवतो वा सवितुः अनुज्ञयेति । (*viprasya bṛhataḥ vipaścitaḥ—medhāvinaḥ mahataḥ stutyasya jñānavato vā savituḥ anujñayeti |*). This god Savitṛ is very intelligent, wise, one who knows the form of all rites, one who knows well the rites of the seven Hotṛs. All the rites that these seven Hotṛs and the other priests and sacrificers have to perform, this god Savitṛ alone can perform.
His power is extraordinary; therefore the sentence of the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa, सविता वै प्रसवानामिशा (*savitā vai prasavānāmiśā*) (Ai. Brā. 7-16), supports this.

In the Havirdhāna-pravartana, when the cart (रराट्यामवनद्धायां (*rarāṭyāmavanaddhāyāṃ*)) ⟨NOTE:119⟩ is bound, this Ṛk विश्वा रूपाणि (*viśvā rūpāṇi*) is the anuvacanīyā. The sūtra says: विश्वा रूपाणि प्रति मुंचते कविरिति व्यवस्तायां (*viśvā rūpāṇi prati muṃcate kaviriti vyavastāyāṃ*) (Ā. 4-9). The poet, the wise Savitṛ, binds on himself, that is, bears, all forms. Further, he has permitted what is good, auspicious, relating to going and the like. For whom? For the biped, man, and the quadruped, cattle, horses and the like. Further, Savitṛ, the god who impels all, being adorable, has made known the नाकं (*nākaṃ*); he makes it manifest. What? The नाकं (*nākaṃ*): in it there is no aka, no pain; hence it is heaven. The meaning is that he makes heaven manifest for the sacrificer. That god shines after the going forth of Uṣas, that is, her rising; for Uṣas rises before the rising of Savitṛ.
notes: number ೪ printed at the end of the Pada of the third Ṛk

en: - प्रति मुंचते (*prati muṃcate*)—he bears on himself
- द्विपदे (*dvipade*)—for men and others with two feet
- चतुष्पदे (*catuṣpade*)—for cattle and others with four feet
- वि अख्यत् (*vi akhyat*)—he made it shine
- प्रयाणं अनु (*prayāṇaṃ anu*)—following the path of her rising
- वि राजति (*vi rājati*)—he makes it shine

The wise Savitṛ bears all forms on himself. He has made welfare for men and others with two feet and for cattle and others with four feet. The most venerable Savitṛ has made heaven shine. Following the path of the rising of the goddess Uṣas, he makes it shine, and shines himself.

The wise Savitri comprehends all forms (in himself): he has engendered what is good for biped and quadruped : the adorable Savitri has illumed the heaven, and shines in sequence to the passage of the Dawn.

When the carts for bringing Soma, called Havirdhāna-pravartana, are brought, this Ṛk विश्वा रूपाणि (*viśvā rūpāṇi*) is to be recited as an anuvacanīyā Ṛk; this is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra ⟨NOTE:120⟩, विश्वारूपाणि प्रति मुंचते कविरिति व्यवस्तायां (*viśvārūpāṇi prati muṃcate kaviriti vyavastāyāṃ*) (Ā. 4-9).
notes: ಅಧ್ಯಾಸಿ ನ್ಯಾಗದಿನೇ: the machine-read words in Sāyaṇa's sentence are damaged; read here as "today, on this sacrificial day"
ಅಸಗತೇಷ್ವಾಗಃಸು: damaged in the machine-read text; sense uncertain

en: Other gods too, Agni and the rest, follow the going forth of the shining god Savitṛ; that is, they obtain greatness. For without the rising of Savitṛ the Agnihotra and other rites are not accomplished, and those gods would lack oblation, praise and the like. They become endowed with ओजसा (*ojasā*), with strength. Savitṛ, who by his own greatness has measured out the terrestrial realms, that is, the worlds beginning with the earth, that god, एतश (*etaśa*), that is, एतवर्णः (*etavarṇaḥ*), bright, shining, shines; "he shines" is the word to be supplied.
- प्रयाणं अनु (*prayāṇaṃ anu*)—following his very path of going
- अन्ये इत् देवाः (*anye it devāḥ*)—all the other gods also
- पार्थिवानि रजांसि (*pārthivāni rajāṃsi*)—the three worlds beginning with the earth

Following the very path of going of the divine Savitṛ, all the other gods also obtain greatness endowed with power. That same Savitṛ, the divine one, who by his majesty created and divided the three worlds beginning with the earth, shines of bright colour.

After the passage of which divine (being) the other deities proceed to (obtain) majesty with power ; he who by his greatness has measured out the terrestrial regions, the divine Savitri, (is) resplendent.

O god Savitṛ, you go to the three shining worlds, the worlds of heaven; this is said in तिस्रो दिवः पृथिवीः (*tisro divaḥ pṛthivīḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-53-5). Also you unite with the rays of Sūrya: Savitṛ is he who exists before sunrise, Sūrya is he who exists from rising to setting. Also you go around the night on both sides, on both flanks. Also, O god Savitṛ, by your acts of dharma, which uphold the world, you are Mitra, that is, you are the god called Mitra; or else, by granting light and the like, you are the friend of all the world.
- त्रीणि रोचना (*trīṇi rocanā*)—the three shining worlds
- धर्मभिः (*dharmabhiḥ*)—by acts that uphold the world

O god Savitṛ, you travel through the three shining worlds. You become one with the rays of the sun. You go around the night, encircling it on both sides. More than all this, by your acts that uphold the world you become Mitra in form.

Either you traverse, Savitri, the three regions, or combine with the rays of Surya ; or you pass, between the night on either hand ; or you divine Savitri, are Mitra, through your (benevolent) functions.
त्रीणि रोचनोत सूर्यस्य (*trīṇi rocanota sūryasya*)—The commentator has cited a Ṛk saying that the sun holds the three kinds of atmospheric worlds under his control:

त्रिरंतरिक्षं सविता महित्वना त्री रजांसि परिभूस्त्रीणि रोचना । तिस्रो दिवः पृथिवीस्तिस्त्र इन्वति त्रिभिव्रतैरभि नो रक्षति त्मना ॥ (*triraṃtarikṣaṃ savitā mahitvanā trī rajāṃsi paribhūstrīṇi rocanā | tisro divaḥ pṛthivīstistra invati tribhivratairabhi no rakṣati tmanā ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-53-5)

The idea suggested here is that Savitṛ holds under his control the three kinds of atmospheric worlds and the three kinds of earthly worlds, and protects them by his own impulse. These are: the worlds Vāyu, Vidyut, Varuṇa, or Agni, Vāyu, Āditya, which are the intermediate divisions of the atmospheric world. In the same way the three worlds Indra, Prajāpati and Satya are the intermediate divisions of the heavenly world; and likewise the earth (Bhū) world has three intermediate divisions, as the commentator has explained.

O Savitṛ, you alone have power over प्रसवस्य (*prasavasya*), the giving of leave for all rites. Of all who perform rites, worldly ones such as going and Vedic ones such as the Agnihotra, you alone are able to give leave. Also you are Pūṣan, the nourisher, O god, by your goings. Also you shine over this whole world, all that has come to be; you are able to uphold it. Since you are of such great power, O Savitṛ, the seer Śyāvāśva has made this praise for you; thus he speaks of himself in the third person.
- प्रसवस्य (*prasavasya*)—of all the beings that have come into being
- इदं विश्वं भुवनं (*idaṃ viśvaṃ bhuvanaṃ*)—this whole world

O Savitṛ, you alone are the lord of all beings that have come into being; by your acts of going you yourself are called the god Pūṣan. You are the sovereign of the whole world and rule over all. O god Savitṛ, the seer Śyāvāśva offers this praise addressed to you.
You alone rule over (the actions of) living beings : you are Pushan divine (Savitri), by your movements; you are sovereign over the whole world : Shyavashwa offers praise, Savitri, to you.

We, the singers, ask for that enjoyable wealth, well known as what is to be obtained. Whose? The wealth that belongs to the impelling god Savitṛ. Having obtained it, it is excellent, praiseworthy, सर्वधातमं (*sarvadhātamaṃ*), that is, giver of all enjoyments; तुरं (*turaṃ*), destroying foes, for with wealth enemies can be slain. Such wealth, by the favour of Bhaga, the adorable Savitṛ, we would hold, that is, enjoy. Or else: we ask for wealth, and, because of our desire, may we obtain it.
- भोजनं (*bhojanaṃ*)—and fit for enjoyment, the wealth (so as to obtain it)

We desire and pray to obtain the well-known wealth of the divine Savitṛ, fit for enjoyment. May we obtain the wealth of the venerable Bhaga, most excellent, exceedingly fit for enjoyment and destroying foes.
We solicit of the divine Savitri enjoyable (wealth) ; may we receive from Bhaga that which is excellent, all-sustaining, destructive of foes.

Of this Savitṛ, whose fame is exceedingly his own and uncommon, such a dear sovereignty, स्वराज्यं (*svarājyaṃ*), that is, shining by himself, lordship, dear to all, no one, no asuras and the like, impairs; they do not injure it.
- स्वयशस्तरं (*svayaśastaraṃ*)—that which is itself the cause of his uncommon fame
- प्रियं (*priyaṃ*)—and dear to the whole world
No adversary can injure the sovereignty and the wealth of Savitṛ, which is the cause of his uncommon fame by his own greatness and is dear to the whole world.
Nothing impairs the sovereignty of this Savitri, which is most especially renowned and beloved.

He, indeed, Savitṛ Bhaga, the adorable god, gives, that is, sends and bestows, jewels, delightful riches, on me, the giver of oblation. That god's share, the adorable one, the wonderful wealth, चायनीयं (*cāyanīyaṃ*), to be gathered, we ask for; we beg.
- स हि सविता (*sa hi savitā*)—that same god Savitṛ
- दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—to the sacrificer, the giver of oblation
- तं भागं (*taṃ bhāgaṃ*)—a share of that wealth (that praiseworthy wealth)
The adorable Savitṛ gives delightful riches to the sacrificer who is the giver of oblation. We desire and pray for that wealth, which is attractive and worthy of worship.
That savitri, who is Bhaga,bestows precious treasure on the donor
of the offering: we solicit (of him) a valuable portion.

Sāyaṇa states the ritual use: when an unpleasant dream has been seen, one should offer oblation with each Ṛk, with the fourth and the fifth Ṛk, as the Gṛhya-sūtra ordains: अद्या नो देव सवितरिति द्वाभ्यां (*adyā no deva savitariti dvābhyāṃ*) (Ā. Gṛ. Sū. 3-6-6). He then explains the verse. O god Savitṛ, to us, today, in this sacrificial day, send wealth, सौभगं (*saubhagaṃ*), that is endowed with offspring, sons and the like. Send far away the bad dream, दुःस्वप्नं (*duḥsvapnaṃ*), that is, poverty, which is painful like a bad dream. ⟨NOTE:122⟩
notes: ಆ. ೪ ೩: the hyphen is missing between the numbers in the printed text

en: - प्रजावत् (*prajāvat*)—endowed with sons and the like
- दुःस्वप्नं (*duḥsvapnaṃ*)—the troubles such as poverty, painful like a bad dream
O adorable god Savitṛ, provide us in this sacrifice with wealth endowed with sons and the like. Drive far away the troubles such as poverty, which are painful like a bad dream.
Grant us to-day, divine Savitri, affluence with progeny, and drive away evil dreams.

When a bad dream (a nightmare) has occurred, for the removal of its evil one should offer oblation of ghee in the fire with this Ṛk beginning अद्या नः (*adyā naḥ*) and with the next Ṛk beginning विश्वानि देव (*viśvāni deva*). This is set forth by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Gṛhya-sūtra, अद्या नो देव सवितरिति द्वाभ्यां (*adyā no deva savitariti dvābhyāṃ*) (Ā. Gṛ. Sū. 3-6-6).

O god Savitṛ, drive away all evils, दुरितानि (*duritāni*). Whatever is auspicious, भद्रं (*bhadraṃ*), such as offspring, cattle and house, that bring to us, आ सुव (*ā suva*), that is, send it towards us. For the scripture says that offspring is auspicious, cattle are auspicious, the house is auspicious: प्रजा पै भद्रं पशवो भद्रं गृहं भद्रमिति हि श्रुतिः ॥ (*prajā pai bhadraṃ paśavo bhadraṃ gṛhaṃ bhadramiti hi śrutiḥ ‖*) **GLOSS**
- परा सुव (*parā suva*)—drive far away and destroy
O adorable Savitṛ, drive far away and destroy all our sins and misfortunes. Provide us with whatever is auspicious for us.
Remove from us, divine Savitri, all misfortunes : bestow upon us

We, the performers, when Savitṛ the impelling god gives his sanction, may be free from offence, अनागसः (*anāgasaḥ*), that is, without fault, towards Aditi, the indivisible goddess, who is the Earth; for it is on the earth that sins arise. ⟨NOTE:123⟩ We hold, धीमहि (*dhīmahi*), that is, we bear, all desirable riches.
notes: ಸತಾಮನುಷ್ಠಾತ್ಯಾಣಾಂ: "of the performers", the word seems damaged

en: - आदितये (*āditaye*)—in regard to the goddess Aditi
- अनागसः (*anāgasaḥ*)—let us be free from sin
Being obedient to the command of the divine Savitṛ, may we be free from sin in regard to the goddess Aditi. May we obtain all the desired riches.
Let us be void of offence towards Aditi, according to the will of the divine Savitri: may we be possessed of all-desired (riches).

Sāyaṇa gives the ritual use in three places. In the Cāturmāsya sacrifice, at the Vaiśvadeva parvan, this Ṛk, beginning आ विश्वदेवं (*ā viśvadevaṃ*), is the anuvākyā for the oblation to Savitṛ on twelve potsherds; the sūtra says so (Ā. 2-16). In the Prāyaṇīya offering this same Ṛk is the anuvākyā to Savitṛ; the sūtra says so (Ā. 4 3). ⟨NOTE:124⟩ In the offering of the oblations called Devasū this same Ṛk is again the anuvākyā to Savitṛ; the sūtra says so (Ā. 4-11).

विश्वदेवं (*viśvadevaṃ*): he under whose control all the gods stand, such a one. He is all-pervading and the self of all; for the scripture says that they call him Indra, Mitra, Varuṇa, Agni, and so on, the others being his manifestations. सत्पतिं (*satpatiṃ*): the protector of the good, of those who perform the rites. सत्यसवं (*satyasavaṃ*): whose sanction is true. We today, on this sacrificial day, choose and serve the god Savitṛ with hymns, सूक्तैः (*sūktaiḥ*). ⟨NOTE:125⟩
notes: ಆ. ೪-೬ here, but the bhāṣya block cites ಆ. ೪-೩ for the same sūtra; ಸುತ್ರಾಮಾಣಂ here against ಸುತ್ರಮಾಣಂ there
ಸಾವಿತ್ರಿಪತಿ: the bhāṣya has ಸಾವಿತ್ರೀಷ್ಟಿಃ

en: - विश्वदेवं (*viśvadevaṃ*)—who is the inner controller in all the gods
- सत्यसवं (*satyasavaṃ*)—who has a regulation of the nature of truth
- अद्य (*adya*)—on this day of the sacrifice
- आ वृणीमहे (*ā vṛṇīmahe*)—we praise and worship

I praise and worship the god Savitṛ, who is the inner controller in all the gods, the protector of the good, and who has a regulation of the nature of truth, on this day of the sacrifice, with excellent praises.
We glorify to-day with hymns Savitri, the protector of the good,
the observer of truth, (identical with) all the gods.

In the sacrifice called Cāturmāsya, in the Vaiśvadeva parvan, in the oblation on twelve potsherds made with Savitṛ as the deity, this Ṛk beginning आ विश्वदेवं (*ā viśvadevaṃ*) is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra; this is set forth by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra आ विश्वदेवं सत्पतिं वाममद्य सवितः (*ā viśvadevaṃ satpatiṃ vāmamadya savitaḥ*) (Ā. 2-16). In the Prāyaṇīya offering also, in the oblation made with Savitṛ as the deity, this same Ṛk is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra; this is set forth by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra आ विश्वदेवं सत्पतिं य इमा विश्वा जातानि (*ā viśvadevaṃ satpatiṃ ya imā viśvā jātāni*) (Ā. 4-3). And in the oblations called Devasū, in the oblation made to Savitṛ as the deity, this Ṛk is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra; this is set forth by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra आ विश्वदेवं सत्पतिं न प्रमिये सवितुर्दैव्यस्य तत् (*ā viśvadevaṃ satpatiṃ na pramiye saviturdaivyasya tat*) (Ā. 4-11).

The god Savitṛ, who, being स्वाधीः (*svādhīḥ*), of good meditation or of good works, goes in front of these two, day and night, अप्रयुच्छन् (*aprayucchan*), that is, without negligence: him we choose. Thus the construction is completed.
- इमे उभे अहनी (*ime ubhe ahanī*)—of both these day and night
- स्वाधीः (*svādhīḥ*)—is the object of excellent meditation
The Savitṛ who moves about as a guide in front of both day and night, free from negligence and very careful, that same god is the object of excellent meditation.
The divine object of meditation, Savitri, who, ever vigilant, precedes

Sāyaṇa gives three ritual uses. In the Prāyaṇīya offering the Ṛk beginning य इमा विश्वा (*ya imā viśvā*) is the yājyā for Savitṛ; the sūtra says: य इमा विश्वा जातानि सुत्रमाणं पृथिवीं द्यामनेहसं (*ya imā viśvā jātāni sutramāṇaṃ pṛthivīṃ dyāmanehasaṃ*) (Ā. 4-3). In the Aśvamedha, after the horse has been let loose, a Sāvitrī offering is to be performed at each pressing; in it this Ṛk is the anuvākyā at the midday pressing; the sūtra says: य इमा विश्वा जातान्या देवो यातु सविता सुरत्नः (*ya imā viśvā jātānyā devo yātu savitā suratnaḥ*) (Ā. 10-6). Then the sense of the verse: the god who makes all these born beings, that is, creatures, meaning moving ones, hear श्लोकेन (*ślokena*), that is, by fame; the meaning is that all hear his praise. Or else, eager to give rain, he makes all these born beings hear by the sound of his thunder. And further, Savitṛ impels, sends forth; him we choose.
- प्र सुवाति (*pra suvāti*)—gives life to all living beings (such a god Savitṛ we worship)
The god Savitṛ who by his own greatness makes all living beings manifest, and who gives life to all living beings, such a god Savitṛ we worship.
Savitri, who proclaims his glory to all these living beings. and gives them life.

In the Prāyaṇīya offering, this Ṛk beginning य इमा विश्वा (*ya imā viśvā*) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra in the oblation made with Savitṛ as the deity; this is set forth by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra य इमा विश्वा जातानि सुत्रामाणं पृथिवीं द्यामनेहसं (*ya imā viśvā jātāni sutrāmāṇaṃ pṛthivīṃ dyāmanehasaṃ*) (Ā. 4-6). ⟨NOTE:126⟩ And in the Aśvamedha sacrifice, after the horse has been let loose to wander, the after-pressing offering called सावित्रिपति (*sāvitripati*) is to be performed. In that offering, at the time of the midday pressing, this Ṛk is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra; this is set forth by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra य इमा विश्वा जातान्या देवो यातु सविता सुरत्नः (*ya imā viśvā jātānyā devo yātu savitā suratnaḥ*) (Ā. 10-6). ⟨NOTE:127⟩
notes: abbreviations ಅ. ವೇ. and ಅ. ನೇ. printed (Atharvaveda?); ಶಿಖಿಲು/ಶಿಡಿಲು read as lightning
the third verse of Muir's rendering is numbered 1 in the print

en: O praiser, go to the mighty Parjanya and speak, that is, pray. Sāyaṇa notes that the word parjanya has been explained in many ways by Yāska: पर्जन्यस्तृपेराद्यंतविपरीतस्य तर्पयिता जन्यः परो जेता ना जनयिता वा प्रार्जयिता वा रसानां । (*parjanyastṛperādyaṃtaviparītasya tarpayitā janyaḥ paro jetā nā janayitā vā prārjayitā vā rasānāṃ |*) (Ni. 10-10). आभिः (*ābhiḥ*) means with these words of praise (continued below).

Praise him with these words of praise. With नमसा (*namasā*), that is, with food in the form of oblation, serve him on all sides. Parjanya, the bull, the one who rains the waters, जीरदानुः (*jīradānuḥ*), quick in giving, making the sound of thunder, कनिक्रदत् (*kanikradat*), places in the plants the germ, that is, the seed-like water standing in the place of an embryo: praise him.
- नमसा (*namasā*)—with food in the form of oblation
- जीरदानुः (*jīradānuḥ*)—who quickly gives what is desired; such Parjanya
- ओषधीषु (*oṣadhīṣu*)—in the plants (herbs and the like)
- गर्भं (*garbhaṃ*)—standing in the place of an embryo

O praiser, approach the mighty god Parjanya and pray. Praise him with these praises. Serve him fully with food in the form of oblation. Parjanya, who pours rain and quickly gives what is desired, making the sound of thunder places in the plants (herbs and the like) the water that stands in the place of an embryo.
Address the mighty Parjanya who is present : praise him with these hymns ; worship him with reverence, him who is the thunderer, the showerer, the bountiful. who impregnates the plants with rain.

Sāyaṇa says that this mantra is clearly explained in the Nirukta and writes down that same explanation here: पर्जन्यो विहंति वृक्षान्विहंति च रक्षांसि सर्वाणि चास्माद्भूतानि बिभ्यति महावधात् महान् ह्यस्य वधः। अप्यनपराधो भीतः पलायते वर्षकर्मवतो यत्पर्जन्यः स्तनयन्यंति दुष्कृतः पापकृतः । (*parjanyo vihaṃti vṛkṣānvihaṃti ca rakṣāṃsi sarvāṇi cāsmādbhūtāni bibhyati mahāvadhāt mahān hyasya vadhaḥ| apyanaparādho bhītaḥ palāyate varṣakarmavato yatparjanyaḥ stanayanyaṃti duṣkṛtaḥ pāpakṛtaḥ |*) (Ni. 10-11). Parjanya strikes down trees and strikes down demons; all beings fear him because of his great weapon, for great is his stroke; even the innocent man, afraid, runs away from the one who does the work of rain, when Parjanya, thundering, strikes the evil-doer, that is, the one who does sinful deeds.
- वृष्ट्यवतः (*vṛṣṭyavataḥ*)—by this Parjanya, the maker of rain

Parjanya throws down trees and destroys demons. With his great weapon he rebukes the whole world. When Parjanya, thundering, kills sinners, then even the innocent, frightened by this Parjanya, the maker of rain, run away.

He strikes down the trees, he destroys the Rakshasas, he terrifies the whole world by his mighty weapon : even the innocent man flies from the sender of rain, when Parjanya, thundering, slays the wicked.

For this mantra Yāska has given the explanation: विहंति वृक्षान् विहंति च रक्षांसि सर्वाणि चास्मद्भूतानि बिभ्यति महावधान्महान् ह्यस्य वधोऽप्यनपराधो भीतः पलायते वर्षकर्मवतः यत्पर्जन्यः स्तनयन् हंति दुष्कृतः पापकृतः ॥ (*vihaṃti vṛkṣān vihaṃti ca rakṣāṃsi sarvāṇi cāsmadbhūtāni bibhyati mahāvadhānmahān hyasya vadho 'pyanaparādho bhītaḥ palāyate varṣakarmavataḥ yatparjanyaḥ stanayan haṃti duṣkṛtaḥ pāpakṛtaḥ ‖*) (Ni. 10-11).

This god Parjanya strikes the trees and throws them down. And he also smites the demons. Seeing this kind of devastation (work of destruction) all beings are afraid. This work of slaying is very terrible. Even the innocent man, in great fear, seeing this terrible deed, runs away. The chief work of this Parjanya is indeed the pouring of rain. While pouring rain, appearing terrible with lightning and flashes and with a great roar, he strikes and kills those who do sinful deeds: this is the main purport. Here, because the thunderbolt strikes trees and beings and they are destroyed, this very matter is described here by the sentence that Parjanya strikes and kills the doers of sinful deeds.

Like the master of a chariot: as he, urging the horses with the whip, makes his messengers, that is, his warriors, manifest, so this Parjanya also, urging with the whip the clouds, which are his horses, makes manifest the rain-giving messengers, that is, the clouds that like messengers impel the rain, the Maruts. अह (*aha*) is an expletive. This being so, from afar rise the thundering sounds of the cloud, which overpowers or sounds by not raining and which is called the lion, the word सिंह (*siṃha*) being from a root meaning to be strong or to injure, a root of the action of sound. When? When Parjanya makes the sky, नभः (*nabhaḥ*), that is, the atmosphere, rain-bearing.
- रथीव (*rathīva*)—as a charioteer who drives the chariot strikes the horses with his whip and, bringing the warriors who are in the chariot, makes them visible to all, so (Parjanya also)
- दूतान् (*dūtān*)—those that are like messengers, the clouds
- सिंहस्य (*siṃhasya*)—of the clouds that sound like a lion

As a charioteer who drives the chariot strikes the horses with his whip and, bringing the warriors who are in the chariot, makes them visible to all, so Parjanya also, urging the clouds with his whips, makes visible to all the clouds that make rain and are like messengers. When Parjanya fills the atmosphere with rain, then the thundering sounds of the clouds that sound like a lion are heard from afar.
As a charioteer, urging his horses with his whip, brings into view
the messenger (of war), so Parjanya. (driving the clouds before him),
make manifest the messengers of the rain: the roaring of the lion (like
cloud) proclaims from afar that Parjanya overspreads the sky with

The fourth Ṛk, beginning प्रवाता (*pravātā*), is the yājyā in Parjanya's caru offering. The sūtra says: प्र वाता वांति पतयंति विद्युत् इत्यग्न्याधेयप्रकृति (*pra vātā vāṃti patayaṃti vidyut ityagnyādheyaprakṛti*) (Ā. 2-15). The winds blow forth for the sake of rain; the lightnings fly, that is, move about everywhere; the plants spring up, that is, rise and grow; the heaven, स्वः (*svaḥ*), the atmosphere, swells, that is, pours; Irā, the earth, becomes capable for the whole world, for the benefit of the whole universe. When is this so? When the god Parjanya protects the earth with seed, that is, with water; at that time it is so. ⟨NOTE:132⟩
notes: ಹೂ printed for ಷೂ of the verse

en: - उत् जिहते (*ut jihate*)—come forth and grow

When the god Parjanya makes the earth fruitful with water and protects it, then the winds blow strongly. The lightnings dart down from the atmosphere. The plants come forth. The atmosphere becomes liquid. The earth becomes a fit dwelling-place for the whole world.
The winds blow strong, the lightning flash, the plants spring up, the
the firmament dissolves : earth becomes (fit) for all creatures when Parjanya

The fourth Ṛk of this sūkta, beginning प्रवाता (*pravātā*), is to be recited as the yājyā mantra when a cooked offering (caru) is made to the deity Parjanya. This is made clear by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the sūtra प्र वाता वांति पतयंति विद्युत् इत्यग्नाधेयप्रकृति (*pra vātā vāṃti patayaṃti vidyut ityagnādheyaprakṛti*) (Ā. 2-15).

In the vrata, that is the action, of Parjanya the earth bows down exceedingly, that is, becomes lower than all. In his vrata the hoofed creatures such as cattle are nourished (or are filled, or move about). In his vrata, in his action, the plants take all forms, that is, many forms. O Parjanya, such a great one as you, grant us great happiness.
- व्रते (*vrate*)—by the power of the action
- व्रते (*vrate*)—by the greatness of the actions
- व्रते (*vrate*)—by the power of the action

O god Parjanya, by the power of whose action the earth is full of humility, by the greatness of whose actions hoofed animals and the like grow stout, by the power of whose action the plants grow in many forms, such a one as you, grant us happiness in abundance.
O Parjanya, through whose function the earth is bowed down :
through whose function hoofed cattle thrive ; through whose function plants
assume all kinds of forms, grant us great felicity.

O Maruts, you give us rain from the sky (the atmosphere). Cause the streams of water belonging to the rain-giving, pervading horse, that is, the cloud, to flow forth. O Parjanya, come toward us together with this thundering, roaring cloud. What are you doing? Pouring down water. That god, though he is the one who casts down the waters (the asura), is also our father, our protector.
- अश्वस्य (*aśvasya*)—and pervading cloud, belonging to it
- प्र पिन्नत (*pra pinnata*)—increase and pour down abundantly (O Parjanya)
- निषिंचन् (*niṣiṃcan*)—pouring down in the form of rain
- असुरः (*asuraḥ*)—you, the mighty one (the maker of rain)

O Maruts, pour down rain for us from the atmosphere. Increase the streams of water belonging to the rain-making, pervading cloud, and pour them down abundantly. O Parjanya, be pleased to come, pouring down water in the form of rain from this thundering cloud. You, the mighty one, as the maker of rain, are a protector to us.
Send down for us, Maruts, the rain from heaven : drops of the rainy
charger descend : come down Parjanya, sprinkling water by this thundering
(cloud) ; you who are the sender of rain, our protector.

Cry out toward the earth, make sound. The same is repeated for emphasis. Thunder, roar. Place the embryo, that is, the water that stands in the place of an embryo, in the plants. For that purpose go about on every side with a chariot filled with water. Draw down properly, for the sake of rain, the cloud, which is like a leather bag holding water, specially bound and turned with its mouth downward. Or else: draw it thus, with its binding loosened. When this is done, the elevated places and the low places (those whose feet are lowered or drawn down) become level, together in one state; the meaning is that they become filled with water.
- गर्भं (*garbhaṃ*)—the water in the form of an embryo
- आ धाः (*ā dhāḥ*)—place it in the plants and fill them
- दृतिं (*dṛtiṃ*)—the cloud, which is like a leather bag
- विषितं (*viṣitaṃ*)—having made it exceedingly well prepared
- सु कर्ष (*su karṣa*)—drive it for the sake of rain
- समाः (*samāḥ*)—in one and the same manner
- भवंतु (*bhavaṃtu*)—let them become filled with water

O Parjanya, make sound toward the earth. Thunder well, and place in the plants, which are the embryo-water of them, and fill them. Move about everywhere with a chariot filled with water. Make the cloud, which is like a leather bag, well prepared, and drive it with its mouth downward for the sake of rain. May the elevated places and the low places alike be filled with water.
Cry aloud over (the earth) ; thunder ; impregnate the plants ; traverse
(the sky) with your water-laden chariot, draw open the tight-fastened,
downward-turned water bag, and may the low places be made level.

O Parjanya, raise up the great, swollen sheath, that is, the cloud which stands in the place of a sheath, or cause it to rise. Having done so, pour down, make it flow downward. Let the channels, that is, the rivers, released, flow forward, toward the east; for the most part rivers flow eastward. With water (ghṛta) drench heaven and earth thoroughly, make them very wet. For the cows let there be water that is well fit for drinking in abundance.
- कोशं (*kośaṃ*)—the cloud, which is like a bag
- उदच (*udaca*)—lift it up and hold it

O Parjanya, lift up and hold the cloud, which is of great form and like a bag. Pour the water down. Let the rivers flow eastward without hindrance. Make heaven and earth wet with water. For the cows, let water fit for drinking overflow.

Raise on high the mighty sheath (of rain), pour down (its contents); let the rivers flow unimpeded to the east ; saturate with water both heaven and earth, and let there be abundant beverage for the cows.

O Parjanya, when you, sounding exceedingly loud and thundering, strike down the wicked (those who do evil) clouds, that is, tear them apart, then this whole world rejoices. The word "whole" is specified: whatever stands upon the earth, whatever is moving or unmoving, this whole world rejoices, is glad. That rain is the cause of the delight of the entire world is well known.
- कनिक्रदत् (*kanikradat*)—you make a sound in the form of roaring (and)
- यत्किंच (*yatkiṃca*)—whatever living beings there are (all of them rejoice)
O Parjanya, when you make a sound in the form of roaring, and thundering kill the wicked, then the whole world rejoices. All living beings that are upon the earth rejoice.
When, Parjanya, sounding loud and thundering, you destroy the wicked (clouds), this whole (world) rejoices, and all that is upon the earth.

This Ṛk is for the release from excessive rain. O Parjanya, you have rained; you have poured down rain. Hold back well the rain, taking it up; the meaning is, withhold it. You have made the waterless regions, the deserts, watery. For what purpose? In order to pass across them. You have brought forth the plants. For what purpose? For food, that is, for wealth or enjoyment. The word कं (*kaṃ*) is merely a filler of the verse-quarter, as in कमित्ययं शिशिरं जीवनाय कं (*kamityayaṃ śiśiraṃ jīvanāya kaṃ*) (Ni. 1-10). And also, from the creatures you have obtained praise (manīṣā), that is, adoration.
- अवर्षिः (*avarṣiḥ*)—you have poured down rain (O Parjanya)
- वर्षमुदु (*varṣamudu*)—the same rain that falls on without end ⟨NOTE:133⟩
- हू गृभाय (*hū gṛbhāya*)—hold back (so that it may not be excessive) ⟨NOTE:134⟩
- अत्तेतवा उ (*attetavā u*)—so as to be easy to cross
- अकः (*akaḥ*)—you have made them filled with water
- भोजनाय (*bhojanāya*)—so as to be fit for the enjoyment of men
- प्रजाभ्यः (*prajābhyaḥ*)—from men such as the priests
notes: ತ್ವಮಿತ್ಥೇತ್ಮಮಮುಶ್ರಾಂತರಿಕ್ಷೇ and ಪರ್ವಶಾನಾಂ in the bhāṣya are damaged; read as "in this manner" and "of the mountains"
ವಕ್ಷ್ಯತೇ and ಪ್ರತ್ಯಕ್ಷಾ ದೇವತಾಪಿ here differ from ವರ್ಣ್ಯತೇ and ಪ್ರತ್ಯಕ್ಷದೇವತಾಪಿ in the bhāṣya block

en: O Parjanya, you have poured down rain. Hold back that same rain, which falls on without end, so that it does not fall in a way that troubles us. You have made the waterless deserts full of water so that they may be easy to cross. You have produced the plants so that they may be fit for the enjoyment of men. You have also obtained praise from men such as the priests.

You have rained : now check well the rain : you have made the deserts capable of being crossed : you have given birth to plans for (man's) enjoyment : verily you have obtained laudation from the people.

Pṛthivī is of two forms: this one, which is visible, and also a deity; the one declared to be a deity of the middle region is the one addressed and described here. O Pṛthivī, extensive deity of the middle region, you truly bear the shattering, the splitting, of the mountains, or of the clouds. ⟨NOTE:135⟩. O great one, O one of exceeding eminence, or one with abundant flowing water, you who by your greatness, or by great water, delight the visible earth exceedingly.
notes: ಮತ್ತುಗಳಿಗೆ printed; probably the Maruts?

en: - पृथिवि (*pṛthivi*)—O deity of the middle region
O deity of the middle region, you bear the pieces of the clouds exceedingly. O goddess of excellent qualities and of greatness, by the same qualities you delight the earth exceedingly.
Verily you sustain here, Prithivi, the fracture of the mountains : mighty and most excellent. you are she who delights the earth by your greatness.

Concerning this sūkta the Bhāṣyakāra has said: द्विरूपा पृथिवी चैषा प्रत्यक्षा देवतापि च । मध्यस्थाना देवतोक्ता सात्र संबोध्य वक्ष्यते ॥ (*dvirūpā pṛthivī caiṣā pratyakṣā devatāpi ca | madhyasthānā devatoktā sātra saṃbodhya vakṣyate ‖*) ⟨NOTE:136⟩. That is to say, Pṛthivī is the deity of this sūkta. This Pṛthivī is of two kinds. One kind is the Pṛthivī or Bhūmi that is visible to our eyes. The deity who presides over this earth is well known as a deity of the middle region; this is the second kind. The intention is that it is this second kind, the deity of the middle region, that is addressed and praised in this sūkta.

Pṛthivī: the word पृथिवी (*pṛthivī*) or पृथ्वि (*pṛthvi*) is read among the twenty-one names of Pṛthivī (the earth) (Ni. 2-5) and among the sixteen names of the atmosphere (Ni. 2-10). And the word पृथ्वी (*pṛthvī*) (a word in the dual) is read among the names of heaven and earth (Ni. 3-22).

The form of the word Pṛthivī is derived from the root पृथु विस्तीर्णे (*pṛthu vistīrṇe*). Pṛthivī means a very wide region. This meaning applies to the earth, or Bhūmi, and also to the atmosphere (the sky). Since the atmosphere is wider than the earth, the word Pṛthivī is used in many places in the Ṛgveda to indicate the atmosphere. In the present sūkta it is the middle deity, who dwells in the atmosphere, who is praised. Yāska has given an explanation of this Ṛk: सत्यं त्वं पर्वतातां मेघानां खेदनं भेदनं बलममुत्र धारयसि पृथिवि प्रजिन्वसि या भूमिं प्रणवति महत्त्वेन महतीत्युदकवतीति वा ॥ (*satyaṃ tvaṃ parvatātāṃ meghānāṃ khedanaṃ bhedanaṃ balamamutra dhārayasi pṛthivi prajinvasi yā bhūmiṃ praṇavati mahattvena mahatītyudakavatīti vā ‖*) (Ni. 11-37).

O deity of the middle region, you in truth, staying in the atmosphere, strike or pierce the clouds and display your strength in the atmosphere. O goddess of great form (of vast shape), being of the form of water or bearing water, you make the earth moist by your extraordinary greatness and delight it. This is the main intention.
notes: ಅರಮ printed; Aryaman?

en: O Pṛthivī, goddess who move in various ways, the worshippers praise you with their moving hymns. Further, you who cast the filling cloud, which is neighing, that is, roaring, like a horse excited, O bright-coloured one, or O one who goes about, hurl it down.
- विचारिणि (*vicāriṇi*)—O goddess who move in many ways
- वाजं न (*vājaṃ na*)—as one makes a horse fall downward

O goddess of the middle region, of bright colour and of manifold movement, as one makes a roaring horse fall downward, you make the cloud, full of water and filled with the sound of thunder, fall downward; the praisers glorify and worship you, so, with their own hymns.
Wanderer in various ways your worshipers hymn you with (sacred)
songs ; you who, bright-hued, toss the swollen (cloud) like a neighing horse.

This Ṛk is the yājyā for Pṛthivī in the offerings to the gods. The same Ṛk is the opening Ṛk of the sūkta in the Bhūmi-stoma, in the Niṣkevalya śastra; the sūtra was quoted earlier. O Pṛthivī, you who hold the trees by strength together with the firm earth; or, taking दृढ (*dṛḍha*) as a predicative adjective, you hold the trees, making them firm. When the showers belonging to you, that is, the rain-giving clouds, rain from the shining cloud (the genitive being used in the sense of the ablative), from the one that carries off the waters, from the atmosphere or from the sun; or else, when the showers, the masses of water of your cloud, fall from the shining sky.

O goddess of the middle region, when from your cloud the streams of rain pour down from the shining atmosphere, then you, the well-known one, by your strength together with the firm earth make the trees stand firm.
You who, with solid earth, sustain by your strength the forest lords, when the showers of your cloud fall from the shining sky.

It is said in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra that when an oblation is offered to the gods, this Ṛk दृळ्हा चित् (*dṛḷhā cit*) is to be used as the yājyā mantra in the offering to the deity Pṛthivī, and that at the time of reciting the stoma in praise of the earth it is to be recited at the beginning of the sūkta among the mantras of the Niṣkevalya śastra. That detail has been given earlier.

At the end of this sūkta there is a supplementary mantra to be recited: वर्षंतु ते विभावरि दिवो अभ्रस्य विद्युतः । रोहंतु सर्वबीजान्यव ब्रह्मद्विषो जहि ॥ (*varṣaṃtu te vibhāvari divo abhrasya vidyutaḥ | rohaṃtu sarvabījānyava brahmadviṣo jahi ‖*). O shining deity of the middle region, by your favour may the clouds in the atmosphere, together with thunder and lightning, pour down rain. May all the seeds on the earth, refreshed by that rain, sprout and grow as seedlings. O goddess, destroy the haters of the brahman: this is the prayer stated here.

Atri addresses himself: "O Atri, offer a prayer to Varuṇa." Varuṇa is the sovereign, that is, the lord who shines well; renowned, that is, heard of everywhere; the warder-off of calamity, or, in the other sense, the one who covers people, this being the meaning of his name. The prayer to be offered is a great, that is, abundant, profound, that is, hard to fathom and rich in meanings, dear, that is, pleasing, act of praise in the form of a hymn; "offer" means "pray" or "utter aloud". This is the Varuṇa who, as the slaughterer who cuts up the animal spreads out a hide as a spread, has spread out the earth, that is, the broad firmament. On the strength of the śruti that speaks of "the third earth", the word for earth can also denote the firmament. For the sun's spreading he has stretched it out. What is spread out becomes fit for use, so he spread out the firmament for use. This is stated in the verse उरुं हि राजा वरुणश्चकार (*uruṃ hi rājā varuṇaścakāra*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-24-8). ⟨NOTE:145⟩ ⟨NOTE:146⟩
notes: ಅತ್ತ ನೀಚೀನಬಾರಂ ವರುಣಃ ಕವಂಧಂ । ನಿ. ೧೦-೪ ।: ಅತ್ತ unclear in the supplied text; ಕವಂಧ here, ಕಬಂಧ in the verse
ತನಿಷೀಯಂತೋ printed in the bhāṣya; the verse has ತವಿಷೀಯಂತಃ

en: - शमिता (*śamitā*)—the śamitṛ, who cuts up animals
- चर्म इव (*carma iva*)—as one spreads out a hide
- वि जघान (*vi jaghāna*)—has spread out and extended

O Atri, to the god Varuṇa, who shines as a sovereign and is renowned, and who has spread out and extended the firmament for the sun's movement, as the slaughterer who cuts up animals spreads out a hide, recite and offer a hymn of praise that is abundant, endowed with exceedingly profound meanings, and pleasing.
Offer a solemn, profound, and acceptable prayer to the imperial and renowned Varuna, who has spread the firmament as a bed for the sun, as the immolator (spreads) the skin of the victim.

शमिता चर्म इव (*śamitā carma iva*)—as the slaughterer who cuts up animals spreads out the hide of the animal. In a sacrifice, the one who kills the animal and cuts it up is called the slaughterer (śamitṛ). After an animal has been killed in the sacrifice,

the slaughterer spreads out that animal's hide wide in the sun, in order that it may dry. Putting this spreading wide as the simile, the text describes Varuṇa's unequalled power: he spread out the firmament wide, so that it became vast, for the sun's movement. In support of this the Ṛk उरुं हि राजा वरुणश्चकार सूर्याय पंथामन्वेतवा उ॥ (*uruṃ hi rājā varuṇaścakāra sūryāya paṃthāmanvetavā u‖*) is cited. (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-24-8)

This Varuṇa has spread out the firmament over the tops of the trees (the woods). The Vājasaneyaka text has: वनेषु हीदमेषु वृक्षाग्रेष्ट्यंतरिक्षं विततं तस्मादाह वनेषु व्यंतरिक्षं ततानेति । (*vaneṣu hīdameṣu vṛkṣāgreṣṭyaṃtarikṣaṃ vitataṃ tasmādāha vaneṣu vyaṃtarikṣaṃ tatāneti |*) **GLOSS** Strength he has spread in the horses; milk, that is, the liquid, in the cows. The word for cow here is a name of the cow, and a derivation of it is given. In the hearts he has spread the resolve, that is, the purpose of action; for what one meditates on in the mind, one does in act. In the waters he has placed fire, that is, the lightning fire or the submarine fire. "Has spread out" is to be connected with all of these. Moreover, in heaven, the world of the sky, he has set the sun, and on the mountain he has placed Soma.
- वनेषु (*vaneṣu*)—in the upper parts of trees

In the upper parts of the well-known trees he has spread out the firmament, in horses strength, in cows milk, and in hearts the resolve that prompts action. In the waters he has placed fire, in the heaven the sun, and on the mountain Soma.

He has extended the firmament over the tops of the trees, has given strength to horses, milk to cows, determination to the heart : he has placed fire in the waters, the sun in heaven, the Soma-plant in the mountain.

वनेषु वि अंतरिक्षं ततान (*vaneṣu vi aṃtarikṣaṃ tatāna*)—he made the firmament spread out over the tops of the trees. That is, to the people on the earth the firmament appears to rest on the tops of the trees. It is described as his having made it spread out. And the one who has set strength in the horses, milk in the cows, resolve in the mind, fire in the water, the sun in the firmament, and the Soma plants in the mountain region is Varuṇa himself. Therefore it is described that Varuṇa's power is exceedingly great.

Varuṇa has made the cloud, whose opening is turned downward, pour forth. What is it? It is the कवंधं (*kavaṃdhaṃ*): water is called kavana, and that in which it is held is the cloud; he made it so. Or else the water itself is meant: he made that water have a downward outlet; that is, splitting the cloud, he made the water face downward. For whom? It is said: for the heaven-and-earth and the firmament, that is, for the welfare of the three worlds. By that water Varuṇa, the lord of the whole world, that is, of all that has come to be, wets the earth, that is, drenches it. As the rain, the sprinkling male, spreads barley everywhere for its sprouting, so he wets the earth everywhere. Or else the rain is Varuṇa himself, that is, the rainer, Parjanya; on this view the word "man" is to be supplied: as a man (sows) barley. The Nirukta (Ni. 10-4) and the like are to be seen. ⟨NOTE:147⟩
notes: ಪೃಥಿವೀಂ in the verse; the bhāṣya explains it as ಅಂತರಿಕ್ಷಂ "firmament"

en: - अंतरिक्षं (*aṃtarikṣaṃ*)—and for the sake of the firmament
- यवं न (*yavaṃ na*)—as it drenches barley grain
- विश्वस्य भुवनस्य (*viśvasya bhuvanasya*)—of the whole world

Varuṇa, for the sake of heaven-and-earth and of the firmament, made the cloud pour out water downward. As the rain thoroughly drenches barley grain, so Varuṇa, the lord of the whole world, drenches the earth with this same water.

Varuna has set free the (water of the) downward opening cloud for the (benefit of the) heaven, the earth, and the firmament; thence is ne monarch of all the world, watering the soil as the rain bedews the barley.

Yāska has given an explanation of this Ṛk: नीचीनद्वारं वरुणः कबंधं मेघं । कवनमुदकं भवति तदस्मिन् धीयते उदकमपि कबंधमुच्यते बंधिरनिभृतत्वे कमनिभृतं च प्रसृजति द्यावा पृथिव्यौ चांतरिक्षं च महत्वेन तेन सर्वस्य भुवनस्य राजा यवनिव वृष्टिर्व्युनत्ति भूमिं ॥ (*nīcīnadvāraṃ varuṇaḥ kabaṃdhaṃ meghaṃ | kavanamudakaṃ bhavati tadasmin dhīyate udakamapi kabaṃdhamucyate baṃdhiranibhṛtatve kamanibhṛtaṃ ca prasṛjati dyāvā pṛthivyau cāṃtarikṣaṃ ca mahatvena tena sarvasya bhuvanasya rājā yavaniva vṛṣṭirvyunatti bhūmiṃ ‖*) (Ni. 10 4)

नीचीनबारं (*nīcīnabāraṃ*) means नीचीनद्वारं (*nīcīnadvāraṃ*), facing downward; since the cloud, being in the lofty firmament, pours rain upon the earth below, it is described that the mouth or door of the cloud faces downward. कवन (*kavana*) means water; the place in which such water is bound and kept is called कबंध (*kabaṃdha*), that is, the cloud. Or कबंध (*kabaṃdha*) may also be understood to mean water. For the state in which water, whose nature is to spread out or flow away, is bound and made to remain in one place is called water or cloud. Varuṇa makes a door in the lower part of such a cloud and makes its waters fall downward upon the earth. Besides, that same Varuṇa creates (builds) heaven-and-earth and the firmament. That lord of all the worlds, by his own great majesty, drenches the earth with waters, as water soaks the seedlings of barley. This is the main idea.

Varuṇa wets the earth, that is, the broad firmament; that the firmament too can be denoted by the word for earth has been stated before. And he wets also heaven, the world of the sky. When he desires the milked, that is, the fullness of water, or else when "milked" means the water, and by it its product, plants and the like, is indicated; when he desires that the plants and the like may grow, then immediately after that, the mountains, that is, the rocky heights that have ridges, cover themselves with the cloud. Moreover, the Maruts, the heroes, desiring strength, ⟨NOTE:148⟩, and specially the impellers of the rain, loosen the clouds.
notes: ವರುಣಾದಿರೂಪಾವಸಾ ನಾತ್: damaged in the supplied text

en: - दुग्धं (*dugdhaṃ*)—to milk the cloud (to pour out rain)
- तविषीयंतः (*taviṣīyaṃtaḥ*)—who have gained zeal through strength

As soon as Varuṇa desires to pour out rain, he drenches the earth, the firmament and the heaven with water. At that very moment the mountains cover their peaks with clouds. The Maruts, who have gained zeal through strength, make the clouds move.

Varuna waters earth, mid-air, and heaven, when he pleases (to send forth) the milk (of the cloud): thereupon the mountains clothe (their summits) with the rain-cloud, and the hero, (Maruts), exulting in their strength, compel (the clouds) to relax.

The word for "of the asuras" means one related to the asuras; the relation between the asuras and him is that of the slain and the slayer; that is, he is the slayer of the asuras. Or else the asura is the cloud, because it gives life; then it means one related to it. "Of the renowned" means of the famed. "This great", that is, mighty, device, that is, wisdom, I proclaim, that is, I declare. What is this device? It is said: the Varuṇa who, standing in the firmament, measures out the earth, that is, the firmament, by the sun, as if with a measuring rod, that is, a staff, has this device. ⟨NOTE:149⟩
notes: ಅಸ್ಯತ್ತೋ ವಿನಾಶಯ printed; ಅಸ್ಮತ್ತೋ?

en: - मानेनेव (*māneneva*)—as if with a measuring rod
- प्र वोचं (*pra vocaṃ*)—I praise and recite

I praise and recite the great supernatural power of Varuṇa, the slayer of the asuras and the renowned, who, standing in the firmament, measures out the firmament by the sun as if with a measuring rod.
I proclaim this great device ef the renowned Varuna, the destroyer of the Asuras, who abiding in the mid-heaven, has meted the firmament by the sun, as if by a measure.

Of Varuṇa, the one of surpassing wisdom, the god, that is, the shining or the praiseworthy, this universally known great device, that is, wisdom, no one ever assails; no one at all harms it. The two particles are mere fillers. The reason is this: the rivers, bright and swift-flowing, pouring water, that is, many rivers always filling it with water, do not fill even the one ocean. This is Varuṇa's great work. It must not be said that the work extending from the spreading out of the firmament to the non-filling of the ocean befits the Supreme Lord alone and not Varuṇa, since he has the form of Varuṇa and the rest ⟨NOTE:150⟩; for there is the śruti एष ब्रह्मेत्यादि श्रुतेः (*eṣa brahmetyādi śruteḥ*) **GLOSS**
notes: ಯಥಾ ಯದ್ರಿರಿಪುರ್ಲೋಕಯಂತಿ ಪಾಪಮಾರೋಪಯಂತಿ: the supplied text is hard to construe; read as above

en: - यत् (*yat*)—by the greatness of which Varuṇa
- कवितमस्य (*kavitamasya*)—who has the most excellent wisdom

That the ocean has such a depth that many rivers, though they come flowing full of floods, cannot fill it, is Varuṇa's greatness itself. No one at all can resist the famous and great wisdom of Varuṇa, who has such most excellent wisdom and is resplendent.
No one has counteracted the divice of the most sagacious divinity, whereby the lucid water-shedding rivers do not fill the ocean with water.

"O Varuṇa", whether to अर्यम्यं (*aryamyaṃ*), that is, to Aryaman himself, the giver; or else, because he guides and reflects, one who instructs: Aryaman, the teacher; to him; or to मित्र्यं (*mitryaṃ*), the friend, that is, one who is attached to us in affection; or to the companion, that is, one of the same fame; or to the brother, always; constantly to the neighbour, that is, one who dwells in a house close by; or to अरणं (*araṇaṃ*), that is, one without speech; or else to अरणं (*araṇaṃ*), one who does not give, continually. Whatever offence we have committed against any of these, loosen that, destroy it from us. ⟨NOTE:151⟩
notes: ಎಂಭತ್ತನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು "the eightieth sūkta" printed; the sūkta before it is 85

en: - अरम्यं (*aramyaṃ*)—whether against one who has done us a service
- वेशं वा (*veśaṃ vā*)—or against one who lives next door
- अरणं वा (*araṇaṃ vā*)—or against a mute person

O Varuṇa, whether it be against one who has done us a service, or against our friend, companion, brother or a mute person, whatever kind of injury we may have done, destroy all those sinful acts, and so deal that that sin may not cling to us, and forgive us.
If, Varuna, we have ever committed on offence against a benefactor, a friend, a companion, a brother, a near neighbour, or Varuna, a dumb man, remove it from us.

कितवासः (*kitavāsaḥ*) are gamblers; "what have you? all has been won by me", so says one, hence the gambler. "Not in play", that is, in gaming, in the shining; as in play they make a charge and impute sin, so haters of us accuse thus: "you did this sin against me". Here the word for "not" stands in front, as a particle of comparison. ⟨NOTE:152⟩ Or else the particle घ (*gha*) is a filler. The sin which we have committed truly, without any false imputation; and also the sin committed which we do not know: all those, like loosened, that is, slack-bound fruits, release. And, O god, thereafter may we be dear to you.
notes: abbreviation ಅನು. printed

en: - देव (*deva*)—O Varuṇa who are of divine nature
- यत् रिरिपुः (*yat riripuḥ*)—whatever deceitful act we have committed (deliberately)
- न विद्य (*na vidya*)—we have done without knowing
- सर्वा ता (*sarvā tā*)—all those sins also
- शिथिरेव (*śithireva*)—as fruits become loose from the branch and fall down

O Varuṇa, who are of divine nature, as gamblers in dice and the like deliberately commit deceitful acts, so if we have committed deceitful acts, or if through our ignorance we have committed any sinful act, put all that sin far from us, as a fruit loosened from the branch of a tree falls down; only thereafter shall we be dear to you. And grant that it may be so.

If, like gamblers, who cheat at play, (we commit offences) knowingly, or (those) of which we know not, divine Varuna, extricate us from them all, as if from loosened (bonds), so that we may be dear, Varuna, to you.
notes: abbreviation ಛಂ. ಅನು. printed

en: O Indra and Agni, you two who are never parted from each other: the mortal whom you protect in the battles, that mortal breaks even the firm, shining possessions that belong to the enemy. He breaks them as the seer Trita breaks the words of an opponent, that is, like the statements of the opponent. Or else, Agni, who is present in the three places, breaks them like the words of the enemies.
- वाणीरिव (*vāṇīriva*)—as he breaks the words of the opposing side
- दृळ्हा चित् (*dṛḷhā cit*)—even though very strong

O Indra and Agni, the man (the sacrificer) whom you both together protect breaks and scatters in the battles the wealth of the enemies, even though it is guarded very firmly, as Trita breaks the words of the opposing side.
Indra and Agni, the mortal whom you both protect scatters the the substantial treasures (of his enemies), as Trita (confutes) the words (of his opponents).

Indra and Agni, who are hard to overcome in the armies, that is, not to be overpowered; who in the battles, or in the matter of food, are praiseworthy, that is, to be praised; who protect the five peoples, the peoples being men (the word "protect" is to be supplied): those two, of great majesty, we invoke, that is, we praise.
- पंच चर्षणीः (*paṃca carṣaṇīḥ*)—the five peoples beginning with men

O Indra and Agni, you who are unassailable among the enemy armies, who are praised in the battles, and who wholly protect the five peoples beginning with men, such venerable ones, you we praise and invoke.
We invoke the two, Indra and Agni, who are irresistible in conflicts, who are renowned in battles, who protect the five (classes of) men.

The strength, the power, of those two alone is overpowering. Of those two bountiful ones, who possess food or wealth, the lightning, that is, the thunderbolt, is sharp in their hands. Such gods set out, for the gain of the cows, that is, of the waters, carried off by the Paṇis ⟨NOTE:156⟩, in a single swift chariot made of wood, ⟨NOTE:157⟩, for the killing of Vṛtra, the cloud that obstructs, or of the asura Vṛtra of that kind.
notes: ಧೃತಂ printed in the bhāṣya; the verse has ಘೃತಂ
ಏವಯಾಮರುದುಕ್ಕೋ in the Anuvāda against ಏವಯಾಮರುದುಕ್ತೋ in the bhāṣya

en: - तयोः इत् (*tayoḥ it*)—of these very Indra and Agni
- द्रुणा (*druṇā*)—seated in a single swiftly running chariot

The strength of the famous Indra and Agni is that which restrains enemies. The shining thunderbolt of these two wealthy ones shines sharply in their arms. Such great ones set out, for the gain of cows and also for the destruction of Vṛtra, seated in a single swiftly running chariot.
Overpowering is the might of these two: the bright (lightning) is shining in the hands of Maghavan, as they go together in one chariot for the (recovery of the) cows, and the destruction of Vritra.

O gods, those two, of the qualities to be told, we invoke, that is, we praise. For what purpose? For the sending forth of the chariots in the battle. What are you like? Indra and Agni, who are a pair joined with each other; lords of the moving kind of wealth, which has riches and the like as its mark; knowing, that is, all-knowing; to be served most of all with words of praise. Such are you whom we invoke.
- गिर्वणस्तमा (*girvaṇastamā*)—who are worthy of the choicest praises
O Indra and Agni, who are lords of all the moving wealth, all-knowing, and worthy of the choicest praises, you we pray and praise to send your chariots forth for battle.
We invoke you both, Indra and Agni, for (sending) your chariots to the combat, lords of moveable wealth. all-knowing, most deserving of praise.

Those two grow day by day; that is, they are always increased. As an illustration of the growth: as two mortals, that is, two men, grow day by day. The two gods are shining and not to be injured, and worthy of worship, that is, to be honoured exceedingly; the particle चिदिति (*ciditi*) is used in the sense of worship. Such great gods I place in front, that is, I honour first, for the gain of a horse. As for the comparison अंशेव (*aṃśeva*): Aṃśa is a god within the twelve Ādityas, and he stands also for Bhaga. Like two Aṃśas, that is, like two Ādityas, which means blazing.
- अर्वते (*arvate*)—for the gain of a horse
- पुरः दधे (*puraḥ dadhe*)—we honour and worship
O Indra and Agni, who prosper every day like men, who are resplendent and unharmed, and who are resplendent and venerable like the Ādityas, you we honour and worship for the gain of horses.
I adore you, irresistible deities, for (the sake of obtaining) horses : you who are increasing day by day like mortals, who are worthy of worship, like two Adityas.

"Thus", that is, in the manner in which it is now being done, with praise. By Indra and Agni the oblation was given up, that is, offered. What kind of oblation? Strength-giving. Like what? Like the Soma juice, pressed and purified with the stones, that is, the pressing-stones, as if it were ghṛta ⟨NOTE:158⟩. As it is given to you both

"So too" the cooked offering (caru), the cake (puroḍāśa) and the rest. Those two gods, Indra and Agni, are asked to bestow on us, the wise ones who praise them, abundant food or fame, and wealth: "may you hold" (दिधृतं (*didhṛtaṃ*)), that is, "may you bear it". Food too, for those who praise: "may you hold". The repetition is for the sake of respect.
notes: ಕಸ್ಮೈ ವಸ್ತುಭ್ಯಂ ॥ ವಚನವ್ಯತ್ಯಯಃ — reading doubtful

en: - इंद्राग्निभ्यां (*iṃdrāgnibhyāṃ*)—addressed to Indra and Agni together

An oblation, powerful like the Soma juice pressed out by the stones that crush and press the Soma plants, has been offered addressed to Indra and Agni together. May those same gods fill up abundant food and wealth in us, who are wise and who praise them. May they fill up food for those who praise them.

The invigorating oblation has been offered, like the Soma-juice expressed by the sounding stones : bestow food upon the pious; great riches upon those who praise you: bestow food also upon those who praise you.

"Let them go forth" (प्र यंतु (*pra yaṃtu*)): let the praises (मतयः (*matayaḥ*)), born in speech (गिरिजा (*girijā*)), go forth. To whom? The text reads वस्तुभ्यं (*vastubhyaṃ*), and he notes a change of number. ⟨NOTE:160⟩. To Viṣṇu, that is, the all-pervading Indra; to him who is accompanied by the Maruts.

Of whom are the praises? It is said: of the seer named Evayāmarut; the genitive ending is dropped. Or else, this seer is the producer of the speech-born praises; in the second half there is praise of the Maruts. Moreover, let the praises go forth to strength (शर्धाय (*śardhāya*)), that is, to the strength of the Maruts; the other words are all epithets of strength. प्रयज्यवे (*prayajyave*): to the one to be worshipped most excellently. सुखादये (*sukhādaye*): with beautiful ornaments; खादि (*khādi*) is a special ornament. As the Śruti says: "On their hands are khādis" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-168-3) ⟨NOTE:161⟩, and "on their feet khādis" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-54-11). तवसे (*tavase*): to the powerful. भंददिष्टये (*bhaṃdadiṣṭaye*): he whose desired offering is praise; to him. ध्रुनिव्रताय (*dhrunivratāya*): to such a one whose work is to set the clouds in motion. शवसे (*śavase*): to the swift-going.

O Jātavedas, Agni, of known wisdom, you are asked to call to me Śrī who is of this kind. Hiraṇyavarṇā: she whose colour (radiance) is like that of gold. Hariṇī: she of green-golden colour, or she who has taken the form of a doe; the Purāṇa is cited for this: Śrī, having taken the form of a doe, wandered in the forest. Suvarṇarajatasrajām: she who has a garland of golden and silver flowers; the flowers of gold are golden and those of silver are silver, and from the word for a garland it is understood that they are flowers, by their resemblance to flowers; or else, she who has a chain made from gold and silver, whose colour is good being gold and silver, a chain of flowers or a chain made of those. Candrā: shining like the moon, or abiding in that form. Hiraṇmayī: of the nature of gold, or having a body of gold. Lakṣmī: possessed of auspicious marks, citing the Nirukta: Lakṣmī from lakṣaṇa (mark). Śrī of this form, for me, for my sake, bring, call. Agni is the carrier of oblations of the gods; the calling of her follows from that, so it depends on him. This is the sense.
notes: reading unclear
ವೃದ್ಧಶ್ರವಸಃ printed; pada-pāṭha has ವೃದ್ಧಶವಸಃ

en: - एवया मरुत् (*evayā marut*)—of the seer Evayāmarut
- मरुत्वते (*marutvate*)—who is accompanied by the Maruts
- प्र यंतु (*pra yaṃtu*)—let them be offered with fullness
- प्र यज्यवे (*pra yajyave*)—the most worthy of worship
- भंददिष्टये (*bhaṃdadiṣṭaye*)—who has a sacrifice in the form of praise
- शर्धाय (*śardhāya*)—addressed to the host of the Maruts
- प्र (*pra*) (यंतु (*yaṃtu*))—let them go forth and reach
- हिरण्यर्णां (*hiraṇyarṇāṃ*)—she who is resplendent with a bodily radiance as exceedingly brilliant as gold
- हरिणीं (*hariṇīṃ*)—she who has a fair (green-golden) coloured body, or who has taken the form of a doe

- सुवर्णरजतस्रजां (*suvarṇarajatasrajāṃ*)—she who wears a garland made of flowers fashioned of gold and of flowers fashioned of silver, or of yellow flowers of the colour of gold and white flowers of the colour of silver, made of
- चंद्रां (*caṃdrāṃ*)—she who shines like the moon
- हिरण्मयीं (*hiraṇmayīṃ*)—she who has a body of gold
- लक्ष्मीं (*lakṣmīṃ*)—she who is endowed with auspicious marks, the deity called the goddess Śrī
- हिरण्यावर्णां (*hiraṇyāvarṇāṃ*)—she who is distinguished by a radiance like gold
- हरिणीं (*hariṇīṃ*)—she who shines with a bodily radiance of a fair colour
- सुवर्णरजतस्रजां (*suvarṇarajatasrajāṃ*)—she who wears a garland strung of flowers made of gold and silver
- चंद्रां (*caṃdrāṃ*)—she who gives delight to all people
- हिरण्ययीं (*hiraṇyayīṃ*)—she who has the nature of gold, and
- लक्ष्मीं (*lakṣmīṃ*)—the goddess Śrī, famed by the name Lakṣmī

O Indra, may the praises of the seer Evayāmarut, made of speech, be offered with fullness to you, who are great, accompanied by the Maruts, all-pervading; and may these praises go forth and reach the host of the Maruts, which is most worthy of worship, has excellent ornaments, is powerful, has a sacrifice in the form of praise, makes the clouds move, and is swift-moving.

O Agni, who knowest all, bring within me the deity called the goddess Śrī: she who shines with a bodily radiance like gold; who is of a fair colour, or has taken the form of a doe; who wears a garland of flowers made of gold and silver; who has a radiance as delightful as the moon; who has a body of gold; and who is endowed with all auspicious marks.

O Agni, send, or bring, to me the goddess Śrī who is famed by the name Lakṣmī: she who is distinguished by a radiance like gold; who shines with the bodily radiance of a fair colour; who wears a garland strung of flowers made of precious things such as gold and silver; who gives delight (joy) to all people; and who has a body of gold.

May the voice-born praises of Evayamarut reach you, Vishnu, attended by the Maruths : (may they reach) the strong, the adorable, the brilliantly-adorned, the vigorous, praise-loving, cloud-scattering, quick-moving company of the Maruts.
हिरण्यवर्णां हरिणीं सुवर्णरजतस्रजां । चंद्रां हिरण्मयीं लक्ष्मीं जातवेदो म आ वह ॥ १ ॥ (*hiraṇyavarṇāṃ hariṇīṃ suvarṇarajatasrajāṃ | caṃdrāṃ hiraṇmayīṃ lakṣmīṃ jātavedo ma ā vaha ‖ 1 ‖*)

हरिणीं—हरितवर्णां हरिणीरूपधरां वा । श्रीर्धृत्वा हरिणीरूपमरण्ये संचचार ह । (*hariṇīṃ—haritavarṇāṃ hariṇīrūpadharāṃ vā | śrīrdhṛtvā hariṇīrūpamaraṇye saṃcacāra ha |*). Two kinds of meaning have been given for the word हरिणीं (*hariṇīṃ*). हरिद्वर्ण (*haridvarṇa*) means one who is of a fair colour like turmeric. Or else, what is said in the Purāṇas and elsewhere, that the goddess Śrī roamed about having taken the form of a doe, has been cited.

सुवर्णरजतस्रजां (*suvarṇarajatasrajāṃ*)—Two kinds of meaning have been given for this word also. One who wears a garland made of flowers wrought, delightful to the eye, of gold and silver; or one who wears a divine garland strung of flowers of the colour of gold, that is, yellow flowers, and white flowers white like silver. Thus two kinds of explanation have been made.

लक्ष्मीं—लक्षणवतीं (*lakṣmīṃ—lakṣaṇavatīṃ*). "One endowed with auspicious marks" is the explanation of the bhāṣya-writer. With regard to the word लक्ष्मी (*lakṣmī*), Yāska, when giving the etymology for the Ṛk beginning सक्तुमिवतिताउना (*saktumivatitāunā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-71-2), says:

लक्ष्मीर्लाभाद्वा लक्षणाद्दा (लप्स्यनाद्दा) लांछनाद्दा लषतेर्वास्यात् प्रेप्साकर्मणो लग्यतेर्वा स्यादाश्लेषकर्मणो लज्जतेर्वा स्यादश्लाघाकर्मणः ॥ (*lakṣmīrlābhādvā lakṣaṇāddā (lapsyanāddā) lāṃchanāddā laṣatervāsyāt prepsākarmaṇo lagyatervā syādāśleṣakarmaṇo lajjatervā syādaślāghākarmaṇaḥ ‖*) (Ni. 4-9)

Thus he has stated the etymology. That is, the word लक्ष्मी (*lakṣmī*) is derived from words that denote these meanings: लाभाद्वा (*lābhādvā*)—attaining, obtaining; लक्षणाद्वा (*lakṣaṇādvā*)—designating; लप्स्यनात् (*lapsyanāt*)—having a desire to attain; लांछनाद्दा (*lāṃchanāddā*)—making a mark or sign. Or else it may be derived from the root लषति (*laṣati*) with the sense "desire", or from the root लग्यति (*lagyati*) with the sense "cling, hold on", or from the root लज्जति (*lajjati*) with the sense "do not praise". Thus he has explained both the meaning of this word and the derivation of its form.
चंद्रां (*caṃdrāṃ*)... The word चंद्र (*caṃdra*) is stated among the names of gold (Ni. 6-10). And for the word चंद्र (*caṃdra*):

चंद्रश्चंदतेः कांतिकर्मणः । चंदनमित्पप्यस्य भवति । चारु द्रमति चिरं द्रमति चमेर्वा पूर्वं ॥ चारु रुचेर्विपरीतस्य ॥ (*caṃdraścaṃdateḥ kāṃtikarmaṇaḥ | caṃdanamitpapyasya bhavati | cāru dramati ciraṃ dramati camervā pūrvaṃ ‖ cāru rucerviparītasya ‖*) (Ni. 11-5)

That is, the word चंद्र (*caṃdra*), derived from the root चंद् (*caṃd*) having the sense "to shine", has the meaning "shining". The word चंदन (*caṃdana*) (fragrance) is also derived from this same root. चारु—रुचेर्विपरीतस्य (*cāru—rucerviparītasya*) means: by transposing the places of the letters ra and ca in the word रुचि (*ruci*) it becomes चारु (*cāru*), and the sense "shining with exceeding radiance" is just what is set forth in the present Ṛk.

In this Ṛk, Agni is addressed and the prayer is made that the goddess Śrī be brought. For Agni is the होतृ (*hotṛ*) (the one who calls) who brings all the gods. Many scriptural sentences such as अग्ने देवानिहा वह (*agne devānihā vaha*) support the point that Agni is the messenger who brings the gods to the sacrificial ground.

हे जातवेदः अग्ने । हिरण्यवर्णां स्वर्णकांतिं हरिणीं हरितवर्णां हरिद्राभां सुवर्णरजतस्रजां हेमराप्यमयकमलमालां चंद्रां सकलजनाह्लादकारिणीं हिरण्मयीं हिरण्यस्वरूपामेतादृशीं लक्ष्मीं मे मम सर्वाभीष्टसाधनाय आवह प्रेषय ॥ (*he jātavedaḥ agne | hiraṇyavarṇāṃ svarṇakāṃtiṃ hariṇīṃ haritavarṇāṃ haridrābhāṃ suvarṇarajatasrajāṃ hemarāpyamayakamalamālāṃ caṃdrāṃ sakalajanāhlādakāriṇīṃ hiraṇmayīṃ hiraṇyasvarūpāmetādṛśīṃ lakṣmīṃ me mama sarvābhīṣṭasādhanāya āvaha preṣaya ‖*)
In the work called Śrīkaṇṭha-bhāṣya it is said thus:

ओं हिरण्यवर्णामिति सूक्तेनाग्निं प्रार्थयेत् । अग्निस्तुष्टो यजमानाय श्रियं प्रयच्छति । अग्निस्तु रुद्र एव । “रुद्रो वा एषोऽग्निः” इति श्रुतेः । रुद्रो हि पुरुषः । “पुरुषो वै रुद्रः” इति श्रुतेः । तस्य पत्नि भगवत्युमृव लक्ष्मीः । “श्रीश्च ते लक्ष्मीश्च पत्न्यौ” इति पुरुषसूक्तोक्तेः । पुरुषो महादेवः शिवः । वेदाहमेतं पुरुषं महांतमिति तत्रैवोक्तेः । तथा च अग्निस्वरूपिणः परमेश्वरस्योपासनेन तच्छक्तिविभूतेर्महालक्ष्म्याः प्राप्तिर्भविव्यतीति सिद्धं । “धनार्थिभिरग्निरुपास्य ऐश्वर्यार्थिभिरीश्वर” इत्यादि स्मर्यते । आरोग्यं भास्करादिच्छेच्छ्ययमिच्छेद्दुताशनात् । ऐश्वर्यमीश्वरादिच्छेन्नोक्षमिच्छेज्जनार्दनात् ॥ (*oṃ hiraṇyavarṇāmiti sūktenāgniṃ prārthayet | agnistuṣṭo yajamānāya śriyaṃ prayacchati | agnistu rudra eva | “rudro vā eṣo 'gniḥ” iti śruteḥ | rudro hi puruṣaḥ | “puruṣo vai rudraḥ” iti śruteḥ | tasya patni bhagavatyumṛva lakṣmīḥ | “śrīśca te lakṣmīśca patnyau” iti puruṣasūktokteḥ | puruṣo mahādevaḥ śivaḥ | vedāhametaṃ puruṣaṃ mahāṃtamiti tatraivokteḥ | tathā ca agnisvarūpiṇaḥ parameśvarasyopāsanena tacchaktivibhūtermahālakṣmyāḥ prāptirbhavivyatīti siddhaṃ | “dhanārthibhiragnirupāsya aiśvaryārthibhirīśvara” ityādi smaryate | ārogyaṃ bhāskarādicchecchyayamiccheddutāśanāt | aiśvaryamīśvarādicchennokṣamicchejjanārdanāt ‖*)

इति । सूक्ते ऋचः पंचदश । हिरण्यवर्णामिति प्रथमा ऋक् । अस्या अर्थः— हिरण्यवर्णां हिरण्यवर्णरूपां — ज्ञानमात्मनि भा सूर्ये चंद्रे ज्योत्स्ना च खे ध्वनिः । वर्णो हिरण्ये पयसि धृतं त्वमसि मातृके ॥ (*iti | sūkte ṛcaḥ paṃcadaśa | hiraṇyavarṇāmiti prathamā ṛk | asyā arthaḥ— hiraṇyavarṇāṃ hiraṇyavarṇarūpāṃ — jñānamātmani bhā sūrye caṃdre jyotsnā ca khe dhvaniḥ | varṇo hiraṇye payasi dhṛtaṃ tvamasi mātṛke ‖*)

इति श्रीस्तुतावगस्तोक्तेः । हिरण्यवर्णां मणिनूपुरांघ्रिं प्रसन्नवक्रां शुकपद्महस्तां । विशालनेत्रीं प्रणमामि गौरीं वचोविदं वाचमुदीरयंतीं ॥ इति जैमिन्युक्तेः । हिरण्यवर्णसदृग्वर्णां वा । “तप्तस्वर्णसवर्णाभामिति” श्री पुराहाच्च । (*iti śrīstutāvagastokteḥ | hiraṇyavarṇāṃ maṇinūpurāṃghriṃ prasannavakrāṃ śukapadmahastāṃ | viśālanetrīṃ praṇamāmi gaurīṃ vacovidaṃ vācamudīrayaṃtīṃ ‖ iti jaiminyukteḥ | hiraṇyavarṇasadṛgvarṇāṃ vā | “taptasvarṇasavarṇābhāmiti” śrī purāhācca |*)

हरिणीं हरिणीरूपां— यज्ञोग्निर्मृगरूपेण धावति स्म पुराध्वरे । रुद्रस्ता कृष्य तच्छक्तिं मृगीं जग्राह वैष्णवीं ॥ इति वैवर्तदक्षाध्वराध्यायोक्तेः । (*hariṇīṃ hariṇīrūpāṃ— yajñognirmṛgarūpeṇa dhāvati sma purādhvare | rudrastā kṛṣya tacchaktiṃ mṛgīṃ jagrāha vaiṣṇavīṃ ‖ iti vaivartadakṣādhvarādhyāyokteḥ |*)

अथ वा हरिणीं हरिद्राभां हरिद्राचूर्णलिप्तश्वाद्वा । “हरिणीं पूजयेद्दुर्गा० हरिद्राचूर्णनिर्मितां” इति हरिद्रागौरीव्रतकल्पोक्तेः । सुवर्णरजतस्रजां सुवर्णमय्यः रजतमय्यश्च स्रजः हाराः यस्यांस्तां । चंद्रां चदि आह्लादने दीप्त्वा च रकिचंद्रामिति टाबंतरूपं आह्लादिकां प्रकाशिकां च । ज्ञानानंतस्वरूपिणीमिति यावत् । चंद्रे विद्यमाना चांद्री चंद्रिका चंद्रेति विवक्ष्यते । “पूर्णमास्यां चंद्रबिंबे ध्यात्वा श्रीललितांबिकामिति ” हय- (*atha vā hariṇīṃ haridrābhāṃ haridrācūrṇaliptaśvādvā | “hariṇīṃ pūjayeddurgā0 haridrācūrṇanirmitāṃ” iti haridrāgaurīvratakalpokteḥ | suvarṇarajatasrajāṃ suvarṇamayyaḥ rajatamayyaśca srajaḥ hārāḥ yasyāṃstāṃ | caṃdrāṃ cadi āhlādane dīptvā ca rakicaṃdrāmiti ṭābaṃtarūpaṃ āhlādikāṃ prakāśikāṃ ca | jñānānaṃtasvarūpiṇīmiti yāvat | caṃdre vidyamānā cāṃdrī caṃdrikā caṃdreti vivakṣyate | “pūrṇamāsyāṃ caṃdrabiṃbe dhyātvā śrīlalitāṃbikāmiti ” haya-*)

ग्रीवोक्तेः । हिरण्मयीं विकारार्थे मयट् हिरण्यात्मना विकृतां । “तत्सुवर्णमभवत् ” इति श्रुतेः । पवित्रमयीं ना—“पवित्रं वै हिरण्यं” इति श्रुतेः । मूलप्रकृतिर्जगतः परिणाम्युपादानत्वेन सैव हिरण्यरूपेण परिणतेति भावः ॥ (*grīvokteḥ | hiraṇmayīṃ vikārārthe mayaṭ hiraṇyātmanā vikṛtāṃ | “tatsuvarṇamabhavat ” iti śruteḥ | pavitramayīṃ nā—“pavitraṃ vai hiraṇyaṃ” iti śruteḥ | mūlaprakṛtirjagataḥ pariṇāmyupādānatvena saiva hiraṇyarūpeṇa pariṇateti bhāvaḥ ‖*)
हिरण्यरेतसः शंभोः शक्तिः प्रोक्ता हिरण्मया । धनार्थिभिरुपास्यैषा जातवेदसि सर्वदा ॥ (*hiraṇyaretasaḥ śaṃbhoḥ śaktiḥ proktā hiraṇmayā | dhanārthibhirupāsyaiṣā jātavedasi sarvadā ‖*)

इति कालिकापुराणवचनात् । प्राचुर्यार्थे मयट् । हिरण्मयां हिरण्यप्रचुरां । प्राचुर्यं च स्वसमानाधिकरणस्वजातीयाल्पत्वरूपं स्वव्यधिकरणविजातीयाल्पत्वरूपं वा । तेन च धनाधिकां भाग्यसमृद्धां वित्तपूर्णामिति भावः । (*iti kālikāpurāṇavacanāt | prācuryārthe mayaṭ | hiraṇmayāṃ hiraṇyapracurāṃ | prācuryaṃ ca svasamānādhikaraṇasvajātīyālpatvarūpaṃ svavyadhikaraṇavijātīyālpatvarūpaṃ vā | tena ca dhanādhikāṃ bhāgyasamṛddhāṃ vittapūrṇāmiti bhāvaḥ |*)
