लक्ष्मीं शोभासंपत्तिपद्मारूपां । “शोभा संपत्तिपद्मासु लक्ष्मीः श्रीरपि कथ्यते” इति कोशात् । (*lakṣmīṃ śobhāsaṃpattipadmārūpāṃ | “śobhā saṃpattipadmāsu lakṣmīḥ śrīrapi kathyate” iti kośāt |*)

यद्वा लक्षणवतीं— ललिता शारदा लक्ष्मीरेकैव भगवत्युमा । तत्तल्लक्षणसंयुक्ता पुरुषार्थप्रदा नृणां ॥ इति देवीपुराणोक्तेः । तादृशीं श्रियं मे मह्यमावह आकारयेति जातवेदसमग्निं प्रार्थयेत् ॥ (*yadvā lakṣaṇavatīṃ— lalitā śāradā lakṣmīrekaiva bhagavatyumā | tattallakṣaṇasaṃyuktā puruṣārthapradā nṛṇāṃ ‖ iti devīpurāṇokteḥ | tādṛśīṃ śriyaṃ me mahyamāvaha ākārayeti jātavedasamagniṃ prārthayet ‖*)

By this sūkta beginning हिरण्यवर्णां (*hiraṇyavarṇāṃ*) Agni is to be prayed to. Agni, pleased by the praise of the sacrificer, gives him prosperity (aiśvarya). Who is this Agni? He is Rudra himself. There is the Śruti sentence रुद्रो वा एषोऽग्निः (*rudro vā eṣo 'gniḥ*). And many Śruti sentences such as रुद्रो हि पुरुषः । पुरुषो वै रुद्रः (*rudro hi puruṣaḥ | puruṣo vai rudraḥ*) support the point that the Puruṣa is Rudra. The consort of that Rudra, the goddess Umā herself, is Lakṣmī. ह्रीश्च (श्रीश्च) ते लक्ष्मीश्च पत्न्यौ (*hrīśca (śrīśca) te lakṣmīśca patnyau*)—"the goddess Śrī and Lakṣmī are thy two consorts"—so it is said in the Puruṣa-sūkta (Yajurveda). Here Puruṣa means Mahādeva, Śiva. The Śruti sentence वेदाहमेतं पुरुषं महांतं (*vedāhametaṃ puruṣaṃ mahāṃtaṃ*) also supports this. And it is well known that by the worship of Parameśvara, who has the form of Agni, the grace of Mahālakṣmī, the special power (śakti) of that Īśvara, comes to be. धनार्थिभिरुग्निरुपास्य ऐश्वर्यार्थिभिरीश्वरः (*dhanārthibhirugnirupāsya aiśvaryārthibhirīśvaraḥ*)—those who seek wealth should worship Agni, and those who seek prosperity (aiśvarya) should worship Īśvara: there is a Smṛti sentence to this effect also.

A discerning person desires the gain of health by the grace of the Sun, wealth (riches) by the grace of Agni, prosperity (aiśvarya) by the grace of Īśvara, and the human goal called liberation by the grace of Viṣṇu: so a saying of the noble also runs.

In this Śrī-sūkta there are fifteen Ṛks. Among them हिरण्यवर्णां (*hiraṇyavarṇāṃ*) is the first Ṛk. Its meaning is as follows. हिरण्यवर्णां (*hiraṇyavarṇāṃ*) means one who has a bodily radiance glittering like gold. In the Śrī-stuti composed by Agastya it is said:
ज्ञानमात्मनि.भा सूर्ये चंद्रे ज्योत्स्ना च खे ध्वनिः । वर्णो हिरण्ये पयसि धृतं त्वमसि मातृके ॥ (*jñānamātmani.bhā sūrye caṃdre jyotsnā ca khe dhvaniḥ | varṇo hiraṇye payasi dhṛtaṃ tvamasi mātṛke ‖*)

That is, certain qualities abide in certain things as their essence and by nature. Thus: knowledge in the self, radiance in the sun, moonlight in the moon, sound in space, the excellent colour in gold, and ghee (clarified butter) in milk. Just as these are excellent qualities, so, O Mother, thou art the most excellent among the deities: this is the sense suggested here. Therefore this verse has been cited in order to say that the colour of hiraṇya (gold) is exceedingly excellent.
The sage Jaimini also, when praising Gaurī, used this very epithet हिरण्यवर्णां (*hiraṇyavarṇāṃ*):

हिरण्यवर्णां मणिनूपुरांघ्रिं प्रसन्नवक्रां शुकपद्महस्तां । विशालनेत्रीं प्रणमामि गौरीं वचोविदं वाचमुदीरयंतीं ॥ (*hiraṇyavarṇāṃ maṇinūpurāṃghriṃ prasannavakrāṃ śukapadmahastāṃ | viśālanetrīṃ praṇamāmi gaurīṃ vacovidaṃ vācamudīrayaṃtīṃ ‖*)

In this verse, for the word हिरण्यवर्णां (*hiraṇyavarṇāṃ*), हिरण्यवर्णसदृग्वर्णां वा तप्तस्वर्णसवर्णा भामिति श्रीपुराणाच्च (*hiraṇyavarṇasadṛgvarṇāṃ vā taptasvarṇasavarṇā bhāmiti śrīpurāṇācca*): the meaning is one who has a bodily radiance with such a brilliance as gold free of any puṭa shines with. ⟨NOTE:168⟩
हरिणीं—हरिणीरूपां (*hariṇīṃ—hariṇīrūpāṃ*): one who has taken the form of a doe. In this matter:
यज्ञोऽग्निर्मृगरूपेण धावति स्म पुराध्वरे । रुद्रस्त्वा कृष्य तच्छक्तिं मृगीं जग्राह वैष्णवीं ॥ (*yajño 'gnirmṛgarūpeṇa dhāvati sma purādhvare | rudrastvā kṛṣya tacchaktiṃ mṛgīṃ jagrāha vaiṣṇavīṃ ‖*)

—so it is said in the work called Dakṣādhvara. That is, at one time Agni, of the form of sacrifice, took the form of a deer and went running away. Rudra, seeing it, used his power and seized that doe which has the form of sacrifice (since it is said यज्ञो वै विष्णुः (*yajño vai viṣṇuḥ*), the word वैष्णवीं (*vaiṣṇavīṃ*) means "of the form of sacrifice"): this is the intent. Therefore the deity Śrī is here praised as one who has taken the form of a doe. Besides:
as is said in the Haridrā-gaurī-vrata-kalpa, one whose body is smeared with, or made of, turmeric powder; and therefore it may be understood also as one who is of a fair colour.
सुवर्णरजतस्रजां (*suvarṇarajatasrajāṃ*)—one who wears a garland made of things such as gold and silver.

चंद्रां (*caṃdrāṃ*)—चदि आह्लादने दिप्तौ च (*cadi āhlādane diptau ca*): one who shines with a delightful radiance; or it may also be said, one whose nature is knowledge and infinity. And the radiance that is in the moon bears the names चांद्री चंद्रिका चंद्रा (*cāṃdrī caṃdrikā caṃdrā*).
पूर्णमास्यां चंद्रबिंबे ध्यात्वा श्री ललितांबिकां (*pūrṇamāsyāṃ caṃdrabiṃbe dhyātvā śrī lalitāṃbikāṃ*)

According to this statement, since it is said that on the full-moon day one should meditate on the goddess Śrī Lalitā in the shining disc of the full moon, the epithet चंद्रं (*caṃdraṃ*) is employed here.

हिरण्मयां (*hiraṇmayāṃ*)—one who has a body of gold. तत्सुवर्णग्ं हिरण्यमभवत् (*tatsuvarṇagṃ hiraṇyamabhavat*) । तत्सुवर्णस्य हिरण्यस्य जन्म (*tatsuvarṇasya hiraṇyasya janma*) । य एवग्ं सुवर्णस्य जन्मवेद (*ya evagṃ suvarṇasya janmaveda*) । सुवर्ण आत्मना भवति (*suvarṇa ātmanā bhavati*) । And scriptural sentences such as पवित्रं वै हिरण्यं (*pavitraṃ vai hiraṇyaṃ*) set forth the excellence of hiraṇya, or gold.
हिरण्यरेतसः शंभोः शक्तिः प्रोक्ता हिरण्मया । धनार्थिभिरुपास्यैषा जातवेदसि सर्वदा ॥ (*hiraṇyaretasaḥ śaṃbhoḥ śaktiḥ proktā hiraṇmayā | dhanārthibhirupāsyaiṣā jātavedasi sarvadā ‖*)

This is a statement of the Kalikā-purāṇa. ⟨NOTE:169⟩ That is, the power of Īśvara of great glory, whose seed has the form of gold, bears the name हिरण्मया (*hiraṇmayā*). This deity always abides in Agni. Those who seek wealth should worship this goddess: so it is said.
लक्ष्मीं (*lakṣmīṃ*)—the sense is the goddess Śrī who is in the form of radiance, wealth and the lotus. In this matter there is a statement of the lexicon:
शोभासंपत्तिपद्मासु लक्ष्मी श्रीरपि कथ्यते (*śobhāsaṃpattipadmāsu lakṣmī śrīrapi kathyate*)
For the word लक्ष्मीः (*lakṣmīḥ*) it is customary to describe these things, शोभा (*śobhā*)—radiance, संपत्ति (*saṃpatti*)—prosperity, पद्म (*padma*)—the lotus, as the form of Lakṣmī. Besides:
ललिता शारदा लक्ष्मीरेकैव भगवत्युमा । तत्तल्लक्षणसंयुक्ता पुरुषार्थप्रदा नृणां ॥ (*lalitā śāradā lakṣmīrekaiva bhagavatyumā | tattallakṣaṇasaṃyuktā puruṣārthapradā nṛṇāṃ ‖*)

So there is a statement of the Devī-purāṇa. That is, although the names ललिता (*lalitā*), शारदा (*śāradā*), लक्ष्मीः (*lakṣmīḥ*), भगवती (*bhagavatī*) and उमा (*umā*) appear to be different, all of them designate one and the same deity. That deity, endowed in accordance with her name with the respective marks, bestows on the devotees who worship her the human goals that they desire: so it is said. Therefore the meaning of the word लक्ष्मी (*lakṣmī*), "one who is endowed with the respective marks", has been set forth. Agni is prayed to bring near me, for the fulfilment of my wishes, the goddess Śrī who is distinguished by such qualities.
In the work called Śatānanda-vṛtti it is said thus:

ओं हिरण्यवर्णेत्यस्य पंचदशर्चस्य सूक्तस्य । जातवेदा अग्निर्दुर्गामहालक्ष्मीर्देवता । श्रीं बीजं । ह्रीं शक्तिः । क्लीं कीलकं । लक्ष्मीप्रसादसिध्यर्थे जपे विनियोगः । श्रीमित्यादिषडंगन्यासः । ध्यानं ॥ (*oṃ hiraṇyavarṇetyasya paṃcadaśarcasya sūktasya | jātavedā agnirdurgāmahālakṣmīrdevatā | śrīṃ bījaṃ | hrīṃ śaktiḥ | klīṃ kīlakaṃ | lakṣmīprasādasidhyarthe jape viniyogaḥ | śrīmityādiṣaḍaṃganyāsaḥ | dhyānaṃ ‖*)

या सा पद्मासनस्था विपुलकटितटीपद्मपत्रायताक्षी गंभीरावर्तनाभिस्तनभरनमिता शुभ्रवस्त्रोत्तरीया । लक्ष्मीर्दिव्यैर्गजेंद्रॆर्मणिगणखचितैः स्थापिता हेमकुंभैर्नित्यं सा पद्महस्ता मम वसतुगृहे सर्वमांगल्ययुक्ता ॥ (*yā sā padmāsanasthā vipulakaṭitaṭīpadmapatrāyatākṣī gaṃbhīrāvartanābhistanabharanamitā śubhravastrottarīyā | lakṣmīrdivyairgajeṃdrèrmaṇigaṇakhacitaiḥ sthāpitā hemakuṃbhairnityaṃ sā padmahastā mama vasatugṛhe sarvamāṃgalyayuktā ‖*)

हिरण्यवर्णामिति ऋक् प्राथमिकी । हिरण्यं विष्णुराख्यातस्तस्य वर्णस्तु वैष्णवी । लक्ष्मीर्हिरण्यवर्णेति श्रूयते कनकप्रभा ॥ इति श्रीपुराणात् ॥ (*hiraṇyavarṇāmiti ṛk prāthamikī | hiraṇyaṃ viṣṇurākhyātastasya varṇastu vaiṣṇavī | lakṣmīrhiraṇyavarṇeti śrūyate kanakaprabhā ‖ iti śrīpurāṇāt ‖*)

हरिणीं— हरिणीं तु हरेः पत्नीं दारिद्रपरिहारिणीं । प्रपद्येऽहं हरिद्राभां हरिणाक्षीं हिरण्मयीां ॥ इति आथवर्णिकस्तुत् ॥ (*hariṇīṃ— hariṇīṃ tu hareḥ patnīṃ dāridraparihāriṇīṃ | prapadye 'haṃ haridrābhāṃ hariṇākṣīṃ hiraṇmayīāṃ ‖ iti āthavarṇikastut ‖*)

सुवर्णरजतस्रजां— पिशंगधवळाभिश्च स्रग्भिरम्लानमूर्तिभिः । सौवर्णैः कमलैर्नित्यं राजतैः श्रीर्विभूषिता ॥ इति महालक्ष्मिकोशे । (*suvarṇarajatasrajāṃ— piśaṃgadhavaḷābhiśca sragbhiramlānamūrtibhiḥ | sauvarṇaiḥ kamalairnityaṃ rājataiḥ śrīrvibhūṣitā ‖ iti mahālakṣmikośe |*)

चंद्रां चंद्रवत् प्रकाशमानां— “चंद्रां चंद्रनिभास्यां चपलां चंद्रस्य सोदरीं कलये” । इति सुधोद्धरणे ॥ (*caṃdrāṃ caṃdravat prakāśamānāṃ— “caṃdrāṃ caṃdranibhāsyāṃ capalāṃ caṃdrasya sodarīṃ kalaye” | iti sudhoddharaṇe ‖*)

हिरण्मयां हिरण्यरूपेणाभिव्यक्तां । हिंकारो वज्रः रमग्निः तन्मयां तत्कांतिप्रचुरां । दंभोल्यात्मक दिव्यतेजःपुंजमंजुलां रिपुनिग्राहिकां पापघ्नीमिति वा । लक्ष्मीं लक्ष्मवतीं— (*hiraṇmayāṃ hiraṇyarūpeṇābhivyaktāṃ | hiṃkāro vajraḥ ramagniḥ tanmayāṃ tatkāṃtipracurāṃ | daṃbholyātmaka divyatejaḥpuṃjamaṃjulāṃ ripunigrāhikāṃ pāpaghnīmiti vā | lakṣmīṃ lakṣmavatīṃ—*)

ज्ञानैश्वर्यसुखारोग्यधनधान्य जयादिकं । लक्ष्म यस्यास्समुद्दिष्टं सा लक्ष्मीति निगद्यते ॥ इति निरुक्तसारोक्तेः । (*jñānaiśvaryasukhārogyadhanadhānya jayādikaṃ | lakṣma yasyāssamuddiṣṭaṃ sā lakṣmīti nigadyate ‖ iti niruktasārokteḥ |*)

हे जातवेदः शास्त्रयोने भो भगवन् त्वदीयां लक्ष्मीं मे मह्यं आवह आकर्षयेति यज्ञपुरुषं प्रार्थयेत् । “तेन नारायणः प्रीतो लक्ष्मीं भक्ताय दास्यतीति तत्रैवोक्तेः ॥ (*he jātavedaḥ śāstrayone bho bhagavan tvadīyāṃ lakṣmīṃ me mahyaṃ āvaha ākarṣayeti yajñapuruṣaṃ prārthayet | “tena nārāyaṇaḥ prīto lakṣmīṃ bhaktāya dāsyatīti tatraivokteḥ ‖*)

The seers of this Śrī-sūkta beginning with हिरण्यवर्णां (*hiraṇyavarṇāṃ*) are Ānandakardama and the others mentioned before; the deities are Jātavedas Agni, Durgā and Mahālakṣmī; श्रीं (*śrīṃ*) is the seed (bīja), ह्रीं (*hrīṃ*) is the power (śakti), क्लीं (*klīṃ*) is the pin (kīlaka). For the attainment of the grace of Śrī Lakṣmī the recitation (japa) of this sūkta is to be performed; the nyāsa of the limbs and the rest have been stated before. For meditation this verse is to be recited:

या सा पद्मासनस्था विपुलकटितटी पद्मपत्रायताक्षी गंभीरावर्तनाभिस्तनभरनमिता शुभ्रवस्त्रोत्तरीया । लक्ष्मिर्दिव्यैर्गजेंद्रॆर्मणिगणखचितैः स्नापिता हेमकुंभैर्नित्यं सा पद्महस्ता मम वसतु गृहे सर्वमांगल्ययुक्ता । (*yā sā padmāsanasthā vipulakaṭitaṭī padmapatrāyatākṣī gaṃbhīrāvartanābhistanabharanamitā śubhravastrottarīyā | lakṣmirdivyairgajeṃdrèrmaṇigaṇakhacitaiḥ snāpitā hemakuṃbhairnityaṃ sā padmahastā mama vasatu gṛhe sarvamāṃgalyayuktā |*)

The goddess Śrī, who bears the name Lakṣmī, is seated on a lotus seat. This goddess shines with broad hips, with wide eyes like lotus petals, and with a deep navel region. Her body is bent as if by the weight of her breasts, and she wears a pure white garment. Anointed with the waters of golden pots set with many jewels and splendid with choice elephants, holding a lotus flower in her hands, shining with all auspicious ornaments and the like, may this goddess Śrī, the bestower of all good fortune, dwell always in one's own house: this is the main intent.

This mantra beginning with हिरण्यवर्णां (*hiraṇyavarṇāṃ*) is the first Ṛk of this sūkta. In accordance with the verse हिरण्यं विष्णुराख्यातस्तस्य वर्णस्तु वैष्णवीं (*hiraṇyaṃ viṣṇurākhyātastasya varṇastu vaiṣṇavīṃ*), hiraṇya means Viṣṇu; varṇa means his wife. Therefore the meaning of the word हिरण्यवर्णां (*hiraṇyavarṇāṃ*) is Viṣṇu's wife. In accordance with the statement of the Śrī-purāṇa लक्ष्मीर्हिरण्यवर्णेति श्रूयते कनकप्रभा (*lakṣmīrhiraṇyavarṇeti śrūyate kanakaprabhā*) the intent is that Lakṣmī is hiraṇyavarṇā, that is, one whose body has a radiance like that of gold.
हरिणीं तु हरेः पत्नीं दारिद्रपरिहारिणीं । प्रपद्येऽहं हरिद्राभां हरिणाक्षीं हिरण्मयिं ॥ (*hariṇīṃ tu hareḥ patnīṃ dāridraparihāriṇīṃ | prapadye 'haṃ haridrābhāṃ hariṇākṣīṃ hiraṇmayiṃ ‖*)

So it is said in the Ātharvaṇika-stuti. This verse explains the meaning of the word हरिणीं (*hariṇīṃ*). हरिणी (*hariṇī*) means the wife of Hari. This deity removes poverty. The principal meaning is that she shines with the bodily radiance of a yellow (fair) colour, the colour of gold, with wide eyes like the eyes of a doe, and with a body made of gold.
सुवर्णरजतप्रजां (*suvarṇarajataprajāṃ*)—In the work called Mahālakṣmī-kośa it is said thus:
पिशंगधवलाभिश्च स्रग्भिरम्लानमूर्तिभिः । सौवर्ण्यैः कमलैर्नित्यं राजतैः श्रीर्विभूषिता ॥ (*piśaṃgadhavalābhiśca sragbhiramlānamūrtibhiḥ | sauvarṇyaiḥ kamalairnityaṃ rājataiḥ śrīrvibhūṣitā ‖*)
That is, this goddess Śrī shines, adorned with garlands strung of flowers that are yellow and white and never fade, and of lotus flowers made of gold and silver.
चंद्रां चंद्रनिभास्यां चपलां चंद्रस्य सोदरीं कलये (*caṃdrāṃ caṃdranibhāsyāṃ capalāṃ caṃdrasya sodarīṃ kalaye*)

so it is said. There, for the word चंद्र (*caṃdra*), the explanation is given: one who shines with a lotus face like the disc of the moon; or the sister of the moon. Since it is said in the Purāṇas and elsewhere that in former times, when the gods and the demons churned the ocean for the nectar, the moon and Lakṣmī arose there, it is explained here that Lakṣmī is the sister of the moon.

हिरण्मयीं (*hiraṇmayīṃ*)—one who has a golden form, that is, a body made of gold; or, since the syllable हिं (*hiṃ*) is declared to mean the thunderbolt and the letter ra to mean fire, the meaning is one who shines with a bodily radiance like a gleaming thunderbolt and like a brilliantly blazing fire.

लक्ष्मीं-लक्ष्मवतीं (*lakṣmīṃ-lakṣmavatīṃ*)—one who is endowed with all auspicious marks. According to the statement ज्ञानैश्वर्यसुखारोग्यधनधान्य, जयादिकं (*jñānaiśvaryasukhārogyadhanadhānya, jayādikaṃ*), the marks are knowledge, prosperity, happiness, health, wealth, grain and victory; the intent conveyed by the word लक्ष्मी (*lakṣmī*) is that she is endowed with these, that is, one who gives these to her devotees.
जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—Agni who knows everything: the all-knowing. Or else, one who is propounded in the Vedas. In the Mahābhārata:
वेदास्तद्वदर्थं जाताश्च जातवेदास्ततो ह्यसि (*vedāstadvadarthaṃ jātāśca jātavedāstato hyasi*)

so it is said. That is, O Agni, the Vedas have come into being for thee, that is, for the praise of thee; therefore thou art famed by the name जातवेदाः (*jātavedāḥ*): this is the intent. In this Ṛk the prayer is made to Agni, the Sacrifice-Person: "O Agni, bring Lakṣmī to me, for bestowing grace on me."
In the work called मंत्रकल्पावर्ण (*maṃtrakalpāvarṇa*) it is said thus:

हिरण्यवर्णामित्युक्तां श्रीसूक्ते प्रथमामृचं । श्रीं ह्रीं क्षीमिति विन्यस्य हिरण्यप्रतिमां यजेत् ॥ लक्ष्मीं संपूज्य हारिद्रचूर्णसौवर्णपंकजैः । राजतैः पुंडरीकैश्च पूजयेद्दास्सुवासिनीः ।' पूर्णॆंदौ पूर्णकुंभे वा ध्यात्वा नारायणीं परां । प्राप्याक्षमालां सौवर्णीं कमलासनसंस्थितः ॥ (*hiraṇyavarṇāmityuktāṃ śrīsūkte prathamāmṛcaṃ | śrīṃ hrīṃ kṣīmiti vinyasya hiraṇyapratimāṃ yajet ‖ lakṣmīṃ saṃpūjya hāridracūrṇasauvarṇapaṃkajaiḥ | rājataiḥ puṃḍarīkaiśca pūjayeddāssuvāsinīḥ | ' pūrṇèṃdau pūrṇakuṃbhe vā dhyātvā nārāyaṇīṃ parāṃ | prāpyākṣamālāṃ sauvarṇīṃ kamalāsanasaṃsthitaḥ ‖*)

ऋचं तु प्रजपेदाद्यां प्रत्यहं त्रिसहस्रकं । त्रि संध्यमेवं लक्षांते क्षीरैरयुततर्पणं ॥ सहस्रमाज्य होमश्च शतब्राह्मणभोजनं । सुवासिनीनां दशकं सालंकारमथार्चयेत् ॥ एकां धेनुं सवत्सां च शोत्रियाय प्रदापयेत् । (*ṛcaṃ tu prajapedādyāṃ pratyahaṃ trisahasrakaṃ | tri saṃdhyamevaṃ lakṣāṃte kṣīrairayutatarpaṇaṃ ‖ sahasramājya homaśca śatabrāhmaṇabhojanaṃ | suvāsinīnāṃ daśakaṃ sālaṃkāramathārcayet ‖ ekāṃ dhenuṃ savatsāṃ ca śotriyāya pradāpayet |*)

इत्थमक्षरलक्षांतं यो जपेन्नियतव्रतः ॥ हिरण्यपूर्णस्तेजस्वी धनाढ्यो भोगभाग्यवान् । जीवेच्चिरं शरीरांते चंद्रसायुज्यमाप्नुयात् ॥ (*itthamakṣaralakṣāṃtaṃ yo japenniyatavrataḥ ‖ hiraṇyapūrṇastejasvī dhanāḍhyo bhogabhāgyavān | jīvecciraṃ śarīrāṃte caṃdrasāyujyamāpnuyāt ‖*)

In the Śrī-sūkta, हिरण्यवर्णां (*hiraṇyavarṇāṃ*) is the first Ṛk. When this mantra is to be recited, nyāsa and the rest are to be performed together with the seed-syllables श्रीं ह्लीं क्लीं (*śrīṃ hlīṃ klīṃ*) ⟨NOTE:171⟩; an image made of gold is to be set up, and the deity called Lakṣmī is to be invoked in it and worshipped with turmeric, kuṅkuma, lotus flowers made of gold, lotus flowers made of silver, flowers of many kinds, fragrant substances and the like. And cows and married women (suvāsinī) are to be honoured according to one's ability. One should meditate on this Lakṣmī as abiding in the full moon; or one should invoke Lakṣmī in a pot filled with pure water and meditate. Thereafter, holding a rosary in the hand, seated in the lotus posture, meditating on this goddess as made of gold, one should recite the first Ṛk of this sūkta, हिरण्यवर्णां (*hiraṇyavarṇāṃ*), every day in the morning, at noon and in the evening,

up to three thousand in number a day. When one lakh of recitations has been completed in this way, a libation (tarpaṇa) of milk is to be given. In the fire that has been duly installed and consecrated, one thousand oblations of ghee are to be offered. A hundred Brahmins are to be fed. Ten married women are to be honoured and satisfied with ornaments of many kinds, and with garments and jewels. Afterwards a fine cow with her calf, well adorned, is to be given to a Brahmin learned in the Veda (śrotriya). The man who, by this procedure, with restraint, recites as many lakhs as there are syllables in the mantra will obtain gold as he wishes. Becoming radiant and wealthy, he will enjoy all pleasures. Having a long life, living for a long time, at the end he will attain the excellent state called union with the moon (candra-sāyujya).
Here ends the explanation of the meaning of the first Ṛk.

en: The Maruts who were born (प्र जाताः (*pra jātāḥ*)) together with the great (महिना (*mahinā*)) Viṣṇu or Indra, that is, appeared: Evayāmarut praises them (ब्रुवते (*bruvate*)). And those who, quickly and of themselves, were born together with knowledge (विद्मना (*vidmanā*)) of the going to the sacrifice, he praises. The word प्र (*pra*) is to be construed with the verb. The plural in ब्रुवत (*bruvata*) is by change of number; or, if singular, the ending is Vedic. The absence of the accent-lowering is Vedic. Now a direct address: O Maruts, that well-known strength (शवः (*śavaḥ*)) of yours, joined with action (क्रत्वा (*kratvā*)) such as setting in motion, cannot be assailed (नाधृषे (*nādhṛṣe*)) by anyone; it is not to be overcome by the action of other beings such as the Asuras. The ending केन् (*ken*) is in the sense of fitness. Moreover, that strength of yours is endowed with gifts (दाना (*dānā*)), the bestowal of what is desired, and with greatness (मह्ना (*mahnā*)). You are mighty and unassailable; the example is the mountains (अद्रयो न (*adrayo na*)): as they are not to be assailed, so are you.
- विद्मना (*vidmanā*)—having knowledge of the going to the sacrifice
- दाना (*dānā*)—joined with the bestowal of what is desired
- अनपगामिनीं (*anapagāminīṃ*)—she who never leaves me, that is, who abides firmly in my house
- यस्यां (*yasyāṃ*)—when which goddess has come to me
- पुरुषान् (*puruṣān*)—people such as sons, grandsons and servants
- विंदेयं (*viṃdeyaṃ*)—may I obtain; (तां लक्ष्मीं मे अवन (*tāṃ lakṣmīṃ me avana*)—bring such a goddess to my presence.)

The Maruts who were born together with the great Indra, who quickly and of themselves were born with the going to the sacrifice: such Maruts the seer Evayāmarut praises. O Maruts, your well-known strength, joined with extraordinary actions, remains unassailed. That same strength of yours, joined with the bestowal of what is desired and with greatness, remains unmoved like mountains.

O Agni, bring near me the goddess Śrī who bears the name Lakṣmī, of such great glory that, when she comes to my house, by her grace I shall obtain gold, wealth of cows, wealth of horses, sons, grandsons, servants and the like, all of these.

Evayamarut glorifies those who are manifested with the great (Indra), who appear spontaneously and speedily with the knowledge (that the sacrifice is prepared) : your strength in action, Maruts, is not to be resisted, (though qualified) by (your) infinite liberality : you are immoveable as mountains.

अस्य श्रीसूक्तद्वितीय ऋङ्महामंत्रस्य । जातवेदा ऋषिः । श्रीराज्यलक्ष्मीर्देवता । अनुष्टुप् छंदः । श्रीं बीजं । ह्रीं शक्तिः । क्लीं कीलकं । मम राज्यलक्ष्मीप्रसादसिद्ध्यर्थे जपे विनियोगः ॥ ओं श्रीं तां म आवह—अंगुष्ठाभ्यां नमः । (*asya śrīsūktadvitīya ṛṅmahāmaṃtrasya | jātavedā ṛṣiḥ | śrīrājyalakṣmīrdevatā | anuṣṭup chaṃdaḥ | śrīṃ bījaṃ | hrīṃ śaktiḥ | klīṃ kīlakaṃ | mama rājyalakṣmīprasādasiddhyarthe jape viniyogaḥ ‖ oṃ śrīṃ tāṃ ma āvaha—aṃguṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ |*)

ओं ह्रीं जातवेदो लक्ष्मीं—तर्जनीभ्यां नमः । ओं क्लीं अनपगामिनीं—मध्यमाभ्यां नमः । ओं क्ली यस्मां हिरण्यं विंदेयं—अनामिकाभ्यां नमः । ओं ह्रीं गामश्वं—कनिष्ठिकाभ्यां नमः । ओं श्रीं पुरुषानहं —करतलकरसृष्टाभ्यां नमः ओं श्रीं तां म आवह हृदयाय नमः । ओं ह्रीं जातवेदोलक्ष्मीं—शिरसे स्वाहा । ओं क्लीं अनपगामिनीं शिखाय्कॆ वषट् । ओं क्लीं यस्मां हिरण्यं विंदेयं— कवचाय हुं । ओं ह्रीं गामश्वं—नेत्रत्रयाय वषट् । ओं श्रीं पुरुषानहं— अस्त्राय फट् । (*oṃ hrīṃ jātavedo lakṣmīṃ—tarjanībhyāṃ namaḥ | oṃ klīṃ anapagāminīṃ—madhyamābhyāṃ namaḥ | oṃ klī yasmāṃ hiraṇyaṃ viṃdeyaṃ—anāmikābhyāṃ namaḥ | oṃ hrīṃ gāmaśvaṃ—kaniṣṭhikābhyāṃ namaḥ | oṃ śrīṃ puruṣānahaṃ —karatalakarasṛṣṭābhyāṃ namaḥ oṃ śrīṃ tāṃ ma āvaha hṛdayāya namaḥ | oṃ hrīṃ jātavedolakṣmīṃ—śirase svāhā | oṃ klīṃ anapagāminīṃ śikhāykè vaṣaṭ | oṃ klīṃ yasmāṃ hiraṇyaṃ viṃdeyaṃ— kavacāya huṃ | oṃ hrīṃ gāmaśvaṃ—netratrayāya vaṣaṭ | oṃ śrīṃ puruṣānahaṃ— astrāya phaṭ |*)

भूर्भुवस्सुवरोमिति दिग्बंधः ॥ ध्यानं । केयूरैर्मेखलाद्यैर्नवमणिखचितैर्भूषणैर्भासमानां कर्पूरामोदवक्रामपरिमितकृपापूर्णनेत्रागविंदां । हेमाभां दिव्यवस्त्रं मृगमदतिलकां पद्मवक्रामुदारां श्रीलक्ष्मीं पद्महस्तां नतजनवरदां सर्वभूतै नमामि (*bhūrbhuvassuvaromiti digbaṃdhaḥ ‖ dhyānaṃ | keyūrairmekhalādyairnavamaṇikhacitairbhūṣaṇairbhāsamānāṃ karpūrāmodavakrāmaparimitakṛpāpūrṇanetrāgaviṃdāṃ | hemābhāṃ divyavastraṃ mṛgamadatilakāṃ padmavakrāmudārāṃ śrīlakṣmīṃ padmahastāṃ natajanavaradāṃ sarvabhūtai namāmi*)
ओं तां म आवह जातवेदो लक्ष्मीमनपगामिनीं । यस्यां हिरण्यं विंदेयं गामश्वं पुरुषानहं ॥ (*oṃ tāṃ ma āvaha jātavedo lakṣmīmanapagāminīṃ | yasyāṃ hiraṇyaṃ viṃdeyaṃ gāmaśvaṃ puruṣānahaṃ ‖*)

हे जातवेदः अनपगामिनीमपगमनरहितां अनपायिनीमित्यर्थः । तां वक्ष्यमाणां लक्ष्मीं मे मह्यमावह आह्वय । यस्यां श्रीदेव्यामाहूतायां सत्यां हिरण्यं सुवर्णं गां धेनुमश्वं वाजिनं पुरुषान् पुत्रमित्रदासभूतान् अहं विंदेयं प्राप्नुयां ॥ (*he jātavedaḥ anapagāminīmapagamanarahitāṃ anapāyinīmityarthaḥ | tāṃ vakṣyamāṇāṃ lakṣmīṃ me mahyamāvaha āhvaya | yasyāṃ śrīdevyāmāhūtāyāṃ satyāṃ hiraṇyaṃ suvarṇaṃ gāṃ dhenumaśvaṃ vājinaṃ puruṣān putramitradāsabhūtān ahaṃ viṃdeyaṃ prāpnuyāṃ ‖*)

हे जातवेदः श्रुताग्ने यस्यां लक्ष्म्यमागतायां सत्यां आहं पुरुषान् पुत्रादीन् गां पशून् अश्वं तुरगादिवाहनविशेषान् हिरण्यं कनकादिवस्तूनि विंदेयं लभेयं तामनपगामिनीं कदाचिदपि मां त्यक्त्या अन्यत्र गंतुमनुद्युक्तां मदेकाश्रयनिष्ठां लक्ष्मीं मे मदर्थमावह प्रेषय ॥ (*he jātavedaḥ śrutāgne yasyāṃ lakṣmyamāgatāyāṃ satyāṃ āhaṃ puruṣān putrādīn gāṃ paśūn aśvaṃ turagādivāhanaviśeṣān hiraṇyaṃ kanakādivastūni viṃdeyaṃ labheyaṃ tāmanapagāminīṃ kadācidapi māṃ tyaktyā anyatra gaṃtumanudyuktāṃ madekāśrayaniṣṭhāṃ lakṣmīṃ me madarthamāvaha preṣaya ‖*)

तां हिरण्यवर्णत्वादिलक्षणोपेतामनपगामिनीं विष्णोरनपायिनीं लक्ष्मीं— राघवत्वे भवत्सीता रुक्ष्मिणी कृष्णजन्मनि । अन्येष्वप्यवतारेषु विष्णोरेवानपायिनी ॥ इति पराशरपुराणान् ॥ (*tāṃ hiraṇyavarṇatvādilakṣaṇopetāmanapagāminīṃ viṣṇoranapāyinīṃ lakṣmīṃ— rāghavatve bhavatsītā rukṣmiṇī kṛṣṇajanmani | anyeṣvapyavatāreṣu viṣṇorevānapāyinī ‖ iti parāśarapurāṇān ‖*)

आवहेति जातवेदसं प्रार्थयेत् । आगतायां च तस्यां किं ते फलमिति चेदुच्यते-यस्यामिति । यस्यामागतायां हिरण्यं गामश्वं पुरुषांश्चाहं (*āvaheti jātavedasaṃ prārthayet | āgatāyāṃ ca tasyāṃ kiṃ te phalamiti ceducyate-yasyāmiti | yasyāmāgatāyāṃ hiraṇyaṃ gāmaśvaṃ puruṣāṃścāhaṃ*)

विंदेयं— “गावस्तथा हस्तिहिरण्यमश्वानिति” राज्यलक्ष्मीहृदयोक्ते । (*viṃdeyaṃ— “gāvastathā hastihiraṇyamaśvāniti” rājyalakṣmīhṛdayokte |*) — "may I obtain": "cows, likewise elephants, gold and horses," so it is said in the Rājyalakṣmī-hṛdaya. श्रीमित्यादिबीजत्रयेण न्यासः (*śrīmityādibījatrayeṇa nyāsaḥ*) — the nyāsa is made with the three seed-syllables beginning with śrīm. ⟨NOTE:172⟩ Meditation (dhyāna):
चतुरंगबलोपेतां धनधान्यसुखेश्वरीं । अश्वारूढामहं वंदे राजलक्ष्मीं हिरण्मयीं ॥ (*caturaṃgabalopetāṃ dhanadhānyasukheśvarīṃ | aśvārūḍhāmahaṃ vaṃde rājalakṣmīṃ hiraṇmayīṃ ‖*)

ऋचं द्वितीयं श्रीसूक्ते प्रतिसायं सहस्रकं । प्रजपेन्नियताहारः प्रत्यक्षरसहस्रकं ॥ त्रयस्त्रिंशद्दिने रात्र्य स्वप्ने लक्ष्मीः प्रसीदति । शांतिकर्मादिकं सर्वं प्रागुक्तवदुपाचरेत् ॥ अविघ्नेन जपन्सिध्येद्यदि लक्ष्मीप्रसादतः । अनपायां श्रियं याति हिरण्यं गोनरादिकान् ॥ अनपाया भवेल्लक्ष्मस्तस्य जन्मनि नान्यथा ॥ (*ṛcaṃ dvitīyaṃ śrīsūkte pratisāyaṃ sahasrakaṃ | prajapenniyatāhāraḥ pratyakṣarasahasrakaṃ ‖ trayastriṃśaddine rātrya svapne lakṣmīḥ prasīdati | śāṃtikarmādikaṃ sarvaṃ prāguktavadupācaret ‖ avighnena japansidhyedyadi lakṣmīprasādataḥ | anapāyāṃ śriyaṃ yāti hiraṇyaṃ gonarādikān ‖ anapāyā bhavellakṣmastasya janmani nānyathā ‖*)

(Cidvilāsa-vṛtti) In the previous Ṛk this goddess was described as one possessing the marks beginning with golden colour; in this Ṛk her greatness is described by the epithet अनपगामिनीं (*anapagāminīṃ*). The commentary gives two kinds of meaning for the word अनपगामिनीं (*anapagāminīṃ*). One meaning is कदाचिदपि मां त्यक्त्वा अन्यत्र गंतुमनुद्युक्तां मदेकाश्रयनिष्ठां—याव (*kadācidapi māṃ tyaktvā anyatra gaṃtumanudyuktāṃ madekāśrayaniṣṭhāṃ—yāva*): she who never at any time leaves me and goes elsewhere, but is always close to me. The second meaning is: she who never parts from her husband and is always in his company. To support this meaning the verse of the Parāśara-purāṇa is cited:
राघवत्वे भवत्सीता रुक्मिणी कृष्णजन्मनि । अन्येष्वप्यवतारेषु विष्णोरेवानपायिनी ॥ (*rāghavatve bhavatsītā rukmiṇī kṛṣṇajanmani | anyeṣvapyavatāreṣu viṣṇorevānapāyinī ‖*)

This Lakṣmī never separates from her husband Viṣṇu and is always in his company. Famed as Sītā in the incarnation of Rāma, as Rukṣmiṇī in the incarnation of Kṛṣṇa, and under other names in other incarnations, she is always with Viṣṇu, delighting him; this is the main intention.

Here Agni is prayed to bring Lakṣmī. For what purpose should she be brought? What is the benefit when this goddess comes? That is set out in the second half of this Ṛk: if this goddess comes to me, then by her grace I shall obtain wealth and gold, cows, horses, sons, grandsons and the like; such is the seer's intention. In the work called Rājyalakṣmī-hṛdaya it is said गावस्तथा हस्ति हिरण्यमश्वान् (*gāvastathā hasti hiraṇyamaśvān*)—

by the grace of this goddess cows, elephants, gold and horses, all of these, are obtained. As said at the beginning of this Ṛk, nyāsa is to be made with the seed-syllables beginning with śrīm, and meditation is to be made with the verse—
चतुरंगबलोपेतां धनधान्यसुखेश्वरीं । अश्वारूढामहं वंदे राजलक्ष्मीं हिरण्मयीं ॥ (*caturaṃgabalopetāṃ dhanadhānyasukheśvarīṃ | aśvārūḍhāmahaṃ vaṃde rājalakṣmīṃ hiraṇmayīṃ ‖*)

This goddess, who has the form of Rājalakṣmī, is accompanied by an army of four kinds: elephants, horses, chariots and foot-soldiers. She is the mistress of wealth, grain and happiness, and is seated on an excellent horse. She has a body made of gold. The main sense of this verse is: "I reverently salute the goddess named Rājalakṣmī, endowed with such marks."

The Ṛk तां म आवह (*tāṃ ma āvaha*), the second Ṛk of the Śrī-sūkta, is to be recited every evening to the number of one thousand. While reciting, one must keep to restraint in food and the like. For each syllable of the mantra one thousand is to be recited, that is, thirty-three thousand in all. If this is done, on the night of the thirty-third day the goddess Lakṣmī appears in a dream and becomes gracious. The recitation and the rest of this mantra are to be performed according to the rules and restrictions stated earlier. If through Lakṣmī's grace the recitation proceeds without obstacle and is completed, the man who recites obtains imperishable wealth, gold, cows, sons, grandsons and the like, and lives happily. Lakṣmī, being pleased, shows him grace in every birth. For the obtaining of Lakṣmī's grace there is no other means than this.
Here ends the explanation of the second Ṛk.
notes: ಕ್ಷೀಂ printed, ಕ್ಲೀಂ in the verse quotation above

ಒಂಭತ್ತು ಬೀಜಾಕ್ಷರ: the Kannada lists nine seed-syllables, while the Sanskrit line before it begins ಶ್ರೀಂ ಕ್ರೋಂ ಐಂ ಶ್ರೀಂ ಹ್ರೀಂ ಆಂ ಹ್ರೀಂ ಕ್ರೋಂ; and the Kannada gives ಶ್ರೀಂ as bīja, ಬ್ಲೂಂ as śakti, ಕ್ಲೀಂ as kīlaka, whereas the Sanskrit says ಶ್ರೀಂ ಬ್ಲೂಂ ಕ್ಲೀಂ ಬೀಜಾನಿ

en: The Maruts who, coming from the vast (बृहतः (*bṛhataḥ*)) heaven (दिवः (*divaḥ*)), the world of heaven, are heard (शृण्विरे (*śṛṇvire*)), they are praised by Evayāmarut with his speech (गिरा (*girā*)). What are they like? Shining (शुशुक्वानः (*śuśukvānaḥ*)), and well-being (सुभ्वः (*subhvaḥ*)). In the common dwelling (सधस्थे (*sadhasthe*)), their own abode, of those Maruts, no one, no impeller (इरी (*irī*)), is able to disturb them or to set them in motion; आ (*ā*) is in the sense of "and". They are like fires (अग्नयो न (*agnayo na*)), self-radiant (स्वविद्युतः (*svavidyutaḥ*)), shining of themselves; and they are the impellers (स्यंद्रासः (*syaṃdrāsaḥ*)) of the rivers (धुनीनां (*dhunīnāṃ*)) by raining.

अश्वपूर्वां (*aśvapūrvāṃ*) is she whose forerunners are horses; रथमध्यां (*rathamadhyāṃ*) is she in whose middle are chariots; हस्तिनादप्रबोधिनीं (*hastinādaprabodhinīṃ*) is she who is announced by the trumpeting of elephants. देवीं (*devīṃ*) means one given to play, or one who shines. श्रियं (*śriyaṃ*) is Śrī, to be resorted to, of the form of an army; उपह्वये (*upahvaye*) means "I call near." Such a goddess Śrī, being called, may she favour me.

यस्यास्सेनारूपाया अश्वाः पुरोगामिनस्तामश्वपूर्वां रथा एव मध्ये यस्यास्तां रथमध्यामागमनकाले गजध्वनीनां ज्ञापयित्रीं हस्तिनादप्रबोधिनीं देवीं क्रीडादिलक्षणशीलां श्रियं लक्ष्मीमहमुपह्वये मत्समीपमागच्छेत्याह्वये । आहूता च मया श्रीर्देवीः देवीः वचनव्यत्ययश्चांदसः मा मां जुषतां सेवतां ॥ (*yasyāssenārūpāyā aśvāḥ purogāminastāmaśvapūrvāṃ rathā eva madhye yasyāstāṃ rathamadhyāmāgamanakāle gajadhvanīnāṃ jñāpayitrīṃ hastinādaprabodhinīṃ devīṃ krīḍādilakṣaṇaśīlāṃ śriyaṃ lakṣmīmahamupahvaye matsamīpamāgacchetyāhvaye | āhūtā ca mayā śrīrdevīḥ devīḥ vacanavyatyayaścāṃdasaḥ mā māṃ juṣatāṃ sevatāṃ ‖*)

She whose army-form has horses going in front is अश्वपूर्वां (*aśvapūrvāṃ*); she in whose middle are chariots is रथमध्यां (*rathamadhyāṃ*); she who at the time of her coming makes known the roar of elephants is हस्तिनादप्रबोधिनीं (*hastinādaprabodhinīṃ*). The goddess, given to play and the like, Śrī, that is Lakṣmī, I call to my presence, saying "come." Being called by me, may Śrī the goddess favour me. The plural देवीः (*devīḥ*) is a Vedic irregularity of number.
- इरी (*irī*)—the hero who would make them move
- आ न ईष्टे (*ā na īṣṭe*)—no one is able (and which Maruts)
- प्र शृण्वरे (*pra śṛṇvare*)—hear our praises, such
- अश्वपूर्वां (*aśvapūrvāṃ*)—she who has horses at the front of her army
- रथमध्यां (*rathamadhyāṃ*)—she who has chariots in the middle of the army
- हस्तिनादप्रबोधिनीं (*hastinādaprabodhinīṃ*)—she who makes known the nature of the army by the trumpeting of elephants
- देवीं (*devīṃ*)—she who is radiant, or one given to play and the like
- उपह्वये (*upahvaye*)—I pray and call that she may come near me
- श्रीः देवीः (*śrīḥ devīḥ*)—the goddess Śrī, called by me

In whose house no hero who would make them move is able to do so, and who, like fires, are the impellers of the flow of the self-radiant rivers, and who, coming from the vast heaven, hear our praises: such Maruts, shining exceedingly and extraordinary, the seer Evayāmarut praises with his praises.

In the army of the goddess Śrī there are horses at the front, a chariot in the middle, and it shines with the trumpeting of elephants. Seated in the chariot in the middle of such an army, the shining goddess Śrī I pray and call to come near me. Having heard my prayer and come, may that goddess stay near me and show me favour.

श्रीसूक्ते तु तृतीयर्चः श्रीबीजेन समायुतं । न्यासं कृत्वा जपेन्नित्यं प्रातः प्रातः सहस्रकं ॥ आद्वादशाब्दात्सिद्धिः स्यादन्यदुर्गाविधानवत् । मंत्रसिद्धौ भवेद्राजा शत्रून् जित्वा लभेच्छ्रियं ॥ (*śrīsūkte tu tṛtīyarcaḥ śrībījena samāyutaṃ | nyāsaṃ kṛtvā japennityaṃ prātaḥ prātaḥ sahasrakaṃ ‖ ādvādaśābdātsiddhiḥ syādanyadurgāvidhānavat | maṃtrasiddhau bhavedrājā śatrūn jitvā labhecchriyaṃ ‖*)

Having made nyāsa of this third Ṛk of the Śrī-sūkta together with the seed-syllable śrī, one should recite it every day in the morning, one thousand each time. If one recites in this way for twelve years and performs it according to the rules of the worship of Durgā, the king who recites attains success in the mantra. He conquers his enemy kings and obtains immeasurable wealth.
Here ends the explanation of the third Ṛk.

Evayamarut glorifies with praise those who, (coming) brilliant and happy from the vast heaven, hear (his invocation); in whose dwelling there is no one able to disturb them, and, who, like self-radiant fires, are the impellers of the rivers.

अस्य श्रीसूक्ततृतीय ऋज्महामंत्रस्य । आनंद ऋषिः । श्रीलक्ष्मीर्देवता । अनुष्टुप्छंदः । श्रीलक्ष्मीर्देवता । उकारो बीजर । तकारश्यक्तिः । श्रीं कीलकं । सर्वसौभाग्यदायिनी महालक्ष्मीदेवताप्रसादसिद्ध्यर्थे जपे विनियोगः ॥ ओं अश्वपूर्वा०—अंगुष्ठाभ्यां नमः । ओं रथमध्यां—तर्जनीभ्यां नमः । ओं हस्तिनादप्रबोधिनीं—मध्यमाभ्यां नमः । ओं श्रियं देवीं—अनामिकाभ्यां नमः । ओं उपह्वये—कनष्ठिकाभ्यां (*asya śrīsūktatṛtīya ṛjmahāmaṃtrasya | ānaṃda ṛṣiḥ | śrīlakṣmīrdevatā | anuṣṭupchaṃdaḥ | śrīlakṣmīrdevatā | ukāro bījara | takāraśyaktiḥ | śrīṃ kīlakaṃ | sarvasaubhāgyadāyinī mahālakṣmīdevatāprasādasiddhyarthe jape viniyogaḥ ‖ oṃ aśvapūrvā0—aṃguṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ | oṃ rathamadhyāṃ—tarjanībhyāṃ namaḥ | oṃ hastinādaprabodhinīṃ—madhyamābhyāṃ namaḥ | oṃ śriyaṃ devīṃ—anāmikābhyāṃ namaḥ | oṃ upahvaye—kanaṣṭhikābhyāṃ*) ओं श्रीर्मा देवीर्जुषतां—करतलकरप्प- (*oṃ śrīrmā devīrjuṣatāṃ—karatalakarappa-*)

ष्ठाभ्यां नमः । ओं अश्वपूर्वा०—हृदयाय नमः । ओं रथमध्या०—शिरसे स्वाहा । ओं हस्तिनादप्रबोधिनीं—शिखाय्कॆ वषट् । ओं श्रियं देवीं—कवचाय हुं। ओं उपह्वये—नेत्रत्रयाय वौषट् । ओं श्रीर्मा देवीर्जुषतां—अस्त्राय फट् । भूर्भुम्ससवरोमिति दिग्बंधः । ध्यानं । तटिद्वर्णापूर्णां शशिलपनताटंकयुगळां दरस्मेराधीरां करकलितपद्मां द्विनयनां । लसद्रीवां क्षौमांशुकविशदनाभीसरसिजां भजामि त्वां देवीं प्रणतजनसौभाग्यजननीं ॥ इति ध्यात्वा जपं कुर्यात्] ॥ (*ṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ | oṃ aśvapūrvā0—hṛdayāya namaḥ | oṃ rathamadhyā0—śirase svāhā | oṃ hastinādaprabodhinīṃ—śikhāykè vaṣaṭ | oṃ śriyaṃ devīṃ—kavacāya huṃ| oṃ upahvaye—netratrayāya vauṣaṭ | oṃ śrīrmā devīrjuṣatāṃ—astrāya phaṭ | bhūrbhumsasavaromiti digbaṃdhaḥ | dhyānaṃ | taṭidvarṇāpūrṇāṃ śaśilapanatāṭaṃkayugaḷāṃ darasmerādhīrāṃ karakalitapadmāṃ dvinayanāṃ | lasadrīvāṃ kṣaumāṃśukaviśadanābhīsarasijāṃ bhajāmi tvāṃ devīṃ praṇatajanasaubhāgyajananīṃ ‖ iti dhyātvā japaṃ kuryāt] ‖*)
ओं अश्वपूर्वा० रथमध्या० हस्तिनादप्रबोधिनीं । श्रीयं देवीमुपह्वये श्रीर्मा देवीर्जुषतां ॥ (*oṃ aśvapūrvā0 rathamadhyā0 hastinādaprabodhinīṃ | śrīyaṃ devīmupahvaye śrīrmā devīrjuṣatāṃ ‖*)

अश्वपूर्वामश्वा पूर्वे पुरोगाः यस्यास्तां । रथमध्यां रथाः मध्यॆ यस्यास्तां । हस्तिनादप्रबोधिनीं हस्तिनां नादेन बृंहितेन प्रबोधिनीं प्रकर्षण ज्ञापिकां । देवीं देवनशीलां द्योतनशीलां वा । श्रियं श्रयणीयां सेनारूपामुपह्वये समीपं प्रत्याह्वये । एशादृशी देवी श्री मा मां जुषतां सेवतां ॥ (*aśvapūrvāmaśvā pūrve purogāḥ yasyāstāṃ | rathamadhyāṃ rathāḥ madhyè yasyāstāṃ | hastinādaprabodhinīṃ hastināṃ nādena bṛṃhitena prabodhinīṃ prakarṣaṇa jñāpikāṃ | devīṃ devanaśīlāṃ dyotanaśīlāṃ vā | śriyaṃ śrayaṇīyāṃ senārūpāmupahvaye samīpaṃ pratyāhvaye | eśādṛśī devī śrī mā māṃ juṣatāṃ sevatāṃ ‖*)

That troop of Maruts went out (निश्चक्रमे (*niścakrame*)) from the sky, a seat common to all, vast, being wide-striding (उरुक्रमः (*urukramaḥ*)). When the seer Evayāmarut, from his own place (the word अधि (*adhi*) merely repeats the sense of the ablative), by himself, with his going (स्नुभिः (*snubhiḥ*)) leaders (नृभिः (*nṛbhiḥ*)), that is, his own guiding horses, was yoked (अयुक्त (*ayukta*)) in prayer for their coming, then, he now speaks in the plural, they are विस्पर्धसः (*vispardhasaḥ*), of various rivalry: "I go in front, I go in front", such is their rivalry; or else they are without rivalry, for they have no rivals. They are विमहसः (*vimahasaḥ*), of distinguished strength, and शेवृधः (*śevṛdhaḥ*), increasers of शेव (*śeva*), happiness. जिगाति (*jigāti*) means "they go forth"; the singular is by change of number.

कां (*kāṃ*) is she who is beyond the reach of speech and mind, whose nature is hard to define; or she who has the form of Brahman, according to another Śruti and a Purāṇa, which he quotes: "Ka is the name of Brahman." सोस्मितां (*sosmitāṃ*) is she who is accompanied by a smile (the elision of the final vowel being Vedic). हिरण्यप्राकारां (*hiraṇyaprākārāṃ*) is she whose colour or form is golden. आद्र्रां (*ādrrāṃ*) means moist, because she arose from the ocean of milk; or one born under the Ārdrā asterism, or of the form of Rudra; he cites the Vedic text "Rudra goes first with Ārdrā". ज्वलंतीं (*jvalaṃtīṃ*) is shining; तृप्तां (*tṛptāṃ*) is one whose desires are fulfilled, and she satisfies devotees with their wishes. पद्मे स्थितां (*padme sthitāṃ*) is seated on a lotus; पद्मवर्णां (*padmavarṇāṃ*) has the lustre of a lotus. That well-known Śrī I call here.

सोस्क्रितामुत्कृष्टस्मितेन सहितां । हिरण्यप्राकारां सुवर्णावरणां । आद्र्रां शीतलगुणां ज्वलंतीं ज्योतिःस्वरूपां । तृप्तां भक्तिपूज-दिभिरिति यावत् । तर्पयंतीं वरप्रासादानुग्रहविशेषैः स्वभक्तानां वांछापूर्तिकारिणीं । पद्मवर्णां कमलवद्भासमानां । पद्मे स्थितां पद्माधिष्ठितां । तां वाणीं वाक्यरूपां तां श्रियं । इह मत्समीपं प्रति उपह्वये आवाहनं करोमित्यर्थः ॥ (*soskritāmutkṛṣṭasmitena sahitāṃ | hiraṇyaprākārāṃ suvarṇāvaraṇāṃ | ādrrāṃ śītalaguṇāṃ jvalaṃtīṃ jyotiḥsvarūpāṃ | tṛptāṃ bhaktipūja-dibhiriti yāvat | tarpayaṃtīṃ varaprāsādānugrahaviśeṣaiḥ svabhaktānāṃ vāṃchāpūrtikāriṇīṃ | padmavarṇāṃ kamalavadbhāsamānāṃ | padme sthitāṃ padmādhiṣṭhitāṃ | tāṃ vāṇīṃ vākyarūpāṃ tāṃ śriyaṃ | iha matsamīpaṃ prati upahvaye āvāhanaṃ karomityarthaḥ ‖*)

सोस्क्रितां (*soskritāṃ*) is she accompanied by an excellent smile; हिरण्यप्राकारां (*hiraṇyaprākārāṃ*) is she covered with gold; आद्र्रां (*ādrrāṃ*) is she of cool quality; ज्वलंतीं (*jvalaṃtīṃ*) is of the nature of light; तृप्तां (*tṛptāṃ*) is satisfied by the devotion, worship and the like of devotees; तर्पयंतीं (*tarpayaṃtīṃ*) fulfils the wishes of her devotees by special grants of boons and grace; पद्मवर्णां (*padmavarṇāṃ*) shines like a lotus; पद्मे स्थितां (*padme sthitāṃ*) is established on a lotus. That Śrī, of the form of speech, I invoke here, near me.
- स्वात् आधि (*svāt ādhi*)—being at his own place (waiting for the prayer, then)
- आयुक्त (*āyukta*)—(the troop of Maruts) was yoked (and then)
- उरुक्रमः (*urukramaḥ*)—having a wide way of travelling
- शेवृधः (*śevṛdhaḥ*)—and increasers of happiness, the Maruts
- कां (*kāṃ*)—she whose nature is Brahman, beyond the reach of speech and mind
- सोस्मितां (*sosmitāṃ*)—she who is shedding a slight gentle smile
- हिरण्यप्राकारां (*hiraṇyaprākārāṃ*)—she who has an excellent colour or form like the colour of gold
- आद्र्रां (*ādrrāṃ*)—she who has a moist, cool quality, or who has a Rudra-form born under the Ārdrā asterism
- ज्वलंतीं (*jvalaṃtīṃ*)—she who is shining, or who is of the nature of light
- तृप्तां (*tṛptāṃ*)—she whose desires are fulfilled, or who is pleased by the worship and the like of devotees
- तर्पयंतीं (*tarpayaṃtīṃ*)—she who fulfils the wishes of devotees by granting boons and grace
- पद्मेस्थितां (*padmesthitāṃ*)—she who sits on a lotus, or who has the lotus as her seat
- पद्मवर्णां (*padmavarṇāṃ*)—she who has a bodily lustre of the red tinge of a lotus
- तां श्रियं (*tāṃ śriyaṃ*)—that famed goddess Śrī
- उप ह्वये (*upa hvaye*)—I pray and call

As soon as the seer Evayāmarut prayed at his own place for the Maruts, the Maruts, yoked with remarkable horses, went out from the sky, which is very extensive and common to all. The Maruts, who vie with one another in going to the sacrifice, who have exceeding strength and who increase happiness, go forth for the sacrifice.

This goddess Śrī whom I invoke has the nature of Brahman, beyond the reach of speech and mind. She shines with a face radiant with a gentle smile and with a bodily lustre like the colour of gold. Though shining with great radiance in the form of light, she has a cool quality like the light of the moon. She has all her desires fulfilled, and satisfies devotees by granting them the wishes they desire. Making the lotus her seat and sitting on it, shining with a pure bodily lustre like the red tinge of the lotus, that goddess Śrī I pray and call to come near me.

That wide-spreading troop (of Maruts) has issued from a spacious common dwelling-place, (where) Evayamarut (awaits them) when their car has been spontaneously harnessed with its rapid horses; and, emulous, vigorous, and conferring hapiness, they sally forth.

अस्य श्रीश्रीसूक्तचतुर्थऋङ्महामंत्रस्य । आनंद ऋषिः । श्रीलक्ष्मीर्देवता। बृहतीछंदः । कां बीजं । ह्रीं शक्तिः । श्रीं कीलकं । श्री लक्ष्मीदेवता प्रसादसिद्ध्यर्थे जपे विनियोगः ॥ ओं कांसोस्क्रितां—अंगुष्ठाभ्यां नमः । ओं हिरण्य प्राकारां—तर्जनीभ्यां नमः । ओं आद्र्रां ज्वलंतीं—मध्यमाभ्यां नमः । ओं तृप्तां तर्पयंतीं—आनामिकाभ्यां नमः । ओं पद्मेस्थितां पद्मवर्णां-कनिष्ठिकाभ्यां नम॥ । तामिहोपह्वये श्रियं—करतलकरपृष्टाभ्यां नमः । ओं कांसोस्क्रितां— हृदयाय नमः । ओं हिरण्यप्रकारां—शिरसे स्वाहा । ओं आद्र्रां ज्वलतीं-शिखाय्कॆ वषट् । ओं तृप्तां तर्पयंतीं — कवचाय हुं । ओं पद्मे स्थितां पद्मवर्णां— नेत्रत्रयाय नौषट् । ओं तामिहोपह्वये श्रियं—आस्त्राय फट् ॥ (*asya śrīśrīsūktacaturthaṛṅmahāmaṃtrasya | ānaṃda ṛṣiḥ | śrīlakṣmīrdevatā| bṛhatīchaṃdaḥ | kāṃ bījaṃ | hrīṃ śaktiḥ | śrīṃ kīlakaṃ | śrī lakṣmīdevatā prasādasiddhyarthe jape viniyogaḥ ‖ oṃ kāṃsoskritāṃ—aṃguṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ | oṃ hiraṇya prākārāṃ—tarjanībhyāṃ namaḥ | oṃ ādrrāṃ jvalaṃtīṃ—madhyamābhyāṃ namaḥ | oṃ tṛptāṃ tarpayaṃtīṃ—ānāmikābhyāṃ namaḥ | oṃ padmesthitāṃ padmavarṇāṃ-kaniṣṭhikābhyāṃ nama‖ | tāmihopahvaye śriyaṃ—karatalakarapṛṣṭābhyāṃ namaḥ | oṃ kāṃsoskritāṃ— hṛdayāya namaḥ | oṃ hiraṇyaprakārāṃ—śirase svāhā | oṃ ādrrāṃ jvalatīṃ-śikhāykè vaṣaṭ | oṃ tṛptāṃ tarpayaṃtīṃ — kavacāya huṃ | oṃ padme sthitāṃ padmavarṇāṃ— netratrayāya nauṣaṭ | oṃ tāmihopahvaye śriyaṃ—āstrāya phaṭ ‖*) भूर्भुवस्सुवरोमिति दिग्बंधः ॥ ध्यानं । या सा पद्मासनस्था विपुलकटितटी पद्मपत्रायताक्षी गंभीरावर्तनाभिस्तनभरनमिता शुभ्रवस्त्रोत्तरीया । लक्ष्मीर्दिव्यैर्गजेंद्रॆर्मणिगणखचितैः स्नापिता हेमकुंभैर्नित्यं सा पद्महस्ता मम वसतु गृहे सर्वमांगल्ययुक्ता ॥ (*bhūrbhuvassuvaromiti digbaṃdhaḥ ‖ dhyānaṃ | yā sā padmāsanasthā vipulakaṭitaṭī padmapatrāyatākṣī gaṃbhīrāvartanābhistanabharanamitā śubhravastrottarīyā | lakṣmīrdivyairgajeṃdrèrmaṇigaṇakhacitaiḥ snāpitā hemakuṃbhairnityaṃ sā padmahastā mama vasatu gṛhe sarvamāṃgalyayuktā ‖*)

ओं कांसोस्मितां हिरण्यप्राकारामाद्रां ज्वलंतीं तृप्तां तर्पयंतीं । पद्मे स्थितां पद्मवर्णां तामिहोपह्वये त्रियं ॥ (*oṃ kāṃsosmitāṃ hiraṇyaprākārāmādrāṃ jvalaṃtīṃ tṛptāṃ tarpayaṃtīṃ | padme sthitāṃ padmavarṇāṃ tāmihopahvaye triyaṃ ‖*)

कां वाङ्मनसोरगोचरां दुर्निरूपस्वरूपामित्यर्थः ब्रह्मरूपां वा “को हि ते नाम प्रजापते” इति श्रुत्यंतरात् “क इति ब्रह्मणो नाम” इति पुराणाच्च । सोस्मितां आ ईक्षत् उत् उद्धतं यत् स्मितं हासः तेन सहितां । उदंत्यलोपश्रांदसः । हिरण्यप्राकारां हिरण्यस्य प्राकारो वर्णः प्रकृष्णा आकृतिर्वा यस्यास्तां । आद्र्रा० क्लिन्नां—क्षीरोदधेरुत्पन्नत्वात् । आद्र्रान्क्षत्रोत्पन्नां रुद्ररूपां वा । रुद्रशब्दोऽत्र मूर्धन्यस्वरादिः—“आद्र्र्या रुद्रः प्रथमान एति” इत्यादौ तथादर्शनात् । अस्यबाहुलकं । ज्वलंतीं प्रकाशमानां । तृप्तां पूर्णकामां । अपि च तर्पयंतीं भक्तान् मनोरथैरिति शेषः । पद्मे स्थितां कमले आसीनां । पद्मवर्णां कमलवदच्छायच्छविं । तां प्रसिद्धां श्रियं । उपह्वये आह्वये ॥ (*kāṃ vāṅmanasoragocarāṃ durnirūpasvarūpāmityarthaḥ brahmarūpāṃ vā “ko hi te nāma prajāpate” iti śrutyaṃtarāt “ka iti brahmaṇo nāma” iti purāṇācca | sosmitāṃ ā īkṣat ut uddhataṃ yat smitaṃ hāsaḥ tena sahitāṃ | udaṃtyalopaśrāṃdasaḥ | hiraṇyaprākārāṃ hiraṇyasya prākāro varṇaḥ prakṛṣṇā ākṛtirvā yasyāstāṃ | ādrrā0 klinnāṃ—kṣīrodadherutpannatvāt | ādrrānkṣatrotpannāṃ rudrarūpāṃ vā | rudraśabdo 'tra mūrdhanyasvarādiḥ—“ādrryā rudraḥ prathamāna eti” ityādau tathādarśanāt | asyabāhulakaṃ | jvalaṃtīṃ prakāśamānāṃ | tṛptāṃ pūrṇakāmāṃ | api ca tarpayaṃtīṃ bhaktān manorathairiti śeṣaḥ | padme sthitāṃ kamale āsīnāṃ | padmavarṇāṃ kamalavadacchāyacchaviṃ | tāṃ prasiddhāṃ śriyaṃ | upahvaye āhvaye ‖*)

ऋचं चतुर्थीं श्रीसूक्ते प्रजपेदष्टलक्षकं । सहस्रं प्रत्यहं जप्त्वा त्रिसाहस्रं भृगोर्दिने ॥ राकायां पंचसाहस्रं क्षीराहारो जितेंद्रियः । पलाशसमिधा होमः पयसा गोघृतेन च ॥ तर्पणाशीतिसाहस्रं होमश्चाष्ट हस्रकः । ब्राह्मणाष्टशती पूज्या श्रीवाग्बीजयुतं न्यसेस् ॥ संपत्सारस्वतप्राप्तिर्भविष्यति न सं यः । आपंचपूरुषं सिद्धौ नात्र कार्या- विचारणा । (*ṛcaṃ caturthīṃ śrīsūkte prajapedaṣṭalakṣakaṃ | sahasraṃ pratyahaṃ japtvā trisāhasraṃ bhṛgordine ‖ rākāyāṃ paṃcasāhasraṃ kṣīrāhāro jiteṃdriyaḥ | palāśasamidhā homaḥ payasā goghṛtena ca ‖ tarpaṇāśītisāhasraṃ homaścāṣṭa hasrakaḥ | brāhmaṇāṣṭaśatī pūjyā śrīvāgbījayutaṃ nyases ‖ saṃpatsārasvataprāptirbhaviṣyati na saṃ yaḥ | āpaṃcapūruṣaṃ siddhau nātra kāryā- vicāraṇā |*)

श्रीं ऐमिति सपल्लवन्यासः ॥ ध्यान — वरदाभयशुकपुस्तककरकलितां कमलमध्यगां कलये । कमलां सस्मितवदनां कनकावर्णस्थितां कांचित् । (*śrīṃ aimiti sapallavanyāsaḥ ‖ dhyāna — varadābhayaśukapustakakarakalitāṃ kamalamadhyagāṃ kalaye | kamalāṃ sasmitavadanāṃ kanakāvarṇasthitāṃ kāṃcit |*)
The fourth Ṛk of this sūkta, कां सोस्मितां (*kāṃ sosmitāṃ*), is to be recited every day, one thousand each time, on Fridays three thousand each time, and on the full-moon day fifteen thousand

each time, so that in all eight lakhs of recitations are made. On the days of recitation one must recite while living on milk alone, with the senses controlled. Eight thousand oblations are to be made in the fire, with the mantra, with the oblation-materials palāśa-sticks, milk and cow's ghee. Eighty thousand libations (tarpaṇa) are to be made. At the time of the recitation the nyāsa is to be made together with the seed-syllables śrī and vāk. One hundred and eight Brahmins are to be satisfied with worship and the like. If this is done, success in the mantra and abundance of wealth result; of this there is no doubt. The nyāsa is made together with the seed-syllables श्रीं ऐं (*śrīṃ aiṃ*), and meditation is made with the verse वरदाभयशुकपुस्तककरकलितां कमलमध्यगां कलये । कमलां सस्मित वदनां कनकावरणस्थितां कांचित् । (*varadābhayaśukapustakakarakalitāṃ kamalamadhyagāṃ kalaye | kamalāṃ sasmita vadanāṃ kanakāvaraṇasthitāṃ kāṃcit |*) That is: this goddess Śrī, in her four hands, bears in order the gestures called the boon-giving hand and the fearless hand, and a parrot and a book, and is seated in the middle of a lotus. "I meditate on this goddess Śrī, who shines with a bodily lustre of the colour of gold and is accompanied by a gentle smile": such is the main sense of this verse.

O Maruts, your sound (स्वनः (*svanaḥ*)), produced by speed, is not to shake (रेजयत् (*rejayat*)), that is, not to make tremble, me, Evayāmarut; the accusative ending is dropped by the rule on case endings. The sound is then qualified.

The sound is अमवान् (*amavān*), strong; वृषा (*vṛṣā*), a giver of rain; वृष्टेष्टो दीपो (*vṛṣṭeṣṭo dīpo*) ⟨NOTE:162⟩; ययिः (*yayiḥ*), going; तविषः (*taviṣaḥ*), grown great. By this sound, joined together and overcoming your enemies, you ऋंजत (*ṛṃjata*), that is, you accomplish; the imperative is used in the sense of the present. What are you like? स्वरोचिषः (*svarociṣaḥ*), having rays under your own control; स्थारश्मानः (*sthāraśmānaḥ*), having steady rays; हिरण्ययाः (*hiraṇyayāḥ*), having golden ornaments; स्वायुधासः (*svāyudhāsaḥ*), having weapons under your own control; इष्मिणः (*iṣmiṇaḥ*), having food, or having going.

The insertion of the word अहं (*ahaṃ*) here is an error of the copyists. चंद्रां (*caṃdrāṃ*) is one shining like the moon; प्रभासां (*prabhāsāṃ*) is she who has excellent radiance (the feminine affix being by the rule आपं चेत्याप् (*āpaṃ cetyāp*)). यशसा ज्वलंतीं (*yaśasā jvalaṃtīṃ*) is one shining with fame; देवजुष्टां (*devajuṣṭāṃ*) is one served by gods such as Indra, or pleasing to them; उदारां (*udārāṃ*) is bold or generous; पद्मिनीं (*padminīṃ*) is of the form of a lotus-creeper or of a lotus. The particle ईं (*īṃ*) is without meaning, on the authority of Yāska's statement मिताक्षरेष्वनर्थकः किमीमिद्विति (*mitākṣareṣvanarthakaḥ kimīmidviti*); or else it denotes the syllable ī (Śrī). That Śrī, the protectress in this world, I take as my refuge. Therefore, O Śrī, may my misfortune be destroyed; I choose you as my refuge.

चंद्रां संतोषकारिणीं प्रभासां प्रकर्षण भास्वतीं । लोके लोकेषु चतुर्दशसु । यशसा ज्वलंतीमैश्वर्यसंपदौदार्यादिप्रयुक्तकीर्त्या प्रकाशमानां । आत एव देवजुष्टामिंद्रादिसेवितां । उदारां विस्तारां सर्वव्यापिनीमित्यर्थः । पद्मिनीं करधृतकमलामिति यावत् । ईं ईकारवाच्यां तादृशीं श्रियमहं शरणं प्रपद्ये रक्षकी भवेति व्रजामि । मे मम अलक्ष्मीर्या सा नश्यतां नाशं प्राप्नोतु । त्वां लक्ष्मीमहं वृणे मदाश्रितज्येष्ठानिस्सारणाय त्वां प्रति वरणं करिष्ये । (*caṃdrāṃ saṃtoṣakāriṇīṃ prabhāsāṃ prakarṣaṇa bhāsvatīṃ | loke lokeṣu caturdaśasu | yaśasā jvalaṃtīmaiśvaryasaṃpadaudāryādiprayuktakīrtyā prakāśamānāṃ | āta eva devajuṣṭāmiṃdrādisevitāṃ | udārāṃ vistārāṃ sarvavyāpinīmityarthaḥ | padminīṃ karadhṛtakamalāmiti yāvat | īṃ īkāravācyāṃ tādṛśīṃ śriyamahaṃ śaraṇaṃ prapadye rakṣakī bhaveti vrajāmi | me mama alakṣmīryā sā naśyatāṃ nāśaṃ prāpnotu | tvāṃ lakṣmīmahaṃ vṛṇe madāśritajyeṣṭhānissāraṇāya tvāṃ prati varaṇaṃ kariṣye |*) नात्राहंशब्दः प्रक्षिप्तः—“सार्वदेशिकशिष्टपाठसंप्रतिपत्ते” रित्यात्तरीयाः । दाक्षिणात्यपाठे तददर्शनात्पृक्षिप्त एव ॥ (*nātrāhaṃśabdaḥ prakṣiptaḥ—“sārvadeśikaśiṣṭapāṭhasaṃpratipatte” rityāttarīyāḥ | dākṣiṇātyapāṭhe tadadarśanātpṛkṣipta eva ‖*)

चंद्रां (*caṃdrāṃ*) is she who gives delight; प्रभासां (*prabhāsāṃ*) is greatly shining; लोके (*loke*) means in the fourteen worlds; यशसा ज्वलंतीं (*yaśasā jvalaṃtīṃ*) is one shining with fame arising from lordship, wealth, generosity and the like; therefore देवजुष्टां (*devajuṣṭāṃ*) is served by Indra and the others; उदारां (*udārāṃ*) is extended, all-pervading; पद्मिनीं (*padminīṃ*) is one holding a lotus in her hand; ईं (*īṃ*) denotes the syllable ī, so such a Śrī I approach as refuge, that she may become my protector. May whatever misfortune is mine be destroyed; I choose you, Lakṣmī, in order to drive out the misfortune that clings to me. Some say the word अहं (*ahaṃ*) has not been inserted here, on the authority of the agreement of the texts of all regions; since it is not seen in the southern reading it was interpolated.
notes: ಅಜೇಷು printed; pada-pāṭha has ಅಜ್ಮೇಷು

en: - स्वरोचिषः (*svarociṣaḥ*)—having radiance under your own control
- इष्मिणः (*iṣmiṇaḥ*)—having food, you who are such
- न रेजयत् (*na rejayat*)—may it not alarm
- चंद्रां (*caṃdrāṃ*)—she who has a lustre like the moon
- प्रभासां (*prabhāsāṃ*)—she who shines with excellent bodily lustre
- यशसा (*yaśasā*)—by fame, that is, by the fame arising from qualities such as lordship, wealth and generosity
- ज्वलंती (*jvalaṃtī*)—she who is famed or shining
- देवजुष्टां (*devajuṣṭāṃ*)—she who is served by gods such as Indra
- उदारां (*udārāṃ*)—she who gives boons and the like abundantly to devotees, or who is widely extended, pervading everywhere
- पद्मिनीं (*padminīṃ*)—she who bears lotuses in her hands, or who has a body swaying like a lotus-creeper, or who has a bodily form as delightful to the eye as a lotus
- तां ईं श्रियं (*tāṃ īṃ śriyaṃ*)—that same famed goddess Śrī
- शरणं प्रपद्ये (*śaraṇaṃ prapadye*)—I take refuge, that is, I resort to her for protection (by the grace of this goddess)
- नश्यतां (*naśyatāṃ*)—may they be destroyed (O goddess, I)
- वृणे (*vṛṇe*)—I pray and call, for my protection

O Maruts, you who have radiance under your own control, steady rays, ornaments made of gold, weapons of your own and food: may that sound of yours, by which you, facing the enemies, adorn the world, powerful, rain-producing, radiant, moving, grown great, not alarm me, Evayāmarut.
Note—These mantras are ordinarily used as the principal oblation mantras in the marriage homa.

1. (1) May Agni, first of all the gods, come here. Having come, may that Agni protect and guard the offspring of this woman, that is, her child, from the fear of death. May Varuṇa, the lord, also approve this. That is to say: may Agni and Varuṇa grant that this woman may suffer no kind of distress on account of her son and so may not weep on that account.

(2) May this Gārhapatya fire (the fire established in the house for the principal marriage homa) guard this bride well. And may it make the child that this maiden will bear long-lived and protect it. May this woman's lap never be empty; that is, may she always keep a child on her lap, and may her children live. May this woman, as a mother, fully enjoy the delight that comes from her son.

(3) O maiden, in your house, by night (and by day too), let there be no lamentation, that is, no weeping and wailing from grief. May all sorrows, beginning with weeping, go far away to another place. May evil acts such as tearing the hair in grief, lamenting and beating the breast not take place. May you suffer neither separation from your husband nor separation from your sons. May you live long in the house with your husband and rejoice, seeing your children playing happily.

(4) O woman, childlessness, or the death of a child after its birth, or sorrow, and the other kinds of distress that are the fruit of sinful deeds: all these I (Agni) remove, as one takes off from the neck a faded garland of flowers, and so I protect you.

(5) O woman, I (Agni) will destroy the sin and the sorrow that may arise from divine effort, from a Brahmin's curse, or from any other cause. I will strike down and destroy the piśāca and other seizing spirits, the yakṣas, rākṣasas and the like, and untimely death, which torment the child in your womb. May your sons be long-lived and live for a long time.

The Śrī-sūkta is among the appendix mantras (pariśiṣṭa) that are to be recited at the end of the fifth maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā. Since it is the custom to recite this sūkta daily in abhiṣeka, worship, pārāyaṇa and similar rites, it is a matter known to all that it is of use to everyone. Therefore this Śrī-sūkta is written here together with the necessary bhāṣya, explanation, special matters and other details. Although there are many bhāṣyas on this sūkta, of them the Śrī-Vidyāraṇya-bhāṣya and the Pṛthvīdharācārya-bhāṣya are the chief. Therefore, following these two bhāṣyas, there have been added for every mantra the word-meaning, the purport, special matters such as the fruit of recitation (phalaśruti) found in other works, the seer, deity and metre for each mantra, for the use of those who recite it, the aṅganyāsa, karanyāsa, the meditation verse and other useful matters. As stated in the phalaśruti of this sūkta: श्रियः पंचदशर्चं च श्रीकामः सततं जपेत् (*śriyaḥ paṃcadaśarcaṃ ca śrīkāmaḥ satataṃ japet*). In this sūkta there are only fifteen Ṛks. The sixteenth describes the fruit of reciting this sūkta. The mantras recited after that are in the form of ślokas and describe the qualities and greatness of the Goddess. There is no bhāṣya on these. Since it is the custom to recite them, only their main purport is explained, all of them.
वेदार्थस्य प्रकाशेन तमोहार्दं निवारयन् । पुमर्थांश्च तुरो देयाद्विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरः ॥ (*vedārthasya prakāśena tamohārdaṃ nivārayan | pumarthāṃśca turo deyādvidyātīrthamaheśvaraḥ ‖*)
Seers: आनंद, कर्दम, श्रीद, चिक्लीताः, श्रीपुत्राः (*ānaṃda, kardama, śrīda, ciklītāḥ, śrīputrāḥ*).
Metre: अनुष्टुप् । ४. बृहती । ५-६. त्रिष्टुप् । १५. प्रस्तारपंक्तिः (*anuṣṭup | 4. bṛhatī | 5-6. triṣṭup | 15. prastārapaṃktiḥ*).

ओं हिरण्यवर्णामिति पंचदशर्चस्य सूक्तस्य श्री आनंदकर्दमचिक्लीतेंदिरा ऋषयः । श्रीरग्निर्देवता । आद्यास्ति स्रोऽनुष्टुभः । चतुर्थी बृहती । पंचमीषष्टौ त्रिष्टुभौ । ततोऽष्टावनुष्टुभः । अंत्या प्रस्तारपंक्तिः ॥ हिरण्यवर्णामिति बीजं । तां म आ वह जातवेद इति शक्तिः । कीर्तिमृद्धिं ददातु म इति कीलकं ॥ मम श्रीमहालक्ष्मीप्रसादसिद्ध्यर्थे जपे विनियोगः ॥ (*oṃ hiraṇyavarṇāmiti paṃcadaśarcasya sūktasya śrī ānaṃdakardamaciklīteṃdirā ṛṣayaḥ | śrīragnirdevatā | ādyāsti sro 'nuṣṭubhaḥ | caturthī bṛhatī | paṃcamīṣaṣṭau triṣṭubhau | tato 'ṣṭāvanuṣṭubhaḥ | aṃtyā prastārapaṃktiḥ ‖ hiraṇyavarṇāmiti bījaṃ | tāṃ ma ā vaha jātaveda iti śaktiḥ | kīrtimṛddhiṃ dadātu ma iti kīlakaṃ ‖ mama śrīmahālakṣmīprasādasiddhyarthe jape viniyogaḥ ‖*)

- Head: ओं हिरण्यवर्णां हरिणीं सुवर्णरजतस्रजां । चंद्रां हिरण्मयां लक्ष्मीं जातवेदो म आ वह—शिरसि ॥ (*oṃ hiraṇyavarṇāṃ hariṇīṃ suvarṇarajatasrajāṃ | caṃdrāṃ hiraṇmayāṃ lakṣmīṃ jātavedo ma ā vaha—śirasi ‖*)

- Eyes: ओं तां म आ वह जातवेदो लक्ष्मीमनपगामिनीं । यस्यां हिरण्यं विंदेयं गामश्वं पुरुषानहं—नेत्रयोः ॥ (*oṃ tāṃ ma ā vaha jātavedo lakṣmīmanapagāminīṃ | yasyāṃ hiraṇyaṃ viṃdeyaṃ gāmaśvaṃ puruṣānahaṃ—netrayoḥ ‖*)

- Ears: ओं अश्वपूर्णां रथमध्यां हस्तिनादप्रमोदिनीं । श्रियं देवीमुप ह्वये श्रीर्मा देवी जुषतां—कर्णयोः ॥ (*oṃ aśvapūrṇāṃ rathamadhyāṃ hastinādapramodinīṃ | śriyaṃ devīmupa hvaye śrīrmā devī juṣatāṃ—karṇayoḥ ‖*)

- Nose: ओं कांसोस्मितां हिरण्यपाकारामाद्र्रां ज्वलंतीं तृप्तां तर्पयंतीं । पद्मे स्थितां पद्मवर्णां तामिहोप ह्वये श्रियं—नासिकायां । (*oṃ kāṃsosmitāṃ hiraṇyapākārāmādrrāṃ jvalaṃtīṃ tṛptāṃ tarpayaṃtīṃ | padme sthitāṃ padmavarṇāṃ tāmihopa hvaye śriyaṃ—nāsikāyāṃ |*)

- Mouth: ओं ओं चंद्रां प्रभासां यशसा ज्वलंतीं श्रियं लोके देवजुष्टामुदारां ! तां पद्मिनीमिां शरणमहं प्रपद्येऽलक्ष्मीर्मे नश्यतां त्वां वृषे— मुखे॥ (*oṃ oṃ caṃdrāṃ prabhāsāṃ yaśasā jvalaṃtīṃ śriyaṃ loke devajuṣṭāmudārāṃ ! tāṃ padminīmiāṃ śaraṇamahaṃ prapadye 'lakṣmīrme naśyatāṃ tvāṃ vṛṣe— mukhe‖*)

- Throat: ओं आदित्यवर्णॆ तपसोऽधि जातो वनस्पतिस्थव वृक्षोऽथ बिल्वः । तस्य फलानि तपसा नुदंतु मायां तरा याश्च बाह्या अलक्ष्मीः—कंठे ॥ (*oṃ ādityavarṇè tapaso 'dhi jāto vanaspatisthava vṛkṣo 'tha bilvaḥ | tasya phalāni tapasā nudaṃtu māyāṃ tarā yāśca bāhyā alakṣmīḥ—kaṃṭhe ‖*)

- Arms: ओं उषैतु मां देवसखि कीर्तिश्च मणीना सह । प्रादुर्भूतोऽस्मि राष्ट्रेऽस्मिन् कीर्तिमृद्धिं ददातु मे—बाह्वोः ॥ (*oṃ uṣaitu māṃ devasakhi kīrtiśca maṇīnā saha | prādurbhūto 'smi rāṣṭre 'smin kīrtimṛddhiṃ dadātu me—bāhvoḥ ‖*)

- Heart: ओं क्षुत्पिपासामलां जेष्ठामलक्ष्मीं नाशयाम्यहं । अभूतिमसमृद्धिं च सर्वां निर्णुद मे गृहात्—हृदये ॥ (*oṃ kṣutpipāsāmalāṃ jeṣṭhāmalakṣmīṃ nāśayāmyahaṃ | abhūtimasamṛddhiṃ ca sarvāṃ nirṇuda me gṛhāt—hṛdaye ‖*)

- Navel: ओं गंधद्वारां दुराधर्षां नित्यपुष्टां करीषिणीं । ईश्वरीं सर्वभूतानां तामिहोप ह्वये श्रियं—नाभौ ॥ (*oṃ gaṃdhadvārāṃ durādharṣāṃ nityapuṣṭāṃ karīṣiṇīṃ | īśvarīṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ tāmihopa hvaye śriyaṃ—nābhau ‖*)

- Secret part: ओं मनसः काममाकूतिं वाचः सत्यमशीमहि । पशूनां रूपमन्नस्य मयि श्रीः श्रयतां यशः—गुह्ये ॥ (*oṃ manasaḥ kāmamākūtiṃ vācaḥ satyamaśīmahi | paśūnāṃ rūpamannasya mayi śrīḥ śrayatāṃ yaśaḥ—guhye ‖*)
- Feet: ओं कर्दमेन प्रजा भूता मयि संभव कर्दम । श्रियं वासय मे कुले मातरं पद्ममालिनीं—पादौ ॥ (*oṃ kardamena prajā bhūtā mayi saṃbhava kardama | śriyaṃ vāsaya me kule mātaraṃ padmamālinīṃ—pādau ‖*)

- Thighs: ओं आपः सृजंतु स्निग्धानि चिक्लीत वस मे गृहे । नि च देवीं मातरं श्रियं वासय मे कुले—ऊर्वोः ॥ (*oṃ āpaḥ sṛjaṃtu snigdhāni ciklīta vasa me gṛhe | ni ca devīṃ mātaraṃ śriyaṃ vāsaya me kule—ūrvoḥ ‖*)

- Knees: ओं आद्र्रा० पुष्करिणीं पुष्टिं पिंगलां पद्ममालिनीं । चंद्रां हिरण्मयीं लक्ष्मीं जातवेदो म आ वह—जान्वोः ॥ (*oṃ ādrrā0 puṣkariṇīṃ puṣṭiṃ piṃgalāṃ padmamālinīṃ | caṃdrāṃ hiraṇmayīṃ lakṣmīṃ jātavedo ma ā vaha—jānvoḥ ‖*)

- Shanks: ओं आद्र्रां यः करिणीं यष्टिं सुवर्णां हेममालिनीं । सूर्यां हिरण्मयीं लक्ष्मीं जातवेदो म आ वह-जंघयोः ॥ (*oṃ ādrrāṃ yaḥ kariṇīṃ yaṣṭiṃ suvarṇāṃ hemamālinīṃ | sūryāṃ hiraṇmayīṃ lakṣmīṃ jātavedo ma ā vaha-jaṃghayoḥ ‖*)

- Feet: ओं तां म आ वह जातवेदो लक्ष्मीमनपगामिनीं । यस्यां हिरण्यं प्रभूतं गावो दास्योऽश्वान्विंदेयं पुरुषानहं—॥ पादयोः ॥ (*oṃ tāṃ ma ā vaha jātavedo lakṣmīmanapagāminīṃ | yasyāṃ hiraṇyaṃ prabhūtaṃ gāvo dāsyo 'śvānviṃdeyaṃ puruṣānahaṃ—‖ pādayoḥ ‖*)

ओं नमो भगवत्यै, मताक्षत्रै भगवत्यै महालक्ष्मी हैरण्यवर्णायै—अंगुष्ठाभ्यां नमः । ,, ,, हरिण्यै—तर्जनीभ्यां नमः । ,, ,, सुवर्णरजतस्रजाय्कॆ—मध्यमाभ्यां नमः । ,, ,, चंद्रायै—अनामिकाभ्यां नमः । ,, ,, हिरण्मय्कॆ—कनिष्ठिकाभ्यां नमः । ,, ,, लक्ष्मी—करतलकरपृष्ठाभ्यां नमः । ,, ,, हिरण्यवर्णायै—हृदयाय नमः । ,, ,, हरिण्यै—शिरसे स्वाहा । ,, ,, सुवर्णरजतस्रजाय्कॆ—शिखाय्कॆ वषट् । ,, ,, चंद्रायै—कवचाय हुं । ,, ,, हिरण्मय्कॆ—नेत्रत्रयाय वौषट् । ,, ,, लक्ष्मी—अस्त्राय फट् । (*oṃ namo bhagavatyai, matākṣatrai bhagavatyai mahālakṣmī hairaṇyavarṇāyai—aṃguṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ | ,, ,, hariṇyai—tarjanībhyāṃ namaḥ | ,, ,, suvarṇarajatasrajāykè—madhyamābhyāṃ namaḥ | ,, ,, caṃdrāyai—anāmikābhyāṃ namaḥ | ,, ,, hiraṇmaykè—kaniṣṭhikābhyāṃ namaḥ | ,, ,, lakṣmī—karatalakarapṛṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ | ,, ,, hiraṇyavarṇāyai—hṛdayāya namaḥ | ,, ,, hariṇyai—śirase svāhā | ,, ,, suvarṇarajatasrajāykè—śikhāykè vaṣaṭ | ,, ,, caṃdrāyai—kavacāya huṃ | ,, ,, hiraṇmaykè—netratrayāya vauṣaṭ | ,, ,, lakṣmī—astrāya phaṭ |*)

अरुणकमलसंस्था तद्रजःपुंजवर्णा करकमलधृतेष्टाभीतियुग्मांबुजाता । मणिमुकुटविचित्रालंकृतिः पद्ममाला भवतु भुवनमाता संततं श्रीः श्रियै नः ॥ (*aruṇakamalasaṃsthā tadrajaḥpuṃjavarṇā karakamaladhṛteṣṭābhītiyugmāṃbujātā | maṇimukuṭavicitrālaṃkṛtiḥ padmamālā bhavatu bhuvanamātā saṃtataṃ śrīḥ śriyai naḥ ‖*)
कमलं कलशं धेनुं ज्ञानमंजलिमेव च । पंच मुद्राः प्रदर्श्याथ श्रीसूक्तं प्रजपेद्बुधः ॥ (*kamalaṃ kalaśaṃ dhenuṃ jñānamaṃjalimeva ca | paṃca mudrāḥ pradarśyātha śrīsūktaṃ prajapedbudhaḥ ‖*)

This Goddess Śrī is seated on a red lotus flower. Like that same red lotus she shines with a bright radiance of the kind that is desired of a deity. In two of her hands she bears the signs of granting wishes and of giving freedom from fear, and in the other two hands lotus flowers. She wears a crown made of many kinds of jewels and a garland of lotus flowers. She is resplendent with many kinds of wondrous ornaments. May such a Goddess Śrī, the mother of all the worlds, always bring us increase of wealth and be graciously disposed towards us.
Having meditated in this way and having shown the five mudrās called lotus, pitcher, cow, knowledge and añjali, the wise man should then recite this Śrī-sūkta.
यस्यां हिरण्यं प्रभूतं गावो दास्योऽश्वान् विंदेयं पुरुषानहं ॥ १५ ॥ (*yasyāṃ hiraṇyaṃ prabhūtaṃ gāvo dāsyo 'śvān viṃdeyaṃ puruṣānahaṃ ‖ 15 ‖*)
[These fifteen Ṛks are to be recited according to one's ability. Since these Ṛks are explained separately at the time of the explanation of meaning, all of them are to be put together and recited.]
सूक्तस्यैव विधिः प्रोक्तं प्रत्येकं च वदाम्यहं ॥ (*sūktasyaiva vidhiḥ proktaṃ pratyekaṃ ca vadāmyahaṃ ‖*)

The procedure for reciting the sūkta as a whole has been stated above. Now the procedure for reciting each Ṛk separately will be described, together with its aṅganyāsa, meditation, explanation of meaning, phalaśruti and other matters.

अस्य श्रीसूक्तस्थ प्रथम ऋङ्ममहामंत्रस्य । जातवेद ऋषिः । अनुष्टुप् छंदः । सर्वसौभाग्यदायिनी श्री महालक्ष्मीर्देवता । हिरण्यवर्णामिति बीजं । स्वाहा शक्तिः । श्रीं ह्रीं क्लीं कीलकं (अथवा श्रीं बीजं । ह्रीं शक्तिः । क्लीं कीलकं इति पाठांतरं) श्रीसूक्त प्रथम ऋङ्ममहामंत्रप्रसादसिद्ध्यर्थे जपे विनियोगः । ओं हिरण्यवर्णां-अंगुष्ठाभ्यां नमः । (*asya śrīsūktastha prathama ṛṅmamahāmaṃtrasya | jātaveda ṛṣiḥ | anuṣṭup chaṃdaḥ | sarvasaubhāgyadāyinī śrī mahālakṣmīrdevatā | hiraṇyavarṇāmiti bījaṃ | svāhā śaktiḥ | śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ kīlakaṃ (athavā śrīṃ bījaṃ | hrīṃ śaktiḥ | klīṃ kīlakaṃ iti pāṭhāṃtaraṃ) śrīsūkta prathama ṛṅmamahāmaṃtraprasādasiddhyarthe jape viniyogaḥ | oṃ hiraṇyavarṇāṃ-aṃguṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ |*)

अथ ध्यानं ॥ कांत्या कांचनसंनिभां हरगिरिप्रख्यैश्चतुर्भिर्गजैर्हस्तक्षिप्तहिरण्मयामृतघटैरासिच्यमानां श्रियं । नानारत्नसमुज्ज्वलां करलसत्पद्मां किरीटोज्ज्वलां क्षौमाबद्धनितंबबिंबलसितां वंदेऽरविंदस्थितां ॥ इति ध्यात्वा । निर्दिष्टसंख्यया जपं कृत्वा उत्तर न्यासं च कृत्वा देवै जपसमर्पणं कुर्यात् । (*atha dhyānaṃ ‖ kāṃtyā kāṃcanasaṃnibhāṃ haragiriprakhyaiścaturbhirgajairhastakṣiptahiraṇmayāmṛtaghaṭairāsicyamānāṃ śriyaṃ | nānāratnasamujjvalāṃ karalasatpadmāṃ kirīṭojjvalāṃ kṣaumābaddhanitaṃbabiṃbalasitāṃ vaṃde 'raviṃdasthitāṃ ‖ iti dhyātvā | nirdiṣṭasaṃkhyayā japaṃ kṛtvā uttara nyāsaṃ ca kṛtvā devai japasamarpaṇaṃ kuryāt |*)

अस्य श्री श्रीसूक्तपंचमयङ्महामंत्रस्य । आनंद ऋषिः । सर्वैश्वर्यप्रदायिनी श्रीमहालक्ष्मीर्देवता । त्रिष्टुप् छंदः । चं बीजं । णं शक्तिः । श्रीं कीलकं । सर्वदारिद्र्यनाशिनी श्रीमहालक्ष्मीप्रसादसिद्ध्यर्थे जपे विनियोगः । ओं ह्रां चंद्रां प्रभासां—अंग-ष्ठाभ्यां नमः। ओं ह्रीं यशसा ज्वलंतींशर्जनीभ्यां नमः । ओं हूं श्रियं लोके देवजुष्टामुदारां-मध्यमाभ्यांनमः । ओं हैं तां पद्मिनीमीं शरणमहं प्रपद्ये-अनामिकाभ्यां नमः । ओं ह्रौं अलक्ष्मीर्मे नश्यतां—कनिष्ठिकाभ्यां नमः । ओं ह्रः त्वां वृणे—करतलकरपृष्ठाभ्यां (*asya śrī śrīsūktapaṃcamayaṅmahāmaṃtrasya | ānaṃda ṛṣiḥ | sarvaiśvaryapradāyinī śrīmahālakṣmīrdevatā | triṣṭup chaṃdaḥ | caṃ bījaṃ | ṇaṃ śaktiḥ | śrīṃ kīlakaṃ | sarvadāridryanāśinī śrīmahālakṣmīprasādasiddhyarthe jape viniyogaḥ | oṃ hrāṃ caṃdrāṃ prabhāsāṃ—aṃga-ṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ| oṃ hrīṃ yaśasā jvalaṃtīṃśarjanībhyāṃ namaḥ | oṃ hūṃ śriyaṃ loke devajuṣṭāmudārāṃ-madhyamābhyāṃnamaḥ | oṃ haiṃ tāṃ padminīmīṃ śaraṇamahaṃ prapadye-anāmikābhyāṃ namaḥ | oṃ hrauṃ alakṣmīrme naśyatāṃ—kaniṣṭhikābhyāṃ namaḥ | oṃ hraḥ tvāṃ vṛṇe—karatalakarapṛṣṭhābhyāṃ*) ओं ह्रां चंद्रां प्रभासां—हृदयाय नमः । ओं ह्रीं यशसाज्वलंतीं—शिरसे स्वाहा । ओं हूं श्रियं लोके देवजुष्टामुदारां—शिखाय्कॆ वषट् । ओं हैं तां पद्मनीमीं शरणमहं प्रपद्ये-कवचाय हुं । ओं ह्रौं अलक्ष्मीर्मे नश्यतांनेत्रत्रयाय वौषट् । ओं ह्रः त्वां वृणे—अस्त्राय फट् । भूर्भुवस्सुवरोमिति दिग्बंधः ॥ ध्यानं ॥ तेजोमंडलमध्यगां द्विनयनां दिव्यांबरालंकृतां देवीं पद्मवराभयां करतलैश्चिंतामणिं बिभ्रतीं । नानादिव्यविभूषणां च भजतां दौर्भाग्यसंहारिणीं नानाभीष्टवरप्रदाननिरतां वंदे परां देवतां । (*oṃ hrāṃ caṃdrāṃ prabhāsāṃ—hṛdayāya namaḥ | oṃ hrīṃ yaśasājvalaṃtīṃ—śirase svāhā | oṃ hūṃ śriyaṃ loke devajuṣṭāmudārāṃ—śikhāykè vaṣaṭ | oṃ haiṃ tāṃ padmanīmīṃ śaraṇamahaṃ prapadye-kavacāya huṃ | oṃ hrauṃ alakṣmīrme naśyatāṃnetratrayāya vauṣaṭ | oṃ hraḥ tvāṃ vṛṇe—astrāya phaṭ | bhūrbhuvassuvaromiti digbaṃdhaḥ ‖ dhyānaṃ ‖ tejomaṃḍalamadhyagāṃ dvinayanāṃ divyāṃbarālaṃkṛtāṃ devīṃ padmavarābhayāṃ karatalaiściṃtāmaṇiṃ bibhratīṃ | nānādivyavibhūṣaṇāṃ ca bhajatāṃ daurbhāgyasaṃhāriṇīṃ nānābhīṣṭavarapradānaniratāṃ vaṃde parāṃ devatāṃ |*)

चंद्रां प्रभासां यशसा ज्वलंतीं श्रियं लोके देवजुष्टामुदारां । तां पद्मनीमां शरणमहं प्रपद्ये अलक्ष्मीर्मे नश्यतां त्वां वृणे ॥ (*caṃdrāṃ prabhāsāṃ yaśasā jvalaṃtīṃ śriyaṃ loke devajuṣṭāmudārāṃ | tāṃ padmanīmāṃ śaraṇamahaṃ prapadye alakṣmīrme naśyatāṃ tvāṃ vṛṇe ‖*)

आत्राहंशब्दप्रक्षेपः प्रामादिकः । चंद्रां चंद्रवत् प्रकाशमानां प्रभासां प्रकृष्टा भाः कांतियस्यास्त्यां । आपं चेत्याप् । यशसा कीर्त्या ज्वलंतीं प्रकाशमानां । देवजुष्टां देवैरिंद्राद्यैस्सेवितां प्रीतां वा । उदारां प्रगल्भां वा पद्मिनीं पद्मलतारूपां पद्माकारां वा । ईमितिनिपातः अनर्थकः— “मिताक्षरेष्वनर्थकः किमीमिद्विति” यास्कवचनात् । (*ātrāhaṃśabdaprakṣepaḥ prāmādikaḥ | caṃdrāṃ caṃdravat prakāśamānāṃ prabhāsāṃ prakṛṣṭā bhāḥ kāṃtiyasyāstyāṃ | āpaṃ cetyāp | yaśasā kīrtyā jvalaṃtīṃ prakāśamānāṃ | devajuṣṭāṃ devairiṃdrādyaissevitāṃ prītāṃ vā | udārāṃ pragalbhāṃ vā padminīṃ padmalatārūpāṃ padmākārāṃ vā | īmitinipātaḥ anarthakaḥ— “mitākṣareṣvanarthakaḥ kimīmidviti” yāskavacanāt |*) ईकारवाच्यां वा तां श्रियं लोके इहलोके शरणं रक्षित्रीं प्रपद्ये प्रपन्मोऽस्मि । अहमिति शेषः । अतः हे श्रीः मे मम अलक्ष्मीः आश्रीः नश्यतां नाशं प्राप्नोतु । त्वां वृणे शरणत्वेन कुर्वॆ ॥ (*īkāravācyāṃ vā tāṃ śriyaṃ loke ihaloke śaraṇaṃ rakṣitrīṃ prapadye prapanmo 'smi | ahamiti śeṣaḥ | ataḥ he śrīḥ me mama alakṣmīḥ āśrīḥ naśyatāṃ nāśaṃ prāpnotu | tvāṃ vṛṇe śaraṇatvena kurvè ‖*)

Let not the sound (of your approach, Maruts), which is mighty, the announcer of rain, the shedder of light, diffusive, loud, alarm Evayamarut: that sound wherewith,overcoming (your foes), you who are self-irradiating, lasting-rayed, ornamented with golden ornaments, self-weaponed, bestow-ing food, accomplish your functions

देवकृतं ब्राह्मणं कल्पमानं तेन हन्मि योनिषदः पिशाचान् । क्रव्यादो मृत्यूनधरान् पातयामि दीर्घमायुस्तव जीवंतु पुत्राः ॥ (*devakṛtaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ kalpamānaṃ tena hanmi yoniṣadaḥ piśācān | kravyādo mṛtyūnadharān pātayāmi dīrghamāyustava jīvaṃtu putrāḥ ‖*)

श्रीसूक्ते प्रथमे वर्गे प्रजपेत्संचमीमृचं । मायाबीजेन विन्यस्य भक्तितो भुवनेश्वरीं ॥ अक्षीणभासां चंद्राख्यां ज्वलंतीं यशसा श्रियं । देवैर्जुष्टामुदारां च पद्मिनीमां भजाम्यहं ॥ त्वां वृणे त्वत्पसादेन ममालक्ष्मीर्विनश्यतु । (*śrīsūkte prathame varge prajapetsaṃcamīmṛcaṃ | māyābījena vinyasya bhaktito bhuvaneśvarīṃ ‖ akṣīṇabhāsāṃ caṃdrākhyāṃ jvalaṃtīṃ yaśasā śriyaṃ | devairjuṣṭāmudārāṃ ca padminīmāṃ bhajāmyahaṃ ‖ tvāṃ vṛṇe tvatpasādena mamālakṣmīrvinaśyatu |*)

प्रत्यहं त्वेकसाहस्रं गोष्ठस्थः प्रजपेद्यचं ॥ अखंडदीपं प्रज्वाल्य गोघृतेन जितेंद्रियः । प्रत्यक्षरत्रिसाहस्रजपान्मुच्यत संकटैः ॥ मंडलैश्च त्रिभिः पूर्णैर्द्रारिद्रान्मुच्यते ध्रुवं । (*pratyahaṃ tvekasāhasraṃ goṣṭhasthaḥ prajapedyacaṃ ‖ akhaṃḍadīpaṃ prajvālya goghṛtena jiteṃdriyaḥ | pratyakṣaratrisāhasrajapānmucyata saṃkaṭaiḥ ‖ maṃḍalaiśca tribhiḥ pūrṇairdrāridrānmucyate dhruvaṃ |*)

दीक्षितश्च तिलैर्हुत्वा विरजामंगदेवतां ॥ आमिक्षाशी धनं प्राप्य भूमिस्थं राजवंदितः । संग्रामे विजयं प्राप्य चांद्रीं गतिमनाप्नुयात् ॥ अहस्सु प्रजपेत्सौरीं दक्षिणोत्तरमार्गगां । तिलैः श्वेतैस्सहाज्येन जुहुयात्पावके स्वके ॥ जपाद्दशांशं संतर्प्य गंधकर्पूरवारिभिः । होमं कृत्वा दशांशं च पूजयेच्च सुवासिनीः ॥ कमलैरर्चयेद्देवीं गोभ्यो घासं प्रदापयेत् । एतत्पुण्यप्रभावेण दरिद्रोऽपि धनी भवेत् ॥ (*dīkṣitaśca tilairhutvā virajāmaṃgadevatāṃ ‖ āmikṣāśī dhanaṃ prāpya bhūmisthaṃ rājavaṃditaḥ | saṃgrāme vijayaṃ prāpya cāṃdrīṃ gatimanāpnuyāt ‖ ahassu prajapetsaurīṃ dakṣiṇottaramārgagāṃ | tilaiḥ śvetaissahājyena juhuyātpāvake svake ‖ japāddaśāṃśaṃ saṃtarpya gaṃdhakarpūravāribhiḥ | homaṃ kṛtvā daśāṃśaṃ ca pūjayecca suvāsinīḥ ‖ kamalairarcayeddevīṃ gobhyo ghāsaṃ pradāpayet | etatpuṇyaprabhāveṇa daridro 'pi dhanī bhavet ‖*)

ह्रीमित्यादि षडंगन्यासः । ध्यानं— आकाशपद्माकरचंद्रबिंबप्लवोल्लसंतीं परिपूर्णकांतिं । पद्मस्थितां पद्मकरां प्रपद्ये लक्ष्मीलक्ष्मीविनिवृत्तयेऽहं ॥ (*hrīmityādi ṣaḍaṃganyāsaḥ | dhyānaṃ— ākāśapadmākaracaṃdrabiṃbaplavollasaṃtīṃ paripūrṇakāṃtiṃ | padmasthitāṃ padmakarāṃ prapadye lakṣmīlakṣmīvinivṛttaye 'haṃ ‖*)

This fifth Ṛk of the Śrī-sūkta is to be recited with the nyāsa made together with the māyā-bīja (hrīṃ), meditating with devotion on the goddess Śrī. That goddess shines always with an unfailing radiance. Like the moon, she is distinguished by a cool lustre and is delightful. Toward her devotees she is famed for the glory of generosity and the like, granting boons such as favour, the fulfilment of wishes and the removal of poverty and ill fortune. She is served by all the gods, Indra and the others. Seated on a lotus seat and holding lotuses in her hands, this goddess Śrī shines; "I worship her always, and I pray and call that goddess for the destruction of my misfortune and poverty and for her grace": so one should pray. Sitting in the cow-pen where cows are tied, or in some other pure place, with undistracted mind, one should recite every day one thousand each time. During the recitation one should put cow's ghee in lamps and keep them lit so that they do not go out. If three thousand are recited for each syllable of this Ṛk, one is freed from all troubles. If this Ṛk is recited without a break for three maṇḍalas (a maṇḍala being forty-eight days), poverty is surely removed. Having taken the dīkṣā, that is, having purified oneself and made the resolve, if one makes oblations in the fire with sesame, with this mantra, together with the goddess Virajā, the subordinate deity, one finds the hidden treasure laid in the earth; one is honoured by kings, is victorious in battle, and at the end attains the world of the moon. In the daytime one should recite meditating on the sun, who travels the southern and northern paths, and make oblations in the fire with white sesame and with clarified butter. A libation is to be made with water mixed with sandal and camphor, to the tenth part of the number of recitations. Then oblations are to be made to the tenth part of the number of libations, and married women (suvāsinī) are to be honoured. The goddess Śrī is to be worshipped with lotus flowers, and fodder such as grass is to be given to cows. By doing so, that is, by the power of the merit of this recitation and these oblations, however poor one may be, one becomes rich. At the time of the nyāsa of the mantra one makes the nyāsa together with the seed-syllable hrīṃ and meditates as in the verse given below.—माडबेकु.—आकाशपद्माकरचंद्रबिंबप्लवोल्लसंतीं परिपूर्णकांतिं । पद्मस्थितां पद्मकरां प्रपद्ये लक्ष्मीमलक्ष्मीविनिवृत्तयेऽहं ॥ (*māḍabeku.—ākāśapadmākaracaṃdrabiṃbaplavollasaṃtīṃ paripūrṇakāṃtiṃ | padmasthitāṃ padmakarāṃ prapadye lakṣmīmalakṣmīvinivṛttaye 'haṃ ‖*)
Here ends the explanation of the fifth Ṛk.

O Maruts, your greatness (महिमा (*mahimā*)) is boundless. O you of grown strength, may your bright, blazing strength protect me, Evayāmarut; the accusative ending is dropped. You are indeed those who stand, by fixity of station, in the sacrifice that has strong binding and regulation, on the occasion of sight (संदृशि (*saṃdṛśi*)). So protect us from the reviler, the enemy. You shine like fires.

The word वृक्षः (*vṛkṣaḥ*) with अथ (*atha*) is also so read, by the Vedic latitude. आदित्यवर्णे (*ādityavarṇe*) is the vocative of her whose colour is like the colour of the sun. O Śrī, by reason of your austerity (niyama) the वनस्पतिः (*vanaspatiḥ*) (as the Mānava text defines, trees that bear fruit without flowers are called vanaspati), the tree named bilva, arose from your hand, as is said in the Nāmana-purāṇa by Kātyāyana: "the bilva arose from Lakṣmī's hand." Then the ripe fruits of that bilva, by your grace, अंतरा (*aṃtarā*) the māyā (ignorance and its effects) connected with the inner senses, and the बाह्याः (*bāhyāḥ*) misfortunes connected with the outer senses, may they drive away and remove.

अथेत्यनंतरार्थः । हे आदित्यवर्णे सूर्यसमानकांते तपसः तपश्चर्यार्थं वनस्पतिः यो बिल्ववृक्षः तव निवासयोग्यः अधिजातः उत्पन्नः “ बिल्वाटव्यां महालक्ष्मीरूपास्ते बिल्वनायकमिति ” भार्गवपुराणात् । तस्य त्वत्करजातस्य बिल्ववृक्षस्य “ तनुमध्या स्वहस्तात्थं बिल्वद्रुं समुपाश्रितेति ” भार्गवतंत्रोक्तेश्व । प्रसूनादीनि फलानि मा मां प्रति अंतराः अंतर्गताः अलक्ष्मीः या बाह्याश्च अलक्ष्मीः ताः तव तव तपसा करणेन मदाश्रितान्तरगतबाह्यालक्ष्मीरूपदुर्गतीस्सर्वान् नुदंतित्याशयः ॥ (*athetyanaṃtarārthaḥ | he ādityavarṇe sūryasamānakāṃte tapasaḥ tapaścaryārthaṃ vanaspatiḥ yo bilvavṛkṣaḥ tava nivāsayogyaḥ adhijātaḥ utpannaḥ “ bilvāṭavyāṃ mahālakṣmīrūpāste bilvanāyakamiti ” bhārgavapurāṇāt | tasya tvatkarajātasya bilvavṛkṣasya “ tanumadhyā svahastātthaṃ bilvadruṃ samupāśriteti ” bhārgavataṃtrokteśva | prasūnādīni phalāni mā māṃ prati aṃtarāḥ aṃtargatāḥ alakṣmīḥ yā bāhyāśca alakṣmīḥ tāḥ tava tava tapasā karaṇena madāśritāntaragatabāhyālakṣmīrūpadurgatīssarvān nudaṃtityāśayaḥ ‖*)

अथ (*atha*) has the sense "afterwards." O sun-coloured one, for the sake of your austerity the bilva tree arose, suited to your dwelling, as is said in the Bhārgava-purāṇa and in the Bhārgava-tantra. May the fruits of that tree, born of your hand, by your austerity remove all the misfortunes, inner and outer, that cling to me, the evil states in the form of misfortune: such is the intention.
- वृद्धश्रवसः (*vṛddhaśravasaḥ*)—O Maruts, who have exceedingly great strength ⟨NOTE:163⟩
- प्रसित् (*prasit*)—in the sacrifice that has the form of a rule
- संदृशि (*saṃdṛśi*)—for the sake of the sight
- स्थातारो हि स्थान (*sthātāro hi sthāna*)—you must be present regularly
- आदित्यवर्णे (*ādityavarṇe*)—O goddess Śrī, whose bodily lustre shines brilliantly like the radiance of the sun
- वनस्पतिः (*vanaspatiḥ*)—the tree that bears fruit without flowers
- बिल्वः वृक्षः (*bilvaḥ vṛkṣaḥ*)—the tree called bilva
- बाह्याः च (*bāhyāḥ ca*)—and connected with the outer senses
- आलक्ष्मीः (*ālakṣmīḥ*)—sorrow, poverty, misfortune and the like

en: O Maruts, your power is endless. O Maruts of exceedingly great strength, may your shining strength protect me, Evayāmarut. In this sacrifice, which has the form of a rule, you must be present regularly for the sight.
Shining like fires, protect us from the enemies who revile.

O goddess Śrī, whose body shines with great radiance like the radiance of the sun, by your command (grace) the tree called bilva, which bears fruit only, without letting flowers appear, came into being. Then may the fruits of that bilva tree remove the ignorance lodged in the inner senses of human beings and the sorrow and poverty connected with the outer senses.

आदित्यवर्णे तरुणार्कवदरुणवर्णे । " अरुणां करुणातरंगिताक्षीमिति " बालारूपमत्र सूचितं भवति । वनस्पतिबिल्वो वृक्षः तव तपसोऽधिजातः । नीवातटीनीतटी बिल्वारण्यं त्वत्तपसो जातमिति भावः । (*ādityavarṇe taruṇārkavadaruṇavarṇe | " aruṇāṃ karuṇātaraṃgitākṣīmiti " bālārūpamatra sūcitaṃ bhavati | vanaspatibilvo vṛkṣaḥ tava tapaso 'dhijātaḥ | nīvātaṭīnītaṭī bilvāraṇyaṃ tvattapaso jātamiti bhāvaḥ |*) तनुमध्या पुरा बाला नीवातटमुपाश्रिता । बिल्वारण्ये तपश्चक्रे लक्ष्मीर्लोकहितार्थिनी ॥ (*tanumadhyā purā bālā nīvātaṭamupāśritā | bilvāraṇye tapaścakre lakṣmīrlokahitārthinī ‖*)

इति कालिकापुराणवचनात् । तस्य बिल्वस्य फलानि त्वत्तपसा सशक्तिकानि मा मयि स्थिताः अंतराः हृद्गताज्ञानपापादिरूपिण्यः बाह्याः दारिद्राद्रिरूपिण्यः याः दुर्गतयः शाः अलक्ष्मीः नुदंतु निरासयंतु । (*iti kālikāpurāṇavacanāt | tasya bilvasya phalāni tvattapasā saśaktikāni mā mayi sthitāḥ aṃtarāḥ hṛdgatājñānapāpādirūpiṇyaḥ bāhyāḥ dāridrādrirūpiṇyaḥ yāḥ durgatayaḥ śāḥ alakṣmīḥ nudaṃtu nirāsayaṃtu |*)
बिल्वनाथप्रियायास्तु नारायण्यास्तपोबलात् । बिल्वारण्यं फलत्यद्य लोकालक्ष्मीनिवृत्तये ॥ (*bilvanāthapriyāyāstu nārāyaṇyāstapobalāt | bilvāraṇyaṃ phalatyadya lokālakṣmīnivṛttaye ‖*)
इति ब्रह्मांडपुराणवचनात् । तत्रत्यबिल्वफलस्नानाशनादिकमलक्ष्मीपरिहारकं भवत्विति भावः ॥ (*iti brahmāṃḍapurāṇavacanāt | tatratyabilvaphalasnānāśanādikamalakṣmīparihārakaṃ bhavatviti bhāvaḥ ‖*)

द्वितीयवर्गे प्रथमामृचं जपेत्प्रेणाति बाला तरुणारुणश्रीः । यस्यास्तपोयोगबलेन बिल्वफलान्यलक्ष्मीं शमयंति नृणां ॥ (*dvitīyavarge prathamāmṛcaṃ japetpreṇāti bālā taruṇāruṇaśrīḥ | yasyāstapoyogabalena bilvaphalānyalakṣmīṃ śamayaṃti nṛṇāṃ ‖*)

तनुमध्यां महालक्ष्मीं बालां त्रिपुरसुंदरीं । त्रिबिल्वपत्रैस्संपूज्य सहस्रं प्रजपेद्यचं ॥ तिष्टुप् शिवाक्षरा यस्माच्चिवलक्षजपं चरेत् । बिल्वस्य हविषा होम आज्यहोमश्च शस्यते ॥ ऐश्वर्येणार्चयेद्देवीं बिल्वपत्रैर्हरिद्रया । रुद्रलक्षप्रदीपैश्च नीराजनविधिं चरेत् ॥ पक्वबिल्वफलाहारस्सतं नियतव्रतः । शांतिं कृत्वा विधानेन जगदंबाप्रसादतः ॥ अलक्ष्मीं परिभूयाथ महालक्ष्मीं स्थिरां लभेत् ॥ (*tanumadhyāṃ mahālakṣmīṃ bālāṃ tripurasuṃdarīṃ | tribilvapatraissaṃpūjya sahasraṃ prajapedyacaṃ ‖ tiṣṭup śivākṣarā yasmāccivalakṣajapaṃ caret | bilvasya haviṣā homa ājyahomaśca śasyate ‖ aiśvaryeṇārcayeddevīṃ bilvapatrairharidrayā | rudralakṣapradīpaiśca nīrājanavidhiṃ caret ‖ pakvabilvaphalāhārassataṃ niyatavrataḥ | śāṃtiṃ kṛtvā vidhānena jagadaṃbāprasādataḥ ‖ alakṣmīṃ paribhūyātha mahālakṣmīṃ sthirāṃ labhet ‖*)
ऐं क्लीं सौः ऐं ह्रीं श्रीं। इति बीजषट्केन अनुलोमविलोमपरिवर्तितेन षट्त्रिंशन्ना साः । ध्यानं— (*aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ| iti bījaṣaṭkena anulomavilomaparivartitena ṣaṭtriṃśannā sāḥ | dhyānaṃ—*)
उद्यदादित्यसंकाशां बिल्वकाननमध्यगां । शनुमध्यां श्रियं ध्यायेदलक्ष्मीपरिहारिणीं ॥ (*udyadādityasaṃkāśāṃ bilvakānanamadhyagāṃ | śanumadhyāṃ śriyaṃ dhyāyedalakṣmīparihāriṇīṃ ‖*)
