en: यदग्रे आप एवासन्नद्यस्सर्वमभूज्जगत् । नारास्ता अयनं यस्य स हि नारायणः परः ॥ सूते नरांश्च या आपस्ता यदस्यायनं हरेः । तस्य स्वाभाविकी शक्तिर्देवी नारायणी स्मृता ॥ अद्भो हि पृथिवी जाता अग्निरप्यभवत्तथा । वायुरर्कॊ ह्यपां वत्सश्चंद्रमास्सर्वमप्यथ ॥ जीवं जीवरसं दिव्यममृतं जलमुच्यते । जायते लीयते यत्र जगत्तज्वलमारितं ॥ तज्जलासिच शांतात्मा चिरं जलमुपासते । तस्मात्सर्वनिदानानामपां सृष्टत्वमुच्यते ॥ (*yadagre āpa evāsannadyassarvamabhūjjagat | nārāstā ayanaṃ yasya sa hi nārāyaṇaḥ paraḥ ‖ sūte narāṃśca yā āpastā yadasyāyanaṃ hareḥ | tasya svābhāvikī śaktirdevī nārāyaṇī smṛtā ‖ adbho hi pṛthivī jātā agnirapyabhavattathā | vāyurarkò hyapāṃ vatsaścaṃdramāssarvamapyatha ‖ jīvaṃ jīvarasaṃ divyamamṛtaṃ jalamucyate | jāyate līyate yatra jagattajvalamāritaṃ ‖ tajjalāsica śāṃtātmā ciraṃ jalamupāsate | tasmātsarvanidānānāmapāṃ sṛṣṭatvamucyate ‖*)

अप्पु प्रतिष्ठितः स्नेहस्तेनैव परमाणवः । जगद्भावाय संबद्धास्तद्दानौ स्याज्जगल्लयः ॥ तस्मादुपासको देवीं प्रार्थयेदस्वरूपिणीं । भोग्यद्रव्याणि सर्वाणि मम स्निग्धानि मातृका ॥ (*appu pratiṣṭhitaḥ snehastenaiva paramāṇavaḥ | jagadbhāvāya saṃbaddhāstaddānau syājjagallayaḥ ‖ tasmādupāsako devīṃ prārthayedasvarūpiṇīṃ | bhogyadravyāṇi sarvāṇi mama snigdhāni mātṛkā ‖*)

सृजतु श्रीरपां देवी भोगभावाय भामिनी । श्रीदेव्यास्तनयो जज्ञॆ चिक्लीतो नाम मन्मथः ॥ अबन्नविकृतौ चित्ते जातः कामो हि चित्रजः । आयमेव हि संसारहेतुः सर्वार्थसाधकः ॥ (*sṛjatu śrīrapāṃ devī bhogabhāvāya bhāminī | śrīdevyāstanayo jajñè ciklīto nāma manmathaḥ ‖ abannavikṛtau citte jātaḥ kāmo hi citrajaḥ | āyameva hi saṃsārahetuḥ sarvārthasādhakaḥ ‖*)

जगत्कामहितं सर्वं येन दैतफलोदयः । यश्च कामहतो देही श्रोत्रियो ब्रह्मणि स्थितः ॥ ब्रह्म संपत्सते तस्य कर्तव्यं न हि विद्यते । लक्ष्म्यास्त्रिवर्गरूपायाः प्राप्तिः कामनिबंधना ॥ (*jagatkāmahitaṃ sarvaṃ yena daitaphalodayaḥ | yaśca kāmahato dehī śrotriyo brahmaṇi sthitaḥ ‖ brahma saṃpatsate tasya kartavyaṃ na hi vidyate | lakṣmyāstrivargarūpāyāḥ prāptiḥ kāmanibaṃdhanā ‖*)

तस्माच्चिक्षीतनामानं लक्ष्मीपुत्रं हि दुर्जयं । कामदेवं समाराध्य यत्नतः प्रापुयाच्छियं ॥ लक्ष्मीः प्रयत्नसाध्या हि यत्नः कामसमुद्भवः । तस्य धर्माविरुद्धस्य विभूतित्वं हरेद्यतः ॥ (*tasmāccikṣītanāmānaṃ lakṣmīputraṃ hi durjayaṃ | kāmadevaṃ samārādhya yatnataḥ prāpuyācchiyaṃ ‖ lakṣmīḥ prayatnasādhyā hi yatnaḥ kāmasamudbhavaḥ | tasya dharmāviruddhasya vibhūtitvaṃ haredyataḥ ‖*)

चिक्लीत श्रीसुत स्वामिंश्चिरं निवस मद्गृहे । मत्कुले सुचिरं तिष्ठ मच्चित्ते संनिधिं कुरु ॥ त्वदागमनमात्रेण त्वन्माता त्वामनुव्रजेत् । त्वयि प्रीतिपरा सा हि तवच्छंदोनुवर्तिनी ॥ श्रीदेवीं तां मम गृहे चिरं वासय मातरं । नमोऽस्तु तुभ्यं चिक्लीत श्रीदेव्यै च नमो नमः ॥ (*ciklīta śrīsuta svāmiṃściraṃ nivasa madgṛhe | matkule suciraṃ tiṣṭha maccitte saṃnidhiṃ kuru ‖ tvadāgamanamātreṇa tvanmātā tvāmanuvrajet | tvayi prītiparā sā hi tavacchaṃdonuvartinī ‖ śrīdevīṃ tāṃ mama gṛhe ciraṃ vāsaya mātaraṃ | namo 'stu tubhyaṃ ciklīta śrīdevyai ca namo namaḥ ‖*)

एतत्तात्पर्यकां सूक्ते प्रजपेद्दादशीमृचं । चंद्रमा ऋषिरेतस्य देवता त्वम्यतेश्वरी ॥ चिक्लीतमाता श्रीश्चंदोनुष्टुब्बं बीजमुच्यते । चतुःषष्ठि सहस्राणि प्रजपेन्मंत्रसिद्धये ॥ (*etattātparyakāṃ sūkte prajapeddādaśīmṛcaṃ | caṃdramā ṛṣiretasya devatā tvamyateśvarī ‖ ciklītamātā śrīścaṃdonuṣṭubbaṃ bījamucyate | catuḥṣaṣṭhi sahasrāṇi prajapenmaṃtrasiddhaye ‖*)

नद्यासमुद्रगामिन्नास्तिरे बिल्वतरोस्टटे । जलकुंभं समभ्यर्च्य चेष्टिं चाभीष्टकां चरेत् ॥ यच्च याजुषशाखायामुक्तमारुणकेतुके । तेन मंत्रेण सहितं स्वशाखोक्तविधिं चरेत् ॥ प्रपादानं प्रकुर्वित दद्यात्पानीयमेव च । (*nadyāsamudragāminnāstire bilvatarosṭaṭe | jalakuṃbhaṃ samabhyarcya ceṣṭiṃ cābhīṣṭakāṃ caret ‖ yacca yājuṣaśākhāyāmuktamāruṇaketuke | tena maṃtreṇa sahitaṃ svaśākhoktavidhiṃ caret ‖ prapādānaṃ prakurvita dadyātpānīyameva ca |*)

सुवासिनीभ्यो विप्रेभ्यस्तदपत्येभ्य एव च ॥ भूताप्स्यायनतो देवी तुष्यति श्रीर्हरिप्रिया । तस्यान्नं भोग्यजातं च तदिच्छासमकालिकं ॥ हितं मृष्टं समृद्धं च शुद्धं यावदपेक्षितं । तत्कुटुंबस्य पर्याप्तं तदाश्रितजनस्य च ॥ तदावासे तत्कुले च महालक्ष्मीः स्थिरा भवेत् ॥ (*suvāsinībhyo viprebhyastadapatyebhya eva ca ‖ bhūtāpsyāyanato devī tuṣyati śrīrharipriyā | tasyānnaṃ bhogyajātaṃ ca tadicchāsamakālikaṃ ‖ hitaṃ mṛṣṭaṃ samṛddhaṃ ca śuddhaṃ yāvadapekṣitaṃ | tatkuṭuṃbasya paryāptaṃ tadāśritajanasya ca ‖ tadāvāse tatkule ca mahālakṣmīḥ sthirā bhavet ‖*)

According to the Vedic statement आपो ना इदमग्रे सलिलमासीत् (*āpo nā idamagre salilamāsīt*), in the beginning water covered the whole universe; there was no other thing. From that water this whole visible world arose. Water is named नाराः (*nārāḥ*), as in आपो नारा इति प्रोक्ताः (*āpo nārā iti proktāḥ*). The god for whom this water was the dwelling-place came to be named Nārāyaṇa. And those waters, the dwelling-place of that Nārāyaṇa, produced narān, that is, human beings; that is, from water alone the whole world, beginning with human beings, came into being. Therefore those waters called नाराः (*nārāḥ*), the cause of the origin of the world, became, under the name Nārāyaṇī, the natural power of Nārāyaṇa, the goddess. Then from the water principle, from water, as in the Vedic statement अद्भ्यः पृथिवी (*adbhyaḥ pṛthivī*), the earth arose. Then likewise the origin of fire, air, sun, moon and the others took place. Since from this water, the nectar that is the sap sustaining life arose, water came to be named jala. Or, since this whole world of moving and unmoving things is born from this water and dissolves in water itself, water came to be named jala. A man purified by such water, tranquil in spirit, worships the water principle. Therefore, since water is the cause of everything, it is said that water has the power of creation. In water there is the quality called sneha (the property of sticking together). Therefore the atoms, the basic supports of the world, united with one another by the power of sneha of that water, became the cause of the origin of the world. In the end, by the absence of sneha, it is likewise the cause of the dissolution of the world; therefore the goddess is to be worshipped. The goddess is to be meditated on and worshipped as being in the form of the power of water, that is, in the form of water. One should pray that the goddess, who has the form of water and is the mother of the world, may create for my enjoyment all the objects of enjoyment that are most dear to me. To this goddess Śrī a son named चिक्षीत (*cikṣīta*) was born. They call him Manmatha. It has been said before that the chief quality of water is sneha. Since this son of the goddess Śrī, who has the form of water, named Cikṣīta, arose from the mind of the goddess, which is a modification of water, he came to have the names Cittaja and Kāma. ⟨NOTE:179⟩ The desire that appears in the mind is itself

the cause of worldly existence. It is also the accomplisher of every purpose, and it gives room in people's minds to the sense of duality and so is the cause of the dealings of the world. That is to say, a man joined with desire (kāma; the word also means wishing) is engaged in the dealings of the world, and this worldly activity is itself the sense of duality. But the man free of desire, devoid of the sense of duality, attains the non-dual understanding that everything is Brahman alone and that there is no thing apart from Brahman; he is called a Śrotriya and remains absorbed in meditation on Brahman. In this world he has no duty or rite that he must perform. The attainment of the goddess Śrī Lakṣmī, who has the form of the three aims of life, has to come through her son Kāma, or Cikīta. Therefore, if one worships with effort the son of Lakṣmī, named Cikīta, who is famed as the god of desire (Kāmadeva) hard to conquer, and wins his favour, the favour of the goddess Śrī also follows and wealth is gained. To win Lakṣmī over is possible by effort, and that effort must itself come from Kāmadeva, the son of Lakṣmī. Therefore one should gratify the son of Lakṣmī and the goddess Lakṣmī by effort and practice not contrary to dharma, and obtain the fullness of wealth and prosperity.

O Cikkīta, son of Śrī, O lord, dwell in my house for a long time. Abide in my family at all times. Abide in my mind with a gracious disposition. If you come to my house, your mother, the goddess Śrī, out of love for you, will follow you and come along with you. Impel your mother, that goddess Śrī, to dwell in my house for a long time. O Cikkīta, here is a salutation to you, and many salutations to your mother, the goddess Śrī.

The twelfth Ṛk of the Śrīsūkta, which contains the meaning and purport stated above, is to be repeated with a disciplined mind. The seer of this Ṛk is Candra; the deity is the goddess Śrī, the mother of Cikṣīta; the metre is Anuṣṭubh; the seed (bīja) is नं (*naṃ*). For the mantra to be accomplished it must be repeated sixty-four thousand times. On the bank of a river that flows to the sea, or under a bilva tree, in a clean place, one should set up a pot full of water, invoke the deity in it, and worship according to rule. One should follow the rules and injunctions stated in the mantras called Āruṇaketaka in the Yajus branch, and perform the worship in the manner stated by one's own branch, according to the procedure (tantra) stated there. After the worship one should invite Brāhmaṇas, married women (suvāsinī) and their children, and satisfy them by giving drinks such as sweet syrup (pānaka). By this satisfaction of beings the goddess Śrī, dear to Hari, becomes pleased. For the man who performs the worship and the rest in this way, and for the members of his family and his dependants, wholesome, abundant and pure delicious food and many kinds of enjoyable things are obtained in as much plenty as he desires. Mahālakṣmī dwells firmly in his house and in his family.
Here ends the explanation of the twelfth Ṛk.
notes: ರುಕ್ಷ್ಮರೂಪಿಣೀಂ ರುಕ್ಷ್ಮಿಣೀಂ ರುಕ್ಮದೇವತಾಂ ನಾ printed; the closing ನಾ unclear

en: अस्य श्रीश्रीसूक्तस्य आद्र्रां पुष्करिणीमिति त्रयोदशऋग्महामंत्रस्य । जातवेदा ऋषिः । श्री महालक्ष्मीर्देवता । अनुष्टुप् छंदः । आं बीजं । स्वाहा शक्तिः । श्रीं कीलकं । श्रीमहालक्ष्मीप्रसादसिद्ध्यर्थे जपे विनियोगः ॥ (*asya śrīśrīsūktasya ādrrāṃ puṣkariṇīmiti trayodaśaṛgmahāmaṃtrasya | jātavedā ṛṣiḥ | śrī mahālakṣmīrdevatā | anuṣṭup chaṃdaḥ | āṃ bījaṃ | svāhā śaktiḥ | śrīṃ kīlakaṃ | śrīmahālakṣmīprasādasiddhyarthe jape viniyogaḥ ‖*) ओं आद्र्रा० पुष्करिणीं पुष्टिं-अंगुष्ठाभ्यां नमः । ओं पिंगळां-तर्जनीभ्यां नमः । ओं पद्ममालिनीं-मध्यमाभ्यां नमः । ओं चंद्रां हिरण्मयीं लक्ष्मींअनामिकाभ्यां नमः । ओं जातवेदः-कनिष्ठिकाभ्यां नमः । ओं म आवह-करतलकरपृष्ठाभ्यां नमः । (*oṃ ādrrā0 puṣkariṇīṃ puṣṭiṃ-aṃguṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ | oṃ piṃgaḷāṃ-tarjanībhyāṃ namaḥ | oṃ padmamālinīṃ-madhyamābhyāṃ namaḥ | oṃ caṃdrāṃ hiraṇmayīṃ lakṣmīṃanāmikābhyāṃ namaḥ | oṃ jātavedaḥ-kaniṣṭhikābhyāṃ namaḥ | oṃ ma āvaha-karatalakarapṛṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ |*) ओं आद्र्रा० पुष्करिणीं पुष्टिं-हृदयाय नमः । ओं पिंगळां-शिरसे स्वाहा । ओं पद्ममालिनीं-शिखाय्कॆ वषट् । ओं चंद्रां हिरण्मयीं लक्ष्मीं-कवचाय हुं । ओं जातवेदः-नेत्रत्रयाय वषट् । ओं म आ वह-अस्त्राय फट् ॥ भूर्भुवस्सुवरोमिति दिग्बंधः ॥ ध्यानं ॥ (*oṃ ādrrā0 puṣkariṇīṃ puṣṭiṃ-hṛdayāya namaḥ | oṃ piṃgaḷāṃ-śirase svāhā | oṃ padmamālinīṃ-śikhāykè vaṣaṭ | oṃ caṃdrāṃ hiraṇmayīṃ lakṣmīṃ-kavacāya huṃ | oṃ jātavedaḥ-netratrayāya vaṣaṭ | oṃ ma ā vaha-astrāya phaṭ ‖ bhūrbhuvassuvaromiti digbaṃdhaḥ ‖ dhyānaṃ ‖*) ध्यायेत्कल्पतरोर्मूले रत्नसिंहासने स्थितां । पद्मद्वयधरां पद्मां वरदाभयधारिणीं ॥ सर्वरत्नविचित्रांगीं रक्तश्रीपादपीठिकां । नियतः प्रजपेन्मंत्री लक्षसंख्या जपेन्मनुं । पिपासानाशनं बुद्धिदायकं प्रथमं स्मृतं । अभूतिमसमृद्धिं च द्वितीयेन विनाशयेत् ॥ (*dhyāyetkalpatarormūle ratnasiṃhāsane sthitāṃ | padmadvayadharāṃ padmāṃ varadābhayadhāriṇīṃ ‖ sarvaratnavicitrāṃgīṃ raktaśrīpādapīṭhikāṃ | niyataḥ prajapenmaṃtrī lakṣasaṃkhyā japenmanuṃ | pipāsānāśanaṃ buddhidāyakaṃ prathamaṃ smṛtaṃ | abhūtimasamṛddhiṃ ca dvitīyena vināśayet ‖*) **GLOSS**
आद्र्रां पुष्करिणीं पुष्टिं पिंगलां पद्ममालिनीं । चंद्रां हिरण्मयीं लक्ष्मीं जातवेदो म आवह ॥ (*ādrrāṃ puṣkariṇīṃ puṣṭiṃ piṃgalāṃ padmamālinīṃ | caṃdrāṃ hiraṇmayīṃ lakṣmīṃ jātavedo ma āvaha ‖*)

आद्र्रामिति । आद्र्रा० आर्द्रगंधां पुष्करिणीं अभिषेकोद्युक्तदिग्गजशुंडाग्रां पुष्करशब्दो गजशुंडाग्रवाचकः पद्मवतीं वा पद्मलतारूपां वा पुष्टिं पुष्पभिमानिनीं पुष्टिरूपां वा—“पुष्टिरूपेण संस्थितेति” मार्कंडेयवचनात् । पिंगलां पिंगळवर्णां । पद्मालिनीमित्यादि सिद्धमन्यत् ॥ (*ādrrāmiti | ādrrā0 ārdragaṃdhāṃ puṣkariṇīṃ abhiṣekodyuktadiggajaśuṃḍāgrāṃ puṣkaraśabdo gajaśuṃḍāgravācakaḥ padmavatīṃ vā padmalatārūpāṃ vā puṣṭiṃ puṣpabhimāninīṃ puṣṭirūpāṃ vā—“puṣṭirūpeṇa saṃsthiteti” mārkaṃḍeyavacanāt | piṃgalāṃ piṃgaḷavarṇāṃ | padmālinīmityādi siddhamanyat ‖*)

आद्र्रां (*ādrrāṃ*) means she of moist fragrance. पुष्करिणीं (*puṣkariṇīṃ*): she whose elephant-trunk tips, those of the elephants of the quarters, are ready for the anointing (the word पुष्कर (*puṣkara*) denotes the tip of an elephant's trunk); or she who has lotuses, or who has the form of a lotus-creeper. पुष्टिं (*puṣṭiṃ*): the presiding deity of flowers, ⟨NOTE:180⟩ or she who has the form of nourishment (puṣṭi), according to the statement of Mārkaṇḍeya, पुष्टिरूपेण संस्थितेति (*puṣṭirūpeṇa saṃsthiteti*). पिंगलां (*piṃgalāṃ*): of tawny colour. The rest, beginning with पद्मालिनीमित्यादि (*padmālinīmityādi*), is established.

हेजातवेदः संस्कृताग्ने आद्र्रां शीतलगुणां पुष्करिणीं गजशुंडाग्रवतीं वा पुष्टिं पोषणकरीं सुवर्णां शोभनकांतिं हेममालिनीं हेमपद्मरचितस्रग्विणीं सूर्यामैश्वर्यरूपां हिरण्मयीं स्वर्णरूपां मे मदर्थमावह आवाहनं कुरु ॥ (*hejātavedaḥ saṃskṛtāgne ādrrāṃ śītalaguṇāṃ puṣkariṇīṃ gajaśuṃḍāgravatīṃ vā puṣṭiṃ poṣaṇakarīṃ suvarṇāṃ śobhanakāṃtiṃ hemamālinīṃ hemapadmaracitasragviṇīṃ sūryāmaiśvaryarūpāṃ hiraṇmayīṃ svarṇarūpāṃ me madarthamāvaha āvāhanaṃ kuru ‖*)

O Jātavedas, O Agni who are consecrated: आद्र्रां (*ādrrāṃ*) she of cool quality; पुष्करिणीं (*puṣkariṇīṃ*) she who has elephant-trunk tips; पुष्टिं (*puṣṭiṃ*) she who brings nourishment; सुवर्णां (*suvarṇāṃ*) she of beautiful radiance; हेममालिनीं (*hemamālinīṃ*) she who wears a garland made of golden lotuses; सूर्यां (*sūryāṃ*) she who has the form of prosperity; हिरण्मयीं (*hiraṇmayīṃ*) she who has the form of gold. For my sake, for my purpose, bring her, perform the invocation.
notes: ಬೃ. ವೇ. ೫-೧೩ printed; abbreviation not in list, perhaps ಬೃ. ದೇ.

en: - पुष्करिणीं (*puṣkariṇīṃ*)—she who is sprinkled with water from the tips of the elephants' trunks for the anointing
- पुष्टिं (*puṣṭiṃ*)—she who has the form of nourishment, or who is the presiding deity of nourishment
- पिंगलां (*piṃgalāṃ*)—she who has a body of a tawny colour (fair, yellow)
- पद्ममालिनीं (*padmamālinīṃ*)—she who wears a garland tied of lotus flowers
- चंद्रां (*caṃdrāṃ*)—she who has a form delightful like the moon
- हिरण्मयीं (*hiraṇmayīṃ*)—she who is endowed with golden ornaments, or who shines with a body made of gold
- लक्ष्मीं (*lakṣmīṃ*)—the great goddess Lakṣmī, or the goddess Śrī

The goddess Śrī Lakṣmī, though she shines with exceeding brilliance, is pleasing to the eye, endowed with a cool radiance. For the anointing of this goddess the elephants stand ready in the lake, having taken water in their trunks. She gives nourishment to all beings, has a body shining with a fair colour, wears a garland of lotus flowers, gleams with a golden form, and like the moon is a delight to all. O Agni, bring to me such a Mahālakṣmī, endowed with these qualities.

In this Ṛk and in the next Ṛk the goddess Śrī is praised as being in the form of Gajalakṣmī. In this Ṛk she is described as dwelling within the moon's disc, and in the next Ṛk as dwelling within the sun's disc. The special matters of the fourteenth Ṛk apply also to this thirteenth Ṛk.

अथ चतुर्दशी युक्ओं अस्य श्रीश्रीसूक्तस्य चतुर्दर्श्यङ्महामंत्रस्य । जातवेदा ऋषिः । श्रीराज्य लक्ष्मीर्देवता । अनुष्टुप् छंदः । श्रीं बीजं । हं शक्तिः । ह्रीं कीलकं । श्रीराज्य लक्ष्मीप्रसादसिद्ध्यर्थे जपे विनियोगः ॥ (*atha caturdaśī yukoṃ asya śrīśrīsūktasya caturdarśyaṅmahāmaṃtrasya | jātavedā ṛṣiḥ | śrīrājya lakṣmīrdevatā | anuṣṭup chaṃdaḥ | śrīṃ bījaṃ | haṃ śaktiḥ | hrīṃ kīlakaṃ | śrīrājya lakṣmīprasādasiddhyarthe jape viniyogaḥ ‖*)

ओं आद्र्रा० पुष्करिणीं यष्टिं—अंगुष्ठाभ्यां वनुः । ओं सुवर्णां—तर्ज नीभ्यां नमः । ओं हेममालिनीं—मध्यमाभ्यां नमः । ओं सूर्यां हिरण्मयीं अनामिका भ्यां नमः । ओं लक्ष्मी—कनिष्ठिकाभ्यां नमः । ओं जातवेदो म आ वह करतलकरपृष्ठाभ्यां नमः । ओं आर्दां पुष्करिणीं यष्टिं—हृदयाय नमः । ओं हेममालिनीं—शिखाय्कॆ वषट् । ओं सूर्यां हिरण्मयीं—कवचाय हुं । ओं लक्ष्मीं—नेत्रत्रयाय वौषट्। ओं जातवेदो म आवह—अस्त्राय फट् ॥ भूर्भु वस्सुवरोमिति दिग्बंधः ॥ ध्यानं ॥ (*oṃ ādrrā0 puṣkariṇīṃ yaṣṭiṃ—aṃguṣṭhābhyāṃ vanuḥ | oṃ suvarṇāṃ—tarja nībhyāṃ namaḥ | oṃ hemamālinīṃ—madhyamābhyāṃ namaḥ | oṃ sūryāṃ hiraṇmayīṃ anāmikā bhyāṃ namaḥ | oṃ lakṣmī—kaniṣṭhikābhyāṃ namaḥ | oṃ jātavedo ma ā vaha karatalakarapṛṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ | oṃ ārdāṃ puṣkariṇīṃ yaṣṭiṃ—hṛdayāya namaḥ | oṃ hemamālinīṃ—śikhāykè vaṣaṭ | oṃ sūryāṃ hiraṇmayīṃ—kavacāya huṃ | oṃ lakṣmīṃ—netratrayāya vauṣaṭ| oṃ jātavedo ma āvaha—astrāya phaṭ ‖ bhūrbhu vassuvaromiti digbaṃdhaḥ ‖ dhyānaṃ ‖*) पद्मं मणिमयं कुंभमिक्षुचापं च बिभ्रतीं । पुष्पबाणं महालक्ष्मीं ध्यायेद्राज्यप्रदायिनीं ॥ एवं ध्यात्वा जपेल्लक्षं राज्यलक्ष्मीं समश्नुते ॥ (*padmaṃ maṇimayaṃ kuṃbhamikṣucāpaṃ ca bibhratīṃ | puṣpabāṇaṃ mahālakṣmīṃ dhyāyedrājyapradāyinīṃ ‖ evaṃ dhyātvā japellakṣaṃ rājyalakṣmīṃ samaśnute ‖*) **GLOSS**
आद्र्रां यःकरिणीं यष्टिं सुवर्णा० हेममालिनीं । सूर्यां हिरण्मयीं लक्ष्मीं जातवेदो म आवह ॥ (*ādrrāṃ yaḥkariṇīṃ yaṣṭiṃ suvarṇā0 hemamālinīṃ | sūryāṃ hiraṇmayīṃ lakṣmīṃ jātavedo ma āvaha ‖*)

आद्र्रां पूर्वोक्तां यःकरिणीं यष्टिकरां वेत्रहस्तामित्यर्थः । टिलोपश्कांदसः । तद्वतीं दंडकारिणीं दंडकरां वा । यष्टिं दंडरूपां “धर्मदंडस्वरूपिणी” मिति ब्राह्मोक्तेः । सुवर्णां शोभनवर्णां रुक्ष्मरूपिणीं रुक्ष्मिणीं रुक्मदेवतां ना हेममालिनीं हेमविकृतशृंखलादिमालावतीं सूर्यां सूर्य वत्प्रकाशमानां तद्रूपां वा । सिद्धमन्यत् ॥ (*ādrrāṃ pūrvoktāṃ yaḥkariṇīṃ yaṣṭikarāṃ vetrahastāmityarthaḥ | ṭilopaśkāṃdasaḥ | tadvatīṃ daṃḍakāriṇīṃ daṃḍakarāṃ vā | yaṣṭiṃ daṃḍarūpāṃ “dharmadaṃḍasvarūpiṇī” miti brāhmokteḥ | suvarṇāṃ śobhanavarṇāṃ rukṣmarūpiṇīṃ rukṣmiṇīṃ rukmadevatāṃ nā hemamālinīṃ hemavikṛtaśṛṃkhalādimālāvatīṃ sūryāṃ sūrya vatprakāśamānāṃ tadrūpāṃ vā | siddhamanyat ‖*)

आद्र्रां (*ādrrāṃ*) is she who was spoken of before. यःकरिणीं (*yaḥkariṇīṃ*) means she who has a staff (yaṣṭi) in her hand, that is, a cane in her hand; or she who holds a staff, or has a staff in hand. यष्टिं (*yaṣṭiṃ*): of the form of a staff, according to the Brāhma statement धर्मदंडस्वरूपिणी (*dharmadaṃḍasvarūpiṇī*). सुवर्णां (*suvarṇāṃ*): of beautiful colour, who has the form of gold (rukma), the goddess of gold. ⟨NOTE:181⟩ हेममालिनीं (*hemamālinīṃ*): she who has a garland, chain and the like, fashioned of gold. सूर्यां (*sūryāṃ*): she who shines like the sun, or has his form. The rest is established.

हे अग्ने आद्र्रां पूर्वोक्तां पुष्करिणीं करिहस्ताग्रवतीं यष्टिं पाकशालादिदंडरूपां, इष्टिमितिपाठे यागस्वरूपां पिंगळां कद्रूवर्णां पद्ममालिनीं पूर्वोक्तरूपां चंद्रां संतोषकरीं चंद्रमंडलवासिनीर चंद्ररूपां कर्पूरधारिणीं वा हिरण्मयीं सुवर्णमयीं धनरूपां धनप्रचुरां वा लक्ष्मीं मे मदर्थं ममेति पाठे मत्संबंधिप्रयोजनाय आवह ॥ (*he agne ādrrāṃ pūrvoktāṃ puṣkariṇīṃ karihastāgravatīṃ yaṣṭiṃ pākaśālādidaṃḍarūpāṃ, iṣṭimitipāṭhe yāgasvarūpāṃ piṃgaḷāṃ kadrūvarṇāṃ padmamālinīṃ pūrvoktarūpāṃ caṃdrāṃ saṃtoṣakarīṃ caṃdramaṃḍalavāsinīra caṃdrarūpāṃ karpūradhāriṇīṃ vā hiraṇmayīṃ suvarṇamayīṃ dhanarūpāṃ dhanapracurāṃ vā lakṣmīṃ me madarthaṃ mameti pāṭhe matsaṃbaṃdhiprayojanāya āvaha ‖*)

O Agni, आद्र्रां (*ādrrāṃ*) is she spoken of before. पुष्करिणीं (*puṣkariṇīṃ*): she who has elephant-trunk tips. यष्टिं (*yaṣṭiṃ*): of the form of a staff such as is used in a kitchen and the like; in the reading इष्टिमितिपाठे (*iṣṭimitipāṭhe*), of the form of a sacrifice. पिंगळां (*piṃgaḷāṃ*): of the colour of kadrū (tawny). पद्ममालिनीं (*padmamālinīṃ*): of the form spoken of before. चंद्रां (*caṃdrāṃ*): she who gives delight, who dwells in the moon's disc, who has the form of the moon, or who bears camphor. हिरण्मयीं (*hiraṇmayīṃ*): made of gold, of the form of wealth, or abounding in wealth. लक्ष्मीं (*lakṣmīṃ*). मे (*me*): for my sake; in the reading ममेति पाठे (*mameti pāṭhe*), for a purpose connected with me; bring her.
notes: ಬೃ. ದೆ. ೫-೯೮ printed; abbreviation read as ಬೃ. ದೇ.

en: - आद्र्रां (*ādrrāṃ*)—of cool nature, or endowed with a cool radiance
- यष्टिं यःकरिणीं (*yaṣṭiṃ yaḥkariṇīṃ*)—she who holds a cane or staff (the staff of dharma) in her hand
- सुवर्णां (*suvarṇāṃ*)—she who has a beautiful colour
- हेममालिनी (*hemamālinī*)—she who wears a garland of flowers made of gold
- सूर्यां (*sūryāṃ*)—she who shines with great brilliance like the sun, or who has the form of the sun
- हिरण्मयिं (*hiraṇmayiṃ*)—she who is adorned with golden ornaments, or who shines with a body made of gold

O Agni, bring to my side the goddess called Mahālakṣmī, who is of cool nature, or endowed with a cool radiance like the moon; who holds a staff in her hand; who is of beautiful colour; who, wearing a garland of golden flowers, shines with excess of splendour like the sun, or has the form of the sun; and who is adorned with golden ornaments, or has a beautiful golden body.

ममकारो मदश्चेति वर्तेते पार्श्वयोर्द्वयोः । देवते गजरूपिण्य श्रीदेवीमभिषिंचतः ॥ तयोः शुंडाग्रयोर्भात आशाप्रीत्याह्वयावुभौ । सुवर्णकलश्‌ ताभ्यां तृप्तिपूर्णांभसान्वहं ॥ हृत्पद्मवासिनी देवी चिद्रूपिण्यभिषिच्यते । देहे गृहात्मके विष्टेत्सहानंदेन विष्णुना ॥ एतावान् गजलक्ष्म्यास्तु विभूतीर्विस्तरो ध्रुवः । तां स्मरेदभिषेकाद्र्रा० पुष्टिदां पुष्टिरूपिणीं ॥ (*mamakāro madaśceti vartete pārśvayordvayoḥ | devate gajarūpiṇya śrīdevīmabhiṣiṃcataḥ ‖ tayoḥ śuṃḍāgrayorbhāta āśāprītyāhvayāvubhau | suvarṇakalaś tābhyāṃ tṛptipūrṇāṃbhasānvahaṃ ‖ hṛtpadmavāsinī devī cidrūpiṇyabhiṣicyate | dehe gṛhātmake viṣṭetsahānaṃdena viṣṇunā ‖ etāvān gajalakṣmyāstu vibhūtīrvistaro dhruvaḥ | tāṃ smaredabhiṣekādrrā0 puṣṭidāṃ puṣṭirūpiṇīṃ ‖*)

रुक्माभां स्वप्नधीगम्यां सुवर्णां स्वर्णमालिनीं । सूर्यामैश्वर्यरूपां च सावित्रीं सूर्यरूपिणीं ॥ आत्मसंज्ञां च चिद्रूपां ज्ञानदृष्टिस्वरूपिणीं । चक्षुःप्रकाशबां चैव हिरण्यप्रचुरां तथा ॥ स्वर्णात्मनाविर्भूतां च जातवेदो म आवह । ऋचमेतां जपेन्नित्यं पश्यन्नर्कं दिवा द्विजः ॥ (*rukmābhāṃ svapnadhīgamyāṃ suvarṇāṃ svarṇamālinīṃ | sūryāmaiśvaryarūpāṃ ca sāvitrīṃ sūryarūpiṇīṃ ‖ ātmasaṃjñāṃ ca cidrūpāṃ jñānadṛṣṭisvarūpiṇīṃ | cakṣuḥprakāśabāṃ caiva hiraṇyapracurāṃ tathā ‖ svarṇātmanāvirbhūtāṃ ca jātavedo ma āvaha | ṛcametāṃ japennityaṃ paśyannarkaṃ divā dvijaḥ ‖*)

पद्माकरे तटाके वा प्रत्यहं त्रिसहस्रकं । मंडलत्रयपर्यंतं व्रतदीक्षापरायणः ॥ सुवासिनीशतं पूज्यं सालंकारं सदक्षिणं । (*padmākare taṭāke vā pratyahaṃ trisahasrakaṃ | maṃḍalatrayaparyaṃtaṃ vratadīkṣāparāyaṇaḥ ‖ suvāsinīśataṃ pūjyaṃ sālaṃkāraṃ sadakṣiṇaṃ |*)

सिद्धौ गजांतरैश्वर्यमारोग्यं भाग्यमेव च ॥ सर्वार्थसिद्धिमंते तु सूर्यसायुज्यमाप्नुयात् । मैत्र्या दिवृत्तिभिश्चाद्र्रा० विराजःकरुणां श्रियं ॥ दयाद्रार्रा० वेत्रहस्तां च व्रतदंडस्वरूपिणीं । पिंगळाभां प्रसन्नास्यां पद्ममालाधरां तथा ॥ चंद्रस्थां चंद्ररूपां च चंद्रां चंद्रधरां तथा । हिरण्मयां महालक्ष्मीमृचमेतां जपेन्निशि ॥ (*siddhau gajāṃtaraiśvaryamārogyaṃ bhāgyameva ca ‖ sarvārthasiddhimaṃte tu sūryasāyujyamāpnuyāt | maitryā divṛttibhiścādrrā0 virājaḥkaruṇāṃ śriyaṃ ‖ dayādrārrā0 vetrahastāṃ ca vratadaṃḍasvarūpiṇīṃ | piṃgaḷābhāṃ prasannāsyāṃ padmamālādharāṃ tathā ‖ caṃdrasthāṃ caṃdrarūpāṃ ca caṃdrāṃ caṃdradharāṃ tathā | hiraṇmayāṃ mahālakṣmīmṛcametāṃ japenniśi ‖*)

आरभ्य शुक्लपंचम्यामास्वेव दशरात्रिषु । प्राप्तैकोत्तरवृद्धैव जपेद्वतपरायणः ॥ द्वात्रिंशन्वासपर्यंतं पुरश्चरणमुच्यते । चंद्रमंडलमालक्ष लक्ष्मीं श्रीललितांबिकां ॥ सिद्धौ तु सार्वभौमत्वं वशीकरणमेव च । पूर्णानंदप्रतिष्ठां च कीर्तिभोगं महद्दनं । प्राप्यांते चंद्रसायुज्यं प्राप्नोत्येव न संशयः ॥ (*ārabhya śuklapaṃcamyāmāsveva daśarātriṣu | prāptaikottaravṛddhaiva japedvataparāyaṇaḥ ‖ dvātriṃśanvāsaparyaṃtaṃ puraścaraṇamucyate | caṃdramaṃḍalamālakṣa lakṣmīṃ śrīlalitāṃbikāṃ ‖ siddhau tu sārvabhaumatvaṃ vaśīkaraṇameva ca | pūrṇānaṃdapratiṣṭhāṃ ca kīrtibhogaṃ mahaddanaṃ | prāpyāṃte caṃdrasāyujyaṃ prāpnotyeva na saṃśayaḥ ‖*)

Two deities named Mamakāra and Mada, in the form of elephants, stand on the left and right sides of the goddess Śrī and, having filled with the water of contentment, in their trunks, two golden pots named Hope (āśā) and Love (prīti), anoint every day the goddess Śrī, who dwells in the lotus of the heart, whose nature is consciousness (cit), and who sits on a seat in the house that is the body together with Viṣṇu, whose nature is bliss. This splendour is said to be the particular glory of Gajalakṣmī. This Gajalakṣmī is to be meditated on in the following way: this goddess has a body drenched with the water of the anointing; as the presiding deity of nourishment she gives nourishment to all; she shines with a radiance pure as silver; she appears in dreams; shining with the radiance of gold she wears a garland made of gold; she is radiant like the sun and is the embodiment of prosperity; she has the nature of the Self, the form of consciousness, and the nature of the eye of knowledge; she gives light to the eyes; she has a body radiant with gold, and has come forth from a body of gold. One should meditate thus: O Agni, bring to my side this deity called Gajalakṣmī.

Meditating in this way, standing in water in a lake or a pond and looking at the sun, one should repeat this Ṛk every day three thousand times. Having taken up the vow and initiation for three maṇḍalas (a maṇḍala means forty-eight days) in this manner, and repeated it,

at the end one should honour and gratify a hundred married women (suvāsinī) with clothes, ornaments and gifts. By doing so the mantra is accomplished, and one obtains elephant-wealth and the other kinds of prosperity, health and good fortune, and success in all undertakings, and enjoys happiness. At the end, at the dissolution of the body, he also attains the excellent state called union with the sun (sūryasāyujya).

While repeating this mantra one should meditate on the goddess Śrī as endowed, towards her devotees, with qualities such as affection, tenderness, love and a gaze moist with compassion; as holding a staff in her hand, in the form of the staff of dharma, so that people observe the rules; as having a body of fair radiance and a form delightful like the moon; as bearing the disc of the moon; and as being the form of Mahālakṣmī, resplendent with a body of golden form. One should repeat this Ṛk at night. A man who wishes to perform the preparatory rite (puraścaraṇa) should begin the repetition on the fifth day (pañcamī) of the bright fortnight, and from there for ten days, every night, increasing by one thousand each time, repeat up to the full-moon day. On that day, looking at the disc of the moon, he should imagine that Śrī Mahālakṣmī, famed as Śrī Lalitāmbikā, dwells in that moon-disc. In this way, for twelve months, in each month from the fifth day up to the full-moon day, he should repeat. This way of repeating is named the rule of puraścaraṇa. If the course of repetition done by the rule of puraścaraṇa succeeds, the practiser becomes a universal sovereign. All become subject to him. Complete bliss, fame, the means of enjoyment and abundance of wealth are obtained; having enjoyed all enjoyments in this world for a long time, at the dissolution of the body he attains the great state named union with the moon (candrasāyujya).
Here ends the explanation of the meaning of the fourteenth Ṛk.

ओं अस्य श्री श्रीसूक्तस्थ ऋक्पंचदशीमहामंत्रस्य । अंगिरा ऋषिः । श्री लक्ष्मी र्देवता ! अनुष्टुप् छंदः । अथवा कुबेर ऋषिः । श्रीमहालक्ष्मीर्देवता ! प्रस्तार पंक्तिशृंदः। ह्रीं बीजं। श्रीं शक्तिः । ह्रीं कीलकं । श्री राज्यसिंहासनस्थमहालक्ष्मीप्रसाद सिद्ध्यर्थे जपे विनियोगः ॥ (*oṃ asya śrī śrīsūktastha ṛkpaṃcadaśīmahāmaṃtrasya | aṃgirā ṛṣiḥ | śrī lakṣmī rdevatā ! anuṣṭup chaṃdaḥ | athavā kubera ṛṣiḥ | śrīmahālakṣmīrdevatā ! prastāra paṃktiśṛṃdaḥ| hrīṃ bījaṃ| śrīṃ śaktiḥ | hrīṃ kīlakaṃ | śrī rājyasiṃhāsanasthamahālakṣmīprasāda siddhyarthe jape viniyogaḥ ‖*) ओं ह्रीं तां म आवह—अंगुष्ठाभ्यां नमः। ओं श्रीं जातवेदः-तर्जनीभ्यां नमः । ओं ह्रीं लक्ष्मीमनपगामिनीं— मध्यमाभ्यां नमः ! यस्यां हिरण्यं— अनामिकाभ्यां—नमः। ओं श्रीं प्रभूतं गावो दास्योऽश्वान्—कनिष्ठिकाभ्यां नमः । (*oṃ hrīṃ tāṃ ma āvaha—aṃguṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ| oṃ śrīṃ jātavedaḥ-tarjanībhyāṃ namaḥ | oṃ hrīṃ lakṣmīmanapagāminīṃ— madhyamābhyāṃ namaḥ ! yasyāṃ hiraṇyaṃ— anāmikābhyāṃ—namaḥ| oṃ śrīṃ prabhūtaṃ gāvo dāsyo 'śvān—kaniṣṭhikābhyāṃ namaḥ |*)

ओं ह्री पुरुषानहं—करतलकरपृष्ठाभ्यां नमः ॥ ओं ह्रीं तां म आवह-हृदयाय नमः । ओं ह्रीं लक्ष्मीमनसगामिनीं—शिखाय्कॆ वषट् । ओं श्रीं जातवेदः—शिरसे स्वाहा । ओं ह्रीं लक्ष्मीमनसगामिनीं—शिखाय्कॆ वषट् । ओं ह्रीं यस्यां हिरण्यंकवचाय हुं । ओं श्रीं प्रभूतं गावो दास्योऽश्वान्-नेत्रत्रयाय वौषट् । ओं ह्रीं पुरुषानहं—अस्त्राय फट् ॥ भूर्भुवस्सुवरोमिति दिग्बंधः ॥ ध्यानं ॥ (*oṃ hrī puruṣānahaṃ—karatalakarapṛṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ ‖ oṃ hrīṃ tāṃ ma āvaha-hṛdayāya namaḥ | oṃ hrīṃ lakṣmīmanasagāminīṃ—śikhāykè vaṣaṭ | oṃ śrīṃ jātavedaḥ—śirase svāhā | oṃ hrīṃ lakṣmīmanasagāminīṃ—śikhāykè vaṣaṭ | oṃ hrīṃ yasyāṃ hiraṇyaṃkavacāya huṃ | oṃ śrīṃ prabhūtaṃ gāvo dāsyo 'śvān-netratrayāya vauṣaṭ | oṃ hrīṃ puruṣānahaṃ—astrāya phaṭ ‖ bhūrbhuvassuvaromiti digbaṃdhaḥ ‖ dhyānaṃ ‖*) ध्यायॆल्लक्ष्मीं प्रहसितमुखीं राज्यसिंहासनस्थां मुद्राशक्तिं सकलविनुतां सर्वसंसेव्यमानां । अग्नौ पूज्यामखिलजननीं हेमवर्णां हिरण्यां भाग्योपेतां भुवनसुखदां भार्गवीं भूतधात्रीं ॥ इति ध्यात्वा जपंकुर्यात् ॥ (*dhyāyèllakṣmīṃ prahasitamukhīṃ rājyasiṃhāsanasthāṃ mudrāśaktiṃ sakalavinutāṃ sarvasaṃsevyamānāṃ | agnau pūjyāmakhilajananīṃ hemavarṇāṃ hiraṇyāṃ bhāgyopetāṃ bhuvanasukhadāṃ bhārgavīṃ bhūtadhātrīṃ ‖ iti dhyātvā japaṃkuryāt ‖*) **GLOSS**

तां म आवह जातवेदो लक्ष्मीमनपगामिनीं । यस्यां हिरण्यं प्रभूतं गावो दास्योऽश्वान्विंदेयं पुरुषानहं ॥ (*tāṃ ma āvaha jātavedo lakṣmīmanapagāminīṃ | yasyāṃ hiraṇyaṃ prabhūtaṃ gāvo dāsyo 'śvānviṃdeyaṃ puruṣānahaṃ ‖*)

इयं ऋक् द्वितीयया ऋचा व्याख्याता । प्रभूतं भूयिष्ठं गावः गाः । दास्यः परिचारिकाः । उभयत्र शसर्थे जस् । इयान् विशेषः .. ॥ (*iyaṃ ṛk dvitīyayā ṛcā vyākhyātā | prabhūtaṃ bhūyiṣṭhaṃ gāvaḥ gāḥ | dāsyaḥ paricārikāḥ | ubhayatra śasarthe jas | iyān viśeṣaḥ .. ‖*)
This Ṛk has been explained by the second Ṛk. प्रभूतं (*prabhūtaṃ*) means abundant; गावः (*gāvaḥ*) means cows; दास्यः (*dāsyaḥ*) means maidservants. This much is the difference.

हे जातवेदः अग्ने यस्यां लक्ष्म्यामागतायां सत्यां प्रभूतं हिरण्यं पुष्कलं धनं गावः गोमहिष्यादीन् दासीजनान् अश्वान् तुरगादीन् पुरुषान् पुत्रमित्रकलत्रादीन् विंदेयमहं लभेयं । अनपगामिनीं निवृत्तिरहितां तां तादृशीं लक्ष्मीं श्रियं मे मदर्थं आवह आवाहनं कुरु ॥ (*he jātavedaḥ agne yasyāṃ lakṣmyāmāgatāyāṃ satyāṃ prabhūtaṃ hiraṇyaṃ puṣkalaṃ dhanaṃ gāvaḥ gomahiṣyādīn dāsījanān aśvān turagādīn puruṣān putramitrakalatrādīn viṃdeyamahaṃ labheyaṃ | anapagāminīṃ nivṛttirahitāṃ tāṃ tādṛśīṃ lakṣmīṃ śriyaṃ me madarthaṃ āvaha āvāhanaṃ kuru ‖*)

O Jātavedas, O Agni: when that Lakṣmī has come, in whom there is प्रभूतं हिरण्यं (*prabhūtaṃ hiraṇyaṃ*), abundant gold, that is, plentiful wealth, I would obtain cows, that is, buffaloes and the like, servant-women, horses, that is, steeds and the like, and पुरुषान् (*puruṣān*), that is, sons, friends, wives and the like. अनपगामिनीं (*anapagāminīṃ*) means she who does not turn away. Bring, perform the invocation of, such a Lakṣmī, Śrī, for my sake, for my purpose.
- अनपगामिनीं (*anapagāminīṃ*)—she who never leaves me, that is, who dwells firmly in my house
- लक्ष्मीं (*lakṣmīṃ*)—the goddess Śrī, renowned as Mahālakṣmī
- मे (*me*)—to my side, or to show me favour
- यस्यां (*yasyāṃ*)—the goddess Śrī, by whose coming to me
- हिरण्यं (*hiraṇyaṃ*)—gold, or wealth such as money and gold
- दास्यः (*dāsyaḥ*)—male and female servants, that is, attendants
- पुरुषान् (*puruṣān*)—people such as sons, friends and wives
- विंदेयं (*viṃdeyaṃ*)—may I obtain (by the grace of the goddess); bring such a goddess Śrī to my side

O Agni, bring to my side that goddess Śrī, by whose coming to my house I shall obtain, through the favour of that goddess, abundant wealth such as money and gold, wealth of cattle such as cows, male and female servants, horses, and the circle of relatives such as sons, friends and wives.

पंचदश्या ऋचः कुबेरऋषिः प्रस्तारपंक्तिश्छंदः । ह्रीं श्रीं ह्रीमिति बीजानि द्विधाविभक्तमंत्रेण सबीजत्रयेण पल्लवेन त्रिवारमनुलोमविलोमपरिवर्तनतः षोढा न्यासाः । (*paṃcadaśyā ṛcaḥ kuberaṛṣiḥ prastārapaṃktiśchaṃdaḥ | hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīmiti bījāni dvidhāvibhaktamaṃtreṇa sabījatrayeṇa pallavena trivāramanulomavilomaparivartanataḥ ṣoḍhā nyāsāḥ |*) ध्यायेल्लक्ष्मीं प्रहसितमुखीं राज्यसिंहासनस्थां मुद्राशक्तिं सकलविनुतां सर्वसंसेव्यमानां । अग्नौ पूज्यामखिलजननीं हेमवर्णां हिरण्यां भाग्योपेतां भुवनसुखदां भार्गवीं भूतिधात्रीं ॥ (*dhyāyellakṣmīṃ prahasitamukhīṃ rājyasiṃhāsanasthāṃ mudrāśaktiṃ sakalavinutāṃ sarvasaṃsevyamānāṃ | agnau pūjyāmakhilajananīṃ hemavarṇāṃ hiraṇyāṃ bhāgyopetāṃ bhuvanasukhadāṃ bhārgavīṃ bhūtidhātrīṃ ‖*)

मंत्रोऽयं धान्यराशेरुपरि पद्माक्षमालया तुलसीकाष्ठमालया ना प्रत्यहमष्टोत्तरत्रिसहस्रप्रकारेण सहस्रदिवसजपात्सिद्धो भवति । व्याघ्राजिने महेंद्रनीलाक्षमालया पंचलक्षजपाच्छत्रून् जयति । वस्त्रासने दर्भास्तरणे वा रुद्राक्षमालया नवलक्षजपाद्विद्यां प्राप्नोति । वेत्रासने सुवर्णाक्षमालया कोटिजपाद्राज्यं प्राप्नुयात् । ऐहिकसर्वकामप्रदोऽयं मंत्रः । अर्थतस्त्वेषा द्वितीयामृचमनुकरोति । अन्यदन्यत्रोक्तमेवेति समानं ॥ (*maṃtro 'yaṃ dhānyarāśerupari padmākṣamālayā tulasīkāṣṭhamālayā nā pratyahamaṣṭottaratrisahasraprakāreṇa sahasradivasajapātsiddho bhavati | vyāghrājine maheṃdranīlākṣamālayā paṃcalakṣajapācchatrūn jayati | vastrāsane darbhāstaraṇe vā rudrākṣamālayā navalakṣajapādvidyāṃ prāpnoti | vetrāsane suvarṇākṣamālayā koṭijapādrājyaṃ prāpnuyāt | aihikasarvakāmaprado 'yaṃ maṃtraḥ | arthatastveṣā dvitīyāmṛcamanukaroti | anyadanyatroktameveti samānaṃ ‖*)

For this Ṛk of the Śrīsūkta, the fifteenth Ṛk, which begins तां म (*tāṃ ma*), Kubera is the seer; Lakṣmī is the deity; the metre is Prastārapaṅkti. For the convenience of nyāsa the mantra is to be divided into two parts, the three seed syllables are to be joined in direct and reverse order, and the sixfold nyāsa is to be performed. The meditation verse is as follows.

ध्यायॆल्लक्ष्मीं प्रहसितमुखीं राज्यसिंहासनस्थां मुद्राशक्तिं सकलविनुतां सर्वसंसेव्यमानां अग्नौ पूज्यामखिलजननीं हेमवर्णां हिरण्यां भाग्योपेतां भुवनसुखदां भागवीं भूतिधात्रीं ॥ (*dhyāyèllakṣmīṃ prahasitamukhīṃ rājyasiṃhāsanasthāṃ mudrāśaktiṃ sakalavinutāṃ sarvasaṃsevyamānāṃ agnau pūjyāmakhilajananīṃ hemavarṇāṃ hiraṇyāṃ bhāgyopetāṃ bhuvanasukhadāṃ bhāgavīṃ bhūtidhātrīṃ ‖*)

This goddess Śrī, bearing the name Lakṣmī, shines seated on the royal throne, with a gentle smile on her face, holding in her hands the gestures of granting boons, giving fearlessness and the like. She is praised by all people. Invoked in the fire, she is worthy of worship. She is the mother of the whole world. She shines with the radiance of a golden-hued body. The body of this goddess is wholly of gold. Being the mistress of fortune, she brings happiness to the people of all worlds. Born in the family of Bhṛgu and bearing prosperity and the other glories, this goddess Śrī is to be meditated on in this way: such is the main purport.

The practiser who repeats the mantra should sit upon a heap of grain, take as his rosary either a lotus-seed rosary or a rosary of tulasī wood, and repeat this Ṛk every day three thousand one hundred and eight times, for a thousand days; for such men the mantra is accomplished. If he spreads for a seat a tiger skin, sits upon it, and repeats it five hundred thousand times with a rosary of sapphire (indranīla) beads, he conquers his enemies in battles and the like and wins victory over all quarters. If he spreads a cloth, or sits on a seat of darbha grass, and repeats it nine hundred thousand times with a rudrākṣa rosary, he obtains all knowledge. If he sits on a seat of cane (vetra), that is, a seat made of rattan, and repeats it ten million times with a rosary studded with golden beads, he obtains a kingdom. This mantra grants all desires that are enjoyed in this world (aihika). In meaning this mantra is just like the second Ṛk of this sūkta.
Here ends the explanation of the meaning of the fifteenth Ṛk.
यः शुचिः प्रयतो भूत्वा जुहुयादाज्यमन्वहं । श्रियः पंचदशर्चं च श्रीकामः सततं जपेत् ॥ १६ ॥ (*yaḥ śuciḥ prayato bhūtvā juhuyādājyamanvahaṃ | śriyaḥ paṃcadaśarcaṃ ca śrīkāmaḥ satataṃ japet ‖ 16 ‖*)
- शुचिर्भूत्वा (*śucirbhūtvā*)—having become pure by bathing and the like
- श्रियः (*śriyaḥ*)—of this Śrīsūkta that treats of the goddess Śrī
- जुहयात् (*juhayāt*)—must offer in the consecrated fire
- च (*ca*)—and the fifteen Ṛks of this sūkta

The man who desires to obtain the favour of the goddess Śrī and wealth should, with effort, purified by bathing and the like, offer every day in the consecrated fire oblations of ghee with the fifteen Ṛks of this Śrīsūkta. And he should also repeat this sūkta every day according to rule.

ओं । यः शुचिः प्रयतो भूत्वा जुहुयादाज्यमन्वहं । श्रियः पंचदशर्चं च श्रीकामः सततं जपेत् ॥ १६ ॥ (*oṃ | yaḥ śuciḥ prayato bhūtvā juhuyādājyamanvahaṃ | śriyaḥ paṃcadaśarcaṃ ca śrīkāmaḥ satataṃ japet ‖ 16 ‖*)

यः श्रीकामः स शुचिः प्रयतश्च भूत्वा सततं संकल्पदिनादि पंचदशाब्देषु प्रत्यहं स्वशाखोक्तविधानेनाग्निं संस्कृत्य श्रीसूक्तपंचदशऋग्भिः पंचदशाज्याहुतीर्हुत्वा ततः परं श्रियः श्रीसूक्तपंचदशर्चं साकल्येनैकवारमिति यथाशक्त्यखंडपारायणं कुर्यात् । अथवा पंचदशवारमखंडपारायणं कृत्वा तत एकैकामृचं विधिवद्यथासंख्यं जपेत् । तदशक्तौ लौकिकेऽग्नावपि पंचदश ऋग्भिः प्रत्यहं पंचदशाज्याहुतीर्हुत्वा पंचदश वारं श्रीसूक्तं जपेत्तस्य श्रीकामस्य तस्मिन्नेव (*yaḥ śrīkāmaḥ sa śuciḥ prayataśca bhūtvā satataṃ saṃkalpadinādi paṃcadaśābdeṣu pratyahaṃ svaśākhoktavidhānenāgniṃ saṃskṛtya śrīsūktapaṃcadaśaṛgbhiḥ paṃcadaśājyāhutīrhutvā tataḥ paraṃ śriyaḥ śrīsūktapaṃcadaśarcaṃ sākalyenaikavāramiti yathāśaktyakhaṃḍapārāyaṇaṃ kuryāt | athavā paṃcadaśavāramakhaṃḍapārāyaṇaṃ kṛtvā tata ekaikāmṛcaṃ vidhivadyathāsaṃkhyaṃ japet | tadaśaktau laukike 'gnāvapi paṃcadaśa ṛgbhiḥ pratyahaṃ paṃcadaśājyāhutīrhutvā paṃcadaśa vāraṃ śrīsūktaṃ japettasya śrīkāmasya tasminneva*)

जन्मनि महती श्रीप्राप्तिर्भविष्यतीति विज्ञायते । विधिवदनुष्ठानासमर्थस्य तु जन्मांतरे फलानुभवो भविष्यतीति सिद्धांतः ॥ (*janmani mahatī śrīprāptirbhaviṣyatīti vijñāyate | vidhivadanuṣṭhānāsamarthasya tu janmāṃtare phalānubhavo bhaviṣyatīti siddhāṃtaḥ ‖*) तदुक्तं मंत्ररहस्ये (*taduktaṃ maṃtrarahasye*)

अधिकारी यथादेशे यथाकाले यथामनुं । यादृग्विधानसंधानः प्रजपेत्तादृशं फलं ॥ कालदेशक्रियारूपाद्यनुरूपं लभेन्नरः । अत्युत्कटेन पुण्येन तस्मिन्नेव हि जन्मनि ॥ तत्फलं प्राप्नुयात्सिद्दो नात्र कार्या विचारणा । पुण्यस्यानुत्कटत्वे तु चिरात्किंचित्सलं लभेत् ॥ प्रतिबंधकबाहुल्ये फलं जन्मांतरे भवेत् । न देवतोषणं व्यर्थं भविष्यति कदाचन ॥ तस्मान्मंत्रं जपेद्योगी यतः शुद्धेंद्रियक्रियः ॥ इति ॥ (*adhikārī yathādeśe yathākāle yathāmanuṃ | yādṛgvidhānasaṃdhānaḥ prajapettādṛśaṃ phalaṃ ‖ kāladeśakriyārūpādyanurūpaṃ labhennaraḥ | atyutkaṭena puṇyena tasminneva hi janmani ‖ tatphalaṃ prāpnuyātsiddo nātra kāryā vicāraṇā | puṇyasyānutkaṭatve tu cirātkiṃcitsalaṃ labhet ‖ pratibaṃdhakabāhulye phalaṃ janmāṃtare bhavet | na devatoṣaṇaṃ vyarthaṃ bhaviṣyati kadācana ‖ tasmānmaṃtraṃ japedyogī yataḥ śuddheṃdriyakriyaḥ ‖ iti ‖*)

The man who desires wealth, grain and the like, having become pure, from the day on which he makes his resolve, for fifteen years, should offer in the consecrated fire fifteen oblations of ghee, one with each Ṛk of this Śrīsūkta, and every day repeat those fifteen Ṛks according to rule. Or else he should perform the recitation as far as he is able. Or, putting the fifteen Ṛks together, he should perform the unbroken recitation (akhaṇḍa-pārāyaṇa) and afterwards repeat each single Ṛk the prescribed number of times. If he lacks the strength even for that, he should every day offer fifteen oblations of ghee with the fifteen Ṛks in the ordinary fire itself and afterwards repeat the Śrīsūkta fifteen times. By this it is known by experience that the man who desires wealth obtains great prosperity in this very birth. If one lacks the strength to perform the observance according to rule, without the slightest deficiency, then even if he does the repetition and the rest as far as he is able, the fruit comes to him accordingly without fail. If, while the repetition and the rest are being done, many obstacles arise and the observance is not completed, the experience of the fruit will come in a later birth: this is the established conclusion. This matter is stated in the work called Mantrarahasya in the following way.

The man who is qualified to repeat this sūkta, even if for other reasons he is unable to perform the repetition according to rule without the slightest deficiency, receives the fruit in as far as he repeats this mantra, suitably to place and time, that is, as the occasion allows. By the power of exceedingly great merit the mantra is accomplished in this very birth, and its fruit too is obtained. In this matter there is no doubt. If the power of merit is not so great, some fruit is obtained a little, after some time.

If many obstacles arise and the repetition is not carried on, then however small the repetition performed up to then, its fruit will be obtained in the next birth. Repetition, worship and the like done for the pleasure of the deity are never in vain. Therefore the yogin (or the one who repeats) should, having conquered his senses and being pure, repeat these mantras of the Śrīsūkta with devotion.
Here ends the explanation of the Ṛk that is the praise of the fruit.

Notice: in the Śrīsūkta that is stated among the Appendix mantras of the Ṛgveda there are only fifteen Ṛks. One Ṛk, which describes the praise of the fruit, stands at its end. It is well known as the mantra in the form of the praise of the fruit of the Śrīsūkta, spoken by the author of the Nirukta. After reciting these, it is the custom to recite some verses that praise Lakṣmī, or the goddess Śrī. Since these are in easy language, no one has written commentaries and the like upon them. In their number and in the order of recitation, differences and variant readings are seen, as they are in use in different places. As far as possible, these verses and their main purport are explained here in the order that is customary in reciting them.
पद्मासने पद्मऊरू पद्माक्षी पद्मसंभवे । त्वं मां भजस्व पद्माक्षी येन सौख्यं लभाम्यहं ॥ (*padmāsane padmaūrū padmākṣī padmasaṃbhave | tvaṃ māṃ bhajasva padmākṣī yena saukhyaṃ labhāmyahaṃ ‖*)

O Mahālakṣmī, you have made the lotus itself your seat and sit upon it. Your thighs are tender like the lotus. Your eyes are wide and charming like the lotus. You are born in the lotus itself. O Lakṣmī, whose eyes are charming like the lotus, show favour to me, come to my side and abide in my dwelling-place. Thereby I shall come to obtain happiness.
अश्वदायिा गोदायिा धनदायिा महाधने । धनं मे जुषतां देवि सर्वकामार्थसिद्धये ॥ (*aśvadāyiā godāyiā dhanadāyiā mahādhane | dhanaṃ me juṣatāṃ devi sarvakāmārthasiddhaye ‖*)

O Lakṣmī who have great wealth, you are the giver to devotees of horses, cows and riches. Therefore, O goddess, for the accomplishment of all desired aims, that is, so that all the wishes that I desire may be fulfilled, bestow wealth upon me and show favour.
पुत्रपौत्रधनं धान्यं हस्यश्वादिगवे रथं । प्रजानां भवसि माता आयुष्मंतं करोतु मां ॥ (*putrapautradhanaṃ dhānyaṃ hasyaśvādigave rathaṃ | prajānāṃ bhavasi mātā āyuṣmaṃtaṃ karotu māṃ ‖*)
O goddess, mother of all creatures, give me children, grandchildren, wealth, grain, elephants, horses, cows and chariots, all of these, and favour me by making me long-lived.

चंद्राभां लक्ष्मीमीशानां सूर्यभां श्रियमीश्वरीं । चंद्रसूर्याग्नि संकाशां श्रीमहालक्ष्मीमुपास्महे ॥ (*caṃdrābhāṃ lakṣmīmīśānāṃ sūryabhāṃ śriyamīśvarīṃ | caṃdrasūryāgni saṃkāśāṃ śrīmahālakṣmīmupāsmahe ‖*)

We worship the deity called Śrī Mahālakṣmī, who shines with a cool and charming radiance like the moon; who is the mistress of the whole world; who blazes with exceeding splendour like the sun; who is the mistress of prosperity; and who shines with the surpassing splendour that would arise if the splendours of the moon, the sun and fire were all added together.
धनमग्नि र्धनं वायुर्धनं सूर्यो धनं वसुः । धनमिंद्रो बृहस्पतिर्वरुणं धनमश्नुते ॥ (*dhanamagni rdhanaṃ vāyurdhanaṃ sūryo dhanaṃ vasuḥ | dhanamiṃdro bṛhaspatirvaruṇaṃ dhanamaśnute ‖*)
O goddess, the deities Agni, Vāyu, Sūrya, the eight Vasus, Indra, Bṛhaspati, Varuṇa and the rest enjoy the wealth and prosperity that they desire only through your favour.
वैनतेय सोमं पिब सोमं पिबतु वृत्रहा । सोमं धनस्य सोमिनो मह्यं ददातु सोमिनः ॥ (*vainateya somaṃ piba somaṃ pibatu vṛtrahā | somaṃ dhanasya somino mahyaṃ dadātu sominaḥ ‖*)

O Garuḍa, son of Vinatā, drink the soma juice (or the nectar). O Indra, slayer of the demon Vṛtra, you too drink soma. O all you gods who are worthy to drink soma, all of you drink the soma that comes from wealth. And grant wealth and the rest to me also, who drink soma.

न क्रोधो न च मात्सर्यो न लोभो नाशुभा मतिः । भवंतु कृतपुण्यानां भक्तानां श्रीसूक्तं जपेत्सदा ॥ (*na krodho na ca mātsaryo na lobho nāśubhā matiḥ | bhavaṃtu kṛtapuṇyānāṃ bhaktānāṃ śrīsūktaṃ japetsadā ‖*)

For the virtuous people who are devotees of the goddess Śrī and who at all times repeat the Śrīsūkta, there are no such faults as anger, envy (jealousy), greed (miserliness), and a mind set on evil deeds.
वर्षंतु ते विभावरि दिवो अभ्रस्य विद्युतः । रोहंतु सर्वबीजान्यव ब्रह्मद्विषो जहि ॥ (*varṣaṃtu te vibhāvari divo abhrasya vidyutaḥ | rohaṃtu sarvabījānyava brahmadviṣo jahi ‖*)

O radiant goddess Śrī, by your favour may the clouds that stand in the sky, accompanied by thunder and lightning, pour down rain. Refreshed by that rain, may all the seeds and the like in the earth sprout and grow into seedlings. O goddess, destroy the haters of Brahman.

पद्मप्रिये पद्मिनि पद्महस्ते पद्मालये पद्मदळायताक्षि । विश्वप्रिये विष्णुमनोनुकूले त्वत्पादपद्मं मयि संनिधत्स्व ॥ (*padmapriye padmini padmahaste padmālaye padmadaḷāyatākṣi | viśvapriye viṣṇumanonukūle tvatpādapadmaṃ mayi saṃnidhatsva ‖*)

O Mahālakṣmī, the padma, or lotus, is dear to you. You came into being from the lotus itself. In both your hands you hold lotuses. The lotus is your dwelling-place. Your eyes are wide and charming like the petals of the lotus flower. You are dear to the whole world, that is, to all people. You act in accordance with the mind of your husband Viṣṇu. Being endowed with such qualities, set your feet, tender like the lotus, upon me, your devotee, and show favour.

या सा पद्मासनस्था विपुलकटितटी पद्मपत्रायताक्षी गंभीरावर्तनाभिस्तनभरनमिता शुभ्रवस्त्रोत्तरीया । लक्ष्मीर्दिव्यैर्गजेंद्रॆर्मणिगणखचितैः स्नापिता हेमकुंभैर्नित्यं सा पद्महस्ता मम वसतु गृहे सर्वमांगल्ययुक्ता ॥ (*yā sā padmāsanasthā vipulakaṭitaṭī padmapatrāyatākṣī gaṃbhīrāvartanābhistanabharanamitā śubhravastrottarīyā | lakṣmīrdivyairgajeṃdrèrmaṇigaṇakhacitaiḥ snāpitā hemakuṃbhairnityaṃ sā padmahastā mama vasatu gṛhe sarvamāṃgalyayuktā ‖*)

The goddess Śrī, who bears the name Śrī Mahālakṣmī, is seated on a lotus seat. She shines with broad hips, with eyes wide like lotus petals, and with a deep navel. Her body is bent as if by the weight of her breasts, and she wears a spotless garment. Anointed by the trunks of the best of elephants with pure water from golden pots studded with many jewels, holding a lotus flower in her hands, and resplendent with all auspicious ornaments, may this Mahālakṣmī, endowed with all good fortune and bestowing auspiciousness, dwell always in my house.

लक्ष्मीं क्षीरसमुद्रराजतनयां श्रीरंगधामेश्वरीं दासीभूतसमस्तदेववनितां लोकैकदीपांकुरां । श्रीमन्मंदकटाक्षलब्धविभवद्ब्रह्मेंद्रगंगाधरां त्वां त्रैलोक्यकुटुंबिनीं सरसिजां वंदे मुकुंदप्रियां ॥ (*lakṣmīṃ kṣīrasamudrarājatanayāṃ śrīraṃgadhāmeśvarīṃ dāsībhūtasamastadevavanitāṃ lokaikadīpāṃkurāṃ | śrīmanmaṃdakaṭākṣalabdhavibhavadbrahmeṃdragaṃgādharāṃ tvāṃ trailokyakuṭuṃbinīṃ sarasijāṃ vaṃde mukuṃdapriyāṃ ‖*)

Since Śrī Mahālakṣmī arose at the time of the churning of the ocean, she is renowned as the daughter of the ocean of milk, the best of oceans. She is the wife of Śrī Viṣṇu, who dwells in the holy place Śrīraṅga under the name Śrīraṅga. All the wives of the gods serve this Lakṣmī in the manner of maidservants, to win the goddess's favour. She shines with a radiance equal to that of the sun, who makes all the worlds grow. The gods, Brahmā, Indra, Īśvara and the rest, long for the favour to be obtained from this goddess's gentle smile. She nourishes the three worlds like a mother. With devotion I bow to this goddess called Mahālakṣmī, who arose in a lotus flower and is dear to Śrī Viṣṇu.
सिद्धलक्ष्मीर्मोक्षलक्ष्मीर्जयलक्ष्मीः सरस्वती । श्रीलक्ष्मीर्वरलक्ष्मीश्च प्रसन्ना भव सर्वदा ॥ (*siddhalakṣmīrmokṣalakṣmīrjayalakṣmīḥ sarasvatī | śrīlakṣmīrvaralakṣmīśca prasannā bhava sarvadā ‖*)

O Mahālakṣmī, since all aims are accomplished for those who worship you, you have the name Siddhalakṣmī; since you grant liberation, you are praised as Mokṣalakṣmī; since you give victory in battles and in all undertakings, as Jayalakṣmī; since you preside over the Veda, as Sarasvatī; since you are the mistress of wealth, as the goddess Śrī; and since you give devotees the boons each desires, as Varalakṣmī; thus you are praised by many kinds of excellent names. Being such, be ever gracious of mind towards me.

वरांकुशौ पाशमभीतिमुद्रां करैर्वहंतीं कमलासनस्थां । बालार्ककोटिप्रतिभां त्रिणेत्रां भजेऽहमाद्यां जगदीश्वरीं तां ॥ (*varāṃkuśau pāśamabhītimudrāṃ karairvahaṃtīṃ kamalāsanasthāṃ | bālārkakoṭipratibhāṃ triṇetrāṃ bhaje 'hamādyāṃ jagadīśvarīṃ tāṃ ‖*)

This Mahālakṣmī, seated on a lotus or on a lotus seat, holds in her four hands the boon-giving hand, the goad, the noose and the gesture of fearlessness, and shines with three eyes and with the radiance of ten million suns rising at one time. With devotion I worship this goddess, the mistress of the whole world.
सर्वमंगळमांगल्ये शिवे सर्वार्थसाधके । शरण्ये त्र्यंबके देवि नारायणि नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ (*sarvamaṃgaḷamāṃgalye śive sarvārthasādhake | śaraṇye tryaṃbake devi nārāyaṇi namo 'stu te ‖*)

O goddess, you are the embodiment of auspiciousness for all auspicious things, that is, you are the foremost; or you are she who brings auspiciousness to all, who accomplishes all the desired aims of devotees, and who is worthy to be a refuge. You are praised by various names, as the wife of Maheśvara and as the wife of Nārāyaṇa. To you, such as you are, here is my salutation.
विष्णुपत्नीं क्षमां देवीं माधवीं माधवप्रियां । विष्णोः प्रियसखीं देवीं नमाम्यच्युतवल्लभां ॥ (*viṣṇupatnīṃ kṣamāṃ devīṃ mādhavīṃ mādhavapriyāṃ | viṣṇoḥ priyasakhīṃ devīṃ namāmyacyutavallabhāṃ ‖*)

I bow to Śrī Mahālakṣmī, the wife of Viṣṇu, who has the nature of forbearance, who is exceedingly dear to Mādhava, the lord of Lakṣmī, and who is like a dear friend to Viṣṇu, the wife of Śrī Mahāviṣṇu.
महालक्ष्मी च विद्महे विष्णुपत्नै च धीमहि । तन्नो लक्ष्मीः प्रचोदयात् ॥ (*mahālakṣmī ca vidmahe viṣṇupatnai ca dhīmahi | tanno lakṣmīḥ pracodayāt ‖*)
Let us meditate on that Śrī Lakṣmī, whose divine power, belonging to Śrī Mahālakṣmī who bears the name of Viṣṇu's wife, impels us in all undertakings.

श्रीर्वर्चस्य वायुष्यमारोग्यमाविधात्पवमानं महीयते । धनं धान्यं पशुं बहुपुत्रलाभं शतसंवत्सरं दीर्घमायुः ॥ (*śrīrvarcasya vāyuṣyamārogyamāvidhātpavamānaṃ mahīyate | dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ paśuṃ bahuputralābhaṃ śatasaṃvatsaraṃ dīrghamāyuḥ ‖*)

To those who repeat the Śrīsūkta, Śrī Mahālakṣmī grants radiance (lustre and brightness of the face), long life, health, excellence, wealth, grain, wealth of cattle, a numerous progeny of sons, and a full span of a hundred years. That man is honoured and respected by all.
Here ends the explanation of the meaning of the Śrīsūkta.
Some verses recited at the end of a maṇḍala.
विश्वेश्वर विरूपाक्ष विश्वरूप सदाशिव । शरणं भव भूतेश करुणाकर शंकर ॥ (*viśveśvara virūpākṣa viśvarūpa sadāśiva | śaraṇaṃ bhava bhūteśa karuṇākara śaṃkara ‖*) **GLOSS**
हर शंभो महादेव विश्वेशामरवल्लभ । शिव शंकर सर्वात्मन् नीलकंठ नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ (*hara śaṃbho mahādeva viśveśāmaravallabha | śiva śaṃkara sarvātman nīlakaṃṭha namo 'stu te ‖*) **GLOSS**
मृत्युंजयाय रुद्राय नीलकंठाय शंभवे । अमृतेशाय सर्वाय महादेवाय ते नमः ॥ (*mṛtyuṃjayāya rudrāya nīlakaṃṭhāya śaṃbhave | amṛteśāya sarvāya mahādevāya te namaḥ ‖*) **GLOSS**
एतानि शिवनामानि यः पठेन्नियतः सकृत् । नास्ति मृत्युभयं तस्य पापरोगादि किंचन ॥ (*etāni śivanāmāni yaḥ paṭhenniyataḥ sakṛt | nāsti mṛtyubhayaṃ tasya pāparogādi kiṃcana ‖*) **GLOSS**
यज्ञेशाच्युत गोविंद माधवानंत केशव । कृष्ण विष्णो हृषिकेश वासुदेव नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ (*yajñeśācyuta goviṃda mādhavānaṃta keśava | kṛṣṇa viṣṇo hṛṣikeśa vāsudeva namo 'stu te ‖*) **GLOSS**
कृष्णाय गोपिनाथाय चक्रिणे मुरवैरिणे । अमृतेशाय गोपाय गोविंदाय नमो नमः ॥ (*kṛṣṇāya gopināthāya cakriṇe muravairiṇe | amṛteśāya gopāya goviṃdāya namo namaḥ ‖*) **GLOSS**
वासनाद्दासुदेवोऽसि वासितं ते जगत्रयं । सर्वभूतनिवासोऽसि वासुदेव नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ (*vāsanāddāsudevo 'si vāsitaṃ te jagatrayaṃ | sarvabhūtanivāso 'si vāsudeva namo 'stu te ‖*) **GLOSS**
दश सप्त च नामानि मंडलांतेषु यः पठेत् । स शिवस्य पदं गत्वा शिवलोके महीयते ॥ (*daśa sapta ca nāmāni maṃḍalāṃteṣu yaḥ paṭhet | sa śivasya padaṃ gatvā śivaloke mahīyate ‖*) **GLOSS**
एतानि शिवनामानि मंडलांते सकृत्पठेश् ॥ (*etāni śivanāmāni maṃḍalāṃte sakṛtpaṭheś ‖*) **GLOSS**
वेदार्थस्य प्रकाशेन तमो हार्दं निवारयन् । पुमर्थांश्च तुरो देयाद्विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरः ॥ (*vedārthasya prakāśena tamo hārdaṃ nivārayan | pumarthāṃśca turo deyādvidyātīrthamaheśvaraḥ ‖*) **GLOSS**

इति श्रीमद्राजाधिराज परमेश्वर वैदिकमार्गप्रवर्तक श्री वीरबुक्क भूपालसाम्राज्यधुरंधरेण सायणाचार्येण विरचिते माधवीये वेदार्थप्रकाशे यक्संहिताभाष्ये पंचमं मंडलं समाप्तं ॥ (*iti śrīmadrājādhirāja parameśvara vaidikamārgapravartaka śrī vīrabukka bhūpālasāmrājyadhuraṃdhareṇa sāyaṇācāryeṇa viracite mādhavīye vedārthaprakāśe yaksaṃhitābhāṣye paṃcamaṃ maṃḍalaṃ samāptaṃ ‖*) **GLOSS**
Here ends the fifth Maṇḍala in the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, together with the Bhāṣya of Śrī Sāyaṇa and with the Kannada translation.

यदक्षरपदभ्रष्टं मात्राहीनं तु यद्भवेत् । तत्सर्वक्षं क्षम्यतां देव वागीश्वरनमोऽस्तुते ॥ (*yadakṣarapadabhraṣṭaṃ mātrāhīnaṃ tu yadbhavet | tatsarvakṣaṃ kṣamyatāṃ deva vāgīśvaranamo 'stute ‖*) **GLOSS**
वागीशाद्याः सुमनसः सर्वार्थानामुपक्रमे । यं नत्वा कृतकृत्याः स्युस्तं नमामि गजाननं ॥ (*vāgīśādyāḥ sumanasaḥ sarvārthānāmupakrame | yaṃ natvā kṛtakṛtyāḥ syustaṃ namāmi gajānanaṃ ‖*) **GLOSS**
यस्य निश्चसितं वेदा यो वेदेभ्योऽखिलं जगत् । निर्ममे तमहं वंदे विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरं ॥ (*yasya niścasitaṃ vedā yo vedebhyo 'khilaṃ jagat | nirmame tamahaṃ vaṃde vidyātīrthamaheśvaraṃ ‖*) **GLOSS**
वेदः शिवः शिवो वेदो वेदाध्यायी सदाशिवः । तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन वेदमेव सदा जपेत् ॥ (*vedaḥ śivaḥ śivo vedo vedādhyāyī sadāśivaḥ | tasmātsarvaprayatnena vedameva sadā japet ‖*) **GLOSS**
Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, with the Bhāṣya of Sāyaṇa
**The seers who saw the sūktas of the sixth maṇḍala**

In the Ṛk-saṃhitā the sixth maṇḍala is renowned as the Bhāradvāja maṇḍala. Although other seers of the line of Bharadvāja are also the seers of some sūktas of this maṇḍala, the sūktas seen by Bharadvāja are by far the most numerous, and therefore this maṇḍala is renowned by this name.
सपुत्रस्य तु तस्यैतन्मंडलं षष्ठमुच्यते (*saputrasya tu tasyaitanmaṃḍalaṃ ṣaṣṭhamucyate*)

Śaunaka and others have stated clearly that this maṇḍala, seen by Bharadvāja together with his son, is renowned by the name Bhāradvāja maṇḍala. The seers Suhotra, Śunahotra, Nara, Śaṃyu, Garga, Ṛjiśvan and Pāyu, so many of them, belonging to the line of Bharadvāja, are praised as seers of the sūktas of the sixth maṇḍala. The line of Bharadvāja is exceedingly ancient. The name Bharadvāja too is exceedingly renowned throughout the Veda, the Purāṇas and the Itihāsas. But in all these places the one who is praised

is not to be understood as a single seer. Three or four seers bearing the name Bharadvāja are famed in the Purāṇas, Itihāsas and the like. Although in the present context the introduction of the Bharadvāja seers specified in Vedic literature is the main concern, it is necessary also to know the individual nature of the other Bharadvājas; so we may first examine the greatness of the seers specified in Vedic sentences, and afterwards see in how many places, and in what contexts, this name is renowned in the Purāṇas, Itihāsas and the like.
**The seer of the sūktas of the sixth maṇḍala of the Ṛk-saṃhitā.**

The Bharadvāja who saw the sūktas of the Ṛk-saṃhitā belongs to the line of Aṅgiras. He is the son of Bṛhaspati. The greatness of his line and the manner of his origin are told in the Brahma-deity text in this way.
त्रिसांवत्सरिकं सत्त्रं प्रजाकामः प्रजापतिः । आहरत्सहितः साध्यैर्विश्वेदेवैः सहेति च ॥ (*trisāṃvatsarikaṃ sattraṃ prajākāmaḥ prajāpatiḥ | āharatsahitaḥ sādhyairviśvedevaiḥ saheti ca ‖*)
Prajāpati, desiring offspring, performed a sattra of three years. At that time the Sādhyas and the Viśvedevas became his helpers.
तत्र वाग्दीक्षणीयायामाजगाम शरीरिणी । तां दृष्ट्वा युगपत्तत्र कस्याथ वरुणस्य च ॥ (*tatra vāgdīkṣaṇīyāyāmājagāma śarīriṇī | tāṃ dṛṣṭvā yugapattatra kasyātha varuṇasya ca ‖*)

At the time of this rite the goddess of speech came to that place in bodily form. At that time Prajāpati and Varuṇa together saw her. Seeing her form, beautiful and exceedingly attractive, both of them alike, together, felt a disturbance of mind.
शुक्रं चस्कंद तद्वायुरग्नौ प्रास्यद्यदृच्छया । ततोऽर्चिभ्यो भृगुर्जज्ञे अंगारेष्वंगिरा ऋषिः ॥ ( (*śukraṃ caskaṃda tadvāyuragnau prāsyadyadṛcchayā | tato 'rcibhyo bhṛgurjajñe aṃgāreṣvaṃgirā ṛṣiḥ ‖ (*)
Then at once both of them had an emission of semen. Then Vāyu, as he pleased, offered it into the fire. Then from the flames of that fire Bhṛgu arose, and from the embers the seer Aṅgiras.
योऽंगिरेभ्य यषिर्जज्ञे तस्य पुत्रो बृहस्पतिः । बृहस्पतेर्भरद्वाजो विदथीति य उच्यते ॥ (*yo 'ṃgirebhya yaṣirjajñe tasya putro bṛhaspatiḥ | bṛhaspaterbharadvājo vidathīti ya ucyate ‖*)
Bṛhaspati was born from the seer Aṅgiras, who arose from the embers. The son of Bṛhaspati is Bharadvāja. He has also another name, Vidathi.
मरुत्स्वासीद्गुरुर्यश्च स एवांगिरसो नपात् । नपुत्रस्य तु तस्यैतत् मंडलं षष्ठमुच्यते ॥ (*marutsvāsīdgururyaśca sa evāṃgiraso napāt | naputrasya tu tasyaitat maṃḍalaṃ ṣaṣṭhamucyate ‖*)

This same Bhāradvāja, who has the other name Vidathi, is the grandson of Aṅgiras. It is a matter well known, in some places in the Śrutis also, that the sūktas of the sixth maṇḍala of the Ṛk-saṃhitā were composed by this Bhāradvāja and by his sons, grandsons and others. This is the description of the lineage of the seer Bharadvāja.

This Bhāradvāja was the house-priest of one named Abhyāvartin; and it is known from the sentences of the Ṛk-saṃhitā that he was honoured by him in many ways and helped him in many ways. The same matter is told in the Bṛhaddevatā in this way.
अभ्यावर्ती जायमानः प्रस्तोकश्चैव सांज्ञयः । आजग्मतुर्भरदाजं जितौ वारशिख्ययुधि ॥ (*abhyāvartī jāyamānaḥ prastokaścaiva sāṃjñayaḥ | ājagmaturbharadājaṃ jitau vāraśikhyayudhi ‖*)
Abhyāvartin Jāyamāna, who had been defeated by the group called the Vāraśikhas, and Prastoka, the son of Sṛñjaya, came to Bharadvāja and sought his help.
अभिगम्योचतुस्तौ तं प्रसाद्याख्याय नामनी । युधि वारशिखैर्ब्रह्मन्नावां निद्दि विनिर्जितौ ॥ (*abhigamyocatustau taṃ prasādyākhyāya nāmanī | yudhi vāraśikhairbrahmannāvāṃ niddi vinirjitau ‖*)

Then Abhyāvartin Jāyamāna and Prastoka, son of Sṛñjaya, came to Bharadvāja, offered him worship and the like according to rule, greeted him pronouncing their own names, and spoke thus: "O teacher, knower of Brahman, know that we have been conquered by the Vāraśikhas." They told him fully of their defeat and of the enemies who had caused it. Then:
भवत्पुरोहितावानां क्षत्रबंधूञ्च येवहि । क्षत्रं तदपि विज्ञेयं ब्रह्म यत्पाति शाश्वतं ॥ (*bhavatpurohitāvānāṃ kṣatrabaṃdhūñca yevahi | kṣatraṃ tadapi vijñeyaṃ brahma yatpāti śāśvataṃ ‖*)

"O great seer, you are the family priest of all of us. With your help we shall be able to conquer all the Kṣatrabandhus. The power that can protect and honour the power of Brahman, that alone is the true
Kṣatra power. All the others merely joined the Kṣatriya group in name and became engaged in evil deeds. "Therefore help us to destroy such evil powers," they prayed. Then:
ऋषिस्तौ तु तथेत्युक्त्वा पायुं पुत्रमभाषत । अधर्षणीयौ शत्रूणां कुरुष्टौ नृपाविति ॥ (*ṛṣistau tu tathetyuktvā pāyuṃ putramabhāṣata | adharṣaṇīyau śatrūṇāṃ kuruṣṭau nṛpāviti ‖*)

The sage Bharadvāja agreed to help them, made his consent known to them, and then gave this command to his son Pāyu: "Help these two kings, and be the giver of strength to them, so that they conquer their enemies, and after the victory become such that no enemy can oppose them." When he said this, Pāyu, thus commanded by his father, accepted, "So be it," and became their helper in many ways. The details of this will be given later, when Pāyu is dealt with.

Thus Bharadvāja is praised as one born with a divine portion from birth, and as one who, possessing the Brahma-splendour that upholds the Kṣatra duty even in worldly affairs, helped many Kṣatriyas and so helped the protection of Brahman. Therefore we may now examine closely in which contexts, and in what manner, these two kinds of power of Bharadvāja, famed as the seer of the sūktas of the Ṛksaṃhitā, are praised, and what his manifold greatnesses are. In the Ṛksaṃhitā Bharadvāja himself declares the matter of his lineage in this way:

धन्या चिद्दि त्वे धिषणा वष्टि प्र देवाञ्जन गृणते यजध्यै । वेपिष्ठो अंगिरसां यद्ध विप्रो मधु च्छंदो भवति रेभ इष्टौ ॥ (*dhanyā ciddi tve dhiṣaṇā vaṣṭi pra devāñjana gṛṇate yajadhyai | vepiṣṭho aṃgirasāṃ yaddha vipro madhu cchaṃdo bhavati rebha iṣṭau ‖*)

Among the Aṅgirases, this Bharadvāja, the most excellent praiser (रेभः स्तोता भरद्वाजः (*rebhaḥ stotā bharadvājaḥ*)), offers most excellent praises to Agni in the sacrifice performed for the sake of wealth. Thus he has declared that he belongs to the family of Aṅgiras. Moreover:

याभिः सूर्यं परियाथः परावति मंधातारं क्षैत्रपत्येष्वावतं । याभिर्विप्रं त्र भरद्वाजमावतं ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विनागतं ॥ ( (*yābhiḥ sūryaṃ pariyāthaḥ parāvati maṃdhātāraṃ kṣaitrapatyeṣvāvataṃ | yābhirvipraṃ tra bharadvājamāvataṃ tābhirū ṣu ūtibhiraśvināgataṃ ‖ (*)

O Aśvin deities, with whatever protections you went forward to free the Sun, who dwells in a distant region and was enveloped by Rāhu in the form of darkness, from the eclipse; and with whatever helps you protected the seer Māndhātṛ in the discharge of his duties of lordship; and moreover with whatever protections you well protected the wise seer Bharadvāja by giving him food, with all those protections come also to us with kindness. This verse tells how Bharadvāja obtained the help of the gods.

There is a story that the Aśvin deities seated Bharadvāja, who desired wealth, in their own chariot, brought him, and gave him abundant wealth. (भरद्वाजऋषिर्धनकामोऽश्विनौ तुष्टाव । तस्य स्वरथेनानीयाश्विन् प्रभूतं धनं ददतुरिति । (*bharadvājaṛṣirdhanakāmo 'śvinau tuṣṭāva | tasya svarathenānīyāśvin prabhūtaṃ dhanaṃ dadaturiti |*) Sā. Bhā.)⟨NOTE:185⟩ Because he had very great majesty, all the gods came in person and favoured Bharadvāja. The practice of the most excellent celibacy (brahmacarya) is one of these greatnesses. Explaining this point, the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa describes a situation in the form of a legend in this way:

भरद्वाजो ह त्रिभिरायुर्भिब्रह्मचर्यमुवास । तग्ं ह जीर्णिग् स्थविरग्ं शयानं । इंद्र उप प्रज्योवाच । भरद्वाज । यत्ते चतुर्थमायुः र्दद्यां । किमेनेन कुर्या इति । ब्रह्मचर्यमेवैनेन चरेयमिति होवाच । तग्ं ह त्रीन्गिरिरूपानविज्ञातानिव दर्शयांचकार । तेषाग्ं हैकैकस्मान्मुष्टिनाददे । स होवाच । भरद्वाजेत्यामंत्र्य । वेदा वा एते। अनंता वै वेदाः । एतद्वा एतैस्त्रिभिरायुर्भिरन्ववोचथाः । अथ त इतरदननूक्तमेव एहीमं विद्धि । आयं वै सर्वविद्यॆति । तस्मै हैतमग्निग्ं सावित्रमुवाच । तग्ं स विदित्वा! अमृतो भूत्वा। स्वर्ग० लोकमियाय । आदित्यस्य सायुज्यं । अमृतो हैव भूत्वा । स्वर्ग० लोकमेति । आदित्यस्य सायुज्यं । य एवं वेद । (*bharadvājo ha tribhirāyurbhibrahmacaryamuvāsa | tagṃ ha jīrṇig sthaviragṃ śayānaṃ | iṃdra upa prajyovāca | bharadvāja | yatte caturthamāyuḥ rdadyāṃ | kimenena kuryā iti | brahmacaryamevainena careyamiti hovāca | tagṃ ha trīngirirūpānavijñātāniva darśayāṃcakāra | teṣāgṃ haikaikasmānmuṣṭinādade | sa hovāca | bharadvājetyāmaṃtrya | vedā vā ete| anaṃtā vai vedāḥ | etadvā etaistribhirāyurbhiranvavocathāḥ | atha ta itaradananūktameva ehīmaṃ viddhi | āyaṃ vai sarvavidyèti | tasmai haitamagnigṃ sāvitramuvāca | tagṃ sa viditvā! amṛto bhūtvā| svarga0 lokamiyāya | ādityasya sāyujyaṃ | amṛto haiva bhūtvā | svarga0 lokameti | ādityasya sāyujyaṃ | ya evaṃ veda |*)

The great seer Bharadvāja kept celibacy in three lives in succession. At the end of the third life, when he had become old, weak in body and was in his last state, Indra approached him and asked: "O Bharadvāja, if I give you a fourth life, what benefit will you obtain from it? How will you use it?" Then Bharadvāja said: "I will use that fourth life also for the practice of celibacy, just as I used the other three lives." Then Indra showed him three huge and most wonderful mountain-like objects. Taking a handful from each of them, he said to Bharadvāja: "O Bharadvāja, these are the three Vedas, and they are endless. In your three previous lives you have studied and recited only this much of these three Vedas. You have not made known the rest. Now study this Agni-Sāvitra and meditate on it. That is the great knowledge that teaches universal knowledge."

Thus the greatness of Bharadvāja is praised in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa. The Bṛhat-sāman, the support and source of Kṣatra power, which is the best of all powers, was made by Bharadvāja himself; so both when the power of the Bṛhat-sāman is described and when the power of Kṣatra is praised, the greatness of Bharadvāja is highly extolled. Praising this very matter, the Ṛksaṃhitā itself says:

अविंदन् ते अतिहितं यदासीद्यज्ञस्य धाम परमं गुहा यत् । धातुद्युर्त्यानात्सवितुश्च विष्णोर्भरद्याजो बृहदा चक्रे अग्नेः ॥ (*aviṃdan te atihitaṃ yadāsīdyajñasya dhāma paramaṃ guhā yat | dhātudyurtyānātsavituśca viṣṇorbharadyājo bṛhadā cakre agneḥ ‖*)

The Bṛhat-sāman, which was the supporter of sacrifices and the like and possessed an excellent bodily form, lay hidden in a cave, that is, in a deep region unknown to anyone. Dhātṛ and the others realised it and made it manifest to the world. Bharadvāja obtained this same Bṛhat-sāman from this Dhātṛ, and also from Savitṛ, Viṣṇu and Agni, and made it favourable to sacrifices and the like. Describing this same point, the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa says:

तमु ष्टुहि यो अभिभूत्योजा इति सूक्तमभिवदभिभूतै रूपं । अषाळ्मुग्रं सहमानमाभिरित्युग्रवत्सहमानवत्तत् क्षत्रस्य रूपं । तत्पंचदशर्चं भवत्योजो वा इंद्रियं वीर्यं पंचदश ओजः क्षत्रं वीर्यं राजन्यस्तदेनमोजसा क्षत्रेण वीर्येण समर्धयति तद्बारद्वाजं भवति भारद्वाजं वै बृहदार्षेयेण सलोमा एष ह नाव क्षत्रिययज्ञः समृद्धो यो बृहत्पृष्णस्तस्माद्यत्र क्व च क्षत्रियो यजेत बृहदेव तत्र पृष्टं स्यात्तत्समृद्धं ॥ (*tamu ṣṭuhi yo abhibhūtyojā iti sūktamabhivadabhibhūtai rūpaṃ | aṣāḷmugraṃ sahamānamābhirityugravatsahamānavattat kṣatrasya rūpaṃ | tatpaṃcadaśarcaṃ bhavatyojo vā iṃdriyaṃ vīryaṃ paṃcadaśa ojaḥ kṣatraṃ vīryaṃ rājanyastadenamojasā kṣatreṇa vīryeṇa samardhayati tadbāradvājaṃ bhavati bhāradvājaṃ vai bṛhadārṣeyeṇa salomā eṣa ha nāva kṣatriyayajñaḥ samṛddho yo bṛhatpṛṣṇastasmādyatra kva ca kṣatriyo yajeta bṛhadeva tatra pṛṣṭaṃ syāttatsamṛddhaṃ ‖*)

Thus Bharadvāja and the Bṛhat-sāman that belongs to him are praised. The mantra तमु ष्टुहि (*tamu ṣṭuhi*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-18-1) was composed by Bharadvāja; it is in praise of Indra. Here the use of the word अभि (*abhi*) indicates victory. अषाळ्व (*aṣāḷva*), उग्र (*ugra*) and सहमान (*sahamāna*) all indicate the terrible power of the Kṣatriya and his strength to confront the enemy. The number of mantras in this sūkta is fifteen. The Pañcadaśa (stoma) is the symbol of Ojas, Kṣatra and Vīrya. The Rājanya possesses all these qualities. The sūkta whose mantras have the power of the Rājanya, such as Ojas, Vīrya and Kṣatra, is the work of Bharadvāja. In the same way the Bṛhat-sāman too is connected with Bharadvāja. Since the making of both belongs to Bharadvāja, the power of both is one and the same.

Therefore the sacrifice of any Kṣatriya that has the Pṛṣṭha in the form of the Bṛhat-sāman is the one that attains completeness. So whichever Kṣatriya, on whatever occasion, wishes to perform a sacrifice, then the Bṛhat-sāman alone must be arranged as the Pṛṣṭha. Only then does the sacrifice attain perfection. Thus the Bṛhat-sāman, which brings Kṣatra power to perfection, is praised as the work of the great seer Bharadvāja, its source. If the greatness of this Bṛhat-sāman is understood, the nature of the great seer who is its author is understood still better; hence it is now necessary to know what the nature of this sāman is and what its greatness is.

In describing the Mahāvrata, the Mahāvrata has two wings, the right wing and the left wing. ⟨NOTE:186⟩ (Right wing and left wing). Of these, the Rathantara-sāman is the right wing and the Bṛhat-sāman is the left wing. The Rathantara made by Vasiṣṭha reflects Agni and is of a hundred in number. The Bṛhat-sāman made by Bharadvāja is of the same number. Its nature is described in the Aitareya Āraṇyaka in this way:

अथात उत्तरः पक्षः । सोऽसौ लोकः सोऽसावादित्यस्तन्मनस्तद्बृहत्स भरद्वाजस्तच्छतं तानि षड्वीर्याणि भवंति । (*athāta uttaraḥ pakṣaḥ | so 'sau lokaḥ so 'sāvādityastanmanastadbṛhatsa bharadvājastacchataṃ tāni ṣaḍvīryāṇi bhavaṃti |*) (Ai. Ā. 1-4-2)

The Bṛhat-sāman itself is the left wing (Left wing). It is the world above, it is Āditya, it is the mind. It is Bhāradvāja. It is of a hundred in number. Its powers are of six kinds. Which is this number of a hundred? It is thus:

त्वामिद्दि हवामहे त्वं हैहि चेरव इति बृहतः स्तोत्रियानुरूपौ प्रगाथौ । चतस्रः सतीः षड्बृहतीः करोति । तमु ष्टुहि यो अभिभूत्योजाः सुत इत्त्वं निमिश्ल इंद्र सोम इति त्रीण्यभूरेको रयिपते रयाणामित्यष्टौ सूक्तानि । कथा महामवृधत्कस्य होतुरिति संपातः । इंद्रो मदाय नावृध इति पंक्तिः । (*tvāmiddi havāmahe tvaṃ haihi cerava iti bṛhataḥ stotriyānurūpau pragāthau | catasraḥ satīḥ ṣaḍbṛhatīḥ karoti | tamu ṣṭuhi yo abhibhūtyojāḥ suta ittvaṃ nimiśla iṃdra soma iti trīṇyabhūreko rayipate rayāṇāmityaṣṭau sūktāni | kathā mahāmavṛdhatkasya hoturiti saṃpātaḥ | iṃdro madāya nāvṛdha iti paṃktiḥ |*) (Ai. Ā. 5-2-2)
| 6-46-2 | स त्वं नश्चित्र (*sa tvaṃ naścitra*) | 1 | mantra |
| 8-61-8 | त्वं पुरू सहस्राणि (*tvaṃ purū sahasrāṇi*) | 1 | mantra |
| 6-18-1 to 15 | the sūkta beginning तमु ष्टुहि (*tamu ṣṭuhi*) | 15 | mantras |
| 6-23-1 to 10 | the sūkta beginning सुत इत्त्वं निमिश्लः (*suta ittvaṃ nimiślaḥ*) | 10 | mantras |
| 6-24-1 to 10 | the sūkta beginning वृषा मद इंद्रे (*vṛṣā mada iṃdre*) | 10 | mantras |
| 6-25-1 to 9 | the sūkta beginning या त ऊतिरवमा (*yā ta ūtiravamā*) | 9 | mantras |
| 6-31 to 38 | the sūktas in full | 40 | mantras |
| 4-23-1 to 11 | the sūkta beginning कथामहामवृधक्कस्य (*kathāmahāmavṛdhakkasya*) | 11 | mantras |

Total 102 mantras. Leaving out the repetitions 6-46-2 and 8-61-8, a total of 100 mantras are the Bṛhat-sāman mantras made by Bharadvāja. (Among these are included two mantras of the seers Bharga and Gotama.) With the Bṛhat-sāman that contains these mantras, identity with Āditya and with the mind is stated. But here another point must be understood. Ordinarily it is well known that the moon has a direct connection with the mind. Since here Āditya and the mind are both mentioned together, Sāyaṇa has said that Āditya and the moon are to be understood as two parts of one and the same principle. The Bṛhat-sāman is Āditya, the exponent of the principle of mind; its author is Bharadvāja, it is said. The great nature of this Bṛhat-sāman made by Bharadvāja is praised in the Chāndogya in this way:

..........एतद्बृहदादित्ये प्रोतं स य एवमेतत् बृहदादित्ये प्रोतं वेद तेजस्व्यान्नादो भवति सर्वमायुरेति ज्योग्जीवति महान्पजया पशु. भिर्भवति महान्कीर्त्या तपंतं न निंदेत्तद्व्रतं । (*..........etadbṛhadāditye protaṃ sa ya evametat bṛhadāditye protaṃ veda tejasvyānnādo bhavati sarvamāyureti jyogjīvati mahānpajayā paśu. bhirbhavati mahānkīrtyā tapaṃtaṃ na niṃdettadvrataṃ |*)

He who knows this truth, that this Bṛhat-sāman is woven into the Sun, becomes radiant. He lives possessed of abundance of food, long of life, with a life of splendour, with good offspring and cattle, and with the greatest fame. So it is said.
It is Bharadvāja who composed Bṛhat-sāman mantras of such power. He attained the most excellent place among all the seers.

भरद्वाजो ह वा ऋषीणामनूचानतमो दीर्घजीवितमस्तपस्वितम आस स एतेन सूक्तेन पाप्थानमपाहत तद्यद्वारद्वाजं शंसति पाप्मनोऽपहत्या अनूचानो दीर्घजीवी........तस्माद्वारद्वाजं शंसति । (*bharadvājo ha vā ṛṣīṇāmanūcānatamo dīrghajīvitamastapasvitama āsa sa etena sūktena pāpthānamapāhata tadyadvāradvājaṃ śaṃsati pāpmano 'pahatyā anūcāno dīrghajīvī........tasmādvāradvājaṃ śaṃsati |*)

The great seer Bharadvāja was the one of the most excellent knowledge among all the seers, the one of the longest life, and the one of the greatest power of austerity. By reciting the sūkta पिबा सोममभि यमुग्र (*pibā somamabhi yamugra*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-17) he destroyed sin. Therefore it is praised that whoever recites this Bhāradvāja sūkta becomes free from sin, long-lived, and possessed of the greatest power of austerity. For the nature of Bharadvāja is indeed such.

एष उ एव बिभ्रद्वाजः प्रजा वै वाजस्ता एष बिभर्ति यद्विभर्ति तस्माद्भरद्वाजस्तस्माद्भरद्वाज इत्याचक्षत एतमेव संतं । (*eṣa u eva bibhradvājaḥ prajā vai vājastā eṣa bibharti yadvibharti tasmādbharadvājastasmādbharadvāja ityācakṣata etameva saṃtaṃ |*)

वाज (*vāja*) means offspring, or strength, or wealth of food. Because he possesses all these riches, the name Bharadvāja became famous; so the Aitareya Āraṇyaka gives the etymology of this word. He who has mind is the possessor of food. Āditya (or the moon) is the possessor of the principle of mind; therefore Bharadvāja means the exponent of the principle of mind. Thus:

मनो वै भरद्वाज ऋषिरन्नं वाजो यो वै मनो बिभर्ति सोऽन्नं वाजं भरति तस्मान्मनो भरद्वाजऋषिः ॥ (*mano vai bharadvāja ṛṣirannaṃ vājo yo vai mano bibharti so 'nnaṃ vājaṃ bharati tasmānmano bharadvājaṛṣiḥ ‖*)

The seer Bharadvāja is the principle of mind. वाज (*vāja*) means food. Only he who possesses mind possesses food. Therefore the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa states that Bharadvāja means the possessor of food, or the possessor of the principle of mind that is the root of food. The same principle is stated in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā in this way:

अयं पुरो भुव ........ पंचदशाद्बृहद्बृहतो भरद्वाज ऋषिः प्रजापतिगृहीतया त्वया मनो गृह्णामि प्रजाभ्योऽयं पश्वाद्विश्वव्यचाः । (*ayaṃ puro bhuva ........ paṃcadaśādbṛhadbṛhato bharadvāja ṛṣiḥ prajāpatigṛhītayā tvayā mano gṛhṇāmi prajābhyo 'yaṃ paśvādviśvavyacāḥ |*)

From the Pañcadaśa stoma the Bṛhat-sāman arises, and from it the seer Bharadvāja. (Here Bṛhat-sāman means the principle of the Bṛhat-sāman; the commentary explains it as "in the Bṛhat-sāman mantras".) On the basis of these, the principle of mind, which helps the continuity of offspring, is taken up; thus the relation of cause and effect between wealth of offspring and the principle of mind, and the direct connection of both with Bharadvāja, are stated.

The great seer Bharadvāja exerted his power also in the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice and made the Agniṣṭoma pure and fruitful. How, is thus: this occasion is explained in the form of a story in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa.

अग्निष्टोमं वै वेदा आश्रयंतोक्षान्यसुरास्ते समावद्वीर्या एवासन्न व्यावर्तंत तान्भरद्वाज ऋषीणामपश्यदिमे वा असुरा उक्थेषु श्रितास्तानेषां न कश्चन पश्यतीति सोऽग्नि मुदह्वयत् । एहू शुब्रवाणि तेऽग्न इत्थेतरा गिर इति असुरा ह वा इतरा गिरः । सोऽग्निरुपोत्तिष्ठन्नब्रवीत्किंस्विदेव मह्यं कृशो दीर्घः पलितो वक्ष्यतीति भरद्वाजो ह वै कृशो दीर्घः पलित आस । सोऽब्रवीदिमे ना असुरा उक्तेषु श्रितास्तान्वो न कश्चन पश्यतीति । तानग्निरश्वो भूत्वाभ्यत्यद्रवत् ॥ (*agniṣṭomaṃ vai vedā āśrayaṃtokṣānyasurāste samāvadvīryā evāsanna vyāvartaṃta tānbharadvāja ṛṣīṇāmapaśyadime vā asurā uktheṣu śritāstāneṣāṃ na kaścana paśyatīti so 'gni mudahvayat | ehū śubravāṇi te 'gna itthetarā gira iti asurā ha vā itarā giraḥ | so 'gnirupottiṣṭhannabravītkiṃsvideva mahyaṃ kṛśo dīrghaḥ palito vakṣyatīti bharadvājo ha vai kṛśo dīrghaḥ palita āsa | so 'bravīdime nā asurā ukteṣu śritāstānvo na kaścana paśyatīti | tānagniraśvo bhūtvābhyatyadravat ‖*)

When the gods resorted to the Agniṣṭoma, the Asuras resorted to the Uktha. Then they too came to have as much power as the gods. The distinction who were the gods and who the Asuras could not be recognised. But only Bharadvāja, the foremost of all the seers, understood this distinction. "The Asuras are hidden in the Uktha. None of the gods has seen this," he said, and called Agni. Agni came to Bharadvāja and asked why Bharadvāja had called him. Then Bharadvāja said: "O Agni, I shall tell you what the speech of the others (that is, of the Asuras) is like." Agni, rising, wondered: "Why has this Bharadvāja, lean of body, tall of frame, grey-haired (with hair turned white), called me? What can he tell me?" As Agni described, Bharadvāja was indeed lean of body and tall of frame. As soon as Agni drew near, Bharadvāja said: "These Asuras are hidden in the Uktha; none of you can see them." Then Agni took the form of a horse and rushed upon them there. For this very reason he became the source of the Sākamaśva-sāman. Afterwards the gods drove away the Asuras with the help of the Pramaṃhiṣṭhīya-sāman. This narrative praises the greatness of Bharadvāja and explains that Bharadvāja's power is greater than the power of the gods, and that even a secret unknown to the gods became known to Bharadvāja.

The Yajñāyajñīya mantras, which must be recited as the most important ones in this same Agniṣṭoma sacrifice, are also well known as works of Bharadvāja. Even in describing the power of these Yajñāyajñīya mantras, the Bṛhat made by Bharadvāja and the principle of mind that is reflected in its principle, and moreover, as stated before, the atmosphere, the region of the Sun's circuit that is the support of these, are shown to have a direct connection with the principle that the Yajñāyajñīya mantras convey.

बृहदुत्तारे पक्षे । द्यौर्वै बृहद्दौर्हि बर्हिष्ठा दिवमेवास्यैतदुत्तरं पक्षं करोत्यथो उत्तरमेवास्यैतत्पक्षमनस्थिकममृतं करोति ॥ ( (*bṛhaduttāre pakṣe | dyaurvai bṛhaddaurhi barhiṣṭhā divamevāsyaitaduttaraṃ pakṣaṃ karotyatho uttaramevāsyaitatpakṣamanasthikamamṛtaṃ karoti ‖ (*)

After the recitation of the Rathantara-sāman the Bṛhat-sāman mantra is recited. The heavenly world is this principle of the Bṛhat-sāman. The heavenly world is the most extensive of all worlds. If the Bṛhat is made the left wing for Agni, it is as if the heavenly world itself were made; that is, it shows its exceeding extent.

यज्ञायज्ञियं पुच्छं । चंद्रमा वै यज्ञायज्ञियं । यो हि कश्च यज्ञः संतिष्ठत एतमेव तस्याहुतीनां रसः ॥ (*yajñāyajñiyaṃ pucchaṃ | caṃdramā vai yajñāyajñiyaṃ | yo hi kaśca yajñaḥ saṃtiṣṭhata etameva tasyāhutīnāṃ rasaḥ ‖*)

The Yajñāyajñīya, which reflects the principle of the moon, is the tail of this rite. That is, in the Soma sacrifice, in the last part of the Agniṣṭoma section, this Yajñāyajñīya mantra is recited and brings completeness, and the essence of the sacrificial offering goes to the world of the moon; this is the meaning.

Another point must be noticed here. यज्ञायज्ञा वः समना (*yajñāyajñā vaḥ samanā*) is mantra 1-168-1; it was composed by Agastya. Moreover, the mantra 6-48-1, यज्ञा यज्ञा वो अग्नये (*yajñā yajñā vo agnaye*), was composed by Śaṃyu; so there is room for the doubt how these Yajñāyajñīya mantras can be called works of Bharadvāja. It is unnecessary to extend this discussion here. In the recitation of the Yajñāyajñīya mantras there are four kinds of variation of the tune. For the present the answer may be given that Bharadvāja is the maker of all of them.

"In the case of the अग्निष्टोमसामन् (*agniṣṭomasāman*), however, the word सामन् (*sāman*) cannot be taken in its narrow acceptation, but the term has to be understood in the sense of "a hymn chanted in praise of Agni". The words commonly used for this chant, are the first two verses of Rig-Veda.
