VI. 48, a hymn indeed admirably adapted for the purpose of singing Agni's praises, for the first verse beginning "यज्ञायज्ञा वो अग्नये (*yajñāyajñā vo agnaye*)" the chief tune-book, the ग्रामगेयगान (*grāmageyagāna*), has preserved four different tunes, all of which are ascribed to the Rishi Bharadvaja."
[Sacred Books of the East Vol.41. Eggling. Satapatha Brahmana Pt.III.p.XIV

Therefore, in this context, both Bharadvāja's being the seer of the sūktas and the order laid down by him at the time of reciting the sūktas must be noticed. There is no room for the remaining discussions at present.

This Bharadvāja, born of a divine portion and possessed of power greater than that of the gods, as was indicated before, obtained the Brahma-splendour that upholds the Kṣatra duty even in worldly affairs, became a helper to many Kṣatriyas and helped the protection of Brahman; and his help to Abhyāvartin Jāyamāna and to Prastoka was told briefly. For such helps:
तौ तु वारशिखाञ्ञित्वा ततोऽभ्यावर्तिसार्ङ्ज्जयौ । भरद्वाजाय गुरवे ददतुर्विविधं वसु ॥ (*tau tu vāraśikhāññitvā tato 'bhyāvartisārṅjjayau | bharadvājāya gurave dadaturvividhaṃ vasu ‖*)

These same Abhyāvartin Jāyamāna and the Sāṃrjaya,⟨NOTE:189⟩ having completely conquered the Vāraśikhas, offered immeasurably valuable wealth as a gift to Bharadvāja, who was their teacher. While they were carrying this gift, on the way:
भरद्वाजश्च गर्गश्च दृष्टाविंद्रेण वै पथि । द्वयान् प्रस्तोक इत्याभिर्दानं तत्र च तस्य तु ॥ (*bharadvājaśca gargaśca dṛṣṭāviṃdreṇa vai pathi | dvayān prastoka ityābhirdānaṃ tatra ca tasya tu ‖*)

Bharadvāja and his son Garga, while walking along the road, were seen by Indra. Then, with the mantra द्वया अग्ने रथिनो विंशतिं (*dvayā agne rathino viṃśatiṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-27-8) and with the mantra प्रस्तोक्त इन्नु राधसस्त इंद्र (*prastokta innu rādhasasta iṃdra*) (6-47-22), they praised before Indra the wealth given by those two and prayed for the welfare of both; this is well known in the Bṛhaddevatā and other works.

But if examined from the historical point of view, these situations are somewhat problematic. Abhyāvartin and Prastoka are both described as belonging to the Sṛñjaya family. But in some places Abhyāvartin is stated to be the son of Jayamāna, and in some others the son of Sṛñjaya. Abhyāvartin also has the epithet Daivavāta. Not only this, certain Saṃhitā passages give room for the doubt that Bharadvāja and Divodāsa are one and the same. In such contexts the relation of Divodāsa to the Sṛñjaya family must also be examined.

First, it must be examined in which contexts of the Ṛksaṃhitā Abhyāvartin is mentioned and the teacher-pupil relation between Bharadvāja and Abhyāvartin is stated. Since only matters concerning Bharadvāja are being examined here, first Bharadvāja's precise position should be examined from the historical point of view, and afterwards, according to the occasion, if absolutely necessary, the above matters can be discussed suitably.

The word Divodāsa is in some places an epithet of Bharadvāja. The word Bharadvāja is in some places an epithet of Divodāsa. This same word Divodāsa is in some other places an epithet of Prastoka, who received help from Bharadvāja.

On the basis of such contexts there are also those who say that Divodāsa and Bharadvāja are one and the same. (The matter of Divodāsa Atithigva is told briefly in the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, Part 8, p. 788.) This opinion cannot be quite right. How? —
तमिमा नार्या पुरु दिवोदासाय सुन्वते । भरद्वाजाय दाशुषे ॥ (*tamimā nāryā puru divodāsāya sunvate | bharadvājāya dāśuṣe ‖*)

Some English scholars hold that in this Ṛk the word दिवोदासाय (*divodāsāya*) is an epithet of भरद्वाजाय (*bharadvājāya*), that therefore Divodāsa and Bharadvāja are one and the same, and not different persons. But this is wrong. Sāyaṇa has explained both words correctly in this context. When he says लुप्तोपमा एतत् (*luptopamā etat*), that is, यथा दिवोदासाय प्रादाः तथा भरद्वाजाय देहि (*yathā divodāsāya prādāḥ tathā bharadvājāya dehi*), the meaning is: "As you furnished wealth to Divodāsa, so furnish wealth to me, Bharadvāja"; hence it is clear that the two are different persons. Likewise:

यदयातं दिवोदासाय वर्तिर्भरद्वाजायाश्विना हयंता । रेवदुवाह सचनो रथो नां वृषभश्च शिंशुमारश्च युक्ता ॥ (*yadayātaṃ divodāsāya vartirbharadvājāyāśvinā hayaṃtā | revaduvāha sacano ratho nāṃ vṛṣabhaśca śiṃśumāraśca yuktā ‖*)

In this Ṛk too there is room for the doubt that both are the same person. But भरद्वाजाय (*bharadvājāya*) means "to the one who bears vāja (food)"; Sāyaṇa has explained that the sense is "to Divodāsa, who bears food in the form of the oblation". So in this context too there is no room for doubt.
अशिक्षो यत्र शच्या शचीवो दिवोदासाय सुन्वते सुतक्रे भरद्वाजाय गृणते वसूनि । (*aśikṣo yatra śacyā śacīvo divodāsāya sunvate sutakre bharadvājāya gṛṇate vasūni |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-31-4)
In such contexts too they are understood as separate persons. But:

प्रस्तोक इन्नु राधसस्त इंद्र दश कोशयार्दश वाजिनोऽदात् । दिवोदासादतिथिग्वस्य राधः शांबरं वसु प्रत्यग्रभीष्म ॥ (*prastoka innu rādhasasta iṃdra daśa kośayārdaśa vājino 'dāt | divodāsādatithigvasya rādhaḥ śāṃbaraṃ vasu pratyagrabhīṣma ‖*)

Here Sāyaṇa himself has explained that the two names Prastoka and Divodāsa are alternative names of one and the same person. दिवोदासात् एतत्संज्ञात् प्रस्तोकात् (*divodāsāt etatsaṃjñāt prastokāt*): taking the sense as "from Prastoka, who has the other name Divodāsa

", he has shown that both indicate one and the same person. If Prastoka and Divodāsa are one, then, since Bharadvāja is said to be the family priest of Divodāsa, he must be called the family priest of Prastoka. If so, whether Divodāsa also has the epithet Sāṃrjaya,⟨NOTE:191⟩ and whether he too is well known as the son of Sṛñjaya, is also a matter that deserves examination.
इयमददाद्रभसमृणच्युतं दिवोदासं वध्यश्वाय दाशुषे । (*iyamadadādrabhasamṛṇacyutaṃ divodāsaṃ vadhyaśvāya dāśuṣe |*)

It says that this Sarasvatī granted to the seer named Vadhryaśva a son named Divodāsa. No relation of any kind is stated, in any context, between this Vadhryaśva and Sṛñjaya, who is well known as the father of Prastoka. Sṛñjaya is not merely a personal name; although it is a collective name of a people, the name of Vadhryaśva is not included in that group either. That is, it is not easy to say whether Prastoka and Divodāsa, who honoured Bharadvāja, are different persons or alternative names of one person. This discussion will be made in its proper place. For the present, on the basis of the sentence दिवोदासात् एतत्संज्ञकात् प्रस्तोकात् (*divodāsāt etatsaṃjñakāt prastokāt*) explained by Sāyaṇa in the commentary on the above-cited mantra 6-47-22, it can only be said that these two names are identical in one person. The Pañcaviṃśa Brāhmaṇa states clearly that Bharadvāja was family priest to Divodāsa. (Pa. Brā. 15-3-7)⟨NOTE:192⟩ The Kāṭhaka Saṃhitā states that this same Bharadvāja gave the kingdom to Pratardana, the son or descendant of Divodāsa (21-10). But whether the Bharadvāja who was family priest of Prastoka and this one are the same person or different persons is difficult to say. Many different persons named Bharadvāja are well known both in Vedic passages and in the Purāṇas and the like. But here one should only suppose that the Bharadvāja, son of Bṛhaspati, praised in the Vedic passages is the single one who is extolled, and try to understand his greatness. Even in Vedic passages there is room to speak of two Bharadvājas, but since it is not easy for us to find precise grounds for that, we may take him to be one. How the power of Bharadvāja is described in Vedic passages such as the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa, Aitareya Brāhmaṇa and Aitareya Āraṇyaka has been told briefly above. The meaning of the word Bharadvāja is stated in some places also from the spiritual point of view. For example:
इ मावेव गोतमभरद्वाजावयमेव गोतमोऽयं भरद्वाजः (*i māveva gotamabharadvājāvayameva gotamo 'yaṃ bharadvājaḥ*)
These organs of hearing are Gotama and Bharadvāja. Of them, one is Gotama and the other Bharadvāja; thus it states what principle that great seer reflects.
**The Bharadvājas well known in the Purāṇas and Itihāsas**

The Bharadvāja praised in Vedic literature is also well known in the Mahābhārata and other works. It is well known that in the Mahābhārata, the Śrīmad-Bhāgavata, the Viṣṇu Purāṇa and the Matsya Purāṇa the descriptions of the family, origin and nature of the seer Bharadvāja are just as described above in the Bṛhaddevatā. He is the son of Bṛhaspati. This Bharadvāja, son of Bṛhaspati, is described in the Purāṇas as the son of Bharata. This matter is told in the Śrīmad-Bhāgavata in this way:

तस्यासन्नृप वैदर्भ्यः पत्न्यस्ति स्रः सुसंमताः । जघ्नुस्त्यागभयात्पुत्रान्नानारूपा इतीरिते ॥ तस्यैवं वितथे वंशे तदर्थं यजतस्सुतं । मरुत्सोमेन मरुतो भरद्वाजमुपाददुः ॥ (*tasyāsannṛpa vaidarbhyaḥ patnyasti sraḥ susaṃmatāḥ | jaghnustyāgabhayātputrānnānārūpā itīrite ‖ tasyaivaṃ vitathe vaṃśe tadarthaṃ yajatassutaṃ | marutsomena maruto bharadvājamupādaduḥ ‖*)

That Bharata (whose wealth was greater than Indra's) had three wives, daughters of the king of Vidarbha. Seeing the children born of them, the husband Bharata said, "These are not sons worthy of my dignity," and cast them off. Then his wives, afraid that their husband would suspect them of unchastity and would abandon them, killed all those children. In the end, when the situation arose that the family would be cut off for want of offspring, Bharata, desiring offspring, performed the sacrifice called Marutsoma and worshipped the Maruts. Then the Maruts, pleased with Bharata's pure worship and the like, granted him a son named Bharadvāja. The manner of that Bharadvāja's origin is this:

अंतरत्नां भ्रातृपत्न्यां मैथुनाय बृहस्पतिः । प्रवृत्तो वारितो गर्भं शप्ता वीर्यमपासृजत् ॥ तं त्युक्तु कामां ममतां भर्तुस्त्यागविशंकितां । नामनिवचनं तस्य शोकमेतं सुरा जगुः ॥ मूढे भर द्वाजमिमं भर द्वाजं बृहस्पते । यातौ यदुक्त्वा पितरौ भरद्वाजस्ततस्त्वयं ॥ चोद्यमाना सुरैरेवं मत्वा वितथमात्मजं । व्यसृजन्मरुतोऽबिभ्रन् दत्तोऽयं वितथेऽन्वये ॥ (*aṃtaratnāṃ bhrātṛpatnyāṃ maithunāya bṛhaspatiḥ | pravṛtto vārito garbhaṃ śaptā vīryamapāsṛjat ‖ taṃ tyuktu kāmāṃ mamatāṃ bhartustyāgaviśaṃkitāṃ | nāmanivacanaṃ tasya śokametaṃ surā jaguḥ ‖ mūḍhe bhara dvājamimaṃ bhara dvājaṃ bṛhaspate | yātau yaduktvā pitarau bharadvājastatastvayaṃ ‖ codyamānā surairevaṃ matvā vitathamātmajaṃ | vyasṛjanmaruto 'bibhran datto 'yaṃ vitathe 'nvaye ‖*)

Bṛhaspati had a younger brother named Ucathya. He had a wife named Mamatā. At the time when that brother's wife was with child, Bṛhaspati, infatuated with her and overcome with desire, secretly with her

began to have intercourse. Then the child lying in her womb said to Bṛhaspati: "O Bṛhaspati, while I am in the womb, your seed cannot find a place here. Therefore hold back your seed; it must not be emitted." Bṛhaspati became angry. In his wrath he cursed that embryo: "O embryo, become blind," and by force he placed his seed together with it. Though blind, that embryo pushed that new seed outside. Then that seed, spilled on the ground, at once took the form of a son. Then Mamatā, fearing that if she protected and nourished the child born in the form of her son, her husband, suspecting her of unchastity, would abandon her, wished to abandon the child itself. Seeing her firm resolve, the gods contrived a dialogue between Bṛhaspati and Mamatā, so that no kind of suspicion would arise in her husband and so that it would accord with the name of the child born there, and they told it in this way. The purport of that dialogue is interesting. It is this:

Bṛhaspati: "O foolish Mamatā, if a son is born in one man's own field through the company of another man, he is the son of the keeper of the field as well. For that reason you need not fear your husband. Do not abandon this son who belongs equally to both of us; protect and rear him."
Mamatā: "O Bṛhaspati, this son was born because you came by stealth and had intercourse with me. Since he was born of a trespass, you yourself must rear him. I have no reason to rear him."

Thus, both having stated their own personal reasons, he abandoned the child there and went away. From that time the name Bharadvāja arose for him. Although the gods composed such a conciliatory dialogue and told it to Mamatā in the form of instruction, she did not agree, abandoned there the child born of the seed of one who was not her husband, and went away. Then the Maruts reared that son and graciously gave him as a son to Bharata, who desired offspring; so the sage Śuka told King Parīkṣit. Because he was born of Bṛhaspati in the wife of Ucathya, he was named Bharadvāja; and because he became the cause of the growth of the line of Bharata, which was vitatha, that is, childless and fruitless, he was also named Vitatha. Thus the name Bharadvāja became famous for him both because he gave preservation of descent to a household and because he has the capacity to protect all, gods, men and the rest. The sage himself, stating this same purport, has given the etymology of his own name in the Mahābhārata in this way.
भरेऽसुतान्भरे पोष्यान्भरे देवान् भरे द्विजान् । भरे भार्यामहं व्याजाद्भरद्वाजोऽस्मि शोभने ॥ (*bhare 'sutānbhare poṣyānbhare devān bhare dvijān | bhare bhāryāmahaṃ vyājādbharadvājo 'smi śobhane ‖*)

"I have the power to bear those without sons, those who are to be nourished, the gods, the twice-born and my wife. For whatever reason, since I have the power to bear such as are fit to be borne, I am called Bharadvāja," so the account of the conversation between Bharadvāja and a Yātudhāni tells.

In the Ārṣeya Upaniṣad a discussion on the principle arises between Bharadvāja and Gotama, and the two exchange their views with each other. The same discussion on spiritual matters stands in the Mahābhārata in the form of a conversation between Bhṛgu and Bharadvāja. When Yudhiṣṭhira begged Bhīṣma to explain the creation of the world, Bhīṣma tells the conversation that took place on this very subject between Bhṛgu and Bharadvāja. This conversation runs from the 180th to the 190th chapter of the Śāntiparva of the Mahābhārata. But here, by way of example, only one or two occasions on which Bharadvāja questioned Bhṛgu are told, and an introduction to Bharadvāja's spiritual outlook is given briefly.

अत्राप्युदाहरंतीममितिहासं पुरातनं । भृगुणाभिहितं श्रेष्ठं भरद्वाजाय पृच्छते ॥ कैलासशिखरे दृष्ट्वा दीप्यमानमिवौजसा । भृगुं महर्षिमासीनं भरद्वाजोऽन्वपृच्छत ॥ ससागरः सगगनः सशैलः सवराहकः । सभूमिः साग्निपवनः लोकोऽयं केन निर्मितः ॥ कथं सृष्टानि भूतानि कथं वर्णविभक्तयः । शौचाशौचं कथं तेषां धर्माधर्मावथो कथं ॥ (*atrāpyudāharaṃtīmamitihāsaṃ purātanaṃ | bhṛguṇābhihitaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ bharadvājāya pṛcchate ‖ kailāsaśikhare dṛṣṭvā dīpyamānamivaujasā | bhṛguṃ maharṣimāsīnaṃ bharadvājo 'nvapṛcchata ‖ sasāgaraḥ sagaganaḥ saśailaḥ savarāhakaḥ | sabhūmiḥ sāgnipavanaḥ loko 'yaṃ kena nirmitaḥ ‖ kathaṃ sṛṣṭāni bhūtāni kathaṃ varṇavibhaktayaḥ | śaucāśaucaṃ kathaṃ teṣāṃ dharmādharmāvatho kathaṃ ‖*)

Bhīṣma, questioned by Dharmarāja, describes the incident, famed in tradition, in the form of a conversation between Bhṛgu and Bharadvāja. Bharadvāja questioned the great seer Bhṛgu, who formerly lived on the peak of Kailāsa and was of fierce splendour, in this way: "O great seer, by whom and how was this universe created, with all beings such as ocean, sky, mountain, cloud, earth, fire and wind? How was the creation of living beings, and in particular of men, brought about? How did the division of dharma and adharma come about
? What is the nature of the other world? What is the final goal of living beings? What are birth and death?" and so on. When he asked thus, the great seer Bhṛgu:
नारायणो जगन्मूर्तिरंतरात्मा सनातनः । कूटस्थोऽक्षर अव्यक्तो निर्लेपो व्यापकः प्रभुः ॥ (*nārāyaṇo jaganmūrtiraṃtarātmā sanātanaḥ | kūṭastho 'kṣara avyakto nirlepo vyāpakaḥ prabhuḥ ‖*)

Śrīman Nārāyaṇa, the inner controller of all, pervading the world, eternal, unchanging, imperishable, unmanifest, free from fault, and lord of all worlds, is the creator and ruler of the whole universe of moving and unmoving things; thus he explained the manner of creation. Again, to Bharadvāja's questions such as किं तस्य धर्माचरणं किं वा धर्मस्य लक्षणं (*kiṃ tasya dharmācaraṇaṃ kiṃ vā dharmasya lakṣaṇaṃ*)**GLOSS** Bhṛgu has explained the nature of one's own dharma. For fear of lengthening the book this matter has not been explained in detail.

Again, on another occasion Dharmarāja questions Yudhiṣṭhira concerning dharma: "What should be done if, through the nature of the time, dharma declines and affliction comes from enemies such as thieves and robbers?" When he asked this, Bhīṣma said, "In this matter I too shall now tell you what Bharadvāja told Śatruṃtapa; listen," and he explains the Daṇḍanīti, the policy of punishment, taught by Bharadvāja, beginning "For a king the chief instrument is punishment."

Thus, as described in the Bṛhaddevatā and in the Bhāgavata and the like, the origin and power of Bharadvāja are described in the Matsya Purāṇa also. But in the Bṛhaddevatā only the matter of the Maruts giving Bharadvāja to Bharata as a son is absent. The words of the Matsya Purāṇa are as follows.

यषय ऊचुः ॥ भरतस्य भरद्वाजः पुत्रार्थं मारुतैः कथं । संक्रामितो महातेजास्तन्नो ब्रूहि यथातथं ॥ ॥ सूत उवाच ॥ पत्न्यामापन्नसत्त्वायामुशिजः स स्थितो भुवि । भ्रातुर्भार्यां स दृष्ट्वा तु बृहस्पतिरुनाच ह ॥ संक्रामितो भरद्वाजो मरुद्भिर्भरतं प्रति ॥ (*yaṣaya ūcuḥ ‖ bharatasya bharadvājaḥ putrārthaṃ mārutaiḥ kathaṃ | saṃkrāmito mahātejāstanno brūhi yathātathaṃ ‖ ‖ sūta uvāca ‖ patnyāmāpannasattvāyāmuśijaḥ sa sthito bhuvi | bhrāturbhāryāṃ sa dṛṣṭvā tu bṛhaspatirunāca ha ‖ saṃkrāmito bharadvājo marudbhirbharataṃ prati ‖*)**GLOSS**

Since the same matter that is described above in the Bhāgavata, the origin of Bharadvāja and the rest, is told in the Matsya Purāṇa too with the same details, this part has not been explained at length.

The Bharadvāja described in the Araṇya-parva of the Mahābhārata must be different from the Bharadvāja spoken of above. The one described in the Araṇya-parva is also a seer. His matter is explained in chapters 137 to 140 of the Araṇya-parva. His affair is told here only in the briefest form.
भरद्वाजश्च रैभ्यश्च सखायौ संबभूवतुः । तावूषतुरिहात्यंतं प्रीयमाण् वनांतरे ॥ (*bharadvājaśca raibhyaśca sakhāyau saṃbabhūvatuḥ | tāvūṣaturihātyaṃtaṃ prīyamāṇ vanāṃtare ‖*)

Raibhya and Bharadvāja were friends. They lived in mutual affection. Bharadvāja had a son named Yavakrīta. When he behaved very foolishly once or twice towards Raibhya, a minor deity created by the sage Raibhya killed Yavakrīta. Unable to bear grief for his son, Bharadvāja entered the fire. Then Raibhya brought Bharadvāja back to life (Vana-parva 137-140). Another great seer named Bharadvāja is described in the Śalya-parva of the Mahābhārata.

भरद्वाजस्य विप्रर्षेः स्कन्नं रेतो महात्मनः । दृष्ट्वाप्सरसमायांतीं धृताचीं पृथुलोचनां ॥ स तु जग्राह तद्रेतः करेण जपताः वरः । तदापतत्पर्णपुटे तत्र सा संभवत्सुता ॥ तस्यास्तु जातकर्मादि कृत्वा सर्वं तपोधनः । नाम चास्याः स कृतवान्भरद्वाजो महामुनिः ॥ श्रुतावतीति धर्मात्मा देवर्षिगणसंसदि । (*bharadvājasya viprarṣeḥ skannaṃ reto mahātmanaḥ | dṛṣṭvāpsarasamāyāṃtīṃ dhṛtācīṃ pṛthulocanāṃ ‖ sa tu jagrāha tadretaḥ kareṇa japatāḥ varaḥ | tadāpatatparṇapuṭe tatra sā saṃbhavatsutā ‖ tasyāstu jātakarmādi kṛtvā sarvaṃ tapodhanaḥ | nāma cāsyāḥ sa kṛtavānbharadvājo mahāmuniḥ ‖ śrutāvatīti dharmātmā devarṣigaṇasaṃsadi |*)

Once Bharadvāja, seeing the celestial woman Ghṛtācī, was infatuated and his seed was spilled. When he placed it in a leaf-cup, a daughter was born. He performed the birth rites and the rest for her. She became famed in the whole assembly of divine seers as Śrutāvatī. This is the description.

The Bharadvāja praised in the Śrīmad-Rāmāyaṇa is yet another great seer. He is a disciple of the great seer Vālmīki (Rā. Bālakāṇḍa 2).⟨NOTE:197⟩ He lived at the holy place Prayāga. When Śrī Rāma set out for the Daṇḍaka forest, he went to him and asked which region was fit for him to live in; learning that ten krośas from there is the Citrakūṭa mountain and that it is the region fit for dwelling, he came from there and reached Citrakūṭa. The nature of this great seer is described in the Rāmāyaṇa in this way.

स प्रविश्य महात्मानमृषिं शिष्यगणैर्वृतं । संशितव्रतमेकाग्रं तपसा लब्धचक्षुषं ॥ हुताग्निहोत्रं दृष्ट्वैव महाभागं कृतांजलिः । रामः सौमित्रिणा सार्धं सीतया चाभ्यवादयत् ॥ (*sa praviśya mahātmānamṛṣiṃ śiṣyagaṇairvṛtaṃ | saṃśitavratamekāgraṃ tapasā labdhacakṣuṣaṃ ‖ hutāgnihotraṃ dṛṣṭvaiva mahābhāgaṃ kṛtāṃjaliḥ | rāmaḥ saumitriṇā sārdhaṃ sītayā cābhyavādayat ‖*)

Then the two mighty brothers Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, together with Sītā, stood for a while at a distance, waiting to have the sight of the seer Bharadvāja. After a short while Śrī Rāma went into the hermitage and saw Bharadvāja, a man of great spirit, surrounded by a company of disciples, of most strict vows, intent on meditation, possessed of the eye of knowledge obtained by austerity, venerable, seated after performing the Agnihotra. Thus this great seer is praised.

उपानयत धर्मात्मा गामर्थ्यमुदकं ततः । नानाविधान्नरसान् वन्यमूलफलाश्रयान् ॥ तेभ्यो ददौ तप्ततपा वासं चैवाभ्यकल्पयत् ॥ (*upānayata dharmātmā gāmarthyamudakaṃ tataḥ | nānāvidhānnarasān vanyamūlaphalāśrayān ‖ tebhyo dadau taptatapā vāsaṃ caivābhyakalpayat ‖*)

Then the sage Bharadvāja brought water for the arghya and a cow to honour that wise one. And that Bharadvāja, foremost among the ascetics, offered to Sītā, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa roots, tubers and fruits and food and drink of many kinds, and arranged for them a place fit to dwell in.
When Bharata went to bring Śrī Rāma back to Ayodhyā, Bharadvāja, understanding Bharata's intention, praised him and gave a feast to him and his retinue.
After the slaying of Rāvaṇa, Śrī Rāma set out for Ayodhyā with Sītā, Lakṣmaṇa and the others and on the way came to his hermitage. Then Bharadvāja gave a feast to all.

Thus the splendour of the great seer Bharadvāja is described in many places. But apart from the Bharadvāja who is found in the Ṛgveda, it is not possible to say precisely how many seers of this name there were. The sūktas composed by this great seer in the Ṛksaṃhitā are these: 6-1 to 30; 6-37 to 43; 6-53 to 74; 9-67-1 to 3; 10-137-1.

Whether the Bharadvāja who is well known in the Purāṇas and Itihāsas as the son of Bharata and the Bharadvāja who is the seer of the Ṛksaṃhitā sūktas are one and the same person or different is not easy to state with precise

opinion. How Bharadvāja became the son of Bharata has been told above, as explained in the Śrīmad-Bhāgavata and the Matsya Purāṇa. In the Ṛksaṃhitā too the passage in which Bharadvāja speaks of Bharata as his elder is clear. How?
त्वामीळे अध द्विता भरतो वाजिभिः शुनं । ईजे यज्ञेषु यज्ञियं ॥ (*tvāmīḷe adha dvitā bharato vājibhiḥ śunaṃ | īje yajñeṣu yajñiyaṃ ‖*)

Here Bharadvāja praises the episode of Bharata's worshipping Agni. Sāyaṇa has explained here that for the word भरत (*bharata*) the intention is दौष्यंतिरेतत्संज्ञा राजा (*dauṣyaṃtiretatsaṃjñā rājā*), the king of that name, Bharata the son of Duṣyanta. The Purāṇas, as told above, describe that this Bharadvāja was not Bharata's own son, but that the Maruts brought Bharadvāja, abandoned by his mother and father, and gave him to Bharata. In Vedic passages too the direct connection between Bharadvāja and the Maruts is stated. In the Bṛhaddevatā line cited above, मरुत्सासीद्गुरुरश्च (*marutsāsīdgururaśca*) (Bṛ. De. 5-103), the point is stated that Bharadvāja was the teacher of the Maruts. (But the Purāṇas do not state that he was the teacher of the Maruts.) Therefore, by the mantra cited above (6-16-4), Bharadvāja has in effect said that Bharata was venerable to him and an ideal man.

Secondly, just as the Purāṇas say that Bharadvāja was the son of Mamatā, the Bṛhaddevatā passage too states that he was the son of Mamatā. That the Ṛksaṃhitā passage also suggests this same relation can be inferred from some passages. For example:

तमु द्युमः पुर्वणीक होतरग्ने अग्निभिर्मनुष इधानः । स्तोमं यमस्मै ममतेव शूषं धृतं न शुचि मतयः पवंते ॥ (*tamu dyumaḥ purvaṇīka hotaragne agnibhirmanuṣa idhānaḥ | stomaṃ yamasmai mamateva śūṣaṃ dhṛtaṃ na śuci matayaḥ pavaṃte ‖*)

Here it is clear that Bharadvāja regards Mamatā as his ideal woman. But here Sāyaṇa has taken Mamatā to mean the mother of Dīrghatamas. The question also arises why she should not be Bharadvāja's mother. It is both possible and natural that Bharadvāja should say that his own mother was the ideal person for him.
एतेन ह वा ऐंद्रेण महाभिषेकेण दीर्घतमा मामतेयो भरतं दौष्यंतिमभिषिषेच (*etena ha vā aiṃdreṇa mahābhiṣekeṇa dīrghatamā māmateyo bharataṃ dauṣyaṃtimabhiṣiṣeca*) (Ai. Brā. 39-23)
Here it is said that Dīrghatamas, the son of Mamatā, performed the consecration of Bharata, the son of Duṣyanta. Then Mamatā, the mother of Dīrghatamas, and Mamatā, the mother of Bharadvāja,
Whether they may be called two different persons is a question for which there is also room. There is no proper basis for stating anything definitively.

On the whole, on the strength of many points, there is room to say that the Bharadvāja who is famous in Vedic literature and the Bharadvāja described in the Bhāgavata and Matsya Purāṇas are one and the same person. How this sage's divine genius and poetic style are manifested in the many sūktas of the sixth maṇḍala, which are his works, can be learnt in the respective sections.

en: Sāyaṇa says that in the sixth maṇḍala, seen by Bharadvāja, there are six anuvākas; in the first anuvāka there are fifteen sūktas; of these the first is the sūkta of thirteen Ṛks beginning त्वं ह्यग्ने (*tvaṃ hyagne*). Since the Anukramaṇī says that Bharadvāja, descendant of Bṛhaspati, saw the sixth maṇḍala, that same Bharadvāja is the seer, being the seer of the maṇḍala. By the rule for metres that are not specified, the metre is Triṣṭubh; by the rule that governs the beginning of a maṇḍala, the deity is Agni.

Use: this Manotā sūkta is to be recited by the Maitrāvaruṇa priest when the offering of the animal is being cut off in portions. The sūtra says: "He recites 'Tvaṃ hy agne prathamaḥ'" (Ā. 3-6). In the morning recitation (prātaranuvāka), for the Agni kratu in the Triṣṭubh metre, this and the following sūktas, six in all and omitting the second, are applied; the sūtra says: "Of the six beginning 'Tvaṃ hy agne prathamaḥ', one should leave out the second" (A. 4-13).⟨NOTE:198⟩ The first Ṛk is applied at the first upākaraṇa; the sūtra has been stated at the earlier mantra.

The Anuvāda says: this sixth maṇḍala, seen by the seer Bharadvāja, has six anuvākas. The first anuvāka has fifteen sūktas. Among them the sūkta त्वं ह्यग्ने (*tvaṃ hyagne*) is the first; it has thirteen Ṛks. Since the Anukramaṇī says "Bharadvāja Bārhaspatya saw the sixth maṇḍala", the seer of this sūkta is Bharadvāja, the seer of the maṇḍala; the deity is Agni; the metre is Triṣṭubh. It is explained by the sūtra of Āśvalāyana's Śrauta-sūtra, "He recites 'Tvaṃ hy agne prathamaḥ'" (Ā. 3-6), that when the animal sacrifice is performed and the offering is being cut off, this sūkta is to be recited by the priest called Maitrāvaruṇa as the Manotā sūkta. It is explained by the sūtra of the same Śrauta-sūtra, "Of the six beginning 'Tvaṃ hy agne prathamaḥ', one should leave out the second" (Ā. 4-13), that at the time of reciting the morning anuvāka mantras, six sūktas from this sūkta onward, omitting only the second, are applied for the mantras of the Triṣṭubh metre connected with Agni's kratu. The first Ṛk of this sūkta is to be used in the principal offerings of the Adhyāyopākaraṇa and Utsarjana; this is stated in the third sūtra (Ā. 3-5) of Āśvalāyana's Gṛhya-sūtra.

en: "O Agni, you are first (prathama)": first among the gods, or "pratama", the most excellent, or the one who came into being before. You are "manotā": one in whom the minds of the gods are woven in, firmly bound. The word "hi" points to what is well known from Brāhmaṇa passages such as सर्वा मनोताग्नौ मनोताः संगच्छंते (*sarvā manotāgnau manotāḥ saṃgacchaṃte*) (Ai. Brā. 2-10). O "dasma", beautiful to look at, you have become the Hotṛ, the invoker of the gods, of this rite (dhiyaḥ here means the rite). O showerer of desires, you have made everywhere (sīṃ means "on all sides") unassailable, unharmed strength (sahas, power). For what purpose? To overcome (sahadhyai) every powerful enemy.
- प्रथमः (*prathamaḥ*)—the foremost among all the gods
- मनोता (*manotā*)—you are the one who attracts the minds of all
- दस्म (*dasma*)—O Agni, whose form is beautiful to look at

O Agni, you who are foremost among all the gods, are the one who attracts the minds of all. O Agni of beautiful form, you are the Hotṛ of this rite. O Agni, showerer of desires, provide us with the strength needed to withstand all our powerful enemies. May we face and defeat our enemies everywhere.

You, Agni, are the first of the gods ; a deity to whom their minds are devoted : pleasing of aspect, you are the invoker of the deities at this rite: showerer (of benefits), bestow upon us unsurpasstble strength, wherewith to sustain all (hostile) prowess

प्रथमः (*prathamaḥ*)—chief, foremost. Yāska has given the etymology of the word prathama thus: प्रथम इति मुख्यनाम प्रतमो भवति (*prathama iti mukhyanāma pratamo bhavati*) (Ni. 2-22). Prathama means chief; that is, it indicates the sense of most excellent, best, foremost.

सीं (*sīṃ*)—everywhere. Yāska has said: सीमिति परिग्रहार्थीयो वा पदपूरणो वा (*sīmiti parigrahārthīyo vā padapūraṇo vā*) (Ni. 1-7). That is, the word sīṃ is used in the sense of "taking up" (accepting), and the word is also used to fill out a sentence; in support of this he cites the Ṛk प्र सीमादित्यो असृजद्विधर्ता ऋतं सिंधवो वरुणस्य यंति (*pra sīmādityo asṛjadvidhartā ṛtaṃ siṃdhavo varuṇasya yaṃti*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-28-4) and says: प्रसीमादित्यो असृजत् । प्रासृजदिति ना प्रासृजत्सर्वते इति वा । (*prasīmādityo asṛjat | prāsṛjaditi nā prāsṛjatsarvate iti vā |*). In this Ṛk the word sīṃ is used to fill out the pāda, or else one may say that it has the meaning "sarvataḥ", on all sides, in every army. In this matter he says that there is another example also: विसीमतः सुरुजो वेन आवः (*visīmataḥ surujo vena āvaḥ*) (Vā. Saṃ. 13-3).⟨NOTE:199⟩

मनोता (*manotā*)—In explaining the meaning of this word, Sāyaṇa has said in his commentary on the mantra मनोताय्कॆ हविषोऽवदीयमानस्यानुब्रूहीत्याहाध्वर्युः (*manotāykè haviṣo 'vadīyamānasyānubrūhītyāhādhvaryuḥ*) in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa as follows

देवानां मनांस्कोतानि दृढं प्रविष्टानि यस्यां देवतायां सा मनोता। (*devānāṃ manāṃskotāni dṛḍhaṃ praviṣṭāni yasyāṃ devatāyāṃ sā manotā|*) The meaning is that the matter which is firmly established in the minds of the gods is called manotā. The occasion on which this word is used in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa is indicated here:

मनोताय्कॆ हविषोऽवदीयमानस्यानुब्रूहीत्याहाध्वर्युः । त्वं ह्यग्ने प्रथमो मनोतेति सूक्तमन्वाह । (*manotāykè haviṣo 'vadīyamānasyānubrūhītyāhādhvaryuḥ | tvaṃ hyagne prathamo manoteti sūktamanvāha |*) (Ai. Brā. 6-10)

In the sacrifice, after the offering of the vapā of the animal, the Adhvaryu directs the priest called Maitrāvaruṇa with the preṣa mantra मनोताय्कॆ हविषोऽवदीयमानस्यानुब्रूहि (*manotāykè haviṣo 'vadīyamānasyānubrūhi*). Then the Maitrāvaruṇa recites the sūkta (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-1) beginning त्वं ह्यग्ने प्रथमो मनोता (*tvaṃ hyagne prathamo manotā*).

A little explanation is necessary here. When the animal offering is made in a sacrifice, first the वपा (*vapā*) and the sacrificial cakes are offered. After that the other parts of the animal are offered separately. After the offering of the वपा (*vapā*), the parts of the animal are placed in wooden ladles named जुहू (*juhū*) and उपभृत् (*upabhṛt*), ājya (ghee) is poured over them, and they are offered. These offerings of parts are eleven. While offering these parts the Adhvaryu places the ladles जुहू (*juhū*) and उपभृत् (*upabhṛt*) one upon the other, places the parts of the animal in them one by one, and offers them while reciting the mantra suited to each occasion. The parts of the animal that are thus offered are: the heart, the tongue, the breast, the two sides, the liver, the parts called वाखौ (*vākhau*) or अतश्नू (*ataśnū*), the left back-bone (सव्यं दोः (*savyaṃ doḥ*)), the right side of the waist, and the middle part of the testicle. All these are placed in the ladle जुहू (*juhū*) and offered. The remaining parts, that is, the right back-bone, the remaining part of the testicle and the left side of the waist, are placed in the ladle उपभृत् (*upabhṛt*) and offered. The part of the penis called वर्षिष्ट (*varṣiṣṭa*) and the tail are cut off and offered separately.

When the parts of the animal mentioned above have been cooked, ghee has been poured over them and they are being offered, the Adhvaryu addresses the Hotṛ with the words quoted above, मनोताय्कॆ हविषोऽवदीयमानस्यानुब्रूहि (*manotāykè haviṣo 'vadīyamānasyānubrūhi*), that is: "Recite the mantras suited to the occasion, in order to offer to the deities who desire the parts of the animal mixed with the oblation." Then the Maitrāvaruṇa, who belongs to the group of Hotṛs, recites the present sūkta त्वं ह्यग्ये प्रथमः (*tvaṃ hyagye prathamaḥ*). Since these deities desire the parts of the animal, they are called manotā (those who have the desire in their minds, or in whose minds it abides). These deities are Agni, Soma, Agni-Soma, Indra-Agni, the Aśvins, Vanaspati, and the Devas Ājyapas (the gods who drink the ājya). Among them Agni is the first and the chief; therefore in this sūkta, or in the offering of the animal's parts,
त्वं ह्यग्ने प्रथमो मनोता (*tvaṃ hyagne prathamo manotā*): "O Agni, among the deities who desire the parts of the animal you are the first, or the best": thus Agni is praised.
तदाहुर्यदन्यदेवत्य उत पशुर्भवथ्यत कस्मादाग्नेयीरेव मनोताय्कॆ हविषोऽवदीयमानस्यान्वाहेति । (*tadāhuryadanyadevatya uta paśurbhavathyata kasmādāgneyīreva manotāykè haviṣo 'vadīyamānasyānvāheti |*)

Among the manotā deities Agni is the first, but there are also other deities such as Soma. Yet in this sūkta, त्वं ह्यग्ने प्रथमो मनोता (*tvaṃ hyagne prathamo manotā*), which is recited as the Manotā sūkta, only Agni is praised; there is nothing about the other manotā deities. That being so, some argue: is it not wrong to recite this sūkta, which is about Agni alone, in order to praise the other manotā deities? The answer to this is given:

तिस्रो वै देवानां मनोतास्तासु हि तेषां मनांस्कोतानि वाग्वै देवानां मनोता तस्यां हि तेषां मनांस्कोतानि गोर्वै देवानां मनोता तस्यां हि तेषां मनांस्कोतान्यग्निर्वै देवानां मनोता तस्मिन्हि तेषां मनांस्कोतान्यग्निः सर्वा मनोता अग्नौ मनोताः संगच्छंते तस्मादाग्नेयिरेह मनोतायै हविषोऽवदीयमानस्यान्वाहा । (*tisro vai devānāṃ manotāstāsu hi teṣāṃ manāṃskotāni vāgvai devānāṃ manotā tasyāṃ hi teṣāṃ manāṃskotāni gorvai devānāṃ manotā tasyāṃ hi teṣāṃ manāṃskotānyagnirvai devānāṃ manotā tasminhi teṣāṃ manāṃskotānyagniḥ sarvā manotā agnau manotāḥ saṃgacchaṃte tasmādāgneyireha manotāyai haviṣo 'vadīyamānasyānvāhā |*) (I. Bā. 6-10)⟨NOTE:200⟩

Among the manotā deities, Agni, Gau (the cow) and Vāk (the goddess of speech) are the chief ones, because the minds of all the gods are lodged in these three deities alone. Among these three deities Agni is the chief. It is through this Agni that the oblation is offered to the other deities. Therefore this sūkta त्वं ह्यग्ने प्रथमः (*tvaṃ hyagne prathamaḥ*), which praises Agni, the chief deity, on behalf of all the deities, is recited. The main sense is that by praising Agni, the chief of the manotā deities, all the deities are praised.
notes: ಅಂಗನಾದಿಗುಣವಿಶಿಷ್ಟಂ: sense of ಅಂಗನಾದಿ unclear
ಗನಾದೀನಿ: reading unclear

en: Now, O Agni, you who are "yajīyān", the best of sacrificers, and the Hotṛ, the accomplisher of the offering, have sat down in the place of Iḷā, that is, on the earth in the form of the altar. Doing what? Desiring (iṣayan) food in the form of the animal, the sacrificial cake and the like, and being worthy of praise. Men (nṛ: leaders, human beings, that is, the priests and the sacrificers) desire you as their god, you who are first, before the other deities; knowing (citayantaḥ) you, or making you known by praises, for the sake of great wealth, they have followed you (anu gman, "they went after you first").
- यजीयान् (*yajīyān*)—you who are worthy of worship
- इषयन् (*iṣayan*)—desiring food in the form of sacrificial cakes and the like
- इळः (*iḷaḥ*)—of the earth in the form of the sacrificial altar
- प्रथमं तं त्वा (*prathamaṃ taṃ tvā*)—you, such a chief
- देवयंतः (*devayaṃtaḥ*)—desiring to worship the gods and obtain their favour

O Agni, you who are worthy of worship and the accomplisher of the offering, sit down at this time of sacrifice in the place of the sacrificial altar, desiring food in the form of sacrificial cakes and the like and being worthy of praise. The priests and others, who are devoted to the worship of the gods, have approached you, the chief of all the gods, meditating on you for the gain of great wealth.

Offerer of the oblation, frequent celebrator of sacrifice, now sit down on the foot-mark of Ila, accepting the (sacrificial) food, and being glorificd : devout men, expectant of great riches, have recourse to you as to the first (of the gods).

"Vṛteva" means "by the path"; "iva" is in the sense of "now". By the path that runs between the two worlds, going together with many Vasus, or with the dwellings of the sacrificers, the sacrificers follow you as you go; they worship you. What are they like? In you, the god, they who are wakeful give wealth. What are you like? Shining in colour, Agni, endowed with qualities such as अंगनादि (*aṃganādi*),⟨NOTE:201⟩ beautiful to see, great, one who has the vapā, and shining at all times.
notes: ಏವಮಾಶಾಸ್ತ್ರೇ: sense of the last words unclear; also ದೀದಿನಾಂಸಂ printed for ದೀದಿವಾಂಸಂ

en: - जागृवांसः (*jāgṛvāṃsaḥ*)—the sacrificers devoted to your worship
- रुशंतं (*ruśaṃtaṃ*)—you who have a shining colour
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—you who have the qualities of अंगनादि (*aṃganādi*)
- दर्शतं (*darśataṃ*)—you who have an attractive form
- बृहंतं (*bṛhaṃtaṃ*)—you who have a vast form
- वृतेव (*vṛteva*)—on the path of the atmosphere

O Agni, the sacrificers devoted to your worship, desiring wealth from you, who have a shining colour, who have the qualities of अंगनादि (*aṃganādi*), who have an attractive form, who have a vast form,
one distinguished by oblations and food, who shines at all times, and who goes along the path of the atmosphere together with innumerable Vasus: they have come near you.

Those who are assiduous in (worshipping) you for riches follow you, going with many Vasus by the path (of the firmament); you, the radiant Agni, of goodly aspect, mighty, fed with burnt-offerings, and blazing every day.

Of the shining god Agni, the "pada" is the place of the Āhavanīya fire. The sacrificers of former times, going (vyantaḥ, "gacchantaḥ") there with an oblation or with praise (namasā), desiring food (śravasyavaḥ), obtain (āpan, "prāpnuvanti") śravas, that is, food that is heard of everywhere, amṛkta, unseized and not obstructed by others. O Agni, on account of the sight (saṃdṛṣṭi) of you that is praiseworthy (bhadrāyām) they rejoice (raṇayanta, "ramayanti"). They hold (dadhire, "dhārayanti") names fit for sacrifice (yajñiya) and worthy of homage, such as वैश्वानरो जातवेदा (*vaiśvānaro jātavedā*) and the like. Or else they hold hymns that are the means of bowing.
- देवस्य (*devasya*)—(O Agni) of you, the worshipful
- पदं (*padaṃ*)—the place in the form of the Āhavanīya
- नमसा (*namasā*)—with food in the form of oblation
- व्यंतः (*vyaṃtaḥ*)—those who come and gather (for the sacrifice)
- अमृक्तं (*amṛktaṃ*)—that which cannot be taken away by anyone
- नामानि चित् (*nāmāni cit*)—names also, such as Jātavedas and the like
- वधिरे (*vadhire*)—they obtain in the form of meditation (they recite)

O Agni, the sacrificers, who come and gather for your worship, bringing food in the form of oblation to your place, the Āhavanīya, and who desire food, have prepared food that cannot be taken away by anyone. They rejoice on account of the auspicious sight of you. They recite also your names that are worthy of worship, such as Jātavedas.

Men desirous of food obtain abundance unopposed when repairing to the station of the divinity with oblations ; and when delighting, Agni, in your auspicious persence, they repeat those your names which are to be uttered at sacrifices.

व्यंतः (*vyaṃtaḥ*)—going. Yāska has given the etymology of this word thus: व्यंत इत्येषोऽनेककर्मा । पदं देवस्य नमसा व्यंतः इति पश्यतिकर्मा । व्रीहि शूर पुरोळाशं इति खादतिकर्मा । वीतं पातं पयस उस्रियायाः अश्नीतं पिबतं पयस उस्रियायाः । उस्रियेति गोनाम । उस्राविणोऽस्यां भोगाः । उस्रेति च ॥ (*vyaṃta ityeṣo 'nekakarmā | padaṃ devasya namasā vyaṃtaḥ iti paśyatikarmā | vrīhi śūra puroḷāśaṃ iti khādatikarmā | vītaṃ pātaṃ payasa usriyāyāḥ aśnītaṃ pibataṃ payasa usriyāyāḥ | usriyeti gonāma | usrāviṇo 'syāṃ bhogāḥ | usreti ca ‖*) (Ni. 4-19)

That is: in the Ṛk पदं देवस्य नमसा व्यंतः (*padaṃ devasya namasā vyaṃtaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-1-4) the word vyantaḥ is used in the sense of "seeing". Sāyaṇa has taken it to mean "they approach". In the Ṛk इमा ब्रह्म ब्रह्मवाहः (*imā brahma brahmavāhaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-41-3) the word is used in the sense of "eating". In the Ṛk उत वां विक्षु (*uta vāṃ vikṣu*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-153-4) also the word वीतं (*vītaṃ*) has the meaning "eating". The word उस्रिया (*usriyā*) means a cow, because in this cow the means of enjoyment, such as milk, flow, that is, are milked. Therefore the main sense of the etymology is that the word उस्रिया (*usriyā*) or उस्रा (*usrā*) means a cow.

O Agni, the kṣitayaḥ, that is, men, the priests, make you grow on the earth in the form of the altar. The riches (rāyaḥ) of the sacrificers (janānām) are of two kinds (ubhayāsaḥ), consisting of animals and of what is not animals; the priests, the Adhvaryu and the others, increase them with reference to you. Or else: they increase you in order to obtain the two kinds of wealth, such as गनादीनि (*ganādīni*),⟨NOTE:202⟩ for the sake of the sons and others of the people. O taraṇe, Agni who carry across from suffering, you, to be known (cetya) and praised, have become the protector (trātā). Moreover you have always become father and mother to men (mānuṣāṇām), us your praisers, standing in the place of mother and father.
notes: ಸ್ತೋತ್ಥನಸ್ಮಾನ್: garbled; read as "us the praisers"

en: - पृथिव्यां (*pṛthivyāṃ*)—in the place of the altar
- उभयासः (*ubhayāsaḥ*)—in the form of cattle and wealth
- त्वां (*tvāṃ*)—you (they worship for the sake of those riches)
O Agni, the sacrificers cause you to blaze up and grow in the place of the altar. They worship you, who bring to men riches in the form of cattle and wealth, for the sake of those riches.
O Agni, the protector, you have become a worshipful protector. To men you are at all times both mother and father.

Men exalt you upon earth : they exalt you for both kinds of affluence, (cattle and treasure, which you bestow upon) men : you who extricate (us from evil) are to be known as our preserver, as the unfailing father and mother of mankind.

That Agni is worthy of worship (saparyeṇya) and dear (priya), the fulfiller of desires. Among the people (vikṣu) he is the Hotṛ, the accomplisher of the offering; he is mandra, delightful; he is yajīyān, the best sacrificer to the other gods, or else the one who is to be sacrificed to. Such a greatly powerful Agni has sat down; then he was made visible. We, the sacrificers, in the house (dame) approach you who are blazing, bending our knees (jñubādhaḥ, "bending the knees", bowing low), with praise (namasā). "May we approach" (upa sadema) means "may we bring near"; or else it is a wish "may we sit near".⟨NOTE:203⟩
notes: ಉಕ್ಷೈಃ printed; ಉಕ್ಥೈಃ in the Saṃhitā

en: - यजीयान् (*yajīyān*)—one who conducts the sacrifice in the highest degree
- तं त्वा (*taṃ tvā*)—you such as that
- उप आ सदेम (*upa ā sadema*)—we approach

Agni, who is worthy of worship, the fulfiller of desires, the accomplisher of the offering among the people, the giver of delight, and the one who conducts the sacrifice in the highest degree, has been established in the house of sacrifice. O Agni, we approach you who are shining, bowing down on bended knee and with praise.

Agni, who is adorable, affectionate, the offerer of oblations amongst men, the giver of delight, the celebrator of worship, has sat down (upon the altar: let us approach you, kindled in our dwellings, on bended knees, with praise.
O Agni, to you, such a greatly powerful and praiseworthy (navya) one, we who are of good mind (sudhyaḥ), desiring happiness (sumnāyavaḥ), and desiring you as god, make our request (īmahe).

"We make our request" means "we praise". O Agni, you are shining (dīdyāna). By what? By great, radiant brilliance. Shining thus, you have led (anayaḥ, "agamayaḥ") the people (viśaḥ), us your praisers,⟨NOTE:204⟩ to heaven (divaḥ), that is, to the world of svarga. Or else the connection is: with the sun, which is the rocana, you led them to heaven; that is, by the path of the sun.
notes: ಐದನೆಯ ಮಂಡಲದಲ್ಲಿ ಎರಡನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು printed ("fifth maṇḍala"); the sūkta head on p. 382 and the bhāṣya say Maṇḍala 6

en: - देवयंतः (*devayaṃtaḥ*)—desiring the favour of the gods

O Agni, we, who have excellent intelligence, who desire wealth and who desire the favour of the gods, praise you, the praiseworthy. O Agni, you who shine with abundant brilliance lead the sacrificers to heaven.
Intelligent, hoping for happiness, and devout, we glorify you, adorable Agni: shining with exceeding lustre, lead men to heaven.

"We praise Agni" is the word to be supplied. "Śaśvatī" means eternal; "viśām" means of the people, that is, of the priests and sacrificers; "viśpati" means lord. Agni is kavi, far-seeing (krāntadarśin); nitośana, the destroyer of enemies; vṛṣabha, the showerer of desires; carṣaṇī, the praisers, that is, men, whose lord he is; preti-ṣaṇi, one whose going is accomplished; iṣayantam, one who makes food; pāvaka, the purifier; rājantam, shining or making others shine; and yajata, to be worshipped for the gain of riches (rayāṇām).
- शश्वतीनां (*śaśvatīnāṃ*)—of those who always perform sacrifice
- प्रतीषणिं (*pratīṣaṇiṃ*)—the bringer of the desired object

We praise and worship Agni, who is the lord of the priests and others who perform sacrifice every day, who is far-seeing, the destroyer of enemies, the showerer of desires, the bringer of the desired object to the praisers, the provider of food, the purifier, the shining, who is worshipped for the sake of riches.

(We glorify) the lord of men, of ever-existing men; the wise, the destroyer (of foes), the showerer (of benefits) on mankind, the moving, the bestower of food, the purifier, the resplendent, Agni, who is worshipped for (the sake of) riches.

O Agni, that mortal, that sacrificer, worships you (ईजे (*īje*), "yajate") and praises you (शशमे (*śaśame*), "stauti"). Since कशमान (*kaśamāna*) is read among the words for praise, this word too means praise. The sacrificer who performs for you, with fuel (samidhā), the gift of oblations (havyadāti, "ānaṭ karoti"); and moreover the sacrificer who with salutations, that is, with praises, gives the offering (āhuti), consisting of ghee and the like, all round (pari veda, "paritaḥ vetti", meaning "gives"): that sacrificer, protected by you, holds (dadhate, "dhārayati") all desirable (vāmā, "vananīyāni") riches.

O Agni, the sacrificer who offers you the gift of oblation with fuel, and who offers the oblation of ghee all round with praises, he alone truly worships you and praises you. That same sacrificer, protected by you, obtains all attractive riches.

The man. Agni, who worships you, who praises you, who offers oblations to you with kindled fuel, who presents burnt-offerings to you with prostrations, he verily, protected by you, obtains all desired wealth.
शशमे (*śaśame*)—praises. The word शशमानः (*śaśamānaḥ*) is read among the names that mean "worship" (Ni. 3-9), and this word is also used in the sense of "praise". Yāska has said:
शशमानः । शंसमानः । यो नां यज्ञैः शशमानो ह दाशति कविर्होता यजति मन्मसाधनः (*śaśamānaḥ | śaṃsamānaḥ | yo nāṃ yajñaiḥ śaśamāno ha dāśati kavirhotā yajati manmasādhanaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-151-7)
Having said that the word शशमानः (*śaśamānaḥ*) means one who is praised, one who is lauded, he has given as an example, in support of it, the Ṛk beginning यो नां यज्ञैः (*yo nāṃ yajñaiḥ*).

O Agni, to you, the great (mahe), we offer service (vidhema, "paricarema") exceedingly (mahi). With what? With salutations (namobhiḥ), with fuel (samidhā), and also with oblations (havyaiḥ). O son of strength (sahasaḥ sūno), on the altar (vedī), with hymns (gīrbhiḥ), that is, with praises, and with recitations (śastras), we serve: this is the connection.⟨NOTE:205⟩ Moreover may we strive (yatema, "āgacchema", that is, "may we become") toward your auspicious (bhadrāyām, praiseworthy) good will of favour (sumati).
notes: ಆ. ೧೨-೨ in the Kannada; Sāyaṇa's text has ಆ. ೧೦. ೨.

en: - सहसः सूनो (*sahasaḥ sūno*)—O Agni, son of strength
- आ यतेम (*ā yatema*)—may we be sheltered

O Agni, to you, the great one, we offer worship exceedingly, with salutations, with fuel and with śastra mantras. O Agni, son of strength, on the sacrificial altar we worship you with praises and with śastra mantras. We worship so that your auspicious, favouring intention may rest upon us.

To you, mighty Agni, we offer exceeding adoration with prostrations, with fuel, with oblations : (we glorify you) on the altar, son of strength, with hymns and with prayers: may we be successful in our efforts(to gain) your auspicious favour.

O Agni, you who have spread (vyā tatantha, "vyatanoḥ") heaven and earth (rodasī) with light (bhāsā, "dīptyā"). Moreover you, the deliverer (taruttra, "tāraka"), by praises (śravobhiḥ, "stutibhiḥ") are also श्रवस्यः (*śravasyaḥ*). O such Agni, with great (bṛhadbhiḥ) foods (vājaiḥ), with thick, substantial (sthavirebhiḥ) and wealthy (revadbhiḥ, "rayimadbhiḥ") ones, shine for us (asme, "asmadartham") exceedingly (vitaram, "viśiṣṭataram"); that is, shine in a special manner (vi bhāhi).
- वि आ ततंथ (*vi ā tataṃtha*)—have spread and pervaded

O Agni, you who have spread and pervaded both heaven and earth with your brilliance, and who, being the protector, are worshipped with praises: such as you are, shine for us exceedingly, with abundant foods and plentiful riches.

Do you, Agni, who have spread heaven and earth with light, who are the preserver (of man), and (who are) to be glorified with praises, shine brightly upon us with abundant food, and with substantial riches.

O Vasu, that is, O Agni who bestow dwelling and wealth, always place (dhehi, "sthāpaya") in us wealth accompanied by men (nṛvat, "manuṣyairupetam"). Moreover place abundant (bhūri) cattle (paśvaḥ, "paśūn"). For what purpose? For our son (tokāya) and his son (tanayāya). Moreover may there be with us foods of the stated kind: pūrvīḥ, those that fulfil desires, or many; bṛhatīḥ, great; and āre-aghāḥ, those in which sins are far away. May there be with us auspicious (bhadrā) and well-famed (sauśravasāni) conditions.
- अस्मे संतु (*asme saṃtu*)—may there be for us

O wealthy Agni, always provide us with wealth accompanied by men. Provide our sons and their sons with plentiful cattle. Provide also foods that are abundantly satisfying, great in measure and free from sin. May auspicious conditions that bring fame be ours.

Possessor of wealth, bestow upon us at all times opulence conjoined with dependants, and (grant) abundance of cattle to our sons and grandsons: may there be to us abundant food, satisfying our wishes, and free from blame; and may there be auspicious and reputable (means of subsistence).

The thirteenth Ṛk, पुरूण्यग्न (*purūṇyagna*), is the invitatory verse (anuvākyā) to Agni Kṣatravat in the Ukhāsaṃbharaṇīya offering. The sūtra says: पुरूण्यग्ने पुरुषा त्वाया स चित्र चित्रं जितयंतमस्मे! (*purūṇyagne puruṣā tvāyā sa citra citraṃ jitayaṃtamasme!*) (Ā. 4-1). O Agni, king, may I obtain, for the sake of wealth (vasutā, "vasumattvāya"), your many (purūṇi) treasures (vasūni) of many kinds (purudhā), in the form of cows, horses and the like; that is, may I pervade, may I enjoy. Here Bharatasvāmin took वसूतात (*vasūtāta*) as one word in the locative, while Bhaṭṭabhāskara Miśra took one word in the vocative. O puruvāra, Agni, to be chosen by many, in you who shine (rājani) there are many riches (vasu), which are to be given to me who serve (vidhate, "paricarate") you.
- पुरुधा (*purudhā*)—of many kinds, in the form of cows, horses and the like
- संति हि (*saṃti hi*)—are they not established

O lord Agni, may I obtain from you, for the sake of increase of prosperity, your abundant riches of many kinds, in the form of cows, horses and the like. O Agni, honoured by many, are not the riches that are in you, the shining one, established for me, who serve you?

Royal Agni, may I obtain from you your many and various treasures whereby to be enriched; for, Agni, who are the desired of multitudes, infinite are the riches(aggregated) in you, fit, monarch, for your worshipper.

This Ṛk, beginning पुरुण्यग्ने (*puruṇyagne*), is to be used as an anuvākya mantra, to be recited by the kṣatriya (the sacrificer) when he makes the offering to Agni in the iṣṭi called Ukhāsambharaṇa; this is set out by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra aphorism पुरुण्यग्ने पुरुधा त्वाया स चित्र चित्रं चितयंतमस्मे (*puruṇyagne purudhā tvāyā sa citra citraṃ citayaṃtamasme*) (Ā. 4-1).

वसुता ते (*vasutā te*): although the Pada-pāṭha clearly divides the words as वसुता (*vasutā*), ते (*te*), Bharatasvāmin, when explaining the meaning of this Ṛk in his bhāṣya, takes वसुताते (*vasutāte*) as one word and says that it is a word in the locative, while Bhaṭṭabhāskara Miśra says that it is a word in the vocative and explains the meaning accordingly; Sāyaṇa points this out here, that is, in his own bhāṣya. It need not be said separately that it is not right to depart from the word-division given by Śaunaka and the other ṛṣis, the Pada-pāṭha makers of the Ṛgveda, to divide the words differently as suits the occasion, and to explain the meaning in various ways.
वेदार्थस्य प्रकाशेन तमो हार्दं निवारयन् । पुमर्थांश्च तुरो देयाद्विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरः ॥ (*vedārthasya prakāśena tamo hārdaṃ nivārayan | pumarthāṃśca turo deyādvidyātīrthamaheśvaraḥ ‖*) **GLOSS**

इति श्रीमद्राजाधिराज परमेश्वर वैदिकमार्गप्रवर्तक श्री वीरबुक्क भूपालसाम्राज्य - धुरंधरेण सायणाचार्येण विरचिते माधवीये वेदार्थप्रकाशे ऋक्संहिताभाष्ये चतुर्थाष्टके चतुर्थोऽध्यायः समाप्तः ॥ (*iti śrīmadrājādhirāja parameśvara vaidikamārgapravartaka śrī vīrabukka bhūpālasāmrājya - dhuraṃdhareṇa sāyaṇācāryeṇa viracite mādhavīye vedārthaprakāśe ṛksaṃhitābhāṣye caturthāṣṭake caturtho 'dhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ ‖*)
Here ends the fourth adhyāya in the fourth aṣṭaka of the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, with the bhāṣya of Śrī Sāyaṇa and with the Kannada translation.

यदक्षरपदभ्रष्टं मात्राहीनं तु यद्भवेत् । तत्सर्वक्षं क्षम्युतां देव वागीश्वर समोऽस्तुते ॥ (*yadakṣarapadabhraṣṭaṃ mātrāhīnaṃ tu yadbhavet | tatsarvakṣaṃ kṣamyutāṃ deva vāgīśvara samo 'stute ‖*) **GLOSS**
वागीशाद्याः सुमनसः सर्वार्थानामुपक्रमे । यं नत्वा कृतकृत्याः स्युस्तं नमामि गजाननं ॥ (*vāgīśādyāḥ sumanasaḥ sarvārthānāmupakrame | yaṃ natvā kṛtakṛtyāḥ syustaṃ namāmi gajānanaṃ ‖*) **GLOSS**
यस्य निश्चसितं वेदा यो वेदेभ्योऽखिलं जगत् । निर्ममे तमहं वंदे विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरं ॥ (*yasya niścasitaṃ vedā yo vedebhyo 'khilaṃ jagat | nirmame tamahaṃ vaṃde vidyātīrthamaheśvaraṃ ‖*) **GLOSS**
वेदः शिवः शिवो वेदो वेदाध्याया सदाशिवः । तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन वेदमेव सदा जपेत् ॥ (*vedaḥ śivaḥ śivo vedo vedādhyāyā sadāśivaḥ | tasmātsarvaprayatnena vedameva sadā japet ‖*) **GLOSS**

O Agni, you indeed go towards the यशः (*yaśaḥ*), the food in the form of the oblation, which is क्षैतवत् (*kṣaitavat*). क्षितिः (*kṣitiḥ*) is क्षयोऽपचयः (*kṣayo 'pacayaḥ*) (waste, decay); what belongs to it is क्षैतं (*kṣaitaṃ*), dry wood; क्षैतवत् (*kṣaitavat*) is what is joined with that. पत्यसे (*patyase*) means you approach, you go. An example is given: like Mitra, the deity presiding over the day. Or else: यशः (*yaśaḥ*) is a name for a house; क्षैतवत् (*kṣaitavat*) is food in the form of the oblation, which is "that which dwells" (क्षितं निवासकं (*kṣitaṃ nivāsakaṃ*)), joined with it; you approach the sacrificer's house like a man who is a friend. Or else: the root पति (*pati*) has the sense of lordship; you rule over food of this kind. For this reason, O one who sees everything in particular (विचर्षणे (*vicarṣaṇe*)), O giver of dwelling (वसो (*vaso*)) Agni, you make grow the famed food (श्रवः (*śravaḥ*)) that is in the sacrificer's house, and the nourishment that is its result. The word न (*na*) here has the sense of "and".
- यशः (*yaśaḥ*)—in order to accept the oblation
- विचर्षणे (*vicarṣaṇe*)—who are able to see everything fully
- श्रवः (*śravaḥ*)—in the sacrificer's house, wealth of food
- पुष्टिं (*puṣṭiṃ*)—wealth of cattle that gives nourishment

O Agni, you come like Mitra, desiring the oblation provided with dry wood. You, who can see everything fully and give a dwelling, increase in the sacrificer's house the wealth of food and likewise the wealth of cattle that gives nourishment.
You alight, Agni. like Mitra, upon the oblation offered with the dry fuel: therefore, beholder of all, possessor of riches, you cherish us with food and nourishment.
अग्ने त्वं हि मित्रो न क्षैतवत् यशः पत्स्यसे (*agne tvaṃ hi mitro na kṣaitavat yaśaḥ patsyase*): the bhāṣya-writer has given two or three kinds of meaning for this sentence.

(1) क्षितिः क्षयोऽपचयः । तत्संबंधि क्षैशं शुष्कं काष्ठं । तद्युक्तं यशोऽन्नं हनिर्लक्षणं पत्यसे । अभिपतसि । गच्छसि । (*kṣitiḥ kṣayo 'pacayaḥ | tatsaṃbaṃdhi kṣaiśaṃ śuṣkaṃ kāṣṭhaṃ | tadyuktaṃ yaśo 'nnaṃ hanirlakṣaṇaṃ patyase | abhipatasi | gacchasi |*) Here क्षिति (*kṣiti*) means what has fallen from a tree, shed. क्षैतं (*kṣaitaṃ*) means dry wood that is related to that. क्षैतवत् (*kṣaitavat*) means dry wood, or

provided with kindling-sticks, is the intention. यशः (*yaśaḥ*) means food, or the oblation that has the form of food. Therefore, one kind of meaning for this sentence is: O Agni, in order to accept the oblation provided with kindling-sticks, you come, aiming at it, like Mitra, the deity presiding over the day.

(2) यद्वा यश इति गृहनाम । क्षैतवत् क्षैतं निवासकं हविर्लक्षणमन्नं तद्युक्तं यजमानगृहं मित्रभूतः पुरुष इवाभिपतसि ॥ (*yadvā yaśa iti gṛhanāma | kṣaitavat kṣaitaṃ nivāsakaṃ havirlakṣaṇamannaṃ tadyuktaṃ yajamānagṛhaṃ mitrabhūtaḥ puruṣa ivābhipatasi ‖*) Or else, यश (*yaśa*) is a name for a house. क्षैत (*kṣaita*) means dwelling, or being. Another kind of meaning is: O Agni, as a man who is a friend of the sacrificer comes to his house for the excellent food that is in the sacrificer's house, so you come desiring the food in the form of the oblation that is made ready in the sacrificer's house.

(3) यद्वा पत्यतिरैश्वर्यकर्मा । ईदृशमन्नं पत्यसे ईशिषे । (*yadvā patyatiraiśvaryakarmā | īdṛśamannaṃ patyase īśiṣe |*) Or else, since the root पत्यति (*patyati*) has the sense of lordship, O Agni, you are the master of the food in the form of the oblation that is in the sacrificer's house; therefore, desiring that food, you come there. This is yet another kind of meaning.

O Agni, it is you alone whom men (चर्षणयः (*carṣaṇayaḥ*)) praise with offerings, the means of sacrifice, and with hymns (गीर्भिः (*gīrbhiḥ*)). And वाजी (*vājī*): vāja is going; the Sun, who possesses it, goes to you, that is, enters you. So it is heard in the Veda: the Sun enters Agni in the evening, and therefore Agni is seen from afar at night. The word वाजि (*vāji*) is heard in some places as denoting the Sun: अग्निर्वायुः सूर्यस्ते वै वाजिनः (*agnirvāyuḥ sūryaste vai vājinaḥ*) (Tai. Brā. 1. 6. 3. 9) **GLOSS**

And likewise वायुः सप्तिरादित्यो वाजी (*vāyuḥ saptirādityo vājī*) **GLOSS** What sort of वाजी (*vājī*) is he? He is अवृकः (*avṛkaḥ*), free from those who injure. रजस्तूः (*rajastūḥ*): here रज (*raja*) is said to be water; he is the impeller of it, which has the nature of rain. Or else: he is the one who crosses, who goes through, the रजसां लोकानां (*rajasāṃ lokānāṃ*), the worlds. विश्वचर्षणिः (*viśvacarṣaṇiḥ*) is the seer of all.
- त्वां हि स्म (*tvāṃ hi sma*)—you alone
- यज्ञेभिः (*yajñebhiḥ*)—with offerings that are the means of sacrifice
- अवृकः (*avṛkaḥ*)—the one who is not a harmer
- रजस्तूः (*rajastūḥ*)—the one who pours down rain-water
- विश्वचर्षणिः (*viśvacarṣaṇiḥ*)—the one who looks at all the worlds
- वाजी (*vājī*)—the Sun, who is of the nature of revolving

O Agni, the people praise you alone with offerings that are the means of sacrifice and with hymns. The Sun, who does no harm, who pours down rain-water, who looks at all the worlds, who is of the nature of revolving, approaches you.
n verily worship you with sacrifice and with praises: the inoffensive sun, the sender of rain, the beholder of the universe, proceeds to you. ⟨NOTE:208⟩
notes: ಪುತ್ರಪಾತ್ರಾದಿ in Sāyaṇa; the Kannada Pratipadārtha has ಪುತ್ರಪೌತ್ರಾದಿ "sons, grandsons and the like"

en: त्वां वाजी अवृकः रजस्तूः विश्वचर्षणि याति (*tvāṃ vājī avṛkaḥ rajastūḥ viśvacarṣaṇi yāti*): here the bhāṣya-writer states the meaning that the Sun approaches Agni and enters into it, and in support of this meaning he has cited a Śruti sentence of the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa:
अग्निं वावादित्यः सायं प्रविशति । तस्मादग्निर्दूर्रान्नक्तं ददृशे । (*agniṃ vāvādityaḥ sāyaṃ praviśati | tasmādagnirdūrrānnaktaṃ dadṛśe |*) (Trai. Brā. 2-1-2-9) ⟨NOTE:209⟩
The meaning explained here is that the Sun, in the evening, enters Agni and becomes one with it.
वाजि (*vāji*): for the word वाजी (*vājī*) the Śruti sentence वायुः सप्तिरादित्यो वाजी (*vāyuḥ saptirādityo vājī*) (Tai. Brā. 1-7-8), in which the word has the meaning "the Sun", has been cited.
notes: ಚಿರಕಾಲಜೀವನಂ ನಾ ಕ್ಷಯಂ: ನಾ unclear in the machine-read text

en: O Agni, the सजोषः (*sajoṣaḥ*), those who are pleased together, the नरः (*naraḥ*), the leaders, the priests, of praise (दिवः (*divaḥ*) is glossed as praise), kindle you, the केतुं (*ketuṃ*), the one who makes the sacrifice known; that is, they make you kindled. If it is asked when: यद्ध (*yaddha*), when that man (मानुषः (*mānuṣaḥ*)), the person born of Manu, the sacrificer or the hotṛ, desiring सुम्न (*sumna*), happiness, for himself, जुह्वे (*juhve*), calls you in the अध्वरे (*adhvare*), the sacrifice that is free from injury and obstacle; that is the meaning: then.
- स्यः (*syaḥ*)—the one who is well known as the sacrificer
- मानुषः जनः (*mānuṣaḥ janaḥ*)—and the man who belongs to Manu
- जुह्वे (*juhve*)—he prays to you and calls you (then)

O Agni, when the sacrificer who belongs to Manu, desiring to obtain happiness, prays to you and calls you to the sacrifice, then the priests, who have equal affection and are leaders for the praises, make you, who make the sacrifice known, blaze.
The offerers of praise, sympathizing in satisfaction, kindle you the banner of the sacrifice, when man, the descendant of Manu, desiring happiness, invokes you to the rite.

यधत् (*yadhat*): may that sacrificer prosper. O Agni, to you, सुदानवे (*sudānave*), of good gifts (the dative is used in the sense of the genitive), the mortal, the sacrificer subject to death, who through your धिया (*dhiyā*), that is, rite, शशमते (*śaśamate*), toils; or else the root शमति (*śamati*) has the sense of praise: being engaged in the rite for your sake, he praises. That sacrificer, through the protection (ऊती (*ūtī*)) belonging to you, who are great (बृहतः (*bṛhataḥ*)) and shining (दिवः (*divaḥ*)), overcomes his haters (द्विषः (*dviṣaḥ*)), as if they were sin (अंहः (*aṃhaḥ*)) that is of a striking nature; तरति (*tarati*) means he surpasses.
- मर्तः (*martaḥ*)—the sacrificer who is a man
- सुदानवे ते (*sudānave te*)—addressing you, who are worthy of excellent gifts
- अंहो न (*aṃho na*)—as one crosses sins

O Agni, may the mortal sacrificer who, addressing you, the giver of excellent gifts, offers praise joined with an excellent rite, attain prosperity. The same man, with the protections of you, who are great in nature and shining, overcomes his enemies as he crosses all his sins.
May the mortal prosper who propitiates you, (his) benefactor, by holy rites : through the protection of you who are resplendent, he over- comes those who hate him, as if they were mortal sins.

O Agni, the mortal, the man, who attains (नशत् (*naśat*); the root नति (*nati*) has the sense of pervading) your oblation (आहुतिं (*āhutiṃ*)), made thin (निशितां (*niśitāṃ*), तनूकृतां (*tanūkṛtāṃ*)) and consecrated by mantra, together with the समिधा (*samidhā*), the fuel that is the means of kindling: that man, the sacrificer, makes grow (पुष्यति (*puṣyati*)) the house (क्षयं (*kṣayaṃ*)) that has वयावंतं (*vayāvaṃtaṃ*), branches, पुत्रपात्रादिलक्षणाः (*putrapātrādilakṣaṇāḥ*) ⟨NOTE:210⟩, and is joined with them, शतायुषं (*śatāyuṣaṃ*), with many kinds of food and long life ना (*nā*) ⟨NOTE:211⟩; and he stays there for a long time.
notes: ಮನು. printed; not in the list of abbreviations, read as Manu
ತ್ವಮತ್ತೋ ನ ಸತತಗಾಮಿಾ printed; Pada has ಅತ್ಯಃ

en: - यः मर्त्यः (*yaḥ martyaḥ*)—the sacrificer, who is a man
- वयावंतं (*vayāvaṃtaṃ*)—joined with branches (descendants) such as sons and grandsons

O Agni, the sacrificer, a man, who fills with kindling-sticks your oblation, consecrated by mantra, and makes it ripe, that same sacrificer makes grow a house that is joined with branches such as sons and grandsons and with long life.
The mortal who feeds your consecrated burnt-offering with fuel enjoys, Agni, a dwelling peopled with descendants, and a life of a hundred years.

O Agni, the smoke of you who are त्वेषः (*tveṣaḥ*), shining, is शुक्रः (*śukraḥ*), clean or of a white colour; spread out and extended in the sky (the atmosphere), it ऋण्वति (*ṛṇvati*), that is, goes, having been transformed into the form of a cloud. And, O purifying Agni, like the sun, you, who are praised with a hymn that is able to turn you towards the worshipper in favour, shine with brilliance; you are indeed lit up.
- त्वेषः (*tveṣaḥ*)—(O Agni) of you who are shining
- आततः सन् (*ātataḥ san*)—having spread out widely
- ऋण्वति (*ṛṇvati*)—is transformed into the form of a cloud
- कृपा (*kṛpā*)—praised with a hymn able to obtain your favour
- रोचसे हि (*rocase hi*)—do you not shine?

O Agni, the white smoke of you who are shining spreads widely in the atmosphere and is transformed into the form of a cloud. O purifying Agni, you, who are praised with a hymn able to obtain your favour, shine with your brilliance like the sun, do you not?
The pure smoke of you the resplendent spreads through firma- ment, matures (in clouds), and you, the purifier, shine with radiance like the sun. when propitiated by praise.

And further, O Agni, among the people (विक्षु (*vikṣu*)) you are ईड्यः (*īḍyaḥ*), to be praised; the word हि (*hi*) is used in the sense of "since". Since this is so, you are our guest; this is a comparison with the word of likeness dropped: you are dear like a guest. Or else: having become one who goes constantly to carry the oblations, you are dear to us. Likewise, like an old man (जूर्यः (*jūryaḥ*)) in a city, one who is advanced in age and gives advice for one's good, or like a king, you are रण्वः (*raṇvaḥ*), delightful, one to be approached. Likewise, like a son (सूनुर्न (*sūnurna*)) you are त्रययाय्कः (*trayayāykaḥ*), one to be guarded and protected by the sacrificers. He says that this is a form from the root meaning "to protect"; or else it is an epithet of the son: one who goes to a triad, namely knowledge, austerity and rite. Or else त्रययाय्कः (*trayayāykaḥ*) means one who has obtained three births. The three births are remembered thus: मातुरग्रेऽधिजननं द्वितीयं मौंजिबंधनात् । तृतीयं यज्ञदीक्षाया इति जन्मत्रयं स्मृतं । (*māturagre 'dhijananaṃ dvitīyaṃ mauṃjibaṃdhanāt | tṛtīyaṃ yajñadīkṣāyā iti janmatrayaṃ smṛtaṃ |*) (Ma. Smṛ. 2-169) **GLOSS** ⟨NOTE:212⟩. Such a son you are; you are delightful.
notes: ದಿವಃ ಸ್ತುತೇರ್ನ್ನೇನ್ತಸ್ಯ ನಸ್ಮಾನ್ garbled

en: - अध हि (*adha hi*)—precisely because you possess great qualities
- जूर्यः इव (*jūryaḥ iva*)—like an old man (who gives advice for the good of all)
- रण्वः (*raṇvaḥ*)—as one who is beneficial and dear
- त्रययाय्यः (*trayayāyyaḥ*)—one who is to be protected by the sacrificers
- सूनुः न (*sūnuḥ na*)—like a son (you are dear)

O Agni, precisely because you possess great qualities, you are worthy of praise among all the people. You are a guest dear to us. As in a city an old man, who gives advice for the good of all, is beneficial and dear, and as a son who is to be protected by the sacrificers in the house is dear, so you are dear to all.
You are now to be praised amongst the people, for you are our well beloved guest, venerated like an elder in the city, and to be cherished like a son.

O Agni, you who are present in the द्रोणे (*droṇe*), in the tree, in the wood, the fire-stick, are अज्यसे (*ajyase*), made manifest, by the work, the क्रत्वा (*kratvā*), that has the form of churning. And you are like a वाजी (*vājī*), a horse that has speed, कृत्त्वः (*kṛttvaḥ*): कृत्व (*kṛtva*) is a name for work; you are the doer of the works such as carrying the oblation. As a horse carries a man, so is the carrying of the oblation; this is Agni's likeness to a horse. And you are परिज्जीव (*parijjīva*), one who goes all round, everywhere, like the wind, going everywhere in the form of a forest fire and the like. स्वधा (*svadhā*) is a name for food; you are food and also the house (गयः (*gayaḥ*)).

That is, you are the giver of both. And further, you who are शिशुः (*śiśuḥ*), a child just born, are like a thoroughbred horse that goes constantly ⟨NOTE:213⟩, ह्वार्यः (*hvāryaḥ*), crooked, one who goes hither and thither. He says that this is a form of the root ह्वृ कौटिल्य (*hvṛ kauṭilya*).
notes: sentence breaks off: ಈ ಸೂಕ್ತದ ಪಿಸಿಯೋಗವಿರುವುದೇ

en: - द्रोणे (*droṇe*)—you who stand in the fire-stick that has the form of wood
- क्रत्वा (*kratvā*)—by the act in the form of churning
- वाजी न (*vājī na*)—like a swift horse
- कृत्व्यः (*kṛtvyaḥ*)—you are engaged in works such as carrying the oblation
- परिज्जीव (*parijjīva*)—you are all-pervading like the wind that moves everywhere
- स्वधा (*svadhā*)—and the food in the form of the oblation
- अत्यो न (*atyo na*)—like a swift-going horse
- ह्यार्यः (*hyāryaḥ*)—you move about everywhere with a crooked course

O Agni, you who stood in the fire-stick, which has the form of wood, become manifest by the act of churning. Like a swift horse, you are engaged in works such as carrying the oblation. Like the wind that moves everywhere, you are all-pervading. You yourself are both the food in the form of the oblation and the house. Although just born and in the form of a child, you move about everywhere with a crooked course, like a swift-going horse.

You are manifested in the timber. Agni. by the act of attrition : you are the bearer (of the oblation). as a horse (is of his rider): you are like the circumambient wind : you are food and dwelling: you are like a (new-born) babe, and variable (in movement) as a horse.

Application: in the Kārīrī, for the Agni of the Dhāmacchad offering, this is the alternative anuvākyā; and it is laid down in the sūtra: त्वं त्या चिदच्युताग्ने पशुर्न यवसे । धामा ह यत्ते अजर वना वृश्चंति शिक्वसः ॥ ९ ॥ त्वं । त्या । चित् । अच्युता । अग्ने । पशुः । न । यवसे । धाम । ह । यत् । ते । अजर । वना । वृश्चंति । शिक्वसः ॥ ९ ॥ कारीर्यामग्नेर्धामच्छदो वैकल्पिक्यनुवाक्यात्वं त्येति । सूत्रितं च । त्वं त्या चिदच्युता धामंते विश्वं भुवनमधिश्रितं । (*tvaṃ tyā cidacyutāgne paśurna yavase | dhāmā ha yatte ajara vanā vṛścaṃti śikvasaḥ ‖ 9 ‖ tvaṃ | tyā | cit | acyutā | agne | paśuḥ | na | yavase | dhāma | ha | yat | te | ajara | vanā | vṛścaṃti | śikvasaḥ ‖ 9 ‖ kārīryāmagnerdhāmacchado vaikalpikyanuvākyātvaṃ tyeti | sūtritaṃ ca | tvaṃ tyā cidacyutā dhāmaṃte viśvaṃ bhuvanamadhiśritaṃ |*) (Ā. 2-13). O Agni, you त्या (*tyā*), those pieces of wood; the word चित् (*cit*) has the same sense as "even" and stands in a different order; अच्युता (*acyutā*), even those that cannot be made to fall; the word "beyond" is to be supplied. An example is given: पशुर्न (*paśurna*), like an animal let loose in the pasture to graze; as he eats everything, so you burn up grown wood and the like in a moment. O ageless Agni, यत् (*yat*), of you who are shining, the radiances (धाम (*dhāma*)) वना (*vanā*), the forests that are desirable and to be resorted to, वृश्चंति (*vṛścaṃti*), cut, hew; "you" is connected with what came before. ह (*ha*) is a filler of the line.
- यवसे (*yavase*)—let loose to graze in a pasture
- पशुः न (*paśuḥ na*)—as an animal eats the grass completely
- आच्युता चित् (*ācyutā cit*)—even though they have firm roots (you burn them completely and bring them down)
- अजर (*ajara*)—O Agni, who are free from old age
- वना (*vanā*)—all the trees and the like of the forest
- वृश्चंति हि (*vṛścaṃti hi*)—burn and consume, do they not

O Agni, as an animal let loose to graze in a pasture eats the grass completely, you burn the trees and the like completely and bring them down, although they have firm roots. O ageless Agni, the radiances of you who are shining burn and consume all the trees of the forest, do they not?
You :consume, Agni, the unfallen (trees) as an animal (feeds) upon pasture, when, undecaying deity, the flames of you who are resplendent shear the forests.

In the Kārīrī iṣṭi, in the alternative purodāśa offering made to Agni of the Dhāmacchad offering, this Ṛk, beginning त्वं त्या (*tvaṃ tyā*), is to be used as an anuvākyā mantra; this is set out by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra aphorism (Ā. 2-13) that is quoted in the bhāṣya above, ending with "or".

O Agni, in the house of the sacrificers who desire the sacrifice for themselves (अध्वरीयतां (*adhvarīyatāṃ*)), you, being the hotṛ, the caller of the gods, वेषि (*veṣi*), desire praise or oblations; therefore, O protector of the people (विश्वते (*viśvate*)), make us sacrificers (समृधः (*samṛdhaḥ*)) prosperous (कृणु (*kṛṇu*) is "do"). Having done so, O अंगिरः (*aṃgiraḥ*), endowed with qualities such as अंगनादि (*aṃganādi*), or in the form of embers, partake of (जुषस्व (*juṣasva*), "serve") our oblation.
- अध्वरीयतां (*adhvarīyatāṃ*)—of the sacrificers who desire the sacrifice
- वेषि हि (*veṣi hi*)—you desire oblations and the like
- विश्वते (*viśvate*)—O Agni, protector of the people
- अंगिरः (*aṃgiraḥ*)—O Agni, endowed with qualities such as अंगनादि (*aṃganādi*)

O Agni in the form of Aṅgiras, being the hotṛ in the house of the sacrificers who desire the sacrifice, you desire oblations and the like. O Agni, protector of the people, make all the sacrificers endowed with prosperity, and afterwards accept their oblation and partake of it.
You enter as the ministrant priest into the habitations of men who wish to perform sacrifice : render them prosperous, benefactor of mankind : be propitiated, Angiras, by oblation.

O मित्रमहः (*mitramahaḥ*), favourably shining one, O divine Agni, endowed with qualities such as giving, you who abide in रोदस्योः (*rodasyoḥ*), heaven and earth, वोचः (*vocaḥ*), speak, that is, say, to the gods who are to be worshipped, Indra and the others, turning towards them (अच्छ (*accha*)), our सुमतिं (*sumatiṃ*), praise. Then वीहि (*vīhi*): lead us, who are of दिवः (*divaḥ*), of praise, and are the leaders (the text of this phrase is damaged) ⟨NOTE:214⟩, to स्वस्तिं (*svastiṃ*), imperishable well-being, that is endowed with a good dwelling (सुक्षितिं (*sukṣitiṃ*)); the root वे (*ve*) here is to be seen as containing a causative sense, "cause to go". And we

may overcome (तरेम (*tarema*), may we pass beyond) the द्विषः (*dviṣaḥ*), haters, the enemies, and the अंहांसि (*aṃhāṃsi*), sins, and the दुरिता (*duritā*), which are their fruits, hard to get through. Likewise may we overcome those (ता (*tā*)) sins and the like, set apart (that is, removed in time), that were done in other births. The meaning already stated is repeated for the sake of firmness. O Agni, by your protection may we completely overcome the haters and the others.
notes: ಉಷಿತ್ವಾ ಚ unclear

en: - रोदस्योः (*rodasyoḥ*)—you who pervade all of heaven and earth
- नृन् (*nṛn*)—us who are the makers (us who offer hymns)
- सुक्षितिं (*sukṣitiṃ*)—endowed with excellent houses and the like
- ता (*tā*)—the impressions of sin from other births
- तरेम (*tarema*)—may we face all those causes of sorrow and be freed from sorrow

O Agni, of favourable radiance and divine nature, you who pervade all of heaven and earth, facing the gods, recite and offer our hymn. Unite us, who are the makers of praises, with welfare that is endowed with excellent houses and the like and is imperishable. May we overcome our enemies, our sins and the painful fruits of sin. O Agni, being joined with your protection, may we face all those causes of sorrow and be freed from sorrow.

Divine Agni, reverenced as a friend, you are abiding in heaven and earth, communicate our praise to the gods: conduct the offerer of adoration to domestic felicity ; and may we overcome our adversaries, our iniquities, our difficulties : may we overcome those (sins of a prior existence) may we overcome them by your protection.

O Agni, that sacrificer क्षेषत् (*kṣeṣat*), dwells, abides; the meaning is that he would live a long time. What kind of sacrificer? ऋतपा (*ṛtapā*), the protector of ṛta, the sacrifice, and ऋतेजा (*ṛtejā*), born for the sake of the sacrifice. And उषित्वा (*uṣitvā*) ⟨NOTE:216⟩, your devotee (देवयुः (*devayuḥ*)), desiring the gods for himself, that sacrificer obtains उरु (*uru*), the vast, ज्योतिः (*jyotiḥ*), the light called the sun. O shining god Agni, the mortal, the man, the sacrificer, whom you, together with Mitra and Varuṇa (the nominative stands in the sense of the instrumental), being pleased together with them (सजोषाः (*sajoṣāḥ*)), protect (पासि (*pāsi*)) from sin (अंहः (*aṃhaḥ*)) with the weapon (त्यजसा (*tyajasā*)), the means of casting away: that sacrificer is what is connected with the earlier part.
notes: ರಾಕ್ಷಸಾದೇಃ ಸ್ವಭೂತಾ ದದಾತೀತಿ ಶೇಷಃ not clear

en: - ऋतेजाः (*ṛtejāḥ*)—born for the sake of the sacrifice itself
- देवयुः (*devayuḥ*)—the same sacrificer who desired worship
- ज्योतिः (*jyotiḥ*)—the light in the form of the sun

O Agni, of divine nature, you, together with Mitra and Varuṇa and endowed with a sharp weapon, protect a sacrificer from sin; such a sacrificer, a protector of the sacrifice and born for the sake of the sacrifice itself, attains an excellent life. The same sacrificer, who desired your worship, attains an extremely vast ⟨NOTE:217⟩ light.
notes: ಯಶ್ಚ ಮರಣರಹಿತೋರ್ನಿರ್ದಿವಾಹ್ನಿ ನೃನ್ನೇತ್ಯನ್ ದೇವಾನವಿರ್ಭಿಃ ಸಂಯೋಜಯತಿ: the machine-read Sanskrit is damaged and the sense of the alternative cannot be construed

en: The offerer of sacrifice, born for religious rites, who lives devoted Agni, to you obtains abundant light, and is a man whom you, sympathizing in satisfaction with Mitra and Varuna, protect by your shield from iniquity.

The sacrificer who gives oblations to Agni who is ऋधद्वाराय (*ṛdhadvārāya*), whose choice wealth (वारं (*vāraṃ*)) is abundant, that sacrificer ईजे (*īje*), has sacrificed with यज्ञेभिः (*yajñebhiḥ*), all sacrifices; that is, he becomes one who has performed them. Likewise, through the works called शमीभिः (*śamībhiḥ*), such as the Kṛcchra and Cāndrāyaṇa, he शशमे (*śaśame*), becomes tranquil; the meaning is that through the sacrifice to Agni he obtains every fruit. And further, अजुष्टिः (*ajuṣṭiḥ*), the non-attainment of sons who are renowned (यशसां (*yaśasāṃ*)), does not at all reach that sacrificer; he is certainly one who has sons. Likewise, sin (अंहः (*aṃhaḥ*)) does not reach that mortal, a man; and arrogance, a cause of harm, and ostentation do not reach him.
- यधद्वाराय (*yadhadvārāya*)—endowed with the desired abundance of wealth
- ईजे (*īje*)—is just as one who has performed the sacrifice
