- शमीभिः (*śamībhiḥ*)—joined with all works such as the Kṛcchra and Cāndrāyaṇa
- यशसां (*yaśasāṃ*)—of sons and the like that are causes of fame
- न एव नशते (*na eva naśate*)—does not reach at all
- प्रदृप्तिः (*pradṛptiḥ*)—arrogance that is a cause of harm
The sacrificer who, in the name of Agni, endowed with the desired abundance of wealth, offers an oblation attains the fruit of having performed all the sacrificial rites, and tranquility of mind.
For him there is no lack of sons and the like, who are causes of fame. No kind of sin, nor arrogance that is a cause of harm, approaches that sacrificer.

He who has presented (oblations) to Agni, the possessor of desired (wealth), sacrifices with (all) sacrifices, and is sanctified by (all) holy acts : him, the want of excellent (posterity) does not afflict, nor does sin or pride affect such a mortal.

सूरो न (*sūro na*), like the sun, of which Agni the sight (दृशतिः (*dṛśatiḥ*), appearance) is अरेपाः (*arepāḥ*), free from sin. O Agni, of you who blaze, whose धीः (*dhīḥ*), the supporting flame, becoming terrible (भीमा (*bhīmā*)), goes all round (एति (*eti*)). This Agni, हेषस्वतः (*heṣasvataḥ*), those that are endowed with sound, शुरुधः (*śurudhaḥ*), like the cows that stop grief (शुचः (*śucaḥ*)), of अक्तोः (*aktoḥ*), the night: अक्तुरिति (*akturiti*) is a name for night, and by it a rākṣasa or the like that moves about there is meant; "he gives his own to the rākṣasa and the others" is what is to be supplied ⟨NOTE:218⟩. This is the dwelling (वसतिः (*vasatiḥ*)), the abode of all, वनेजाः (*vanejāḥ*), born in the forest; कुत्रा चित् (*kutrā cit*), in some place only, on a mountain peak and the like, he is रण्वः (*raṇvaḥ*), delightful.
notes: ಋಕ್ಸಂಖ್ಯೆ—೨ printed; the Anuvāda and the bhāṣya say eight Ṛks

en: - सूरो न (*sūro na*)—(O Agni) like the radiance of the sun

O Agni, whose manifestation, like the radiance of the sun, is free from fault, whose shining flame goes terribly all round in the night like bulls that roam about bellowing, that form of yours, which is the abode of all and is born in the forest, is delightful in all regions.

When the fearful flames of you, whose appearance is (as) faultless as (that of) the sun, spread on every side as (if they were) the lowing heifers of the night, then this Agni, the asylum of all, generated in the woods, is everywhere beautiful.
The path of going (एम (*ema*)) of this Agni is sharp (तिग्मं (*tigmaṃ*)), because it cannot be touched. His form (वर्पः (*varpaḥ*)) is great and abundant. भसत् (*bhasat*) means that he shines.

What kind of Agni is he? Like a horse (अश्वो न (*aśvo na*)), champing grass and the like with its mouth. Likewise like an axe: as an axe plunges its own edge into wood, so he casts his own tongue, that is, his flame, spreading it into trees and shrubs, burning the wood. Like a goldsmith (द्रविर्न (*dravirna*)), the one who causes to melt: as he melts gold and the like, so Agni melts the whole forest. The meaning is that he reduces what has form to ashes.
- परशुर्न (*paraśurna*)—as the edge of an axe enters wood
- विजेहमानः (*vijehamānaḥ*)—spreading in trees, shrubs and the like
- द्रविर्न (*dravirna*)—as a goldsmith melts gold and the like

The path of going of this Agni is sharp and his form is abundant; he is radiant like a horse champing grass with its mouth. As the edge of an axe enters timber, so the flame of Agni spreads in trees, shrubs and the like, burning trees and the rest; and as a goldsmith melts gold and the like, so Agni too burns and melts everything.
Sharp is his path, and his vast body shines like a horse champing fodder with his mouth, darting forth his tongue like a hatchet and burning timber to ashes like a goldsmith who fuses (metal).

That same Agni, like an archer (अस्ता इव (*astā iva*)) who shoots an arrow or the like, directs (प्रति धात् (*prati dhāt*)) his own flame: as an archer fits the arrow towards the target, so he fits his flame; this is the meaning. Having directed it, and about to hurl the flame (असिष्यन् (*asiṣyan*)), he sharpens his own radiance (शिशीत (*śiśīta*) is explained as: he sharpens, makes keen). An example is given: like the edge of iron (अयसो न धारां (*ayaso na dhārāṃ*)), as one who wishes to hurl an iron axe or the like sharpens its edge. Having sharpened it, he is of variegated motion (चित्रध्रजतिः (*citradhrajatiḥ*)), and he approaches at night (अक्तोः (*aktoḥ*) is explained as of the night), like a bird (वेर्न (*verna*)) sitting in trees, with feet able to fall lightly (रघुपत्मजंहा (*raghupatmajaṃhā*)). The Agni who is such, he: this is to be connected with what precedes.
- रघुपत्नजंहाः (*raghupatnajaṃhāḥ*)—having light feet fit for moving swiftly
- अस्ता इव (*astā iva*)—as an archer swiftly looses his arrow
- प्रति धात् (*prati dhāt*)—spreads his flame fiercely
- आयसः (*āyasaḥ*)—of a weapon made of steel
- धारां न (*dhārāṃ na*)—as a warrior rubs the edge and makes it sharp
- असिष्यन् (*asiṣyan*)—with the intention of spreading his flame

The Agni who is of variegated motion, who moves about in the night, and who, like a bird hiding in a tree, has light feet fit for moving swiftly, that same Agni fiercely spreads his flame, as an archer swiftly looses his arrow towards the target. As a warrior rubs the edge of a weapon made of steel and makes it sharp, so, with the intention of spreading his flame, he makes his radiance sharp.
He casts (afar his flames) as an archer (his arrows), and sharpens when about to dart his radiance, as (a warrior whets) the edge of his iron
(weapons). he who, variously moving, passes through the night, like the light-falling foot of a bird perched upon a trec.

That same Agni, like the praiseworthy sun (रेभो न (*rebho na*)), covers himself (प्रति वस्ते (*prati vaste*)) with his shining flames (उस्राः (*usrāḥ*)). Likewise, as one whose light is favourable to all (मित्रमहाः (*mitramahāḥ*)), he makes a loud sound (रारपीति (*rārapīti*)) with his lustre. This Agni, who by night is bright (अरुषः (*aruṣaḥ*), shining), as by day, impels men each to his own work; the second यः (*yaḥ*) is a complement. Likewise, being immortal, of deathless nature, bright or free from anger, the Agni who by day, with shining lustre, sends forth his own rays: this is connected with what precedes. Or else: this Agni is bright by night, and the one who is free from death ... ⟨NOTE:219⟩. The repetition in यो दिवा नृन् (*yo divā nṛn*) is for emphasis.
notes: ಅಸ್ತುಪಮಾರ್ಥಸ್ಯ printed; the reading of the first word is doubtful

en: - रेभो न (*rebho na*)—like the praiseworthy sun
- नृन् (*nṛn*)—men and others (he impels to their respective works)
- अमूर्त्यः (*amūrtyaḥ*)—free from the nature of death

As the praiseworthy sun makes his own rays his covering, so the Agni of the great qualities described before makes his own flames his covering. Having a favourable light, he makes a loud sound with his radiance. That same Agni, being luminous throughout the night, impels men and others by day to their respective works. That same Agni, free from the nature of death and of attractive brilliance, spreads his rays with his shining radiance.

Like the adorable sun, he clothes himself with brilliant (rays) : diffusing friendly light, he crackles with (his flame) : (he it is) who is luminous by night, and who lights men (to their work) by day ; who is immortal and radiant ; who lights men by day.

Of whom, like the shining sun (दिवो न (*divo na*)), who makes rays (विधतः (*vidhataḥ*)), a loud sound (नवीनोत् (*navīnot*)) arose, of that Agni. He explains this: the showerer of desires (वृषा (*vṛṣā*)), the shining one (रुक्षः (*rukṣaḥ*)), that Agni made a loud sound among the plants (ओषधीषु (*oṣadhīṣu*)) while they were being burnt. And he who, like a moving, as it were blazing, lustre (घृणा न (*ghṛṇā na*)), with his going radiance (ध्रजसा (*dhrajasā*)), flying (पत्मना (*patmanā*)) hither and thither, goes about, that Agni, subduing our enemies (दं (*daṃ*)), fills heaven and earth (रोदसी (*rodasī*)), who are well provided with husbands or protectors (सुपत्नि (*supatni*)), with wealth (वसुना (*vasunā*)).
- दिवो न (*divo na*)—like the shining sun
- रुक्षः (*rukṣaḥ*)—and the shining one, that same Agni
- ओषधीषु (*oṣadhīṣu*)—among plants and the like that are being burnt
- फृणा न (*phṛṇā na*)—like a lustre of movement
- ध्रजसा (*dhrajasā*)—and like a lustre of going
- पत्नना (*patnanā*)—in the manner of moving from one place to another
- वसुना (*vasunā*)—with wealth in the form of radiance

The Agni who spreads his rays like the shining sun, and of whom a sound arose, the showerer of desires, the shining one, that same Agni made a loud sound among plants and the like that were being burnt. The Agni who, like a lustre of movement, moves from one place to another, destroys our enemies, and fills heaven and earth, the excellent protectors, with wealth in the form of radiance.

Of whom a sound is heard when scattering his rays like (that of) the sun : the brilliant showerer (of benefits) clamours among the (burning) plants; he who, moving not with a shifting variable motion, but humbling (our foes), fills the well-wedded earth and heaven with wealth.

The Agni who goes with धायोभिर्वा (*dhāyobhirvā*), that is, with bearing horses as it were, with युज्येभिः (*yujyebhiḥ*), those that are yoked of themselves, with अर्कैः (*arkaiḥ*), worshipful flames. That Agni, like lightning, with his own (स्वेभिः (*svebhiḥ*)) शुष्मैः (*śuṣmaiḥ*), drying radiances, shines (दविद्योत् (*davidyot*) means he shines). And he who, like the strength (शर्धो वा (*śardho vā*)) of the Maruts, the gods so named, makes thin (ततक्ष (*tatakṣa*)), that is, makes everything sharp, which means that he dries it up. This same Agni, like the sun shining widely, brilliant (त्वेषः (*tveṣaḥ*)), making speed (रभसानः (*rabhasānaḥ*)), shines (अद्यात् (*adyāt*) means he shines forth).
- युज्येभिः (*yujyebhiḥ*)—fit to be yoked to a chariot
- धायोभिर्वा (*dhāyobhirvā*)—and bearing a burden, like horses
- अर्क्यैः (*arkyaiḥ*)—he who is endowed with worshipful rays
- दविद्योत् (*davidyot*)—he who shines, such a one, (and)
- शतक्ष (*śatakṣa*)—who makes sharp (who burns everything), that same Agni

The Agni who, like horses fit to be yoked to a chariot and bearing the burden, is endowed with worshipful rays, who like lightning shines with his own radiances, and who, like the host of the Maruts, burns everything, that same Agni, like the shining sun, brilliant and swift-moving, shines forth.

He who (goes) with sacred (rays), as if with self-harnessed, well-governed (steeds), who shines like lightning with his own scorching (flames), who impairs the vigour of Maruts, he glows radiant and rapid as the wide-shining sun.

O Hotṛ, invoked by the gods, O son of strength (सहसः सूनो (*sahasaḥ sūno*)), Agni: in the manner in which, at the sacrifice (देवताता (*devatātā*), which is a name for sacrifice) of Manu, that is, of the sacrificer Prajāpati, you worship the gods with sacrifices (यज्ञेभिः (*yajñebhiḥ*)), that is, with the oblations that are the sacrificer's means, so, O Agni, today, at this sacrifice of ours, desiring (उशन् (*uśan*)) Indra and the others who are like you, you quickly (समना (*samanā*)) worship (यक्षि (*yakṣi*)) the gods who desire to be worshipped (उशतः (*uśataḥ*)). Or else: a sacrifice in which the gods are regarded as equal is called समनो (*samano*); it is to be construed as "in that".
- सहसः सूनो (*sahasaḥ sūno*)—O Agni, son of strength
- यज्ञेभिः (*yajñebhiḥ*)—with oblations, the means of sacrifice
- समानान् (*samānān*)—Indra and the others, worshipful like you

O Agni, in the form of the Hotṛ, son of strength: in the manner in which you worshipped the gods with oblations, the means of sacrifice, at the sacrifice of Manu, the sacrificer, in the same manner, O Agni,
at this sacrifice of ours, desiring to worship Indra and the others who are worshipful like you, worship quickly those same gods who desire the sacrifice.

Son of strength, invoker (of the gods), in like manner as at the worship of the gods by Manu you offered worship with sacrifices, so now, Agni, with willing mind, worship for us the assenting deities, regarding them as youʳ equals.

That Agni, like the illuminator of the day (वस्तोः (*vastoḥ*) is explained as by day), the sun, specially shining (विभावा (*vibhāvā*)), to be known or obtained by all (वेद्यः (*vedyaḥ*)), may grant us (धात् (*dhāt*) means let him give, let him bestow) adorable, praiseworthy food (वंदारु (*vaṃdāru*)). विश्वायुः (*viśvāyuḥ*) is the food of all, or the cause of life for all; अमृतः (*amṛtaḥ*) is free from death; अतिथिः (*atithiḥ*) is the constant goer for the carrying of oblations; जातवेदाः (*jātavedāḥ*) is the knower of all that is born, or one whose wealth is born. The Agni who, such as he is, among mortals, that is, among the sacrificers, wakes at dawn for the oblation of the Agnihotra, he: this is connected with what precedes.
- विश्वायुः (*viśvāyuḥ*)—the cause of life for all
- अतिथिः (*atithiḥ*)—in the form of a guest
- उषर्बुद्भूत् (*uṣarbudbhūt*)—who wakes at dawn (for the Agnihotra), such a one

May that same Agni, who shines like the sun that shines by day, who is known by all, the support of life for all, free from death, in the form of a guest, in the form of Jātavedas, and who wakes at dawn among men for the Agnihotra, provide us with praiseworthy food.

May that Agni, who, like the illuminator of the day, is resplendent and cognizable (by all), grant us commendable food; he who is the life of all, immortal. who knows all that exists, who is our guest, waking amongst men at dawn.

The word न (*na*) is in the sense of "now". And it has been said: अस्तुपमार्थस्य संप्रत्यर्थे प्रयोगः (*astupamārthasya saṃpratyarthe prayogaḥ*) (Ni. 7-31) **GLOSS** ⟨NOTE:221⟩. The praisers (द्यावः (*dyāvaḥ*)), now, praise (पनयंति (*panayaṃti*)) the great deed (अभ्वं (*abhvaṃ*)) of which Agni; that Agni, like the sun, being of white colour (शुक्रः (*śukraḥ*)), covers himself (वस्ते (*vaste*)) with radiances (भासांसि (*bhāsāṃsi*)). And he who is ageless (अजरः (*ajaraḥ*)), the purifier (पावकः (*pāvakaḥ*)) of all, Agni, pervades everything with his light (विनोति (*vinoti*)); this same Agni breaks (शिश्नथत् (*śiśnathat*) means he injures) the ancient cities (पूर्व्याणि (*pūrvyāṇi*)) even of the pervading rākṣasa and the like.
notes: ಯಹು printed; ಯಹ್ವ intended?

en: - वस्त्रे (*vastre*)—he puts on as a cover
- पावकः (*pāvakaḥ*)—and the purifier, that same Agni
- वि इनोति (*vi inoti*)—pervades everything with his light
- अश्वस्य चित् (*aśvasya cit*)—even though spread out in many places

The Agni whose great deed the praisers now praise, like the sun, having a bright colour, spreads his radiances everywhere (covers himself with them). The Agni who is ageless and the purifier pervades everything everywhere with his light. Even though the cities of the Asuras are spread out and scattered in many places, he destroys them completely.

Whose great deeds his worshippers now celebrate, who is clothed with light, radiant as the sun, exempt from decay. the purifier, he illumes (all things), aud destroys the ancient cities of the dispersed (evil beings).

O son of strength (सूनो (*sūno*)); or, from the root षू (*ṣū*) in the sense of impelling, O Agni, impeller of all. You are to be addressed with praise, you are worthy of praise (वदनीयः (*vadanīyaḥ*)). The latter foot is in the indirect (third-person) form. Agni, who sits on the oblations that are his own proper seats, sitting down to receive the oblation, makes for the sacrificers, by birth, that is, by his own nature, अज्म (*ajma*), which is a name for house, a house and food. O giver (ऊर्जसन (*ūrjasana*)) of strengthening food, Agni, such as you are, give ऊर्जं (*ūrjaṃ*), food, to us. Likewise, like a king (राजीव (*rājīva*)), conquer (जेः (*jeḥ*)) our enemies. For all this, dwell (क्षेषि (*kṣeṣi*)) in the midst of our fire-house, which is free from hindering rākṣasas and the like (अवृके (*avṛke*)).
- पद्मा असि (*padmā asi*)—you are worthy of homage
- अवृके (*avṛke*)—of our sacrificial house, free from the harm of rākṣasas and the like

O Agni, son of strength, you are worthy of homage. Agni, who abides among the oblations, provides the sacrificer, without being asked, with a house and with food. O Agni, giver of food, you the renowned, supply us with food, and be victorious like a lord. Dwell in the middle of our sacrificial house, which is free from rākṣasas and the like.
Son of strength, you are to be praised: Agni, sitting upon the (sacrificial) viands, has given (to his worshippers), from their birth, habitat-
ion and food ; giver of strength, bestow strength upon us ; triumph like a prince, so that you may abide in our unassailed (dwelling).

The Agni who sharpens (नितिक्ति (*nitikti*) means he makes keen) his own light, which wards off darkness (वारणं (*vāraṇaṃ*)), and who eats (अत्ति (*atti*)) the food, the oblation given by the sacrificers. And so it is heard: अन्नादोऽवा एषोऽन्नपतियर्दग्निरिति (*annādo 'vā eṣo 'nnapatiyardagniriti*) **GLOSS**. That Agni, like the wind (वायुर्न (*vāyurna*)), is राष्ट्री (*rāṣṭrī*), a name for the lord; राष्ट्रं (*rāṣṭraṃ*) is a kingdom, and he possesses it. As the wind rules everything by its own greatness, so he; the meaning is that he is lord of all. Being such, he goes beyond (अत्येति (*atyeti*)) the nights (अक्तून् (*aktūn*)), that is, he overcomes the darkness found in them. And by your grace may we destroy (तुर्याम (*turyāma*)) the man who is a non-giver  of the oblations being offered to you. Or else: ⟨NOTE:222⟩, may we destroy the man among us who is hostile. And you, like a swift horse (अत्यो न (*atyo na*)), a well-bred horse, be the slayer of the harming enemies who rush upon you face to face (पततः (*patataḥ*)), reckoning them up (परिह्रुत् (*parihrut*)).
notes: ಕೈ. ಸಂ. printed; ತೈ. ಸಂ. intended? reference 1-5-1 1 as printed

en: - वारणं (*vāraṇaṃ*)—the light that wards off darkness
- अन्नं (*annaṃ*)—the food in the form of oblation
- अत्येति (*atyeti*)—crosses (puts an end to the darkness of the night)
- तुर्याम (*turyāma*)—(may we also cross that darkness)
- ते (*te*)—to you, that which is to be offered
- अरातीः (*arātīḥ*)—who does not give (may we destroy him also), (you also)
- अत्यो न (*atyo na*)—like a swift horse
- पततः (*patataḥ*)—who fall upon us face to face, the enemies

The Agni who makes keen his light that wards off darkness, and who eats the food in the form of oblation, that Agni, like the wind, as lord of all, crosses the nights, that is, puts an end to the darkness of the night. May we also cross that darkness. O Agni, may we destroy also the man who does not give the oblations that are to be offered to you. You also, like a swift horse, rush upon and destroy the harming enemies who fall upon us face to face.

He who whets his (gloom)-dispersing (radiance), who eats the (offered) oblation, a sovereign like Vayu, overcomes the nights; may we prevail (over him) who is not a donor of the oblations that are due, (Agni) to you and (swift) as a horse, be the destroyer of the foes assailing (us).

O Agni, you overspread (ततंथ (*tataṃtha*), you cover specially) heaven and earth (रोदसी (*rodasī*)) with radiance (भासा (*bhāsā*)). An example is given: like the sun (सूर्यो न (*sūryo na*)) with its splendid (भानुमद्भिः (*bhānumadbhiḥ*)), worshipful (अर्कैः (*arkaiḥ*)) rays: as the sun spreads, so you. The latter half of the verse is in the indirect form. पत्नन् (*patnan*) is the path, that on which one goes; on it, like the Auśija: the उशिजः (*uśijaḥ*) are the praisers, and the sun, connected with them through being praised, is the Auśija. Like him, going (दीयन् (*dīyan*)), joined (अक्तः (*aktaḥ*)) with radiance (शोचिषा (*śociṣā*)), and therefore wonderful (चित्रः (*citraḥ*), worthy to be seen), Agni leads round (परि णयत् (*pari ṇayat*) means he leads away on every side) the darknesses (तमांसि (*tamāṃsi*)) of the night; the meaning is that he turns them back from every quarter.
- सूर्यो न (*sūryo na*)—as the sun spreads everywhere
- वि आ ततंथ (*vi ā tataṃtha*)—you have pervaded and spread
- तमांसि (*tamāṃsi*)—the black darkness of the night

O Agni, as the sun spreads everywhere with radiant and worshipful rays, so you have pervaded and spread heaven and earth with your splendour. Moving on his path like the sun, joined with his own radiance and attractive, Agni drives far away the black darkness of the night.
You overspread, Agni, heaven and earth with radiance, like the sun with his lustrous rays; the wonderful Agni disperses the glooms like the adorned (sun) moving on his path, imbued with light.

O Agni, most delightful, most praiseworthy (मंद्रतमं (*maṃdratamaṃ*)), we choose you, we serve you, because you are endowed with worshipful flames (शोकैः (*śokaiḥ*)), that is, radiances (अर्कशोकैः (*arkaśokaiḥ*)); that is, we serve you with praises that are the means of kindling you. Therefore hear (श्रोषि (*śroṣi*) means listen) our great (महि (*mahi*)) praise. O Agni, the priests, the best leaders (नृतमाः (*nṛtamāḥ*)) of the praises, with strength (शवसा (*śavasā*)) satisfy (पृणंति (*pṛṇaṃti*) means they please) you, the goer (वायुं (*vāyuṃ*)); or else, you who are endowed with strength like Vāyu, like Indra, whose self is the divinity, with wealth (राधसा (*rādhasā*)) in the form of oblation.
- नृतमाः (*nṛtamāḥ*)—the priests, the best among men
- शवसा वायुं (*śavasā vāyuṃ*)—like the strong Vāyu
- देवता त्वा (*devatā tvā*)—you, whose self is the divinity
- राधसा (*rādhasā*)—with food in the form of oblation

O Agni, we worship you, the most praiseworthy, with worshipful praises. Hear our great praise. The priests, the best among men, satisfy you, whose self is the divinity, like the strong Vāyu and like Indra, with food in the form of oblation.

We celebrate you, who are most adorable, with sacred praises : hear Agni, our laudation: the leaders (of rites) earnestly honour you with offerings, you who are divine like Indra, and like Vayu in strength,

O Agni, lead us quickly (नु (*nu*)), by paths free from thieves (अवृकेभिः (*avṛkebhiḥ*); the वृकाः (*vṛkāḥ*) are thieves), to riches (रायः (*rāyaḥ*) means wealth), with well-being (स्वस्ति (*svasti*) means with safety); वेषि (*veṣi*) means cause to go, cause to reach. Take us across from sin (अंहः (*aṃhaḥ*)) by the paths described. Those delights (सुम्मानि (*summāni*), pleasures) that are to be given by you to the wise (सूरिभ्यः (*sūribhyaḥ*), the praisers), those give (रासि (*rāsi*) means give) to me who praise (गृणते (*gṛṇate*)). And we, living a hundred winters (शतहिमाः (*śatahimāḥ*), a hundred years), with good sons (सुवीराः (*suvīrāḥ*): the वीराः (*vīrāḥ*) are sons and the like, born of vigour), endowed with excellent sons, grandsons and the like, may rejoice (मदेम (*madema*) means may we be glad).
- सूरिभ्यः (*sūribhyaḥ*)—which are fit to be given to your praisers
- सुवीराः (*suvīrāḥ*)—with excellent sons and the like

O Agni, lead us quickly and with safety by paths free from thieves into the presence of wealth. Make us free from sin. Give to me, who now praise you, the wealth, renowned and fit to be given to your praisers. May we rejoice for a hundred years, endowed with excellent sons and the like.

Quickly conduct us, Agni, by unmolested paths to riches and prosperity : (convey us) beyond sin : those delights which you give to ,your adorers (extend) to him who (now) glorifies you, and may we, living for a hundred winters, and blessed with excellent posterity, be happy.

"O Agni, *vaḥ*": the plural stands by interchange of number, for "you". "I invoke you with *matis*, that is, with hymns worthy of reflection." What kind of Agni? The son (*sūnu*) of *sahas*, of strength: for Agni is born when it is churned with strength. *Yuvan* is "ever young", or else one who mixes (the fruit). *Adroghavāc* is one in whom a praiseworthy speech in the form of praise, free from injury, is employed. *Yaviṣṭha* is exceedingly young. *Pracetāḥ* is of excellent knowledge. *Puruvāra* is to be chosen and resorted to by many (*puru*), and *adhruk* is one who does not injure the sacrificers. Such an Agni, who sends forth (*invati*, impels) all the riches (*dravina*) that are choiceworthy, worthy of being shared and praiseworthy (*viśvavāra*), that is, gives them to the singers: "you, that Agni, I invoke" is the connection with what precedes.
- अध्रुक् (*adhruk*)—one who does no harm to the sacrificers and others
- सहसः सूनुं (*sahasaḥ sūnuṃ*)—the son of strength

O Agni, you who are of excellent knowledge, honoured by many, and do no harm to the sacrificers and others, you who give to the sacrificers the riches wished for by all and praiseworthy: you, the son of strength, ever young, and worthy of praising speech, we call, praying, with venerable hymns.
I invoke you, Agni, the son of strenth, the irreproachable. the very young ; vou who are wise, the sought of many, the merciful. who bestow trcasures acceptalbe to all.

वः (*vaḥ*)—त्वां (*tvāṃ*), you. Here a plural is used in place of the singular. सर्वे विधयच्छंदसि विकल्प्यंते (*sarve vidhayacchaṃdasi vikalpyaṃte*) means that in verses bound by metre, or in Vedic sentences, the rules of case, number, gender and so on need not be according to grammar or according to literary or linguistic usage; that is, they may or may not accord with the rules of grammar and the like. The idea is that usages of this kind are not at all contrary to rule. In the Ṛgveda the interchange of case and number for the convenience of the metre is especially frequent. In the present Ṛk, in place of the word त्वां (*tvāṃ*), the accusative singular of the word *yuṣmad*, the plural of the same case, the word वः (*vaḥ*), is used.

सूनुं सहसः (*sūnuṃ sahasaḥ*)—the son of strength. In the sacrifice, Agni is churned out and produced, as curd is churned, in pieces of wood called *araṇi*. Because in this churning much strength or force has to be used, it is a special custom in the Ṛgveda to call Agni one produced by the application of strength, or the son of strength. The words सहसः सूनु (*sahasaḥ sūnu*), सहसः पुत्र (*sahasaḥ putra*), सहसः यहु (*sahasaḥ yahu*) and so on indicate this same meaning.⟨NOTE:223⟩

युवानं यविष्ठं (*yuvānaṃ yaviṣṭhaṃ*)—it is customary to call Agni youthful. For in human beings and other creatures the stage called youth (the time marked by exceeding capacity) exists only in a fixed period. This stage lies between childhood and old age. Since this stage is limited in time, no creature can remain always in youth; its strength must gradually decrease and it must reach old age. But the case of Agni is not so. When Agni is churned only a small spark is produced, and so it is then called an infant (शिशुं जातन बिभ्रति (*śiśuṃ jātana bibhrati*)); that is, that stage of Agni is called the stage of infancy. After that they place it in the fire-pit and make it blaze with materials such as fuel sticks and ghee. Then Agni is said to be in the stage of youth. For as long as, that is, for as much time as, they put in wood and the like, so long Agni remains blazing, shining, in the stage of youth. There is no limit of time to this state of Agni. For as long as one wishes, by putting in wood and the like, Agni may be kept bright (in the stage of youth). It is for this very reason that Agni is praised as युवा (*yuvā*) and यविष्ठ (*yaviṣṭha*), young and exceedingly young.
अद्रोघवाचं (*adroghavācaṃ*)—without words that injure or revile; that is, the meaning is praiseworthy speech in the form of praise.

पुरुवारः (*puruvāraḥ*)—पुरुभिर्बहुभिः वरणीयः (*purubhirbahubhiḥ varaṇīyaḥ*): one wished for by many, or by the many sacrificers who perform the sacrifice. Since a sacrifice cannot be performed without Agni, all who perform sacrifices desire Agni. The use of this word occurs also with regard to many deities such as Agni and Indra. The meaning and use of the word विश्ववाराणि (*viśvavārāṇi*) are just like those of the word पुरुवार (*puruvāra*). In the present Ṛk the meaning is explained as riches needed by everyone.

अध्रुक् (*adhruk*)—अद्रोग्ना यजमानानां (*adrognā yajamānānāṃ*): this word is used as an epithet of Agni in the sense of one who does no injury or harm to the sacrificers and others who perform the sacrifice.
notes: ಅ. ೪-೬ printed; abbreviation ಅ. not in list

en: "O Agni of many flames (*puruṇīka*), Hotṛ, caller of the gods, in you (*tve*), at night (*doṣā*) and by day (*vastoḥ*), the sacrificers worthy of sacrifice (*yajñiyāsaḥ*) send forth riches (*vasūni*) in the form of oblations", that is, they offer them, directing them towards you. "All (*viśvā*) beings (*bhuvanāni*), as on the earth (*kṣāmā iva*), in whom, the purifier Agni, the gods have well placed good fortunes (*saubhagāni*), that is, riches." A Brāhmaṇa says: अग्नौ नामं वसु सं नृपधत । (*agnau nāmaṃ vasu saṃ nṛpadhata |*) (Kai. Saṃ. 1-5-1 1).⟨NOTE:224⟩ "In him, in you" is to be joined with what precedes.
notes: ಋಕ್ number not printed for this Ṛk; 6 by sequence

en: - होतः (*hotaḥ*)—one in the form of the Hotṛ, O Agni
- वसूनि (*vasūni*)—riches in the form of oblations
- क्षामेव (*kṣāmeva*)—as if established on the earth itself
- यस्मिन् पावके (*yasmin pāvake*)—in you the purifier
- सौभगानि (*saubhagāni*)—all riches of an auspicious nature
- सं दधिरे (*saṃ dadhire*)—the gods have established

O Agni of abundant flames, in the form of the Hotṛ, the sacrificers fit to perform sacrifice offer to you, by day and by night alike, riches in the form of oblations. As all beings are established on the earth itself, so in you, the purifier, the gods have established all auspicious riches.

Bright-blazing Agni, invoker of the gods, to you the adorahle deities have appropriated, by night and day, the riches (of the oblation): they have deposited in the purifier (Agni) all good things, as they have placed all beings upon earth.

"O Agni, you (*tvam*), *pradivaḥ*": this is a name meaning "ancient". You sit (*sīdaḥ*), that is, you abide, in the peoples of ancient times and in these peoples that are seen now; you exist as the inner self of all. So too, by your own action (*kratvā*), you have become the conveyer (*rathī*) of choiceworthy riches (*vāryāṇām*): the one who speeds them and brings them to the sacrificers. Therefore, O knowing (*cikitvaḥ*) Jātavedas, knower of the beings that are born,
O Agni, to the sacrificer who serves you (*vidhate*) you send variously (*vi noṣi*) riches, in such a way that it is continuous (*ānuṣak*, uninterrupted), that is, unceasing.
- आसु विक्षु (*āsu vikṣu*)—in these very peoples
- सीदः (*sīdaḥ*)—you abide in the form of Vaiśvānara
- रथीः अभवः (*rathīḥ abhavaḥ*)—you have become the conveyer
- जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—O Agni, in the form of Jātavedas
- विधते (*vidhate*)—to the sacrificer who worships you

O Agni, you abide in the form of Vaiśvānara in these very peoples of the ancient lineage. By your own action you have become the conveyer of the riches wished for by the sacrificers. Therefore, O wise Agni in the form of Jātavedas, provide everlasting riches to the sacrificer who worships you.
You abide from of old in these people, and by your deeds have been (to them) the conveyer of good things; thence, sage Jatavedas, you bestow continually wealth upon the sacrificer.

In the Pravargya, in the Abhiṣṭava, the triplet beginning यो नः सनुत्य (*yo naḥ sanutya*) is used. It is also given in the sūtra: यो नः सनुत्यो (*yo naḥ sanutyo*) and भवा नो अग्ने सुमना उपेताविति दृचाः (*bhavā no agne sumanā upetāviti dṛcāḥ*) (Ā. 4-6). "O Agni, the enemy who is *sanutyaḥ*": सनुतरित्यंतर्हितनाम (*sanutarityaṃtarhitanāma*), it is a name for "hidden". Being in a hidden place, he *abhidāsat*, that is, he harms and afflicts us; and he who, being *antaraḥ*, inside, near, *vanuṣyāt*, would injure us, O Mitramahas, O one brilliant in a way favourable to friends, or one who makes friends great, O Agni: that enemy of both kinds, O most heated (*tapiṣṭha*) Agni, you who are endowed with heat (*tapasvān*) through radiance (*tapasā*), burn (*tapa*) with your own flames, which are ageless, showering, causes of rain, and belong to you alone.
- तपस्वान् (*tapasvān*)—one who blazes, you who are such

O Agni, you who are favourable like a friend, who burn most fiercely, and who blaze with radiance: whichever enemy injures us staying in secrecy, and whichever injures us staying close by, burn those enemies of both kinds with your radiances, which are ageless and causes of rain.
You, protector of (your) friends, are most resplendent blazing with radiance consume; your own imperishable flames him who injures us abiding in secret, or when near to us designs us harm.

In the Pravargya sacrifice, this Ṛk यो नः सनुत्यः (*yo naḥ sanutyaḥ*) is to be recited as the second Ṛk in the Abhiṣṭava, as is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra भवा नो अग्ने सुमना उपेताविति द्वृचाः (*bhavā no agne sumanā upetāviti dvṛcāḥ*) (A. 4-6).⟨NOTE:225⟩
notes: block begins with fragment ಸಾಯುಧಃ ಸ್ತೋತ್ರಂ; earlier part of the bhāṣya missing?

en: "O son of *sahas*, of strength, O Agni: the sacrificer who serves (*dadāśat*) you with sacrifice (*yajñena*), that is, with a rite; who serves you with fuel (*samidhā*), the wood that is the means of kindling; who serves you with recited praises (*ukthaiḥ*), with *śastras*, and with *arkas*, hymns of praise; O immortal one (*amṛta*), Agni, free from the nature of death: that sacrificer, being among mortals (*martyeṣu*), among men, of excellent knowledge (*pracetāḥ*), shines forth (*vi bhāti*), that is, shines in a special way, with wealth (*rāyā*), with *dyumna*, which is shining, and with *śravas*, which is renowned food or fame."
- सहसः सूनो (*sahasaḥ sūno*)—O son of strength
- अमृत (*amṛta*)—O Agni, free from the nature of death
- अर्कॆभिः (*arkèbhiḥ*)—with praiseworthy hymns of praise, praises

O Agni, son of strength, free from the nature of death: the sacrificer who serves and worships you with sacrifice, with the means of kindling, with *śastra* mantras and with praiseworthy hymns of praise, that same
sacrificer shines exceedingly among men, as one of excellent knowledge, together with wealth and with shining food.
He who propitiates you, son of strength, with sacrifice, with fuel, with prayers, with praises, shines immortal amongst men, eminent in wisdom and possessed of splendid opulence and (abuudant) food.

notes: ಋಕ್ number not printed for this Ṛk; 2 by sequence

en: "O Agni, you, being sent (*iṣitaḥ*), that is, impelled, quickly (*tūyam*) do (*kṛdhi*) that." What is that? He says: "You who are powerful (*sahasvān*), strong, drive away (*bādhasva*), that is, destroy, those who contend (*spṛdhaḥ*), by strength (*sahasā*), by the force that is able to overcome others, or by radiance. You are anointed (*aktaḥ*), thoroughly sprinkled, with shining (*dyubhiḥ*) radiances. That which (*yat*) is praised (*śasyase*), that is, extolled, with words (*vacobhiḥ*), with sentences in the form of praise: that is, the hymn which the singers make with you in view, that thought (*manma*), worthy to be reflected on, worthy to be proclaimed (*ghoṣi*): accept (*juṣasva*), that is, be pleased with, the hymn of the singer (*jarituḥ*)."
- सहस्वान् (*sahasvān*)—you who are endowed with strength
- स्पृधः (*spṛdhaḥ*)—the enemies who fight with us
- वचोभिः (*vacobhiḥ*)—with words in the form of praise
- यत् शस्यसे (*yat śasyase*)—for whatever purpose you are praised
- तत् (*tat*)—for the accomplishment of that very purpose
- मन्म (*manma*)—that which is of the nature of meditation
- घोषि (*ghoṣi*)—and of the nature of proclamation

O Agni, you the renowned, as soon as you are prayed to by us, fulfil our wishes. You who are powerful, destroy with your powerful radiance the enemies who fight with us. You who are joined with shining radiances: for the accomplishment of the purpose for which you are praised with words in the form of praise, accept the hymn of the praiser, which is of the nature of meditation and of proclamation.

Accomplish quickly, Agni, that for with you are solicited : endowed with strength, oppose by strength our adversaries: be pleased, you are annointed with radiance, by the loud vocification of your worshipper, by whom you are adored with hymus.

For the offering "to Agni, for a wish, a cake on eight potsherds", the Ṛk beginning अग्नये कामाय पुरोडाशमष्टाकपालमित्यस्याश्यामेत्येषा याज्या (*agnaye kāmāya puroḍāśamaṣṭākapālamityasyāśyāmetyeṣā yājyā*) is the offering verse. It is also given in the sūtra: अश्वाम तं काममग्ने तवोतीति कामाय (*aśvāma taṃ kāmamagne tavotīti kāmāya*) (Ā. 2-10). "O Agni, may we obtain (*aśyāma*), that is, attain, that wish (*kāma*) by your (*tava*) protection (*ūtī*)." He explains that very wish: "O wealthy one (*rayivaḥ*), may we attain wealth (*rayim*) accompanied by good sons and the like (*suvīram*). So too, desiring food (*vājayantaḥ*) for ourselves, may we attain, directly (*abhi*), the food given by you. O ageless (*ajara*) Agni, may we attain your ageless, shining *dyumna*, that is, your fame."
- सुवीरं (*suvīraṃ*)—accompanied by excellent sons and the like

O Agni, by your protection may we obtain our desired object. O wealthy Agni, may we possess wealth accompanied by excellent sons and the like. May we, desiring food, enjoy at once the food given by you. O Agni, free from decay, may we too obtain your imperishable and shining fame.

ay we obtain through your protetion, Agni, that which we desire : giver of riches, may we obtain of you riches and descendants : desiring food, may we obtain food : may we obtain, imperihable Agni, impershable fame (through you).

अग्नये कामाय पुरोडाशमष्टाकपालं (*agnaye kāmāya puroḍāśamaṣṭākapālaṃ*)—when the offering of a cake is made addressed to Agni, this Ṛk अश्वामतं (*aśvāmataṃ*) is to be recited as the offering verse (*yājyā*); this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra अश्वाम तं काममग्ने तवोतीति कामाय (*aśvāma taṃ kāmamagne tavotīti kāmāya*) (Ā. 2-10).

⟨NOTE:227⟩ The praiser (*stotā*), desiring (*icchamānaḥ*) food (*avaḥ*) or protection, and joined with a newer (*navyasā*) sacrifice, goes forth (*pra jigāti*), that is, moves forward, towards (*acchā*) Agni, the son of strength (*sahasaḥ sūnum*), who is to be approached, or to be praised (*gātum*). What kind of Agni? One by whom the forest, the trees, has been cut, that is, burnt (*vṛścadvanam*); dark-pathed (*kṛṣṇayāmam*), that is, one whose way is black; white-hued (*ruśantam*); the Hotṛ, the sacrificer, with a beloved (*vītī*) sacrifice; the divine, one who exists in heaven.
notes: ವಿ ತೇ ನಿಷ್ಪಕ್ printed; ವಿ ತೇ ವಿಷ್ವಕ್ intended?

en: - वृश्चद्वनं (*vṛścadvanaṃ*)—one who burns the forest trees
- दिव्यं (*divyaṃ*)—born in the world of the gods
- सहसः सूनुं (*sahasaḥ sūnuṃ*)—the son of strength, Agni

The praiser who desires food, joined with a new sacrifice, approaches Agni, who burns the forest trees, has a black path, is shining, worships the gods with a radiant sacrifice, is born in the world of the gods, is worthy of praise and is the son of strength.

He who is desirous of food has recourse with a new sacrifice, approachable son of strenght, (Agni), to you, the consumer of forests, the dark-pathed, the bright-shining, the ministrant (to the gods) of (sacrificial) food, the divine;

notes: ಋಗ್ವೇ- printed; abbreviation not in list

en: That Agni is *śvitāna*, that is, white-shining, of white colour. *Tanyatu* is one who makes sound. *Rocanasthāḥ*: that in which the planets, stars and the like shine is *rocana*, the atmosphere; he stands there, joined with the ageless (*ajarebhiḥ*), exceedingly roaring (*nānadadbhiḥ*) Maruts, or with rays; *yaviṣṭha* is the most youthful. The purifying Agni, being exceedingly abundant (*purutanu*), goes along (*anuyāti*), that is, follows, devouring (*bharvan*) many (*purūṇi*), thick (*pṛthūni*) pieces of wood; "he exists thus, in this way": this is the connection with what precedes.
- रोचनस्थाः (*rocanasthāḥ*)—one who stays in the atmosphere, together with orbs of radiance
- नानदद्धिः (*nānadaddhiḥ*)—exceedingly noisy; one joined with rays
- पृथूनि (*pṛthūni*)—and thick, wood and the like

That Agni, who makes sound, stays in the atmosphere with orbs of radiance, is joined with ageless rays that make exceeding noise, is most youthful and purifying, and who, being exceedingly abundant, moves about devouring wood and the like of many kinds and thick: such an Agni is white-hued. (He is shining.)

(You who are) white-hued, vociferous, abiding in the firmament, (associated) with the imperishable, resounding (winds), the youngest (of the gods, Agni, who, purifying and most vast, proceeds, feeding upon numerous and substantial (forests).

When contact among the fires such as the Gārhapatya arises from some cause, an iṣṭi addressed to Agni, अग्नये विविचये (*agnaye vivicaye*), is to be performed as an expiation of that fault. Then this Ṛk वि ते निष्पक् (*vi te niṣpak*) is to be recited as the *anuvākyā* mantra in that iṣṭi; this is indicated in the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra (Ā. 3-13).⟨NOTE:229⟩
notes: ಯುವಸ್ವ ವಿಭಾಗಮಾಡಿಟ್ಟರು printed, with "(ಕೊಡು)" added at the end of the Bhāvārtha; the past plural does not fit an imperative

en: When the Gārhapatya and other fires come into contact with one another, an iṣṭi addressed to Agni Vivici is to be performed; in it this Ṛk, beginning वि त (*vi ta*), is the *anuvākyā* (Ā. 3-13). "O pure, or shining, Agni, your (*te*) flames (*bhāmāsaḥ*), driven by the wind (*vātajūtāsaḥ*), pure (*śucayaḥ*), move about (*vi caranti*) everywhere (*viṣvak*), that is, go in various ways. Those rays, *tuvimrakṣāsaḥ*, that is, burning much wood, divine (*divyāḥ*), existing in Agni who shines in heaven, *navagvāḥ*, of new motion, *vananti* the woods (*vanā*), that is, resort to them; the meaning is, they burn them. Doing what? Breaking (*rujantaḥ*) the woods with a daring (*dhṛṣatā*), overpowering radiance."
- नवग्वाः (*navagvāḥ*)—and of new form, these rays of yours

O Agni, the wholly pure: your radiances, driven by the wind and stainless, move about everywhere. Your rays, which burn much wood, are shining and of new form, and with radiances that overpower enemies they destroy the woods and burn them.
Pure Agni, your bright flames, fanned by the wind, spread wide in every direction, consuming abundant (fuel); divine, fresh-rising, they play upon the woods, enveloping them in lustre.

"O shining (*śuciṣmaḥ*) Agni, your (*te*) bright (*śukrāsaḥ*) radiances (*śucayaḥ*) which shear (*vapanti*), that is, make bald, the earth (*kṣām*), the ground": the meaning is that they burn the plants and trees, which stand in the place of hair. अग्निर्ह दाति रोमा पृथिव्याः (*agnirha dāti romā pṛthivyāḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-65-4) is another Vedic passage.⟨NOTE:230⟩**GLOSS** Those rays, like horses let loose (*viṣitāsaḥ*), that is, set free, go hither and thither: this is what is to be supplied.

Then, at that time, your (*te*) wandering (*bhramaḥ*) mass of flames, towards the raised place (*sānu*), the summit of a mountain and the like, above (*adhi*) the many-coloured (*pṛśneḥ*) earth, urging (*yātayamānaḥ*) forward its own tip, shines (*vi bhāti*) widely (*urviyā*), that is, much; it shines in a special way.
notes: abbreviation ವಾ. ಸಿಂ. printed

en: - क्षां (*kṣāṃ*)—the earth (the plants and the like)
- विषितासः (*viṣitāsaḥ*)—like horses that have thrown off their bridles (move about in all directions)
- पृश्नेः (*pṛśneḥ*)—of the earth of many forms

O Agni, endowed with light: your bright radiances, which cut the plants and the like on the earth, that is, burn them, those rays, like horses that have thrown off their bridles, move about in all directions. At this time your wandering masses of flames, resorting to the mountain slope region on the upper part of the earth of many forms, spread very widely and shine exceedingly.
Resplendent Agni, your bright rays, horses let loose (from the rein), shear the earth ; your (band of flame), mounting above the high-lands of the many-tinted (earth), blazes fiercely.

"And further, the flame (*jihvā*) of Agni the showerer (*vṛṣṇaḥ*) falls forth (*pra pāpatīti*) again and again, that is, it moves." The illustration: गोषुयुधो नाशनिः सृजाना (*goṣuyudho nāśaniḥ sṛjānā*). Indra, fighting for the cows when they were seized by the Asuras, is *goṣuyudh*; the thunderbolt (*vajra*) is like a thunderbolt (*aśani*) hurled by him. So too, as the binding (*prasiti*) of a man endowed with heroism is hard for others to bear, so the *kṣāti* of Agni, his flame, is impossible to bear. "Furthermore, *durvartu*, that which cannot be warded off by others, terrible (*bhīma*), fearful Agni burns (*dayate*) the woods": दयतिरत्र दहतिकर्मा (*dayatiratra dahatikarmā*).
- वृष्णः (*vṛṣṇaḥ*)—of Agni, the cause of rain
- गोषुयुधः (*goṣuyudhaḥ*)—of Indra, the protector of cattle
- प्र पापतीति (*pra pāpatīti*)—falls with exceeding speed (spreads)
- दुर्वर्तुः (*durvartuḥ*)—one with strength that none can check

The flame of Agni, the cause of rain, spreads with exceeding speed like the thunderbolt hurled by Indra, the protector of cattle. Like the blow of a hero, the flame of Agni is unbearable. Agni, who has strength that none can check and who is terrible, burns the forest trees.

The flame of the showerer, (Agni), repeatedly descends like the hurled thunderbolt of the rescuer of the cattle : like the prowess of a hero is the destroying (energy) of Agni: irresistible and fearful, he consumes the forests.

"O Agni, with radiance (*bhānunā*) you have spread (*tatantha*), that is, covered, the earthly (*pārthivāni*) *jrayāṃsi*": ज्रयतिर्गतिकर्मा (*jrayatirgatikarmā*), that is, places to be gone to, along with the daring (*dhṛṣatā*), overpowering ray of the great (*mahaḥ*) impeller (*todasya*). "You, such a one, drive away (*apa bādhasva*) all that causes fear (*bhayā*). So too, with strong (*sahobhiḥ*) powers or radiances, able to overcome, harming (*vanuṣyan*) those who contend (*spṛdhaḥ*), strike down (*ni jūrva*), that is, slay, the injuring (*vanuṣaḥ*) enemies": जूर्वतिर्हंतिकर्मा (*jūrvatirhaṃtikarmā*).
- ज्रयांसि (*jrayāṃsi*)—the regions to be gone to
- भया (*bhayā*)—all the sources of fear to us
- स्पृधः (*spṛdhaḥ*)—the enemies who fight with us

O Agni, you who are of great nature and an impeller: with your powerful radiances you have pervaded and covered all the regions of the earth to be gone to. Such a one, destroy all the sources of fear to us. Harming with powerful radiances the enemies who fight with us, conquer the enemies who injure us.
You overspread the accessible places of the earth with light by
the energy of your powerful, exciting (influence) : you disperse all perils
and, baffling (our) adversaries by your mighty (powers), destroy (our) foes.

In the Ukhāsaṃbharaṇa rites this verse is the yājyā offered to Agni, who is possessed of kṣatra (for a sacrificer of the warrior class). The sūtra says so (Ā. 4-1). Sāyaṇa explains: O wonderful one, who is to be piled (cāyanīya); O one of wonderful strength, or one whose wealth is to be piled; or O delightful Agni, the giver of joy: such as you are, grant wealth to us who praise you with delighting praises (the singular "to the one who praises" stands for the plural, a change of number). "Yuvasva" means "set apart". What kind of wealth? Wonderful and worthy of being piled; making one known, for by wealth a man becomes renowned; most wonderful, that is, astonishing in the highest degree; the supporter and producer of food (vayas); delightful; accompanied by many heroes, that is, by sons, grandsons and the like; great. The meaning is: give us such wealth.
- चित्रक्षत्र (*citrakṣatra*)—the one possessed of wonderful strength
- चंद्र (*caṃdra*)—the one of delightful nature, O Agni
- पुरुवीरं (*puruvīraṃ*)—that which is accompanied by heroic sons and the like

O attractive one, O one of wonderful strength, O delightful Agni: such a one as you, to all of us who praise you with praises that produce delight, set apart in portions and placed wealth that is attractive, that makes known our duty, that is astonishing, that gives food, that is accompanied by heroic sons and the like, and that is abundant. (Give it.)
notes: ಋ. ಸಂ. ೧-೧೬೪ ೫೧ printed without a hyphen before 51; abbreviation ಸ. printed, preceding references read ನಿ.

en: Wonderful Agni. of wonderful strength, bestower of delight, grant to us, and to him who praises you with gratifying (praises), most wonderful riches, conferring fame, supplying food, comprehending male descendants, delectable and infinite.

In the sacrifice called Ukhāsaṃbharaṇa, in the oblation made to Agni, if the sacrificer is a Kṣatriya, this Ṛk beginning "Sa citra" is to be recited as the yājyā mantra; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, स चित्र चित्रं चितयंतमस्मे अग्निरीशे बृहतः क्षत्रियस्य (*sa citra citraṃ citayaṃtamasme agnirīśe bṛhataḥ kṣatriyasya*) (Ā. 4-1).

Mūrdhānam means the one who is the head. Of what? Of heaven (diva), that is, of the world of heaven, and of the earth (pṛthivyāḥ), that is, of the extended earth. Aratim means one who goes; or, the master to whom one must go. Vaiśvānara means one connected with all men. Ṛte: ṛta is a name for truth and for sacrifice; the case is the locative of cause, so "for the sake of the sacrifice" or "turned towards the sacrifice". Jātam means born, that is, produced at the beginning of creation. Kavi is the far-seeing one; samrāj, the one who shines well; atithi of the people, that is, of the sacrificers, one who constantly goes to carry the oblation; or, one to be honoured like a guest. Āsan is a locative used in the sense of the accusative (for āsye, "in the mouth"): the gods eat the oblations by the mouth in the form of Agni. Pātram is the protector, the guardian; or, the holder by the mouth. Such a Vaiśvānara Agni, endowed with these qualities, the gods, that is, the praisers, the ṛtvijs, or the gods themselves, generated, that is, with a view to the sacrifice they produced him from the two kindling sticks.
- ऋते (*ṛte*)—for the sake of the sacrifice
- आ जातं (*ā jātaṃ*)—one who was produced
- अतिथिं (*atithiṃ*)—the one in the form of a guest
- आसन् (*āsan*)—in the form of a mouth
- पात्रं (*pātraṃ*)—the one who has the vessel (that carries the oblation)
- वैश्वानरं अग्निं (*vaiśvānaraṃ agniṃ*)—Agni, who is of the form of Vaiśvānara

The gods produced Agni, who is of the form of Vaiśvānara, the head of the heavenly world, the master of the earth, born for the sake of the sacrifice, far-seeing, fully shining, a guest to the sacrificers, and possessed of a vessel for carrying the oblation in the form of a mouth.
The gods have generated Vaishwanara, Agni, as the brow of heaven,
the unceasing pervader of earth, born for (the celebration of) sacrifice, wise,
imperial. the guest of men, in whose mouth (is) the vessel (that conveys
the the oblation to the gods).

Agni is the nave, the binding link, of the sacrifices such as the Jyotiṣṭoma, and the abode, the one resting-place, of riches. He is great, and he is the "āhāva", that is, the place into which the oblations are called; or else, "āhāva" is the water-trough that holds the rain-water, to which Agni is compared. Such an Agni the worshippers praise together on every side. Vaiśvānara is the one who belongs to all men, the "ratha-driver" of the sacrifices: as a charioteer drives his own chariot, so he is the leader, the one who makes the sacrifices go and reach their end; he is the banner of the sacrifice, the one that makes it known. Such an Agni the gods, that is, the worshipping priests, or the gods themselves, bring forth, that is, produce by churning.
- यज्ञानां (*yajñānāṃ*)—to the sacrifices such as the Jyotiṣṭoma
- नाभिं (*nābhiṃ*)—the one in the form of the nave (the binder)
- आहावं (*āhāvaṃ*)—the one who receives the oblations, that Agni
- रथ्यं (*rathyaṃ*)—the one who carries them through
- केतुं (*ketuṃ*)—the one who makes it known
- वैश्वानरं (*vaiśvānaraṃ*)—that Agni who is of the form of Vaiśvānara

The worshippers stand all round and praise Agni, who is the nave of the sacrifices such as the Jyotiṣṭoma, the abode of riches, of great form, and the receiver of the oblations. The gods produced Agni, who is of the form of Vaiśvānara, the leader of all mankind, the one who carries the sacrifices through, and the one who makes the sacrifice known.
(The worhippers) glorify together, (Agni), the bond of sacrifices, the
abode of riches the great receptacle of burnt-offerings : the gods generate
Vaishwanara, the conveyer of oblations, the emblem, of sacrifice.

O Agni, the offerer who is "vājī", that is, the man who has oblations in the form of food, becomes wise, a "vipra", through you: by giving you the oblation he becomes wise. Likewise heroes are born through you as those who overcome the "abhimāti", the enemies. Since this is so, O Vaiśvānara, O king, O shining Agni, place in us, your devotees, desirable riches.
- वाजी (*vājī*)—the sacrificer who has the oblation
- अभिमातिषाहः (*abhimātiṣāhaḥ*)—(become) possessed of the power that destroys enemies
- वैश्वानर (*vaiśvānara*)—O Agni, who is of the form of Vaiśvānara

O Agni, the sacrificer who has the oblation is born wise through your help alone. Heroes also become possessed of the power that destroys enemies through your help alone. O shining one, O Agni of the form of Vaiśvānara, fill us with riches worthy of the utmost regard.
The offerer of (sacrificial) food becomes wise, Agni, from you: from
you heroes become the vanquishers of foes : therefore royal Vaishwanara,

O immortal Agni, free from the nature of death, all the gods, that is, the worshippers, praise you as you are being born from the two churning-sticks, as one praises a child. Or else, the "devas" are the rays, since they shine; all of them come to you at your birth, as fathers come to a son. And further, O Vaiśvānara Agni, when you shine between the two parents, who are the guardians, heaven and earth, then through your rites, the sacrifices such as the Jyotiṣṭoma, the sacrificers obtain immortality, the state of gods.
- अमृत (*amṛta*)—O Agni, free from the nature of death
- शिशुं न (*śiśuṃ na*)—like a young child
- अभि सं नवंते (*abhi saṃ navaṃte*)—honour and worship
- वैश्वानर (*vaiśvānara*)—O Agni, of the form of Vaiśvānara
- पित्रोः (*pitroḥ*)—between heaven and earth, the protectors of the worlds

O immortal Agni, free from the nature of death, all the worshippers honour and worship you, born from the churning-stick, as one does a young child. O Agni, of the form of Vaiśvānara, when you shine between heaven and earth, the protectors of the worlds, then by the rites connected with you, the sacrifices and the rest, the sacrificers and others obtain freedom from death.

All the worshippers together praise you, immortal Agni, when born like an infact : when you shine Vishwanara, between the parental (heaven and earth), they obtain immortality through your (sacred) rites.
O Vaiśvānara Agni, who belongs to all men, those well-known great rites of yours no one else can withstand or hinder.

When you, being born in the lap of your parents, heaven and earth, in the intermediate space, on the paths to be traversed, find the banner of the days, the sun, which is the one that makes it known, covered by Svarbhānu, you drive away by your own radiance the demon who is of the form of darkness, that is, you establish the sun. Then those rites of yours are such that no one can hinder them. ⟨NOTE:244⟩
notes: ವರ್ಗ— ೦: the number is not legible in the print

en: - वैश्वानर (*vaiśvānara*)—O Agni, of the form of Vaiśvānara
- नकिः आ दधर्ष (*nakiḥ ā dadharṣa*)—no one can hinder
- पित्रोः (*pitroḥ*)—of heaven and earth, who are like parents to you
- अह्नां केतुं (*ahnāṃ ketuṃ*)—the sun, who makes the day known
- वयुनेषु (*vayuneṣu*)—on the paths of the intermediate space

O Agni, of the form of Vaiśvānara, no one can hinder your well-known rites of great power. When you are born in the lap of heaven and earth, who are like parents to you, then you establish the sun, who makes the day known, on the paths of the intermediate space.
Agni, Vaishwanara, these your mighty deeds no one can resist; when born on the lap of your parents, you have stationed the banner of the days on the paths of the firmament.

By the radiance of Vaiśvānara, that is, of Agni, who is beneficial to all men, and by the one who makes known the "amṛta", the water, the "sānūni", the lofty places of heaven, the starry regions, are measured out, that is, built. Or else, the "sānūni" of the intermediate space, the lofty places, which are the clouds, are built, since they are a transformation of smoke. In the very head of this same Vaiśvānara, that is, in the smoke that stands above like a head and has turned into cloud, all the "bhuvanāni", the pervading waters, dwell. Or else, all beings dwell in the head, the upper region, of the supreme Brahman who is of the nature of Vaiśvānara. And the seven gliding rivers, or rivers of the number seven, the Gaṅgā and the rest, spring up like branches; they come forth from this very Vaiśvānara. The meaning is that through the oblation the whole world arises from Agni.
- मूर्धनि (*mūrdhani*)—in the upper part, in the smoke that has turned into cloud
- सप्त विस्सुहः (*sapta vissuhaḥ*)—the seven rivers in the form of streams also
- रुरुहुः (*ruruhuḥ*)—come forth from this Vaiśvānara alone

By the radiance of Vaiśvānara Agni, who makes known the rain-water, the lofty regions of the heavenly world are built. In the upper part of that same Vaiśvānara Agni, in the smoke that has turned into cloud, all the waters dwell. The seven rivers also, in the form of streams, come forth like branches from this Vaiśvānara alone.
The summits of the fimament are measured by the light of Vaishwa
nara, the manifester of ambrosial (rain) : all the regions are overspread
(by the vapour) on his brow, and the seven gliding (streams) spring from

Vaiśvānara Agni, the doer of good works, who is beneficial to all men, built the "rajāṃsi", the waters, the worlds. And being far-seeing, he built the shining bodies that belong to the heavenly world, the stars and the rest. He who spread all the beings, or the waters, all round, this one, unharmed by anyone, the guardian of all, is the protector, the keeper, of the "amṛta", the water that is the cause of freedom from death. The word "is" is to be supplied.
- परि पप्रथे (*pari paprathe*)—has pervaded all round
- वैश्वानरः (*vaiśvānaraḥ*)—that same Agni of the form of Vaiśvānara
- अमृतस्य (*amṛtasya*)—of all the water that is of the nature of ambrosia
He who is the doer of excellent works and has built all the worlds, the far-seeing one who has built the spheres of radiance of the intermediate space, who has pervaded all the worlds all round,
that same Agni of the form of Vaiśvānara, unassailed and the guardian of the world, is the keeper of all the water that is of the nature of ambrosia.

Vaishwanara, the performer of sacred acts, is he who made the regions ; foreseeing (he has made) the luminaries of heaven, and has spread throughout all worlds; the irresistible guardian (of all), the protector of ambrosial (rain).

"Pṛkṣa" means touched, pervaded; or else "pṛkṣa" is food in the form of oblations, so that it means the one who has it. Of the showerer, the radiant Jātavedas, the knower of what is born, Vaiśvānara Agni, I quickly proclaim in the sacrifice the might, the power to overcome; that is, I praise it greatly. One "nu" is a filler. This praise, which is newer, pure, or the purifier of the singers, beautiful, a thing to be thought about, flows forth to this Vaiśvānara Agni, flows from me; the meaning is that it goes out of itself, like Soma. As Soma flows from the ten-fold filter, so this praise.
- सोम इव (*soma iva*)—like a stream of Soma juice

I now praise in the sacrifice the uncommon strength of Agni, the all-pervading, the showerer of desires, the shining, of the form of Jātavedas. That praise, new, pure and charming, flows without hindrance, directed to Agni of the form of Vaiśvānara, like a stream of Soma juice.
I commemorate promptly at the holy ceremony the might of the
all-pervading! jatavedas, the showerer, the radiant : new, pure, and
graceful praise issues (from me), like the Soma juice (from the filter) to

That Vaiśvānara Agni, the protector of rites, born in the highest sky and appearing in the form of the sun, protects the rites, the works, worldly and Vedic. He also built the intermediate space, that is, he built the three worlds characterised by it. Likewise Vaiśvānara Agni, the doer of good works, touched with his own greatness, his radiance, the heavenly world.
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni, who is of the form of Vaiśvānara
- जायमानः (*jāyamānaḥ*)—born (in the form of the sun)

Agni of the form of Vaiśvānara, the protector of rites, born in the form of the sun in the highest intermediate space, protects the Vedic rites of men. He has also built the intermediate space. Vaiśvānara Agni, the doer of excellent works, has taken possession of the heavenly world by his greatness.
That Agni who, as soon as born in the highest heaven, the protector
of sacred rits, protects the pious acts (of men), he has made the manifold
firmament : Vaishwanara, the performer of good deeds, has attained

Vaiśvānara Agni, who is a friend to all, wonderful, great, a marvel, propped apart heaven and earth, the two "rodasī"; he held them up in particular so that they do not fall down, that is, he set them in their own place. Likewise by his radiance he made the darkness hidden, concealed within. The form is that of a root meaning movement, in the jug-ending class. And further, as one who has slaughtered an animal spreads out its two skins to dry, so he spread apart the two supporters, heaven and earth; he made them open and extended. What more need be said: this Vaiśvānara Agni holds all the virile power, he bears it.
- चर्मणेव (*carmaṇeva*)—as one who dismembers the sacrificial animal spreads out the skins
- वैश्वानरः (*vaiśvānaraḥ*)—Agni of the form of Vaiśvānara

Vaiśvānara Agni, the friend of all and of wonderful nature, has held up both heaven and earth. By his radiance he has hidden the darkness. As the one who dismembers the sacrificial animal, the cutter, spreads out the two skins, so Agni has spread heaven and earth widely. Agni, of the form of Vaiśvānara, has received the whole generative capacity.

The friend (of all), the wonderful (Agni), has upheld heaven and earth : he has hidden darkness within light : he has spread out the two sustaining (worlds, heaven and earth), like two skins : Vaishwanara comprehends all (creative) energy.

"Āpaḥ" is a name of the intermediate space. In the lap, the middle, of the intermediate space, the "mahiṣāḥ", the great Maruts ("mahiṣa" being a name for "great"), seized this Vaiśvānara, who was present as lightning; the meaning is that they did not know him. ⟨NOTE:247⟩ And having seized him, the people, the subjects, stood near the king, their lord, worthy of praise, and praised him. And further, this Vaiśvānara Agni, who before was near the sun, Mātariśvan, the swift one, or the messenger of the gods, that is, the wind, carried from far away, from Vivasvat, the Āditya; he brought him to this world.
notes: ಚೇಷ್ಟಾಶ್ಚಾತುಃ ಸ್ಯಾದ್ವಸ್ತ್ರಂ in the verse as supplied is doubtful

en: - अगृभ्यत (*agṛbhyata*)—grasped (the form of Vaiśvānara, who is in the shape of lightning)
- वैश्वानरं (*vaiśvānaraṃ*)—who is of the form of Vaiśvānara
- परावतः (*parāvataḥ*)—who is in a very distant region
- आ भरत् (*ā bharat*)—has taken and brought

The Maruts of great form, who are in the middle part of the intermediate space, grasped the form of Vaiśvānara, who is in the shape of lightning. All the people praised this worshipful lord, Agni. The wind, the messenger of the gods, has taken Agni, who is of the form of Vaiśvānara, from Āditya, who is in a very distant region, and brought him.
The mighty Maruts have seized upon him on the lap of the waters
(in the firmament), and men have acknowledged him as their adorable
sovereign : Matarishwan, the messenger of the gods. has brought Agni
Vaishwanara (hither) from the distant (sphere of the) sun.

O Agni, in every age, at every time, "vidathya" is that which is fit for the "vidatha", the sacrifice; directed to you, who are worthy of it, give wealth and a famed son to us who utter a newer praise. And further, O shining, ageless Agni, with your own radiance, like a thunderbolt, strike down the enemy who proclaims evil, as one cuts down a tree, so that he becomes low, laid prostrate.
- विदथ्यं (*vidathyaṃ*)—directed to you, who are fit for the sacrifice
- यशसं (*yaśasaṃ*)—and famed sons and the rest
- आजर (*ājara*)—O one who is free from death
- वनिनं न (*vaninaṃ na*)—as one cuts down a tree
- अघशंसं (*aghaśaṃsaṃ*)—the enemy who wishes us harm

O Agni, provide wealth and famed sons and the rest to us, who recite a newly made praise in every age, directed to you, who are fit for the sacrifice. O Agni, free from death and shining, with your radiance, sharp like a thunderbolt, cut down the enemy who wishes us harm, as one cuts down a tree, so that he falls down.
To those, Agni, who repeat new (praises) to you the object of their
worship from age to age, grant riches and famous (posterity) : strike down
undecaying sovereign, the sinner with your blaze like the thunderbolt, as

O Agni, the word "asmākam" is a genitive in the sense of the locative: in us, who are "maghavat", possessed of wealth in the form of oblations, establish "kṣatra", wealth. Of what kind: not to be bent, that is, not to be carried off; ageless, free from old age, imperishable; with excellent vigour. And further, O Vaiśvānara Agni, through your protections we may win "vāja", food, that is "śatin", of the number of a hundred or accompanied by a hundred men, and likewise "sahasriṇa", of the number of a thousand.
- मघवत्सु (*maghavatsu*)—who have wealth in the form of oblations
- सुवीर‍्यं (*suvīryaṃ*)—which has excellent sons and the rest
- तव ऊतिभिः (*tava ūtibhiḥ*)—accompanied by your protection
- शतिनं (*śatinaṃ*)—of the number of a hundred
- सहस्रिणं (*sahasriṇaṃ*)—and of the number of a thousand

O Agni, establish in us, who have wealth in the form of oblations, wealth that is not carried off by thieves, that is imperishable and has excellent sons and the rest. O Agni, of the form of Vaiśvānara, accompanied by your protection may we obtain food of the number of a hundred and of a thousand, that is, in abundance.

Grrnt, Agni, to us who are affluent in (offerings), wealth that cannot be taken away, that is exempt from decay, and that comprehends excellent male descendants : may we obtain, Agni Vishwanara, hundreds and thousands of viands through your protection.

O "iṣṭe", you who are to be sacrificed to or to be sought, O "tri-ṣadhastha", you who abide together in the three worlds, or else, you who abide together in the three sites such as the Āhavanīya with the gods to whom sacrifice is offered, O Agni: with your radiances that are protectors ("gopā"), undamaged by anyone, protect our "sūri", our singers. O Vaiśvānara Agni, protect also the strength of us who have given oblations. Being praised, carry us over and advance us.
- इष्टे (*iṣṭe*)—you who are fit for sacrifice
- त्रिषधस्थ (*triṣadhastha*)—you who abide in all three worlds, O Agni
- सूरीन् (*sūrīn*)—who are your singers of praise
- स्तवानः (*stavānaḥ*)—you who are to be praised by us
- प्र च तारीः (*pra ca tārīḥ*)—cause to increase, or carry across (from sin)

O Agni, you who are fit for sacrifice and abide in all three worlds, protect us, your singers of praise, with your irresistible protecting radiances. O Agni, of the form of Vaiśvānara, protect the strength of us who offer oblations. You who are to be praised by us, grow strong.

Adored Agni, present in the three worlds, protect your worshippers with your irresistible protections, preserve the strength of us who offer (oblations) : glorified (by us), Agni Vaishwanara, transport us (beyond evil.

"Aha" is that on which a man brings ("āharati") his works. "Kṛṣṇa" is black. By agreement in gender, the word "aha" here means the night, black with darkness; and "arjuna", white by the solar radiance, is the day. The two "rajasī", lighting the whole world each with its own light, revolve in various ways by their "vedyā", their activities, which are to be known as favourable. Or else, the "rajasī" are heaven and earth, which is an indication of the three worlds: they turn about the three worlds. And this is, it is to be supplied, by the command of Vaiśvānara Agni, who is here the deity to be set forth. And this Vaiśvānara Agni, being born, appearing and growing like a king, destroyed the darknesses with his radiance. The root "avatirati" has the sense of killing; it means he destroys.
- अर्जुनं च (*arjunaṃ ca*)—possessed of its own radiance
- वेद्याभिः (*vedyābhiḥ*)—by their revolutions, which are visible to all
- वैश्वानरः (*vaiśvānaraḥ*)—who is of the form of Vaiśvānara
- जायमानः (*jāyamānaḥ*)—as soon as he is born
- राजा न (*rājā na*)—shining like a lord

The night-time, possessed of darkness, and the day, possessed of its own radiance, under the command of Vaiśvānara, lighting up the world, move in turns by their revolutions, which are visible to all,
moving about in alternation. Agni, of the form of Vaiśvānara, as soon as he is born, shining like a lord, has completely destroyed the darkness with his radiance.
The dark day and the light day revolve alternate, affecting (the world) by their recognizable (properties): Agni Vaishwanara, manifested like a prince, dispels darkness by his lustre.

The sacrificialists hold that the seer, wishing to proclaim the greatness of Vaiśvānara, here pictures the sacrifice as a cloth and so shows how hard it is to know. The "tantu", the threads, are the extended threads of the cloth, the warp; for the cloth that is the sacrifice these are the metres such as Gāyatrī and the stuta-śastras. These, he says, "I do not know". Likewise the "otu": the woof, the threads laid across; here these are the Yajus mantras and the acts of the Adhvaryu. These too he does not know. Moreover, he does not know the cloth, the form of the sacrifice, that results from both, the cloth which the priests, "atamānāḥ", that is, constantly exerting themselves at the "samara", the meeting in the place of worship of the gods, weave, that is, they spin out warp and woof and produce them in the form of a cloth. "Kasya svit": here in this world; "svit" is in the sense of doubt. Of whom indeed the son, a man, would speak the things that are to be spoken, those that belong to the yonder world:

The sentence is completed thus: the one who abides yonder, in the other world, is Sūrya; he is instructed by his father, the "avara", Vaiśvānara Agni, who abides in this world; so instructed, he speaks ("vadāti" means "would speak"). The meaning is that no one is able to speak. This is stated by those who know the tradition in a verse: Vaiśvānara's son is he who stands beyond, in heaven; the metres, the stuta-śastras, are the threads of the sacrificial cloth; the Yajus mantras and the sacrificial acts are the woof, and the sacrifice is the cloth to be woven; Sūrya stands beyond, and the father, Agni, is held to be terrestrial. ⟨NOTE:249⟩

Those who know the Self hold that, by means of a metaphor, the ṛk shows how hard the creation of the world is to know. "Tantu": the subtle, unmixed elements, ether and the rest, which stand in the place of the warp threads, he does not know. "Otu": the gross, mixed elements, ether and the rest, which stand in the place of the woof, he does not know either. Nor does he know their product, the manifold world that stands in the place of the cloth, which worldly beings, constantly exerting themselves in the union of warp and woof, weave, that is, produce. For their enjoyment the Lord creates; hence agency is ascribed to them figuratively. "Iha": in this matter. The things to be spoken that lie beyond the range of the intellect: whose son, instructed by an "avara", a later being born after the creation, his own father, would speak them? Knowing nothing of the events before his own origin, no one would speak. This is the meaning.
notes: ಜಾರರೂಪೇಣ printed; the sense seems to be the digestive fire

en: - तंतुं (*taṃtuṃ*)—the form of the threads of the warp needed for weaving cloth
- न वि जानामि (*na vi jānāmi*)—have not known
- यं (*yaṃ*)—which cloth of the form of the sacrifice
- समरे (*samare*)—at the time of the sacrifice
- अतमानाः (*atamānāḥ*)—the priests intent on their work
- पित्रा (*pitrā*)—by the father of the form of Vaiśvānara (instructed)
- परः (*paraḥ*)—of the other world, (in the form of a son) the Sun
- इह (*iha*)—at this time of the sacrifice
- वक्त्वानि (*vaktvāni*)—the sentences fit to be recited
- कस्य स्वित् (*kasya svit*)—of which master of the house in this house of sacrifice
- पुत्रः (*putraḥ*)—the son (can recite? it is possible for no one)

I have not known the form of the threads of the warp needed for weaving the cloth that is the sacrifice, nor the threads called the woof. Nor do I know the form of the cloth of the sacrifice that these priests, intent on their work, weave. The Sun, who in the other world is in the form of a son, instructed by the father who is in this world in the form of Vaiśvānara, can recite sentences that are to be recited at this time of the sacrifice; but no master of the house here, nor his son, nor anyone, is able to recite them.

I understand not the threads (of the warp), nor the threads of the woof, nor that (cloth) which those who are assiduous in united exertion weave: of what (man) may the son declare the words that are to be spoken in the next world, (instructed) by a father abiding below.

The commentator has given two kinds of meaning for this ṛk: one relating to the sacrifice, the other relating to the Self. Both kinds of meaning fit this ṛk well. In this ṛk the seer says that he does not know the form of the sacrifice or of the Self, and in the next ṛk he describes the greatness of Vaiśvānara Agni by saying that Vaiśvānara Agni alone knows this matter.
**Explanation of the meaning relating to the sacrifice**

न अहं तंतुं वि जानामि (*na ahaṃ taṃtuṃ vi jānāmi*)—तंतवः पटस्य प्रागायतनानि सूत्राणि । तानि च यज्ञात्मकस्य वस्त्रस्य गायत्रादीनि छंदांसि स्तुतशस्त्राणि च । तानि अहं न वि जानामि! (*taṃtavaḥ paṭasya prāgāyatanāni sūtrāṇi | tāni ca yajñātmakasya vastrasya gāyatrādīni chaṃdāṃsi stutaśastrāṇi ca | tāni ahaṃ na vi jānāmi!*) Here the sacrifice is compared to cloth. When cloth is woven, threads are used. These threads are of two kinds. Some threads are set lengthwise in the loom; these are called the warp. The threads that are passed across, crosswise, through the warp are called the woof. With the help of the loom, the woof is joined to the warp one thread at a time, and the cloth is woven. This is the making of cloth, that is, the manner of weaving cloth. Taking this very manner as the example, the meaning of this ṛk has been explained. Here, that is, in the sacrifice, the metres beginning with Gāyatrī and the śastra mantras are the threads called the warp, which are used for weaving the cloth. The seer says "I do not know these"; that is, he says "I do not know the nature and the like of the various metres beginning with Gāyatrī used in sacrifices, and of the śastra mantras such as आश्विन (*āśvina*), निष्केवल्य (*niṣkevalya*), आग्नि मारुत (*āgni māruta*) and आज्य (*ājya*)"; he states his own littleness, that is, that his knowledge is very small, in order to make known the greatness of Vaiśvānara Agni.

तथा ओतुं न (वि जानामि) (*tathā otuṃ na (vi jānāmi)*)—ओतवस्तिरश्चीनानि सूत्राणि । तानि चात्र यजूंष्याध्वर्यवाणि कर्माणि च । तान्यहं न वि जानामि । (*otavastiraścīnāni sūtrāṇi | tāni cātra yajūṃṣyādhvaryavāṇi karmāṇi ca | tānyahaṃ na vi jānāmi |*) And I do not know the threads called the woof. Here, in the sacrifice, the cross-threads called the woof are the mantras of the Yajurveda and the subsidiary acts of the sacrifice that the priests such as the Adhvaryu perform in sacrifices and the like; the seer says that he does not know the nature of these either.

समरे अतमानाः यं वयंति (तदपि अहं) न (जानामि) (*samare atamānāḥ yaṃ vayaṃti (tadapi ahaṃ) na (jānāmi)*)—अपि चैतदुभय साध्यं तं पटं यज्ञलक्षणं न वि जानामि । यं पटं यज्ञलक्षणं समरे संगमने देवयजने सततं वेष्टमाना ऋत्विजः वयंति तंतूनोतूंश्च संतन्वंति वस्त्ररूपेण निष्पादयंति तदपि नाहं जानामि । (*api caitadubhaya sādhyaṃ taṃ paṭaṃ yajñalakṣaṇaṃ na vi jānāmi | yaṃ paṭaṃ yajñalakṣaṇaṃ samare saṃgamane devayajane satataṃ veṣṭamānā ṛtvijaḥ vayaṃti taṃtūnotūṃśca saṃtanvaṃti vastrarūpeṇa niṣpādayaṃti tadapi nāhaṃ jānāmi |*) Besides this, I do not know the manner of weaving by joining the warp and the woof. That is, the seer says that he does not know the mantras that the priests and others recite when they perform the various acts in sacrifices, the subsidiary acts of the sacrifice that are to be performed at the proper times, or the order of when and how these are to be done.

कस्य स्वित् पुत्र इह वक्त्वानि परः अवरेण पित्रा वदाति (*kasya svit putra iha vaktvāni paraḥ avareṇa pitrā vadāti*)—कस्य खलु पुत्रः मनुष्यः वक्तव्यानि तानीमानि अमुष्मिन् लोके वर्तमानस्य सूर्यस्य पित्रा अस्मिन्‌लोके वर्तमानेन वैश्वानराग्निनानुशिष्टान् वदेत् । न कश्चिदपि प्रवदितुं शक्नोतीत्यर्थः ॥ (*kasya khalu putraḥ manuṣyaḥ vaktavyāni tānīmāni amuṣmin loke vartamānasya sūryasya pitrā asminloke vartamānena vaiśvānarāgninānuśiṣṭān vadet | na kaścidapi pravadituṃ śaknotītyarthaḥ ‖*) Besides, what is to be said on these matters: what man indeed could say it with precision, accompanied by the Sun who shines in the atmosphere and by Vaiśvānara Agni who shines on the earth in sacrifices and the like? No one can.
Here the Sun is described as the son of Vaiśvānara Agni. Some great seers who know the tradition state this matter in this way:

वैश्वानरस्य पुत्रोऽसौ परस्ताद्दिवि यः स्थितः । छंदांस्यध्वरवस्तस्य स्तुतशस्त्राणि तंतवः । यजूंषि चेष्टाश्चौतुः स्याद्वस्त्रं वातव्यमध्वरः । परः परः स्थितः सूर्यः पिताग्निः पार्थिवो मतः ॥ (*vaiśvānarasya putro 'sau parastāddivi yaḥ sthitaḥ | chaṃdāṃsyadhvaravastasya stutaśastrāṇi taṃtavaḥ | yajūṃṣi ceṣṭāścautuḥ syādvastraṃ vātavyamadhvaraḥ | paraḥ paraḥ sthitaḥ sūryaḥ pitāgniḥ pārthivo mataḥ ‖*)

That is: this Sun who shines in the atmosphere is the son of Vaiśvānara Agni; the metres and the śastra mantras recited in sacrifices are the warp threads of the cloth called the sacrifice; the Yajurveda mantras and the subsidiary acts of the sacrifice performed by the priests are the woof threads of this cloth. The sacrifice itself is the cloth. For the Sun who is in heaven, the sacrificial fire is the father. In this way the matters stated in this ṛk, that is, the cloth and the manner of weaving it, have been explained by comparing them with the metres and mantras used in the sacrifice, and with the sacrifice.
**Explanation of the meaning relating to the Self**
In this illustration the threads are compared to the five elements, earth and the rest, and the cloth to the creation of the world.

न अहं तंतुं वि जानामि-तंतुस्थानानि सूक्ष्माणि वियदादीन्यपंचीकृतानि भूतानि न विजानामि । (*na ahaṃ taṃtuṃ vi jānāmi-taṃtusthānāni sūkṣmāṇi viyadādīnyapaṃcīkṛtāni bhūtāni na vijānāmi |*) Before the creation of the world, Prajāpati created पृथिव्यप्तेजोवायुराकाश (*pṛthivyaptejovāyurākāśa*)

that is, the five elements, earth, water, fire, air and ether, and by the process of their fivefold combination (that is, by mixing one with another) he created this visible world. Therefore the five elements beginning with ether, which are the cause of the creation of the world, are here the warp threads of the cloth. The seer says that he does not know their nature.
