तथा ओतुं न (वि जानामि) (*tathā otuṃ na (vi jānāmi)*)—ओतून् पंचीकृतानि स्कूलान्वोतुस्थानीयान्यपि वियदादीनि न विजानामि । (*otūn paṃcīkṛtāni skūlānvotusthānīyānyapi viyadādīni na vijānāmi |*) Likewise, the woof threads here are the many things of this world visible to our eyes that arise from the fivefold combination (mixing) of the five elements beginning with ether. I do not know their nature.

समरे अतमानाः यं वयंति (तदपि अहं) न (जानामि)—न च तत्कार्यं पटस्थानीयं प्रपंचं विजानामि यं प्रपंचं समरे तंतूनामोतूनां चॆ संगमेऽतामानाः सततं चेष्टमानाः संसारिणो वयंति उत्पादयंति तदपि न जानामि । (*samare atamānāḥ yaṃ vayaṃti (tadapi ahaṃ) na (jānāmi)—na ca tatkāryaṃ paṭasthānīyaṃ prapaṃcaṃ vijānāmi yaṃ prapaṃcaṃ samare taṃtūnāmotūnāṃ cè saṃgame 'tāmānāḥ satataṃ ceṣṭamānāḥ saṃsāriṇo vayaṃti utpādayaṃti tadapi na jānāmi |*) The five elements beginning with ether, and the things that arise from their fivefold combination: out of these the creator of the world creates the world, and in that world the embodied souls, caught in worldly existence, fix their own conditions by their own actions. I do not know these either.

कस्य स्वित् पुत्र इह वक्तानि परः अवरेण पित्रा वदाति इहास्मिन्विषये परः परस्ताद्भुद्धेरविषये वर्तमानानि वक्तव्यानीमान्यवरेणार्वाचीनेन सृष्ट्युत्तरकालमुत्पन्नेन पित्रा स्वजनकेनानुशिष्टः सन् कस्य खलु पुत्रो वदाति ! स्वोत्पत्तेः प्राचीनं वृत्तांतमजानानः कश्चिदपि न वदेदित्यर्थः । (*kasya svit putra iha vaktāni paraḥ avareṇa pitrā vadāti ihāsminviṣaye paraḥ parastādbhuddheraviṣaye vartamānāni vaktavyānīmānyavareṇārvācīnena sṛṣṭyuttarakālamutpannena pitrā svajanakenānuśiṣṭaḥ san kasya khalu putro vadāti ! svotpatteḥ prācīnaṃ vṛttāṃtamajānānaḥ kaścidapi na vadedityarthaḥ |*) In this matter of creation, what is going on now and what happened before, that is, the conditions that existed before creation and how creation came about: what son born of a father could know these? That is, what man could know, without the help of others, the events that took place before his own birth? No one can know; this is the intention.

Although these matters are hard to know in the way described, Vaiśvānara Agni knows and speaks them; this the ṛk sets forth. "Sa it": that same Vaiśvānara Agni knows fully the "tantu", the threads, that is, the metres such as Gāyatrī and the stuta-śastras that stand in the place of the warp threads; likewise he alone knows the "otu", the Yajus mantras and the acts of the Adhvaryu that stand in the place of the woof. "Ṛtuthā" means at each time, at the time of each performance; he speaks what is to be spoken. "Vadāti" means "he would speak". Who is this Vaiśvānara? He is the "gopā" of "amṛta", that is, the guardian of water; moving "avaḥ", below, in the terrestrial world, in the form of the terrestrial fire; "paraḥ", beyond, in heaven, in "anyena", another form, that of the Sun, he beholds and illuminates the whole world; "īm", these beings seen all around, "ciketat", he knows. "Sa eva", "he alone", is to be connected with what precedes.

Or else: he alone knows the subtle elements that stand in the place of the warp threads, and no one else; likewise he alone knows the gross elements that stand in the place of the woof. He alone speaks the things that are to be spoken, to be taught, "ṛtuthā", at each time, whenever the tradition of knowledge is cut off. Who is it that could know and speak? To this he answers: Vaiśvānara, of the nature of all men, the Supreme Self, is the "gopā", the guardian, of "amṛta", that is, of immortality, of liberation; "avaḥ", below, in the state of worldly existence, moving, that is, equipped with the inner organ and moving in the condition of the individual self; "paraḥ", beyond ignorance, abiding above it, "anyena", by another form, different from the one described, free of limiting conditions, with the nature of being, consciousness and the like, he beholds and illuminates the whole world; he knows these, "īm". So too it is heard of the Supreme Self: तमेव भांतमनुभाति सर्वं तस्य भासा सर्वमिदं विभाति । (*tameva bhāṃtamanubhāti sarvaṃ tasya bhāsā sarvamidaṃ vibhāti |*) ⟨NOTE:250⟩ **GLOSS**
notes: ಈ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರನನ್ನು: the verb "behold" (ನೋಡಿರಿ) seems to be missing

en: - चरन् (*caran*)—moving in the form of the terrestrial fire
- अन्येन (*anyena*)—in the form of the Sun
- स इत् (*sa it*)—that same Vaiśvānara Agni
- तंतुं (*taṃtuṃ*)—as threads are the very parts of a cloth
- ओतुं (*otuṃ*)—of the form of the woof
such as the Yajus mantras and the rest, he knows.
- ऋतुथा (*ṛtuthā*)—according to the time of each rite
- वक्तानि (*vaktāni*)—the sentences that are to be recited

That Vaiśvānara Agni who, as the protector of water, moves on the earth in the form of the terrestrial fire, beholds the whole world in the world of heaven in the form of the Sun, and knows all the beings referred to, that same Vaiśvānara Agni fully knows the praises and the śastras, the parts of the sacrifice, just as threads are the very parts of a cloth. He too knows the Yajus mantras and the rest, which are of the form of the woof. He also recites the sentences that are to be recited according to the time of each sacrifice.

He verily knows the threads of the warp and of the woof, he speaks in due season what is to be said, who comprehends all this (universe) ; who is the protector of ambrosial water, sojourning both above and below, and contemplating (the world) under a different (manifestation).

This Vaiśvānara Agni is the first, the foremost, Hotṛ; the human Hotṛ is the second. "O men, behold him", that is, serve him. Among mortals, that is, in bodies whose nature is to die, this immortal light, free from death, called Vaiśvānara, abides in the जाररूपेण (*jārarūpeṇa*) form. ⟨NOTE:251⟩

Moreover, this same Agni is "dhruva", unmoving, and "ā niṣatta", seated all around, that is, all-pervading; for that very reason he is "amartya", free from death, and yet, through his connection with a body, he "jajñe", is born; and he is figuratively said to be growing.
notes: ವಿಶ್ವಾಸನಾತ್ಮಕಂ in the bhāṣya seems damaged

en: - प्रथमः होता (*prathamaḥ hotā*)—the first among all the Hotṛs
- इदं ज्योतिः (*idaṃ jyotiḥ*)—this light of the form of Vaiśvānara
- अमृतं (*amṛtaṃ*)—that which is free from death

This Vaiśvānara Agni is the first among all the Hotṛs. O men, this Vaiśvānara; this light, of the form of Vaiśvānara, is free from death among men. ⟨NOTE:252⟩. Although this same god is unmoving, all-pervading and free from death, he has obtained a body and come to be born. He also attains growth.
notes: abbreviation ಅ. printed

en: This Vaishwanara is the first offerer of burnt-offerings : behold him : this is the light immortal amongst mortals : he has been born in a bodily shape, immovable, all-pervading, immortal, ever increasing.

"Dhruva" means unmoving; "javiṣṭha" means exceedingly swift, swifter even than the mind. Such a light, called Vaiśvānara, has been placed ("nihita") by Prajāpati "antar", in the midst, among beings who move ("patayatsu", those that go). For what purpose? "Dṛśaye kam": for the sake of seeing. Moreover, all the gods, "samanasaḥ", of one mind, and "saketāḥ", of one understanding, being so, properly and completely approach the one chief, or the goer, "kratu", the doer of rites; "abhi vi yanti" means that they approach him facing him, in various ways; the meaning is that they serve him.

Or else: "patayatsu" means among those that go, beings; "antar" means in the middle, in the heart; "manaḥ" is the mind, here "javiṣṭha", exceedingly swift even beyond the mind, "dhruva", unmoving, free of conceptual alternatives. So the Vājasaneyaka says: अनेजदेकं मनसो जवीयः (*anejadekaṃ manaso javīyaḥ*) (Vā. Saṃ. 40-4) **GLOSS** The light is Brahman, consciousness; it is "nihita", placed by no one. So it is heard: यो वेद निहितं गुहायां परमे व्योमन् (*yo veda nihitaṃ guhāyāṃ parame vyoman*) (Tai. Ā. 8-1) **GLOSS** For what purpose? "Dṛśaye", for the sake of seeing; for by knowledge all is known. Moreover, "devāḥ" are the senses, because they shine; "viśve devāḥ" are all the senses, the eye and the rest, "samanasaḥ", functioning together with the mind, "saketāḥ", possessed of radiance, aiming at the one, the one without a second, "kratu", the doer of the acts of creation and the rest, the Supreme Self whose nature is विश्वासनात्मकं (*viśvāsanātmakaṃ*) ⟨NOTE:253⟩, they "sādhu", properly, "vi yanti", go in various ways; that is, they approach him facing him, in various ways; the meaning is that they worship him. So it is heard: तद्देवा ज्योतिषां ज्योतिरायुर्होपासतेऽमृतं । (*taddevā jyotiṣāṃ jyotirāyurhopāsate 'mṛtaṃ |*) (Śa. Brā. 14-7-2-20) **GLOSS**
notes: ವಿಘ್ನ್ಯುಕ್ತವಾಗಿ printed; the gloss has ಅತಿಶಯವಾಗಿ "exceedingly"; read here as "without hindrance"?

en: - पतयत्सु (*patayatsu*)—among living beings of a moving nature
- दृशये कं (*dṛśaye kaṃ*)—for the sake of seeing
- सकेताः (*saketāḥ*)—being of one kind of understanding
- अभि वि यंति (*abhi vi yaṃti*)—approach and serve

The light of Vaiśvānara, which is unmoving and exceedingly swifter than the mind, has been placed by Prajāpati among living beings of a moving nature, for the sake of seeing and as a guide. All the gods, being of one mind and of one kind of understanding, approach Vaiśvānara, the chief and the doer of rites, and serve him well.

A steady light, swifter than throught, stationed among moving beings to show (the way) to happiness : all ,the gods being of one mind, and of like wisdom, proceed respectfully to the presence of the one (chief) agent, (Vaishwanara).

For me, who wish to hear Vaiśvānara, my ears "vi patayataḥ", go in various ways, because the things to be heard, his qualities, are many. Likewise, for me who wish to see Vaiśvānara, the organ of the eye goes in various ways, because the things to be seen, his forms, are many. Likewise the light, the illuminator, placed in the heart, in the lotus of the heart, that principle called buddhi, also goes in various ways to know the Self that is Vaiśvānara. Moreover, "dūra-ādhīḥ" means that whose meditation is on a distant, remote object; the change of gender is Vedic. My mind too ranges in various ways. Thus, while all the senses are engaged, each vying with the others, what shall I say of the form of Vaiśvānara? "Kim u nu": what indeed shall I now think, that is, grasp with the mind? Because the qualities of Vaiśvānara are endless, he cannot be known by me, whose understanding is slow. This is the meaning.
- वि पतॆयतः (*vi patèyataḥ*)—spread all around (to hear the qualities of Vaiśvānara)
- वि (*vi*)—spread out (to see his divine form)
- हृदये (*hṛdaye*)—in the lotus of the heart
- यत् ज्योतिः (*yat jyotiḥ*)—which radiant principle of understanding there is
- दूरआधीः (*dūraādhīḥ*)—able to grasp even a distant object
- किं स्वित् वक्ष्यामि (*kiṃ svit vakṣyāmi*)—which qualities of Vaiśvānara shall I praise?
- किं नु मनिष्ये (*kiṃ nu maniṣye*)—which form shall I know?

To hear the endless qualities of Vaiśvānara my ears spread out all around. To see his endless form the organs of my eyes spread out all around. My principle of understanding, placed in the lotus of the heart, is also eager to know him. My mind, which is able to grasp even a distant object, also ranges everywhere. Which of the endless qualities of Vaiśvānara shall I praise? Which of his endless forms shall I know?

My ears are turned (to hear him), my eyes (to behold hlm); this light that in placed in the heart (seeks to know him); my mind, the receptacle of distant (objects), hastens (towards him): what shall I declare (him)? how shall I comprehend him ?

O Vaiśvānara, all the gods bow to you, who stand "tamasi", in darkness. For what reason? "Bhiyānāḥ", because they are afraid of the darkness. Such a one, the immortal, free from death, Vaiśvānara Agni, "ūtaye", with protection, that is, by protecting, "avatu", may he protect us. The repetition is for the sake of respect.
- अमर्त्यः (*amartyaḥ*)—Agni, who is free from the nature of death
O Vaiśvānara, all the gods, frightened, bow to you, who are hidden in darkness. May that Vaiśvānara, free from the nature of death, protect us together with his protections.
All the gods, alarmed, venerate you, Agni, abiding in darkness : may Vaishwanara preserve us with his protection : may the immortal Agni preserve us with his protection.

"O priests and sacrificers, you": "mandra" means delightful, to be praised; "divya" means born in heaven; "suvṛkti" means well free of faults, or not easily to be abandoned; such an Agni "prayati", goes forth. In the sacrifice that is being performed, which is "adhvara", not to be injured by Rākṣasas and the like, or free of injury and obstruction, "puraḥ dadhidhvam": set him before you, hold him in front in the form of the Āhavanīya fire. Or else: appoint him as purohita. "Ukthebhiḥ": with praises and śastras, set him before you. "Vibhāvā" means shining in a special manner; "Jātavedas" means the knower of what is born. Since that Agni "svadhvarā", makes us possessors of fine sacrifices, "karati" (that is, "karoti"), therefore set him before you; such is the construction.
- दिव्यं (*divyaṃ*)—who is born in the world of heaven
- प्रयति (*prayati*)—that which is going on in the present case
- उक्तेभिः (*uktebhiḥ*)—with the praises, śastras and mantras

O priests and sacrificers, establish in front of you Agni, who is to be praised, born in the world of heaven and free of faults, together with the praises, śastras and mantras, in the sacrifice that is going on in the present case and is free from injury. That same Agni makes us persons of excellent sacrifice.
Place before you at progressive, uninterrupted sacrifice, the divine, adorable, pefect Agni, with prayers ; for he, the resplendent Jatavedas, makes us prosperous in sacred rites.

"O Dyumat", possessed of radiance, "purvaṇīka", of many flames, "hotṛ", the invoker of the gods, Agni, "agnibhiḥ", together with other fires that are parts of yourself, "idhānaḥ", kindled and shining, hear that praise of man, the praiser; the verb "hear" is the remainder to be supplied. The particle "u" fills out the foot. That praise, "śūṣa", which brings happiness, "pure", like clarified butter strained through the two purifiers, "śuci", clean, "asmai", for this Agni, "matayaḥ", the thinkers, the praisers, "mamateva": Mamatā is the name of a woman expounder of Brahman, the mother of Dīrghatamas. As she did, they "pavante", purify, that is, refine it; the meaning is that they utter it free of fault. "That praise" is the construction.
- होतः (*hotaḥ*)—who calls the gods to the sacrifice
- अग्निभिः (*agnibhiḥ*)—together with the other fires, your parts
- धृतं न (*dhṛtaṃ na*)—like clarified butter, which is pure
- ममता इव (*mamatā iva*)—as the woman named Mamatā offered

O Agni, possessed of radiance, of many flames, who call the gods to the sacrifice, kindled together with the other fires that are your parts, hear that same praise which these men, the praisers, offer in purity, directed to Agni, as the woman named Mamatā offered it, a pure praise like clarified butter, which brings happiness and is pure.

Brilliant, may-rayed Agni, invoker of the gods, kindled with many fires, (hear) this (praise) of men ; which delightful praise, pure as the clarified butter (that has been filtered), his worshippers offer unto him as Mamata (formerly offered it).

That sacrificer, among mortals, that is, among men, "pīpāya", grows, "śravasā", through food. The wise one, the sacrificer who "dadāśa", gives, offers, oblations "ukthaiḥ", together with praises: that sacrificer "citraśociḥ", Agni of manifold radiance, "citrābhiḥ", with wondrous "ūtibhiḥ", protections, "dadhāti", holds in the enjoying, "sātā", of the herd, "vraja", the cow-pen "gomat", filled with cows.

The wise sacrificer who offers oblations accompanied by praises, directed to Agni, that same sacrificer grows among men, possessed of food. Agni of manifold radiance makes that same sacrificer enjoy a herd of cows, accompanied by protections of many kinds.

He thrives in abundance amongst men, who pious, presents to Agni (oblations) with prayers : the wonderfully radiant Agni places him with marvellous protection in the enjoyment of pasturage full of herds of cattle.

"Kṛṣṇādhvā" means he whose path is black. The Agni who, "jāyamānaḥ", being born, that is, manifesting, fills "urvī", the two wide, heaven and earth, with "bhāsā", with a light "dūre-dṛśā", seen from afar: "ā papprau" means he fills them. That purifying Agni, "adha", thereafter, "ūrmyāyāḥ" (this is a name of night), belonging to night, "bahu cit", even much, "tamaḥ", darkness, is seen "dadṛśe", overcoming it with his radiance "śociṣā".
- जायमानः (*jāyamānaḥ*)—as soon as he is born
- उर्वि (*urvi*)—the two wide, heaven and earth

That same Agni, possessed of a black-coloured path, as soon as he is born fills the two wide, heaven and earth, with a radiance seen even from afar. Then Agni, the purifier, destroys with his own radiance even the very great darkness of the night, and shines.
The dark-pathed, as soon as generated, filled with his afar-seen light the two spacious (worlds) : he, the purifier, is now beheld dispersing with bis radiance the thick glooms of night.

"O Agni, to us, "maghavadbhyaḥ", who are possessed of wealth in the form of oblations, with "purūvājābhiḥ", much food, and "ūtī", with protections, "citram", a wondrous, desirable "rayim", wealth, "nu", quickly, "dhehi": give, bestow. The word "ca" is for combination with what is to be said. Those who by "rādhasā", wealth, and "śravasā", food, and "suvīryebhiḥ", fine vigour, surpass other men, "ati abhi santi", overcome them greatly: give us sons of that kind also." This is the meaning.
- मघवद्भ्यः (*maghavadbhyaḥ*)—who possess wealth in the form of oblations
- अभि संति (*abhi saṃti*)—surpass (give such sons also)

O Agni, to us, who possess wealth in the form of oblations, give quickly wealth that is accompanied by many kinds of food and by protections, and that is attractive. Give also such sons as will exceed other men exceedingly in wealth, in food and in many kinds of strength.
Bestow quickly, Agni, upon us who are affluent (in oblations), wondrous wealth, with abundant viands, and protections, such as enrich other men with wealth, with food, and with male descendants.

"O Agni, "uśan", desiring, you accept this sacrifice, this food of the nature of an oblation, "dhāḥ": place it in yourself. And the sacrificer, seated and possessed of the oblation, offers to you the cake and the rest; accept that." This is the construction. Moreover, "bharadvājeṣu", among the Bharadvāja seers, "suvṛktim", praise well free from faults, "dadhiṣe": hold. "Gadhyasya": the root "gadhyati" has the sense of mixing; so "of what is to be mixed", that is, of what is to be obtained, "vājasya", of food, "sāt", for the sharing in it as the cause: "avīḥ", protect those seers also.
- भरद्वाजेषु (*bharadvājeṣu*)—of the seers of the Bharadvāja line

O Agni, desiring that very cake which the sacrificer, seated in his seat and possessing the oblation, offers to you, hold in yourself this oblation, the means of the sacrifice. Hold in yourself the pure praises of the seers of the Bharadvāja line. And give them many kinds of food and protect them.

Agni, desirous (of the offering), accept this sacrifice, this food which the presenter (of the oblation), sitting down (before you), offers unto you : accept the blameless (praises) of the Bharadwaja (race), and favour them that they may obtain many sorts of food.

"O Agni, "dveṣāṃsi", our hating enemies, "vīnuhi": drive in various directions. Increase our "iḷām", our food. And we, "suvīrāḥ", possessed of fine heroes, that is, sons, grandsons and the rest, for "śatahimāḥ", a hundred winters, that is, years, "madema": may we rejoice, may we be satisfied."
- वि इनुहि (*vi inuhi*)—scatter in various directions
O Agni, scatter our enemies in various directions. Increase our food. May we, together with excellent sons, pass a hundred years in joy.
Scatter (our) enemies ; augment our abundance ; and may we, blessed with virtuous male descendants, enjoy happiness for a hundred winters.

"O Hotṛ, Agni, invoker of the gods, "yajīyān", most worshipful, you, "iṣitaḥ", sent, that is, requested by us: "na" is in the sense of "now"; now, at the sacrifice being performed, worship the host of the Maruts, "bādhaḥ", the repeller of foes." Or else the two sentences are these: "O Hotṛ Agni, worship the gods" is one sentence; "prayukti" is force, since it is applied; "marutām na prayukti" means "like the force of the Maruts"; "bādhaḥ": repel our enemies; this is the second sentence. Moreover, "mitrāvaruṇā": Mitra is the deity presiding over the day, Varuṇa the deity presiding over the night. "Nāsatyā": leaders of truth, or of true nature, or the Aśvins, born of the nose. "Dyāvāpṛthivī": heaven and earth. These gods "ā vavṛtyāḥ": turn hither, bring them for our sacrifice. This is the meaning.
- होतः (*hotaḥ*)—who call the gods to the sacrifice
- यजीयान् (*yajīyān*)—you who are most worthy of worship
- प्रयुक्ति (*prayukti*)—in the sacrifice that is being performed

O Agni, who call the gods to the sacrifice, you who are most worthy of worship, being requested by us, worship at the sacrifice now being performed the foe-destroying host of the Maruts. Bring Mitra and Varuṇa, the Aśvin deities, and Heaven and Earth, for our sacrifice.

Agni invoker of the gods, you who are adorable, being instigated by us, worship at our present rite the foe-repelling (troop) of the Maruts and bring to our sacrifice Mitra and Varuna, the Nasatyas and Heaven and Earth.

"O Agni, you, being among mortals, that is, among men, at the sacrifice ("vidathā") become the Hotṛ, the invoker of the gods. Of what kind are you? "Mandratamaḥ", most praiseworthy; "naḥ", for us; "adhrug", free from hostility toward us, that is, always a friend; "devaḥ", endowed with qualities such as generosity. And, O Agni, "juhvā": the flame is "juhū", because oblations are offered into it; with that purifying one, with the mouth, being the mouth of the gods, you, "vahniḥ", the bearer of the oblations, worship "tava svām", your own body called Sviṣṭakṛt."
- होता (*hotā*)—as the one who gives the invitation to the gods
- वह्निः (*vahniḥ*)—you who carry the oblation to the gods
- आसा (*āsā*)—being the mouth of the gods
- स्वा तन्वं (*svā tanvaṃ*)—the form called Sviṣṭakṛt

O Agni, you who are most praiseworthy, who do not wish us harm, who are of divine nature, are the one who gives the invitation to the gods at this sacrifice taking place among men. O Agni, you who carry the oblation to the gods, worship by means of your flame, which is purifying and is the mouth of the gods, your own body called Sviṣṭakṛt.

You are amidst mortals at the celebration (of sacrifice), the invoker of the gods ( you who are) most deserving of praise, a divinity doing us no harm ; the bearer (of the oblation) offers (the gods), Agni your own body with purifying flame as if with their mouth

"Dhanyā": wishing for wealth, being the cause of wealth, "dhiṣaṇā", the praise, O Agni, wishes you ("tve" is "you"). The word "cit" only fills out the foot. For what purpose? In order to worship excellently ("pra yajadhyai") the gods who are to be worshipped, Indra and the rest; your "janma", your manifestation, is for the sacrificer who praises, for a sacrificer of this kind. When indeed, among the Aṅgirasa seers, Bharadvāja, "vepiṣṭhaḥ", the one who most impels praise, "vipraḥ", the wise one, "rebhaḥ", the praiser, at the sacrifice ("iṣṭau") pronounces the "madhu", honeyed, delight-giving "chandaḥ", the hymn of praise, then the praise wishes you. This is the construction.
- देवान् (*devān*)—the gods, Indra and the rest

O Agni, when Bharadvāja, who among the Aṅgirases praises exceedingly, who is wise and a praiser, recites at the sacrifice the delightful hymn of praise, the praise recited with desire for wealth desires you and praises you, for the sacrificer who extols your manifestation in order to worship Indra and the other gods without hindrance.⟨NOTE:255⟩
notes: ಯಜ್ಞನಾಮೃತತ್ printed; read ಯಜ್ಞನಾಮ ಋತತ್?

en: Praise, solicitous of wealth. is ever addressed. Agni, to you inasmuch as your manifestation (enables) the worshipper to sacrifice to the gods when the pi us sage, the most earnest adorer amongst the Angirasas, the reciter (of the hymn), repeats at the ceremony, the gratifying measure.

This Agni "adidyutat": shines well, is lit up. Of what kind is he? "Apākaḥ": "pāka" is one whose understanding has still to ripen, a fool; the opposite of that is "apāka". "Vibhāvā": radiant. The rest of the sentence is in direct address: "O Agni, you, as such, worship with the oblation "rodasī", heaven and earth, which are widely spread, "urūcī". "Āyuṃ na": like a human guest, you whom "pañca janāḥ", the five peoples, men, namely the priests and the sacrificers, "rātahavyāḥ", having given the oblation, anoint, sprinkle, satisfy with "namasā", with food in the form of oblation, you who have "suprayasam", a fine oblation. Worship, such as you are." This is the construction.
- पंचजनाः (*paṃcajanāḥ*)—all men, priests, sacrificers and the rest
- आयुं न (*āyuṃ na*)—like a human guest

Agni, who possesses full understanding and is radiant, is shining exceedingly. O Agni, you who have an excellent oblation, whom all men satisfy with homage while offering oblations, such as you are, worship with the oblation heaven and earth, which are very widely spread.

The brilliant Agni, mature in wisdom, has shone resplendently; offer worship to the wide-spread heaven and earth, you whom well-fed, the five races of men, bearing oblations, propitiate, with (sacrificial) food, as if you were a mortal guest.

"Yaddha": when indeed, together with "namasā", the oblation, near Agni, the sacred grass is "vṛñje": the root "vṛj" has the sense of cutting; it is cut, that is, it is brought. "Suvṛktiḥ": free from faults; "ghṛtavatī": full of ghee; the ladle is "ayāmi": it is held, it is placed on the sacred grass. Likewise, on the earth, "sadane", in the place, "sadma", the altar for the placing of the oblation, is "amyakṣi": the root "myakṣ" has the sense of going; it is reached, it is taken possession of. At that time the sacrifice is "aśrāyi": the sacrificer becomes its resting place. The illustration is "sūrye na cakṣuḥ": as the light that illumines unites in the sun, the impeller of all, so it is here.
- बर्हिः (*barhiḥ*)—the sacred grass, for the seat
- आयामि (*āyāmi*)—is placed on the sacred grass seat (and when)
- चक्षुः न (*cakṣuḥ na*)—as the light finds its support
- अश्रायि (*aśrāyi*)—finds its support in the sacrificer

When, together with the oblation, the sacred grass for the seat is cut near Agni, when the ladle, free from faults and full of ghee, is placed on the sacred grass seat, and when the sacrificial altar is taken up in the prepared place on the earth, then at once, as the light finds its support in the sun, the sacrifice finds its support in the sacrificer.

When the holy grass has been cut, (to be presented) to Agni, with the oblation, when the well-trimmed ladle, filled with butter, has been lifted up, then your receptacle (the alter) has been prepared on the surface of the earth, and the sacred rite is had recourse to as light (concentrates) in the sun.

"O Purvaṇīka, many-flamed, Hotṛ, invoker of the gods, Agni, being kindled, blazing, together with the shining gods, the fires that are his manifestations, give us riches ("rāyaḥ"): "daśasya" means "bestow". O son of strength, Agni, we, "vāvasānāḥ", clothing you with the oblation, "vṛjanaṃ na", as one passes an enemy, may pass beyond "aṃhaḥ", sin: "ati prasema" means may we go beyond, may we cross over." This is the meaning.⟨NOTE:256⟩
notes: ವಯಾಃ: the Kannada gloss gives ಪಕ್ಷಿಗಳು "birds", while Sāyaṇa's illustration speaks of branches (ಶಾಖಾ) of a tree

en: - होतः (*hotaḥ*)—who are of the form of the Hotṛ
- देवेभिः (*devebhiḥ*)—shining and being your special members
- सहसः सूनो (*sahasaḥ sūno*)—Agni, son of strength
- पावसानाः (*pāvasānāḥ*)—we who clothe you with the oblation
- अति प्रसेम (*ati prasema*)—may we cross over

O Agni, who have many flames and are of the form of the Hotṛ, kindled together with the other fires, which are shining and are special members of yours, give us riches. O Agni, son of strength, may we, who clothe you with the oblation, cross over sin as one crosses over an enemy.
Agni, many-rayed, invoker of the gods, blazing with brilliant fires bestow upon us riches; and may we, Son of strength clothing you with oblations, overcome iniquity (like) a foe.

"Hotā": the invoker of the gods; "barhiṣaḥ rāṭ": the lord of the sacrifice, Agni; "todasya": "tudyate" means he is afflicted by austerity, so "toda" is the sacrificer; in his house, "duroṇe", in the middle, he sits: this is the remainder to be supplied. For what purpose? "Rodasī", heaven and earth, "yajadhyai", to worship them. He, such as he is, "sahasaḥ sūnuḥ", son of strength, "ṛtāvā", true or possessed of the sacrifice, Agni, "sūryo na", like the sun, "dūrāt", from afar, "śociṣā", with his brilliance, "tatāna": spreads out, extends. This is the meaning: even though he is in a distant place, like the sun he illumines the whole world.
- होता (*hotā*)—of the form of the Hotṛ
- सूरो न (*sūro na*)—as the sun, though far away, pervades the whole world with its rays

Agni, of the form of the Hotṛ and lord of the sacrifice, is situated in the middle of the sacrificial house of the sacrificer, in order to worship heaven and earth. As the sun, though far away, pervades the whole world with its rays, so that same Agni, the truthful, the son of strength, spreads his brilliance widely from very far away and illumines the world.

Agni, the inovker of the gods, the lord of sacrifice, abides in the dwelling of the institutor of the rite, to offer sacrifice to heaven and earrh; he the Son of strength, the observer of truth, has overspread (the world) from afar, like the sun, with light.

"Dyauḥ" is the praiser; "sarvatāteva": the word "iva" is only a filler. "Sarvatātā" is a name of the sacrifice⟨NOTE:257⟩: it is the sacrifice being extended by all. Or else, "sarvatāti" is formed from the word "sarva" with a suffix that adds no meaning of its own; "sarvaḥ" is the praiser.

"O Yajatra, adorable one, "rājan", shining Agni, in you, "apāke", the wise, "su", exceedingly, "nu", quickly, "ā yakṣat": he offers, he pours the oblations. "Triṣadhasthaḥ": abiding together in the three worlds; or else abiding in a threefold manner in the forms of Gārhapatya and the rest. You, being such, "tatarūṣo na", like the one who crosses, the sun, "jaṃhaḥ": be a swift goer; "jaṃhaḥ" is a form of the root "han" in the sense of motion. Or else, from the root "tṝ" in the sense of floating and crossing, the form "tatarvān" arises, and its genitive is "tatarūṣaḥ"; so "may your speed be like that of the one who crosses, the sun". For what purpose? "Maghāni": praiseworthy, "mānuṣā": belonging to men, "havyā": oblations, "yajadhyai": in order to offer, to give to the gods.
notes: ಅಪಾಂ ನಪ್ರಾ printed; Sāyaṇa's Sanskrit has ಅಪಾಂ ನಪ್ತಾ

en: - यस्मिन् त्वे (*yasmin tve*)—in whom, in you
- त्रिषधस्थः (*triṣadhasthaḥ*)—you who pervade the three worlds, such as you are
- यजध्यै (*yajadhyai*)—to carry and distribute to the gods

O adorable and resplendent Agni, in you, the wise, to whom the praiser at the sacrifice offers the oblation exceedingly and quickly, you who pervade the three worlds, such as you are, be swift-going like the sun, in order to carry to the gods and distribute the oblations that are offered by men and are worthy of honour.

Adorable and resplendent Agni, to whom, mature in wisdom, the worshipper offers oblations at every sacred rite, you who are present in the three (worlds) move with the speed of the traverser (of the sky, the sun) to convey the valuable oblations of men (to the gods).

The "aratiḥ", the moving flame, of which Agni, being "tejiṣṭhā", most brilliant, shines in the forest ("vanerāṭ") in the form of a forest fire, growing ("vṛdhasānaḥ"): that Agni shines ("adyaut") on his own path, in the atmosphere, like "todaḥ", the sun, the impeller of all. Moreover, "adrogho na": one who is not to be harmed; or else, like Vāyu, who in the form of breath does no harm to any being; such an Agni, immortal, free from death, among the "oṣadhīṣu": "oṣa" is burning, and it is placed ("dhīyate") in them, so the "oṣadhis" are the forests. Among them, being swift-going ("dravitā") and "avatraḥ", not to be checked by anything, he "cetati", makes known, illumines the whole world by himself, by his own light alone.
- वनेराट् (*vanerāṭ*)—shines in the forest in the form of a forest fire (which)
- अध्वन्न (*adhvanna*)—as he shines in the atmosphere, his path of movement
- अमर्त्यः (*amartyaḥ*)—Agni, free from the nature of death

The flame of that Agni, spreading everywhere and having exceeding splendour, shines in the forest in the form of a forest fire; that Agni, who grows, shines like the sun that shines in his path of movement,
the atmosphere. And Agni, who like the wind is free from the nature of death, being swift in spreading among the plants, illumines the whole world with his own radiance.

He whose pure and spreading flame blazes in the forest, shines with increasing intensity, like the sun on his (celestial) path : rushing like the innocuous (wind) amongst the plants. immortal, unimpeded, he lights up (all things) by his own (lustre).

"Jātavedāḥ": one in whom wealth is born, or in whom knowledge is born. That Agni is praised by our praisers "etarī na": as praises that exist in a petitioner who goes to a patron are exceedingly pleasing, so he is praised, facing us, with "śūṣaiḥ", pleasing praises, in "dame", our sacrificial house. Moreover, "druvannaḥ": "dru" is a tree, and he whose food that is is so called. Therefore "vanvan", sharing in forests, "kratvā na", by his own action, he is also "arvā", a goer. The illustration is "usraḥ piteva": "pitā" is the protector and begetter of calves, the bull ("usraḥ"); as that goes swiftly for mating, so he. "Yajñaiḥ", by those who have sacrifices, the sacrificers, "jārayāyi": he is praised; this is the form of the root "jṝ" in the sense of praising.
- जातवेदाः (*jātavedāḥ*)—who is of the form of Jātavedas
- एतरि न (*etari na*)—like the excellent praises that are in a petitioner
- क्रत्वा न (*kratvā na*)—intent on his own work

Agni, who is of the form of Jātavedas, is praised exceedingly in the sacrificial house by us, who have composed pleasing hymns of praise like the excellent praises that are in a petitioner. Having trees as his food, a destroyer of forests, he becomes swift-going, intent on his own work like a bull. And, born from the sacrificers, he is praised.

Agni, who knows all that exists, is propitiated in our dwelling by our praises, like those gratifying (commendations which proceed) from one soliciting (a favour) : feeder upon trees, consumer of forests, impetuous in act as bull, the (progenitor of calves), he is glorified by the celebration of sacrifices.

On the word जारयायि (*jārayāyi*) Yāska has given the explanation उस्र इव गोपिताजायि यज्ञैः (*usra iva gopitājāyi yajñaiḥ*) (Ni. 6-15). जारयायि (*jārayāyi*) means अजायि (*ajāyi*), that is, he has been born. The intention is that, as a bull protects its herd of cows, so Agni has been born on this sacrificial ground in order to protect those who worship him for the sake of the sacrifice.

"Adha": in this world; "sma" is only a filler. "Asya", of this Agni, "bhāsaḥ", the rays, "panayanti": the praisers praise. When "vṛthā", without effort, "takṣat", paring away, that is, reducing the forests, burning them well, he follows ("anuyāti") the broad earth, the forest-land, then they praise: this is the construction. That Agni, "syandraḥ", flowing, "viṣitaḥ", released, free from restraint, therefore at once, quickly, becomes "dhavīyān", the swiftest goer. Like whom? "Ṛṇo na tāyuḥ": the root "ṛṇ" has the sense of motion, and "tāyu" is a name for a thief; as a thief is a swift goer, so this Agni, having passed over "dhanva", the desert land, shines ("rāṭ"). Or else "dhanva" is the atmosphere; having traversed the atmosphere greatly, he shines.
- ऋणो न तायुः (*ṛṇo na tāyuḥ*)—as a thief runs, having carried off wealth

When Agni, burning the forests completely without any effort, overruns the forest regions, all the people of this world praise the rays of Agni. That same Agni, quivering and unrestrained, spreads everywhere quickly, as a thief runs having carried off wealth. And, overrunning all the deserts, he shines exceedingly.

Th y glorify his flames in this world: when, easily thinning the woods, they spread over the earth: he, who glides along unarrested, and rapid in movement as a fast flying thief, shines over the desert.

"O Arvan, Agni, goer, you, being such, protect us from "nidāyāḥ", from a blameworthy progeny or from blame itself": this is the remainder to be supplied. Being what? "Viśvebhiḥ", with all the fires that are your branches, being kindled. And "rāyaḥ", riches, you "veṣi": you bring, you make go to us. Or else you "veṣi": you desire riches in the form of oblations. "Duccunā": the hostile armies that bring distress you "vi yāsi": you drive apart in various directions. And we, "suvīrāḥ", with fine sons and grandsons, for "śatahimāḥ", a hundred winters, that is, years, "madema": may we rejoice.

O swift-going Agni, you who possess the qualities described above, blazing together with all the fires that are your branches (the Āhavanīya, the Gārhapatya and the rest), save us from blame. And provide us with riches. Scatter the enemies who cause distress far away. May we, together with heroic sons, be in joy for a hundred years.

Quick-moving Agni, kindled with all (your) fires, (guard) us from reproach : you bestow riches, you scatter adversaries : may we, blessed with excellent male descendants, enjoy happiness for a hundred winters.

O Subhaga, Agni of good wealth, all riches go forth from you in many ways, since gold is the root of all riches and gold arose from Agni. For this he cites the śruti तस्य रेतः परापतत्तद्धिरण्यमभवत् (*tasya retaḥ parāpatattaddhiraṇyamabhavat*) (Tai. Brā. 1-1-3-8) **GLOSS**. An illustration of going forth: as branches go forth in many ways from a tree, so do riches from you. Likewise cattle and herds, here called riches, go swiftly out from you alone; he quotes पशवो वै रयिः पशूनेवावरुंध इति तैत्तिरीयकं (*paśavo vai rayiḥ paśūnevāvaruṃdha iti taittirīyakaṃ*) **GLOSS**. In the battle that destroys the Vṛtras, the enemies, the strength to conquer enemies comes from you. The rain that comes from heaven, from the atmosphere, also goes forth from you alone, because the oblation cast into Agni reaches the Sun, from the Sun rain is born, from rain food, and from that creatures; so the smṛti says अग्नौ प्रास्ताहुतिः सम्यगादित्यमुपतिष्ठते । आदित्याज्जायते वृष्टिर्वृष्टेरन्नं ततः प्रजा इति (*agnau prāstāhutiḥ samyagādityamupatiṣṭhate | ādityājjāyate vṛṣṭirvṛṣṭerannaṃ tataḥ prajā iti*) **GLOSS**. Therefore you, praised by all, are the one who sends the waters. ⟨NOTE:258⟩
notes: ಅಸ್ಸಾಮಪಾಮಾಪ್ತವ್ಯಾನಾಂ: reading doubtful; the Kannada gloss gives ಕರ್ಮಕರ್ತನೂ for ಅಪ್ಪಾಂ

en: - वनिनः न (*vaninaḥ na*)—as they go out from a tree
- रयिः (*rayiḥ*)—the wealth of cattle and the like
- श्रुष्टि (*śruṣṭi*)—that which is to be manifested from you
- वृत्रतूर्ये (*vṛtratūrye*)—in the battle that destroys Vṛtra
- वृष्टिः (*vṛṣṭiḥ*)—the rain (to be produced by your will alone)

O Agni, possessor of excellent wealth, as birds go out from a tree, so all riches also come forth from you alone. The wealth of cattle and the like, the strength needed for the battle that destroys Vṛtra, and the rain from the atmosphere are produced by your will alone. You, the impeller of the waters, are most worthy of praise.

Auspicious Agni, all good things proceed from you, like branches (from the trunk) of a tree, renowned riches, vigour for the destruction of foes, the rain of heaven : you are to be glorified, the sender of the waters.

O Agni, you who are to be worshipped (भगः (*bhagaḥ*)), bring to us (इषे (*iṣe*) is a form of the root meaning "to go", here "bring, bestow") pleasing riches. The word हि (*hi*) is merely a filler. You, of beautiful radiance, dwell everywhere, like the wind that goes all around. Or else, the root क्षयति (*kṣayati*) has the sense of lordship: you rule over all. O Agni, like Mitra, the protector from death, you are the giver of great water and of the sacrifice; here the root क्षदति (*kṣadati*) has the sense of giving. And, O shining Agni, you are the giver of abundant and desirable wealth: this is the carrying-on of the construction.
- मित्रो न (*mitro na*)—like the god Mitra
- क्षत्ता असि (*kṣattā asi*)—you are the giver
- वामस्य (*vāmasya*)—and attractive wealth (you are the giver)

O Agni, revered one, bestow upon us delightful wealth. You of attractive radiance dwell everywhere like the all-pervading wind. O Agni, like the god Mitra you are the giver of great water. O shining Agni, you are the giver of the most abundant and attractive wealth.

You are adorable; bestow upon us precious wealth : beautiful with radiance, you pass (around) like the circumambient (wind): you, divine Agni, are like Mitra, the giver of abundant water and ample wealth.

O Agni, that man who is the protector of the good kills with strength the Vṛtra, the obstructing enemy. And being wise, he carries off from the Paṇi, the trader and Asura, his food or strength, taking it away after separating it. O Agni, of excellent knowledge, born for the sacrifice (ṛta is a name of the sacrifice), you who are united with the lightning fire, the grandson of the waters, the son who is in the middle region, send that man, the one whom you impel for the sake of wealth, to slay: this is the construction. The third case in राया (*rāyā*) stands for the fourth.
- अपां नप्रा (*apāṃ naprā*)—with the lightning fire, the protector of the waters ⟨NOTE:259⟩
notes: ಅವೃತಃ: Sāyaṇa ರಕ್ತಪ್ರಭೃತಿಭಿರನಾಚ್ಛಾದಿತಂ "not covered by blood and the like"; the Kannada gloss gives ಅಸುರರಿಂದ ಅಪಹೃತವಾಗದೆ "not seized by the Asuras"

en: O Agni, of excellent knowledge and born for the sacrifice, you unite with the lightning fire, the protector of the waters, and impel a sacrificer for the sake of wealth. That same sacrificer, the protector of the good, kills with his strength the enemy who attacks him. Being wise, he carries off the food of the Asura.

That man, the protector of the virtuous, destroys, Agni, his enemy by his strength, and baffles, intelligent, the might of (the Asura) Pani, whom you, the wise, the parent of sacrifice, consentient with the grandson of the waters, encourage (in the hope) of riches.

O Agni, son of strength, the mortal, the sacrificer, who by praises (गीर्भिः (*gīrbhiḥ*)), by recitations (उक्थैः (*ukthaiḥ*), that is, śastras), by sacrifices (that is, the sacrificer's means, the oblations) brings (आनट् (*ānaṭ*) means causes to reach) your sharpness to the altar, the sacrificial ground, that mortal, O shining Agni, holds everything sufficient and grain too (वा (*vā*) has the sense of "and"), and is united with riches (वसवैः (*vasavaiḥ*)).
- सहसः सूनो (*sahasaḥ sūno*)—O son of strength
- यज्ञैः (*yajñaiḥ*)—by oblations, the means of sacrifice

O Agni, son of strength and divine in nature, the man who brings your sharp radiance to the sacrificial ground by praises, by recitations and by oblations, the means of sacrifice, obtains all satisfying grain and is united with riches.
The mortal who by praise, by prayers, by sacrifices, attracts, Son of strength, your heightened (radiance) to the altar, enjoys all-sufficiency and corn, and abounds in wealth.

O Agni, son of strength, bring from the enemy folk those riches, rich in excellent sons (सुवीरा (*suvīrā*)) and in good food (सौश्रवसा (*sauśravasā*)), and place them in us. For what purpose? For our nourishment. Or else: place them in us, the leaders of praises, and give them directly to us. You, joined with strength, make that abundant sustenance from cattle, such as curds, for the enemy who does not give and who harasses; bring that food, and give it to us. This is the meaning.
- सहसः सूनो (*sahasaḥ sūno*)—O son of strength
- सुवीरा (*suvīrā*)—that which is accompanied by excellent sons
- शवसा (*śavasā*)—you who are joined with strength
- पश्वः (*paśvaḥ*)—that which comes from cattle, in the form of milk and the like
- वृकाय (*vṛkāya*)—for the one who does not give
- कृणोषि (*kṛṇoṣi*)—you produce (prepare that food for us alone)

O Agni, son of strength, fill in for us, your praisers, the renowned wealth that is accompanied by excellent sons and has excellent food. The abundant food from cattle, in the form of milk and the like, which you, joined with strength, produce for the enemy who does not give and who is harmful, prepare that food for us alone.

Grant, Son of strength, to men (who praise you), those abundant viands and excellent descendants, (that may contribute) to their prosperity: grant also that copious sustenance from cattle, which by your strength you take away from a churlish and malignant adversary.

O Agni, son of strength, विहायाः (*vihāyāḥ*) is a name meaning "great": you, the great one, be for us a speaker, a giver of counsel for our good. And give us a son, a grandson, and food. I, the praiser, with all praises that have you as their subject, would attain the fulfilment of my desires.
- सहसः सूनो (*sahasaḥ sūno*)—O son of strength
- वद्या (*vadyā*)—be a counsellor for our good

O Agni, son of strength, you, the great one, be our counsellor for our good. Give us a son, a grandson and food. By means of all praises may I obtain the fulfilment of my desires. Accompanied by excellent sons, may we be in joy for a hundred years.

Agni, Son of strength, you are mighty, be our councillor : give us sons and grandsons, together with food : may I, by all my praises, obtain the fulfilment of my desires: may we, blessed with excellent male descendants, enjoy happiness for a hundred winters

The mortal, the man, who offers service to Agni and the rite of sacrifice and the like, together with praises, that mortal, becoming foremost among the earlier ones, quickly shines forth; that is, he becomes possessed of excellent radiance. For the protection of sons and the rest he also obtains food; that is, he receives it from the enemy.
- धियं (*dhiyaṃ*)—the rite of sacrifice and the like
- अवसे (*avase*)—for the protection of sons and the rest

The man who performs worship directed to Agni, and the rite of sacrifice and the like, together with praises, that same man, foremost of all, quickly shines. He obtains food for the protection of his sons and the rest.
May the mortal who propitiates Agni by devotion and worship, together with praises, quickiy become distinguished as first (amongst men), and acquire ample food for the support (of his children).

Agni alone is of excellent knowledge; no one else is. Since this is so, he is the greatest maker, the supreme performer of rites such as the carrying of oblations, and he is a seer, the beholder of all. The people (विशः (*viśaḥ*)) of the man, the sacrificer, that is, those who are the priests, praise at the sacrifices such an Agni, the invoker of the gods.
- ऋषिः (*ṛṣiḥ*)—one who has the power to see everything
- मनुष्य (*manuṣya*)—belonging to the sacrificer, the man
- होतारं (*hotāraṃ*)—who invites the gods to the sacrifice

Agni alone is possessed of excellent knowledge, and for that very reason he is the best performer of rites and has the power to see everything. All the people belonging to the man who is the sacrificer praise at the sacrifices Agni, who invites the gods to the sacrifice.
Agni verily is most wise ; he is the chief performer of religious rites a holy sage : the progeny of men glorify Agni as the invoker of the gods at sacrifices.

O Agni, the riches of the enemy, separated in many ways from the enemy's side, contend for the protection of those who have arisen from you; each says, "I alone shall protect, I alone shall protect." The men, the praisers, harassing the dasyu, the enemy who wastes away others, by rites addressed to you, wish to endure and overcome the man who is without rites, who opposes the rites.
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—the riches that have been seized
- स्पर्धंते (*spardhaṃte*)—contend in the protection of the sacrificer

O Agni, riches that have been seized in many ways contend in the protection of the sacrificer, each saying "I, I", in order to protect your praiser. The men who are your praisers, harassing the harmful enemy, become able by rites such as sacrifice to face the one fallen from rites.
The manifold treasures of the enemy (detached from them) are emulous, Agni, for the presrvation (of your worshippers) : men who worship
you, triumphing over the spoiler, seek to shame him who celebrates no sacred rite by (their) observances.

This Agni gives a heroic son; he bestows him on the praisers. What kind of son? One who is the sharer in the rites that are to be attained, who overcomes and endures the enemies (ऋतीषहं (*ṛtīṣahaṃ*)), who is the protector of the rites of the good. At the sight of that hero, through fear of his strength, the enemies tremble and are shaken. This is the construction. ⟨NOTE:260⟩
notes: ದ್ವೇಷ್ಟವಾನ್: reading doubtful in the bhāṣya

en: - सं चक्षि (*saṃ cakṣi*)—at the mere sight
- त्रसंति (*trasaṃti*)—tremble and run away (such a one)

Agni gives to the praiser a heroic son, a performer of rites, a defeater of enemies and a protector of the good, at the mere sight of whom, through fear of his strength, all enemies tremble and run away.

Agni bestows (upon his worshippers) a male descendant, (the performer of good) works, the subduer of foes, the protector of the virtuous, at whose appearance his enemies tremble through fear of his prowess.

सहावा (*sahāvā*): sahas is strength; the divine Agni who has it, endowed with qualities such as generosity and joined with knowledge, protects that mortal, the sacrificer, from the reviler. The word हि (*hi*) is a filler. The mortal whose wealth, in the form of the oblation, is not covered by blood and the like, and at the sacrifices is not shared by other sacrificers, that sacrificer who has the oblation he protects. This is the construction. ⟨NOTE:261⟩
notes: ನಾ ವಸ್ತ್ರಂ: reading unclear in the bhāṣya

en: - अवृतः (*avṛtaḥ*)—is not obtained by other sacrificers (such)
- देवः (*devaḥ*)—who is endowed with generosity and other qualities

The sacrificer whose wealth is not seized by the Asuras and is not obtained at the sacrifice by other sacrificers, such a sacrificer Agni, who is mighty and endowed with generosity and other qualities, protects from reviler, being joined with knowledge.
The mighty and divine Agni, endowed with knowledge, protects the mortal from reproach whose rich (offerings) are unobstructed (by evil spirits), and unshared by other (offerers) at sacrifices.

Sāyaṇa says that this Ṛk has been explained already, and gives the meaning of its words. O Agni of favourable radiance, endowed with generosity and other qualities, you who have gone to heaven and earth, speak our good praise to the gods who are to be worshipped. Cause us who are the praisers to reach a good dwelling that does not perish. And through your favour may we overcome the haters, sins, their fruits and the hard-to-cross things; and may we overcome those which were done in other births, and the things that stand between. By your protection may we overcome them completely. ⟨NOTE:262⟩
notes: ಸುಧಿತಂ glossed ಸುಪ್ತನಾಗಿದ್ದವನೂ "who lay dormant"; Sāyaṇa has ಸುಷ್ಟು ನಿಹಿತಂ "well placed"

en: - रोदस्योः (*rodasyoḥ*)—in all heaven and earth (you who pervade them)
- सुक्षितिं (*sukṣitiṃ*)—that which is accompanied by excellent homes
- स्वस्तिं (*svastiṃ*)—with welfare that does not perish
- ता (*tā*)—and the impressions of sin from other births
- तरेम (*tarema*)—may we cross all that sorrow

O Agni of favourable radiance and divine in nature, you who pervade all heaven and earth, face the gods and recite and offer our praises. Unite us, the composers and reciters of praises, with welfare that is accompanied by excellent homes and the like and does not perish. May we cross our enemies, our sins and the painful fruits of sin. O Agni, joined with your protection, may we cross all those sorrows.

Divine Agni, revered as a freind, who, abiding in heaven and earth communicates our praise to the gods, conduct the offerer of adoration to domestic felicity, and may we overcome our adversaries, our difficulties : may we overcome them by your protection.

O seer Vītahavya Bharadvāja, you worship this very Agni with praise; that is, you prepare him well. Yāska is cited for the root: यंजतिः प्रसाधनकर्मेति यास्कः (*yaṃjatiḥ prasādhanakarmeti yāskaḥ*) **GLOSS**. What kind of Agni? A guest, one who goes constantly; or else, one to be honoured like a guest; one who is awake at dawn; the lord and protector of all the peoples. Pure by birth, of himself, Agni comes at some time of the sacrifice from the heavenly world; at that time prepare him. This is the construction. Thus prepared, Agni, who lies as an embryo between the two kindling sticks, or else, who is the embryo of heaven and earth, eats for a long time that oblation which does not fail, milk and the like, the constant means of the Agnihotra and the other rites. ⟨NOTE:263⟩
notes: ಸಾಯಣಭಾಷ್ಯ: ದೀಪ್ತೇರ್ನಿವಾಸಭೂತಂ ಮುಕ್ಷಂ । ತಾದೃಶವಾಕ್ಯೋಪೇಶಮರತಿಮರ್ಯಂ damaged; construction of ದ್ಯುಕ್ಷವಚಸಂ and ಅರತಿಂ unclear

en: - अतिथिः (*atithiḥ*)—to be honoured like a guest
- गर्भः (*garbhaḥ*)—Agni who is as an embryo in the kindling stick

O seer, Agni, pure by nature and by birth, comes from the heavenly world at the time of sacrifice. Worship exceedingly with praise this very Agni, who is to be honoured like a guest, who awakes at dawn and who is the protector of all the peoples. Agni, who is as an embryo in the kindling stick, accepts and eats for a long time the oblation that does not perish.

Propitiate by praises this guest who wakes at dawn, the cherisher of all people, who on every occasion descends, pure cf origin, from heaven, and, present as the embryo (in the wood of attrition), consumes immediately the offered (oblation).

वः (*vaḥ*)—त्वं (*tvaṃ*). In place of the word "you" (singular), the accusative plural form वः (*vaḥ*) of the pronoun *yuṣmad* is used. Such interchange of case and number occurs in many places in the Ṛgveda.

यंजतिः प्रसाधनकर्मा (*yaṃjatiḥ prasādhanakarmā*). Yāska says that the word *yañjati* is used in the sense "gratify, worship", and as an example he gives the Vedic sentence आ व यंजसे ऊर्जां व्युष्टिषु इत्यपि निगमो भवति (*ā va yaṃjase ūrjāṃ vyuṣṭiṣu ityapi nigamo bhavati*) **GLOSS**

अतिथिं (*atithiṃ*)—It is usual to praise Agni as a guest, to be honoured with worship. When Yāska gives the derivation of this word, he cites the Ṛk जुष्टो दमूना अतिथिर्दुरोण इमं नो यज्ञमुप याहि विद्वान् । (*juṣṭo damūnā atithirduroṇa imaṃ no yajñamupa yāhi vidvān |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-4-7) **GLOSS** and then says अतिथिरभ्यतितो गृहान् भवति अभ्येति तिथिषु परकुलानीति वा परगृहाणीति वा आयमपीतरो अतिथिरेतस्मादेव (*atithirabhyatito gṛhān bhavati abhyeti tithiṣu parakulānīti vā paragṛhāṇīti vā āyamapītaro atithiretasmādeva*) (Ni. 4-4). A guest (*atithi*) means one who goes to another's house suddenly, without sending previous notice; or, since there is no restriction that he must come on such and such a day (*a* + *tithi*), one who comes without any rule of date. Durgācārya has explained this word thus: because this one (the guest) comes seeking houses, he is called a guest; or he comes and joins the houses of those who perform sacrifices on the lunar days (*tithi*) such as the full moon. This meaning applies especially to Agni.

गर्भः (*garbhaḥ*)—अरण्योर्मध्यॆ गर्भवद्वर्तमानः । यद्वा । द्यावापृथिव्योर्गर्भभूतः । (*araṇyormadhyè garbhavadvartamānaḥ | yadvā | dyāvāpṛthivyorgarbhabhūtaḥ |*) Since Agni is produced by rubbing the pieces of wood called the *araṇis*, the meaning is that before his production Agni lies hidden in the *araṇis* in the form of an embryo. Or else it can be said that he is established between heaven and earth, on the sacrificial ground, in the fire-pits such as the Āhavanīya.

Agni is placed well in the wood, that is, in the kindling sticks. He is to be praised, and his splendour rises upward. The Bhṛgus, the great seers, set him in their house as one sets a friend. Sāyaṇa addresses him: O wonderful, great Agni, being such, be well pleased with the seer named Vītahavya, since day after day you are honoured with excellent praises. If the seer is Bharadvāja, then "to Vītahavya" is to be construed as "to Bharadvāja, who has given the oblation".
- वीतहव्ये (*vītahavye*)—in respect of the seer named Vītahavya
notes: ಋಗ್ವೇ. ೧-೬೧-೧೫ abbreviation ಋಗ್ವೇ. not in the list

en: O Agni, of mighty form, you who lay dormant in the kindling stick, who are to be praised, whose splendour spreads high upward, whom the great seers, the Bhṛgus, established like a friend: such as you are, be gracious to the seer named
Vītahavya. Therefore you are worshipped every day with excellent praises.
Wonderful Agni, whom, adorable and upward flaming, the Bhrigus regard as a friend, deposited in the wood of (attrition), be pleased with Vitahavya, since you are glorified by (his) praise every day.

वनस्पत् सुधितं (*vanaspat sudhitaṃ*)—*Vanaspati* means a large tree. Here it is the pieces of wood, products of a tree. These are called *araṇis*. There are two of these *araṇis*: one is large and broad, below. On it another piece of wood, like a stick, is placed, and by rubbing, they produce Agni. This is the second piece of wood. Therefore the main idea is that Agni stays hidden in this piece of wood called the *araṇi*, and that after the rubbing he appears so that all can see him.

भृगवः (*bhṛgavaḥ*)—For this word Yāska has given the derivation अर्चिषि भृगुः संबभूव । भृगुर्भृज्यमानो न देहे (*arciṣi bhṛguḥ saṃbabhūva | bhṛgurbhṛjyamāno na dehe*) (Ni. 3-17). That is, the great seer named Bhṛgu was born in the flames of Agni. Though he was burnt by the flames, no harm came to his body. In this matter Durgācārya, the commentator on the Nirukta, says प्रजापतिना किल शुक्रमात्मीयवादाय अग्नौ हुतं । ततः अर्चिषि ज्वालायां भृगुर्नाम महर्षिः संबभूव (*prajāpatinā kila śukramātmīyavādāya agnau hutaṃ | tataḥ arciṣi jvālāyāṃ bhṛgurnāma maharṣiḥ saṃbabhūva*). That is, formerly Prajāpati took his seed and offered it as an oblation in Agni. Then a flame of Agni arose from it, and in it the seer Bhṛgu was born. Because he was not burnt by the flame of Agni, he came to be called Bhṛgu.

वीतहव्य (*vītahavya*)—Vītahavya is the seer who saw this sūkta. The meaning of this word is दत्तहविष्टे (*dattahaviṣṭe*), that is, one who has offered oblation in Agni. It has been said before that the seer who saw this sūkta is Vītahavya or Bharadvāja. Since the meanings of the words Vītahavya and Bharadvāja are more or less alike, it is doubtful whether these two are one person or different persons. Both were born in the Āṅgirasa line. For the word Bharadvāja Yāska says भरणाद्भरद्वाजः (*bharaṇādbharadvājaḥ*) (Ni. 3-17), meaning one who stands holding oblations and the like in order to offer them to Agni. Sāyaṇa makes this meaning clear in the next Ṛk by the words भरद्वाजाय (*bharadvājāya*) संभृतहनिर्लक्षणान्नाय (*saṃbhṛtahanirlakṣaṇānnāya*). In the present Ṛk either meaning may be taken.

Sāyaṇa addresses Agni: such as you are, free from any harm, you become the increaser of the one who is able to carry out the rite. Likewise you become the one who carries across, safe from the enemy who is far away and from the enemy who is near. For this reason, O son of strength, you who are extended on every side, give among mortals riches and a house to Bharadvāja, who has gathered the oblation of food. Or "to Vītahavya" is to be construed with Bharadvāja, meaning one by whom the oblation has been made to go to the gods. The repetition "extended" is for respect.
- दक्षस्य (*dakṣasya*)—of the master of sacrifice who has the power to perform rites
- अंतरस्य (*aṃtarasya*)—from the enemy who is near
- तरुषः (*taruṣaḥ*)—be the one who carries us across
- सहसः सूनो (*sahasaḥ sūno*)—O Agni, son of strength
- सप्रथः (*saprathaḥ*)—you who are greater than all
- भरद्वाजाय (*bharadvājāya*)—who has gathered and set down oblation

O Agni, you of unobstructed power have become the increaser of the master of sacrifice who has the power to perform rites. Carry us across the enemy who is far away and the enemy who is near. O Agni, son of strength, you who are greater than all, give riches and a house to Bharadvāja, who is ready to gather oblation in abundance and offer it among men.

Agni, you, who are unresisted, become the benefactor of him who is skilled (in sacred rites), his defender against a near or distant enemy : Son of strength, who are ever renowned, grant wealth and a dwelling to Vitahavya, the offerer of the oblation.

Sāyaṇa addresses Vītahavya: with beautiful praises, adorn, that is, gratify, the god Agni, the bearer of oblations. Of what kind is he? Shining; worthy of honour like a guest for you; the leader to heaven; the invoker of the gods in the sacrifice of Manu, that is, of Prajāpati; the one of good sacrifice; like a wise sage, a learned man. The next phrase, in which he explains the dwelling of brilliance and a certain speech, is damaged in the supplied text, but he closes by calling Agni the lord, who is free from the reproach of the unworthy. ⟨NOTE:265⟩
notes: ಸಾ. ಭಾ. abbreviation not in the list; Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya read as Sā. Bhā.

en: - अतिथिं (*atithiṃ*)—worthy of honour like a guest
- विप्रं न (*vipraṃ na*)—like a wise praiser

O Vītahavya, adorn with excellent praises Agni, who is radiant, worthy of honour for you like a guest, who takes one to heaven, who is the Hotṛ in the sacrifice of Manu, the excellent performer of sacrifice, who has radiant speech like a wise praiser, who is worthy of worship, who carries the oblation and is divine in nature. (praise him)

Propitiate with pious praises the radiant Agni, your guest, the guide to heaven, the invoker of the gods (at the sacrifice) of Manu, the celebrator of holy rites, the speaker of brilliant words like a learned sage, the bearer of oblations (to the gods), the lord, the divine.

Agni shines on the earth with a flame that purifies and makes aware, as the dawns shine with their light. Further, like a man slaying enemies in battle, he blazes quickly in the fight of the seer named Etaśa with the Sun, to help him. Sāyaṇa cites another Vedic text for this, प्रतशं सूर्ये पस्पृधानं (*prataśaṃ sūrye paspṛdhānaṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-61-15) ⟨NOTE:266⟩. He adds that surely all the gods gave him help. And the god who, being thirsty, is by his power all-devouring and free from old age: that god is to be worshipped. This is the connection with the previous Ṛk.
notes: ಜಾತವೇದಸ್ಯನಿವಿದ್ವಾ ನಾರ್ಥಃ damaged; construction unclear

en: - उषसो न (*uṣaso na*)—as the dawn shines
- ततृषाणः (*tatṛṣāṇaḥ*)—who is of a nature to devour everything
- अजरः (*ajaraḥ*)—who is without decay, praise such an Agni

Praise that Agni who shines on the earth with a purifying and life-giving radiance as the dawn shines with its lustre; who, as a hero presses forward in battle, shines quickly in the battlefield of Etaśa to help Etaśa; who is of a nature to devour everything and is free from old age.

(Propitiate him) who shines upon the earth with purifying and enlightening lustre, as the dawns with light; him, who like (a warrior) discomfiting (his foes) quickly blazed forth in the contest in defence of Etasha ; him, who is satiated (with food), exempt from decay.

एतशस्य (*etaśasya*)—The word एतश (*etaśa*) has two meanings. The Sun's horse is called एतश (*etaśa*); and there is also a seer named Etaśa. In the present Ṛk the meaning is "in the battle fought with the seer named Etaśa". This matter is also touched on in the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-61-15 and Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-121-13. In explaining it, the commentator tells an old story: स्वश्वनामा कश्चिद्राजा । स च पुत्रार्थं सूर्यमुपास्ते । स च सूर्यः पुत्ररूपेण स्वयमेव तत्रोत्पन्नः सन् एतशाख्येन महर्षिणा सार्धं युद्धं चकार । तदानीं स ऋषिः युद्धे जयार्थमिंद्रं तुष्टाव । स इंद्रः तेन सूयमानः सन् स्वश्वपुत्रस्य सूर्यस्य संबंधिनः संग्रामात् एनमपाल यदिति ॥ (*svaśvanāmā kaścidrājā | sa ca putrārthaṃ sūryamupāste | sa ca sūryaḥ putrarūpeṇa svayameva tatrotpannaḥ san etaśākhyena maharṣiṇā sārdhaṃ yuddhaṃ cakāra | tadānīṃ sa ṛṣiḥ yuddhe jayārthamiṃdraṃ tuṣṭāva | sa iṃdraḥ tena sūyamānaḥ san svaśvaputrasya sūryasya saṃbaṃdhinaḥ saṃgrāmāt enamapāla yaditi ‖*) (Sā. Bhā. 1-61-15) ⟨NOTE:267⟩. In ancient times there was a king named Svaśva. He worshipped the Sun in order to have a son. Then the Sun himself was born as his son. While this son was fighting with the seer called Etaśa, that seer praised Indra so that victory in the battle might fall to him. Then Indra, pleased with his praise, protected the seer Etaśa in the battle connected with Svaśva's son. This is what is suggested here. But in the present Ṛk it is said that Agni shone to help this seer Etaśa. In many places in the Ṛgveda the qualities of Indra are attributed to Agni and he is praised in the many heroic deeds of Indra, such as the slaying of Vṛtra. This too may be called one example of such occasions.
notes: ಸೌಮಿ ! and ಪುರಸ್ಕರೋಮಾತಿ ಶೇಷಃ damaged in the print

en: Sāyaṇa addresses our praisers: worship with fuel, or with kindlings, Agni, Agni alone and no other god, who is exceedingly dear to you, honoured like a guest, and fit to be praised. Or else the word meaning "fit to be praised" is taken as a locative: Agni, who stands as the object in the praise. Further, approach the immortal Agni, who never dies, with praises, and serve him. For among the gods the god Agni, who has the quality of giving and the like, accepts what is choice, such as the fuel; and since among the gods the god Agni accepts our service, therefore serve him. This is the construction.
- अतिथिं (*atithiṃ*)—who is honoured like a guest
- गृणीषणि (*gṛṇīṣaṇi*)—who is exceedingly worthy of praise
- देवः (*devaḥ*)—Agni, who is worthy of worship
- देवः (*devaḥ*)—Agni, who is worthy of worship
- अमृतं (*amṛtaṃ*)—Agni, who is free from mortality

O praisers, worship with fuel and the like that very Agni who is exceedingly dear, honoured by you like a guest and exceedingly worthy of praise. For the reason that Agni, worthy of worship among the gods, accepts with regard the fuel he desires and our services, for that very reason approach the immortal Agni and serve him with praises.
Worship repeatedly the adorable Agni with fuel; (him) who is ever your dear friend, your guest: approach the immortal Agni with praises, for he. a god among gods, accepts our homage.

On the tenth day, in the Āgnimāruta, the three Ṛks beginning समिद्धं (*samiddhaṃ*) serve for the nivid-type of Jātavedas ⟨NOTE:268⟩; and it is laid down in the sūtra (Ā. Sū. 8-12) with the Ṛk beginning "samiddham agnim" and the three Ṛks. Sāyaṇa explains: I praise the well-kindled Agni with the praise that is the cause of kindling. Or else "with fuel" is taken as "with logs, well kindled". Further, that pure Agni, who is himself clean, the purifier of all and firm, immovable, we place before us in the sacrifice, this being the word to be supplied ⟨NOTE:269⟩.

Likewise the wise one, the invoker of the gods, who is much chosen, that is, to be praised by many; who injures none, that is, is favourable to all; the seer, who sees beyond; Jātavedas, who knows all that is born: that Agni we approach with pleasure-giving praises. Or else the third case stands in the sense of the second, and the meaning is: we ask for riches.
notes: ಸ್ಮೃತ್ಯೇತತ್ಪಾದಪೂರಣಂ printed; ಸ್ಮೃತ್ಯ read as the particle
ಕ್ರಿಯಾಗ್ರಹಣಂ ಕರ್ತವ್ಯಮಿತಿ ಕರ್ಮಣಃ ಸಂಪ್ರದಾನತ್ವಾಚ್ಚತುರ್ಥೀ । ಕವಿಂ ತ್ವಾಂ ಧೀತಿಮಾನಟ್ ಪ್ರಾಪಯತಿ read doubtfully

en: I praise with praises the Agni who is kindled with fuel. I worship in the sacrifice the Agni who is pure of himself, who purifies others and is firm. We praise with pleasure-giving praises the Agni who is wise, the Hotṛ, desired by many, free from injury, far-seeing and all-knowing.

I glorify with praise the kindled Agni, pure, purifying, permanent, (placed) before (us) at the sacrifice : let us celebrate with pleasant (hymns) the wise Agni, the invoker of the gods, the adored of many, the benevolent the far-seeing, him who knows all that exists.

On the tenth day of the sacrifice, at the time of reciting the mantras of the Agnimāruta-śastra, the three Ṛks 7-9 of this sūkta beginning समिद्धमग्निं (*samiddhamagniṃ*) are to be used for the nivid-type sūkta mantras that praise Agni called Jātavedas. This is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra समिद्धमग्निं समिधा गिरा गृण इति तृचश्च (*samiddhamagniṃ samidhā girā gṛṇa iti tṛcaśca*) (Ā. Sū. 8-12).

Sāyaṇa addresses Agni: gods and mortal men have made you their messenger. Of what kind are you? Immortal; in every age, that is, at the time of each sacrifice, the bearer of oblations; the protector; the one to be praised. Further, both these kinds of beings approach with obeisance, or with the food that is the oblation, that Agni who is ever awake, all-pervading, the protector of the peoples.

O Agni, you who are free from mortality, in every age the gods and men have obtained you as messenger. And they approached with obeisances and worshipped the Agni who bears the oblation, protects, is to be praised, is awake, all-pervading and the protector of the peoples.

You, Agni, have gods and men in every age retained as their messenger, immortal bearer of oblations, beneficent, adorable : they have placed him with reverence (upon the altar), vigilant, prevading, the protecter of mankind,

O Agni, you adorn both kinds, gods and men, in a special way. Following the rites, that is, in the sacrifices, you go about as the messenger of the gods between the two worlds, heaven and earth: you go to the world of heaven to bring the gods, and to this world to bring the oblations. Further, since we choose for you the rite and the beautiful praise, that is, we offer them, for this reason, O you of the three places, be kind to us, that is, give us happiness. The word *sma* serves to fill out the verse-quarter ⟨NOTE:270⟩.
notes: ಹವಿಷೋ ನಾ ನಿಶಿತಂ ವಾ, ವೋದಿತಿಮುದ್ದಮನಂ damaged

en: - उभयान् (*ubhayān*)—all the gods, men and the rest
- त्रिवरूथः (*trivarūthaḥ*)—you who are in the three places beginning with the earth

O Agni, favouring all the gods, men and the rest, being in all rites the messenger of the gods, you always move about pervading all of heaven and earth. For the reason that we offer to you the rite and the excellent praise, for that very reason, you who are in the three places beginning with the earth, be kind to us.

Showing grace, Agni, to both (gods and men), and at each sacred rite the messenger of the gods, you traverse earth and heaven : inasmuch as we offer you worship and praise, therefore you, who are the guardian of the three (regions), be auspicious to us.

रजसी समियसे (*rajasī samiyase*)—द्यावापृथिव्य संचरसि । देवानानेतुं द्युलोकं गच्छसि हवींषि च नेतुमिमं—लोकं । (*dyāvāpṛthivya saṃcarasi | devānānetuṃ dyulokaṃ gacchasi havīṃṣi ca netumimaṃ—lokaṃ |*) The praise here says that you move about in the world of heaven and in the world of earth. The meaning is: since Agni is the messenger who carries the oblations to the gods, he goes to the world of heaven to bring the gods to the sacrificial ground in the sacrifices that human sacrificers perform on earth, and to the earth to receive the oblations that are offered in Agni in the sacrifice for the gods.

त्रिवरूथः (*trivarūthaḥ*)—One who is in three places. That is, it is customary to describe Agni as being in three places, because he is in heaven in the form of the Sun, in the atmosphere in the form of lightning, and on earth in the form of the earthly fire, the sacrificial fire or the common fire.

In the Prātaranuvāka and in the two Aśvina-śastras, in the Āgneya rite, in the Triṣṭubh metre, the six Ṛks beginning तं सुप्रतीकमिति षट् (*taṃ supratīkamiti ṣaṭ*) are used, and this is laid down in the sūtra (Ā. Sū. 4-13). Sāyaṇa explains: we who have no knowledge, of little understanding, serve that Agni who is wiser, that is, all-knowing, who has a fair body, who sees well, who goes well. Further, may such an Agni worship the gods. May Agni, who knows all that is to be known, announce our oblation among the immortal gods, that is, those free from death, saying: the oblation has been prepared for you, therefore come.
- अमृतेषु (*amṛteṣu*)—among the gods, who are free from mortality

We, of little knowledge, worship Agni who is exceedingly wise, who has an excellent body, a good form and an excellent gait. May that same Agni worship the gods. May Agni, who has all knowledge, proclaim our oblation among the gods, who are free from mortality.

We of little wisdom adore the most wise Agni, the well-formed, the well-looking, the graceful-moving : may Agni, who knows all things that are to be known, offer the sacrifice : may he announce the oblation to the immortals.

At the time of reciting the Prātaranuvāka mantra, the six Ṛks of this sūkta beginning तं सुप्रतीकं (*taṃ supratīkaṃ*) have their use for the mantras in the Triṣṭubh metre connected with the Āgneya rite, as is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra तं सुप्रतीकमिति षट् (*taṃ supratīkamiti ṣaṭ*) (Ā. Sū. 4-13).

O Agni, that man you protect, and you fill him with his desires, who attains for you, the hero, the one who sees beyond, the rite or the praise. Or else, because the rite is the one to whom something is given, the fourth case is used; and the construction is that the rite leads you, the seer, to the sacrifice, and that man you protect ⟨NOTE:271⟩. Further, whoever attains the sacrifice, or the preparation of the oblation which is its means, or the offering that follows it, that same man you fill with strength, and you fill him with wealth ⟨NOTE:272⟩.
notes: ಶಿಸ್ತ್ರಃ printed here; the bhāṣya has ತಿಸ್ತ್ರಃ
ಐ. ಬ್ರಾ. ೫-೨ printed here; the bhāṣya cites ಐ. ಬ್ರಾ. ೧-೨೮ for the passage beginning ಕುಲಾಯಮಿವ

en: - पिपर्षि (*piparṣi*)—you satisfy with the things he desires
- यज्ञस्य (*yajñasya*)—of the sacrifice, or of the oblations
- उदितिं (*uditiṃ*)—the offering that is accompanied by purification, whoever undertakes it

O Agni, endowed with valour, the man who offers praise to you, who see beyond, that man you protect, and you satisfy him with the things he desires. Whoever undertakes the preparation of the sacrifice or of the oblations, or the offering accompanied by purification, that very man you fill with strength and with wealth.

You cherish, you protect, Agni, that man who offers worship, hero, to you, the far-seeing : you reward with strength and with riches him (who undertakes) the insititution, (who effects) the accomplishment, of the sacrifice.

O Agni, protect us thoroughly from the violent enemy. O mighty Agni, you yourself protect us from sin. May the food, the oblation given by us, free from fault, come to you well. May the desirable wealth, in thousands, given by you, come to us well.
- पाथः (*pāthaḥ*)—food in the form of the oblation
- सं (*saṃ*)—may it come and join us from you

O Agni, protect us thoroughly from the violent enemy. O mighty Agni, you yourself save us from sins. May the food, free from fault and in the form of the oblation, come and join you. May the wealth, worthy of esteem and in thousands, come to us from you.
Protect us, Agni, from the malignant, preserve us, mighty one, from wickedness : may the offering come to you free from defects ; may desirable riches, by thousands, (reach us).

On the fifth day of the Vyūḍha daśarāṭra, at the Āgnimāruta recitation, the three Ṛks beginning अग्निर्होता (*agnirhotā*) are the nivid-type verses concerning Jātavedas; he cites the sūtra "Agni is the invoker, the lord of the house, he is king: the three" (Ā. 8-8). At the Patnīsaṃyāja offerings it is the first anuvākyā verse of Gṛhapati; the sūtra is cited with its continuation (Ā. 1-10). It is also the pratipad of the Āśvina śastra; the sūtra is cited (Ā. 6-5). Sāyaṇa explains: the hotā is the caller of the gods, the rājā is the shining one; that Agni is the lord of the houses, their master. He, Jātavedas, endowed with knowledge from birth, knows all beings that have births. Among the gods, Indra and the others, and also among mortals, that Agni is the greatest sacrificer, and he is ṛtāvā, possessed of truth or of the sacrifice. May that Agni worship the gods excellently.
- गृहपतिः (*gṛhapatiḥ*)—is the master of all houses
- जातवेदाः (*jātavedāḥ*)—Agni, endowed with knowledge from birth
- देवानां (*devānāṃ*)—to the gods, Indra and the others
- यजिष्ठः (*yajiṣṭhaḥ*)—is the most worthy of worship
- प्र यजतां (*pra yajatāṃ*)—let him worship exceedingly on our behalf all the gods

Agni, the accomplisher of the oblation and the shining one, is the lord of the house. Agni, endowed with knowledge from birth, knows all created things. The Agni who is most worthy of worship to the gods, Indra and the others, and to men, and who is of true nature, may that same Agni worship all the gods exceedingly on our behalf.

Agni is the invoker of the gods, the lord of the house, the ruler, who knows all that is, knows all existing beings; he is the most assiduous worshipper amongst gods or men : let him who is observant of truth offer worship.

At the fifth day of the ten-night sacrifice called Vyūḍha, at the time of reciting the mantras of the Āgnimāruta śastra, the Ṛks 13-15 of this sūkta, beginning अग्निर्होता (*agnirhotā*), are to be recited as nivid-type mantras concerning Jātavedas; this is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, अग्निर्होता गृहपतिः स राजेति शिस्त्रः (*agnirhotā gṛhapatiḥ sa rājeti śistraḥ*) (Ā. 8-8). ⟨NOTE:273⟩

At the Patnīsaṃyāja offering this Ṛk is to be recited as the first anuvākyā mantra concerning Gṛhapati; this is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, अग्निर्होता गृहपतिः स राजा हव्यवाळग्निरजरः पिता न इति पत्निसंयाजाः (*agnirhotā gṛhapatiḥ sa rājā havyavāḷagnirajaraḥ pitā na iti patnisaṃyājāḥ*) (Ā. 1-10). And in the mantras of the Āśvina śastra this Ṛk is to be recited as the pratipad mantra; this is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, अग्निर्होता गृहपतिः स राजेति प्रतिपदेकपातिनी पच्छः (*agnirhotā gṛhapatiḥ sa rājeti pratipadekapātinī pacchaḥ*) (Ā. 6-5).
notes: ನಿರಮಂಥತ್ಯ printed after ಪುಷ್ಕರಾದಧ್ಯರ್ಥರ್ವಾ, glued to the reference

en: This Ṛk is the yājyā of the Sviṣṭakṛt in the new-moon and full-moon sacrifices; the sūtra is cited: "he offers with अग्ने यदद्य विशो अध्वरस्य होतः (*agne yadadya viśo adhvarasya hotaḥ*), without the anuvāka" (Ā. 1-6). Sāyaṇa explains: O Agni, performer of the sacrifice, purifying and bright, today seek whatever is to be done for the man, the sacrificer. Since you are the sacrificer of the gods, therefore worship the gods in the sacrifice. And since by your greatness you pervade, therefore, O youngest Agni, whatever oblations we offer today for you, carry them: bring them to your own form called Sviṣṭakṛt.
- आद्य (*ādya*)—at this time of the sacrifice
- यज्वा (*yajvā*)—are the worshipper of the gods
- आद्य (*ādya*)—at this time of the sacrifice

O Agni, accomplisher of the sacrifice, bright with purifying radiance, at this time of the sacrifice desire whatever rite the human sacrificer has. Since you are a worshipper of the gods, worship the gods in the sacrifice. O exceedingly youthful Agni, you pervade everywhere by your greatness. For that reason oblations are offered to you. Carry all of them to the gods, offer them to them.
Agni, minister of the sacrifice, bright with purifying lustre, approve of that (worship) which is this day celebrated by the institutor of the rite :
