you verily are the sacrificer, therefore address the worship (to the gods); and since by your greatness you are all-pervading, therefore, youngest (of the gods), accept the oblations which are to-day (presented) to you.

This Ṛk beginning अग्ने यदद्य (*agne yadadya*) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra at the Sviṣṭakṛt offering of the new-moon and full-moon sacrifices; this is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, अग्ने यदद्य विशो अध्वरस्य होतरित्यनवानं यजति (*agne yadadya viśo adhvarasya hotarityanavānaṃ yajati*) (Ā. 1-6).

O Agni, you look upon the oblations in the form of food that are well placed, set down on the altar; the particle हि (*hi*) is a filler. Heaven and Earth, and with them all the gods, have set you there to sacrifice: this sacrificer has set you. O wealthy Agni, protect us in battle, or when food is to be shared, as the cause of it. And may we cross over all evils, all sufferings. The rest is as already explained.
- अभि ख्यः (*abhi khyaḥ*)—cause to be heard with kindness
- यजध्यै (*yajadhyai*)—to worship the gods with sacrifice
- त्वा नि दधीत (*tvā ni dadhīta*)—have appointed you
- वाजसात् (*vājasāt*)—in the battle waged for food

O Agni, look kindly upon the oblations offered on the altar. Heaven and Earth have appointed you to worship the gods with sacrifice. O wealthy Agni, protect us in this battle waged for food. Cause us to cross all sufferings. By your protection alone may we cross all those sufferings.

Look, Agni, upon the (sacrificial) viands duly deposited (upon the altar): Heaven and Earth detain you to sacrifice (to the gods): opulent Agni, protect us in battle, whereby we may pass safe over all evils: may we pass over those of a prior existence; may we pass over them by your protection.

At the Agnipraṇayana this Ṛk is to be recited; the sūtra is cited: "he should stop at the half-verse अग्ने विश्वेभिः स्वनीक देवैरित्यर्धर्च (*agne viśvebhiḥ svanīka devairityardharca*)" (Ā. 2-17). Sāyaṇa explains: O well-flaming Agni, together with all the gods, being first, chief among all the gods, sit down on the place, the upper altar, furnished with wool. What kind of place? Kulāyin: kulāya is a nest; like it, provided with guggulu and other materials. So it is heard: कुलायमिव हैतद्यज्ञॆ क्रियते यत्प्रैतुदारनाः परिधयो गुल्गुलूर्णास्तुकाः सुगंधितेजनानि । (*kulāyamiva haitadyajñè kriyate yatpraitudāranāḥ paridhayo gulgulūrṇāstukāḥ sugaṃdhitejanāni |*) (Ai. Brā. 1-28). Dhṛtavat means furnished with ghee for the vyāghāraṇa. Thus seated on the upper altar, convey well and straightly the sacrifice of such a sacrificer, the presenter of oblations, to the gods.
- ऊर्णावंतं (*ūrṇāvaṃtaṃ*)—having a seat soft like wool
- प्रथमः (*prathamaḥ*)—you who are chief of all the gods

O Agni with excellent flames, on this sacrificial altar, which has a seat soft like wool, is furnished with ghee and compact like a nest, sit down together with all the gods, you who are chief of all the gods. Carry in the best manner to the gods the share of the sacrifice of the sacrificer who offers the oblation.

Bright-rayed Agni, sit down first with all the gods, upon the altar lined with wool, a nest (of perfumes) and suffused with ghee, and rightly convey (to the deities) the sacrifice of the institutor of the rite, of the presenter of the oblation.

In the sacrificial rite called Agnipraṇayana, in which Agni is taken to the upper altar and established, this Ṛk beginning अग्ने विश्वेभिः (*agne viśvebhiḥ*) is to be recited as an anuvākyā mantra; this is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, अग्ने विश्वेभिः स्वनीकदेवैरित्यर्धर्च आरमेत् (*agne viśvebhiḥ svanīkadevairityardharca āramet*) (Ā. 2-17).

In the rite called Agnipraṇayana the Hotṛ recites eight Ṛks in all. Among them this Ṛk beginning अग्ने विश्वेभिः (*agne viśvebhiḥ*) is the fifth. About its application the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa (Ai. Brā. 5-2) gives this explanation:

अग्ने विश्वेभिः स्वनीकदेवैरूर्णावंतं प्रथमः सीद योनिमिति विश्वैरेवैनं तद्देवैः सहासादयति । कुलायिनं धृतवंतं सवित्र इति कुलायमिव ह्येतद्यज्ञॆ क्रियते यत्प्रतुदारवाः परिधयो गुग्गुलूर्णास्तुकाः सुगंधितेजनानीति यज्ञं नय यजमानाय साध्विति यज्ञमेव तदृजुधा प्रतिष्ठापयति ॥ (*agne viśvebhiḥ svanīkadevairūrṇāvaṃtaṃ prathamaḥ sīda yonimiti viśvairevainaṃ taddevaiḥ sahāsādayati | kulāyinaṃ dhṛtavaṃtaṃ savitra iti kulāyamiva hyetadyajñè kriyate yatpratudāravāḥ paridhayo guggulūrṇāstukāḥ sugaṃdhitejanānīti yajñaṃ naya yajamānāya sādhviti yajñameva tadṛjudhā pratiṣṭhāpayati ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 5-2) ⟨NOTE:274⟩

O Agni, endowed with armies called flames, come and sit down, chief of all the gods, in this navel-place called the upper altar: this is the main purport of the first half of this Ṛk. The use of the word विश्वेभिः (*viśvebhiḥ*) here indicates that all the gods are established together with Agni; that is, the meaning is that Agni, together with all the gods, takes his seat on the upper altar (the sacrificial pit), which is like a bird's nest made soft by spreading threads of wool. The purport of the second half of the Ṛk is: abiding on the upper altar, the navel-region of the sacrifice, which is rich with wood and the like and sprinkled with ghee, accomplish well the sacrificial rites of the sacrificer. The words कुलायिनं धृतवंतं (*kulāyinaṃ dhṛtavaṃtaṃ*) in the third pāda here suggest a bird's nest. That is, a bird builds its nest by joining and weaving together small twigs of the khadira or deodar tree, gum, woollen threads, and a kind of fragrant grass. The navel-place of Agni (the sacrificial pit) is compared here to that nest. How? In building the nest the bird uses twigs; here the logs called paridhi placed around Agni are the twigs. In the same way, in place of gum there is the fragrant material such as ghee prepared for the oblation, in place of woollen threads there are sacrificial animals such as the goat, and in place of the grass there are the kindling sticks, all prepared and placed around Agni; therefore the upper altar (the fire-pit) established for Agni is described by comparison with a bird's nest.
The prayer is expressed here that Agni, established in the place of the upper altar that is like such a bird's nest, may well accomplish the sacrificial acts of the sacrificer.
For the detailed explanation of the sacrificial rite called Agnipraṇayana, see what we have explained in Ṛ. Saṃ. Part 14, pp. 541-549.
notes: Sāyaṇa makes the forty-sixth Ṛk (ವೀತೀ ಯೋ ದೇವಂ) Triṣṭubh and the 47th and 48th Anuṣṭubh; the Anuvāda reads ನೀತೀ ಯೋ ದೇವಂ

en: The vedhas, that is, the Ṛtvijs, the makers of the rites, churn this visible Agni, of the qualities stated before, as the seer called Atharvan churned him of old. They bring forth by friction from the two kindling sticks. अंकूयंतं (*aṃkūyaṃtaṃ*): aṅku is a crooked going; he who wishes it for himself, going away from the gods hither and thither, fleeing from there; अमूरं (*amūraṃ*) is unbewildered. That Agni they bring from the śyāvyās: श्यावी (*śyāvī*) is a name of night, and the masses of darkness arising there are the śyāvyās. From them they bring him; they churn him: this is the construction.
- वेधसः (*vedhasaḥ*)—the priests, the doers of the rite
- अथर्ववत् (*atharvavat*)—as the seer called Atharvāṅgiras churned him of old
- मंथंति (*maṃthaṃti*)—they churn and cause him to blaze
- श्याव्याभ्यः (*śyāvyābhyaḥ*)—from the dark glooms of night

The priests, the doers of the rite, churn this well-known Agni, as the seer Atharvāṅgiras churned him of old, and cause him to blaze. They churn to bring out of the dark glooms of night that same Agni, who has a crooked movement and yet is free from bewilderment.
The priests churn you Agni, as was done by Atharvan, and bring him from the glooms of night, wandering deviously, but not bewildered.

अथर्ववत् (*atharvavat*): that this seer kindled Agni well in the sacrifice performed by him is stated in this Ṛk, in the Ṛk त्वामग्ने पुष्करादध्यर्थर्वा (*tvāmagne puṣkarādadhyartharvā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-16-14) ⟨NOTE:275⟩, and in other Vedas. This seer Atharvan is counted in the list of ancient seers. The matter of how this Atharvan produced Agni, and other matters, are explained in the special topics of Ṛks 13 and 14 of the sixteenth sūkta of this same part.
notes: ಕೊನೆಯ ಮೂರು ಋಕ್ಕುಗಳನ್ನು ಬಿಟ್ಟುಬಿಡಬೇಕು "leave out" printed; the bhāṣya's sūtra ಉದ್ಧರೇತ್ and its Gist read "take up"

en: O Agni, churned in the sacrifice that is spread by all (sarvatātā), be born, appear. For what purpose? For the sacrificer who desires the gods. For the welfare of such a sacrificer, that is, for his non-destruction. And having been born, bring the immortals, free from death, the augmenters of the sacrifice (ṛtāvṛdhaḥ), the gods.
After that, make our sacrifice touch among those gods; that is, bring it to them.
- देववीतये (*devavītaye*)—of this sacrificer who desires the presence of the gods

O Agni, be born for the welfare of this sacrificer, who desires the presence of the gods in this sacrifice. Bring the gods, who are free from mortality and are the augmenters of the sacrifice. Offer our sacrifice to those gods.

Be born, Agni, at the sacrifice, for the welfare of the offerer (of the oblation) to the gods : bring hither the immortal deities, the augmenters of the (sacred) rite : present our sacrifice to the gods.

O Gṛhapati, Agni, protector of sacrifices, among beings it is we who have made you great with fuel, with kindling. For that reason, may our householderships be अस्थूरि (*asthūri*): a cart yoked with one horse is called sthūri, the opposite, a cart furnished with many horses, is asthūri, and by this fullness is indicated; may they be full of sons, cattle, wealth and the like. And sharpen us well with keen radiance, sharpen well, unite us: this is the meaning.
- अस्थूरि (*asthūri*)—make it endowed with all wealth such as sons and cattle

O Agni, protector of the sacrifice, among beings it is we who have made you grow abundantly with kindling sticks. Make the lordship of our house endowed with all wealth such as sons and cattle. Make us pure and stirred up with keen radiance.
Lord of the house, Agni, we, amongst men, promote your increase by fuel : may our domestic fires be supplied with all that is essential : enliven us with brilliant radiance.

अस्थूरि (*asthūri*): for this word the commentator has said अस्थूरि अस्थूरीणि । एकाश्वयुक्तः शकटो स्थूरिरित्युच्यते । तद्विपरीतो बहुभिरश्वैरुपेतः शकटोऽस्थूरिः । तेन च संपूर्णता लक्ष्यते । अस्थूरीणि पुत्रपशुधनादिभिः संपूर्णानि भवंतु । (*asthūri asthūrīṇi | ekāśvayuktaḥ śakaṭo sthūrirityucyate | tadviparīto bahubhiraśvairupetaḥ śakaṭo 'sthūriḥ | tena ca saṃpūrṇatā lakṣyate | asthūrīṇi putrapaśudhanādibhiḥ saṃpūrṇāni bhavaṃtu |*) That is, a cart to which only one horse is yoked is called sthūri. Since asthūri stands here, the meaning of a chariot furnished with many horses is indicated. Where there is such a chariot, cattle, sons and the like must accordingly be there. Therefore Agni is prayed to bring about that many horses, chariots, cattle and other wealth come to us.

O Agni, you are the hotā, the accomplisher of the oblation, of all the sacrifices, which are differentiated in the form of the seven saṃsthās. Or else: you are the caller of the gods in connection with the sacrifices. Why so? Because among the man, the sacrificer, who belongs to Manu, you have been placed by the gods as hotā; therefore: this is the meaning.
O Agni, you have been established by the gods in this sacrificer, who belongs to Manu. Therefore you are the accomplisher of all sacrifices.
You, Agni, have been appointed by the gods, the ministrant for men, the descendants of Manu, at all sacrifices.

अग्ने त्वं विश्वेषां यज्ञानां होता—हे अग्ने त्वं सर्वॆषां सप्तसंस्थारूपेण भिन्नानां यज्ञानां होमनिष्पादकोऽसि । (*agne tvaṃ viśveṣāṃ yajñānāṃ hotā—he agne tvaṃ sarvèṣāṃ saptasaṃsthārūpeṇa bhinnānāṃ yajñānāṃ homaniṣpādako 'si |*) O Agni, the meaning is: you, being the accomplisher of the oblation in all the sacrifices of various kinds by the varieties of the seven saṃsthās, and being the Hotṛ who invokes the gods, cause those sacrifices to be completed fully. Here an explanation is necessary about what the seven saṃsthās are. In the Soma sacrifice there are seven varieties. It is customary to call them the seven Soma saṃsthās. Their names are Agniṣṭoma, Atyagniṣṭoma, Ukthya, Ṣoḍaśī, Atirātra, Aproryāma and Vājapeya. Among these the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice is of the nature of the prakṛti. That is, this sacrifice is the basis (Base) of the other Soma sacrifices; with some modifications it becomes the other six Soma sacrifices.

O Agni, you, for us in the sacrifice, with the tongues, the flames, that are exhilarating or worthy of praise, worship the great gods; satisfy them with oblations. How that is done is stated: bring the gods who are to be worshipped, Indra and the others; and then worship them, that is, give them the oblations: this is the meaning.
O Agni, you, the well-known, in our sacrifice, with your flames that cause delight, worship the gods of great nature. Bring those gods to us and worship them.
Therefore at our sacrifice offer oblations to the great deities with exhilarating flames : bring hither the gods : offer them worship.

In the offering to Agni Pathikṛt, this Ṛk is the anuvākyā; the sūtra is cited (Ā. 3-10). Sāyaṇa explains: O Vedhas, creator, O Sukratu, doer of good deeds, O god Agni, endowed with qualities such as generosity, you know in the sacrifices, in the new-moon and full-moon sacrifices and others, the great roads and also the small paths, directly and straightly. Since it is so, bring the sacrificer who has fallen away from the path of the sacrifice back to that path: this is the meaning.
- यज्ञेषु (*yajñeṣu*)—in our new-moon and full-moon sacrifices and the others
- वेत्थ हि (*vettha hi*)—you know, do you not
notes: printed "immorta" before a line break; "immortal"?

en: O Agni, creator, doer of excellent deeds, of divine nature, in our new-moon and full-moon sacrifices and the others you know, do you not, the great roads and the small roads (that is, all the ways of performing the sacrifice) by your direct sight alone.
Agni, doer of great deeds, creator, you know (how to traval over) with speed (great) roads and (little) paths at sacrifices.

In the offering made to Agni Pathikṛt, अग्नये पथिकृते (*agnaye pathikṛte*), this Ṛk beginning वेत्था (*vetthā*) is to be recited as an anuvākyā mantra; this is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, वेत्था हि वेदो अध्वन आ देवानामपि पंथामगन्म (*vetthā hi vedo adhvana ā devānāmapi paṃthāmaganma*) (Ā. 3-10).

O Agni, Bharata, the king of that name, son of Duṣyanta, together with the vājins (vāja is food in the form of oblation; those who have it) praised you, for the sake of happiness divided in two ways: the obtaining of what is desired and the removal of what is undesired. And having praised, he worshipped you, who are worthy of sacrifice, with sacrifices. To him you gave the two kinds of happiness: this is the meaning. ⟨NOTE:279⟩
notes: ಸ್ವಾಧ್ಯಃ ಶೋಭನಾಧ್ಯಾನಾಃ in the bhāṣya "of good meditation", the Kannada gloss says "reciting excellent praise"; the block ends ಯಾಚಂತೇ ನಾ, the last word looks damaged

en: - वाजिभिः (*vājibhiḥ*)—with food in the form of oblations
- द्विता शुनं (*dvitā śunaṃ*)—for the two kinds of happiness, the obtaining of what is desired and the removal of what is undesired
- यज्ञियं (*yajñiyaṃ*)—you who are worthy of sacrifice

O Agni, Bharata, son of Duṣyanta, with food in the form of oblations, has praised you for the two kinds of happiness, the obtaining of what is desired and the removal of what is undesired. He has worshipped you, who are worthy of sacrifice, with sacrifices. Bestow on him both those kinds of happiness.
Bharata, with the presenters of the oblation, has joyfully praised you in your (two-fold capacity), and has worshiped you, the adorable with sacrifices.

In this Ṛk there is mention of a king named Bharata; Sāyaṇa has said that he is the son of Duṣyanta. It is understood that the king Bharata was king of the people of the Āryan tribe called the Bharatas, who were very powerful in the time of the Ṛgveda. Probably that tribe got its name from this king. It is understood that the seer Viśvāmitra was the priest of this king or of his descendants, and that Viśvāmitra had great friendship and trust among these Bharata people. In the Ṛks 11 and 12 of Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-33, in praising the rivers विराट्टुतुद्रि (*virāṭṭutudri*), he prayed those rivers to reduce their waters so that it might be convenient for the kings of the Bharata family or their followers to cross the river. Since the account of the Bharata people and the relation of the seer Bharadvāja with them is extensive, it will be explained later. But the statement of the commentator that this king Bharata is the son of Duṣyanta is supported in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa. On the occasion of the great anointing of Indra there are also descriptions of the royal anointing of many famous kings. Among them there is also the description of the royal anointing of the king named Bharata, son of Duṣyanta. That we shall explain here.

एतेन ह वा ऐंद्रेण महाभिषेकेण दीर्घतमा मामतेयो भरतं दौष्पंतिमभिषिषेच तस्मादु भरतो दौष्पंतिः समंतं सर्वतः सृथिवीं जयन्परीयायाश्वैरु च मुध्यॆरीजे ॥ (*etena ha vā aiṃdreṇa mahābhiṣekeṇa dīrghatamā māmateyo bharataṃ dauṣpaṃtimabhiṣiṣeca tasmādu bharato dauṣpaṃtiḥ samaṃtaṃ sarvataḥ sṛthivīṃ jayanparīyāyāśvairu ca mudhyèrīje ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 39-23)

The description of the great anointing of Indra, and the order in which the gods performed it, have been stated before. Among the kings anointed according to that order is the king named Bharata, son of Duṣyanta. The famous seer Dīrghatamas, son of the woman Mamatā, performed the rites of the coronation of this king Bharata. After that Bharata set out for the conquest of the quarters, travelled over the earth, conquered various countries, and performed the Aśvamedha sacrifice with excellent horses fit for sacrifice.
To make known the greatness of this anointing of Bharata, five verses are recited. Their explanation is as follows.
हिरण्येन परीवृतान्कृष्णान् शुक्लदतो मृगान् । मष्णारे भरतोददाच्छतं बद्धानि सप्त च ॥ (*hiraṇyena parīvṛtānkṛṣṇān śukladato mṛgān | maṣṇāre bharatodadācchataṃ baddhāni sapta ca ‖*)

This king named Bharata, at the time of his coronation, in the country called Maṣṇāra, gave as a gift a herd of one hundred and seven elephants, black in colour, with white horns, adorned with golden ornaments.
भरतस्यैष दौष्पंतेरग्निः साचीगुणे चितः । यस्मिन्सहस्रं ब्राह्मणा बद्वशो गा विभेजिरे ॥ (*bharatasyaiṣa dauṣpaṃteragniḥ sācīguṇe citaḥ | yasminsahasraṃ brāhmaṇā badvaśo gā vibhejire ‖*)
When this King Bharata, the son of Duṣyanta, performed the sacrificial rite called Agnicayana in the country named Sācīguṇa, he distributed thousands of cows as gifts among the Brāhmaṇas.
अष्टासप्ततिं भरतो दौष्पंतियार्मुनामनु । गंगायां वृत्रघ्नेऽबध्नात्पंचपंचाशतं हयान् ॥ (*aṣṭāsaptatiṃ bharato dauṣpaṃtiyārmunāmanu | gaṃgāyāṃ vṛtraghne 'badhnātpaṃcapaṃcāśataṃ hayān ‖*)

This King Bharata, the son of Duṣyanta, had made ready seventy-eight excellent horses fit for sacrifice on the bank of the river Yamunā, and fifty-five horses in the country called Vṛtraghna on the bank of the river Gaṅgā, binding them for the Aśvamedha sacrifice to be performed in honour of Indra. (That is, he performed the Aśvamedha sacrifice.)
त्रयस्त्रिंशच्छतं राजाश्वान् बध्वायं मेध्यान् । दौष्पंतिरत्यगाद्राज्ञो मायां मायवत्तरः ॥ (*trayastriṃśacchataṃ rājāśvān badhvāyaṃ medhyān | dauṣpaṃtiratyagādrājño māyāṃ māyavattaraḥ ‖*)

It has been said before that this king, the son of Duṣyanta, had bound and made ready, for the sacrifice, a total of one hundred and thirty-three horses fit for sacrifice on the banks of the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā. After preparing the horses for the sacrifice in this way, this king conquered his enemy kings by various devices and by his strength and power.

महाकर्म भरतस्य न पूर्वे नापरे जनाः । दिवं मर्त्य इव हस्ताभ्यां नोदापुः पंच मानवा इति ॥ (*mahākarma bharatasya na pūrve nāpare janāḥ | divaṃ martya iva hastābhyāṃ nodāpuḥ paṃca mānavā iti ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 39-23)

Such a great deed was not done before by anyone of the race of Bharata, and will not be done hereafter. Just as a man among the five peoples beginning with the Brāhmaṇas cannot touch the world of heaven with his hands, so no one can perform such a profound rite as King Bharata performed. All this is praise of the virtues of Bharata. The examination of the subject concerning this king, as it relates to history, we shall make later.

Sāyaṇa says: O Agni, you, these visible, many, desirable and shareable riches, give to Divodāsa who presses Soma. This is a simile with a word omitted: as, to the king named Divodāsa who performs the pressing of Soma, you gave them, so to Bharadwāja the sage, who has offered oblations, give them as well; the word "give" is what must be supplied.
- वार्या (*vāryā*)—deserving the regard of all, the riches
- सुन्वते (*sunvate*)—who presses and offers Soma juice
- भरद्वाजाय (*bharadvājāya*)—to me, Bharadwāja, also (give and favour)

O Agni, as you gave to Divodāsa, who pressed and offered Soma juice, these well-known, exceedingly abundant riches deserving the regard of all, so give them also to me, who offer oblations, and favour me.
As you have conferred these many blessings upon Divodasa when presenting libations, (so now grant them) to the actual offerer, Bharadwaja.

Divodāsa: the king named Divodāsa, or Divodāsa Atithigva, was a very famous king in the time of the Vedas. He was the son of one called Vadhryaśva and the father of one called Sudāsa. This Sudāsa was renowned among the kings of the Tṛtsu line in the Bharata people. Therefore Divodāsa also is called Bharata (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-16-4, 5, 19), and it is said in places such as Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-19-8 that, like Sudāsa, he too was an enemy king, a rival of the Turvaśas and the Yadus. His chief enemy was the Asura or Dāsa called Śambara. This Śambara is described as the chief of the original inhabitants of this country, who lived in the hills and mountains (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-130-7:

2-12-11; 6-26-5; 7-18-20), and it is described that Divodāsa defeated him many times, in the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-112-14; 1-116-18; 1-119-4; 1-130-7 to 10; 2-19-6; 4-26-3; 4-30-20; 1-102-14; 1-106-18; 1-109-4: 1-130-7 to 10; 2-19-6; 4-26-3; 4-30-20; 6-26-3; 6-26-5; 6-43-1; 6-47-21, 22; 9-61-2. Also in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-119-4 it is described that when this king Divodāsa undertook to perform a sacrifice, the Aśvin gods, knowing that his sacrifice would be destroyed by the demon named Śambara and that danger would come to him also, killed the Asura Śambara and protected Divodāsa. Because he worshipped Agni especially, Agni is seen to be called by his name in the Ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-13-2. In the Ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-61-1 and in some of the Ṛks following it, there is a description of this Divodāsa fighting on the bank of the river Sarasvatī with the Paṇis, the Pārāvatas and the Bṛsayas. In places such as Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-112-13, 14; 1-116-18; 6-16-5; 6-31-4, his name is found recited together with the name of the sage Bharadwāja or of that sage's descendants. In Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-130-10 the plural word दिवोदासेभिः (*divodāsebhiḥ*) is used, indicating the descendants of Divodāsa or his subjects. The name of Divodāsa is not found in the 3rd, 5th, 8th and 10th Maṇḍalas.

Sāyaṇa says: You, Agni, who are immortal, not subject to death, becoming the messenger, bring the divine people, those who belong to the gods, to our sacrifice. Doing what? Hearing the good praise of Bharadwāja, the wise.
- अमूर्त्यः (*amūrtyaḥ*)—free from the nature of death
- दूतः (*dūtaḥ*)—having become the messenger of the gods
- दैव्यं (*daivyaṃ*)—those who belong to the gods
O Agni, you who are free from the nature of death, having become the messenger of the gods, hearing the excellent praise of the wise Bharadwāja, bring the gods who are worthy of the sacrifice.
Hearing the adoration of the sage, you, who are the immorta messenger, bring hither the celestial people. ⟨NOTE:280⟩
notes: the sūtra words as quoted in the bhāṣya: ಈಳೇನ್ನೋ, ದೇವನೀತಯೇ; in the Special Topics: ಈಳೇಽನ್ಯೋ, ದೇವವೀತಯೇ

en: Sāyaṇa says: O Agni, to you, the shining god, mortals of good meditation praise and entreat in the sacrifices, for the satisfaction of the gods. ⟨NOTE:281⟩
notes: Saṃhitā prints ೧ for this Ṛk; the Pada-pāṭha prints ೧೧

en: O Agni, mortals who praise you, the shining one, with excellent praises, praise you in the sacrifices in order to satisfy the gods.
Pious mortals invoke you, divine Agni, at sacrificees to convey their (sacrificial) food to the gods.

Sāyaṇa says: O Agni, your radiance, which is well to be seen or else which is the good beholder, the illuminator of all, I worship with distinction; the sense of the words is "I worship" with eminent worship. Moreover, of you, the good giver, I worship the work, or the wisdom. Not I alone: all the other sacrificers also, being endowed with the several desires through your favour, enjoy your radiance and your work, that is, they resort to them.
- सुदानवः (*sudānavaḥ*)—of you, who give excellent wealth and the like
- कामिनः (*kāminaḥ*)—having obtained their desired ends through your favour

O Agni, I worship your attractive radiance that illuminates everything. The sacrificers, who have obtained their desired ends through your favour, praise your excellent works and wisdom, you who give wealth. I also praise that work of yours exceedingly.
I glorify your splendour, and the acts of you, the liberal giver : all who (through your favour) enjoy their desires, glorify you.

Sāyaṇa says: O Agni, you are the Hotā: as Hotā you are established by Manu. With the mouth, that is, with the flame that is your mouth, you are the carrier, the bearer of the oblations, and the most knowing, one who knows to the highest degree. For that reason you worship the Viś, the heavenly people, the divine subjects belonging to the world of heaven.
- होता (*hotā*)—as the accomplisher of the offerings
- आसा (*āsā*)—with your mouth in the form of flame
- विदुष्टरः (*viduṣṭaraḥ*)—the one who has exceeding knowledge, you
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—belonging to the world of heaven
- विशः (*viśaḥ*)—the subjects in the form of gods

O Agni, you are established by Manu in the place of the Hotā. You, who with your mouth in the form of flame bear the oblation and who have exceeding knowledge, worship the subjects belonging to the world of heaven, who are in the form of gods, that is, the gods.
You have been appointed by Manu, the invoker of the gods, the most wise, bearer of oblations (to them) by your mouth : worship, Agni, the people of heaven.

मनुर्हितः (*manurhitaḥ*): although the name of Manu is recited in many places in the Ṛgveda, a fuller account is not found anywhere. Manu may be understood as the original ancestor of the human race and as a guide in the order of performance of sacrifices and the like. See what has been said concerning this Manu in places such as Ṛ. Saṃ. Part 9, pp. 107-108.

Sāyaṇa says: In the Darśa and Pūrṇamāsa sacrifices the three Ṛks beginning "Agni, come" are the Sāmidhenī verses. It is laid down in the sūtra (Ā. Sū. 1-2). Further, when the Gārhapatya and Āhavanīya fires come into contact with each other, an eight-potsherd cake is offered to Agni Vīti; the verse "Agni, come" is the Anuvākyā for it, and this too is laid down in the sūtra (Ā. Sū. 3-13).

Sāyaṇa says: O Agni, come. For what purpose? For the eating of the oblations. And further, to give the oblations to the gods. You, who are praised, becoming the Hotā, sit down, take your seat, upon the spread darbha grass.
- वीतये (*vītaye*)—for the eating of the oblation
- हव्यदातये (*havyadātaye*)—for distributing the oblation to the gods
- गृणानः (*gṛṇānaḥ*)—you who are to be praised
- बर्हिषि (*barhiṣi*)—upon the seat of darbha grass
- होता (*hotā*)—as the accomplisher of the offerings
O Agni, be gracious, both for the eating of the oblation and for distributing it to the gods. You who are to be praised, sit down upon the seat of darbha grass as the accomplisher of the offerings.
Come, Agni, to the (sacrificial) food : being lauded, (come) to convey the oblation, (to the gods) : sit down as the ministrant priest upon the sacred grass.

In the Darśa and Pūrṇamāsa sacrifices, the three Ṛks beginning "Agni, come" (the Ṛks 10 to 12 of this sūkta) are to be recited as Sāmidhenī mantras; this is set forth by the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra, in the sūtra अग्न आ याहि वीतये गृणान ईळेऽन्यो नमस्यस्तिरः (*agna ā yāhi vītaye gṛṇāna īḷe 'nyo namasyastiraḥ*) (Ā. Sū. 1-2). And if through inadvertence there is a contact of the two fires, the Gārhapatya and the Āhavanīya, then one must offer the oblation with अग्नये वीतयेऽष्टाकपालः पुरोडाशः (*agnaye vītaye 'ṣṭākapālaḥ puroḍāśaḥ*). Then this Ṛk "Agni, come" is to be recited as the Anuvākyā mantra; this is set forth by the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra in the sūtra अग्न आ याहि वीतये यो अग्निं देववीतये (*agna ā yāhi vītaye yo agniṃ devavītaye*) (Ā. Sū. 3-13). ⟨NOTE:282⟩
notes: ಅಂಗನಾದಿಗುಣಯುಕ್ತ: the sense of ಅಂಗನಾದಿ unclear
ಆಥರ್ನೈತತ್ಸಂಜ್ಞಕ ಋಷಿಸ್ತಾಂ: damaged

en: Sāyaṇa says: O Aṅgiras, Agni, who are endowed with the qualities of the kind called aṅgana, or who are of the form of embers (aṅgāra), or son of Aṅgiras: you, of the qualities already stated, we make to grow with fuel, that is, with logs that are the means of kindling, and with ghee, that is, clarified butter. Therefore, O youngest Agni, the most youthful, blaze greatly and exceedingly: shine. ⟨NOTE:284⟩
notes: abbreviation ಋ. ಸರಿ. printed

en: O Agni, named Aṅgiras, we cause you, who possess well-known qualities, to grow with kindling-sticks and with the offering of ghee. O Agni, exceedingly young, shine exceedingly.
We augment you, Angiras, with fuel and with butter : blaze fiercely, youngest (of the gods).

अंगिरः (*aṃgiraḥ*): here the word अंगिरः (*aṃgiraḥ*) is used to address Agni. In many instances of addressing Agni in the Ṛgveda the word अंगिरः (*aṃgiraḥ*) is used. In many Ṛks, Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-1-6; 1-31-1; 1-31-17; 4-3-15; 4-9-7; 5-8-4; 5-10-7; 5-11-6 and so on, Agni is called by the word अंगिरः (*aṃgiraḥ*). What is the reason that Agni came by this name? What is the relation between Agni and the sage Aṅgiras? These and similar matters are explained at length in places such as Ṛ. Saṃ. Part 1, pp. 640-641; Part 3, p. 520; Part 5, p. 672; Part 6, p. 442; Part 10, p. 269.

Sāyaṇa says: O shining god Agni, you, who have the qualities stated before, make come towards us wealth that is wide, extensive, to be heard of, that is, praiseworthy, great, and endowed with good heroism. "Vivāsasi" means: cause to go towards. In this connection the Vājasaneyaka says: अच्चा देव विवाससीति तन्नो गमयेत्यैवैतदाहेति ॥ (*accā deva vivāsasīti tanno gamayetyaivaitadāheti ‖*) **GLOSS**
- सुवीर्यं (*suvīryaṃ*)—endowed with excellent heroism, the wealth
- अच्छ (*accha*)—so as to turn towards us
O shining Agni, you who are described above, send to us, so as to turn towards us, wealth that is wide, praiseworthy, great, and endowed with excellent heroism.
Divine Agni, bestow upon us (wealth), excellent, great, and(comprehending) worthy male descendants.

Sāyaṇa says: In the churning of fire, the three Ṛks beginning "O Agni, from the lotus" are to be recited after the act. It is laid down in the sūtra (Ā. Sū. 2-16). O Agni, the sage of the name Atharvan churned you out upon the lotus leaf, that is, produced you from the two kindling-woods. ⟨NOTE:285⟩ From what kind of lotus leaf? From the one that holds like a head, the bearer of the whole world, of everything. For on the lotus leaf Prajāpati spread out the earth, according to the Śruti पुष्करपर्णॆ हि प्रजापतिर्भूमिमप्रथयत् तत्पुष्करपर्णॆऽप्रथयत् । (*puṣkaraparṇè hi prajāpatirbhūmimaprathayat tatpuṣkaraparṇè 'prathayat |*) (Tai. Brā. 1-1-3-6) **GLOSS**. And the earth is the support of the whole world; thus the lotus leaf is the bearer of the whole world. Here the word for lotus is used to name the lotus leaf. And this is clearly stated in the Taittirīyaka: त्वामग्ने पुष्करादधीत्याह पुष्करपर्णॆ हैनमुपश्रितमविंदत् । (*tvāmagne puṣkarādadhītyāha puṣkaraparṇè hainamupaśritamaviṃdat |*) (Tai. Saṃ. 5-1-4-4) **GLOSS**
notes: abbreviation ಛಾಂ. ಉ. printed

en: - मूर्ध्नः (*mūrdhnaḥ*)—in the form of the head
- पुष्करात् अधि (*puṣkarāt adhi*)—upon the lotus leaf
- निरमंथत (*niramaṃthata*)—churned and caused to be produced
O Agni, the sage named Atharvan churned you upon the lotus leaf, which is in the form of the head and is the bearer of the whole world, and caused you to be produced.
The sage, Atharvan, extracted you from upon the lotus-leaf, the head, the support of the universe.

That this Ṛk "O Agni, from the lotus" is to be recited at the time of churning fire is set forth by the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra, in the sūtra त्वामग्ने पुष्करादधीति तिसृणामर्धर्चं शिष्टारमेत् (*tvāmagne puṣkarādadhīti tisṛṇāmardharcaṃ śiṣṭāramet*) (Ā. Sū. 2-16). The account of the churning of fire given in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa we have given in the Special Topics of the 40th, 41st and 42nd Ṛks of this same sūkta. In what circumstance the present Ṛk is to be recited, and other explanations connected with this Ṛk, can be known by looking there.

In the present mantra the churning of Agni from the lotus by the sage Atharvan is praised. Besides, the lotus is praised as the head of the universe and as the bearer of the whole world. The purport of the mantra is that the production of Agni from the lotus, which is the supporter and the bearer of the world, came about through the effort of the sage Atharvan. This description cannot be a description of the worldly lotus leaf or lotus flower. The word puṣkara reflects the principle that is all-pervading, the support of the universe, and bears all the worlds, both worldly and beyond the world. But it is necessary to know why that principle became known by the name puṣkara, and what the meaning of the word puṣkara is.

Sāyaṇa, in the commentary on this mantra, has taken the word puṣkara to mean the lotus leaf and has shown the identity of the lotus leaf with the earth. This identity shows that the earth also has the character of supporting the world. Here the earth does not mean merely the sense current in usage. There are also many contexts in which all the worlds are signified by the word earth. If this extended meaning is to hold, what is the exact meaning of the word puṣkara?

The author of the Nirukta has said that this word is derived from the root puṣ, which gives the meaning "to nourish". (There is the Uṇādi sūtra पुषः कित् । पुष्यतेः करः (*puṣaḥ kit | puṣyateḥ karaḥ*), Uṇ. Sū. 4-4.) It is the opinion of the author of the Nirukta that the word puṣkara is current for the atmosphere because it nourishes all beings (Ni. 5-14). Yāska has explained the derivation of this word by citing a sentence of the Ṛk Saṃhitā. This word is recited among the names of the atmosphere, अंबरं, वियत्, व्योम............पुष्करं, सगरः (*aṃbaraṃ, viyat, vyoma............puṣkaraṃ, sagaraḥ*) and the rest (Ni. 2-10). Afterwards he states the derivation of the form.

उतासि मैत्रावरुणो वसिष्ठोर्वश्या ब्रह्मन्मनसोऽधिजातः । द्रप्सं स्कन्नं ब्रह्मणा दैव्येन विश्वेदेवाः पुष्करे त्वाददंत ॥ (*utāsi maitrāvaruṇo vasiṣṭhorvaśyā brahmanmanaso 'dhijātaḥ | drapsaṃ skannaṃ brahmaṇā daivyena viśvedevāḥ puṣkare tvādadaṃta ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-33-11) **GLOSS**

In the mantra उतासि मैत्रावरुणो वसिष्ठोर्वश्या ब्रह्मन्मनसोऽधिजातः । द्रप्सं स्कन्नं ब्रह्मणा दैव्येन विश्वे देवाः पुष्करे त्वाददंत ॥ (*utāsi maitrāvaruṇo vasiṣṭhorvaśyā brahmanmanaso 'dhijātaḥ | drapsaṃ skannaṃ brahmaṇā daivyena viśve devāḥ puṣkare tvādadaṃta ‖*) the account of the birth of Vasiṣṭha in the lotus is told. (The full purport of this mantra will be explained later.) The author of the Nirukta, citing this mantra, has stated here the derivation of the form of the word पुष्कर (*puṣkara*) and the chief purport of this word, in this manner.

पुष्करमंतरिक्षं पोषति भूतान्युदकं । पुष्करं पूजाकरं पूजयितव्यं वा । इदमपीतरत् पुष्करमेतस्मादेव पुष्करं वपुष्करं वा । पुष्पं पुष्पतेः ॥ (*puṣkaramaṃtarikṣaṃ poṣati bhūtānyudakaṃ | puṣkaraṃ pūjākaraṃ pūjayitavyaṃ vā | idamapītarat puṣkarametasmādeva puṣkaraṃ vapuṣkaraṃ vā | puṣpaṃ puṣpateḥ ‖*) (Ni. 5-14)

As stated above, the word पुष्कर (*puṣkara*) is derived from the root पुष् (*puṣ*). It has this name because it nourishes the world and because it is productive of worship. The explanation is that the lotus flower, famous in the world, also is called by the name पुष्कर (*puṣkara*) for this very reason, that is, because it is a means of worship. Therefore the first meaning of the word पुष्कर (*puṣkara*) is the atmosphere. It is in this meaning that the word is used throughout the Saṃhitās and the rest. But this explanation is contrary to what is said in some other places. For example, in the present mantra (6-16-13) Sāyaṇa has stated the identity of the lotus and the earth. Therefore the question naturally arises whether the word पुष्कर (*puṣkara*) reflects the principle of the earth or the principle of the atmosphere. But there is no contradiction in taking it in this way, once as earth and another time as atmosphere. For the word earth does not mean merely the portion of land current in worldly usage. There are also many contexts in which the three worlds are indicated by this word itself. For example,

परः सो अस्तु तन्वा ३ तना च तिस्रः पृथिवीरधो अस्तु विश्वाः । प्रति शुष्यतु यशो अस्य देवा यो नो दिना दिप्सति यश्च नक्तं ॥ (*paraḥ so astu tanvā 3 tanā ca tisraḥ pṛthivīradho astu viśvāḥ | prati śuṣyatu yaśo asya devā yo no dinā dipsati yaśca naktaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-104-11)

in this, the gods are prayed to destroy the Rākṣasas. In explaining where such Rākṣasas can be, it is stated that they can be spread over all three worlds. Those three worlds together are here signified by the word earth. Sāyaṇa has clearly given the meaning "the three worlds" here for the word earth. Likewise, earlier also, when the purport of the mantra यदिंद्राग्नी अवमस्यां पृथिव्यां (*yadiṃdrāgnī avamasyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ*) (Ṛ. Sari. 1-108-9) was explained, it was stated that the word earth has the meaning of the three worlds. ⟨NOTE:286⟩ Therefore, if the word lotus is given the meaning earth, it is not merely the land that is meant; one must understand it to be the great principle that reflects the three worlds. If it has such an extended meaning, then what is the meaning of the statements that in the lotus Agni was churned and appeared, and that Vasiṣṭha arose, must be examined in the present context.

It can be said boldly that the great principle called the Brahma-tree, which is the root of the creation of the universe, the support of the universe and pervading the universe, and which is famous in the Saṃhitā and in the Brāhmaṇas and the rest, is the very same great principle that is signified here by the word पुष्कर (*puṣkara*). But one must form an exact opinion on whether the particulars described there and the particular described in the present context are of one kind, and whether the two set forth the details of the development of one and the same principle.

किं स्विध्वनं क उ स वृक्ष आस यतो द्यावापृथिवी निष्पतक्षुः । मनीषिणो मनसा पृच्छतेदु तद्यदध्यतिष्ठद्भुवनानि धारयन् ॥ (*kiṃ svidhvanaṃ ka u sa vṛkṣa āsa yato dyāvāpṛthivī niṣpatakṣuḥ | manīṣiṇo manasā pṛcchatedu tadyadadhyatiṣṭhadbhuvanāni dhārayan ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-81-4)

What was that (Brahma) tree, from what material and cause were heaven and earth all fashioned? What was that forest? O great seers, know by the action in the form of meditation, in your mind, what its position was when it was supporting all the worlds. In answer to this question, in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa it is said,

ब्रह्म वनं ब्रह्म स वृक्ष आसीत् । यतो द्यावापृथिवी निष्पतक्षुः । मनीषिणो मनसा विब्रवीमि वः । ब्रह्माध्यतिष्ठद्भुवनानि धारयन् ॥ (*brahma vanaṃ brahma sa vṛkṣa āsīt | yato dyāvāpṛthivī niṣpatakṣuḥ | manīṣiṇo manasā vibravīmi vaḥ | brahmādhyatiṣṭhadbhuvanāni dhārayan ‖*) (Tai. Brā. 2-8-9-6)

Brahman itself is this forest, Brahman itself is this tree. From the root itself heaven and earth all were created. O great seers, know that this tree itself is the supporter of the universe. The principle that is described as the tree in such contexts is described as the lotus in the present mantra. Just as it is said that this tree issues from the navel of the primal god reclining on Śeṣa in the ocean of milk and pervades the universe, so it is described that this lotus arises from the same navel and is the support of this same creator. This lotus bears in its opened heart the Parabrahman himself, the maker of the universe. Brahmā is described by epithets such as नाभिज, अब्बज, अब्बयोनि, कमलासन, पद्मासन (*nābhija, abbaja, abbayoni, kamalāsana, padmāsana*). Nārāyaṇa, resting in the ocean, is also described as पद्मनाभ, पुष्करनाभ (*padmanābha, puṣkaranābha*) and so on. Therefore, although the Brahma-tree and the lotus which is the seat of Brahmā are one, there is a slight difference in their description. The Brahma-tree is praised as pervading the universe, containing all beings. This lotus, the seat of Brahmā, is praised as nourishing all beings and as the support of the universe. Although its pervasiveness is not described from the material point of view, there are also many contexts in which it is described as all-pervading from the spiritual point of view. The very lotus that is described as the lotus of the heart is also praised as the great principle pervading the universe.

अथ यदिदमस्मिन् ब्रह्मपुरे दहरं पुंडरीरं वेश्म दहरोऽस्मिन्नंतराकाशस्तस्मिन् यदंतस्तदन्नेष्टव्यं तद्वाव विजिज्ञासितव्यं । (*atha yadidamasmin brahmapure daharaṃ puṃḍarīraṃ veśma daharo 'sminnaṃtarākāśastasmin yadaṃtastadanneṣṭavyaṃ tadvāva vijijñāsitavyaṃ |*) (Chā. U. 8-1-1)

In this heart, which is described as the city of Brahman, there is a dwelling in the form of a lotus. Its material form is small. Inside it there is a small space; one should seek that and know its secret. Thus the very lotus of the heart that is the support of the small ether is also praised as all-pervading.

यावान्ना अयमाकाशस्तानानेषोऽंतर्हृदय आकाश उभे अस्मिन् द्याना पृथिवी अंतरेव समाहिते उभावग्निश्च वायुश्च सूर‍्याचंद्रमसावुभौ विद्युन्नक्षत्राणि यच्चास्येहास्ति यच्च नास्ति सर्वं तदस्मिन्समाहितमिति । (*yāvānnā ayamākāśastānāneṣo 'ṃtarhṛdaya ākāśa ubhe asmin dyānā pṛthivī aṃtareva samāhite ubhāvagniśca vāyuśca sūryācaṃdramasāvubhau vidyunnakṣatrāṇi yaccāsyehāsti yacca nāsti sarvaṃ tadasminsamāhitamiti |*) (Chā. U. 8-1-7) ⟨NOTE:287⟩

In this small ether, in this very one, heaven and earth, fire, air, sun and moon, lightning, the stars, and all things whether of the nature of being or of not-being, in short everything, are contained.

अथ य एषोऽंतरे हृत्पुष्कर एवाश्रितोऽन्नमत्ति स एषोग्निर्दिवि श्रितसौरः कालाख्योऽदृश्यः सर्वभूतान्यन्नमत्तीति ॥ (*atha ya eṣo 'ṃtare hṛtpuṣkara evāśrito 'nnamatti sa eṣognirdivi śritasauraḥ kālākhyo 'dṛśyaḥ sarvabhūtānyannamattīti ‖*) (Maitruśiniṣat 6-2) ⟨NOTE:288⟩
The person who is established in this lotus of the heart and eats the food is the Agni in the atmosphere, called Time, invisible, in the form of the sun, who consumes all beings.

कः पुष्करः किं मयो वेति । इदं नाव तत्पुष्करं योऽयमाकाशोऽस्ये माश्चतस्रो दिशश्चतस्र उपदिशोदलसंस्था आसं । अर्वाग्विचरत एत् प्राणादित्या एता उपासीतोमित्येतदक्षरेण व्याहृतिभिः सावित्र्या चेति ॥ (*kaḥ puṣkaraḥ kiṃ mayo veti | idaṃ nāva tatpuṣkaraṃ yo 'yamākāśo 'sye māścatasro diśaścatasra upadiśodalasaṃsthā āsaṃ | arvāgvicarata et prāṇādityā etā upāsītomityetadakṣareṇa vyāhṛtibhiḥ sāvitryā ceti ‖*) (Maitryupaniṣat 6-2)

What is this lotus? What is its nature? What principle is contained in it? This lotus itself is the outer space. The four directions and the four intermediate directions, pervading the outer space, are the leaves of this lotus. This ether of the lotus of the heart, which is located in the heart and is of the nature of breath, and the Āditya pervading the outer space, are mutually attracted. One should worship it with the utterances in the form of Oṃ and with the Gāyatrī mantra. This lotus is itself the earth and is this very Agni. (The ocean which is described in the Purāṇas and elsewhere as the ocean of milk)

is itself this lotus. That is to say, it is the thing that has contained within itself the whole principle of the universe. Describing this very thing in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, the identity of truth and the lotus is stated. It is also stated that the lotus is the womb of truth. But the womb of truth may be in various forms such as the earth; one may say that the lotus too is one among them, or one may say that the earth, the lotus and the rest all reflect one and the same principle. The sentences that show the identity of all these can be seen in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa.
अथ पुष्करपर्णमुपदधाति। योनिर्वै पुष्करपर्णं। योनिमेवैतदुपदधाति । (*atha puṣkaraparṇamupadadhāti| yonirvai puṣkaraparṇaṃ| yonimevaitadupadadhāti |*) (Śa. Brā. 7-4-1-2)

Afterwards the lotus leaf is placed in the middle of the altar. Since the lotus itself is the womb for the production of Agni, he establishes the womb in the form of the lotus. To the question, why should this lotus leaf be placed, यद्वेव पुष्करपर्णमुपदधाति (*yadveva puṣkaraparṇamupadadhāti*), the answer is as follows.

आपो वै पुष्करं तासामियं पर्णं यथा ह वा इदं पुष्करपर्णमप्सध्याहितमेवमियमप्सध्याहिता सेयं योनिरग्नेरियग् ह्यग्निरस्यै हि सर्वोऽग्निश्चीयत इमामेवैतदुपदधाति तामनंतर्हिताग्ं सत्यादुपदधातीमां तत्सत्ये प्रतिष्ठापयति तस्मादियग्ं सत्ये प्रतिष्ठिता................। (*āpo vai puṣkaraṃ tāsāmiyaṃ parṇaṃ yathā ha vā idaṃ puṣkaraparṇamapsadhyāhitamevamiyamapsadhyāhitā seyaṃ yoniragneriyag hyagnirasyai hi sarvo 'gniścīyata imāmevaitadupadadhāti tāmanaṃtarhitāgṃ satyādupadadhātīmāṃ tatsatye pratiṣṭhāpayati tasmādiyagṃ satye pratiṣṭhitā................|*) (Śa. Brā. 7-4-1-8)

The lotus means the principle of the waters. In it this earth is one leaf. In the way that the lotus leaf lies spread out over the water, in the same way this earth also lies spread out and shines in the water in the form of the atmosphere. Since this earth is itself the sacrificial altar, one must understand that this is the womb for the production of Agni. Therefore, by the establishment of the lotus leaf, this very earth is established. The purpose of this establishment is that it should not become separated from truth. Therefore the establishment of the lotus shows that this earth is established on the basis of truth. This earth, even in the midst of all the worlds, has the full nature of truth.

अपां पृष्ठमसि । योनिरग्नेरिति । अपाग्ंहीयं पृष्ठं योनिर्हिर्यमग्नेः समुद्रमभितः पिन्वमानमिति समुद्रो हीमामभितः पिन्वते वर्धमानो महाग्ं....पुष्कर इति वर्धमानो महीयस्व पुष्कर इत्येतद्दिवो मात्रया वरिम्मा स्वेत्यनुविमार्ष्ट्यसौ वा आदित्य एषोऽग्निर्नो हैतमन्यो दिवो वरिमा ॥ (*apāṃ pṛṣṭhamasi | yoniragneriti | apāgṃhīyaṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ yonirhiryamagneḥ samudramabhitaḥ pinvamānamiti samudro hīmāmabhitaḥ pinvate vardhamāno mahāgṃ....puṣkara iti vardhamāno mahīyasva puṣkara ityetaddivo mātrayā varimmā svetyanuvimārṣṭyasau vā āditya eṣo 'gnirno haitamanyo divo varimā ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 7-4-1-9)

O lotus, you are the back of the waters. O vessel of the production of Agni, this earth is the back of the waters and the womb of Agni. Around this earth the ocean (the atmosphere) spreads widely. Therefore, O support of truth, be established spread out upon the lotus; spread out with the extent of the atmosphere and with the same breadth. This Agni is a transformation of the Āditya. Just as only the very wide atmosphere can bear the Āditya, in the same way the support for bearing this Agni must be of very great extent in order to bear the Āditya who is of the form of Agni. Therefore the lotus, the womb of Agni, is prayed to: you also, taking on the form of the atmosphere, bear Agni in me.

In the above description two particulars of the lotus are clear. First, the lotus is the womb of Agni; second, the lotus has the extent of the atmosphere. The outer lotus is only a symbol of the lotus within the heart (the lotus of the heart). Therefore, since the very same extent of the atmosphere belongs also to the lotus of the heart, heaven and earth all are contained in it. Before one knows the nature of the lotus of the heart within the body, one must examine the purport of the metaphor called the lotus.

Among the places where the metaphor of the lotus is specified in the Ṛk Saṃhitā, the passage that describes the origin of Vasiṣṭha is the very first. The statement of the origin of Agni in the present mantra is in the same manner. The manner of the origin of Vasiṣṭha is described in the Saṃhitā thus.

उतासि मैत्रावरुणो वसिष्ठोर्वश्या ब्रह्मन्मनसोऽधिजातः । द्रप्सं स्कन्नं ब्रह्मणा दैव्येन विश्वे देवाः पुष्करे त्वाददंत ॥ (*utāsi maitrāvaruṇo vasiṣṭhorvaśyā brahmanmanaso 'dhijātaḥ | drapsaṃ skannaṃ brahmaṇā daivyena viśve devāḥ puṣkare tvādadaṃta ‖*) (7-33-11)

O Vasiṣṭha, foremost in Brahman, as related to Mitra and Varuṇa you were born of Urvaśī. All the gods also served you, the pure one, with divine rites and bore you in the lotus with the mantras prescribed in the Veda: thus he is praised. This same matter is stated in the Bṛhaddevatā as follows.

तयोरादित्ययोः सत्ते दृष्टाप्सरसमुर्वशीं । रेतश्चस्कंद तत्कुंभे न्यपतद्वासतीवरे ॥ तेनैव तु मुहूर्त्तेन वीर्यवंतौ तपस्विना । अगस्यश्च वसिष्ठश्च तत्रर्षी संबभूवतुः ॥ बहुधा पतिते शुक्रे कलशेऽथ जले स्थले । (*tayorādityayoḥ satte dṛṣṭāpsarasamurvaśīṃ | retaścaskaṃda tatkuṃbhe nyapatadvāsatīvare ‖ tenaiva tu muhūrttena vīryavaṃtau tapasvinā | agasyaśca vasiṣṭhaśca tatrarṣī saṃbabhūvatuḥ ‖ bahudhā patite śukre kalaśe 'tha jale sthale |*)

स्थले वसिष्ठस्तु मुनिः संभूत ऋषिसत्तमः ॥ कुंभेस्त्वगस्यः संभूतो जले मत्स्यो महाद्युतिः । उदियाय ततोऽगस्यः शम्यामात्रो महायशाः ॥ मानेन संमितो यस्मात् तस्मान्मान्य इहोच्यते । यद्वा कुंभादृषिर्जातः कुंभेनापि हि मीयते ॥ कुंभ इत्यभिधानं तु परिमाणस्य लक्ष्यते । ततोऽप्सु गृह्यमाणासु वसिष्ठः पुष्करे स्थितः ॥ सर्वत्र पुष्करं तत्र विश्वे देवा आधारयन् । उत्थाय सलिलात्तस्मादथ तेपे महत्तपः ॥ (*sthale vasiṣṭhastu muniḥ saṃbhūta ṛṣisattamaḥ ‖ kuṃbhestvagasyaḥ saṃbhūto jale matsyo mahādyutiḥ | udiyāya tato 'gasyaḥ śamyāmātro mahāyaśāḥ ‖ mānena saṃmito yasmāt tasmānmānya ihocyate | yadvā kuṃbhādṛṣirjātaḥ kuṃbhenāpi hi mīyate ‖ kuṃbha ityabhidhānaṃ tu parimāṇasya lakṣyate | tato 'psu gṛhyamāṇāsu vasiṣṭhaḥ puṣkare sthitaḥ ‖ sarvatra puṣkaraṃ tatra viśve devā ādhārayan | utthāya salilāttasmādatha tepe mahattapaḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 5-199 to 155) ⟨NOTE:289⟩

Both Mitra and Varuṇa, the Ādityas, saw Urvaśī at a good time. Then, being at once infatuated with desire, there was an emission of their seed. It then fell into the vessel called Vasatīvarī. Immediately, Agastya and Vasiṣṭha, both powerful and ascetics, were produced from it. That fallen seed fell in the pot, in the water, and on the earth. From the part that fell on the earth Vasiṣṭha was produced. From the part that fell in the pot Agastya was produced, and from the part that fell in the water a shining fish. Agastya alone, having the measure of a peg, was born of the measure (the pot), and therefore his name became Mānya. For that very reason he also became famous as the pot-born. Afterwards, at the time of the taking of water, the fact that Vasiṣṭha was standing in the lotus came into view. Then all the gods, receiving Vasiṣṭha who stood in the lotus, praised him. Coming out of the water, Vasiṣṭha performed austerity. ⟨NOTE:290⟩
नामास्य गुणतो जज्ञे वसतेः श्रैष्ट्यकर्मणः (*nāmāsya guṇato jajñe vasateḥ śraiṣṭyakarmaṇaḥ*) (Bṛ. De. 5-156) ⟨NOTE:291⟩

By his excellent qualities and by his good actions this name became famous for him. The explanation of the sentence of the Bṛhaddevatā is that the name Vasiṣṭha is formed from the root वस् (*vas*), which shows excellence.

In the same way, in the present mantra the nature of the churning of fire in the lotus and the manner of the origin of Agni are described. In the Atharvaveda also the same matter is stated, but there is a slight difference in the description (Ath. Saṃ. 10-8-34). ⟨NOTE:292⟩ Thus, in all such contexts the reference to the number three is noteworthy.
Father = Mitra, Varuṇa, Dyau. Mother = Urvaśī, Pṛthvī. Son = Vasiṣṭha, Agni, Āyu.

In this way the triad of divine fatherhood, divine motherhood and divine sonship is famously praised in the Saṃhitās. Moreover, there are many contexts that show the identity of these three divine sons, Agni, Vasiṣṭha and Āyu. In mantras such as एकायुरग्रे, विश आविवाससि (*ekāyuragre, viśa āvivāsasi*) (1-31-5) and विश्वायुरग्ने गुहा गुहं गाः (*viśvāyuragne guhā guhaṃ gāḥ*) (1-67-6) **GLOSS**, and also in
“ आ यस्ते अग्न इधते अनेकं वसिष्ठ शुक्र दीदिवः पावक । (*ā yaste agna idhate anekaṃ vasiṣṭha śukra dīdivaḥ pāvaka |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-1-8) **GLOSS**

and other such mantras, this view becomes clear. In such contexts it has to be said that the words विश्वायु (*viśvāyu*) and वसिष्ठ (*vasiṣṭha*) are adjectives describing the qualities of Agni. But there is also a point to consider: whether there is a difference of purport between the statement that Agni was born from the lotus and the statement that Vasiṣṭha stood in the lotus. First, when it is said पुष्करे स्थितः (*puṣkare sthitaḥ*), one must understand what the precise meaning of the word स्थितः (*sthitaḥ*) is.

It is not right to give the word स्थितः (*sthitaḥ*) the meaning "he was standing in the lotus". स्थितः (*sthitaḥ*) means that he appeared, manifested in his own form. In the Gītā verse ब्रह्माणमीशं कमलासनस्थं (*brahmāṇamīśaṃ kamalāsanasthaṃ*) (Bha. Gī. 11-15) ⟨NOTE:293⟩ **GLOSS** and in Upaniṣad passages such as “स्थितं च यच्च सच्च त्यच्च (*sthitaṃ ca yacca sacca tyacca*)” (Bṛ. U. 2-3-1) **GLOSS**, the word स्थित (*sthita*) has the sense of "manifested" and "pervading"; in the same way it has to be said in the present case.

As explained above, there is on the one hand an identity between Vasiṣṭha who is established in the lotus and Agni who is born from the lotus; on the other hand there is an identity of the lotus, the earth, the atmosphere and the waters. Whether all the descriptions in such contexts can be said to describe one and the same subject: to understand this precisely, some further matters must be examined.

The principle that is described as lotus-based is described also as earth-based. Everything produced from water stands supported by the earth alone. He who is established in the lotus, which is of the form of the earth, is the one whose standing is eternal.
“ पुंडरीकं नवद्वारं....... तस्मिन् यद्यक्षमात्मनत् तद्वै ब्रह्मविदो विदुः । (*puṃḍarīkaṃ navadvāraṃ....... tasmin yadyakṣamātmanat tadvai brahmavido viduḥ |*) (Ath. Saṃ. 10-8-43) ⟨NOTE:294⟩ **GLOSS**

The sight of the lotus, which has nine doors, which is of the form of the seat of Brahman, which belongs to the Self, and in which the Brahman-formed Yakṣa is established, is the goal of the search of the knowers of Brahman; that Brahman-city which is thus described, the Chāndogya Upaniṣad describes as follows:

या वै सा पृथिवीयं वाव सा यदिदमस्मिन् पुरुषे शरीरमस्मिन् हीमे प्राणाः प्रतिष्ठिता एतदेव नातिशीयंते ॥ (*yā vai sā pṛthivīyaṃ vāva sā yadidamasmin puruṣe śarīramasmin hīme prāṇāḥ pratiṣṭhitā etadeva nātiśīyaṃte ‖*) (Chā. U. 3-12 3) ⟨NOTE:295⟩

The principle that is of the form of the earth is also present in the form of the body of man. In it all these vital principles are contained; they do not go beyond that body: so it is praised. Sāyaṇa too, when explaining the purport suggested in the present mantra, in his commentary on this mantra (6-16-13), has stated the same purport.
“ भूमिश्च सर्वजगत आधारभूतेति पुष्करपर्णस्य सर्वजगद्धारकत्वं ॥ (*bhūmiśca sarvajagata ādhārabhūteti puṣkaraparṇasya sarvajagaddhārakatvaṃ ‖*) ” (Sā. Bhā.) ⟨NOTE:296⟩

“Lotus” means lotus leaf. It is the earth that is indicated in this way. Because the earth supports the whole world, the lotus leaf is also praised as the supporter of the whole world. Stating the same matter in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa as well:

सोऽपश्यत्पुष्करपर्णं तिष्ठत् । सोऽमन्यत ।....................स पृथिवीमध अर्थत् । तस्या उपहत्योदमज्जत् । तत्पुष्करपर्णेऽप्रथयत् । यदप्रथयत् । तत्पृथिव्यै पृथिवित्वं ॥ (*so 'paśyatpuṣkaraparṇaṃ tiṣṭhat | so 'manyata |....................sa pṛthivīmadha arthat | tasyā upahatyodamajjat | tatpuṣkaraparṇe 'prathayat | yadaprathayat | tatpṛthivyai pṛthivitvaṃ ‖*) (Tai. Brā. 1-1-3 6) ⟨NOTE:297⟩

Here the manner in which Prajāpati, the creator of the world, created the world is told. Before the creation of the world everything was of the form of water. Then Prajāpati, having a plan in the form of meditation as to in what manner the creation of beings could take place, saw in that very water a lotus leaf standing with its root upward. Then, resolving that this lotus leaf must be the support of the whole world, moving and unmoving, he dived into the water near the lotus leaf in order to seize in the water the earth, which is the support of beings. He then took out the earth, which was of the form of clay, placed it on the lotus and made it spread out widely. That became the earth, the support of the world. Therefore it is understood from this that water, atmosphere, lotus and earth have all become transformations of one source. Or it may be said that the lotus itself was transformed into the form of the earth.
श्यामग्ने पुष्करादधीश्वाह पुष्करवर्णे ह्येनमुपाश्रितमविंदत् । ( (*śyāmagne puṣkarādadhīśvāha puṣkaravarṇe hyenamupāśritamaviṃdat | (*) (Kai. Saṃ. 5-1-4-4) ⟨NOTE:298⟩

Sāyaṇa has also quoted the Taittirīya Saṃhitā passage that the Aṅgirases realised Agni, who had taken refuge in the lotus leaf. There too the aim is to show the identity of the earth and the lotus. The epithet अपांनपात् (*apāṃnapāt*) makes known the nature of Agni born from water. Since the lotus leaf is also a part of that same great water, Agni who has taken refuge in the lotus leaf is likewise described by the very epithet अपांनपात् (*apāṃnapāt*). But if it is asked what connection there is between the statement that Agni took refuge in the lotus leaf and the statement that Vasiṣṭha was standing in the lotus leaf, and what occasion there is for joining the two matters together, the answer is that it has been subtly shown above that Vasiṣṭha too is a transformation of Agni. There are also many contexts in which the identity of Agni and Vasiṣṭha is stated.
“ आदब्बव्रतप्रमतिर्वसिष्ठ इत्यग्निर्वै देवानां वसिष्ठः (*ādabbavratapramatirvasiṣṭha ityagnirvai devānāṃ vasiṣṭhaḥ*) ” (Ai. Brā. 1-28)

Here, in explaining the Ṛk-saṃhitā sentence (2-9-1), the identity is clearly shown: Agni himself, being in the highest degree the cause of dwelling, is Vasiṣṭha, the best among the gods. Moreover, that very Prajāpati who caused the beings that were enveloped in water to be established in the lotus leaf is also described as Vasiṣṭha.

प्रजापतिर्ह ना एतेनाग्रे यज्ञेनेजे !..................स वै दक्षो नाम । तद्यदेनेन सोऽग्रेऽयजत तस्माद्दाक्षायणयज्ञो नामोतैनमेके वसिष्ठयज्ञ इत्याचक्षत एष वै वसिष्ठ एतमेव तदन्वा चक्षते स एतेन यज्ञेनेजे । (*prajāpatirha nā etenāgre yajñeneje !..................sa vai dakṣo nāma | tadyadenena so 'gre 'yajata tasmāddākṣāyaṇayajño nāmotainameke vasiṣṭhayajña ityācakṣata eṣa vai vasiṣṭha etameva tadanvā cakṣate sa etena yajñeneje |*) (Śa. Brā. 2-4-4-2)

Prajāpati, wishing first for offspring, worshipped with a sacrifice. He himself is the one named Dakṣa; that sacrifice became famous as the Dākṣāyaṇa sacrifice. Since this same Prajāpati is also renowned as Vasiṣṭha, it is customary to call it the Vasiṣṭha sacrifice: thus the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa shows the identity of Prajāpati and Vasiṣṭha. The description that this Prajāpati, being of the form of Vasiṣṭha, created the world on the support of the lotus occurs in many places. For example:

तस्य नाभेरभूत्पद्मं सहस्रार्कोरुदीधिति । सर्वजीवनिकायैको यत्र स्वयनुभूत्स्वराट् ॥ सोऽनुविष्टो भगवता यः शीते सलिलाशये । लोकसंस्थां यथापूर्वं निर्ममे संस्थया स्वया ॥ (*tasya nābherabhūtpadmaṃ sahasrārkorudīdhiti | sarvajīvanikāyaiko yatra svayanubhūtsvarāṭ ‖ so 'nuviṣṭo bhagavatā yaḥ śīte salilāśaye | lokasaṃsthāṃ yathāpūrvaṃ nirmame saṃsthayā svayā ‖*) (Śrīmad Bhāgavata 3-20-15, 16)

From the navel of Prajāpati a lotus came forth. It shone like a thousand suns. In that very lotus the self-born Prajāpati held sovereignty, and it was the dwelling of all living beings. The Lord entered into that very lotus. It stood in the water and became the support and the means of the conduct of the world. In this way the description of Prajāpati's resolve to create and the description of the lotus, the support of the world, occur in the Purāṇas and others just as they do in the Saṃhitās and others.
Just as the sacrificial altar, which is the navel of the universe, is famous as the womb of Agni, so also the lotus is the womb and the support of Agni.

“ अग्निर्देवेभ्य उदक्रामत्सोऽपः प्राविशत्ते देवाः प्रजापतिमब्रुवंस्वमिममन्विच्छ ........पुष्करपर्णे विवेद (*agnirdevebhya udakrāmatso 'paḥ prāviśatte devāḥ prajāpatimabruvaṃsvamimamanviccha ........puṣkaraparṇe viveda*) ” (Śa. Brā. 7-3-2-14)

When Agni disappeared from the gods, the gods addressed Prajāpati: "You are the father of Agni. He will appear to you. Therefore search and find where he is." When they prayed thus, Prajāpati searched for Agni and at last found Agni, who was in the lotus leaf: so it says.

Just as the altar, the womb of Agni, is said to be the navel of the whole universe, so the lotus, the womb of Agni, is praised as the navel of the whole universe. The Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, stating this matter, has made clear all the points explained above. While constructing the sacrificial altar, which is the womb of Agni and the navel of the universe, it shows the identity of lotus, earth, water and truth, and describes that, as in the present mantra, the lotus leaf of the nature of truth is the supporter and bearer of the world. The procedure to be followed when constructing the sacrificial altar is stated thus:
अथ पुष्करपर्णमुपदधाति । योनिर्वै पुष्करपर्णं योनिमेवैतदुपदधाति। (*atha puṣkaraparṇamupadadhāti | yonirvai puṣkaraparṇaṃ yonimevaitadupadadhāti|*) (Śa. Brā. 7-4-1-7)
Since the lotus leaf is itself the womb of Agni, it is to be placed in the middle of the sacrificial altar in the form of an ornament. (The purport is that it is the source of the origin of Agni.)

यद्वेव पुस्करपर्णमुपदधाति । आपो वै पुष्करं तासामियं पर्णं यथा ह वा इदं पुष्करपर्णमप्सृध्याहितमेवमियमप्सृध्याहिता सेयं योनिरग्नेरियग्स् ह्यग्निरस्मै हि सर्वोऽग्निश्चीयत इमामेवैतदुपदधाति तामनंतर्हिताग्ं सत्याद्दुपदधातीमां तत्सत्ये प्रतिष्ठापयति तस्मादियग्ं सत्ये प्रतिष्ठिता........ ॥ (*yadveva puskaraparṇamupadadhāti | āpo vai puṣkaraṃ tāsāmiyaṃ parṇaṃ yathā ha vā idaṃ puṣkaraparṇamapsṛdhyāhitamevamiyamapsṛdhyāhitā seyaṃ yoniragneriyags hyagnirasmai hi sarvo 'gniścīyata imāmevaitadupadadhāti tāmanaṃtarhitāgṃ satyāddupadadhātīmāṃ tatsatye pratiṣṭhāpayati tasmādiyagṃ satye pratiṣṭhitā........ ‖*) (Sa. Brā. 7-4-1-8) ⟨NOTE:299⟩

Why should the lotus leaf be placed in the middle of the sacrificial altar? The answer: the lotus is water. This earth is its leaf. Just as the lotus leaf lies spread on the water, so this earth lies spread on the water of the atmosphere. This earth is the womb of Agni. In it the sacrificial altar too is constructed. From it Agni is born. Therefore, by placing the lotus leaf in the middle of the altar, the earth itself is established in it. Thereby the earth is established in truth. This establishing shows the identity of the earth, which is of the form of the lotus, with truth.

अपां पृष्ठमसि । योनिरग्नेरिति । अपां हीयं पृष्ठं योनिर्हियमग्नेः समुद्रमभितः पिन्वमानमिति समुद्रो हीमामभितः पिन्वते.......... (*apāṃ pṛṣṭhamasi | yoniragneriti | apāṃ hīyaṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ yonirhiyamagneḥ samudramabhitaḥ pinvamānamiti samudro hīmāmabhitaḥ pinvate..........*) (Śa. Brā. 7-4-1-9)
Here there is a description of Agni in the lotus that is spread widely in the middle of the water. This explanation has been given above. After that:

यद्वेव पुष्करपर्ण उपदधाति । प्रतिष्ठा वै पुष्करपर्णमियं वै पुष्करपर्णमियमु वै प्रतिष्ठा यो वा अस्यामप्रतिष्ठितोऽपि दूरे सन्नप्रतिष्ठित एव स रश्मिभिर्वा एषोऽस्यां प्रतिष्ठितोऽस्यामेवैनमेतत्पतिष्ठायां प्रतिष्ठापयति ॥ (*yadveva puṣkaraparṇa upadadhāti | pratiṣṭhā vai puṣkaraparṇamiyaṃ vai puṣkaraparṇamiyamu vai pratiṣṭhā yo vā asyāmapratiṣṭhito 'pi dūre sannapratiṣṭhita eva sa raśmibhirvā eṣo 'syāṃ pratiṣṭhito 'syāmevainametatpatiṣṭhāyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 7-4-1-12)

The question again is why the lotus leaf should be established. The lotus is this earth. This earth is the support of everything. Therefore the lotus too is the holder and support of everything. He who is not firmly established on this earth always remains one of unstable condition. Even Āditya in the atmosphere has obtained stability by making this very earth his support in the form of his rays. Therefore, if this lotus is established on the sacrificial altar, a support in the form of the earth is also provided for Agni: so it says. But if it is asked what is the reason for its getting the name Puṣkara, the answer is as follows.

इंद्रो वृत्रग्ंहत्वा नास्तृषीति मन्यमानोऽपः प्राविशत्ता अब्रवीद्विभेमि वै पुरं मे कुरुतेति स योऽपाग्ं रस आसीत्तमूर्ध्वग्ं समुदौहंस्तामस्मै पुरमकुर्वंस्तद्यदस्मै पुरमकुर्वंस्तस्मात्पूष्करं पूष्करं ह वै तत्पुष्करमित्याचक्षते परोक्षं परोक्षकामा हि देवाः ॥ (*iṃdro vṛtragṃhatvā nāstṛṣīti manyamāno 'paḥ prāviśattā abravīdvibhemi vai puraṃ me kuruteti sa yo 'pāgṃ rasa āsīttamūrdhvagṃ samudauhaṃstāmasmai puramakurvaṃstadyadasmai puramakurvaṃstasmātpūṣkaraṃ pūṣkaraṃ ha vai tatpuṣkaramityācakṣate parokṣaṃ parokṣakāmā hi devāḥ ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 7-4-1-13)

Indra, thinking that Vṛtrāsura, though struck with the thunderbolt, had not yet fallen, entered the water in fear. Then he prayed to the gods: "I am afraid. Make a fortress for my protection." Then they gathered the essence of the water and made from it a protective fortress. Because they made (kar) a fortress (pūḥ), it got the name Puṣkara. Because the gods are fond of the indirect, they called the Puṣkara by the name Pūṣkara. Thus the supporting nature and firmness of this lotus are described. It is clear that the very essence of the water in which he stood before the creation of the universe, the support of the universe, is this lotus, and that this same lotus is spread out in the form of the earth.
(On this same lotus they place the golden vessel that reflects the disc of the sun. The golden vessel, the representative of this solar disc, reflects the Supreme Person.)

In this way this lotus, which is described as the support of the whole universe, is the essence of the water that is the root of the world. This water principle is both pervading and nourishing the universe. As has been explained in some places before (Ṛ. Saṃ. Part 12, page 233), that the solar principle known as the Vāruṇa horse has obtained a firm refuge in the water of the atmosphere, so also in the present case the purport is that all who have obtained the refuge of this lotus attain a stable condition. The same kind of description as was explained before of the water of the atmosphere, the refuge of the Vāruṇa horse, is also given of the lotus, which is a refuge and support. In this account the lotus, which is the boat form of Vasiṣṭha, another embodiment of Agni, is described.

आ यद्रुहाव वरुणश्च नावं प्र यत्समुद्रमीरयाव मध्यं । अधि यदपां स्नुभिश्चराव प्र प्रेंख ईंखयावहै तुभे कं ॥ (*ā yadruhāva varuṇaśca nāvaṃ pra yatsamudramīrayāva madhyaṃ | adhi yadapāṃ snubhiścarāva pra preṃkha īṃkhayāvahai tubhe kaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7. 88. 3)
When I (Vasiṣṭha) and Varuṇa together board the boat and enter the ocean of the atmosphere, and when we enter the middle of the water, then we two experience a rocking and pleasant voyage.

वसिष्ठं ह वरुणो नाव्याधादृषिं चकार स्वपा महोभिः । स्तोतारं विप्रः सुदिन्वते अह्नां यान्नु द्यावस्ततनन्यादुषासः ॥ (*vasiṣṭhaṃ ha varuṇo nāvyādhādṛṣiṃ cakāra svapā mahobhiḥ | stotāraṃ vipraḥ sudinvate ahnāṃ yānnu dyāvastatananyāduṣāsaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-88-4)

When Varuṇa seated Vasiṣṭha in the boat for the voyage through the atmosphere, and when he made him, taken under his protection, a doer of good works, then the wise Vasiṣṭha provided for his worshipper pleasant and long days and nights. This boat of Vasiṣṭha reflects the vehicle of the conscious being that carries on the journey of life. The lotus itself is this vehicle.

This vehicle, which is of the form of the lotus, is of two kinds. One reflects the earth and the other the atmosphere. But this does not mean that the earth and the atmosphere are two different principles. The earth is only a replica of the atmosphere.

अपां पृष्ठमसि सप्रथा उर्वग्निं भरिष्यदपरावपिष्ठं । वर्धमानं मह आ च पुष्करं दिवो मात्रया वरिणा प्रथस्व ॥ (*apāṃ pṛṣṭhamasi saprathā urvagniṃ bhariṣyadaparāvapiṣṭhaṃ | vardhamānaṃ maha ā ca puṣkaraṃ divo mātrayā variṇā prathasva ‖*) (Tai. Saṃ. 4-1-3-1)

O earth, you are the back of the waters. You have an expanse that bears Agni. Take on the firmness of the lotus and the expanse of the atmosphere: thus the similarity of nature with the atmosphere is praised. The Aitareya Brāhmaṇa states this same point still more clearly.
अस्य वै लोकस्यासौ लोकोऽनुरूपोऽमुष्य लोकस्यायं लोकोऽनु रूपः । (*asya vai lokasyāsau loko 'nurūpo 'muṣya lokasyāyaṃ loko 'nu rūpaḥ |*) (Ai. Brā. 8-2)

The two worlds, earth and atmosphere, correspond to each other. It means that each is the reflection of the other. The purport is that these two are not different principles. Or these may also be called the higher water and the lower water. The fact that this has been divided into two, the ocean on the earth and the ocean in the atmosphere, has been explained before together with the explanation in the sentences of the Nirukta authors. (This point was explained earlier while treating of the ocean.) Explaining this same point in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa also:
“ अग्ने दिवो अर्णमच्छा जिगासीति । आपो वा अस्य दिवो अर्णः (*agne divo arṇamacchā jigāsīti | āpo vā asya divo arṇaḥ*) ” (Śa. Brā. 7-1-1-24)
It is stated in sentences such as: O Agni, in the form of smoke you enter the flow of the ocean of the atmosphere. Moreover, explaining the same view further:

“ तौ होचतुः । मुख्यौ वा आवां यज्ञस्य स्वो यावध्वर्यो इह नाविमं पुरस्ताद्ग्रहं पर्याहरताभि द्विदेवत्यानीति ताभ्यामेतं........................ तृतीय एव वषट् क्रियतेऽथ यदश्विनावितीमे हीदग्ं सर्वमाश्नुवातां पुष्करस्रजावित्यग्निरेवास्यै पुष्करमादित्योऽमुष्यै ॥ ( (*tau hocatuḥ | mukhyau vā āvāṃ yajñasya svo yāvadhvaryo iha nāvimaṃ purastādgrahaṃ paryāharatābhi dvidevatyānīti tābhyāmetaṃ........................ tṛtīya eva vaṣaṭ kriyate 'tha yadaśvināvitīme hīdagṃ sarvamāśnuvātāṃ puṣkarasrajāvityagnirevāsyai puṣkaramādityo 'muṣyai ‖ (*) (Śa. Brā. 4-1-5-16)
Here the praise of the Aśvin gods, who wear lotus garlands, occurs. In this praise Agni is praised as the lotus of the earth and the Sun as the lotus of the atmosphere.

In this way the description that Agni, who is of the form of the lotus, obtained his existence in the lotus shows, in the present mantra, the nature of the lotus, which is the supporter of the whole world and the bearer of the world.

In this lotus, which is the bearer and supporter of the universe, the statement that the seer Atharvan churned Agni and brought him forth carries a spiritual purport. Who is this seer Atharvan? Is he born of a divine portion, or does he belong merely to the company of men? This matter must be considered. The Taittirīya Saṃhitā tells of the seer Atharvan in this way:
प्रजाप्रतिर्वा अथर्वाग्निरेव दध्यज्ञाथवर्णस्तस्येष्टका । (*prajāpratirvā atharvāgnireva dadhyajñāthavarṇastasyeṣṭakā |*) (Tai. Saṃ. 5-6-6-3)

Here it is stated that Atharvan is Prajāpati and that his son Dadhīci is Agni. When the nature of the lotus was described above, it was told how Prajāpati, before the creation of the universe, standing in the water, made the lotus the support of his creation. The explanation of the present mantra is that this very Prajāpati, the creator, being designated Atharvan, churned Agni and brought him forth. The same matter of Atharvan's churning of Agni is also stated by reciting this very mantra (Tai. Saṃ. 3-5-11-3). In all the Upaniṣads Atharvan is very famous as a knower of Brahman.

ओं ब्रह्मा देवानां प्रथमः संबभूव विश्वस्य कर्ता भुवनस्य गोप्ता । स ब्रह्मविद्या सर्वविद्यांप्रतिष्ठामथर्वाय ज्येष्ठपुत्राय प्राह ॥ अथर्वणे यां प्रवदेत ब्रह्माधर्वा तां पुरोवाचांगिरे ब्रह्मविद्यां ॥ (*oṃ brahmā devānāṃ prathamaḥ saṃbabhūva viśvasya kartā bhuvanasya goptā | sa brahmavidyā sarvavidyāṃpratiṣṭhāmatharvāya jyeṣṭhaputrāya prāha ‖ atharvaṇe yāṃ pravadeta brahmādharvā tāṃ purovācāṃgire brahmavidyāṃ ‖*) (Mu. U. 1-1-1) ⟨NOTE:300⟩

Among all the gods Brahmā came into being first. He became the maker of the whole universe and its protector. Brahmā taught the knowledge of Brahman, the support of all knowledge, to his eldest son Atharvan. Atharvan afterwards taught it to the seer Aṅgirā. Thus in many ways Atharvan is praised as the very source of all the knowledge of Brahman that has come to men. The matter described in the present mantra is explained in the Śatapatha as follows.

अथर्वा त्वा प्रथमो निरमंथदग्न इति प्राणो वा अथर्वा प्राणो ना एतमग्ने निरमंथत्तद्योऽसावग्रेऽग्निरसृज्यत । त्वामग्ने पुष्करादथर्वा निरमंथतेत्यापो वै पुष्करं........ .... वाघतः सर्वस्य मूर्ध्न इत्येतत् । (*atharvā tvā prathamo niramaṃthadagna iti prāṇo vā atharvā prāṇo nā etamagne niramaṃthattadyo 'sāvagre 'gnirasṛjyata | tvāmagne puṣkarādatharvā niramaṃthatetyāpo vai puṣkaraṃ........ .... vāghataḥ sarvasya mūrdhna ityetat |*) (Śa. Brā. 6-4-2-1, 2)

Agni is the supporter of all. It was Atharvan who first caused this Agni to be born. Atharvan is of the form of the vital breath. This vital breath became the means of the churning of fire. The lotus which is praised in the statement that he caused Agni to appear from the lotus is the water. Atharvan, who is of the form of the vital breath

caused Agni to be born from the water: thus an account containing a spiritual secret is given. Another special point must also be noticed. The words वाघतः सर्वस्य मूर्ध्न इत्येतत् (*vāghataḥ sarvasya mūrdhna ityetat*) mean that he caused him to appear from the head of each sacrificer and from the head of the universe itself.
Since Atharvan was the cause of the first appearance of Agni after the time of creation, all who perform sacrificial rites follow the procedure that Atharvan followed.
इममु त्यमथर्ववदग्निं मंथंति वेधसः । यमंकूयंतमानयन्नमूरं श्याव्याभ्यः ॥ (*imamu tyamatharvavadagniṃ maṃthaṃti vedhasaḥ | yamaṃkūyaṃtamānayannamūraṃ śyāvyābhyaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-15-17)

In the manner in which Atharvan formerly churned this wise and intelligent Agni and caused him to be born, the other priests too, following the same rule, perform the act of churning fire: thus Atharvan's quality of being a guide is praised.

अग्निर्जातो अथर्वणा विदद्विश्वानि काव्या । भुवद्दूतो विवस्वतो वि वो मदे प्रियो यमस्य काम्यो विवक्षसे ॥ (*agnirjāto atharvaṇā vidadviśvāni kāvyā | bhuvaddūto vivasvato vi vo made priyo yamasya kāmyo vivakṣase ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-21-5)

Agni, born from Atharvan's act of churning, knows all the acts of praise. In praising him as the messenger of all sacrificers and a benefactor of the world, there is praise of the seer Atharvan as the cause of this benefit to the world. That this same Atharvan was the cause and guide of the world's progress on the path of truth is praised in sentences such as “ यज्ञैरथर्वा प्रथमो वि धारयद्देवा दक्षैर्भृगवः सं चिकित्रिरे (*yajñairatharvā prathamo vi dhārayaddevā dakṣairbhṛgavaḥ saṃ cikitrire*) ” (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-92-10) and others. Moreover:

यज्ञैरथर्वा प्रथमः पथस्तते ततः सूरो व्रतपा वेन अजनि । आ गा आजदुशना काव्यः सचा यमस्य जातममृतं यजामहे ॥ (*yajñairatharvā prathamaḥ pathastate tataḥ sūro vratapā vena ajani | ā gā ājaduśanā kāvyaḥ sacā yamasya jātamamṛtaṃ yajāmahe ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-83-5)

When the Paṇis stole the cows, the seer named Atharvan performed a sacrifice addressed to Indra. With the help of that sacrifice he found, before all others, the paths by which the cows had been carried off. Then Indra, the guardian of vows, the radiant one, appeared in the form of the sun to show the way. With this help Atharvan recovered the cows. In such ways too Atharvan's benefit to the world is praised.

It is praised in the Atharvaveda that this great-souled Atharvan lives in the world of heaven as a friend of the gods (Ath. Saṃ. 4-1-7) ⟨NOTE:301⟩. Because Atharvan had such greatness, the sacrificial fire born from him is also designated by this very name.

आ नूनमश्विनोर्यषिः स्तोमं चिकेत वामया । आ सोमं मधुमत्तमं घर्म० सिंचादथर्वणि ॥ (*ā nūnamaśvinoryaṣiḥ stomaṃ ciketa vāmayā | ā somaṃ madhumattamaṃ gharma0 siṃcādatharvaṇi ‖*) (Ma. Sa. 8-9-7) ⟨NOTE:302⟩ **GLOSS**

In sentences such as this it is stated that Agni too, since he was churned out by Atharvan, is praised as Atharvan himself. The Nirukta authors have given the explanation of the word अथर्वन् (*atharvan*) in this way.

The purport is that they are those who have no ever-moving, wandering way, that is, they are steady in nature, not of fickle disposition, masters of the Self: thus the nature of Atharvan and of his line is told. The greatness of this great seer is praised in the Purāṇas and elsewhere in this way.

ततः स भगवांस्तत्र अंगिराः समदृश्यत । अथर्ववेदमंत्रैश्च देवेंद्रं समपूजयत् ॥ ततस्तु भगवानिंद्रः संहृष्टः समपद्यत । वरं च प्रददौ तस्मै अथर्वांगिरसे तदा ॥ अथर्वांगिरसं नाम वेदेऽस्मिन्वै भविष्यति । उदाहरणमेतद्धि यज्ञभागं च लप्स्यसे ॥ (*tataḥ sa bhagavāṃstatra aṃgirāḥ samadṛśyata | atharvavedamaṃtraiśca deveṃdraṃ samapūjayat ‖ tatastu bhagavāniṃdraḥ saṃhṛṣṭaḥ samapadyata | varaṃ ca pradadau tasmai atharvāṃgirase tadā ‖ atharvāṃgirasaṃ nāma vede 'sminvai bhaviṣyati | udāharaṇametaddhi yajñabhāgaṃ ca lapsyase ‖*) (Mahābhārata, U. Pa. 18-5 to 7) ⟨NOTE:303⟩

Then the sage Aṅgiras stood before Indra and praised Indra with the mantras of the Atharvaveda. Indra was thereby delighted and said to that great seer: "Let this be the sign that in the Atharvaveda there will be a part called Atharvāṅgirasa and that you are the seer of that mantra. You will receive the chief share in the sacrifice." So he is praised.

en: Sāyaṇa says: O Agni, that very you, of the qualities stated, Dadhyañc by name, the seer, the son of Atharvan, kindled, that is, caused to blaze. Of what kind? वृत्रहणं (*vṛtrahaṇaṃ*), the slayer of the enemies who are obstructers, and पुरंदरं (*puraṃdaraṃ*), the splitter of the cities of the Asuras.
- पुरंदरं (*puraṃdaraṃ*)—the destroyer of the cities of enemies
O Agni, that very you, the slayer of Vṛtrāsura and the destroyer of the cities of enemies, the seer Dadhīci, son of the seer Atharvan, caused to blaze.
The Rishi, Dadhyanch, the son of Atharavan, kindled the slayer of Vritra, the destroyer of the cities of the Asuras.

Dadhyañc the seer: the seer called Dadhyañc or Dadhīci is famous in the Purāṇas and elsewhere. The commentator tells a story here. While the seer Dadhyañc, the son of one called Atharvan, was alive, the Asuras fled in fear at the mere sight of him. After he died and went to heaven, the Asuras spread fearlessly over the whole earth. Then Indra, unable to fight these Asuras, looked for that seer. It became known that the seer had gone to heaven. Then Indra asked those who were near whether any remnant of the seer's limbs was left, and they said that only the skull of the horse's head, with which Dadhīci had once taught the Madhu-vidyā to the Aśvin gods, remained, and that where even that was, they did not know. When Indra then told them to search for it, they found it lying in the lake called Śaryaṇāvat near Kurukṣetra

and brought it. With the bones of that skull Indra conquered the Asuras. That is, he made the magical net of the Asuras fail "nine times", that is, eight hundred and ten times. Here, in explaining the number "nine times ninety", the commentator says: To conquer the gods who are in the three worlds, the Asuras at first had three kinds of magical divisions.
