Since each of these was of three kinds, present, past and future, there were nine kinds in all. Again, these nine magics, combined with the three powers beginning with energy, became 9 × 3 = 27. Again, combined with the three qualities beginning with sattva, they became 27 × 3 = 81. Since these eighty-one magics are practised in the ten directions, the total became 81 × 10 = 810, or "nine times ninety", 9 × 90 = 810. Indra rendered useless in this way the magical nets of the Asuras, who are of the form of Vṛtra: so he explains (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-80-16).

Skandasvāmin tells another story. Formerly there were Asuras called Kālakañjas. Becoming powerful, they killed the gods and caused them great trouble. Then the gods went to Brahmā and prayed that he would tell them a means of destroying these Asuras. Brahmā said: "O gods, there is a seer named Dadhyañc. Go near him. He will tell you a suitable means for the destruction of the Asuras." The gods, as Brahmā had said, went to the seer Dadhīci and reported that Brahmā had sent them. That seer, knowing by yogic vision the purpose for which they had come, gave up his vital breaths in yogic trance. Then Indra destroyed the Asuras with the bones of that seer. Skandasvāmin explains that this very matter is described in this Ṛk (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-80-16).

It is traditionally said that the head of the seer Dadhīci was like a horse's head and that it had been given to him by the Aśvin gods. After the seer Dadhīci died, Indra searched for his head, which was like a horse's head. It is explained in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-84-13 that it was found hidden behind a mountain in a lake called Śaryaṇāvat.

On the question how the seer Dadhīci came to have a horse's head, Skandasvāmin tells an earlier story. Indra taught the seer Dadhīci, son of Atharvan, the nature of the Supreme Brahman called Madhu, and said that he must not tell it to anyone and that if he did tell it, his head would fall off. After some time the Aśvin gods came near that seer Dadhīci and asked him to explain the nature of Brahman that Indra had taught him. The seer Dadhīci said to them that Indra had said that if he told them this matter his head would fall off, and that out of that fear

he would not tell. The Aśvin gods said: "Do not worry about that. If your head falls off, we shall give you another head." Dadhīci agreed and told them. Then, when the head of the seer Dadhīci fell off, the Aśvin gods cut off the head of a horse, brought it and joined it to the body of the seer Dadhīci. Thus it is described that the head of the seer Dadhīci is like the head of a horse. The seer Kakṣīvān describes this matter in the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-12 and 1-117-22.

The name of this seer is mentioned in the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in the Ṛks 1-80-16; 1-84-13; 1-84-14; 1-116-12; 1-117-22; 1-119-9 and others, and in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā 5-1-4-4; 5-6-6-3, the Kāṭhaka Saṃhitā 19-4, the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 4-1-5-18; 6-4-2-3; 14-1-1-18; 14-1-1-20; 14-1-1-25; 14-1-4-13, and the Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 2-5-22; 4-5-28 and other places.

Sāyaṇa says: Pāthya Vṛṣan is the name of a certain seer. O Agni, that very you he kindled, that is, caused to blaze. Of what kind? दस्युहंतमं (*dasyuhaṃtamaṃ*), in the highest degree the slayer of the enemies ⟨NOTE:304⟩, and धनंजयं (*dhanaṃjayaṃ*), the winner of riches in every battle.
notes: ನಪುರಾದ printed in the gloss; garbled

en: O Agni, that very you, the destroyer of enemies and the winner of wealth in every battle, the seer called Vṛṣan, the son of Pathya, caused to blaze exceedingly.
(The Rishi) Pathya, the showerer, kindled you, the destroyer of the Dasyu, the winner of spoil in battle.

Pāthya Vṛṣan: the name of a seer called Pathya occurs nowhere else than in this Ṛk. But the name of a seer called Vṛṣan occurs only in this Ṛk and in the Ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-36-10. In both places there is mention only of this seer's kindling Agni well. Since the name of this seer occurs nowhere else, nothing more can be said about him.

Sāyaṇa states the use. In the Ukthya rite, at the third pressing, the two tṛcas beginning with एहू षु (*ehū ṣu*) are the stotriya and anurūpa of the Maitrāvaruṇa priest (Ā. 6-1). In the Abhiplavika Ukthya rites they are alternative stotriya and anurūpa, and this is also laid down in the sūtra: एह्यू षु ब्रवाणि त अग्निरगामि भारतः (*ehyū ṣu bravāṇi ta agniragāmi bhārataḥ*) (Ā. 7-8). In the Punarādheyikī Iṣṭi the verse beginning एहू षु (*ehū ṣu*) is the anuvākyā of the later Ājyabhāga offering; and this too is laid down in the sūtra: एह्यू षु ब्रवाणि त इत्याग्नेयावाज्यभागौ (*ehyū ṣu bravāṇi ta ityāgneyāvājyabhāgau*) (Ā. 2-8).

Sāyaṇa explains: O Agni, come. For you, for your sake, I shall speak the praises well, in this manner; this is a wish: listen to those praises. The particle उ (*u*) is said to be तूरकं (*tūrakaṃ*) ⟨NOTE:305⟩. The word "listen" is to be supplied after "other praises", meaning the praises made by the Asuras. The Brāhmaṇa also says so: अग्न इत्थेतरा गिर इत्यसुर्या ह वा इतरा गिरः (*agna itthetarā gira ityasuryā ha vā itarā giraḥ*) (Ai. Brā. 3-49). Moreover, you grow with these Soma drops; increase.
notes: ನಮ್ಮರಾದ printed; sense uncertain

en: O Agni, be pleased to come. I shall recite, addressed to you, also the praises recited by others, in this prescribed manner and exceedingly. By these praises and by these Somas you grow strong.
Come, Agni, that I may address to you other praises in this manner : augment with these libations.

At the third pressing of the sacrifice called Ukthya, the priest called Maitrāvaruṇa is to recite as stotriya and anurūpa mantras the two tṛcas beginning with एह्यू षु (*ehyū ṣu*) (the Ṛks 16 to 21 of this sūkta); and likewise in the Ukthya sacrifices connected with the Abhiplava these Ṛks are to be used as alternative stotriya and anurūpa mantras. This is set forth by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, एह्यू षु ब्रवाणि त आग्निरगामि भारतः (*ehyū ṣu bravāṇi ta āgniragāmi bhārataḥ*) (Ā. 7-8). And in the offering called Punarādheya this Ṛk beginning एह्यू षु (*ehyū ṣu*) is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra of the Ājyabhāga; this is set forth by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, एह्यू षु ब्रवाणि त इत्याग्नेयावाज्यभागौ (*ehyū ṣu bravāṇi ta ityāgneyāvājyabhāgau*) (Ā. 2-8).

Sāyaṇa says: O Agni, wherever, in whatever place, with whatever sacrificer your mind, that is, your inner organ of favour, is present, there, in that sacrificer, you bear a higher, better दक्षं (*dakṣaṃ*), that is, strength-giving food. And you also make a seat there, that is, you make a dwelling place in that sacrificer.
- मनः (*manaḥ*)—mind of the nature of favour
- क्व च (*kva ca*)—in whatever sacrificer (it is directed)
- तत्र (*tatra*)—in that place and in that sacrificer

O Agni, in whatever place and in whatever sacrificer your mind, which is of the nature of favour, is directed, in that place and in that sacrificer you bring about more abundant and strong food; and you also make for yourself an excellent place.
Wherever, and upon whatever your mind is directed, you bestow uncommon vigour, and there you make your abode.

Sāyaṇa says: O Agni, may your पूर्तं (*pūrtaṃ*), filling brilliance, not become अक्षिपत् (*akṣipat*), one that falls upon the eyes, a destroyer; may it always give us the power of sight. O नेमानां वसो (*nemānāṃ vaso*): the word नेम (*nema*) means "few"; you are the one who gives dwelling to some few sacrificers among men. Therefore accept दुवः (*duvaḥ*), the service done by us, the sacrificers.
- अक्षिपत् (*akṣipat*)—being of a sharpness that pierces our eyes
- नहि भुवत् (*nahi bhuvat*)—may it not become
notes: ಸಂಹಿತಾಪಾಠ ends ॥ ೨೧ ॥ but ಪದಪಾಠ ends ॥ ೨೦ ॥; Ṛk number taken from the Saṃhitā line

en: O Agni, giver of dwelling to sacrificers of our own only ⟨NOTE:307⟩, may your full brilliance not become of a sharpness that pierces our eyes. For that very reason accept our services.
notes: abbreviation ಋಗ್ವೇ. printed

en: Let not your full (blaze) be distressing to the eye, giver of dwellings, to your humble votaries, and therefore accept our worship.

Sāyaṇa says: This Agni has been approached by us with praises. Of what kind? भारतः (*bhārataḥ*), the bearer of the oblations; the slayer of the enemies of King Divodāsa, so named; the knower of many, that is, all-knowing; सत्पतिः (*satpatiḥ*), the protector of good sacrificers.
- आ आगामि (*ā āgāmi*)—has been brought here (by our praises)
Agni, the bearer of the oblation, the destroyer of the enemies of the king called Divodāsa, the all-knowing, the protector of good sacrificers, has been brought here by our praises.
Agni, the bearer (of oblations), the destroyer of the enemies of Divodasa, the cognizant of many, the protector of the good, has been brought hither (by our praises).
Divodāsa: see what we have explained about Divodāsa on pages 570-571.

Sāyaṇa says: That Agni, surpassing all beings born on the earth, by his greatness, that is, by his own glory, let him give us wealth. Or else: let him give in excess all wealth that exists on the earth. Of what kind is Agni? By his greatness, that is, his brilliance, वन्वन् (*vanvan*), injuring wood or enemies; अवातः (*avātaḥ*), not approached by other enemies; अस्तृतः (*astṛtaḥ*), injured by none.
- दाशत् (*dāśat*)—may he favour us and give
May that very Agni, the injurer of enemies, not struck down by enemies, injured by none, favour me and give all the riches of the earth and the wealth that surpasses them by his superiority.
Surpassing all earthly things, may he bestow upon us riches, destroying his enemies by his greatness, unresisted, unassailed.

notes: abbreviation ಗೃ. printed

en: Sāyaṇa addresses Agni: you, who are of the qualities described before, spread out the great firmament with your lustre, which is ancient-like, newer, radiant, and rightly pervading.
- सः (*saḥ*)—you, who have been described before
- प्रश्नवत् (*praśnavat*)—as in former times, so also now
- ततंथ (*tataṃtha*)—you have pervaded so that it becomes still more vast

O Agni, you who have been described before, have pervaded the very vast firmament, so that it becomes still more vast, with your lustre, which is new, radiant and concentrated, and which exists now just as it did in all former times.
You have overspread, Agni, this vast (firmament) with radiant concentrated lustre, recent like that of old.
O friends, fellow-officiants, you sing the stoma, the praise, to Agni, who is the vanquisher of enemies and the creator. Likewise offer the sacrificial means, the oblation.
- यज्ञं च (*yajñaṃ ca*)—and the oblation, which is the means of the sacrifice
O friendly officiating priests, recite the hymn of praise addressing Agni, who vanquishes enemies and is the creator. And offer also the oblation, which is the means of the sacrifice.
Sing praise and offer sacrifice, my friends, to the foe-diseomfiting, the creator, Agni.

सखायः (*sakhāyaḥ*)—It is the custom to call the officiating priests, who take part in sacrifices and work in co-operation with the sacrificer, the friends of the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice. There is a sentence of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā: ऋत्विजो वा अस्य सखायः (*ṛtvijo vā asya sakhāyaḥ*).

That Agni indeed, may he sit down, take his seat on the sacred grass at our sacrifice, he who is the hotā, the invoker of the gods, and kavikratu, of far-reaching wisdom. The human ages, मानुषाणि युगानि (*mānuṣāṇi yugāni*), are the periods of time, belonging to men, suited to sacrifice, in which sacrifices are performed. For all this time he is the messenger of the gods, and he is the carrier of oblations, the bearer of the offerings.
- मानुषा युगा (*mānuṣā yugā*)—in every age of men
- दूतः (*dūtaḥ*)—who is the messenger of the gods
- हव्यवाहनः (*havyavāhanaḥ*)—and who is the bearer of the oblation
- सीदत् (*sīdat*)—may he be established (at our sacrificial altar)

May that very Agni, who is the performer of the offering, of far-reaching wisdom, the messenger of the gods in every age of men, and the bearer of oblations, be established, sitting down, at our sacrificial altar.
May that Agni indeed sit down (at our sacrifice), who in every age of man has been the invoker the of gods, the doer of wise deeds, the messenger of the gods, the bearer of oblations.

Those two well-known, resplendent ones, of pure rites, Mitra and Varuṇa, and the Ādityas, the sons of Aditi, Dhātṛ and the others, and the company of the Maruts, and heaven and earth: O Agni, the giver of dwelling, worship these gods here, at this sacrifice.
- वसो (*vaso*)—O Agni, the giver of dwelling
- शुचिव्रता (*śucivratā*)—who are of pure rites, Mitra and Varuṇa
- मारुतं गणं (*mārutaṃ gaṇaṃ*)—the host of the Maruts
O Agni, giver of dwelling, worship in this sacrifice Mitra and Varuṇa, who are well known, resplendent and of pure rites, the Ādityas, the host of the Maruts, and heaven and earth.
Giver of dwellings, worship on this occasion the two regal divinities, Mitra and Varuna, whos acts are holy, the Adityas, the company of the Maruts, and heaven and earth.

O Agni, son of strength, that is, son of force: of you, who are immortal, free from death, the radiance, संदृष्टिः (*saṃdṛṣṭiḥ*), is वस्वी (*vasvī*), that is, causing to dwell, which means praiseworthy. That radiance gives food to the mortal, the man who is the sacrificer: इषयते (*iṣayate*) means that it desires food, that is, it gives.
- ऊर्जः नपात् (*ūrjaḥ napāt*)—O son of strength
- मर्त्याय (*martyāya*)—to the sacrificer, who is a man
O Agni, son of strength, your radiance, which is free from death, being praiseworthy, supplies food to the sacrificer, who is a man.
Son of strength, Agni, the glorious radiance of you who are immortal, bestows food upon (your) mortal worshipper.

O Agni, today, now, let the sacrificer, the giver, who honours you by the rite of attendance and offers the oblations, be exceedingly praiseworthy; and let him be possessed of fine wealth. And let that mortal, the man, attain good praise directed to you; the meaning is that he is always to be your praiser.
- दाः (*dāḥ*)—and who offers oblations, the sacrificer
- मर्तः (*martaḥ*)—that same sacrificer, who is a man
- आनाश (*ānāśa*)—let him be one who offers to you

O Agni, now let the sacrificer, who worships you by sacrifices and other rites and offers oblations, be most praiseworthy. Let him also be possessed of exceeding wealth. Let that same sacrificer, who is a man, be one who offers to you the most excellent praise.
May the donor (of the oblation). propitiating you by his acts to-day, be exalted, and (rendered) very opulent : may (such) mortal be diligent in (your) praise.

O Agni, those who are yours, who praise you, those praisers, protected by you, desiring food for themselves, obtain all food; this is the word to be supplied. Or else, wishing for it, they obtain life itself, which is marked by a hundred years; this too is the word to be supplied. Likewise they overcome, pass beyond, certain hostile armies of assailants, and they destroy certain hostile armies of assailants; this is the word to be supplied.
O Agni, those who praise you, desiring food, such praisers, being protected by you, defeating and destroying the enemies who fall upon them, obtain all food.
Those, Agni. who are protected by you, wishing for the whole (term of) life (obtain it), overcoming hostile assailants, destroying hostile assailants.
This Agni, with his sharp flame, that is, his fiery energy, let him strike down all devourers, the Rākṣasas and the like. And further, let Agni give us wealth, riches.
Let Agni destroy with his sharp flame all the Rākṣasas and the like; let Agni grant us wealth.
May Agni, with his sharp flame, demolish the devourer (of the oblation): may Agni grant us riches.

Sāyaṇa addresses Agni as Jātavedas, one who possesses knowledge or possesses wealth, and as Vicarṣaṇi, the one who sees in a special degree. He asks him to bring wealth that is accompanied by good heroes, that is, by sons, grandsons and the like. He then addresses him as Sukratu, doer of good deeds, and asks him to destroy the Rākṣasas.
- जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—one who is of the nature of Jātavedas
- विचर्षणे (*vicarṣaṇe*)—one who possesses a surpassing power of sight
- सुकृतो (*sukṛto*)—O Agni, the doer of excellent deeds

O Agni, who are of the nature of Jātavedas, or who know everything, and who possess a surpassing power of sight, bring wealth accompanied by excellent heroes. O Agni, the doer of excellent deeds, destroy the Rākṣasas and the like.
Jatavedas, all-beholder, bring us wealth with good posterity : doer of good deeds, destroy the Rakshasas.
O Jātavedas, protect us from sin. And O Agni, kavi of the mantra that takes the form of praise, who cause it to be uttered, who make it sound: for Agni produces sound.

And so it is recalled that the mind strikes the bodily fire, and the fire impels the wind, and the wind moving in the chest produces a low tone. Such an Agni, protect us from the enemy who wishes us harm, that is, who wishes us evil.
- ब्रह्मणस्कवे (*brahmaṇaskave*)—O Agni, the reciter of praise
- अघायतः (*aghāyataḥ*)—from the enemy who does us evil
O Agni, who are of the nature of Jātavedas, protect us from sin. O Agni, the reciter of praise, protect us from the enemy who does us evil.
Preserve us, Jatavedas, from sin: enunciator of prayer, protect us from the malevolent.

ब्रह्मणस्कवे—स्तुतिरूपस्य मंत्रस्य कवे कावयितः शब्दयितरग्ने । (*brahmaṇaskave—stutirūpasya maṃtrasya kave kāvayitaḥ śabdayitaragne |*) Because Agni is the author of mantras in the form of praise and prompts men to utter them, he is here addressed with the word ब्रह्मणस्कवे (*brahmaṇaskave*). अग्निर्हि शब्दमुत्पादयति— मनः कायाग्नि माहंति स प्रेरयति मारुतं । मारुतस्तूरसि चरन् मंद्रं जनयति स्वरं ॥ (*agnirhi śabdamutpādayati— manaḥ kāyāgni māhaṃti sa prerayati mārutaṃ | mārutastūrasi caran maṃdraṃ janayati svaraṃ ‖*) (Pā. Śi. 6-7). How Agni is the prompter of sound: the feelings that arise in the mind stir up the fire that dwells in the body (in the form of the digestive fire). That fire sets in motion the wind moving in the heart and the other parts of the body. That wind gently sends out from the mouth a tone or a sound; so it is said in the Pāṇinīya Śikṣā. Therefore, for the feelings that arise in the mind to be brought out in the form of speech, the help of Agni is necessary. For this reason Agni is here praised as the poet who composes sentences in the form of hymns.
O Agni, the man of evil intent who directs against us his own weapon, which is his vadha, that is, who strikes us with a weapon: from that man, and from sin, protect us.
O Agni, protect us from the man of evil mind who aims weapons against us to kill us, and from sin.
The malevolent mortal who threatens us with murderous weapon, from him defend us, and also from sin.
O shining Agni, with your tongue, your flame, drive away on every side, that is, strike down on all sides, the evil-doer who is to be described, the man who wishes to kill us.
O shining Agni, destroy completely with your flame such an evil-doer, the man who wishes to kill us.
Scatter, divine Agni, by your flame, that evil-doer, the man who seeks to kill us.
O Sahantya, Agni, overcomer of enemies, to me, Bharadvāja the seer, give on every side wide and spreading happiness or a house; and likewise give desirable wealth.
- भरद्वाजाय (*bharadvājāya*)—to me, who am named Bharadvāja
O Agni, who vanquish enemies, give very abundant happiness to me, who am named Bharadvāja. Give also excellent wealth, which all people most urgently need.
Subduer of foes, grant to Bharadwaja infinite happiness and desirable wealth.

This verse, अग्निर्वृत्राणि (*agnirvṛtrāṇi*), is the anuvākyā of the ājyabhāga offering to Agni at the full-moon sacrifice. It is laid down in the sūtra (Ā. Sū. 1-5) that it is the anuvākyā of the former ājyabhāga. In iṣṭis, animal sacrifices and Soma sacrifices, wherever no special rule such as वृधन्वंत् पुष्टिमंता (*vṛdhanvaṃt puṣṭimaṃtā*) is seen, there everywhere this very verse is

the first ājyabhāga anuvākyā. This verse is the anuvākyā of the offering to Agni at the Upasad, and at the evening offering it is the yājyā. This too is laid down in the sūtra (Ā. Sū. 4-8): there is an interchange of the yājyā and the anuvākyā verses. Sāyaṇa then explains the verse. Agni, praised with praise, विपन्यया (*vipanyayā*), desiring wealth, dravina, for the praisers, or else desiring for himself wealth in the form of the oblation, let him smite hard the obstructors, वृत्राणि (*vṛtrāṇi*), the Rākṣasas and the like, or the darknesses. What kind of Agni is he? He is kindled, well lit, and for that very reason bright, of white colour, and offered to with oblations.
- द्रविणस्युः (*draviṇasyuḥ*)—who wishes to give wealth to the praisers
- आहुतः (*āhutaḥ*)—to whom the offering of oblations is made
May Agni, who is praised with praises, who wishes to give wealth to the praisers, who is fully kindled, radiant, and receives the offering of oblations, destroy the enemies completely.
May Agni. propitiated by praise, desirous of (sacrificial) affluence, kindled, bright, and fed with burnt offerings. destroy all adversaries.

In the sacrifices of the new and full moon, in the sacrifice performed at the full moon, this Ṛk अग्निर्वृत्राणि (*agnirvṛtrāṇi*) is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra of the ājyabhāga offering; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, अग्निर्वृत्राणि जंघनदिति पूर्वस्थ्याच्यभागस्यानुवाक्या (*agnirvṛtrāṇi jaṃghanaditi pūrvasthyācyabhāgasyānuvākyā*) (Ā. Sū. 1-5). And in the iṣṭi, the animal sacrifice and the Soma sacrifice, in cases where special rules such as वृधन्वती (*vṛdhanvatī*) and पुष्टिमती (*puṣṭimatī*) are absent, this Ṛk अग्निर्वृत्राणि (*agnirvṛtrāṇi*) is used as the anuvākyā mantra of the first ājyabhāga. And in the iṣṭi called Upasad, this Ṛk is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra in the offering made to Agni, and as the yājyā mantra in the offering made in the evening; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, अग्निर्वृत्राणि जंघनद्य उग्र इव शर्यहेति विसर्यासो याज्यानुवाक्यानां (*agnirvṛtrāṇi jaṃghanadya ugra iva śaryaheti visaryāso yājyānuvākyānāṃ*) (Ā. Sū. 4-8).

द्रविणस्युः (*draviṇasyuḥ*)—Here the commentator has given two kinds of meaning for dravina: wealth, or the oblation. If it is taken to mean wealth, the word द्रविणस्युः (*draviṇasyuḥ*) means that Agni wishes to give the wealth that is in him to those who worship him. If it is taken to mean the oblation, the intention is that Agni wishes (in the form of the offering) for the wealth, in the form of the oblation (the food), that the sacrificers or the officiating priests offer in the sacrifice.

Here the words mother and father denote earth and heaven, according to the śruti द्यौर्वः पिता पृथिवी माता (*dyaurvaḥ pitā pṛthivī mātā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-191-6). ⟨NOTE:309⟩ In the womb of the mother, the earth, that is, in the middle, in the imperishable place called the altar, shining forth in a special manner, the father of the father, the protector of the world of heaven by the giving of oblations: such an Agni, sitting on the womb of the sacrifice, the northern altar, the place called dhiṣṇya, sits on the northern altar and smites the obstructors. This is the construction.
notes: ಹವಿರ್ಯಚಮೇವ printed in the bhāṣya, looks damaged; read here as the Ṛk itself becoming the oblation; verse and bhāṣya have ತಪ್ಪಂ, the Pratipadārtha has ತಷ್ಟಂ

en: - योनिं (*yoniṃ*)—in the place that takes the form of the northern altar
- आ सीदन् (*ā sīdan*)—being seated (he destroys enemies)

Agni, who shines on the sacrificial altar, which is the middle of the earth and is imperishable, and who is the protector of the world of heaven, being seated (sitting down) in the place of the sacrifice that takes the form of the northern altar, destroys enemies.
Radiant in the embryo of the maternal (earth), on the imperishable (altar); the cherisher of the paternal (heaven), sitting on the seat of sacrifice.

In this Ṛk the word मातुः (*mātuḥ*) indicates the earth and the word पितुः (*pituḥ*) the world of heaven. Garbha means the region that lies between heaven and earth. That heaven and earth stand to Agni in the place of father and mother is supported by the Ṛk दौर्वः पिता पृथिवी माता सोमो भ्रातादिति स्वसा (*daurvaḥ pitā pṛthivī mātā somo bhrātāditi svasā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-191-6), and so the commentator has given this Ṛk as an example. The meaning of this Ṛk is plain.

ऋतस्य योनिं (*ṛtasya yoniṃ*)—Ṛta means truth or sacrifice. Here it is used in the sense of sacrifice. Yoni means the place of origin, or the navel region, the middle place. Therefore ऋतस्य योनिं (*ṛtasya yoniṃ*) means the northern altar, which stands as the navel of the sacrifice.

O Jātavedas, knower of what is born, O Vicarṣaṇi, special seer, Agni, bring brahma, that is, food, together with progeny, accompanied by sons and grandsons. The meaning is: the brahma that shines in heaven, in the world of heaven, that is, the praised food that shines among the gods, bring that.
- विचर्षणे (*vicarṣaṇe*)—who have a surpassing power of sight
- प्रजावत् (*prajāvat*)—accompanied by sons and the like
O Agni, who are of the nature of Jātavedas and have a surpassing power of sight, provide for us such food, accompanied by sons and the like, as shines exceedingly in the world of heaven.
Bring to us, Jatavedas, all-beholder, food with progeny ; such (food) as is brilliant in heaven.

प्रजावत् ब्रह्म (*prajāvat brahma*)—The word brahma means a hymn of praise and also food. Food accompanied by sons and the like means that Agni is prayed to give offspring, sons, grandsons and the like, and food (nourishment) for their sustenance and ours.

O Sahaskṛta, Agni, born of sahas, strength, we, who have prayas, that is, who have food in the form of the oblation, send forth praises, गिरः (*giraḥ*), towards you, whose appearance is pleasing or whose appearance is worthy of praise. The meaning is that we release, we utter.
O Agni, son of strength, offering the oblation to you, we recite hymns of praise addressed to you, who are of pleasing form, and so we extol you.
Strength-begotten Agni, we, offering (sacrificial) food, address praises to you who are of pleasing aspect.

O Agni, of golden appearance, whose lustre is beneficial and pleasing or whose lustre shines like gold, of you who are bright, we come to the shelter, the refuge, the support. The illustration is: as people scorched by heat go to shade, so we.
- छायां इव (*chāyāṃ iva*)—as one wearied by the heat takes refuge in shade
- हिरण्यसंदृशः (*hiraṇyasaṃdṛśaḥ*)—who have an attractive form like gold
O Agni, as one wearied by the heat takes refuge in shade, we obtain the shelter of you, who have an attractive form like gold and are shining.
We have recourse, Agni, to the shelter of you, the lustrous, the golden-feathered, as to the shade (of a tree).

In the Upasad, for the morning offering to Agni this verse, य उग्र इव (*ya ugra iva*), is the yājyā; for the evening offering this very verse is the anuvākyā. It is laid down in the sūtra (Ā. Sū. 4-8). The Agni who is like a fierce one, of swollen strength, like an archer, the slayer with śaryas, arrows, of enemies; who is like a sharp-horned bull of desirable gait: O Agni, you broke the cities, the three cities of the Asuras. You have broken them. He cites the śruti रुद्रो वा एष यदग्निः (*rudro vā eṣa yadagniḥ*) (Tai. Brā. 2 1-3-1),

meaning that the burning of Tripura, though done by Rudra, was done by Agni; thus Agni is praised. Or else, because Agni stood as the point of the arrow that was the means of burning Tripura, Agni is said to have broken the cities. A Brāhmaṇa beginning देवासुरा वा विषु लोकेषु समयतंत (*devāsurā vā viṣu lokeṣu samayataṃta*) (Ai. Brā. 1-23) is to be attended to.
- उग्र इव (*ugra iva*)—like a fierce archer
- वंसगो न (*vaṃsago na*)—and like a bull of the forest
O Agni, you who are like a fierce archer, who kills enemies with arrows, and like a bull of the forest with sharp horns, have destroyed the cities of enemies.
You, Agni, who are like a fierce archer, or like a sharp-horned bull, have destroyed the cities (of the Asuras).

In the sacrifice called Upasad, in the offering made to Agni, this Ṛk य उग्र इव (*ya ugra iva*) is to be used as the yājyā mantra in the morning and as the anuvākyā mantra in the evening; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, अग्निर्वृत्राणि जंघनद्य उग्रइव शर्यहा (*agnirvṛtrāṇi jaṃghanadya ugraiva śaryahā*) (Ā. Sū. 4-8).

In this Ṛk it is stated that Agni destroyed the cities of the Asuras, who were enemies. Here the commentator cites the śruti sentence रुद्रो वा एष यदग्निः (*rudro vā eṣa yadagniḥ*) (Tai. Brā. 2-1-3-1), that is, Agni is Rudra, and so indicates the idea that when it is said that Agni destroyed the cities of the Asuras, it was Rudra in the form of Agni who destroyed them; in support of this he has cited a sentence of the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa: देवासुरा वा एषु लोकेषु समयतंत ते ना असुरा इमानेव लोकान्पुरोऽकुर्वत यथौजीयांसो बलीयांस एवं ते वा (*devāsurā vā eṣu lokeṣu samayataṃta te nā asurā imāneva lokānpuro 'kurvata yathaujīyāṃso balīyāṃsa evaṃ te vā*)

अयस्मयामेवेमामकुर्वत रजतामंतरिक्षं हरणीं दिवं ते तथेमांल्लोकान्पुरोऽकुर्वत ते देवा अब्रुवन् पुरो वा इमेऽसुरा इमांल्लोकानक्रत पुर इमांल्लोकान्प्रतिकरनामहा इति तथेति ॥ (*ayasmayāmevemāmakurvata rajatāmaṃtarikṣaṃ haraṇīṃ divaṃ te tathemāṃllokānpuro 'kurvata te devā abruvan puro vā ime 'surā imāṃllokānakrata pura imāṃllokānpratikaranāmahā iti tatheti ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 4-23)

In former times the Devas and the Asuras prepared for battle. At the time of war, kings naturally build impregnable forts and ramparts so that the enemy armies may not break into their city. In the same way the Asuras built three strong forts. They surrounded this earth with an iron rampart, the atmosphere with a rampart of silver (rajata), and the heavenly world with a rampart of gold, and so turned them into strong fortresses. In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā of the Yajurveda this matter is stated thus:

तेषामसुराणां तिस्रः पुर आसन्नयस्मय्यवमाथ रजताथ हरिणी ता देवा जेतुं नाशक्कु वन्ता उपसदैवाजिगीषन् तस्मादाहुर्यश्चैवं वेद यश्च नोपसदा वै महापुरं जयंतीति त इषुग्ं समस्कुर्वताग्निमनीकग्ं सोमुग्ं शल्यं विष्णुं तेजनं त्रेऽब्रुवन् क इमामसिष्यतीति रुद्र इत्यब्रुवन् रुद्रो वै क्रूरः सोऽस्यत्विति सोऽब्रवीद्वरं वृणा अहमेव पशूनामधिपतिरसानीति तस्माद्रुद्रः पशूनामधिपतिस्ताग्ं रुद्रो वा सृजत्स तिस्त्रः पुरो भित्वैभ्यो लोकेभ्योऽसुरान्प्राणुदत ॥ (*teṣāmasurāṇāṃ tisraḥ pura āsannayasmayyavamātha rajatātha hariṇī tā devā jetuṃ nāśakku vantā upasadaivājigīṣan tasmādāhuryaścaivaṃ veda yaśca nopasadā vai mahāpuraṃ jayaṃtīti ta iṣugṃ samaskurvatāgnimanīkagṃ somugṃ śalyaṃ viṣṇuṃ tejanaṃ tre 'bruvan ka imāmasiṣyatīti rudra ityabruvan rudro vai krūraḥ so 'syatviti so 'bravīdvaraṃ vṛṇā ahameva paśūnāmadhipatirasānīti tasmādrudraḥ paśūnāmadhipatistāgṃ rudro vā sṛjatsa tistraḥ puro bhitvaibhyo lokebhyo 'surānprāṇudata ‖*) (Tai. Saṃ. 6-2-3-1 2) **GLOSS**

In former times, when war broke out between the Devas and the Asuras, the Asuras held three cities. One of them was covered with an iron rampart, another with a silver rampart, and the third with a golden rampart, so that they were impregnable to enemies. The Devas were not able to besiege these cities and conquer them. Therefore all the Devas assembled and, after long deliberation as to how these cities could be besieged and conquered, and whether there was anyone among them with the strength to conquer them, they came at last to a decision. They made ready a bow and arrows to take aim at those cities and strike them. The arrow that is fixed to the bow and shot must be very sharp and powerful. Therefore, in preparing the arrow, they made Agni its tip (point), Soma its shalya (the upper part of the arrow), and Viṣṇu its shaft. After the arrow had been made ready in this way, they searched among themselves to see who was able to fix this arrow to the bowstring and shoot it. Then they determined that Rudra alone was fit to do this work, because the one who behaves cruelly in facing enemies

is none other than Rudra; this they came to know. Then they went to Rudra and prayed: "O Rudra, in order to help the Devas, fix this arrow that we have prepared to your bow, take aim at the cities of the Asuras, strike them and destroy them." To this Rudra said: "Very well, let it be so. But in return for doing this difficult task you must grant me a boon. I must become the lord of all animals. If you grant this boon I shall do your work." For this very reason Rudra became famous as the lord of animals. When the Devas agreed to Rudra's word, Rudra fixed the arrow prepared by the Devas to his bow, took aim at the cities of the Asuras, shot, and destroyed them. This story is told both in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa and in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā.

In this context, since the Devas, in making the arrow, made Agni its tip (the point of the arrow), and since that sharp tip itself was the cause of the destruction of the cities of the Asuras, the matter that Agni destroyed the cities of the enemy Asuras is explained in the present Ṛk.

When Agni is being produced by churning, the verse beginning "ā yaṃ haste" is the anuvākyā. This is laid down in the sūtra: one should begin with the half-verse "ā yaṃ haste na khādinam" (Ā. Sū. 2-16). The Agni born of churning, like a newborn child, is held by the adhvaryus in their hands, turned towards them. The first "na" is a particle of comparison, here placed in front by transposition. "Khādinam na" means like a devourer, like a tiger or the like; just as men who hold such a creature are watchful, so are they. Or else "na" is in the sense of "now": now they hold in the hand that Agni, the devourer of the oblations, who is the accomplisher of a good sacrifice (svadhvara) for the people. O priests, serve that Agni; this is the word to be supplied.
- खादिनं न (*khādinaṃ na*)—like tigers and others that devour everything
- आ बिभ्रति (*ā bibhrati*)—the priests hold, such a one and
- स्वध्वरं (*svadhvaraṃ*)—the accomplisher of an excellent sacrifice

Worship that Agni whom the priests receive in the hand, like a newborn babe, just as tigers and other creatures devour everything, he who devours the oblations, and who is the accomplisher of an excellent sacrifice for the people.
(Worship) that Agni whom (the priests) bear in their hands like a new-born babe; the devourer (of the oblation), the (conveyer of the) holy sacrifices of men.

It is shown by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, आ यं हस्ते न खादिनमित्यर्धर्च आरमेत् (*ā yaṃ haste na khādinamityardharca āramet*) (Ā. Sū. 2-16), that at the time of churning Agni, as soon as Agni has been produced, this Ṛk "ā yaṃ haste" is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra. The 40th, 41st and 42nd Ṛks of this sūkta are very important mantras in the rite of Agni-churning. The order of reciting them and their explanation are given at length in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa. That very matter we explain here, with the mantras and the necessary explanation.
**Description of the rite of Agni-churning (as in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa)**
When Agni is produced in a sacrifice, two pieces of wood of the aśvattha tree or the śamī tree are placed one upon the other and rubbed hard. From that Agni is produced. In this matter:
शमिगर्भादग्निं मंथति । एषा ना अग्नेय्यज्ञिया तनूः । तामेवास्मै जनयति ॥ (*śamigarbhādagniṃ maṃthati | eṣā nā agneyyajñiyā tanūḥ | tāmevāsmai janayati ‖*) (Tai. Brā. 1-1--9-1) **GLOSS**

so runs the sentence of the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa. The procedure for producing Agni by churning, with mantras and with the rites, in sacrifices and the like, is stated in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa (Ai. Brā. 3-5) as follows. Since the churning of Agni is the matter spoken of in this Ṛk, it is proper to explain that procedure here. In a sacrifice, after the rite called Somavikrayaṇa (obtaining the Soma plant by purchase from those who have brought it from mountains, forests and the like) is completed, the work of Agni-churning begins. Then the priest called Adhvaryu addresses the priest called Hotṛ and speaks thus:

अग्नये मध्यमानायानुब्रूहित्याहाध्वर्युरभि त्वा देव सवितरिति सावित्रीमन्वाह तदादुर्यदग्नये मध्यमानायानुवाचाहाथ कस्मात्सावित्रीमन्वाहेति । सविता वै प्रसवानामीशे सवितृप्रसूत एवैनं तन्मंथति तस्मात्सावित्रीमन्वाह । (*agnaye madhyamānāyānubrūhityāhādhvaryurabhi tvā deva savitariti sāvitrīmanvāha tadāduryadagnaye madhyamānāyānuvācāhātha kasmātsāvitrīmanvāheti | savitā vai prasavānāmīśe savitṛprasūta evainaṃ tanmaṃthati tasmātsāvitrīmanvāha |*)

The Adhvaryu, addressing the Hotṛ, speaks the praiṣa mantra अग्नये मध्यमानायनुब्रू ३ हि (*agnaye madhyamānāyanubrū 3 hi*). A praiṣa mantra is the recitation of a mantra by which, when various rites are performed in a sacrifice, the Adhvaryu and others, addressing the person concerned, enjoin in the form of a command: "Perform such and such a rite (or oblation)." Hearing it, the Hotṛ recites the mantra addressed to Savitṛ (the Sāvitrī Ṛk):
अभि त्वा देव सवितरीशानं नार्याणां । सदावन् भागमीमहे ॥ (*abhi tvā deva savitarīśānaṃ nāryāṇāṃ | sadāvan bhāgamīmahe ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-24-3) **GLOSS**

Here a doubt arises. Although the Adhvaryu has directed the Hotṛ to say the mantra necessary for the churning of Agni, why does the Hotṛ, not doing so, recite a Ṛk addressed to the deity Savitṛ? Is this not a mistake? The answer is that it is not. As the sentence सविता वै प्रसवानामिशे (*savitā vai prasavānāmiśe*) says, in all rites such as sacrifices, whatever has to be produced, Savitṛ is the lord of all that production; therefore it is natural that, for the beginning of the work of producing Agni, called Agni-churning, the permission of the deity Savitṛ should be asked. For that reason the Hotṛ first recites the Ṛk addressed to Savitṛ.

मही द्यौः पृथिवी च न इति द्यावापृथिवीयामन्वाह । तदाहुर्यदग्नये मध्यमानायानुवाचाहाथ कस्माद्ध्यावापृथिवीयामन्वाहेति द्यावापृथिवीभ्यां ना एतं जातं देवाः पर्यगृण्णंस्ताभ्यामेवाद्यापि परिगृहीतस्तस्माद्ध्यावापृथिवीयामन्वाह ॥ (*mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca na iti dyāvāpṛthivīyāmanvāha | tadāhuryadagnaye madhyamānāyānuvācāhātha kasmāddhyāvāpṛthivīyāmanvāheti dyāvāpṛthivībhyāṃ nā etaṃ jātaṃ devāḥ paryagṛṇṇaṃstābhyāmevādyāpi parigṛhītastasmāddhyāvāpṛthivīyāmanvāha ‖*)
मही द्यौः पृथिवी च न इमं यज्ञं मिमिक्षतां । पितृतां नो भरीमभिः ॥ (*mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca na imaṃ yajñaṃ mimikṣatāṃ | pitṛtāṃ no bharīmabhiḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-22-13) **GLOSS**

he recites the Ṛk addressed to Dyāvāpṛthivī (Heaven and Earth). Some raise this objection: when he is told to say a Ṛk for the work of Agni-churning, addressed to Agni, why does this Hotṛ recite a Ṛk addressed to Dyāvāpṛthivī? The answer is that in former times, when Agni was produced, the Devas received him between Dyāvāpṛthivī (earth and heaven). (They held him.) Therefore the same must be done now. Since the Agni named Pāvaka is received by the earth, and the Agni in the form of the Sun is received by heaven, it is proper that for the reception of Agni a Ṛk addressed to Dyāvāpṛthivī should be recited.

त्वामग्ने पुष्करादधीति तृचमाग्नेयं गायत्रमन्वाहाग्नौ मध्यमाने स्वयैवैनं तद्देवतया स्वेन छंदसा समर्धयति । अथर्वा निरमंथतेति रूपसमृद्धमेतदै यज्ञस्य समृद्धं यद्रूपसमृद्धं यत्कर्म क्रियमाणमृगभिवदति ॥ (*tvāmagne puṣkarādadhīti tṛcamāgneyaṃ gāyatramanvāhāgnau madhyamāne svayaivainaṃ taddevatayā svena chaṃdasā samardhayati | atharvā niramaṃthateti rūpasamṛddhametadai yajñasya samṛddhaṃ yadrūpasamṛddhaṃ yatkarma kriyamāṇamṛgabhivadati ‖*)
Then, for the churning of Agni, the Hotṛ recites the three Ṛks addressed to the deity Agni:

त्वामग्ने पुष्करादध्यथर्वा निरमंथत । मूर्ध्नो विश्वस्य वाघतः । तमु त्वा दध्यज् ऋषिः पुत्र ईधे अथर्वणः । वृत्रहणं पुरंदरं ॥ त मु त्वा पाथ्यो वृषा समीधे दस्युहंतमं । धनंजयं रणेरणे ॥ (*tvāmagne puṣkarādadhyatharvā niramaṃthata | mūrdhno viśvasya vāghataḥ | tamu tvā dadhyaj ṛṣiḥ putra īdhe atharvaṇaḥ | vṛtrahaṇaṃ puraṃdaraṃ ‖ ta mu tvā pāthyo vṛṣā samīdhe dasyuhaṃtamaṃ | dhanaṃjayaṃ raṇeraṇe ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-16-13, 14. 15) **GLOSS**

These three Ṛks praise the deity Agni alone, and they are Ṛks in the Gāyatrī metre, which is dear to Agni. For both Agni and the Gāyatrī metre were produced by Prajāpati, so the Gāyatrī metre is said to be Agni's own metre. Now, in the second pāda of the first Ṛk it is said अथर्वा निरमंथत (*atharvā niramaṃthata*): the seer named Atharvan churned Agni and produced him. This seer Atharvan was the first of all to churn Agni in the aranis (the two fire-sticks) and produce him. Therefore there is the prayer that Agni, born as a son to the seer Atharvan, may grow abundantly in the sacrifice and flourish. For this reason it is natural to recite these Ṛks, which give the meaning that Agni, produced and shaped from the aranis (that is, in his complete form as Agni), may blaze up in the sacrificial rite (burning high) and shine. Whatever mantra is recited in a sacrifice, its meaning must be such as to explain the rite concerned. This is called rūpasamṛddhi.

स यदि न जायेत यदि चिरं जायेत राक्षोघ्नो गायत्रोऽनूच्याः अग्ने हंसिन्य १ त्रिणमित्येताः रक्षसामपहत्यै रक्षांसि ना एनं तर्हालभंते यर्हि न जायते यर्हि चिरं जायते ॥ (*sa yadi na jāyeta yadi ciraṃ jāyeta rākṣoghno gāyatro 'nūcyāḥ agne haṃsinya 1 triṇamityetāḥ rakṣasāmapahatyai rakṣāṃsi nā enaṃ tarhālabhaṃte yarhi na jāyate yarhi ciraṃ jāyate ‖*)

The five Ṛks mentioned above are to be recited while churning Agni in the aranis. If, even when this is done, Agni is not produced, or if he is produced slowly after a long time, with smoke and the like coming, then the following Rākṣoghna sūkta in the Gāyatrī metre is to be recited:

अग्ने हंसि नृ १ त्रिणं दीद्यन्मर्तेष्वा । स्वे क्षये शुचिव्रत ॥ उत्तिष्ठसि स्वाहुतो घृतानि प्रतिमोदसे । यत्त्वा स्सुचः समस्थिरन् ॥ स आहुतो वि रोचतेऽग्निरीळेन्यो गिरा । सुचा प्रतीकमज्यते ॥ घृतेनाग्निः समज्यते मधुप्रतीक आहुतः । रोचमानो विभावसुः । जरमाणः समिध्यसे देवेभ्यो दव्यवाहन । तं त्वा हवंत मर्त्याः ॥ तं मर्ता अमर्त्यं घृतेनाग्निं सपर्यत । अदाभ्यं गृहपतिं ॥ अदाभ्येन शोचिषाग्ने रक्षस्त्वं दह । गोपा ऋतस्य दीदिहि । स त्वमग्ने प्रतीकेन प्रत्योष यातुधान्यः । उरुक्षयेषु दीद्यत् ॥ तं त्वा गीर्भिरुरुक्षया हव्यवाहं समाधिरे । यजिष्यं मानुषे जने ॥ (*agne haṃsi nṛ 1 triṇaṃ dīdyanmarteṣvā | sve kṣaye śucivrata ‖ uttiṣṭhasi svāhuto ghṛtāni pratimodase | yattvā ssucaḥ samasthiran ‖ sa āhuto vi rocate 'gnirīḷenyo girā | sucā pratīkamajyate ‖ ghṛtenāgniḥ samajyate madhupratīka āhutaḥ | rocamāno vibhāvasuḥ | jaramāṇaḥ samidhyase devebhyo davyavāhana | taṃ tvā havaṃta martyāḥ ‖ taṃ martā amartyaṃ ghṛtenāgniṃ saparyata | adābhyaṃ gṛhapatiṃ ‖ adābhyena śociṣāgne rakṣastvaṃ daha | gopā ṛtasya dīdihi | sa tvamagne pratīkena pratyoṣa yātudhānyaḥ | urukṣayeṣu dīdyat ‖ taṃ tvā gīrbhirurukṣayā havyavāhaṃ samādhire | yajiṣyaṃ mānuṣe jane ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-118-1 to 9) **GLOSS**

There are nine Ṛks in this sūkta. They drive away the Rākṣasas and kill them. Therefore, by reciting these Ṛks the Rākṣasas are destroyed. The reason why Agni is not produced at the time of churning, or is produced late, is that these Rākṣasas obstruct Agni and keep him in their power without releasing him. Therefore the killing of the Rākṣasas is necessary in order to set Agni free. For that reason it is said that the Rākṣoghna sūkta of these nine Ṛks is to be recited.

स यद्येकस्यामेवानूक्तायां जायेत यदि द्वयोरथोत ब्रुवंतु जंतव इति जाताय जातवतीमभिरूपामनुब्रूयात् ॥ (*sa yadyekasyāmevānūktāyāṃ jāyeta yadi dvayorathota bruvaṃtu jaṃtava iti jātāya jātavatīmabhirūpāmanubrūyāt ‖*)
While the Rākṣoghna sūkta is being recited, if Agni is produced after one Ṛk has been recited in the middle, or after the recitation of two, three or more Ṛks, then at that very moment
उत ब्रुवंतु जंतव उदग्निर्वृत्रहाजनि । धनंजयो रणेरणे (*uta bruvaṃtu jaṃtava udagnirvṛtrahājani | dhanaṃjayo raṇeraṇe*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-74-3) **GLOSS**

this Ṛk is to be recited at once. For the matter set forth in this Ṛk is favourable to the production of Agni. The word जातवतीं (*jātavatīṃ*) is used in order to state this favourableness. Then, in the second pāda उदग्निर्वृत्रहाजनि (*udagnirvṛtrahājani*)
the word अजनि (*ajani*), "he was born", which indicates birth, is recited. Therefore it is said that as soon as Agni is produced, this suitable Ṛk is to be recited at that very moment.

यद्यज्ञेऽभिरूपं तत्समृद्धं आ यं हस्तेन खादिनमिति हस्ताभ्यां ह्येनं मंथंति शिशुं जातमिति शिशुरिव वा एष प्रथमजातो यदग्निः न बिभ्रति विशामग्निं स्वध्वरमिति यद्वै देवानां नेति तदेषामो ३ मिति प्र देवं देवनीतये भरता वसुवित्तममिति प्रह्रियमाणायाभिरूपा यद्यज्ञेऽभिरूपतत्समृद्धं आ स्वे योन् निषीदत्वति एष ह वा अस्य स्वो योनिर्यदग्निरग्नेः ॥ (*yadyajñe 'bhirūpaṃ tatsamṛddhaṃ ā yaṃ hastena khādinamiti hastābhyāṃ hyenaṃ maṃthaṃti śiśuṃ jātamiti śiśuriva vā eṣa prathamajāto yadagniḥ na bibhrati viśāmagniṃ svadhvaramiti yadvai devānāṃ neti tadeṣāmo 3 miti pra devaṃ devanītaye bharatā vasuvittamamiti prahriyamāṇāyābhirūpā yadyajñe 'bhirūpatatsamṛddhaṃ ā sve yon niṣīdatvati eṣa ha vā asya svo yoniryadagniragneḥ ‖*) **GLOSS**

Having stated so far the six Ṛks used for the churning of Agni (the six Ṛks अभित्वा (*abhitvā*), महीद्याः (*mahīdyāḥ*), त्वामग्ने (*tvāmagne*), तमुत्वा (*tamutvā*), तमुत्वा (*tamutvā*) and उतब्रुवंतु (*utabruvaṃtu*)), the Hotṛ now recites, as the seventh Ṛk,
आ यं हस्ते न खादिनं शिशुं जातं न बिभ्रति । विशामग्निं स्वध्वरं ॥ (*ā yaṃ haste na khādinaṃ śiśuṃ jātaṃ na bibhrati | viśāmagniṃ svadhvaraṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-16-40)

The meaning of this Ṛk is as follows. As one lifts a newly born child in the hands, the priests lift in their hands the Agni who has been produced in the araṇi. This Agni in the form of a child plays the chief part in the sacrifice performed by the people and is the devourer of the oblations and the like: this is its chief purport. The use of the word "hand" in the first pāda is because the priests churn this Agni with their hands; therefore it is said that they take him up in their hands. In the second pāda the example of a newborn child is given for the Agni who has only just been produced. The word "na" used here denotes the sense of assent, "om". In ordinary speech the word "na" denotes only negation; but in the Vedas this word denotes negation, comparison and assent. Here assent is the intended sense. And the word "devānām" may mean either "by the mantras that set forth the deities", or, by transposition of letters, "vedānām", that is, "pertaining to the Vedas". Now, the eighth Ṛk of the churning of Agni, that is,
प्र देवं देववीतये भरता वसुवित्तमं । आ स्वे योन् नि जीवतु ॥ (*pra devaṃ devavītaye bharatā vasuvittamaṃ | ā sve yon ni jīvatu ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-16-41)

the Hotṛ recites. "O priests, place the Agni who has now been produced in his own place, the Āhavanīya pit. May he sit there in his own place, Agni's own." This Ṛk, which has this meaning, is suited to the occasion of the rite of placing Agni in the Āhavanīya pit. Here, in each rite,

in accordance with the praiṣa mantra that is recited, the Hotṛ recites a mantra that is suited to that rite and of right meaning. Thus: as soon as Agni is produced, the Adhvaryu, addressing the Hotṛ, speaks the praiṣa mantra जातायानुब्रू ३ हि (*jātāyānubrū 3 hi*). In answer to it the Hotṛ recites the suitable Ṛk उत ब्रुवंतु बंतवः (*uta bruvaṃtu baṃtavaḥ*). Likewise, when the Agni that has been produced is placed in the pit called Āhavanīya, as soon as the Adhvaryu speaks the praiṣa mantra प्रह्रियमाणायानुब्रू ३ हि (*prahriyamāṇāyānubrū 3 hi*), the Hotṛ recites the Ṛk प्र देवं देवनीतये (*pra devaṃ devanītaye*), which is right for that occasion. It should be understood that it goes thus in every rite. In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā of the Yajurveda this matter is stated thus:

अग्नये मध्यमानायानुब्रूहीत्याह सावित्रिमृचमन्वाह सवितृप्रसूत एवैनं मंथति जातायानुब्रूहि प्रक्रियमाणायानुब्रूहीत्याह कांडेकांड एवैनं क्रियामणे समर्धयति गायत्रीः सर्वा अन्वाह ॥ (*agnaye madhyamānāyānubrūhītyāha sāvitrimṛcamanvāha savitṛprasūta evainaṃ maṃthati jātāyānubrūhi prakriyamāṇāyānubrūhītyāha kāṃḍekāṃḍa evainaṃ kriyāmaṇe samardhayati gāyatrīḥ sarvā anvāha ‖*) (Tai. Saṃ. 6-3-5-2, 3) **GLOSS**

and so on. This very matter is explained here by the sentence यद्यच्छेभिरूपं तत्समृद्धं (*yadyacchebhirūpaṃ tatsamṛddhaṃ*). That is, in each rite the mantra that corresponds to that rite is to be recited and the sacrifice carried out. The chief purport is that all the mantras must be in the Gāyatrī metre. At the end, as soon as आ स्वे योन् निषीदतु (*ā sve yon niṣīdatu*) has been said, they place Agni in the Āhavanīya pit; for the Āhavanīya place is said to be the place of the churned (just produced) Agni.

आ जातं जातवेदसीति जात इतरोः जातवेदा इतरः प्रियं शिशीतातिथिमित्येष द ना अस्य प्रियोऽतिथिर्यदग्नि रग्नेः स्कोन आ गृहपतिमिति शांत्यामेवैनं तद्दधाति । अग्निनाग्निः समिध्यते कविर्गृहपतियुर्वा । हव्यवाड्जुह्वास्य इत्यभिरूपा यद्यज्ञेऽभिरूपं तत्समृद्धं । त्वं ह्यग्ने अग्निना विप्रो विप्रेण सन्त्सतेति विप्र इतरो विप्र इतरः सन्नितरः सन्नितरः सखा सख्या समिध्यस इत्येष ह वा अस्य स्वः सखा यदग्निरग्नेः ॥ (*ā jātaṃ jātavedasīti jāta itaroḥ jātavedā itaraḥ priyaṃ śiśītātithimityeṣa da nā asya priyo 'tithiryadagni ragneḥ skona ā gṛhapatimiti śāṃtyāmevainaṃ taddadhāti | agnināgniḥ samidhyate kavirgṛhapatiyurvā | havyavāḍjuhvāsya ityabhirūpā yadyajñe 'bhirūpaṃ tatsamṛddhaṃ | tvaṃ hyagne agninā vipro vipreṇa santsateti vipra itaro vipra itaraḥ sannitaraḥ sannitaraḥ sakhā sakhyā samidhyasa ityeṣa ha vā asya svaḥ sakhā yadagniragneḥ ‖*) **GLOSS**
Now the Hotṛ recites, as the ninth Ṛk,
आ जातं जातवेदसि प्रियं शिशीतातिथिं । स्कोन आ गृहपतिं (*ā jātaṃ jātavedasi priyaṃ śiśītātithiṃ | skona ā gṛhapatiṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-16-42)

The chief purport of this Ṛk is as follows. In this Ṛk two kinds of Agni are indicated. जातं (*jātaṃ*) means the Agni who has just been produced by churning; this is the first. Because he has only just been produced, he is indicated by the word जातं (*jātaṃ*). The Agni already established in the Āhavanīya pit is the second. He is called

जातवेदसं (*jātavedasaṃ*). Because he knows the nature of the Agni produced by churning, the Āhavanīya Agni is explained by the word जातवेदसं (*jātavedasaṃ*). Here the newly churned Agni is, to the Agni called जातवेदस (*jātavedasa*) who was already established in the place of the Āhavanīya Agni, like a dear guest. Therefore the chief purport is that this churned Agni, who is dear and guest-like, is established in the Āhavanīya pit in order to secure a comfortable dwelling. Then the Hotṛ
अग्निनाग्निः समिध्यते कविर्गृहपतियुर्वा । हव्यवाड्जुह्वास्यः (*agnināgniḥ samidhyate kavirgṛhapatiyurvā | havyavāḍjuhvāsyaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-12-6)

Its meaning is: the newly churned Agni, joining the Agni already established in the Āhavanīya pit, blazes and shines brightly. This churned Agni is a seer who knows all, the protector of the house or of the sacrificer, ever young, the bearer of oblations and the like to the gods, one who holds in his mouth the ladle called Juhū, the instrument of the oblation. (That is, because ghee and the like are offered into Agni's flame with the ladle called Juhū, Agni is called जुह्वास्यः (*juhvāsyaḥ*).) Thus a mantra suited to the time is recited here. After this the Hotṛ
त्वं ह्यग्ने अग्निना विप्रो विप्रेण सन्त्सता । सखा सख्या समिध्यसे ॥ (*tvaṃ hyagne agninā vipro vipreṇa santsatā | sakhā sakhyā samidhyase ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-43-14)
The purport is: "O new Agni, you who are wise, joining the wise Āhavanīya Agni, be happy as a friend is happy when joined with a friend."

तं मर्जयंत सुक्रतुं पुरोयावानमाजिषु । स्वेषु क्षयेषु वाजिनमिति एष ह ना अस्य स्वः क्षयो यदग्निरग्नेः । यज्ञेन यज्ञमयजंत देवा इत्युत्तमया परिदधाति । यज्ञेन वै तद्देवा यज्ञमयजंत यदग्निनाग्निमयजंत ते स्वर्गं लोकमायन् तानि धर्माणि प्रथमान्यासन् । ते ह नाकं महिमानः सचंत यत्र पूर्वे साध्याः संति देवा इति छंदासि वै साध्या देवास्तेऽग्रेऽग्नि नाग्निमयजंत ते स्वर्गं लोकमायन् ॥ (*taṃ marjayaṃta sukratuṃ puroyāvānamājiṣu | sveṣu kṣayeṣu vājinamiti eṣa ha nā asya svaḥ kṣayo yadagniragneḥ | yajñena yajñamayajaṃta devā ityuttamayā paridadhāti | yajñena vai taddevā yajñamayajaṃta yadagnināgnimayajaṃta te svargaṃ lokamāyan tāni dharmāṇi prathamānyāsan | te ha nākaṃ mahimānaḥ sacaṃta yatra pūrve sādhyāḥ saṃti devā iti chaṃdāsi vai sādhyā devāste 'gre 'gni nāgnimayajaṃta te svargaṃ lokamāyan ‖*) **GLOSS**

Then the Hotṛ recites the Ṛk तं मर्जयंत सुक्रतुं (*taṃ marjayaṃta sukratuṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-85-8). Having said this and established Agni in the Āhavanīya fire, his own dwelling, he then recites the last Ṛk of the churning of Agni, that is, the thirteenth Ṛk, यज्ञेन यज्ञमयजंत देवाः (*yajñena yajñamayajaṃta devāḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-90-16)

and so completes the work of churning Agni. Here, the placing of the churned Agni (the Agni being made) joined with the Āhavanīya Agni is what is called अग्निनाग्निमयजंत (*agnināgnimayajaṃta*). Or else this very rite is what is stated in the last Ṛk, यज्ञेन यज्ञमयजंत देवाः (*yajñena yajñamayajaṃta devāḥ*). Here the word साध्याः (*sādhyāḥ*) means the presiding deities of the metres, the Gāyatra and the others. These deities in former times worshipped the Āhavanīya Agni with the churned Agni. By that they obtained the world of heaven.

आदित्याश्चैवेहासन्नंगिरसश्च तेऽग्रेऽग्निनाग्निमयजंत ते स्वर्गं लोकमायन् सैषा स्वर्गाहुतिर्यदग्न्याहुतिर्यदि ह वा अस्यब्राह्मणोक्तो यदि दुरुक्तोक्तो यजतेऽथ हैषाहुतिर्गच्छत्येव देवान पाप्मना संसृज्यते गच्छत्यस्याहुतिर्देवानास्स्याहुतिः पाप्मना संसृज्यते य एवं वेद ॥ (*ādityāścaivehāsannaṃgirasaśca te 'gre 'gnināgnimayajaṃta te svargaṃ lokamāyan saiṣā svargāhutiryadagnyāhutiryadi ha vā asyabrāhmaṇokto yadi duruktokto yajate 'tha haiṣāhutirgacchatyeva devāna pāpmanā saṃsṛjyate gacchatyasyāhutirdevānāssyāhutiḥ pāpmanā saṃsṛjyate ya evaṃ veda ‖*)

In the same way the Ādityas and the Aṅgirases, as stated before, performed the sacrifice and went to the world of heaven. This offering into Agni is the direct road to the world of heaven. While such a sacrificial rite is in progress, even if the chief priest is not a Brāhmaṇa as prescribed by the śāstra, or is a bad man, the offering into Agni performed in the sacrifice alone brings the sacrificer to heaven. The faults and the like of the priest do not touch the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice; that is, no harm comes to the sacrificer from them. He who knows the order of this offering into Agni, explained above, joins the gods in heaven. He has no contact with sin of any kind.

Here, it is said in the sentence above "even if he is not a Brāhmaṇa as prescribed by the śāstra". An explanation of this is necessary. Although some Brāhmaṇas, by birth alone, are Brāhmaṇas and have obtained the right of officiating at sacrifices (the right of having sacrifices performed), they misuse their right and become guilty of fault. These non-Brāhmaṇas are said in the Smṛtis to be of six kinds. Thus:

अब्राह्मणास्तु षट् प्रोक्ता इति शातातपोऽब्रवीत् । आद्यस्तु राजभृत्यः स्याद्वितीयः क्रयविक्रया ॥ तृतीयो बहुयाज्याख्यश्च तुर्थोऽश्रौतयाजकः । पंचमो ग्रामयाजी च षष्ठो ब्रह्मबंधुः स्मृतः ॥ (*abrāhmaṇāstu ṣaṭ proktā iti śātātapo 'bravīt | ādyastu rājabhṛtyaḥ syādvitīyaḥ krayavikrayā ‖ tṛtīyo bahuyājyākhyaśca turtho 'śrautayājakaḥ | paṃcamo grāmayājī ca ṣaṣṭho brahmabaṃdhuḥ smṛtaḥ ‖*)

On the question who the non-Brāhmaṇas are, Śātātapa has spoken thus. (1) The servants of kings, that is, those who, for their livelihood, depend on a king and serve him. (2) Those who live by buying and selling and the like, who keep a shop or the like and live by selling goods. (3) Those who, although they have an income sufficient for their livelihood, out of the evil desire to gain more wealth have it as their profession to have sacrifices

(or priestly offices) performed for anyone at all, are called Bahuyājins. (4) The Aśrautayājakas, that is, those who, although accomplished in the study of the Veda for performing Śrauta rites, that is, sacrifices and the like, do not engage in Śrauta rites in that way and do not have them performed for others, but engage only in Smārta rites, which are not of the highest kind, are called Aśrautayājakas. (5) The Grāmayājakas, that is, those who, in villages or in cities, for the sake of wealth have sacrifices performed for anyone at all, worthy or unworthy, are called village and city priests. (6) The Brahmabandhu, that is, those who do not perform the twilight rites and the like at the proper time, at sunrise and sunset, are called Brahmabandhus. The rite performed by these six kinds of priests is what was spoken of above as अब्राह्मणोक्त अथवा दुरुक्कोक्त (*abrāhmaṇokta athavā durukkokta*).

ता एतास्त्रयोदशान्वाह रूपसमृद्धा एतद्वै यज्ञस्य समृद्धं यद्रूपसमृद्धं यत्कर्म क्रियमाणमृगभिवदति । तासां त्रिःप्रथमामन्वाह त्रिरुत्तमां ताः सप्तदश संपद्यंते सप्तदशो नै प्रजापतिर्द्वादश मासाः पंचर्तवस्तावान्संवत्सरः संवत्सरः प्रजापतिः प्रजापत्यायतनाभिरेवाभी राध्योति य एवं पेद त्रिः प्रथमां त्रिरुत्तमामन्वाह यज्ञस्यैव तद्बर्सौ नह्यति स्थेन्ने बलायाविस्रंसाय ॥ (*tā etāstrayodaśānvāha rūpasamṛddhā etadvai yajñasya samṛddhaṃ yadrūpasamṛddhaṃ yatkarma kriyamāṇamṛgabhivadati | tāsāṃ triḥprathamāmanvāha triruttamāṃ tāḥ saptadaśa saṃpadyaṃte saptadaśo nai prajāpatirdvādaśa māsāḥ paṃcartavastāvānsaṃvatsaraḥ saṃvatsaraḥ prajāpatiḥ prajāpatyāyatanābhirevābhī rādhyoti ya evaṃ peda triḥ prathamāṃ triruttamāmanvāha yajñasyaiva tadbarsau nahyati sthenne balāyāvisraṃsāya ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 3-5)

Thus the Ṛks used in the work of churning Agni are thirteen in all. The nine Ṛks addressed to the deity of the Rākṣoghna are not included in this. By reciting these thirteen Ṛks at their respective times, the rites of churning Agni, producing Agni, carrying Agni and placing him in the Āhavanīya, and joining him there with the Āhavanīya Agni, are all carried out completely by the recitation of the appropriate Ṛks; this is called rūpasamṛddhi. Of these thirteen Ṛks the first Ṛk (the Ṛk अभि त्वा देव सवितः (*abhi tvā deva savitaḥ*)) and the last Ṛk (the Ṛk यज्ञेन यज्ञमयजंत देवाः (*yajñena yajñamayajaṃta devāḥ*)) must be recited by the Hotṛ three times each. Therefore in all, seventeen Ṛks are recited in this work of churning Agni. Prajāpati is of the nature of the number seventeen. For twelve months and five seasons together make one year, and that year is Prajāpati. Therefore he who knows the meaning of these Ṛks, which are placed in Prajāpati, attains prosperity. By reciting the first and the last Ṛks thrice each, the bonds (knots) of the sacrifice become firm and tight, and there is room for them to stand steady, without slipping. Thus the description of the work of churning Agni is set out in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa (Ai. Brā. 3-5).

At the churning of Agni, when the Agni that has been produced is cast into the Āhavanīya, this Ṛk, together with the next, is to be recited as the anuvākyā. This is laid down in the sūtra (Ā. Sū. 2-16). O Adhvaryus, cast forth Agni, who is divine, shining, the finder and bringer of wealth; that is, throw him into the Āhavanīya fire. For what purpose? For the eating of the gods. So also a Brāhmaṇa says that for the one who is being cast in, this Ṛk is suitable, and what is suitable in the sacrifice is successful (Ai. Brā. 1-16). And may that Agni sit down in his own source, that is, in his own place, the Āhavanīya; may he be seated in it. And there is a Brāhmaṇa: this is indeed his own source, the Agni of Agni (Ai. Brā. 1-16).
- देवं (*devaṃ*)—(O Adhvaryus) the one divine in nature
- वसुवित्तमं (*vasuvittamaṃ*)—the bestower of abundant wealth, Agni
- देववीतये (*devavītaye*)—for the gods, to eat the oblation
- स्वे योन्सौ (*sve yonsau*)—(that same Agni) in his own place, the Āhavanīya
- आ नि षीदतु (*ā ni ṣīdatu*)—let him sit down
O Adhvaryus, establish Agni, who is divine in nature and the bestower of abundant wealth, so that he may eat the oblation for the gods. May that same Agni sit down in his own place, the Āhavanīya.
Conduct the divine (Agni), the bestower of infinite wealth, to (receive charge of) the food of the gods: let him sit down on his appropriate seat.

That at the time of churning Agni, after Agni has been produced, when that Agni is placed in the fire-pit called Āhavanīya, this Ṛk प्र देवं देववीतये (*pra devaṃ devavītaye*) and the following Ṛk are to be recited, is shown by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, प्र देवं देववीतय इति द्वे अग्निनाग्निः समिध्यते (*pra devaṃ devavītaya iti dve agnināgniḥ samidhyate*) (Ā. Sū. 2-16).
The rite of Agni-churning has been explained at length in the special topics of the preceding Ṛk (the 40th Ṛk). See that.

O Adhvaryus, cause the Agni who has been born, who has appeared, to be established; he is dear like a guest (the word of comparison is omitted here). Therefore he is the lord of the houses. Establish him in the Āhavanīya fire, the comfortable one, which is the Agni of born wisdom. The word "śiśīta" means "make to lie down, establish"; or else it means "make to go, cause to reach"; or else it means "sharpen, prepare, cast in". The words "jāta itaro jātavedā itaraḥ" and the Brāhmaṇa passage that begins with them (Ai. Brā. 1-16) are to be considered here.
- गृहपतिं (*gṛhapatiṃ*)—the protector of the house, Agni
- स्कोने (*skone*)—in the Āhavanīya, which is comfortable
O Adhvaryus, establish Agni, who has arisen, who like a guest is beneficent, who is the protector of the house, in the Āhavanīya, which is the support of knowledge and comfortable.
(Welcome him) as soon as born, like a beloved guest, and place the lord of the mansion upon the sacred (altar) whence wisdom is derived.

For the special application and the explanation of this Ṛk, see the last part of the description of the rite called Agni-manthana (kindling of fire by friction) in the special topics of the 41st Ṛk of this same sūkta.

Sāyaṇa addresses the shining Agni: harness to your own chariot those horses. The horses that are yours are "sādhavaḥ", that is, accomplishing or of good disposition, and they carry sufficiently ("aram" is "alam", enough). For what purpose? मन्यवे (*manyave*): "manyu" means the sacrifice, because here the gods are thought of as to be sacrificed to; for that sacrifice the horses are to be harnessed to the chariot. "Hi" means "indeed".
- मन्यवे (*manyave*)—for the sake of the sacrifice
O Agni of divine nature, join to the chariot, for the sake of the sacrifice, those horses of yours, of good disposition, which carry you comfortably, so that you may come.
Harness, divine Agni, your well-trained horses; they bear you quickly to the sacrifice.

O Agni, come to us, facing us. Likewise, having in view the foods in the form of oblations ("prayāṃsi"), bring the gods. For what purpose? वीतये (*vītaye*): for the enjoyment of those oblations. And likewise bring those gods for the drinking of Soma, सोमपीतये (*somapītaye*).
- वीतये (*vītaye*)—for the eating of the oblations
- सोमपीतये (*somapītaye*)—for the drinking of Soma as well
O Agni, graciously come to us, facing us. For the eating of the oblations, bring the gods, facing the oblations. For the drinking of Soma as well, bring them.
Come, Agni, to our presence ; bring hither the gods to partake of the (srcrificial) viands, to drink the Soma juice.

O Bhārata, bearer of the oblations, Agni, blaze up; shine higher. He explains this: O ageless Agni, you who are shining greatly, shine forth specially with a brilliance that is radiant (the instrumental ending is dropped), unceasing and uninterrupted. Or else the root "bhā" here has a causative sense: first blaze up, and afterwards illumine the whole world with your own brilliance; so it is to be construed. The word दविद्युतत् (*davidyutat*) is explained by him as "shining intensely".
- अजस्रेण (*ajasreṇa*)—with the brilliance that is unceasing
O Agni, bearer of the oblation, shine exceedingly. O imperishable Agni, being exceedingly radiant, shine forth exceedingly with brilliance that is luminous and unceasing.
Blaze up, Agni, bearer of oblations : shine, undecaying Agni, radiant with undecaying lustre.

The mortal, the man, who is "havismān", provided with oblations, the sacrificer, who with desired food in the form of oblation worships some deity or other, should in that sacrifice also praise Agni; that is, in all sacrifices Agni is honoured. What kind of Agni? The caller of those who dwell in the two worlds, heaven and earth ("rodasyoḥ"), and the one who sacrifices with a true, unfailing oblation. Further, this sacrificer, standing with uplifted hands, his hands folded in salutation, should attend upon such an Agni with reverence or with an oblation ("ā vivāset" means "should serve").
- अध्वरे (*adhvare*)—at that same time of the sacrifice that sacrificer
- होतारं (*hotāraṃ*)—the one who gives the invocation
- सत्ययुजं (*satyayujaṃ*)—the one who performs the sacrifice whose nature is truth

Whichever man, possessing oblation, worships whichever deity with the oblation, as an auxiliary to that, at that time of the sacrifice he should also praise Agni, who gives the invocation to heaven and earth and who performs the sacrifice whose nature is truth. Raising the folded hands upward, he should attend upon him with salutation.

Whatever mortal, offering oblations, worships a deity with (sacrificial) food, let him at the ceremony also worship Agni, the invoker of heaven and earth, the sacrificer with truth; let him adore (Agni) with uplifted hands.

Āśvalāyana holds that by this Ṛk the study of the Veda is praised (Gṛ. 1-1-5).⟨NOTE:310⟩ O Agni, we bring to you, with the heart, the oblation तप्पं (*tappaṃ*), that is, prepared, which exists in the form of the Ṛk; making the Ṛk itself the oblation, we bring it.⟨NOTE:311⟩ By the word "te" ("that") the oblation in Ṛk form under discussion is referred to, its masculine gender and plural number being by regard to what it is pointed back to. That oblation in Ṛk form, for you, let it become bulls ("ukṣaṇaḥ", able to sprinkle), "ṛṣabhāsaḥ" (bulls) and also "vaśāḥ" (cows). The rest is to be supplied thus: having been transformed into the form of bulls and cows, let it be for your eating.
notes: abbreviation ಆ. ಗೃ. printed
ಗೋಸಂಬಂಧೂರ್ಯರ್ವಂ: reading doubtful; read as the herd connected with cows

en: - ऋचा (*ṛcā*)—and in the form of the Ṛk
- आ भरामसि (*ā bharāmasi*)—we offer (this very oblation)

O Agni, we offer to you wholeheartedly the well-prepared oblation that is in the form of the Ṛk. May this very oblation be for you like bulls that have the power of sprinkling, strong, and like cows that supply the ghee and the like fit for oblation.
We offer to you, Agni, the oblation sanctified by the heart, and (identified) with the sacred verse : may the vigorous bulls and the cows be (as such an oblation) to you.

It is the view of the great sage Āśvalāyana that the praise of the study of the Veda is stated in this Ṛk of this sūkta (Ā. Gṛ. Sū. 1-1-5).⟨NOTE:312⟩ It is the opinion of the great sage Āśvalāyana, the author of the Śrauta and Gṛhya Sūtras and others, that in order that the study of the Veda may succeed, one should meditate on Agni alone in the mind with this Ṛk and offer oblations of ghee and the like in the fire, and that Agni is thereby satisfied.
notes: block b6 ವಾಜಾನ್ ॥ ೨ ॥ is a stray repeat of the last word of the Pada under the ಸಾಯಣಭಾಷ್ಯಂ label

en: The gods kindle this Agni, who is the chief and the foremost slayer of Vṛtra. By this Agni the treasures that the Asuras had carried off were brought back; or, according to the other explanation, the foods in the form of oblations were brought back, whether from the Asuras or from the sacrificer. By this mighty Agni the Rākṣasas, who are hostile to the sacrifice, were crushed and destroyed. The gods kindle that Agni: such is the construction.
- वसूनि (*vasūni*)—the treasures carried off by the Asuras
- वाजिना (*vājinā*)—by which Agni endowed with strength

The gods cause to blaze that Agni, the chief among the gods and the destroyer of Vṛtra, by whom the treasures carried off by the Asuras were brought back, and by whom, being endowed with strength, all the Asuras were destroyed.
The gods kindle Agni as the chief (of them) ; as the special destroyer of Vritra ; by whom the treasures(of the Asuras) are carried off ; by whom the Rakshasas are destroyed.
वृत्रहंतारं (*vṛtrahaṃtāraṃ*)—Since the word vṛtra also means an enemy, Agni is praised here as the one who restrains the enemies, the Rākṣasas and the like (the Rakṣohan Agni).

वसूनि आधृता वाजिना रक्षांसि तृळ्हा (*vasūni ādhṛtā vājinā rakṣāṃsi tṛḷhā*)—The word vasu means wealth. Here the commentator has given two kinds of meaning for this word: first, the foods in the form of oblations (हविर्लक्षणान्यन्नानि (*havirlakṣaṇānyannāni*))

and second, the wealth carried off by the Asuras (असुरैरपहृतानि धनानि (*asurairapahṛtāni dhanāni*)). Since this Ṛk speaks of the Asuras being destroyed by Agni (रक्षांसि तृळ्हा (*rakṣāṃsi tṛḷhā*)), the second meaning, wealth carried off by the Asuras, is the fitting one for the word vasūni. The principal sense is that the gods caused such an Agni to blaze well in the sacrifice, in order to obtain through Agni their share of the oblation.
वेदार्थस्य प्रकाशेन तमो हार्दं निवारयन् । पुमर्थांश्च तुरो देयाद्विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरः ॥ (*vedārthasya prakāśena tamo hārdaṃ nivārayan | pumarthāṃśca turo deyādvidyātīrthamaheśvaraḥ ‖*)

इति श्रीमद्राजाधिराज परमेश्वर वैदिकमार्गप्रवर्तक श्री वीरबुक्कभूपालसाम्राज्यधुरंधरेण सायणाचार्येण विरचिते माधवीये वेदार्थप्रकाशे ऋक्संहिताभाष्ये चतुर्थाष्टके पंचमोऽध्यायः समाप्तः ॥ (*iti śrīmadrājādhirāja parameśvara vaidikamārgapravartaka śrī vīrabukkabhūpālasāmrājyadhuraṃdhareṇa sāyaṇācāryeṇa viracite mādhavīye vedārthaprakāśe ṛksaṃhitābhāṣye caturthāṣṭake paṃcamo 'dhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ ‖*)
Here ends the fifth chapter, in the fourth aṣṭaka of the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, accompanied by the bhāṣya of Śrī Sāyaṇa and by a Kannada translation.
यदक्षरपदभ्रष्टं मात्राहीनं तु यद्भवेत् । तत्सर्वं क्षम्यतां देव वागीश्वर नमोऽस्तुते ॥ (*yadakṣarapadabhraṣṭaṃ mātrāhīnaṃ tu yadbhavet | tatsarvaṃ kṣamyatāṃ deva vāgīśvara namo 'stute ‖*)
वागीशाद्याः सुमनसः सर्वार्थानामुपक्रमे । यं नत्वा कृतकृत्याः स्युस्तं नमामि गजाननं ॥ (*vāgīśādyāḥ sumanasaḥ sarvārthānāmupakrame | yaṃ natvā kṛtakṛtyāḥ syustaṃ namāmi gajānanaṃ ‖*)
यस्य निश्वसितं वेदा यो वेदेभ्योऽखिलं जगत् । निर्ममे तमहं वंदे विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरं ॥ (*yasya niśvasitaṃ vedā yo vedebhyo 'khilaṃ jagat | nirmame tamahaṃ vaṃde vidyātīrthamaheśvaraṃ ‖*)
वेदः शिवः शिवो वेदो वेदाध्यायी सदाशिवः । तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन वेदमेव सदा जपेत् ॥ (*vedaḥ śivaḥ śivo vedo vedādhyāyī sadāśivaḥ | tasmātsarvaprayatnena vedameva sadā japet ‖*)
Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, with the bhāṣya of Sāyaṇa.
The sixth chapter in the fourth aṣṭaka.

In this sixth maṇḍala, seen by the seer Bharadvāja, sūktas 1–16 have Agni as their deity. They were explained in the previous chapter. The following sūktas, 17–46, have Indra as their deity. The present sixth chapter contains only sūktas 17–28 (eleven in all), so all the sūktas of this chapter are mantras that praise Indra. Only in the 28th sūkta is it said that the cows are the deity of six Ṛks, yet the sūkta as a whole is stated, as an alternative, to have Indra as its deity. We have explained Indra at length in Ṛ. Saṃ. Part 16, pp. 631–683, and in many other places. Therefore here only the derivation of the form of the word Indra will be explained, and later, wherever there are particular matters concerning Indra in the respective mantras, only those will be pointed out in their places.
Indra—In explaining the derivation of the word Indra, the commentator has cited the Nirukta of Yāska itself:

इंद्र इरां दृणातीति वेरां ददातीति वेरां दधातीति वेरां दारयतीति वेरां धारयतीति वेंदवे द्रवतीति वेंदौ रमत इति वेंधे भूतानीति वा तद्यदेनं प्राणैः सम्यंधंस्तदिंद्रस्येंद्रत्वमिति विज्ञायत इदंकरणादित्याग्रायण इदंदर्शनादित्यौपमन्यद इंदतेर्वैश्वर्यकर्मण इंदञ्छत्रूणां दारयिता ना द्रावयिता नादयिता च यज्जनां । (*iṃdra irāṃ dṛṇātīti verāṃ dadātīti verāṃ dadhātīti verāṃ dārayatīti verāṃ dhārayatīti veṃdave dravatīti veṃdau ramata iti veṃdhe bhūtānīti vā tadyadenaṃ prāṇaiḥ samyaṃdhaṃstadiṃdrasyeṃdratvamiti vijñāyata idaṃkaraṇādityāgrāyaṇa idaṃdarśanādityaupamanyada iṃdatervaiśvaryakarmaṇa iṃdañchatrūṇāṃ dārayitā nā drāvayitā nādayitā ca yajjanāṃ |*) (Ni. 10-8).
He himself has given the meaning of this:

(1) The root दृ (*dṛ*) means to split, to cut. Irā means food, which we obtain from the plants and trees, that is, from the vegetable kingdom. For that vegetable kingdom to grow, water is necessary. For that water, that is, in order that rain may fall, he cuts the cloud (with lightning, the thunderbolt); therefore he is named Indra.
(2) The root दा (*dā*) means to give. He gives irā, that is, food, by means of vṛṣṭi (rain); therefore he is named Indra.
(3) The root धा (*dhā*) means to nourish. He nourishes the plants and the like that yield food by bestowing water (rain); therefore he is named Indra.
(4) Land has to be ploughed for the production of food. When the land is ploughed, he makes it split by the plough and makes it favourable for the crop; therefore he is named Indra.
(5) As said before, he nourishes the plants and the like and protects them so that they do not perish; therefore he is named Indra.

(6) इंदुः (*iṃduḥ*) is Soma, the juice of the creeper. Indu means the Soma juice prepared from the Soma plant. He runs (hastens) to the place of sacrifice for the drinking of such Soma; therefore he is named Indra.
(7) He delights and sports in the Soma juice mentioned before, being satisfied with it; therefore he is named Indra.

(8) The root इंथ् (*iṃth*) means to shine, to illumine. Entering the bodies of living beings in the form of the vital spirit, he shines, urging them to do their respective deeds; therefore he is named Indra.

(9) Because worshippers kindled (made to shine well) this god, who is the Supreme Self, through meditation, uniting him with the organs such as speech and sight, and with the vital airs such as prāṇa and apāna, and with grain, as if shining forth well; for that reason the name Indra came about.

(10) The sage named Āgrāyaṇa holds that the derivation is that he makes this (idam-karaṇa). Indra, in the form of the Supreme Self, makes this world. Idaṃkaraṇa means that, in the form of the Supreme Self, Indra builds (creates) this world; for this reason this god received the name Indra, says the sage named Āgrāyaṇa.

(11) The sage named Aupamanyava says that the derivation is that he sees this (idam-darśana). Here idam means what is not directly perceived, what does not appear directly to the eye. For this very reason the Śruti says परोक्षप्रिया इव हि देवाः (*parokṣapriyā iva hi devāḥ*). Aupamanyava says that because he sees this, that is, everything, the name Indra came about.

(12) The root इदि (*idi*) has the meaning of supreme lordship. This god has, through his own māyā, the supreme lordship of taking the form of the world; hence the name Indra. This view is supported by the Vedic sentence इंद्रो मायाभिः पुरुरूप ईयते (*iṃdro māyābhiḥ pururūpa īyate*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-47-18).

(13) The word ina denotes the Lord. When the vowel a following the n of this word ina is dropped, the word इन् (*in*) remains. The root दृ (*dṛ*) means fear. That Supreme Lord causes fear to enemies; hence he is named Indra.
(14) The root द्रु (*dru*) means going, that is, to go, to run away. This god makes enemies run away; hence he is named Indra.
(15) He honours those who worship him with sacrifices and the like, and removes their fear; therefore this god is named Indra.
In the same way, many derivations can be devised for the word Indra.

O Indra, fierce and of uplifted strength, you who are praised by the Aṅgirases: in order to drink which Soma you made manifest the great herd of cattle that had been carried off by the Paṇis (the word ऊर्वं (*ūrvaṃ*) here means a mass or herd).⟨NOTE:313⟩ The root tṛd, which commonly has the sense of harming, has here the sense of making manifest. Drink that Soma. O bold one, assailant of enemies, O thunderbolt-handed Indra, you who, together with your strengths, have slain every enemy Vṛtra, the encloser: that same you drink the Soma. Such is the connection.
notes: ಹರಿಷ್ಠಾಃ: Kannada gloss ಅಶ್ವಗಳ ಸ್ಥಾಪಕ "establisher of horses"; Sāyaṇa has ಹರ್ಯೋಃ ಸ್ಥಾತಾಸಿ "you stand on the two bay horses"

en: - गृणानः (*gṛṇānaḥ*)—you who are praised by the Aṅgirases
- यं अभि (*yaṃ abhi*)—having in view which Soma for drinking
- वज्रहस्त (*vajrahasta*)—holder of the thunderbolt, O Indra
- वि वधिषः (*vi vadhiṣaḥ*)—have destroyed (such you, drink the Soma)
O Indra, of fearsome strength, you who are praised by the Aṅgirases: drink that very Soma, having in view the drinking of which you made manifest the herd of cows carried off by the Paṇis.
Drink it. O Indra, assailant of enemies and holder of the thunderbolt: you who, joined with your strengths, have destroyed the whole host of enemies, the encloser, such you drink the Soma.

Fierce Indra, glorified by us, drink that Soma, (animated) by which you have discovered the vast herd of cattle (stolen by the Panis), and, overcomer of enemies, wielder of the thunderbolt, you have slain, by your strength all opposing foes.

Formerly the Asuras called Paṇis carried off the cows of the Aṅgirasa seers and hid them in the caves of a mountain so that no one could see them. For the release of those cows the Aṅgirasa seers praised Indra in the sacrifice and offered him Soma juice for drinking. In the present Ṛk Indra is prayed to become powerful for the release of the cows, and for that to drink Soma.

O Indra, ṛjīṣin: by the word ṛjīṣa is meant the Soma whose juice is spent; you who possess it are tarutra, the one who carries across the enemies, that is, overcomes them. You are śiprāvān, one with handsome jaws. You are the showerer of desires for the praisers (the word मतीनां (*matīnāṃ*) means the praisers). Such as you are, drink this Soma. O Indra, you who bear the thunderbolt, you who are the splitter of the gotras, that is, of the mountains or of the clouds, you who are the one who stands on the two bay horses: O Indra, such as you are, make manifest to us the various and manifold foods.
notes: no label ವಿಶೇಷವಿಷಯಗಳು in kn.md before ಈ ಋಕ್ಕಿನಲ್ಲಿಯೂ; the line ॥ ೮. ಕ್ರಿಯಾಪದಗಳು ॥ precedes it

en: - ऋजीषी (*ṛjīṣī*)—you who possess Soma whose juice is spent
- अभि तृंधि (*abhi tṛṃdhi*)—make manifest to us
notes: ಮಾತರ್ ನಿರ್ಮಾಣ್ಯಾವೃತಸ್ಯ: reading damaged

en: O Indra, you who possess Soma whose juice is spent, who overcome and defeat the enemies, who have handsome cheeks, who are the showerer of desires for the praisers: such you, drink this Soma juice. O Indra, bearer of the thunderbolt, you who are the splitter of mountains, who are the establisher of horses: such you, provide us with foods of many kinds.

Drink it, Indra, you who enjoy the flavourless Soma ; you who are the preservr, the handsome-chinned, the showerer (of benefits) on those who praise you; you are the breaker of the mountains, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the curber of steeds, bestow us various food.

ऋजीषी (*ṛjīṣī*)—Ṛjīṣa means the husks of the Soma creeper that remain after the juice has been pressed out. In these the Soma juice is not abundant. Therefore these husks are soaked well in water, and the little juice that remains is pressed out well once more.

Mixed with barley flour, this is offered to Indra at the third pressing of the sacrifice. Since he drinks the Soma that is in such ṛjīṣa, the addressing of Indra as ṛjīṣin is seen especially in the Ṛgveda. We have explained the word ṛjīṣa in detail earlier, in the story of the fetching of the Soma.

O Indra, as you drank the ancient Somas of former times, so drink this Soma of ours. May that Soma, drunk by you, exhilarate you. Hear the praise made by us, and increase by our praises in the form of words. Make manifest also Sūrya, the god who impels all; that is, act so that we may see the sun. Nourish us with foods; make them swell for us. Slay our rivals the enemies; destroy them. O Indra, make manifest the cows carried off by the Paṇis.
- प्रश्नधा (*praśnadhā*)—just as you drank the former Soma juices
- अभि तृंधि (*abhi tṛṃdhi*)—cause to come back
