notes: abbreviation ಋಗ್ವೇ. printed

en: - पतने (*patane*)—as the result of the blow
- सूरस्य सातौ (*sūrasya sātau*)—for the worship of the sun

When the Asura named Śuṣṇa met his death as the result of the blow of the vajra weapon, then the all-pervading strength of that deceiver, who was possessed of great power, was hidden. That same Indra, for Kutsa, who was his charioteer, made the one chariot common to both very wide, for the worship of the sun.

When Sushna passed away upon the falling of the thunderbolt, then the universal strength of the great oppressor was annihilated; and Indra enlarged their common car for (the use of) his charioteer Kutsa, for (the sake of) the worship of the sun.

The hawk, the Suparṇa, brought to this Indra the intoxicating soma; the word "na" is here used in the sense of conjunction, and "pra" has the sense of "ā"; the verb "brought" is supplied because the preposition is seen. And this Indra also, crushing the head of the Asura named Namuci, the destroyer of living beings, protected the sage named Nami, the son of Sapa, who was asleep, and joined that sage with wealth such as cattle and with food. ⟨NOTE:349⟩
notes: abbreviation ಋಗ್ವೇ. printed

en: The Suparṇa bird brought to Indra the intoxicating soma. Cutting off the head of the violent Namuci, Indra protected the sage called Nami, the son of Sapana, who was asleep. With imperishable wealth and with food he made that sage rich.

And the hawk bore to Indra the exhilarating Soma, when bruising the head of the oppressor Namachi, and protecting the slumbering Nami, the son of Saya, he provided, for the well-being (of the sage), riches and food.

The matter of the Suparṇa or Śyena bird bringing the soma that was in heaven, and the matter of Indra slaying the rākṣasa called Namuci, we have already explained in detail earlier in this same part. The matter of Namuci is also stated in Ṛ. Saṃ. Part 10, page 550.

O Indra, wielder of the vajra, with your strength you have split the firm cities, that is, the ramparts and other strongholds, belonging to the Asura Pipru, whose deceptions are deadly; the word "na" only fills out the pāda. This is seen from: त्वं पिप्रोर्नृमणः प्रारुजः पुरः (*tvaṃ piprornṛmaṇaḥ prārujaḥ puraḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-51-5) **GLOSS** ⟨NOTE:350⟩, and शतं पूर्भिरायसीभिर्नि पाहि (*śataṃ pūrbhirāyasībhirni pāhi*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-3-7) **GLOSS** ⟨NOTE:351⟩. And further, O Indra, good giver, to the royal sage named Ṛjiśvan, who had given offerings, you gave the wealth, in the form of oblation, that no one can overcome, which was his own.
notes: ಪಿಪು printed in the gloss for ಪಿಪ್ರು
ಜೇಯಧ್ಯಾ ಏತುಂ ದ್ಯೋತನಾಯ್ಕೆತತ್ಸಂಜ್ಞಾಯ in the Sāyaṇa block damaged

en: - वज्रिन् (*vajrin*)—O Indra, bearer of the vajra weapon
- दात्रं (*dātraṃ*)—wealth in the form of oblation
- ऋजिश्वने (*ṛjiśvane*)—to the royal sage named Ṛjiśvan
- अप्रमृष्यं (*apramṛṣyaṃ*)—which cannot be destroyed by anyone
notes: two references printed after the quotation: ಋ. ಸಂ. ೧೨-೮೯-೮ and ಋ. ಸಂ. ೧-೪೯-೪

en: O Indra, bearer of the vajra weapon, you have split by your strength the firm strongholds of the Asura named Pipu, whose deceptive acts are destructive. O Indra, excellent giver, to the royal sage named Ṛjiśvan, who offers wealth in the form of oblation, you have given your wealth that cannot be destroyed by anyone.

You have scattered by force, wielder of the thunderbolt, the strong cities of the deadly-deluding Pipru : you have given, bountiful Indra, uninjurable wealth to Rijiswat, the donor of sacrificial gifts.

Pipu and Ṛjiśvan. The Asura Pipu is an enemy of Indra. That Indra defeated this Asura in order to protect the sage Ṛjiśvan is stated in many Ṛks of the Ṛgveda, namely in the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-101-2; 4-16-13; 5-29-11; 6-20-7; 8-49-10; 10-99-11; 10-138-3; 1-103-8; 2-14-5; 6-18-8. And in the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-51-5; 6-21-7 mention is made of the city of Pipru. In the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-32-2; 10-138-3 he is called Dāsa and Asura. In Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-101-1; 4-16-13 the impression appears that he was connected with the dark people, the earlier inhabitants of this country. The name of Ṛjiśvan is recited in the Ṛgveda in the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-51-5; 1-53-8; 1-101-1; 6-20-7; 8-49-10; 10-99-11; 10-138-3. But not many particulars can be learned. It is suggested that he helped Indra when Indra fought with the Asura Pipu. In the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-16-13; 5-29-11 he is clearly called Vaidathina, the son of one named Vidathin.

He by whom desirable, approachable comforts are to be given, that Indra, brought under control the Asura named Vetasu, of many deceptions, and Daśoṇi, and Tūtuji, and also the Asura named Tugra and likewise the Asura named Ibha, for the sake of a king of that name, Dyotana, constantly; the example is that of a mother: as a son becomes obedient to his mother, so he made them obedient. The word "sīm" only fills out the pāda. ⟨NOTE:353⟩
notes: Ṛk number not printed at the end of the Saṃhitā or Pada text; 10 taken from the sequence

en: - मातुः न (*mātuḥ na*)—as a son comes forward obedient before his mother
- शश्वत् (*śaśvat*)—so that they may be wholly obedient
- उप सृज (*upa sṛja*)—he brought under his power

That same Indra, who gives attractive wealth, brought under the power of the king named Dyotana the Asura named Vetasu, a deceiver in many ways, and likewise the Asuras Daśoṇi, Tūtuji, Tugra and Ibha, so that, as a son comes forward obedient before his mother, they came humbly before him and were wholly obedient.

Indra, the granter of wished-for felicity, compelled the many-fraudulent Vetasu and Dasoni, Tutuji, Tugra, and Ibha, always to come submissively to (the Raja) Dyotana, as a son (comes before a mother.)

In this Ṛk it is said that Indra defeated the Asuras Vetasu, Daśoṇi, Tūtuji, Tugra and Ibha and delivered them into the power of the king named Dyotana. That Indra defeated the Asura Vetasu is stated in the Ṛk
अहं पितेव वेतसूरभिष्टये तुग्रं कुत्साय स्मदिभं च रंधयं । (*ahaṃ piteva vetasūrabhiṣṭaye tugraṃ kutsāya smadibhaṃ ca raṃdhayaṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 12-89-8) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-49-4) **GLOSS** ⟨NOTE:354⟩

and also in the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-58-5; 6-26-4; 6-20-8; 10-49-4. The word Tugra, in this Ṛk and in 10-49-4 given as an example, denotes an Asura of that name. In other places Tugra is a famous king, and it is said in many places that the Aśvins saved his son Bhujyu from drowning in the sea. Therefore there is no room for doubt that Tugra the king is one person and Tugra the Asura another.
दशोणिं (*daśoṇiṃ*)—his name is recited in the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-20-4; 6-28-8; 10-96-12; 8-52-2,
इभं (*ibhaṃ*)—in the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-57-3; 6-20-8; 1-84-17; 4-4-1. Their matter will be explained in detail later.
notes: ಯದುಷು ತುರ್ವಶೇಷು ಎಂದು ಬಹುವಚನಗಳು ... sentence incomplete as printed

en: Bearing in his hand his own weapon, the vajra, the slayer of enemies, unopposed by enemies, that Indra slays these rivals, Vṛtra and the others. He mounts his two horses; the example is a thrower, a hero, who mounts a chariot. In the same way the two horses, yoked by a word alone, or else yoked by the praises of the praisers, carry the great Indra.
- अस्तेव (*asteva*)—as a hero who destroys enemies mounts and sits
- वचोयुजा (*vacoyujā*)—those horses that join the chariot by the mere command of speech

The unopposed Indra, bearing in his hand the enemy-destroying vajra weapon, destroys Vṛtra and the others who rival him. As a hero who destroys enemies mounts and sits in a chariot, Indra mounts and sits in his chariot (to which the horses are yoked). Those horses, which join the chariot by the mere command of speech, carry the great Indra.

Bearing in his hand the foe-destroying thunderbolt, Indra, unresisted, demolishing these his adversaries ; he mounts his two-horse (car), as warrior (ascends) his chariot ; harnessed at a word, his steeds convey the mitgty Indra.

notes: abbreviation ಋಗ್ವೇ. printed

en: O Indra, by your protection we, the praisers, would obtain new wealth given by you. The Pūrus, men, the praisers, praise you with sacrifices accompanied by this praise. The reason is this: you, O Indra, giving riches to the king named Purukutsa and slaying the hostile offspring of the enemy who harm rites, have split with your vajra the seven cities belonging to the Asura named Śarat; therefore the praisers praise you.
- शारदीः (*śāradīḥ*)—belonging to the Asura named Śarat

O Indra, favoured by your protection, may we obtain new wealth. O Indra, by that greatness of yours by which you destroyed the harmful Asuras, and, giving riches to the king named Purukutsa, split the seven cities belonging to the Asura named Śarat
with the vajra weapon, praising that same greatness, the human praisers praise you with sacrifices accompanied by these praises.

(Favoured) by your protection, Indra, we solicit new (wealth): by this adoration men glorify you at sacrifices, for that you have shattered with your bolt the seven cities of Sharat, killing the opponents (of sacred rites), and giving (their spoils) to Purukutsa.
We have already explained the matter of Purukutsa earlier.

O Indra, you, the ancient, desiring wealth for Kāvya, the son of the poet, Uśanas of the line of Bhṛgu, have become an increaser; you are the increaser of the praisers. Having slain the Asura named Navavāstva, you delivered his own son, the son of Uśanas, who had been seized by enemies in battle and was to be given back, to the great father, Uśanas, who was to be protected; having slain his enemy, you gave him forth.
- वृधः भूः (*vṛdhaḥ bhūḥ*)—you have become an increaser of the praisers
- अनुदेयं (*anudeyaṃ*)—who was to be given back
- स्वं नपातं (*svaṃ napātaṃ*)—the son of Uśanas
- महे पित्रे (*mahe pitre*)—to the great father, that is, to Uśanas

O Indra, you, the ancient, desiring wealth for Uśanas, the poet's son, have become an increaser of the praisers. Having destroyed the Asura named Navavāstva, you delivered the son back to the great Uśanas.

Desirous of opulence, you, Indra, have been an ancient benefactor of Ushanas, the son of Kavi : having slain Navavastwa, you have given back his own grandson, who was (fit) to be restored to the grandfather.

नववास्त्वं (*navavāstvaṃ*)—the name of Navavāstva occurs in the Ṛgveda in three places only. In Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-36-18 it is said that Agni defeated him; in Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-20-11 that Indra defeated him and gave the son of Uśanas, who was in his power, into his father's power; and in Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-49-6 there is a description of Indra's defeating him. In two places he is also called Bṛhadratha.

O Indra, shaker of enemies, you have brought the waters, those in which the Asura named Dhuni was present as an obstructer, flowing forth like rivers; that is, having slain Dhuni, you make the waters obstructed by him flow. O hero Indra, when, having crossed the ocean, you reach the other shore, then you carry over in safety Turvaśa and Yadu, who stood across the ocean; you ferried them over the ocean.
- धुनिमतीः (*dhunimatīḥ*)—obstructed by the Asura named Dhuni
- अति प्र पर्षि (*ati pra parṣi*)—you cross and reach the shore (then)

O Indra, you who make enemies tremble have transformed the waters obstructed by the Asura named Dhuni into streams flowing like rivers. O valiant Indra, when you cross the ocean and reach the shore, then you carry Turvaśa and Yadu across in safety.

You, Indra, who make (your enemies) tremble, have caused the waters, detained by Dhuni, to flow like rushing rivers : so, hero, when, having crossed the ocean, you have reached the shore, you have brought over in safety Turvasa and Yadu.
We have already told of the Asura Dhuni earlier.

तुर्वशं यदुं (*turvaśaṃ yaduṃ*)—wherever the names of the two persons Yadu and Turvaśa occur, it is understood that both were royal sages and recipients of the favour of Indra and Agni. The plurals यदुषु तुर्वशेषु (*yaduṣu turvaśeṣu*), in which these two names have come together, occur, one may say, in this one place only in the whole Ṛksaṃhitā. ⟨NOTE:356⟩
अग्निना तुर्वशं यदुं परावत उग्रादेवं हवामहे (*agninā turvaśaṃ yaduṃ parāvata ugrādevaṃ havāmahe*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-36-18) **GLOSS**
त्वमाविथ नर्यं तुर्वशं यदुं त्वं तुर्वितिं वय्यं शतक्रतो । (*tvamāvitha naryaṃ turvaśaṃ yaduṃ tvaṃ turvitiṃ vayyaṃ śatakrato |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-54-6) **GLOSS**
In these and other such Ṛks it is stated that both royal sages obtained the protection of Agni and of Indra. The chief deed of daring of Turvaśa was his fighting with Sudāsa.

पुरोळा इत्तुर्वशो यक्षुरासीद्राये मत्स्यासो निशिता अपीव । श्रुष्टिं चक्रुर्भृगवो द्रुह्यवश्च सखा सखायमतरद्विषूचोः । (*puroḷā itturvaśo yakṣurāsīdrāye matsyāso niśitā apīva | śruṣṭiṃ cakrurbhṛgavo druhyavaśca sakhā sakhāyamataradviṣūcoḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-18-6) **GLOSS**

In this Ṛk the fight of Turvaśa is described. But it is not clear whether Turvaśa here received help from Indra or received punishment. Sāyaṇa has given both kinds of meaning. First, that when Turvaśa went to fight with Sudāsa, the friend of Indra, Indra punished Turvaśa and protected his friend; and second, that at the time when war arose between Turvaśa and his enemies, Indra helped his friend Turvaśa. Therefore the purport of this Ṛk is not clear. In the same way it is said in the Ṛk
पुरः सद्य इत्याधिये दिवोदासाय शंबरं । अध त्यं तुर्वशं यदुं ॥ (*puraḥ sadya ityādhiye divodāsāya śaṃbaraṃ | adha tyaṃ turvaśaṃ yaduṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-61-2) **GLOSS**
that both Yadu and Turvaśa suffered defeat from Indra. From this it is understood that Indra subdued Yadu and Turvaśa for the sake of his friend Divodāsa. But in many Ṛks, such as
प्रयत्नमुद्रमति शूर पर्षि पारया तुर्वशं यदुं स्वस्ति (*prayatnamudramati śūra parṣi pārayā turvaśaṃ yaduṃ svasti*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-174-9) **GLOSS**
उत त्या तुर्वशायदू अस्नातारा शचीपतिः । इंद्रो विद्वा अवारयत् । (*uta tyā turvaśāyadū asnātārā śacīpatiḥ | iṃdro vidvā avārayat |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-30-17) **GLOSS**
त्वमपो यदने तुर्वशायारमयः सुदुघाः पार इंद्र । (*tvamapo yadane turvaśāyāramayaḥ sudughāḥ pāra iṃdra |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-31-8) **GLOSS**
महत्ते वृष्णो अभिचक्ष्यं कृतं पश्येम तुर्वशं यदुं । (*mahatte vṛṣṇo abhicakṣyaṃ kṛtaṃ paśyema turvaśaṃ yaduṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-4-7) **GLOSS**
it is stated that both Yadu and Turvaśa received help directly from Indra.
notes: ಋಕ್ಸಂಖ್ಯೆ—೧೩ printed, while the bhāṣya and the Anuvāda say twelve (ದ್ವಾದಶರ್ಚಂ, ಹನ್ನೆರಡು)

en: "O Indra, in the battle all that is pervaded by such a deed is yours alone." What kind of deed? It is explained: the two asuras named Dhuni and Chumuri, whom you put to sleep, "slept" in the battle, that is, they lay dead. The second ह (*ha*) is a mere filler of the verse-quarter. Thereafter, O Indra, for you the royal seer named Dabhīti, pouring out Soma, cooking the oblations, and bearing or fetching the fuel, makes you shine with Somas and with the oblation-foods that are the chants; he kindles you. The meaning is: for him you slew Dhuni and Chumuri. So it is seen in त्वं नि दस्युं चुमुरिं धुनिं च (*tvaṃ ni dasyuṃ cumuriṃ dhuniṃ ca*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-19-4) ⟨NOTE:357⟩.
notes: ದೇವತಾ line gives ೧೧ both to Indra and to ವಿಶ್ವೇದೇವಾಃ; ಋಕ್ ೧೩ is not counted

en: - त्यत् (*tyat*)—whatever famous deed there is, that
- तव ह (*tava ha*)—is your deed indeed
- सस्तः (*sastaḥ*)—lay dead in the battle (O Indra)
- आर्कैः (*ārkaiḥ*)—with the foods in the form of oblations

O Indra, whatever deed there is in battle, all of it, the famous one, is your deed. The asuras Dhuni and Chumuri, whom you made languid, lay dead in the battle. O Indra, the royal seer Dabhīti, who presses Soma for you, cooks and offers the oblations and collects the fuel, makes you shine with the Somas and with the foods in the form of oblations (he worships you).

All this, Indra, has been your work in war : you have put to sleep, (in death), the slumbering Dhuni and Chumuri ; and thereupon Dabhiti, pouring the libition, preparing the oblation, and supplying the fuel, has glorified you with Soma offerings.
दभीतिं (*dabhītiṃ*)—Dabhīti is spoken of as a warrior in some places and as a seer in others.
इंद्रो धुनिं च चुमुरिं च दंभयञ्छद्धामनस्या शृणुते दभीतये । (*iṃdro dhuniṃ ca cumuriṃ ca daṃbhayañchaddhāmanasyā śṛṇute dabhītaye |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-113-9)
स्वप्नेनाभ्युप्या चुमुरिं धुनिं च जघंथ दस्युं प्र दभीतिमावः । (*svapnenābhyupyā cumuriṃ dhuniṃ ca jaghaṃtha dasyuṃ pra dabhītimāvaḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-15-9)

In these Ṛks Dabhīti is called a royal seer, and it is said that Indra conquered Chumuri and Dhuni for him. It is understood that he pressed and offered Soma juice to Indra and thereby obtained Indra's favour.
अस्वापयद्दभीतये सहस्रा त्रिंशतं हथैः । (*asvāpayaddabhītaye sahasrā triṃśataṃ hathaiḥ |*) दासानामिंद्रो मायया । (*dāsānāmiṃdro māyayā |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-30-21)
अरज्जा दस्यून्तमुनब्दभीतये सुप्राव्यो अभवः सासुक्थ्यः । (*arajjā dasyūntamunabdabhītaye suprāvyo abhavaḥ sāsukthyaḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-13-9)
In these Ṛks it is described how Indra, for Dabhīti, put thirty thousand Dāsas (dark people) to sleep, and bound all the Dasyus without a rope.

Of Purutama, that is, of one who desires much. Of the praiser Bharadvāja, these praiseworthy, laudable hymns (the thoughts, that is, the praises) invoke you, O hero Indra, who are to be invoked. How are you? Standing on the chariot, free from old age, ever newer. The particle उ (*u*) is a filler. Moreover, the excellent, praiseworthy wealth, which causes the glory of the world and consists of oblations, goes to you.
- पुरुतमस्य (*purutamasya*)—of him who has great desire
- कारोः (*kāroḥ*)—and is the praiser, of Bharadvāja
- रथेस्थां (*rathesthāṃ*)—you who are mounted on the chariot
- विभूतिः (*vibhūtiḥ*)—cause of the wealth of the world
- रयिः (*rayiḥ*)—wealth in the form of oblations
notes: ತತ್ರಸ್ಥಾನೇವಾನಿತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ unclear

en: O mighty Indra, these praiseworthy hymns of Bharadvāja, who has great desire and is the praiser, pray and call you, who are mounted on the chariot, free from old age, of new form and worthy of worship. Moreover, the excellent wealth in the form of oblations, which is the cause of the wealth of the world, comes and reaches you.

These earnest adorations of the much-desiring worshipper glorify you, hero, Indra, who are adorable : mounted on your car, undecaying, ever new, and to whom the wealth (of sacrifice), the most excellent opulence proceeds.

Indra, who is विदानः (*vidānaḥ*), that is, knows all or is known by all, who is to be borne by songs, who is grown great by sacrifices, that very Indra I praise. Of him who is of much wisdom or of much deception, whose greatness, by his own majesty, exceeds the heavenly world and the earth: the accusative दिवं (*divaṃ*) stands in the sense of the ablative. The connection is: him I praise.
- यज्ञवृद्धं (*yajñavṛddhaṃ*)—and who grows great by sacrifices
- अति रिरिचे (*ati ririce*)—has exceeded; such an Indra (I praise)

I praise that very Indra, who knows everything, is praised by hymns and grows great by sacrifices. I praise that Indra, of exceeding knowledge, whose greatness has exceeded the heavenly world and the earthly world by his own majesty.

I glorify that Indra who is the propitiated by praises, exalted by sacrifices, who knows all things ; the magnitude of whom, the possessor of various wisdom, exceeds in vastness (that of) heaven and earth.

That same Indra made the darkness, which is without knowledge (the destroyer of knowledge), spread by वृत्तेण (*vṛtteṇa*) ⟨NOTE:361⟩, full of light in the sky by the sun, the god set in the heavens. The latter half-verse is made direct address. O mighty Indra, possessor of स्वधा (*svadhā*), mortals wishing to worship your eternal abode called heaven, कदा (*kadā*), that is, at any time, which means always, do not harm any living creature ⟨NOTE:362⟩.
notes: ಪ್ರಶ್ನಾಸಃ printed, Pada has ಪ್ರತ್ನಾಸಃ; ಅಂಗಿರಃ ಪ್ರಕೃತಿಗಳು printed
ನೂಶನಾಸಃ printed, Pada has ನೂತನಾಸಃ

en: - वयुनवत् (*vayunavat*)—as made luminous (fit to be known)
- धाम (*dhāma*)—abode (the gods who are in heaven)
- न मिनंति (*na minaṃti*)—do not harm any living being

The renowned Indra made the darkness, which was devoid of light and spread out by Vṛtra, luminous by the sun. O mighty Indra, men, wishing to worship the gods in heaven, your deathless abode, never harm any living being.

He who made the indistinct, wide-spreading darkness distinct wtth the sun : whenever, possessor of strength, mortals are seeking to adore the dwelling of you who are immortal, they harm not (any living being).

स इत् अवयुनं ततन्वत् तमः सूर्येण वयुनवत् चकार (*sa it avayunaṃ tatanvat tamaḥ sūryeṇa vayunavat cakāra*)—Indra made the darkness, which was devoid of light and covered by Vṛtra, that is, the gloom, luminous through the sun. Concerning the word वयुनवत् (*vayunavat*) here, Yāska says:

वयुनं वेतेः कांतिर्वा प्रज्ञा वा । (*vayunaṃ veteḥ kāṃtirvā prajñā vā |*) स इत्तमोऽवयुनं ततन्नत्सूर्येण वयुनवच्चकार । (*sa ittamo 'vayunaṃ tatannatsūryeṇa vayunavaccakāra |*) तमोऽप्रज्ञानं ततन्नत् सूतं सूर्येण प्रज्ञानवच्चकार ॥ (*tamo 'prajñānaṃ tatannat sūtaṃ sūryeṇa prajñānavaccakāra ‖*) (Ni. 5-15)

Having given this explanation, he cites this very Ṛk as the example. That is, the word वयुन (*vayuna*), formed from the root वि (*vi*), gives the meaning splendour (light) or intelligence. In the present Ṛk, because the sun was enveloped in darkness, gloom covered every place. Then, because there was no light, it was not possible to see any object or to know it by seeing. In this state Indra drove away the darkness that had covered every place by the light of the sun, made all things visible by that light, and enabled people to know them by intelligence: this is the chief meaning.

Those well-known deeds mentioned above, the slaying of Vṛtra and the rest, which Indra did: where is that Indra now? To which person, that is, to which region, does he go? In which peoples does he abide? Because of the greatness of Indra's power this cannot be determined. Now a direct praise: O Indra, what sort of sacrifice is pleasing to your mind? What sort of अर्क (*arka*), that is, mantra, is able to win you? And the invoker, that is, the one who is able to call you to choose you, what sort of man is he?
- कुह स्वित् (*kuha svit*)—in what region is he now?
- आ चरति (*ā carati*)—does he move about
- कासु विक्षु (*kāsu vikṣu*)—with what peoples does he have dealings
- होता सः (*hotā saḥ*)—he who praises you (the hotṛ)

Where is now that Indra who did the famous deeds? In what region does he move about? With what peoples does he have dealings? O Indra, what kind of sacrifice is pleasing to your heart? What mantra is able to choose and obtain you? What sort of man is the hotṛ who praises you?

What is he, the Indra who has done these deeds ? what region does he frequent ? among what people (does he abide) ? what worship, Indra, gives satisfaction to your mind ? what praise is able to gratify you ? which of your invokers (is most acceptable to you) ?

The पुराजाः (*purājāḥ*) are those born in an earlier time; the प्रत्नासः (*pratnāsaḥ*) are the ancient ones, Aṅgiras and the rest. The word इदा हि (*idā hi*) means "as now"; the word हि (*hi*) is used in the sense of comparison. Attaining the rites, O Indra, doer of many deeds, they were your friends, that is, your praisers. Those who were born in the middle time and those who are recent, of the present day, all of these have been praisers. For that reason, hear also my praise, mine who am of the latest time, O Indra invoked by many; take note of it.
- पुरुकृत् (*purukṛt*)—O Indra, who performs many rites
- प्रश्नासः (*praśnāsaḥ*)—ancient, the Aṅgirases and the rest ⟨NOTE:363⟩
- इदा हि (*idā hi*)—just as in this time
- मध्यमासः (*madhyamāsaḥ*)—were born in the middle time
- नूशनासः (*nūśanāsaḥ*)—those who are born in the present time ⟨NOTE:364⟩ (all of them are your friends); therefore
- अवमस्य (*avamasya*)—this praise of me, the latest
- पुरुहूत (*puruhūta*)—O Indra, who are called by many
notes: ವಾಗ್ನಿರ್ನಿಬಬಂಧುಃ printed
ಶಿಷ್ಠ in the bhāṣya and Pada, ತಿಷ್ಠ in the Saṃhitā

en: O Indra, who performs many rites, the Aṅgirases and the rest, who were born in earlier times and were elders, performed rites as they are done in this time and were friends to you. All those who were born in the middle time are your friends. Therefore know this praise of mine, the latest.

Doer of many deeds, these elders, born former times, engaged in sacred rites, have been, as they are now, your friends ; so have those of mediaeval and those of recent (date) : therefore, invoked of many, take notice of your (present) humble (adorer).

O hero, brave one, O Indra who are to be borne by the brahmans, that is, by mantras, the later men, the recent human beings, पृच्छंतः (*pṛcchaṃtaḥ*), that is, worshipping you who have the qualities spoken of. The root पृच्छति (*pṛcchati*) has the sense of worshipping.

पराणि (*parāṇi*) means excellent; प्रत्ना (*pratnā*), ancient; श्रुत्या (*śrutyā*), to be heard: they have bound your deeds, of this kind, by words in the form of praises ⟨NOTE:365⟩. In the same way we too worship you, the mighty, the abundant; we praise you. The connection is: we praise you with those very deeds that we know.
notes: ಯತ್ printed; not in the Saṃhitā

en: - अनु येमुः (*anu yemuḥ*)—have praised (in the same way)
- तात् (*tāt*)—with the help of those deeds we praise you

O Indra, brave and borne by praise, humble men, worshipping you, have praised your excellent, ancient and famous deeds. In the same way we too worship you, who are possessed of abundant qualities. With those deeds that we know, we worship you.

Humble (worshippers), adoring him, commemorate, Indra, your excellent. ancient, and glorious (deeds): so, hero, who are attracted by prayer. we praise you who are mighty, for those great actions with which we are acquainted.

The strength of the Rākṣasas, in the form of armies, has taken its stand facing you, O Indra. In the same way, you too, facing that great strength which has arisen, stand firm and well ⟨NOTE:366⟩. Having stood, O bold Indra, assailant of enemies, drive away that strength with your thunderbolt; that is, split it. With what kind of thunderbolt? With the ancient one, the fit one to be employed, the constant helper and friend.
notes: ಏಷ್ವಾ printed; Saṃhitā ಏಷ್ಟೌ, Pada ಆಇಷ್ಟ್

en: - पाजः (*pājaḥ*)—the strength in the form of armies
- तत् अभि (*tat abhi*)—facing that very strength

O Indra, the strength of the Rākṣasas, in the form of armies, stands surrounding you. Facing that same strength, which has appeared before you and has great power, stand firm. O Indra, destroyer of enemies, destroy that strength with your thunderbolt, which is ancient, to be employed against enemies, and friendly.

The strength of the Rakshasas is concentrated against you : bear up well against that mighty manifested (effort) : scatter them, valiant (Indra), with your old associate, your friend, the thunderbolt.

O supporter of the praisers, O hero Indra, you, that famous one, hear quickly my praise, mine who am of the present day and wish to make a hymn of praise. For the reason that, O Indra, when you are well invoked at the sacrifice or in desire, you have for a long time, in the earlier age, been the kinsman of our forefathers, the Aṅgirases, for that reason listen to my praise: this is the connection.
- एष्वा (*eṣvā*)—at the time of the sacrifice ⟨NOTE:368⟩
- पित्तूणां (*pittūṇāṃ*)—to the Aṅgirases, our forefathers and grandfathers
- बभूथ (*babhūtha*)—you have been (a helper) (by that favour)
- ब्रह्म ण्यतः (*brahma ṇyataḥ*)—and praising you, of me, my praise
notes: ಮಿತ್ರಮಹರಭಿಮಾನಿನಂ ಚ repeated twice in the bhāṣya
ಪದಪಾಠ ends with ॥೧೦॥, the Saṃhitā has ॥ ೧೧ ॥

en: O supporter of the praisers, O brave Indra, by the gracious thought with which you, well entreated at the time of the sacrifice, have always been in the past a kinsman and helper to our forefathers and grandfathers, the Aṅgirases, by that same favour hear quickly the praise of me, who was born in this time and praise you, you the renowned.

Supportor of (your) worshipers, hero, Indra, listen (to the praises) of your present adorer, for you have always attended to invocations at sacrifices in ancient times, as the kinsman of our forefathers.

In this Ṛk the Viśvedevas are praised. O Bharadvāja, today, Varuṇa, the presiding deity of the night, and Mitra, the presiding deity of the day ⟨NOTE:369⟩, and the famous Indra, and the Maruts, the troops of Maruts, make face us for our satisfaction and protection. Moreover, Pūṣan, who bears that name, and Viṣṇu, the all-pervading deity, and Puraṃdhi, he of many thoughts and many deeds, Agni, and Savitṛ, the impeller of all, the deity, the Oṣadhīs, that is, the deities presiding over the herbs, and the mountains, the rocks: these gods, for our satisfaction and protection, make face us by praise.
notes: ಅನೇಕ ಕಾವ್ಯಕರ್ತನೂ in the Bhāvārtha; ಅನೇಕ ಕಾರ್ಯಕರ್ತನೂ in the Pratipadārtha

en: - ओषधीः (*oṣadhīḥ*)—the presiding deities of the herbs
- पर्वतांश्च (*parvatāṃśca*)—and the presiding deities of the mountains
- प्र कृष्ण (*pra kṛṣṇa*)—make them face us

O Bharadvāja, make Varuṇa, Mitra, Indra, the host of Maruts, the god Pūṣan, Viṣṇu, Agni, the performer of many rites, the god Savitṛ, the presiding deities of the herbs and the presiding deities of the mountains face us, for our satisfaction and for our protection.
Propitiate to-day, for our protection and preservation, Varuna, Mitra, Indra, and the Maruts, Pushan, Vishnu, Agni of many rites, Savitri, the herbs, the mountains.

In this Ṛk the seer Bharadvāja, praising the Viśvedevas beginning with Varuṇa, addresses himself. That is, although he himself is the seer of this sūkta, he refers to himself by the prathama-puruṣa (third person), in the manner of addressing others.

O Puruśāka, of much power, O Prayajyu, Indra, to be worshipped in an excellent manner, these praisers praise you with अर्कैः (*arkaiḥ*), that is, with hymns of praise worthy to be sung; they praise you. Likewise, O deathless Indra, you who are praised, hear the invocation, that is, the hymn, of me who praise you. Moreover, there is no other god like you, different from you.
- हुवानः (*huvānaḥ*)—you who are praised by us
- आ हुवतः (*ā huvataḥ*)—of me who praise you
- न अस्ति (*na asti*)—there is none at all

O Indra, of many kinds of power and worthy of excellent worship, these praisers worship you with hymns of praise. O deathless Indra, you who are praised by us, hear the hymn of me who praise you. There is no other god like you but you.

Indra, of great power, and to be devoutly worshipped, these your adorers glorify you with hymns : do you, who are invoked, hear the invocation of (him) invoking you, for there is no other divinity than you, immortal (Indra), such as you are.

notes: abbreviation ಋಗ್ವೇ. printed

en: This Ṛk too is Vaiśvadevī, as has been said. O son of strength, Indra, you, the all-knowing, come quickly to my words, that is, my hymns of praise, together with all the adorable gods. Indra, so described, is prayed to, because the sūkta is addressed to Indra. The gods whose tongue is Agni, for Agni is in the place of the tongue for them, who touch the rite, the sacrifice, and are present at it, and the gods who, for the casting down of enemies, made Manu, the royal seer, उपरं (*uparaṃ*), that is, superior to the Dasyus: come with them. Thus it is connected with what has gone before.
- सहसः सूनो (*sahasaḥ sūno*)—O Indra, son of strength
- अग्नि जिह्वाः (*agni jihvāḥ*)—have the flame of Agni as tongue
- ऋतसापः (*ṛtasāpaḥ*)—and take a share in the sacrifice
- विश्वेभिः (*viśvebhiḥ*)—all the gods, together with them
- आ याहि (*ā yāhi*)—be gracious and come

O Indra, son of strength, you, the all-knowing, be gracious and come towards my hymns of praise, together with all the gods who have fire for their tongue and take a share in the sacrifice, and who, for the destruction of enemies, made Manu superior to the enemies.

Come quickly, Son of strength, you who know (all things), upon my prayer; together with all the adorable (divinities): they who, with the tongue of Agni, are partakers of the sacrifice, who rendered Manu (victorious) over his adversaries.

O Indra, maker of paths, all-knowing, you, be our leader who goes before, in the paths that are easy to travel and also in those that are hard to travel. Whatever horses of yours are free from fatigue, great, the best bearers, with those horses, O Indra, bring us food.

O Indra, maker of paths and all-knowing, you be our guide in all kinds of paths, whether easy to travel or hard to travel. With the horses that are free from fatigue, of great power and fit for bearing, bring us food.

Costructor of paths, who are cognizant (of all things), be our preceder, whether in easy or difficult (ways) : bring to us food, Indra, with those your (steeds), who are unwearied, large, and bearers of great burdens.

Indra, who among the people is the one alone to be invoked in times of distress: with these praises, which take the form of words of eulogy, the seer praises that Indra. This Indra approaches his praisers; or else he rules over the worlds. What kind is he? He is the showerer of desires, powerful, true, that is, never contradicting himself; सत्वा (*satvā*) means the one who brings down enemies, or the giver of desires, the form being derived from सदेर्वा सनोतेर्वेदं रूपं (*sadervā sanotervedaṃ rūpaṃ*). He is of much wisdom and overpowering. The construction is: I praise that Indra.

That Indra who is the showerer of desires, powerful, of the nature of truth, giver of desired objects, possessing manifold wisdom and power to defeat enemies, who is unequalled and worthy of worship among all men, and who turns toward his praisers: that same Indra I worship with these praises.

I glorify with these praises, Indra, who alone is to be invoked by man : who comes (to his worshippers) the showerer (of benefits), the vigorous, the observer of truth, the subduer of foes, the possessor of manifold know- ledge, the mighty.

The ancient ones, the nine-month sacrificers, seven in number, the wise, making food in the form of an offering for Indra, or making Indra strong and vigorous (the causative meaning being "he makes that"), such are our fathers, the Aṅgirases; that same Indra they praised with hymns, the verb "praised" being understood. What kind is he? One who injures the enemies who come against him; the verb of motion is the sense of the root. He is the crosser, the one stationed on the mountains, whose commands are not to be transgressed and whose form is such, and the most powerful.
- नः पितरः (*naḥ pitaraḥ*)—our fathers, the Aṅgirases
- नक्षद्दाभं (*nakṣaddābhaṃ*)—the one who checks enemies rushing upon him

The ancient Aṅgirases, called Navagvas, seven in number, wise, desirous of food, our fathers, praised with hymns that same Indra, who checks enemies rushing upon him, who is swift-going, stationed on the mountain, whose command is not transgressed, and who is endowed with power.

To him the seven sages, our ancient, progenitors, performing the nine days' rite, were offerers of (sacrificil) food, celebrating with hymns the very strong (Indra) the humiliator of foes, the traveser of the heavens, the dweller in the clouds, whose commands are not be disobeyed.
On the word नक्षद्दाभं (*nakṣaddābhaṃ*) Yāska has given the Nirukta explanation:

नक्षद्दा भमश्नुवानदाभमभ्यशनेन दभ्नोतीति । नक्षद्दाभं ततुरिं पर्वतेष्ठामित्यपि निगमो भवति ॥ (*nakṣaddā bhamaśnuvānadābhamabhyaśanena dabhnotīti | nakṣaddābhaṃ taturiṃ parvateṣṭhāmityapi nigamo bhavati ‖*) (2. 6-3)

That is: योऽभ्यशनेन दभ्योति हिनस्ति स नक्षद्दाभ इत्युच्यते (*yo 'bhyaśanena dabhyoti hinasti sa nakṣaddābha ityucyate*). Nakṣaddābha means: he who injures, that is, strikes, a man who is making ready to come near is called Nakṣaddābha. Or, he who rushes swiftly at an enemy coming near him or against him and strikes him with a weapon is called Nakṣaddābha. And this name applies also to one who dwells on a mountain. In this matter the present Ṛk itself is given as the example, "Nakṣaddābhaṃ taturiṃ parvateṣṇāṃ".

Of this wealth of him who has many sons and grandsons, who has attendants, who has much food or much fame: the genitive stands in the sense of the accusative. We ask that Indra for it. The wealth that is unbroken, ageless and joyful: O Indra, lord of the bay horses, with your own horses, bring that wealth to us, to gladden us.
- पुरुवीरस्य (*puruvīrasya*)—accompanied by many heroic sons and the like
- पुरुक्षोः (*purukṣoḥ*)—possessed of wealth in cattle and the like
- हरिवः (*harivaḥ*)—O Indra, possessed of horses named Hari

For this wealth, which is accompanied by many heroic sons and the like, full of attendants, and possessed of wealth in cattle and the like, we beg that same Indra. O Indra, lord of the horses named Hari, bring for our satisfaction that wealth which is lasting without break, free from decay and endowed with happiness.

We solicit that Indra for wealth, comprehending numerous descend- ants, followers, and much cattle, and which is undisturbed, imperishable, and the source of felicity : such riches, lord of steeds, bestow upon us to make us happy.
On the word अस्कृधोयुः (*askṛdhoyuḥ*) Yāska, giving the explanation, says:

अस्कृधोयुरकृध्वायुः । कृध्विति ह्रस्वनाम निकृत्तं भवति । यो अस्कृधोयुरजरः स्वर्वान् इत्यपि निगमो भवति ॥ (*askṛdhoyurakṛdhvāyuḥ | kṛdhviti hrasvanāma nikṛttaṃ bhavati | yo askṛdhoyurajaraḥ svarvān ityapi nigamo bhavati ‖*) (Ni. 6-3)

Askṛdhoyuḥ means one who has a long life. The word कृधु (*kṛdhu*) means cut off, made short. Akṛdhu means not short, long; āyuḥ is life; one having life. Therefore the word askṛdhoyuḥ or akṛdhvāyuḥ means one who is not short, that is, one who has a long life, one who lives for a long time. In this matter the Nirukta-writers have given the present Ṛk itself as the example.

O Indra, if in former times your praisers obtained happiness, tell us of that happiness, each in turn. O unassailable one, O destroyer of enemies, O much-invoked one, O possessor of much wealth, Indra, slayer of the asuras: what portion of yours is ordained in the sacrifices? What food, in the form of the offering, is ordained?

The sense is: if any of the ancient ones obtained happiness from you even in former times, then I too shall obtain that happiness; reflecting thus, the delay in my obtaining happiness would not be endurable to me.
- पुरुषसो (*puruṣaso*)—one possessed of exceedingly great wealth, O Indra
- कः भागः (*kaḥ bhāgaḥ*)—which portion of the sacrifice is appointed?
- वयः किं (*vayaḥ kiṃ*)—what kind of oblation is appointed?

O Indra, if your praisers in former times obtained any happiness, supply that same happiness to us also. O Indra, of unobstructed power, who make enemies suffer, who are called by many, who possess exceedingly great wealth, and who destroy the asuras: which portion of the sacrifice is appointed for you? What kind of oblation is appointed?

If Indra, your worshippers have formerly obtained felicity, confer that also upon us : irresistible Indra, subduer of foes, invoked of many abounding in wealth, what is the portion, what the offering (due) to you who are the slayer of the Asuras ?

Addressed by the preceding Ṛk, Indra gave the seer his desires; then the seer, his desires fulfilled, says: the seer worships (the verb of asking has the sense of worship) that Indra, who holds the thunderbolt in his hand and stands on his chariot. The word for the quivering is a rite such as a sacrifice; the praise that bends the qualities (towards the deity) belongs to the sacrificer who has such a rite. What kind of Indra does he worship? One who takes up many, who does many deeds and who gives vigour. That sacrificer goes to happiness, and goes also against the enemy who wearies others.
- वज्रहस्त (*vajrahasta*)—holding the thunderbolt weapon in his hand

The sacrificer by whom rites such as sacrifice, and praise of Indra's qualities, are carried out, worshipping that Indra who holds the thunderbolt weapon in his hand, who is seated in the chariot, who accepts many, who is a doer of many deeds ⟨NOTE:371⟩ and who gives strength, obtains happiness. And he courageously faces the enemy and advances.
notes: ಸುತುಕಾ—ಸುಲಭವಾಗಿ ಕೆಳಗೆಬಿಳುವಂತೆ in the Kannada gloss; Sāyaṇa: ಶೋಭನಹಿಂಸೋಪೇತಾನಿ

en: He whose ceremonial and eulogistic hymn is commemorating Indra, the holder of the thunderbolt, seated in his car, the accepter of many, the
doer of many great deeds, the bestower of strength, proceeds promptly to acquire happines, and encounters (with confidence) the malevolent.

O Indra, of strength that is your own, with your own weapon, the thunderbolt, which is swift as the mind and many-edged, as is seen in वज्रेण शतपर्वणा (*vajreṇa śataparvaṇā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-80-6 ⟨NOTE:372⟩) **GLOSS**, you have shattered that famous Vṛtra who was growing by this cunning. Likewise, O Indra of fine splendour, O great Indra, you have broken with the daring thunderbolt the cities that are firm, even though they are indestructible and unshaken.
notes: ಐ. ಅ. ೫-೨-೨ printed in the bhāṣya; ಐ. ಆ. ೫-೨-೨ in the Kannada Anuvāda

en: - स्वतवः (*svatavaḥ*)—O Indra, of strength that is naturally his own
- मनोजुवा (*manojuvā*)—swift as the speed of the mind
- पर्वतेन (*parvatena*)—with the thunderbolt weapon, which has edges
- दृढा चित् (*dṛḍhā cit*)—even though firm (enemy cities)
- दृढता (*dṛḍhatā*)—with the crushing thunderbolt (you have destroyed)

O Indra, of naturally own strength, with your thunderbolt, swift as the mind and with sharp edges, you have destroyed Vṛtra, who grew by deceitful acts. However firm the enemy cities were, which do not fall and are not loose, you have destroyed those enemy cities with your thunderbolt, which is of your own nature.

Self-invigorated Indra, you have crushed by your knotted (thunder- bolt), quick as thought, that Vritra, growing in strength by this cunning : very radiant and mighty (Indra), you have demolished by (your) irresistible (shaft) the unyielding, compact, and strong (cities of the Asuras).

With a newer praise, O Indra, I have set out to spread abroad on every side your fame, as the ancient seers did, you who are most mighty and ancient. That Indra, who is immeasurable and a fine bearer, may carry us over all that is hard to cross, all difficulties.
- परितंसयध्यै (*paritaṃsayadhyai*)—I have begun to spread out and praise
- अति वक्षत् (*ati vakṣat*)—may he supply (may he protect us from troubles also)

O Indra, as the ancient seers praised you, who are most mighty, ancient and famous, so I too have begun to spread out and praise you with a new praise. May that same Indra, who is without limit and a bearer of excellent things, supply us with all hard victories. May he carry us across troubles also.

(I have undertaken) to spread around with a new hyma, as it was done of old, (the glory of) you, the ancient and most mighty (Indra): may that Indra, who is illimitable, and is a sure conveyance, bear us over all difficulties.

O Indra, set ablaze all the places that belong to the earth, to heaven and to the atmosphere, for the harmful person, the injurer of good people, a Rākṣasa and the like; the dative stands in the sense of the genitive. Set them blazing on every side. O Indra, showerer of desires,

burn with your own radiance those Rākṣasas and the like who exist everywhere. Moreover, for the hater of the Brāhmaṇas, a Rākṣasa and the like, that is, in order to burn the hater of the Brahman, make the earth and the atmosphere blaze; the word for waters is a name of the atmosphere.
- अंतरिक्षा (*aṃtarikṣā*)—and belonging to the atmosphere, all these places
- आ दीपयः (*ā dīpayaḥ*)—make them blaze up
- ब्रह्मद्विषे (*brahmadviṣe*)—also for the one fallen from rites who hates Brāhmaṇa rites

O Indra, make all the places that belong to the earth, to the heavenly world and to the atmosphere blaze up for the Rākṣasas and the like who do harm. O Indra, showerer of desires, burn with your radiance those Rākṣasas and the like who pervade everywhere. For the one fallen from rites, who hates Vedic rites, make the earth and the atmosphere blaze as well.

Make hot the regions of earth, of heaven, of mid air, for the oppressive race (of the Rakshasas) : showerer (of benefits). consume them everywhere with your radiance, make the heaven and the firmament (too) hot for the impious,

O Indra of flaming aspect, you are the king and lord of the people who are in heaven; you are king of the moving world and of the earthly. Place the thunderbolt in your right hand, and with that placed thunderbolt you drive off all the Asura deceits. O Indra, whom none can age, you do so.
- दिव्यस्य (*divyasya*)—who are in the heavenly world
- पार्थिवस्य (*pārthivasya*)—people of the earthly world also (you are king)
- दक्षिणे हस्ते (*dakṣiṇe haste*)—in your right hand
- अजुर्य (*ajurya*)—of strength that cannot be diminished

O Indra of radiant form, you are king of the gods and others who are in the heavenly world and of the people of the moving earthly world. O Indra, of strength that cannot be diminished, hold the thunderbolt weapon in your right hand and destroy all the Asura deceits.

Bright-flaming Indra, you are the king of the people of heaven, and of the moving races of earth : grasp in your right hand the thunderbolt, wherewith, Indra, who are beyond all praise, you baffle all the devices (of the Asuras).

O Indra, for the overcoming of enemies bring to us great, unharmed and concentrated prosperity, a store of well-being. O wielder of the thunderbolt, by that prosperity you have made the dāsas, those who are without rites and born as men, ārya, that is, furnished with rites; the word for "relating to men" is the word derived from nahuṣa, which is a name for man. By it you have made the enemies, the Vṛtras, furnished with excellent injury. ⟨NOTE:373⟩
notes: ಉಪಕ್ಷಪಯಿತ್ಯನ್ reading doubtful

en: - सुतुका (*sutukā*)—you have made them fall down easily; such
- संयतं (*saṃyataṃ*)—in the form of a store

O Indra, bring to us, for the conquest of enemies, that great, unharmed, store-like and auspicious wealth by which you made people without rites into people furnished with rites, and made the enemies who are related to men fall down easily.

Bring to us, Indra, concentrated, vast, and unassailable prosperity beyond the reach of enemies, and by which, wielder of the thunderbolt, you have rendered human enemies, whether Dasas or Aryas, easy to be overcome.

O much-invoked one, O creator, O Indra who are to be worshipped in an excellent manner: you come to us with your horses, which are chosen by all and to be shared by all. The horses that neither the asura nor the god holds back, with these come quickly, turning toward me.
- प्रयज्यो (*prayajyo*)—one worthy of excellent worship, O Indra
- आ गहि (*ā gahi*)—be pleased to come
- आ याहि (*ā yāhi*)—be pleased to come

O Indra, called by many, creator and worthy of excellent worship, be pleased to come to us with your horses, which are honoured by all. Come, turned toward me, with such horses as neither god nor asura can hold back.
Invoked of many, creator, object of sacrifice, come to us with your all-admired steeds, whom neither Asura nor deity arrests : come with them quickly to our presence.

When Soma has been pressed, when a great hymn is being uttered and the uktha, the śastra, is being recited, O Indra, you, being united, yoking your two bay horses, O Maghavan, holding in your hands your own weapon, the thunderbolt, come with the two bay horses yoked to the chariot. The construction is that all this happens when Soma has been pressed.
- स्तोमे (*stome*)—as soon as the hymn is recited
- शस्यमाने (*śasyamāne*)—as soon as it is recited
- निमिश्लः (*nimiślaḥ*)—having yoked your horses to the chariot
- यद्वा यासि (*yadvā yāsi*)—be pleased to come

O wealthy Indra, as soon as the soma juice is pressed, the great hymn is recited and the śastra mantra is recited, you yoke your horses to the chariot, bear the thunderbolt weapon in your hands, and be pleased to come with the horses joined with the chariot.

When the Soma Juice, Indra, is being effused, the sacred hymn chanted, the prayer recited, be prepared (to harness your horses), or, Maghavan, with your horses ready harnessed, come (hither), bearing the thunderbolt in your hand.
O Indra, in heaven, when the battle that slays Vṛtra, which is to be shared by heroes and warriors, is to be reached, you protect the sacrificer who presses Soma; or whatever else you do,

the word for "or" is for combining. For the man who is able in sacrifices and the like and is afraid of enemies, you, O Indra, being without fear, subdued the Dasyus, the enemies who strive in battle and wear down ⟨NOTE:375⟩; or whatever you bring under control: all that is connected with the former, as happening when Soma is pressed. So it has been said: यद्बाह्वोर्धारयन्वज्रं हरिभ्यां यासि वृत्रहन् । यच्च रक्षसि संग्रामे नृन् सोममभिषुण्वतः ॥ यच्च कर्म सुदक्षस्य यजमानस्यापारयः । वशीकरोषि तांस्तस्मै बिभ्यते भीतिवर्जितः ॥ तत्सोमेऽभिषुते स्तोत्रशस्त्रयोश्च प्रवृत्तयोः । इति द्वचोऽयमेकार्थः सुत इत्त्वमिति द्वयमिति ॥ (*yadbāhvordhārayanvajraṃ haribhyāṃ yāsi vṛtrahan | yacca rakṣasi saṃgrāme nṛn somamabhiṣuṇvataḥ ‖ yacca karma sudakṣasya yajamānasyāpārayaḥ | vaśīkaroṣi tāṃstasmai bibhyate bhītivarjitaḥ ‖ tatsome 'bhiṣute stotraśastrayośca pravṛttayoḥ | iti dvaco 'yamekārthaḥ suta ittvamiti dvayamiti ‖*) **GLOSS**
notes: ಮಮ in Sāyaṇa's gloss of ವರ್ಧನಾನಿ; ವಿವಿಷ್ಟಃ in the bhāṣya, ವಿವಿಸ್ಮಃ in the Kannada gloss

en: - वृत्रहत्ये (*vṛtrahatye*)—in the battle that destroys enemies
- सुष्टिं (*suṣṭiṃ*)—the sacrificer who presses and offers Soma
- बिभ्युषः (*bibhyuṣaḥ*)—and afraid of enemies, for the sacrificer
- यद्वा (*yadvā*)—whatever there is (all of it was accomplished as soon as the soma was pressed)

O Indra, whatever there is, that you protect the sacrificer who presses and offers Soma, though engaged in heaven in the battle to be fought with heroes and destructive of enemies, and whatever there is, that fearless you made the harmful enemies fall down for the sacrificer who is able to perform sacrifice and afraid of enemies: all this was accomplished as soon as the soma was pressed.

Or as, although engaged in heaven in the horo-animating conflict with foes, you protect the offerer of the libation, and humble, undaunted Indra, the Dasyus, the disturbers of the pious and terrified worshipper, (so come when the Soma is effused).

Sāyaṇa says: let Indra be a drinker of the Soma that has been pressed (सुतं (*sutaṃ*)); let him be given to drinking. What kind of Indra? By the way of protection (ऊती (*ūtī*)) he leads the praiser (जरितारं (*jaritāraṃ*)) forward, for प्रणेनीः (*praṇenīḥ*) means "he who leads on in an excellent manner"; he is fierce (उग्रः (*ugraḥ*)). For the capable sacrificer (वीराय (*vīrāya*)), skilled in sacrifices and the like, who presses Soma (सुष्टये (*suṣṭaye*)), he is the maker of a place (लोकं (*lokaṃ*)), that is, the giver of it. The word उ (*u*) serves to fill out the foot. To the praiser (कीरये चित् (*kīraye cit*)), who offers praise (स्तुवते (*stuvate*)), he is the giver of wealth (वसु (*vasu*)); चित् (*cit*) is in the sense of "and", and कीरि (*kīri*) is a name for a praiser.
- प्रणेनीः (*praṇenīḥ*)—he who leads to a well-protected place
- सुष्टये (*suṣṭaye*)—to the sacrificer who presses and offers Soma
- कीरये चित् (*kīraye cit*)—even to the praiser
- सुतं सोमं (*sutaṃ somaṃ*)—the Soma pressed and made ready

May Indra, who with his protections leads the praiser to a well-protected place, who makes an excellent place for the sacrificer who, being capable in sacrificial work, presses and offers Soma, who gives wealth to the praiser who is a singer of praise,
and who is fearsome, drink here the Soma that has been pressed and made ready.

May Indra be the drinker of the effused Soma, he who is the fierce conductor of the worshipper to security: may he be the donor of the world to the presenter of the libation, the giver of wealth to the man who adores him.

Sāyaṇa says: let Indra, with his two bay horses (हरिभ्यां (*haribhyāṃ*)), be a goer (गंता (*gaṃtā*)) to the three savanas (सवना (*savanā*)), which he calls इयंति (*iyaṃti*) and glosses as हृदयस्थानि (*hṛdayasthāni*). ⟨NOTE:376⟩ What kind of Indra? He is the bearer (बभ्रिः (*babhriḥ*)), the holder, of the thunderbolt (वज्रं (*vajraṃ*)), his own weapon; the drinker (पपिः (*papiḥ*)) of the pressed Soma; the giver (ददिः (*dadiḥ*)) of cows (गाः (*gāḥ*)). He is the maker, that is, the giver, to the sacrificer of a son (वीरं (*vīraṃ*)) who is beneficial to men (नर्यं (*naryaṃ*)) and endowed with many sons (सर्ववीरं (*sarvavīraṃ*)). He is the hearer (श्रोता (*śrotā*)) of the invocation (हवं (*havaṃ*)), the praise, belonging to the praiser (गृणतः (*gṛṇataḥ*)) who sings praises, and he is स्तोमवाहाः (*stomavāhāḥ*), one to be borne by stomas, that is, by praises.
notes: no verse number printed after ಲೋಕಂ ॥; number 7 follows the sequence

en: - नर्यं (*naryaṃ*)—the one who is beneficial to men
- स्तोमवाहाः (*stomavāhāḥ*)—who is borne by praises; Indra
- गंता (*gaṃtā*)—let him be the one who comes

May Indra, who bears the thunderbolt, drinks the Soma juice, gives cows, and who bestows on the sacrificer a heroic son who is beneficial to men and all-capable, who hears the praise of the praiser and is borne by praises, come with his horses to the three attractive savanas.

May Indra, with his steeds, come to as many (daily) rites (as may be celebrated), bearing the thunderbolt, drinking the Soma, bestowing cattle, granting manly and multiplied posterity, hearing the invocation of his adorer, and being the accepter of (our) praises.

Sāyaṇa says: the ancient (प्रदिवः (*pradivaḥ*)) Indra who does for us (नः (*naḥ*)) the work of nourishment and the like (अपः (*apaḥ*); कः (*kaḥ*) means "does", करोति (*karoti*)) and who desires (ववान (*vavāna*)) the praises and the like: for that Indra we pervade (विविष्मः (*viviṣmaḥ*)), that is, we perform that. When the Soma has been pressed (सुते (*sute*)) we praise (स्तुमसि (*stumasi*)), that is, we make praises for Indra. Reciting (शंसत् (*śaṃsat*)) means those who recite the śastras that rise out of the uktha. The word ब्रह्म (*brahma*) is the food that has the nature of the oblation; it is meant for Indra, and the sense is that we make it so that it may be a cause of his increase (वर्धनं (*vardhanaṃ*)) and may come to be (असत् (*asat*)).
- अपः (*apaḥ*)—the works of nourishment and the like
- अस्मै इंद्राय (*asmai iṃdrāya*)—addressed to that same Indra
- तद्विविष्मः (*tadviviṣmaḥ*)—I worship so as to fill him with satisfaction
- उक्था (*ukthā*)—praises that have the nature of the uktha
- ब्रह्म (*brahma*)—the food that has the form of the oblation
- वर्धनं यथा (*vardhanaṃ yathā*)—in such a way that his power increases

We praise that same Indra, the ancient one who does for our good the works of nourishment and the like and who desires our praises. And before that we prepare the Soma juice. We recite the praises that have the form of the uktha. Addressing Indra, we offer the food that has the form of the oblation in such a way that his power increases.

To that Indra, who of old has rendered us good offices, we address (the praises) that he is pleased by : we celebrate him when the Soma is effused, repeating the prayer that the (sacrificial) food (offered) to Indra may be for his augmentation.

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, since you have made the praises (ब्रह्माणि (*brahmāṇi*)) increasing (वर्धनानि (*vardhanāni*)), that is, causing growth of their own accord, for that reason we pervade (विविष्टः (*viviṣṭaḥ*)) you with our minds (मतिभिः (*matibhiḥ*)) with so many such praises (तावत् (*tāvat*)). The sense is that you have so arranged the praises that they may be for my growth (मम (*mama*)). ⟨NOTE:377⟩ Moreover, O drinker of the pressed Soma (सुतपा (*sutapā*)), may we make praises (क्रियास्मै (*kriyāsmai*), meaning करवाम (*karavāma*)) which are the most productive of happiness (शंतमानि (*śaṃtamāni*)), delightful (रांद्र्या (*rāṃdryā*), meaning रमणीयानि (*ramaṇīyāni*)), joined with sacrifices, that is, with oblations (यज्ञैः (*yajñaiḥ*)), and conveying (वक्षणानि (*vakṣaṇāni*), meaning वाहकानि (*vāhakāni*)).
notes: ಗೋಋಜೀಕಂ in the bhāṣya and saṃhitā block; the pada block and Kannada gloss have ಗೋಯಜೀಕಂ / ಗೋಯಜೀಕಂ

en: - मतिभिः (*matibhiḥ*)—united with our minds (and offering them)
- सुतपाः (*sutapāḥ*)—O Indra, drinker of the Soma juice

O Indra, the praises that you have understood to be causes of your increase, just those praises we shall offer to you, united with our minds, and so satisfy you. O Indra, drinker of the Soma juice, when the Soma juice has been pressed, we recite praises that bring happiness, are delightful, are joined with sacrifices and are conveying.

Since, Indra you have made the (sacred) prayers (the means of ) your augmentation, we address such to you, along with our praises : may we, drinker of the effused libation, offer gratifying and acceptable eulogies with (our) sacrifices.

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, rejoicing (रराणः (*rarāṇaḥ*)), you take note (बोधि (*bodhi*), meaning बुध्यस्व (*budhyasva*)) of our oblation, characterised as the purodāśa. Moreover, drink quickly (तु (*tu*), पिब (*piba*)) the Soma that has been pressed and prepared with products of the cow such as curds (गोऋजीकं (*goṛjīkaṃ*)). ⟨NOTE:379⟩ For that, sit (आ सीद (*ā sīda*), meaning अभिविश (*abhiviśa*), enter) on this sacred grass of the sacrificer. After that, make wide (उरुं (*uruṃ*), meaning विस्तीर्णं (*vistīrṇaṃ*); कृधि (*kṛdhi*), meaning कुरु (*kuru*)) the place (लोकं (*lokaṃ*)) of the sacrificer who desires you (त्वायतः (*tvāyataḥ*)). The word उ (*u*) is a filler.
notes: ವಿಶ್ವವಾರಸ್ಯ in the bhāṣya; the Kannada Pratipadārtha has ವಿಶ್ವವಾರಾಯ

en: - पुरोडाशं (*puroḍāśaṃ*)—the oblation that has the form of the purodāśa
- गोयजीकं (*goyajīkaṃ*)—mixed with curds and the like
- इदं बर्हिः (*idaṃ barhiḥ*)—on this seat of darbha grass
- त्वायतः (*tvāyataḥ*)—of the sacrificer who desires your service

O Indra, you who have attained delight, know the oblation in the form of the purodāśa offered by us. Drink quickly the Soma juice mixed with curds and the like. Sit down on this seat of darbha grass prepared by the sacrificer. Make the place of the sacrificer who desires your service a spacious one.

Accept, Indra, who are condescending, our cakes and butter : drink the Soma mixed with curds: sit down upon this sacred grass (strewn by) the worshipper : grant ample possessions to him who depends upon you.

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra of fierce strength (उग्रोद्धर्णबलेंद्र (*ugroddharṇabaleṃdra*)), rejoice (मंदस्व (*maṃdasva*), meaning मोदस्व (*modasva*)) according to your pleasure (अनु जोषं (*anu joṣaṃ*)), that is, as agrees with your desires. The word हि (*hi*) is a filler. May these sacrifices (यज्ञासः (*yajñāsaḥ*)), that is, these Somas, reach you (प्राश्नुवंतु (*prāśnuvaṃtu*), meaning प्राप्नुवंतु (*prāpnuvaṃtu*)). O Puruhūta, invoked by many, may these our invocations (हवासः (*havāsaḥ*), meaning हवाः (*havāḥ*), praises) reach you. May this praise (धीः (*dhīḥ*), glossed as "praise") draw you (यम्याः (*yamyāḥ*), meaning आयच्छतु (*āyacchatu*), नियच्छतु (*niyacchatu*)) to our protection (अवसे (*avase*)). ⟨NOTE:380⟩
notes: ಪ್ರ ಮುಂಹಿಷ್ಠಾಯ in the bhāṣya; the Kannada Anuvāda has ಪ್ರ ಮಂಹಿಷ್ಠಾಯ

en: - उग्र (*ugra*)—O Indra of exceedingly great strength
- अनु जोषं (*anu joṣaṃ*)—as much as satisfies you
- प्र (*pra*)—let them come and reach you
- आ याम्याः (*ā yāmyāḥ*)—let them come and join

O Indra of exceedingly great strength, experience as much delight as satisfies you. May these Soma juices pervade you. O Indra, called by many, may these praises recited by us come and reach you. To urge you to our protection, may it come and join you.
Rejoice, fierce Indra, according to your pleasure : let these libations reach you : invoked of many, may these our invocations ascend to you : may this praise influence you for protection.

Sāyaṇa says: O friends (सखायः (*sakhāyaḥ*)), praisers, when the Somas have been pressed (सुतेषु (*suteṣu*)), fill together (सं पृणत (*saṃ pṛṇata*), meaning संपूरयत (*saṃpūrayata*)) with Somas, as you desire, this very Indra (तमीमेतमिंद्रं (*tamīmetamiṃdraṃ*)), the bountiful one (भोजं (*bhojaṃ*)), that is, the giver. For that Indra let there be abundant provision (कुवित् (*kuvit*), which he says is a name meaning "much"; आसति (*āsati*) meaning अस्तु (*astu*)). For what purpose? For our (नः (*naḥ*)) support, that is, nourishment (भराय (*bharāya*)). Indra does not harm (न मृधाति (*na mṛdhāti*), meaning न बाधते (*na bādhate*)) the sacrificer who is inclined to press Soma (सुष्टिं (*suṣṭiṃ*)), for his satisfaction (अवसे (*avase*), meaning तर्पणाय (*tarpaṇāya*)).
- सुतेषु (*suteṣu*)—when the Soma juice is pressed
- सुष्टिं (*suṣṭiṃ*)—the sacrificer who presses and offers Soma

O praisers, when you have pressed the Soma juice, satisfy with Soma juices this same famous Indra, the giver. For our nourishment let a very large share be prepared for that Indra. Indra does not harm, for his own satisfaction, the sacrificer who presses and offers Soma.

Friends, when the libations are effused, satisfy that liberal Indra with the Soma juices : let there be plenty for him, that (he may provide) for our nourishment: Indra never neglects the carc of him who presents copious libations.

Sāyaṇa says: Indra, the lord (क्षयत् (*kṣayat*), meaning ईश्वर (*īśvara*)) of the sacrificer who is wealthy (मघोनः (*maghonaḥ*)), that is, rich in oblations, has been praised in this very way (एव इत् (*eva it*)) in me, Bharadvāja (भरद्वाजेषु (*bharadvājeṣu*)), when the Soma has been pressed. The sense is that he has been praised so that Indra may be, for the praiser (जरित्रे (*jaritre*)), a guide (सूरिः (*sūriḥ*)) on the good path, and also the giver of the wealth (रायः (*rāyaḥ*)) that is desired by all (विश्ववारस्य (*viśvavārasya*)). ⟨NOTE:381⟩ He says that the two words as given are fillers: इदिति द्वयं पूरणं (*iditi dvayaṃ pūraṇaṃ*).
notes: ಉಕ್ಕೋಕ್ಷೇನ ಶಸ್ತ್ರೇಣ in the bhāṣya, reading damaged

en: - सूरिः (*sūriḥ*)—as the guide on the good path
- दाता (*dātā*)—as the giver (he will become in that same manner)
- मघोनः (*maghonaḥ*)—to the sacrificer who is wealthy in the form of the oblation
- एव इत् (*eva it*)—in this very manner

In whatever manner Indra will become the guide on the good path for the praiser, and the giver of the wealth desired by all, in that very manner Indra, the lord of the sacrificer who is wealthy in the form of the oblation, was praised in this way by me, Bharadvāja, when the Soma juice was pressed.

Thus has Indra, the lord of the opulent, been glorified by the Bharadwajas, upon the libation being effused, that he may be the director of his eulogist (to virtue), that Indra may be the giver of all desirable riches.

Sāyaṇa says: in the rites where Soma is present (सोमेषु (*someṣu*)), the exhilaration (मदः (*madaḥ*)) produced in Indra by drinking Soma is a rainer (वृषा (*vṛṣā*)), a shower of the sacrificer's desires; or else it is the maker of the rain that gladdens all people. Together with (सचा (*sacā*)) the recited śastra, the śloka, a word in the form of praise, also becomes a rainer. ⟨NOTE:383⟩ Indra is the drinker of the pressed Soma (सुतपाः (*sutapāḥ*)); he is ऋजीषी (*ṛjīṣī*), one who does not abandon even Soma whose juice has gone. ⟨NOTE:384⟩ He is wealthy (मघवा (*maghavā*)); that Indra becomes worthy of worship (अर्चत्र्यः (*arcatryaḥ*)) for the men (नृभ्यः (*nṛbhyaḥ*)), the leaders of praises, by the praises (उक्तैः (*uktaiḥ*)). He is the dweller in heaven (द्युक्षः (*dyukṣaḥ*)) and the lord (राजा (*rājā*)) of the praises (गिरां (*girāṃ*)), and he has unwasting protection (अक्षितोतिः (*akṣitotiḥ*)).
notes: ಋಜೀವಸಂಜ್ಞಕವಾದ in the Pratipadārtha; the Bhāvārtha has ಋಜೀಷೀಸಂಜ್ಞಕವಾದ
ಇರಚಿಯಂತೆ printed; read as "like an axle" (ಅಕ್ಷ)

en: - सोमेषु (*someṣu*)—in the sacrifices where Soma is offered
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—becomes a rainer of desires for the sacrificers
- उक्षा सचा (*ukṣā sacā*)—joined with the śastra mantra
- श्लोकः (*ślokaḥ*)—the praise of Indra also (is a rainer of desires)
- ऋजीषी (*ṛjīṣī*)—the drinker of Soma that bears the name ऋजीव (*ṛjīva*) ⟨NOTE:385⟩
- उक्षैः (*ukṣaiḥ*)—by the recitation of the śastra mantras
- द्युक्षः (*dyukṣaḥ*)—dweller in the world of heaven
- अक्षितोतिः (*akṣitotiḥ*)—becomes one who has imperishable protection
notes: ಆರ್ಯಃ ಚೆ printed; the saṃhitā and bhāṣya have ಅರ್ಯಃ ಚ

en: In the sacrifices where Soma is offered, the delight produced in Indra becomes a rainer of desires for the sacrificer. The praise of Indra joined with the śastra mantra also is a rainer of desires. Indra, who drinks Soma, who has the Soma named ऋजीषी (*ṛjīṣī*), and who is wealthy, becomes worthy of worship for the men who are praisers, through the recitation of the śastra mantras. Indra, who dwells in the world of heaven and is the lord of the praises, becomes also one who has imperishable protection.

At the rites at which the Soma (is offered) the exhilaration (produced) in Indra is a shower (of benefits to the offerer); so is the chaunted hymn with the (recited) prayer : therefore the drinker of the Soma, the partaker of the stale Soma, Maghavan, is to be propitiated by men with praises ; dweller in heaven, he is the lord of sacred songs, unwearied in the protection (of his votaries).

Sāyaṇa says: Indra, the possessor of food (वाजी (*vājī*)), when he is praised by us at the sacrifice (विदथे (*vidathe*)), gives food (वाजं (*vājaṃ*)); he gives it to us. What kind of Indra? He is ततुरिः (*taturiḥ*), the destroyer of enemies; वीरः (*vīraḥ*), the valiant; नर्यः (*naryaḥ*), beneficial to men; विचेताः (*vicetāḥ*), of discerning knowledge; the hearer (श्रोता (*śrotā*)) of our invocation (हवं (*havaṃ*)), that is, our praise; the wide protector (उर्व्यूतिः (*urvyūtiḥ*)) of the praising worshipper (गृणतः (*gṛṇataḥ*)); वसुः (*vasuḥ*), one who causes men to dwell; शंसः (*śaṃsaḥ*), worthy of praise among men (नरां (*narāṃ*)), the worshippers; and कारुधायाः (*kārudhāyāḥ*), the supporter of the कारू (*kārū*), the praisers. The connection is that Indra, being such, gives food.
- विचेताः (*vicetāḥ*)—the one who has knowledge filled with discernment
- नरां (*narāṃ*)—for the men who are praisers

May Indra, the destroyer of enemies, the valiant, the one beneficial to men, the one who has knowledge filled with discernment, the one who hears our praise, the one who protects abundantly the sacrificer who praises, the giver of dwellings, the one worthy of honour among the men who are praisers, the supporter of the praisers, the possessor of food, being praised at the sacrifices, give us food.

The surpasser (of foes), a hero, the friend of man, the discriminator, the hearer of the invocation, the great protector of his adorers, the giver of dwellings, the ruler of man, the cherisher of his worshippers, the bestower of food, grants us, when glorified at the sacrifice, (abundant) sustenance.

Sāyaṇa says: O valiant (शूर (*śūra*)) Indra, your great (बृहन् (*bṛhan*)) greatness (मह्ना (*mahnā*)) exceeds (प्र रिरिचे (*pra ririce*), meaning अतिरिच्यते (*atiricyate*)) heaven and earth (रोदस्योः (*rodasyoḥ*)); that is, it is greater than heaven and earth. The illustration here: like the axle (अक्षो न (*akṣo na*)) of a chariot that has gone out beyond the two wheels (चक्रोः (*cakroḥ*)). O Puruhūta (पुरुहूत (*puruhūta*)), Indra invoked by many, your many (पूर्विः (*pūrviḥ*)) protections (ऊतयः (*ūtayaḥ*)) spread out specially (वि रुरुहुः (*vi ruruhuḥ*)). The illustration there: like the branches (वयाः (*vayāḥ*), meaning शाखा (*śākhā*)) of a tree (वृक्षस्य नु (*vṛkṣasya nu*)) that spread out.
- प्र रिरिचे (*pra ririce*)—has exceeded and spread
- वृक्षस्य नु वयाः (*vṛkṣasya nu vayāḥ*)—the branches of a tree, in whatever manner they
- वि रुरुहुः (*vi ruruhuḥ*)—have spread out specially
notes: ನಾಲ್ವೇಭಾವಯಂತಿ: the word is damaged in the machine reading; the sense "make small" is taken from the Kannada gloss ಕ್ಷಯಿಸುವಂತೆ

en: O valiant Indra, your great greatness has spread out beyond heaven and earth, like an axle that spreads out beyond the wheels. O Indra, called by many, as the branches of a tree spread out on all sides, so your exceedingly great protections have spread out specially.

Mighty hero, by your magnitude, (the extant) of heaven and earth is exceeded, as the axle by the (circumference of the) wheels : invoked of many, your numerous benefits, Indra, spread out like the branches of a tree.
For the sentence in this Ṛk, वृक्षस्य नु ते पुरुहूत वयाः (*vṛkṣasya nu te puruhūta vayāḥ*), Yāska has given the following etymology:

वृक्षस्य नु ते पुरुहूत वयाः । वृक्षस्येव ते पुरुहूत शाखाः । वयाः शाखाः वेतेर्वातायना भवंति । शाखाः खशयाः शक्नोतेर्वा । (*vṛkṣasya nu te puruhūta vayāḥ | vṛkṣasyeva te puruhūta śākhāḥ | vayāḥ śākhāḥ vetervātāyanā bhavaṃti | śākhāḥ khaśayāḥ śaknotervā |*) (Ni. 1-4)

The word वयाः (*vayāḥ*) is formed from the root वि (*vi*), "to move", and indicates the meaning "branches of a tree". These branches or boughs move by the wind. Therefore the word वयाः (*vayāḥ*) means the boughs of a tree that move (sway) by the wind. Or else the word वयाः (*vayāḥ*) or शाखाः (*śākhāḥ*) may also be formed from the root शक् (*śak*), "to stand". How? By transposing the letters of the word शाखा (*śākhā*) it becomes खशा (*khaśā*). ख (*kha*) means the atmosphere; शा (*śā*) are those that are in it or abide there. Therefore the boughs of a tree are called शाखाः (*śākhāḥ*) or वयाः (*vayāḥ*): this is the chief sense of the etymological sentence.

Sāyaṇa says: O Puruśāka (पुरुशाक (*puruśāka*)), Indra of many works, your powers or works (शाकाः (*śākāḥ*)), you who are possessed of wisdom (शचीवतः (*śacīvataḥ*)), move about everywhere; "move about" is the word to be supplied. The illustration: as the tracks (स्रुतयः (*srutayaḥ*)) of cows, of milch cows, are movable everywhere (संचरणीः (*saṃcaraṇīḥ*)). Also like the cords (तंतयः (*taṃtayaḥ*)) of calves: a तंति (*taṃti*) is a long stretched rope to which many calves are bound by fixed side-ropes. As the cords are binders of many calves, O Sudāman (सुदामन् (*sudāman*)), Indra of excellent gifts, so your powers are possessed of bonds (दामन्वंतः (*dāmanvaṃtaḥ*)), binders of many enemies, and not themselves bound (आदामानः (*ādāmānaḥ*)) by others.
- पुरुशाक (*puruśāka*)—O Indra, who have many works
- स्रुतय इव (*srutaya iva*)—like the paths of movement
- संचरणीः (*saṃcaraṇīḥ*)—spread everywhere and are fit for movement

O Indra of many works, as the paths of movement of cows, though spread out and scattered everywhere, gather together again, so your various powers, you who are possessed of wisdom, though they spread and move everywhere, gather and unite again. O Indra, excellent giver, your powers are such as bind enemies, and are not themselves bound.

Accomplisher of many acts, the energies of you who are (ever) active (congregate from all directions), like the converging tracks of cattle : they are the bonds (of foes) themselves unfettered, munificent Indra, like the tethers of (many) calves.

Sāyaṇa says: this Indra today (अद्य (*adya*)) does one work (कर्वरं (*karvaraṃ*), which he says is a name for work), and tomorrow (श्वः (*śvaḥ*)) another, quite different from the one stated. This is explained: असत् (*asat*) is the inauspicious work such as hurling the thunderbolt, and सत् (*sat*) is the auspicious work such as raining. Or else: the killing and the like of the three-headed Viśvarūpa is the inauspicious work, and the killing and the like of an asura such as Vṛtra, who harasses the world, is the auspicious work; again and again (मुहुः (*muhuḥ*)) this Indra is the doer (आचक्रिः (*ācakriḥ*)). The sense is that, repeating by his own greatness works that differ from one another, every day he does another work that others cannot share. Indra, such as he is, in this sacrifice, let him be the one who conducts to its end (पर्येतास्ति (*paryetāsti*), meaning परिगमयिता भवतु (*parigamayitā bhavatu*)) the fruit to be desired (वशस्य (*vaśasya*)), such as heaven, for us. Mitra (मित्रः (*mitraḥ*)) is the deity presiding over the day, Varuṇa (वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)) the deity presiding over the night, Pūṣan (पूषा (*pūṣā*)) the nourishing deity, and Arya the impeller, Savitṛ; these, controlled by Indra, are to be conductors of our desire. Or else Mitra and the others are also named here in their own right; each of Mitra and the others, and Indra, is to be the conductor of our desire. And so it is said in the Bṛhaddevatā: प्रोतयेऽन्यदिति त्वेते वैश्वदेव्यावृचौ स्मृते इति (*protaye 'nyaditi tvete vaiśvadevyāvṛcau smṛte iti*) **GLOSS**
- अन्यदु (*anyadu*)—does a different kind of work
- वशस्य (*vaśasya*)—to the heaven and the like that are desired
- पर्येतास्ति (*paryetāsti*)—let him be the one who leads
- आर्यः चॆ (*āryaḥ cè*)—and the venerable Savitṛ (let them, together with Indra, be our helpers) ⟨NOTE:387⟩
notes: ಸ್ಥಿರಾಯ: the Kannada gloss says "an enemy of firm strength"; Sāyaṇa says "unshaken in battle"; ಗಂಭೀರೇ ಚಿತ್: the Kannada gloss says "the deep sea", Sāyaṇa says "an unfathomable place"

en: Indra, who is able for many works, does one kind of work today and another kind of work another day. Indra accomplishes all works, the auspicious and the inauspicious, again and again. May this valiant Indra, in this sacrifice, be the one who leads us to the desired heaven and the like. May Mitra, Varuṇa, the god Pūṣan and the venerable Savitṛ also, together with Indra, be helpers to us.
Indra achieves one act to-day, another to-morrow, evil and good repeatedly : may he, and Mitra, Varuna, Pushan, Arya, be on this occasion promoters of the desired result.

O Indra, the worshippers, with uktha-recitations, that is, with hymns of praise (śastras), and with sacrifices, that is, with oblations, draw their desires from you and bring them in many ways to themselves, just as waters come down from the upper part of a mountain. Further, O Indra, who are borne by hymns (गिर्वाहः (*girvāhaḥ*): carried by praise-words), the well-known you, whom they make strong, or else, desiring food (vāja), the Bharadvājas, the praisers, approach with these aforesaid excellent praises, as horses, the bearers, quickly reach the battle. This is the illustration of swift going.
- आपः न (*āpaḥ na*)—as waters flow swiftly down
- वि अनयंत (*vi anayaṃta*)—(the sacrificers) make the things they desire come down
- आजिं न (*ājiṃ na*)—as they go swiftly to the battle and join it
- अभिः सुष्टुतिभिः (*abhiḥ suṣṭutibhiḥ*)—with these praises, praying

O Indra, as waters flow swiftly down from the upper part of a mountain, the sacrificers obtain the things they desire by worshipping you with their śastra-mantras and with oblations. O Indra, who are borne by praises, as horses go swiftly to battle and join it, the seers who desire food pray to you, the well-known, with these praises and attain you.
By praises and by sacrifices, Indra, (men) bring down (what they desire) from you, as waters (descend) from the top of the mountain:
desirous of food, they approach you, who are accessible by praise, with these their eulogies, as (eagerly as) coursers rush to battle.

The years (शरदः (*śaradaḥ*)) do not make Indra old; they do not wear him away. Likewise the months do not wear him away, and likewise the days do not diminish him ⟨NOTE:388⟩. Of this Indra, grown great as he is, may the body, being praised with our hymns (stoma) and with the uktha-recitations (śastras), grow; may it become greatly increased.
notes: the Sanskrit of the phrase ಕಿಂಚಾಕ್ತೋ ರಾತ್ರೇವ್ಯುಷ್ಟೌ ವಿವಾಸೇಽಹಿ ಪರಿತಕ್ಮ್ಯಾಯಾಂ ರಾತ್ರ್ಯೇ is damaged in the machine reading; the sense is taken from the Kannada gloss

en: - मासाः (*māsāḥ*)—the months (do not make him slack)
- न अवकर्शयंति (*na avakarśayaṃti*)—do not make him waste away; such
- वृद्धस्य चित् (*vṛddhasya cit*)—of the one who has grown great
May the body of that same Indra, who has grown great and whom neither years, nor months, nor days can make slack or waste away, be praised by our hymns and by our śastras and attain increase.
May the person of that vast Indra, celebrated by praises and prayers, ever increase; Indra, whom neither years nor months make old, nor days enfeebl.

Indra, being praised by us, does not bend, that is, does not come under the power of, the sacrificer who is of firm body; nor does he bend to one who is steady and unshaken in battle. To the sacrificer who is bold and is impelled by Dasyus, that is, by those devoid of rites, he does not submit. The meaning is that although such praisers have many merits, Indra does not come under the power of those who are joined with Dasyus. Further, mountains, great as they are, become easy to go over, easy to cross, for Indra; and even in a deep, unfathomable place there is for this Indra a shallow, a ford, as his domain. ⟨NOTE:389⟩
notes: ಧೈಯದಿಂದ: ಧೈರ್ಯ or ಧ್ಯೇಯ; Sāyaṇa has ಮನಸಾ "with the mind"

en: - स्तवान् (*stavān*)—Indra, who is praised by us
- वीळवे (*vīḷave*)—even to one with a firm body
- न नमते (*na namate*)—does not submit and bow
- स्थिराय (*sthirāya*)—to an enemy of firm strength
- शर्धते (*śardhate*)—who has attained zeal through strength
- दस्युजूताय (*dasyujūtāya*)—even to a man devoid of rites
- गंभीरे चित् (*gaṃbhīre cit*)—even in the very deep sea

Indra, who is praised by us, does not submit and bow to one of firm body. He does not submit even to an enemy of firm strength. Mountains of great form are easily traversable for Indra. Even in the very deep sea a land region (a bottom) is found for this Indra.

Glorified by us, he bows not down to the robust, nor to the resolute, nor the persevering (worshipper) who is instigated by the (irreligious) Dasyus : the lofty mountains are easy of access to Indra ; to him there is a bottom in the (lowest) deep.

O Indra, possessor of amatra, that is, of strength, O drinker of the pressed Soma, grant us, with some profound, hard-to-fathom and wide mind, foods and strengths. Further, at the dawning of night and in the night, O Indra, for our protection, being without harm to us, stand ready and firm. ⟨NOTE:390⟩
notes: ಕರ್ಮಣಾಮುಪಕ್ಷಪಯಿತ್ರಿರ್ವಿತ್ವಾಃ: the machine reading is damaged; the sense is taken as "destroyers of rites"

en: - अक्तोः व्युष्टौ (*aktoḥ vyuṣṭau*)—when night has passed and it is day
notes: ತ್ವಾಮರ್ಯೋಽರಯೋ । ಪ್ರಾಪಯಿತಾರ: the machine reading is damaged; the Kannada gloss of ನೃತಮಾಸಃ and ಆರ್ಯಃ differs from Sāyaṇa

en: O Indra, mighty one and drinker of Soma, provide us with foods and strengths by your profound and wide resolve. In the time of night and in the time of day, remaining without harm, be ready for our protection.

Powerful Indra, drinker of the Soma juice, (actuated) by a profound and comprehensive (purpose), grant us food and strength: be ever diligent, benevolent Indra, for our protection by day and by night.

O Indra, accompany, that is, attend, the leader of rites and praises in battle for his protection. From the enemy (रिषः (*riṣaḥ*)), whether near at hand or far away, the particle वा (*vā*) joining the unexpressed alternative that is meant, protect that praiser. Likewise, protect him from the enemy in the house, अमेति गृहनाम (*ameti gṛhanāma*), and in the forest. After that, may we, blessed with good sons, rejoice for a hundred winters, that is, for a hundred years.
- नायं (*nāyaṃ*)—the sacrificer who leads the rites
- इतो वा (*ito vā*)—whether he be near at hand (or far away)
- सुवीराः (*suvīrāḥ*)—we, endowed with excellent heroic sons

O Indra, follow the sacrificer who leads the rites, and stay with him in battle for his protection. Protect that praiser from the enemy, whether near at hand or far away. Protect him from all enemies in the house and in the forest. May we, endowed with excellent heroic sons, enjoy happiness for a hundred years.

Accompany, Indra, the leader in battle for his protection; defend him against a near (or distant) foe; protect him from an enemy, whether in (his) house or in a forest, and may we, blessed with excellent male descendants, be happy for a hundred winters.
